children.text: Śrīpūjyapādācāryaviracitā Sarvārthasiddhiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s> (Accomplishment of All Purposes) composed by the venerable <s>Pūjyapādācārya</s>

children.text: Prathamo ’dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: First Chapter

children.text: mokṣamārgasya netāraṃ bhetāraṃ karmabhūbhṛtām |
children.translated_text: I bow to the guide of the path to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), the destroyer of the mountains of <s>karma</s>,

children.text: jñātāraṃ viśvatattvānāṃ vande tadguṇalabdhaye ||1||
children.translated_text: the knower of the principles of the universe, for the attainment of His qualities. ||1||

children.text: § 1. kaścid bhavyaḥ pratyāsannaniṣṭhaḥ prajñāvān svahitam upalipsur vivivkte paramaramye bhavyasattvaviśrāmāspade kvacid āśramapade munipariṣan madye saṃniṣaṇṇaṃ mūrttam iva mokṣamārgam avāgvisargaṃ vapuṣā nirūpayantaṃ yuktyāgamakuśalaṃ parahitapratipādanaikakāryam āryaniṣevyaṃ nirgranthācāryavaryam upasadya savinayaṃ paripṛcchati sma. bhagavan, kiṃ nu khalu ātmane hitaṃ syād iti ? sa āha mokṣa iti. sa eva punaḥ pratyāha — kiṃ svarūpo ’sau mokṣaḥ kaścāsya prāptyupāya iti? ācārya āha — niravaśeṣanirākṛtakarmamalakalaṃkasyāśarīrasyātmano ’cintyasvābhāvikajñānādiguṇam avyābādhasukham ātyantikam avasthāntaraṃ mokṣa iti.
children.translated_text: § 1. A certain aspirant (<s>bhavya</s>), close to final attainment, wise, desirous of his own welfare, in a solitary and supremely beautiful hermitage that is a resting place for aspirant beings, having approached—seated in the midst of an assembly of sages, like the embodied path to liberation itself, exhibiting [it] through his form without the emission of speech, skilled in reasoning and scripture, solely engaged in establishing the welfare of others, revered by the noble, the best among the <s>Nirgrantha</s> (Jain) teachers—respectfully asked: 'Venerable one, what indeed would be beneficial for the self?' He replied: '<s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation).' He then again asked: 'What is the nature of that <s>mokṣa</s>, and what is the means of attaining it?' The teacher said: '<s>Mokṣa</s> is the ultimate state of the self—when the stain of the impurity of <s>karma</s> has been completely eliminated, when [the self] is disembodied—[a state] of inconceivable, innate qualities such as knowledge etc., of unobstructed bliss, absolute and final.'

children.text: § 2. tasyātyantaparokṣatvāc chadmasthāḥ pravādinas tīrthakaraṃ manyās tasya svarūpam aspṛśantībhir vāgbhir yuktyābhāsanibandhanābhir anyathaiva parikalpayanti
caitanyaṃ puruṣasya svarūpam, tacca jñeyākāraparicchedaparāṅmukham
children.translated_text: [Some say:] 'Consciousness is the essential nature of <s>Puruṣa</s> (the self), and that [consciousness] turns away from the delimitation by the forms of objects of knowledge'—

children.text: iti. tat sad apy asad eva nirākāratvād iti.
children.translated_text: thus [they say]. That, though existent, is as good as non-existent, due to being formless.

children.text: buddhyādivaiśeṣikaguṇocchedaḥ puruṣasya mokṣaḥ
children.translated_text: [Others say:] 'The destruction of the particular qualities belonging to <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) etc. [of the Vaiśeṣika system] is the liberation of <s>Puruṣa</s>'—

children.text: iti. tad api parikalpanam asad eva, viśeṣalakṣaṇaśūnyasyāvastutvāt.
children.translated_text: that too is a mere fabrication, as good as non-existent, because what is devoid of distinguishing characteristics is not a real entity.

children.text: pradīpanirvāṇakalpam ātmanirvāṇam
children.translated_text: [Yet others say:] 'The extinction (<s>nirvāṇa</s>) of the self is like the extinction of a lamp'—

children.text: iti ca. tasya kharaviṣāṇakalpanā tair evāhatya nirūpitā. ity evam ādi. tasya svarūpam anavadyam uttaratra vakṣyāmaḥ.
children.translated_text: the fabrication of that [view] is like [the fabrication of] a hare's horn, as has been refuted by those [thinkers] themselves. And so on. The true nature of that [mokṣa], which is faultless, we shall state later.

§ 2. Since that [mokṣa] is extremely remote [from ordinary perception], those in the state of delusion (<s>chadmastha</s>), the disputants, not accepting the <s>Tīrthaṅkara</s> (ford-maker), imagine its nature quite otherwise through words that do not touch its true form, based on mere semblances of reasoning—

children.text: § 3. tatprāptyupāyaṃ praty api te visaṃvadante —
jñānād eva cāritranirapekṣāt tatprāptiḥ, śraddhānamātrād eva vā, jñānanirapekṣāc cāritramātrād eva
children.translated_text: [Some say:] 'Attainment of that [mokṣa comes] from knowledge alone, independent of conduct; or from faith alone; or from conduct alone, independent of knowledge'—

children.text: iti ca. vyādhyabhibhūtasya tadvinivṛttyupāyabhūtabheṣajaviṣayavyastajñānādisādhanatvābhāvavad vyastaṃ jñānādir mokṣaprātyupāyo na bhavati.
children.translated_text: and so on. Just as for one afflicted by disease, separate knowledge etc. regarding the medicine that is the means of curing that [disease] are not [individually] the means [of cure], so too separate knowledge etc. is not the means of attaining <s>mokṣa</s>.
§ 3. Regarding the means of attaining it, they also disagree—

children.text: § 4. kiṃ tarhi? tat tritayaṃ samuditam ity āha —
children.translated_text: § 4. What then? It is the three combined together—thus he says—

children.text: samyagdarśanajñānacāritrāṇi mokṣamārgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Right faith (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), right knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>), and right conduct (<s>samyakcāritra</s>) [together constitute] the path to liberation (<s>mokṣamārga</s>). ||

children.text: § 5. samyag ity avyutpannaḥ śabdo vyutpanno vā. añcateḥ kvau samañcatīti samyag iti. asyārthaḥ praśaṃsā. sa pratyekaṃ parisamāpyate. samyagdarśanaṃ samyagjñānaṃ samyakcāritram iti. eteṣāṃ svarūpaṃ lakṣaṇato vidhānataś ca purastād vistareṇa nirdekṣyāmaḥ. uddeśamātraṃ tv idam ucyate — padārthānāṃ yāthātmyapratipattiviṣayaśraddhānasaṃgrahārthaṃ darśanasya samyagviśeṣaṇam. yena yena prakāreṇa jīvādayaḥ padarthā vyavasthitās tena tenāvagamaḥ samyagjñānam. vimohasaṃśayaviparyayanivṛttyarthaṃ samyagviśeṣaṇam. saṃsārakāraṇanivṛttiṃ pratyāgūrṇasya jñānavataḥ karmādānanimittakriyoparamaḥ samyakcāritram. ajñānapūrvakācaraṇanivṛttyarthaṃ samyagviśeṣaṇam.
children.translated_text: § 5. '<s>Samyak</s>' is either an underived or a derived word. From the root <s>añc</s> (to go), with the prefix <s>sam</s>, [it means] '<s>samañcati</s>' (goes well), hence '<s>samyak</s>.' Its meaning is commendation. It applies to each [term] separately: right faith (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), right knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>), right conduct (<s>samyakcāritra</s>). The essential nature of these will be specified in detail later, both by definition and by prescription. Only a brief indication is given here: the qualifier 'right' (<s>samyak</s>) for 'faith' (<s>darśana</s>) is for the purpose of including the disposition of belief (<s>śraddhāna</s>) regarding the true nature of the categories of reality (<s>padārtha</s>). The understanding of the categories such as <s>jīva</s> (soul) etc. exactly as they are constituted is right knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>). The qualifier 'right' is for the purpose of excluding delusion, doubt, and misapprehension. The cessation of activity that is the cause of the influx of <s>karma</s>, on the part of one who possesses knowledge and who has turned away toward the cessation of the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), is right conduct (<s>samyakcāritra</s>). The qualifier 'right' is for the purpose of excluding conduct preceded by ignorance.

children.text: § 6. paśyati dṛśyate ’nena dṛṣṭimātraṃ vā darśanam. jānāti jñāyate ’nena jñaptimātraṃ vā jñānam. carati caryate ’nena caraṇamātram vā cāritram. nanv evaṃ sa eva kartā sa eva karaṇam ity āyātam. tac ca viruddham. satyaṃ, svapariṇāmapariṇāminor bhedavivakṣāyāṃ tathābhidhānāt. yathāgnir dahatīndhanaṃ dāhapariṇāmena. uktaḥ kartrādisādhanabhāvaḥ paryāyaparyāyiṇor ekatvānekatvaṃ pratyanekāntopapattau svātantryapāratantryavivakṣopapatter ekasminn apy arthe na virudhyate. agnau dahanādikriyāyāḥ kartrādisādhanabhāvavat.
children.translated_text: § 6. '<s>Darśana</s>' (faith/vision): one sees, or it is seen through this, or it is mere seeing. '<s>Jñāna</s>' (knowledge): one knows, or it is known through this, or it is mere cognition. '<s>Cāritra</s>' (conduct): one moves, or it is moved through this, or it is mere movement. But then it would follow that the agent and the instrument are the same—and that is contradictory. True, but when one intends the distinction between [the self as] that which undergoes modification and the modification itself, such designation is [justified]. Just as fire burns fuel through the modification of burning. The relation of agent-instrument etc. between the correlate and its correlative, being one and many according to the principle of non-absolutism (<s>anekānta</s>), since the intention of independence and dependence is possible, is not contradictory even in a single entity—just as in fire, the agent-instrument relation of the action of burning etc. [is non-contradictory].

children.text: § 7. jñānagrahaṇam ādau nyāyyaṃ, darśanasya tatpūrvakatvāt alpāctaratvāc ca. naitad yuktaṃ, yugapad utpatteḥ. yadāsya darśanamohasyopaśamāt kṣayāt kṣayopaśamād vā ātmā samyagdarśanaparyāyeṇāvirbhavati tadaiva tasya matyajñānaśrutājnānanivṛttipūrvakaṃ matijñānaṃ śrutajñānaṃ cāvirbhavati ghanapaṭalavigame savituḥ pratāpaprakāśābhivyaktivat. alpāctarād abhyarhitaṃ pūrvaṃ nipatati. katham abhyarhitatvam? jñānasya samyagvyapadeśahetutvāt. cāritrāt pūrvaṃ jñānaṃ prayuktaṃ, tatpūrvakatvāc cāritrasya.
children.translated_text: § 7. [Objection:] The mention of knowledge first would be proper, since faith is preceded by it, and also because it is of lesser extent. This is not correct, because they arise simultaneously. When, through the subsidence, destruction, or destruction-cum-subsidence of the delusion pertaining to faith (<s>darśanamoha</s>), the self manifests in the mode of right faith, at that very moment, preceded by the cessation of wrong sensory knowledge (<s>matyajñāna</s>) and wrong scriptural knowledge (<s>śrutājñāna</s>), sensory knowledge (<s>matijñāna</s>) and scriptural knowledge (<s>śrutajñāna</s>) manifest—like the manifestation of the heat and light of the sun when a dense layer of clouds is removed. [Response:] That which is of lesser extent but more honored is placed first. How is it more honored? Because knowledge is the cause for the designation 'right' (<s>samyak</s>). Knowledge is placed before conduct, because conduct is preceded by it.

children.text: § 8. sarvakarmavipramokṣo mokṣaḥ. tatprāptyupāyo mārgaḥ. mārga iti caikavacananirdeśaḥ samas tasya mārgabhāvajñāpanārthaḥ. tena vyastasya mārgatvanivṛttiḥ kṛtā bhavati. ataḥ samyagdarśanaṃ samyagjñānaṃ samyakcāritram ity etat tritayaṃ samuditaṃ mokṣasya sākṣān mārgo veditavyaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 8. <s>Mokṣa</s> is the complete release from all <s>karma</s>. The means of attaining it is the path (<s>mārga</s>). And the use of the singular 'path' is to indicate the unified nature of the path. Thereby the denial of path-status to [any of the three] taken separately is accomplished. Therefore, this triad—right faith, right knowledge, and right conduct—combined together, should be understood as the direct path to <s>mokṣa</s>.

children.text: § 9. tatrādāv uddiṣṭasya samyagdarśanasya lakṣaṇanirdeśārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 9. Now, for the purpose of specifying the definition of right faith (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), which was mentioned first among those [three], this is stated—

children.text: tattvārthaśraddhānaṃ samyagdarśanam ||
children.translated_text: Belief in the categories of reality (<s>tattvārthaśraddhāna</s>) is right faith (<s>samyagdarśana</s>). ||

children.text: § 10. tattvaśabdo bhāvasāmānyavācī. katham? tad iti sarvanāmapadam. sarvanāma ca sāmānye vartate. tasya bhāvas tattvam. tasya kasya? yo ’rtho yathāvasthitas tathā tasya bhavanam ity arthaḥ. aryata ity artho niścīyata iti yāvat. tattvenārthas tattvārthaḥ. athavā bhāvena bhāvavato ’bhidhānam, tadavyatirekāt. tattvam evārthas tattvārthaḥ. tattvārthasya śraddhānaṃ tattvārthaśraddhānaṃ samyagdarśanaṃ pratyetavyam. tattvārthaś ca vakṣamāṇo jīvādiḥ.
children.translated_text: § 10. The word '<s>tattva</s>' denotes existence in general (<s>bhāvasāmānya</s>). How? '<s>Tad</s>' is a pronoun. And a pronoun refers to a general [entity]. Its being (<s>bhāva</s>) is '<s>tattva</s>.' Of what? That which is the meaning (<s>artha</s>), as it actually is—its being [as it is]—that is the meaning. '<s>Artha</s>' means that which is ascertained (<s>aryate</s>). The meaning characterized by <s>tattva</s> (reality) is <s>tattvārtha</s>. Alternatively, since there is no difference between an attribute and its possessor, the designation is of the possessor through the attribute. <s>Tattva</s> itself is the <s>artha</s> (meaning/reality): <s>tattvārtha</s>. The belief in <s>tattvārtha</s> is <s>tattvārthaśraddhāna</s>, which should be understood as right faith (<s>samyagdarśana</s>). And the <s>tattvārthas</s> are the [categories] beginning with <s>jīva</s> (soul), which will be stated [below].

children.text: § 11. dṛśer ālokārthatvāt śraddhānārthagatir nopapadyate? dhātunām anekārthatatvād adoṣaḥ. prasiddhārthatyāgaḥ kuta iti cet? mokṣamārgaprakaraṇāt. tattvārthaśraddhānaṃ hy ātmapariṇāmo mokṣasādhanaṃ yujyate, bhavyajīvaviṣayatvāt. ālokakas tu cakṣurādinimittaḥ sarvasaṃsārijīvasādhāraṇatvān na mokṣamārgo yuktaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 11. [Objection:] Since the root <s>dṛś</s> means 'to see' (illumination), the meaning of 'belief' (<s>śraddhāna</s>) is not applicable? [Reply:] No fault, since verbal roots have multiple meanings. [Objection:] Why abandon the well-known meaning? [Reply:] Because the context is the path to liberation. For belief in the categories of reality, being a transformation of the self, is appropriate as a means to liberation, since it pertains to aspirant souls (<s>bhavyajīva</s>). But mere seeing, which is caused by the eye etc. and is common to all transmigrating souls, is not appropriate as the path to liberation.

children.text: § 12. arthaśraddhānām iti cet? sarvārthaprasaṃgaḥ. tattvaśraddhānam iti cet? bhāvamātraprasaṃgaḥ. ‘sattādravyatvaguṇatvakarmatvādi tattvam’ iti kaiścit kalpyata iti. tattvam ekatvam iti vā sarvaikyagrahaṇaprasaṃgaḥ. ‘puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam’ ity ādi kaiścit kalpyata iti. evaṃ sati dṛṣṭeṣṭavirodhaḥ. tasmād avyabhicārārtham ubhayor upādānam. tad dvividhaṃ, sarāgavītarāgaviṣayabhedāt praśamasaṃvegānukampāstikyādyabhivyaktilakṣaṇaṃ prathamam. ātmaviśuddhimātram itarat.
children.translated_text: § 12. [Objection:] If [the sūtra said] 'belief in meanings' (<s>arthaśraddhāna</s>)? [Reply:] That would entail all objects [without restriction]. [Objection:] If [it said] 'belief in reality' (<s>tattvaśraddhāna</s>)? [Reply:] That would entail mere existence. [Some say:] 'Existence, substance-ness, quality-ness, action-ness, etc. constitute <s>tattva</s> (reality).' [Others say:] '<s>Tattva</s> is oneness'—that would entail grasping the unity of all things. [As some fabricate:] '<s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this' etc. In such a case, there would be contradiction with what is observed and desired. Therefore, both [words <s>tattva</s> and <s>artha</s>] are employed to avoid deviation. That [right faith] is of two kinds, due to the distinction between [those with] attachment and those free from attachment: the first is characterized by the manifestation of tranquility (<s>praśama</s>), ardor (<s>saṃvega</s>), compassion (<s>anukampā</s>), faith in [the categories] (<s>āstikya</s>), etc. The other is merely the purity of the self.

children.text: § 13. athaitat samyagdarśanaṃ jīvādipadārthaviṣayaṃ katham utpadyata ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 13. Now, how does this right faith (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), whose object is the categories beginning with <s>jīva</s> (soul), arise? To this he says—

children.text: tannisargād adhigamād vā ||
children.translated_text: That [right faith arises] from innate nature (<s>nisarga</s>) or from instruction (<s>adhigama</s>). ||

children.text: § 14. nisargaḥ svabhāva ity arthaḥ. adhigamo ’rthāvabodhaḥ. tayor hetutvena nirdeśaḥ. kasyāḥ? kriyāyāḥ. kā ca kriyā? utpadyata ity adhyāhriyate, sopaskāratvāt sūtrāṇām. tad etat samyagdarśanaṃ nisargād adhigamād votpadyata iti.
children.translated_text: § 14. '<s>Nisarga</s>' means inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). '<s>Adhigama</s>' means the comprehension of meaning. Their mention is as causes. Of what? Of an action. And what action? 'Arises' (<s>utpadyate</s>) is to be supplied, since <s>sūtras</s> have elliptical constructions. Thus: this right faith arises from innate nature or from instruction.

children.text: § 15. atrāha — nisargaje samyagdarśane ’rthādhigamaḥ syād vā na vā. yady asti, tad api adhigamajam eva nārthāntaram. atha nāsti, katham anavabuddhatattvasyārthaśraddhānām iti? naiṣa doṣaḥ, ubhayatra samyagdarśane antaraṅgo hetus tulyo darśanamohasyopaśamaḥ kṣayaḥ kṣayopaśamo vā. tasmin sati yad bāhyopadeśāvṛte prādur bhavati tan naisargikam. yat paropadeśapūrvakaṃ jīvādy adhigamanimittaṃ tad uttaram. ity anayor ayaṃ bhedaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 15. Here one objects: In right faith born from innate nature, is there comprehension of the meaning or not? If there is, then that too is born from instruction—it is not something different. If there is not, how can there be belief in the meaning for one who has not understood the reality? This is no fault: in both cases of right faith, the internal cause is the same—the subsidence, destruction, or destruction-cum-subsidence of faith-deluding [karma]. When that [subsidence etc.] occurs, that which manifests without external instruction is innate (<s>naisargika</s>). That which [manifests] preceded by the instruction of another, occasioned by the comprehension of [categories] such as <s>jīva</s> etc., is the latter. This is the difference between the two.

children.text: § 16. tadgrahaṇaṃ kim artham? anantaranirdeśārtham. anantaraṃ samyagdarśanaṃ tadity anena nirdiśyate. itarathā mokṣamārgo ’pi prakṛtas tasyābhisaṃbandhaḥ syāt. nanu ca ‘anantarasya vidhir vā bhavati pratiṣedho vā’ ity anantarasya samyagdarśanasya grahaṇaṃ siddham iti cet? na, ‘pratyāsatteḥ pradhānaṃ balīyaḥ’ iti mokṣamārga eva saṃbadyeta. tasmāt tadvacanaṃ kriyate.
children.translated_text: § 16. What is the purpose of the word 'that' (<s>tad</s>)? For the purpose of indicating the immediately preceding [topic]. Right faith, being immediately preceding, is indicated by 'that.' Otherwise, the path to liberation, which is also under discussion, would be connected. [Objection:] But by the rule 'what is immediately preceding receives either a prescription or a prohibition,' the reference to right faith is already established? [Reply:] No, because by the principle 'due to proximity, the principal [topic] is stronger,' it would be connected to the path to liberation itself. Therefore, the word 'that' is used.

children.text: § 17. tattvārthaśraddhānaṃ samyagdarśanam ity uktam. atha kiṃ tattvam ity ata idam āha —
children.translated_text: § 17. It has been said: 'Belief in the categories of reality is right faith.' Now, what are the categories (<s>tattvas</s>)? To this, this is stated—

children.text: jīvājīvāsravabandhasaṃvaranirjarāmokṣās tattvam ||
children.translated_text: Soul (<s>jīva</s>), non-soul (<s>ajīva</s>), influx (<s>āsrava</s>), bondage (<s>bandha</s>), stoppage (<s>saṃvara</s>), shedding (<s>nirjarā</s>), and liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>)—these are the categories (<s>tattva</s>). ||

children.text: § 18. tatra cetanālakṣaṇo jīvaḥ. sā ca jñānādibhedād anekadhā bhidyate. tadviparyayalakṣaṇo ’jīvaḥ. śubhāśubhakarmāgamadvārarūpaṃ āsravaḥ. ātmakarmaṇor anyo ‘nyapradeśānupraveśātmako bandhaḥ. āsravanirodhalakṣaṇaḥ saṃvaraḥ. ekadeśakarmasaṃkṣayalakṣaṇā nirjarā. kṛtsnakarmaviyogalakṣaṇo mokṣaḥ. eṣāṃ prapañca uttaratra vakṣyate. sarvasya phalasyātmādhīnatvād ādau jīvagrahaṇam. tadupakārāthatvāt tadanantaram ajīvābhidhānam. tadubhayaviṣayatvāt tadanantaram āsravagrahaṇam. tatpūrvakatvāt tadanantaraṃ bandhābhidhānam. saṃvṛtasya bandhābhāvāt tatpratyanīkapratipattyarthaṃ tadanantaraṃ saṃvaravacanam. saṃvare sati nirjaropapattes tadantike nirjarāvacanam. ante prāpyatvān mokṣasyānte vacanam.
children.translated_text: § 18. Among these: <s>jīva</s> (soul) is characterized by consciousness (<s>cetanā</s>). And that [consciousness] is divided manifoldly according to the distinctions of knowledge etc. <s>Ajīva</s> (non-soul) is characterized by the opposite of that. <s>Āsrava</s> (influx) is in the form of the doorway for the incoming of auspicious and inauspicious <s>karma</s>. <s>Bandha</s> (bondage) is the mutual interpenetration of the spatial units (<s>pradeśa</s>) of the self and of <s>karma</s>. <s>Saṃvara</s> (stoppage) is characterized by the obstruction of influx. <s>Nirjarā</s> (shedding) is characterized by the partial destruction of <s>karma</s>. <s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation) is characterized by complete separation from all <s>karma</s>. The elaboration of these will be stated later. Since all results depend on the self, <s>jīva</s> is mentioned first. Since it serves the purpose of [understanding] that [jīva], <s>ajīva</s> is mentioned next. Since it pertains to both of those, <s>āsrava</s> is mentioned thereafter. Since it is preceded by that [āsrava], <s>bandha</s> is stated next. Since for one who has attained stoppage there is no bondage, and for understanding its opposite, <s>saṃvara</s> is stated next. Since shedding (<s>nirjarā</s>) is possible when there is stoppage, it is stated adjacent to it. Since liberation is what is to be finally attained, it is stated at the end.

children.text: § 19. iha puṇyapāpagrahaṇaṃ kartavyam. ‘nava padārthāḥ’ iti anyair apy uktatvāt. na kartavyam āsrave bandhe cāntarbhāvāt. yady evam āsravādigrahaṇam anarthakam, jīvājīvayor antarbhāvāt. nānarthakam. iha mokṣaḥ prakṛtaḥ. so ’vaśyaṃ nirdeṣṭavyaḥ. sa ca saṃsārapūrvakaḥ. saṃsārasya pradhānahetur āsravo bandhaś ca. mokṣasya pradhānahetuḥ saṃvaro nirjarā ca. ataḥ pradhānahetuhetumatphalanidarśanārthatvāt pṛthagupadeśaḥ kṛtaḥ. dṛśyate hi sāmānye ’ntarbhūtasyāpi viśeṣasya pṛthagupādānaṃ prayojanārtham. ‘kṣatriyā āyātāḥ sūravarmā ’pi’ iti.
children.translated_text: § 19. Here, merit (<s>puṇya</s>) and demerit (<s>pāpa</s>) should also be included [as categories]. [Because] 'there are nine categories' has been stated by others too. [Reply:] They need not be [separately mentioned], since they are included within influx (<s>āsrava</s>) and bondage (<s>bandha</s>). If so, then the mention of influx etc. would be purposeless, since they too are included within soul (<s>jīva</s>) and non-soul (<s>ajīva</s>). [Reply:] It is not purposeless. Here, <s>mokṣa</s> is the main topic. It must necessarily be specified. And it is preceded by <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration). The principal cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> is influx and bondage. The principal cause of <s>mokṣa</s> is stoppage and shedding. Therefore, the separate mention is for the purpose of illustrating the principal cause, the caused [effect], and the result. For indeed, even when a particular is included in a general category, its separate mention for a purpose is observed: [e.g.,] 'The <s>Kṣatriyas</s> have come, and <s>Sūravarmā</s> too.'

children.text: § 20. tattvaśabdo bhāvavācīty uktaḥ. sa kathaṃ jīvādibhir dravyavacanaiḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ pratipadyate? avyatirekāt tadbhāvādhyāropāc ca sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ bhavati. yathā ‘upayoga evātmā’ iti. yady evaṃ tattalliṅgasaṃkhyānuvṛttiḥ prāpnoti? ‘viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasaṃbande saty api śabdaśaktivyapekṣayā upāttaliṅgasaṃkhyāvyatikramo na bhavati.’ ayaṃ krama ādisūtre ’pi yojyaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 20. It was said that the word '<s>tattva</s>' denotes existence. How then does it enter into co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) with substance-denoting words like '<s>jīva</s>' etc.? [Reply:] Due to non-difference and through the superimposition of that being [upon them], co-referentiality occurs—just as [in the statement] '<s>upayoga</s> (active consciousness) is itself the self.' [Objection:] If so, then the gender and number of those respective [terms] should carry over? [Reply:] 'Even when there is a qualifier-qualified relation, there is no deviation from the gender and number of the [syntactically] adopted [term], in dependence on the capacity of the word.' This principle should be applied to the first <s>sūtra</s> as well.

children.text: § 21. evam eṣām uddiṣṭāṇāṃ samyagdarśanādīnām jīvādīnāṃ ca saṃvyavahāraviśeṣavyabhicāranivṛtttyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 21. Thus, for the purpose of preventing the deviation of particular conventional usages regarding these enumerated [categories]—right faith etc. and <s>jīva</s> etc.—he says—

children.text: nāmasthāpanādravyabhāvatas tannyāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their designation is by name (<s>nāma</s>), representation (<s>sthāpanā</s>), substance (<s>dravya</s>), and state (<s>bhāva</s>). ||

children.text: § 22. atadguṇe vastuni saṃvyavahārārthaṃ puruṣakārān niyujyamānaṃ saṃjñākarma nāma. kāṣṭhapustacitrakarmākṣanikṣepādiṣu so ’yam iti sthāpyamānā sthāpanā. guṇair guṇān vā drutaṃ gataṃ guṇair droṣyate guṇān droṣyatīti vā dravyam. vartamānatatparyāyopalakṣitaṃ dravyaṃ bhāvaḥ. tad yathā, nāmajīvaḥ sthāpanājīvo dravyajīvo bhāvajīva iti caturdhā jīvaśabdārtho nyasyate. jīvanaguṇam anapekṣya yasya kasyacin nāma kriyamāṇaṃ nāma jīvaḥ. akṣanikṣepādiṣu jīva iti vā manuṣyajīva iti va vyavasthāpyamānaḥ sthāpanājīvaḥ. dravyajīvo dvividhaḥ āgamadravyajīvo noāgamadravyajīvaś ceti. tatra jīvaprābhṛtajñāyī manuṣyajīvaprābhṛtajñāyī vā anupayukta ātmā āgamadravyajīvaḥ. noāgamadravyajīvas tredhā vyavatiṣṭhate jñāyakaśarīrabhāvitadvyatiriktabhedāt. tatra jñātur yac charīraṃ trikālagocaraṃ taj jñāyakaśarīraṃ. sāmānyāpekṣayā noāgamabhāvijīvo nāsti, jīvanasāmānyasya sadāpi vidyamānatvāt. viśeṣāpekṣayā tv asti. gatyantare jīvo vyavasthito manuṣyabhavaprāptiṃ pratyabhimukho manuṣyabhāvijīvaḥ. tadvyatiriktaḥ karmanokarmavikalpaḥ. bhāvajīvo dvividhaḥ āgamabhāvajīvo noāgamabhāvajīvaś ceti. tatra jīvaprābhṛtaviṣayopayogāviṣṭo manuṣyajīvaprābhṛtaviṣayopayogayukto vā ātmā āgamabhāvajīvaḥ. jīvanaparyāyeṇa manuṣyajīvatvaparyāyeṇa vā samāviṣṭa ātmā noāgamabhāvajīvaḥ. evam itareṣām api padārthānāṃ nāmādinikṣepavidhir niyojyaḥ. sa kim arthaḥ? aprakṛtanirākaraṇāya prakṛtanirūpaṇāya ca. nikṣepavidhinā śabdārthaḥ prastīryate. tac chabdagrahaṇaṃ kim artham? sarvasaṃgrahārtham. asati hi tacchabde samyagdarśanādīnāṃ pradhānānām eva nyāsenābhisaṃbandhaḥ syāt, tadviṣayabhāvenopagṛhītānāṃ jīvādīnāṃ apradhānānāṃ na syāt. tacchabdagrahaṇe punaḥ kriyamāṇe sati sāmarthyāt pradhānānām apradhānānāṃ ca grahaṇaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text: § 22. An act of designation (<s>saṃjñākarma</s>) is when human effort is applied for the purpose of conventional usage to a thing that does not possess that quality. The placing of [an identity statement] 'this is he' in wooden images, painted pictures, or dice-casting and the like is <s>sthāpanā</s> (figurative establishment). <s>Dravya</s> (substance) is that which will quickly lose its qualities or will [soon] acquire qualities. <s>Bhāva</s> (state) is a substance characterized by its currently obtaining mode. Thus, the meaning of the word <s>jīva</s> (soul) is set forth in four ways: <s>nāma-jīva</s> (nominal soul), <s>sthāpanā-jīva</s> (figurative soul), <s>dravya-jīva</s> (substantial soul), and <s>bhāva-jīva</s> (modal soul). A <s>nāma-jīva</s> is when the name is given to anyone whatsoever without regard to the quality of being alive. A <s>sthāpanā-jīva</s> is that which is figuratively established as 'soul' or 'human soul' in dice-casting and the like. The <s>dravya-jīva</s> is twofold: <s>āgama-dravya-jīva</s> (scriptural-substantial soul) and <s>noāgama-dravya-jīva</s> (non-scriptural-substantial soul). Therein, a self that is not actively engaged [in cognition], which will be designated as a soul in the <s>prābhṛta</s> [texts] or as a human soul in the <s>prābhṛta</s> [texts], is the <s>āgama-dravya-jīva</s>. The <s>noāgama-dravya-jīva</s> is threefold, based on the distinction between the cognizer's body, the conditioned, and that which is different from both. Therein, the body of the knower that pertains to the three times is the 'cognizer's body.' From the standpoint of the general, there is no <s>noāgama-bhāvi-jīva</s> (non-scriptural-future soul), since the general characteristic of being alive always exists. But from the standpoint of the particular, there is. A soul established in another state of existence, facing toward the attainment of human existence, is a <s>manuṣya-bhāvi-jīva</s> (human-future soul). That which is different from this admits the alternatives of <s>karma</s> and <s>nokarma</s>. The <s>bhāva-jīva</s> is twofold: <s>āgama-bhāva-jīva</s> (scriptural-modal soul) and <s>noāgama-bhāva-jīva</s> (non-scriptural-modal soul). Therein, a self engaged in the cognitive activity pertaining to the subject of the <s>jīva-prābhṛta</s>, or endowed with cognitive activity pertaining to the subject of the <s>manuṣya-jīva-prābhṛta</s>, is the <s>āgama-bhāva-jīva</s>. A self that is pervaded by the mode of being alive or by the mode of being a human soul is the <s>noāgama-bhāva-jīva</s>. Thus the method of predication through <s>nāma</s> and the rest should be applied to the other categories (<s>padārthas</s>) as well. What is its purpose? For the removal of what is not under discussion and for the determination of what is under discussion. Through the method of predication, the meaning of words is spread out. And what is the purpose of using the word 'tat' (that)? For the purpose of comprehensive inclusion. For without that word, the predication would apply only to the principal [topics] like <s>samyagdarśana</s> (right faith) and the like, and would not apply to the subsidiary [topics] like <s>jīva</s> and the like, which are included as their objects. But when the word 'tat' is employed, the inclusion of both the principal and subsidiary [topics] is accomplished by [its] capacity.

children.text: § 23. evaṃ nāmādibhiḥ prastīrṇānām adhikṛtānāṃ tattvādhigamaḥ kutaḥ ity ata idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 23. Thus, [the question arises]: whence is the understanding of the <s>tattvas</s> (realities) that have been spread out through <s>nāma</s> and the rest and made the subject of discussion? To this, he says —

children.text: pramāṇanayair adhigamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Understanding [is attained] through <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) and <s>nayas</s> (standpoints).

children.text: § 24. nāmādinikṣepavidhinopakṣiptānāṃ jīvādīnāṃ tattvaṃ pramāṇābhyāṃ nayaīś cādhigamyate. pramāṇanayā vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇavikalpāḥ. tatra pramāṇaṃ dvividhaṃ svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca. tatra svārthaṃ pramāṇaṃ śrutavarjjam. śrutaṃ punaḥ svārthaṃ bhavati parārthaṃ ca. jñānātmakaṃ svārthaṃ vacanātmakaṃ parārtham. tadvikalpā nayāḥ. atrāha — nayaśabdasya alpāctaratvāt pūrvanipātaḥ prāpnoti. naiṣa doṣaḥ. abhyarhitatvāt pramāṇasya pūrvanipātaḥ. abhyarhitatvaṃ ca sarvato balīyaḥ. kuto ’bhyarhitatvam? nayaprarūpaṇaprabhavayonitvāt. evaṃ hy uktaṃ
pragṛhya pramāṇataḥ pariṇativiśeṣād arthāvadhāraṇaṃ nayaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Having grasped [the object] through <s>pramāṇa</s>, the determination of a thing due to a particular aspect is <s>naya</s>.'

children.text: iti. sakalaviṣayatvāc ca pramāṇasya. tathā coktaṃ
children.translated_text: And because <s>pramāṇa</s> has the totality of objects as its domain. As it is also stated:

children.text: sakalādeśaḥ pramānādhīno vikalādeśo nayādhīnaḥ
children.translated_text: 'A complete statement (<s>sakalādeśa</s>) is governed by <s>pramāṇa</s>; a partial statement (<s>vikalādeśa</s>) is governed by <s>naya</s>.'

children.text: iti. nayo dvividhaḥ dravyārthikaḥ paryāyārthikaś ca. paryāyārthikanayena bhāvatattvam adhigantavyam. itareṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ dravyārthikanayena, sāmānyātmakatvāt. dravyam arthaḥ prayojanam asyety asau dravyārthikaḥ. paryāyo ’rthaḥ prayojanam asyety asau paryāyārthikaḥ. tatsarvaṃ samuditaṃ pramāṇenādhigantavyam.
children.translated_text: <s>Naya</s> is twofold: <s>dravyārthika</s> (substance-oriented) and <s>paryāyārthika</s> (mode-oriented). Through the <s>paryāyārthika naya</s>, the reality of <s>bhāva</s> (modal states) is to be understood. The other three [realities] are to be understood through the <s>dravyārthika naya</s>, since they are of a general nature. That whose object and purpose is <s>dravya</s> (substance) is <s>dravyārthika</s>. That whose object and purpose is <s>paryāya</s> (mode) is <s>paryāyārthika</s>. All that, taken together, is to be understood through <s>pramāṇa</s>.

§ 24. The true nature of <s>jīva</s> and the rest, which have been set forth through the method of predication beginning with <s>nāma</s>, is understood through the two <s>pramāṇas</s> and the <s>nayas</s>. The <s>pramāṇas</s> and <s>nayas</s> have characteristics and varieties that will be described. Among these, <s>pramāṇa</s> is twofold: <s>svārtha</s> (for oneself) and <s>parārtha</s> (for others). Of these, the <s>pramāṇa</s> for oneself excludes <s>śruta</s> (testimony). <s>Śruta</s>, however, is both for oneself and for others: as knowledge, it is for oneself; as verbal expression, it is for others. <s>Nayas</s> are the partial perspectives of those [pramāṇas]. Here an objection [is raised]: since the word <s>naya</s> has fewer syllables [than <s>pramāṇa</s>], it should be placed first [in the compound]. This is not a fault. <s>Pramāṇa</s> is placed first because of its greater authority. And its greater authority prevails over all [other considerations]. Whence its greater authority? Because it is the source and origin of the exposition of <s>naya</s>. For thus it has been stated:

children.text: § 25. evaṃ pramāṇanayair adhigatānāṃ jīvādīnāṃ punar apy adhigamopāyāntarapradarśanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 25. Thus, to demonstrate another means of understanding <s>jīva</s> and the rest that have been understood through <s>pramāṇas</s> and <s>nayas</s>, he says —

children.text: nirdeśasvāmitvasādhanādhikaraṇasthitividhānataḥ ||
children.translated_text: [Understanding is also] through specification (<s>nirdeśa</s>), ownership (<s>svāmitva</s>), causation (<s>sādhana</s>), substratum (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), duration (<s>sthiti</s>), and classification (<s>vidhāna</s>).

children.text: § 26. nirdeśaḥ svarūpābhidhānam. svāmitvam ādhipatyam. sādhanam utpattinimittam. adhikaraṇam adhiṣṭhānam. stithiḥ kālaparicchedaḥ. vidhānaṃ prakāraḥ. tatra samyagdarśanaṃ kim iti praśne tattvārthaśraddhānām iti nirdeśo nāmādir vā. kasyety ukte sāmānyena jīvasya. viśeṣeṇa gatyanuvādena narakagatau sarvāsu pṛthivīṣu nārakāṇām paryāptakānām aupaśamikaṃ kṣāyopaśamikaṃ cāsti. prathamāyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ paryāptāparyāptakānāṃ kṣāyikaṃ kṣāyopaśamikaṃ cāsti. tiryaggatau tiraścāṃ paryāptakānām aupaśamikam asti. kṣāyikaṃ kṣāyopaśamikaṃ ca paryāptāparyāptakānām asti. tiraścīnāṃ kṣāyikaṃ nāsti. aupaśamikaṃ kṣāyopaśamikaṃ ca paryāptikānām eva nāparyāptikānām. manuṣyagatau manuṣyāṇāṃ paryāptāparyāptakānāṃ kṣāyikaṃ kṣāyopaśamikaṃ cāsti. aupaśamikaṃ paryāptakānām eva nāparyāptakānām. mānuṣīṇāṃ tritayam apy asti paryāptikānām eva nāparyāptikānām. devagatau devānāṃ paryāptāparyāptakānāṃ tritayam apy asti. aupaśamikam aparyāptakānāṃ katham iti cec cāritramohopaśamena saha mṛtān prati. bhavanavāsivyantarajyotiṣkāṇāṃ devānāṃ devīnāṃ ca saudharmaiśānakalpavāsinīnāṃ ca kṣāyikaṃ nāsti. teṣāṃ paryāptakānām aupaśamikaṃ kṣāyopaśamikaṃ cāsti.
children.translated_text: § 26. <s>Nirdeśa</s> (specification) is the statement of the intrinsic nature. <s>Svāmitva</s> (ownership) is lordship. <s>Sādhana</s> (causation) is the cause of origination. <s>Adhikaraṇa</s> (substratum) is the locus. <s>Sthiti</s> (duration) is the delimitation of time. <s>Vidhāna</s> (classification) is the variety. Therein, to the question 'What is <s>samyagdarśana</s> (right faith)?', the specification is: 'faith in the <s>tattvas</s> (realities),' or [alternatively, the fourfold predication beginning with] <s>nāma</s>. To the question 'Whose?', [it belongs] generally to the <s>jīva</s> (soul). Specifically, by way of the exposition of <s>gatis</s> (states of existence): in the hellish state (<s>narakagati</s>), in all the [seven] earths, for the hell-beings who have completed development (<s>paryāptaka</s>), both <s>aupaśamika</s> (subsidence-born) and <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s> (subsidence-cum-destructional) [right faith] exist. In the first earth, for both the fully developed and undeveloped, <s>kṣāyika</s> (destructional) and <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s> exist. In the animal state (<s>tiryaggati</s>), for animals who have completed development, <s>aupaśamika</s> exists. <s>Kṣāyika</s> and <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s> exist for both the fully developed and undeveloped. For female animals, <s>kṣāyika</s> does not exist. <s>Aupaśamika</s> and <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s> exist only for the fully developed, not for the undeveloped. In the human state (<s>manuṣyagati</s>), for humans — both fully developed and undeveloped — <s>kṣāyika</s> and <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s> exist. <s>Aupaśamika</s> exists only for the fully developed, not for the undeveloped. For human women, all three exist only for the fully developed, not for the undeveloped. In the divine state (<s>devagati</s>), for gods — both fully developed and undeveloped — all three exist. If asked: how can <s>aupaśamika</s> exist for the undeveloped? — [it applies] to those who die with the subsidence of <s>cāritra-moha</s> (conduct-deluding karma). For the gods and goddesses of the <s>Bhavanavāsī</s>, <s>Vyantara</s>, and <s>Jyotiṣka</s> classes, and for the female celestials of the <s>Saudharma</s> and <s>Aiśāna</s> heavens, <s>kṣāyika</s> does not exist. For their fully developed members, <s>aupaśamika</s> and <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s> exist.

children.text: § 27. indriyānuvādena pañcendriyāṇāṃ saṃjñināṃ tritayam apy asti netareṣām. kāyānuvādena trasakāyikānāṃ tritayam apy asti netareṣām. yogānuvādena trayāṇāṃ yogānāṃ tritayam apy asti. ayogināṃ kṣāyikam eva. vedānuvādena trivedānāṃ tritayam apy asti. apagatavedānām aupaṣamikaṃ kṣāyikaṃ cāsti. kaṣāyānuvādena catuṣkaṣāyāṇāṃ tritayam apy asti. akaṣāyāṇām aupaṣamikaṃ kṣāyikaṃ cāsti. jñānānuvādena ābhinibodhikaśrutāvadhikamanaḥparyayajñānināṃ tritayam apy asti. kevalajñānināṃ kṣāyikam eva. saṃyamānuvādena sāmāyikacchedopasthāpanāsaṃyatānāṃ tritayam apy asti. parihāraviśuddhisaṃyatānām aupaśamikaṃ nāsti, itarad dvitayam apy asti, sūkṣmasāṃparāyayathākhyātasaṃyatānām aupaśamikaṃ kṣāyikaṃ cāsti, saṃyatāsaṃyatānām asaṃyatānām ca tritayam apy asti. darśanānuvādena cakṣurdarśanācakṣurdarśanāvadhidarśanināṃ tritayam apy asti, kevaladarśanināṃ kṣāyikam eva. leśyānuvādena ṣaḍleśyānāṃ tritayam apy asti, aleśyānāṃ kṣāyikam eva. bhavyānuvādena bhavyānāṃ tritayam apy asti, nābhavyānām. samyaktvānuvādena yatra yat samyagdarśanaṃ tatra tad eva jñeyam. saṃjñānuvādena saṃjñināṃ tritayam apy asti, nāsaṃjñinām, tadubhayavyapadeśarahitānāṃ kṣāyikam eva. āhārānuvādena āhārakāṇāṃ tritayam apy asti, anāhārakāṇāṃ chadmasthānāṃ tritayam apy asti, kevalināṃ samudghātagatānāṃ kṣāyikam eva.
children.translated_text: § 27. By way of the exposition of sense-organs: for five-sensed beings possessing mind (<s>saṃjñin</s>), all three [types of right faith] exist, but not for others. By way of body-types: for mobile-bodied beings (<s>trasakāyika</s>), all three exist, but not for others. By way of <s>yoga</s> (activity): for [beings with] the three <s>yogas</s> [mind, speech, and body], all three exist. For those without <s>yoga</s>, only <s>kṣāyika</s> exists. By way of gender (<s>veda</s>): for [beings with] the three genders, all three exist. For those who have shed gender, <s>aupaśamika</s> and <s>kṣāyika</s> exist. By way of passions (<s>kaṣāya</s>): for those with the four passions, all three exist. For those without passions, <s>aupaśamika</s> and <s>kṣāyika</s> exist. By way of knowledge: for those with <s>ābhiniboddhika</s> (sensory), <s>śruta</s> (scriptural), <s>avadhi</s> (clairvoyant), and <s>manaḥparyaya</s> (mind-reading) knowledge, all three exist. For <s>kevalajñānins</s> (omniscients), only <s>kṣāyika</s> exists. By way of restraint: for those with <s>sāmāyika</s> (equanimity), <s>chedopasthāpana</s> (re-initiation), and the unrestraint-cum-restraint, all three exist. For those with <s>parihāraviśuddhi</s> (purificatory restraint), <s>aupaśamika</s> does not exist; the other two exist. For those with <s>sūkṣma-sāṃparāya</s> (subtle-passioned) and <s>yathākhyāta</s> (as-proclaimed) restraint, <s>aupaśamika</s> and <s>kṣāyika</s> exist. For the partially restrained and the unrestrained, all three exist. By way of perception: for those with ocular, non-ocular, and clairvoyant perception, all three exist. For <s>kevala-darśanins</s> (omniscient-perceivers), only <s>kṣāyika</s> exists. By way of <s>leśyā</s> (soul-coloring): for those with the six <s>leśyās</s>, all three exist. For those without <s>leśyā</s>, only <s>kṣāyika</s> exists. By way of capacity: for the capable (<s>bhavya</s>), all three exist; not for the incapable. By way of right faith: wherever a particular type of right faith exists, that very type should be known. By way of cognition-type: for the <s>saṃjñins</s> (rational beings), all three exist; not for the <s>asaṃjñins</s>; for those designated as neither, only <s>kṣāyika</s> exists. By way of nourishment: for those taking nourishment, all three exist; for non-nourishing <s>chadmasthas</s> (non-omniscients), all three exist; for <s>kevalins</s> (omniscients) in the state of bodily extension (<s>samudghāta</s>), only <s>kṣāyika</s> exists.

children.text: § 28. sādhanaṃ dvividham abhyantaraṃ bāhyaṃ ca. abhyantaraṃ darśanamohasyopaśamaḥ kṣayaḥ kṣayopaśamo vā. bāhyaṃ nārakāṇāṃ prakcaturthyāḥ samyagdarśanasya sādhanaṃ keṣāṃcij jātismaraṇaṃ keṣāṃcid dharmaśravaṇaṃ keṣāṃcid vedanābhibhavaḥ. caturthīm ārabhya ā saptamyā nārakāṇām jātismaraṇaṃ vedanābhibhavaś ca. tiraścāṃ keṣāṃcij jātismaraṇaṃ keṣāṃcid dharmaśravaṇaṃ keṣāṃcij jinabimbadarśanam. manuṣyāṇām api tathaiva. devānāṃ keṣaṃcij jātismaraṇaṃ keṣāṃcid dharmaśravaṇaṃ keṣāṃcij jinamahimadarśanaṃ keṣāṃcid devardhidarśanam. evaṃ prāgānatāt. ānataprāṇatāraṇācyutadevānāṃ devardhidarśanaṃ muktvānyat tritayam apy asti. navagraiveyakavāsināṃ keṣāṃcij jātismaraṇaṃ keṣaṃcid dharmaśravaṇam. anudiśānuttaravimānavāsinām iyaṃ kalpanā na saṃbhavati; prāgeva gṛhītasamyaktvānāṃ tatrotpatteḥ.
children.translated_text: § 28. <s>Sādhana</s> (causation) is twofold: internal and external. The internal [cause] is the subsidence, destruction, or subsidence-cum-destruction of <s>darśana-moha</s> (faith-deluding karma). The external [cause] — for hell-beings before the fourth [earth], the cause of right faith for some is recollection of past lives, for some hearing of <s>dharma</s> (religious teaching), and for some the overcoming of pain. From the fourth earth through the seventh, for hell-beings there is recollection of past lives and overcoming of pain. For animals, for some there is recollection of past lives, for some hearing of <s>dharma</s>, and for some the sight of a <s>Jina</s> image. For humans likewise. For gods, for some there is recollection of past lives, for some hearing of <s>dharma</s>, for some the sight of the <s>Jina</s>'s majesty, and for some the sight of a <s>devarddhi</s> (celestial saint). Thus up to the <s>Ānata</s> [heaven]. For the gods of <s>Ānata</s>, <s>Prāṇata</s>, <s>Āraṇa</s>, and <s>Acyuta</s> [heavens], all three [causes] except the sight of a <s>devarddhi</s> exist. For the inhabitants of the nine <s>Graiveyaka</s> [heavens], for some there is recollection of past lives, and for some hearing of <s>dharma</s>. For the inhabitants of the <s>Anudiśa</s> and <s>Anuttara</s> heavenly mansions, this classification is not possible, since only those who have already attained right faith are born there.

children.text: § 29. adhikaraṇaṃ dvividham — abhyantaraṃ bāhyaṃ ca. abhyantaraṃ svasvāmisaṃbandhārha eva ātmā, vivakṣātaḥ kārakapravṛtteh. bāhyaṃ lokanāḍī. sā kiyatī? ekarajjuviṣkambhā caturdaśarajjvāyāmā.
children.translated_text: § 29. <s>Adhikaraṇa</s> (substratum) is twofold: internal and external. The internal is the self itself, which is fit for the relation of owned and owner, since the operation of the grammatical agent depends on the intention [of the speaker]. The external is the <s>loka-nāḍī</s> (channel of the universe). How large is it? One <s>rajju</s> in width and fourteen <s>rajjus</s> in length.

children.text: § 30. sthitir aupaśamikasya jaghanyotkṛṣṭā cāntarmauhūrtikī. kṣāyikasya saṃsāriṇo jaghanyāntamauhūrtikī. utkṛṣṭā trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi sāntarmuhūrtāṣṭavarṣahīnapūrvakoṭidvayādhikāni. muktasya sādir aparyavasānā. kṣāyopaśamikasya jaghanyāntarmauhūrttikī utkṛṣṭāṣaṭṣaṣṭisāgaropamāṇi.
children.translated_text: § 30. The duration of <s>aupaśamika</s> [right faith] is at minimum and maximum a fraction of a <s>muhūrta</s> (48 minutes). For <s>kṣāyika</s> [right faith] of a worldly being, the minimum is a fraction of a <s>muhūrta</s>; the maximum is thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> (ocean-measured periods), with a fraction of a <s>muhūrta</s> added, minus eight years, plus two <s>pūrvakoṭis</s>. For the liberated one, it has a beginning but no end. For <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s> [right faith], the minimum is a fraction of a <s>muhūrta</s>; the maximum is sixty-six <s>sāgaropamas</s>.

children.text: § 31. vidhānaṃ sāmānyād ekaṃ samyagdarśanam. dvitayaṃ nisargajādhigamajabhedāt. tritayaṃ aupaśamikakṣāyikakṣāyopaśamikabhedāt. evaṃ saṃkhyeyā vikalpāḥ śabdataḥ. asaṃkhyeyā anantāś ca bhavanti śraddhātṛśraddhātavyabhedāt. evam ayaṃ nirdeśādividdhir jñānacāritrayor jīvājīvādiṣu cāgamānusāreṇa yojayitavyaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 31. As for classification (<s>vidhāna</s>): in general terms, <s>samyagdarśana</s> (right faith) is one. It is twofold by the distinction of innate (<s>nisargaja</s>) and acquired (<s>adhigamaja</s>). It is threefold by the distinction of <s>aupaśamika</s>, <s>kṣāyika</s>, and <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s>. Thus the varieties are numerable in terms of verbal [categories]. They become innumerable and infinite by the distinction of believers and objects of belief. Thus this method of specification and so forth should be applied, following scripture, to knowledge and conduct, and to <s>jīva</s>, <s>ajīva</s>, and the other [categories].

children.text: § 32. kim etair eva jīvādīnām adhigamo bhavati uta anyo ’py adhigamopāyo ’stīti paridṛṣṭo ’stīty āha —
children.translated_text: § 32. Is the understanding of <s>jīva</s> and the rest accomplished only through these [methods], or is there yet another means of understanding? Observing that there is, he says —

children.text: satsaṃkhyākṣetrasparśanakālāntarabhāvālpabahutvaiś ca ||
children.translated_text: And through existence (<s>sat</s>), enumeration (<s>saṃkhyā</s>), field (<s>kṣetra</s>), extent (<s>sparśana</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), interval (<s>antara</s>), state (<s>bhāva</s>), and relative proportion (<s>alpabahutvam</s>).

children.text: § 33. sad ity astitvanirdeśaḥ. sa praśaṃsādiṣu vartamāno neha gṛhyate. saṃkhyā bhedagaṇanā. kṣetraṃ nivāso vartamānakālaviṣayaḥ. tad eva sparśanaṃ trikālagocaram. kālo dvividhaḥ — mukhyo vyāvahārikaś ca. tayor uttaratra nirṇayo vakṣhyate. antaraṃ virahakālaḥ. bhāvaḥ aupaśamikādilakṣaṇaḥ. alpabahutvam anyo ’nyāpekṣayā viśeṣapratipattiḥ. etaiś ca samyagdarśanādīnāṃ jīvādīnāṃ cādhigamo veditavyaḥ. nanu ca nirdeśād eva sadgrahaṇaṃ siddham. vidhānagrahaṇāt saṃkhyāgatiḥ. adhikaraṇagrahaṇāt kṣetrasparśanāvabodhaḥ. sthitigrahaṇāt kālasaṃgrahaḥ. bhāvo nāmādiṣu saṃgṛhīta eva. punar eṣāṃ kim arthaṃ grahaṇam iti. satyasiddham. vineyāśayavaśāt tattvadeśanādikalpaḥ. kecit saṃkṣeparucayaḥ kecit vistararucayaḥ. apare nātisaṃkṣepeṇa nātivistareṇa pratipādyāḥ. sarvasattvānugrahārtho hi satāṃ prayāsa iti adhigamābhyupāyabhedoddeśah kṛtaḥ. itarathā hi
pramāṇanayair adhigamaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Understanding [is attained] through <s>pramāṇas</s> and <s>nayas</s>'

children.text: ity anenaiva siddhatvād itareṣāṃ grahaṇam anarthakaṃ syāt.
children.translated_text: since [the matter] is already established by this [sūtra] alone, the mention of the others would be purposeless.

§ 33. <s>Sat</s> means the statement of existence. That [word <s>sat</s>] occurring in the sense of praise and so on is not taken here. <s>Saṃkhyā</s> (enumeration) is the counting of distinctions. <s>Kṣetra</s> (field) is the habitat, pertaining to the present time. That very same [thing considered as] <s>sparśana</s> (extent) pertains to the three times. <s>Kāla</s> (time) is twofold: ultimate (<s>mukhya</s>) and conventional (<s>vyāvahārika</s>). The determination of these two will be stated later. <s>Antara</s> (interval) is the duration of absence. <s>Bhāva</s> (state) is characterized by <s>aupaśamika</s> and the like. <s>Alpabahutvam</s> (relative proportion) is the determination of distinction in relation to one another. Through these, the understanding of <s>samyagdarśana</s> and the rest, and of <s>jīva</s> and the rest, should be known. Objection: the comprehension of <s>sat</s> (existence) is already accomplished through <s>nirdeśa</s> (specification) alone; the knowledge of <s>saṃkhyā</s> (number) through the mention of <s>vidhāna</s> (classification); the understanding of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>sparśana</s> (field and extent) through the mention of <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (substratum); the comprehension of <s>kāla</s> (time) through the mention of <s>sthiti</s> (duration); and <s>bhāva</s> (state) is already included in <s>nāma</s> and the rest. What then is the purpose of mentioning these again? True, it is established. But the method of teaching the realities varies according to the dispositions of those to be instructed. Some prefer conciseness, some prefer elaboration, and others are to be taught neither too concisely nor too elaborately. For the effort of the good is for the benefit of all beings — thus the enumeration of the various means of understanding has been made. Otherwise indeed,

children.text: § 34. tatra jīvadravyam adhikṛtya sadādyanuyogadvāranirūpaṇaṃ kriyate. jīvāś caturdaśasu guṇasthāneṣu vyavasthitāḥ. mithyādṛṣṭiḥ sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭiḥ samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭiḥ asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭiḥ saṃyatāsamyataḥ pramattasaṃyataḥ apramattasaṃyattaḥ apūrvakaraṇasthāne upaśamakaḥ kṣapakaḥ anivṛttibādarasāṃparāyasthāne upaśamakaḥ kṣapakaḥ sūkṣmasāmparāyasthāne upaśamakaḥ kṣapakaḥ upaśāntakaṣāyavītarāgachadmasthaḥ kṣīṇakaṣāyavītarāgachadmasthaḥ sayogakevalī ayogakevalī ceti. eteṣām eva jīvasamāsānāṃ nirūpaṇārthaṃ caturdaśa mārgaṇāsthānāni jñeyāni. gatīndriyakāyayogavedakaṣāyajñānasaṃyamadarśanaleśyābhavyasamyaktvasaṃjñāhārakā iti.
children.translated_text: § 34. Now, taking up the substance of <s>jīva</s> (soul), an examination through the doors of inquiry beginning with existence (<s>sat</s>) is made. Souls are situated in fourteen <s>guṇasthānas</s> (stages of spiritual development): (1) <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong believer), (2) <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> (one who has fallen from right faith), (3) <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s> (one with mixed right and wrong faith), (4) <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> (right believer without self-restraint), (5) <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s> (partially self-restrained), (6) <s>pramattasaṃyata</s> (self-restrained with negligence), (7) <s>apramattasaṃyata</s> (self-restrained without negligence), (8) in the stage of <s>apūrvakaraṇa</s> (unprecedented transformation): the subsider and the destroyer, (9) in the stage of <s>anivṛttibādarasāṃparāya</s> (non-retrogressive gross passions): the subsider and the destroyer, (10) in the stage of <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāya</s> (subtle passions): the subsider and the destroyer, (11) <s>upaśāntakaṣāyavītarāgachadmastha</s> (passionless through subsidence, with limited knowledge), (12) <s>kṣīṇakaṣāyavītarāgachadmastha</s> (passionless through destruction, with limited knowledge), (13) <s>sayogakevalī</s> (omniscient with activity), and (14) <s>ayogakevalī</s> (omniscient without activity). For the purpose of examining these very <s>jīva</s> classifications, fourteen <s>mārgaṇāsthānas</s> (stations of investigation) should be known: destiny (<s>gati</s>), sense-organs (<s>indriya</s>), body-type (<s>kāya</s>), activity (<s>yoga</s>), sex-determination (<s>veda</s>), passions (<s>kaṣāya</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), self-restraint (<s>saṃyama</s>), perception (<s>darśana</s>), coloring (<s>leśyā</s>), capacity for liberation (<s>bhavya</s>), right faith (<s>samyaktva</s>), rationality (<s>saṃjñā</s>), and nutrition (<s>āhāraka</s>).

children.text: § 35. tatra satprarūpaṇā dvividhā sāmānyena viśeṣeṇa ca. sāmānyena asti mithyādṛṣṭiḥ sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭir ity evam ādi. viśeṣeṇa gatyanuvādena narakagatau sarvāsu pṛthivīṣu ādyāni catvāri guṇasthānāni santi. tiyaggatau tāny eva saṃyatāsaṃyatasthānādhikāni santi. manuṣyagatau caturdaśāpi santi. devagatau nārakavat. indriyānuvādena ekendriyādiṣu caturindriyaparyanteṣu ekam eva mithyādṛṣṭisthānam. pañcendriyeṣu caturdaśāpi santi. kāyānuvādena pṛthivīkāyādivanaspatikāyānteṣu ekam eva mithyādṛṣṭisthānam. trasakāyeṣu caturdaśāpi santi. yogānuvādena triṣu yogeṣu trayodaśa guṇasthānāni bhavanti. tataḥ paraṃ ayogakevalī. vedānuvādena triṣu vedeṣu mithyādṛṣṭyādyanivṛttibādarāntāni santi. apagatavedesu anivṛttibādarādyayogakevalyantāni.
children.translated_text: § 35. The existential analysis (<s>satprarūpaṇā</s>) is twofold: general and specific. Generally: the <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> exists, the <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> exists—and so forth. Specifically, by the thread of destiny (<s>gatyanuvāda</s>): in the hellish destiny (<s>narakagati</s>), in all the earths [of hell], the first four <s>guṇasthānas</s> exist. In the animal destiny (<s>tiryaggati</s>), those same [four] plus the stage of partial self-restraint (<s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>) exist. In the human destiny (<s>manuṣyagati</s>), all fourteen exist. In the celestial destiny (<s>devagati</s>), [it is] like the hellish. By the thread of sense-organs (<s>indriyānuvāda</s>): among one-sensed beings up to four-sensed beings, there is only the one stage of <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>. Among five-sensed beings, all fourteen exist. By the thread of body-type (<s>kāyānuvāda</s>): among earth-bodied beings up to plant-bodied beings (<s>vanaspatikāya</s>), there is only the one stage of <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>. Among mobile beings (<s>trasakāya</s>), all fourteen exist. By the thread of activity (<s>yogānuvāda</s>): in the three types of activity [mind, speech, body], thirteen <s>guṇasthānas</s> exist; beyond that is the <s>ayogakevalī</s>. By the thread of sex-determination (<s>vedānuvāda</s>): in the three types of sex-determination, [stages] from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>anivṛttibādara</s> exist. In those from whom sex-determination has departed, [stages] from <s>anivṛttibādara</s> up to <s>ayogakevalī</s> exist.

children.text: § 36. kaṣāyānuvādena krodhamānamāyāsu mithyādṛṣṭyādīni anivṛttibādarasthānāntāni santi. lobhakaṣāye tāny eva sūkṣmasāṃparāyasthānādhikāni. akaṣāyaḥ upaśāntakaṣāyaḥ kṣīṇakaṣāyaḥ sayogakevalī ayogakevalī ceti.
children.translated_text: § 36. By the thread of passions (<s>kaṣāyānuvāda</s>): in anger (<s>krodha</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), and deceit (<s>māyā</s>), [stages] from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to the <s>anivṛttibādara</s> stage exist. In the passion of greed (<s>lobha</s>), those same plus the <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāya</s> stage exist. The passionless (<s>akaṣāya</s>) [states are]: <s>upaśāntakaṣāya</s> (passions subsided), <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s> (passions destroyed), <s>sayogakevalī</s>, and <s>ayogakevalī</s>.

children.text: § 37. jñānānuvādena matyājñānaśrutājñānavibhaṅgajñāneṣu mithyādṛṣṭiḥ sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭiś cāsti. ābhinibodhikaśrutāvadhijñāneṣu asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādīni kṣīṇakaṣāyāntāni santi. manaḥparyayajñāne pramattasaṃyatādayaḥ kṣīṇakaṣāyāntāḥ santi. kevalajñāne sayogo ’yogaś ca.
children.translated_text: § 37. By the thread of knowledge (<s>jñānānuvāda</s>): in wrong sensory knowledge (<s>matyājñāna</s>), wrong scriptural knowledge (<s>śrutājñāna</s>), and clairvoyance (<s>vibhaṅgajñāna</s>), the <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> and <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> exist. In sensory knowledge (<s>ābhinibodhika</s>), scriptural knowledge (<s>śruta</s>), and clairvoyant knowledge (<s>avadhijñāna</s>), [stages] from <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s> exist. In telepathic knowledge (<s>manaḥparyayajñāna</s>), [stages] from <s>pramattasaṃyata</s> up to <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s> exist. In omniscient knowledge (<s>kevalajñāna</s>), [there are] <s>sayoga</s> (with activity) and <s>ayoga</s> (without activity).

children.text: § 38. saṃyamānuvādena saṃyatāḥ pramattādayo ’yogakevalyantāḥ. sāmāyikacchedopasthāpanāśuddhisaṃyatāḥ pramattādayo ’nivṛttisthānāntāḥ. parihāraviśuddhisaṃyatāḥ pramattāś ca pramattāś ca.

sūkṣmasāṃparāyaśuddhisaṃyatā ekasminn eva sūkṣmasāṃparāyasthāne. yathākhyātavihāraśuddhisaṃyatā upaśāntakaṣāyādayo ’yogakevalyāntāḥ. saṃyatāsaṃyatā ekasminn eva saṃyatāsaṃyatasthāne. asaṃyatā ādy eṣu caturṣu guṇasthāneṣu.
children.translated_text: Those with <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāyaśuddhi</s> (subtle-passion pure) self-restraint are in the single <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāya</s> stage alone. Those with <s>yathākhyātavihāraśuddhi</s> (conduct-as-described pure) self-restraint [include stages] from <s>upaśāntakaṣāya</s> up to <s>ayogakevalī</s>. The partially self-restrained (<s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>) are in the single <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s> stage alone. The unrestrained (<s>asaṃyata</s>) are in the first four <s>guṇasthānas</s>.

§ 38. By the thread of self-restraint (<s>saṃyamānuvāda</s>): the self-restrained (<s>saṃyata</s>) [include stages] from <s>pramatta</s> up to <s>ayogakevalī</s>. Those with <s>sāmāyika</s> (equanimous), <s>chedopasthāpana</s> (reinitiated), and <s>śuddhi</s> (pure) self-restraint [include stages] from <s>pramatta</s> up to the <s>anivṛtti</s> stage. Those with <s>parihāraviśuddhi</s> (special purificatory) self-restraint are [either] <s>pramatta</s> or <s>apramatta</s>.

children.text: § 39. darśanānuvādena cakṣurdarśanācakṣurdarśanayor mithyādṛṣṭyādīni kṣīṇakaṣāyāntāni santi. avadhidarśane asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādīni kṣīṇakaṣāyāntāni santi. kevaladarśane sayogakevalī ayogakevalī ca.
children.translated_text: § 39. By the thread of perception (<s>darśanānuvāda</s>): in ocular perception (<s>cakṣurdarśana</s>) and non-ocular perception (<s>acakṣurdarśana</s>), [stages] from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s> exist. In clairvoyant perception (<s>avadhidarśana</s>), [stages] from <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s> exist. In omniscient perception (<s>kevaladarśana</s>), [there are] <s>sayogakevalī</s> and <s>ayogakevalī</s>.

children.text: § 40. leśyānuvādena kṛṣṇanīlakapotaleśyāsu mithyādṛṣṭyādīni asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyantāni santi. tejaḥpadmaleśyayor mithyādṛṣṭyādīni apramattasthānāntāni. śuklaleśyāyāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādīni sayogakevalyantāni. aleśyā ayogakevalinaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 40. By the thread of coloring (<s>leśyānuvāda</s>): in the black (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>), blue (<s>nīla</s>), and grey (<s>kapota</s>) colorings, [stages] from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> exist. In the fiery (<s>tejas</s>) and lotus (<s>padma</s>) colorings, [stages] from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to the <s>apramatta</s> stage exist. In the white (<s>śukla</s>) coloring, [stages] from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>sayogakevalī</s> exist. The colorless (<s>aleśyā</s>) is the <s>ayogakevalin</s>.

children.text: § 41. bhavyānuvādena bhavyeṣu caturdaśāpi santi. abhavyā ādya eva sthāne.
children.translated_text: § 41. By the thread of capacity for liberation (<s>bhavyānuvāda</s>): among the capable (<s>bhavya</s>), all fourteen [stages] exist. The incapable (<s>abhavya</s>) are in the first stage alone.

children.text: § 42. samyaktvānuvādena kṣāyikasamyaktve asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādīni ayogakevalyantāni santi. kṣāyopaśamikasamyaktve asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādīni apramattāntāni. aupaśamikasamyaktve asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādīni upaśāntakaṣāyāntāni. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭiḥ samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭir mithyādṛṣṭiś ca sve sve sthāne.
children.translated_text: § 42. By the thread of right faith (<s>samyaktvānuvāda</s>): in destructive right faith (<s>kṣāyikasamyaktva</s>), [stages] from <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>ayogakevalī</s> exist. In destructive-cum-subsidential right faith (<s>kṣāyopaśamikasamyaktva</s>), [stages] from <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>apramatta</s> exist. In subsidential right faith (<s>aupaśamikasamyaktva</s>), [stages] from <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>upaśāntakaṣāya</s> exist. The <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, and <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> are each in their own respective stage.

children.text: § 43. saṃjñānuvādena saṃjñiṣu dvādaśa guṇasthānāni kṣīṇakaṣāyāntāni. asaṃjñiṣu ekam eva mithyādṛṣṭisthānam. tadubhayavyapadeśarahitaḥ sayogakevalī ayogakevalī ca.
children.translated_text: § 43. By the thread of rationality (<s>saṃjñānuvāda</s>): among rational beings (<s>saṃjñin</s>), twelve <s>guṇasthānas</s> up to <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s> exist. Among non-rational beings (<s>asaṃjñin</s>), only the one <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> stage exists. Those beyond both designations are <s>sayogakevalī</s> and <s>ayogakevalī</s>.

children.text: § 44. āhārānuvādena āhārakeṣu mithyādṛṣṭyādīni kevalyantāni. anāhārakeṣu vigrahagatyāpanneṣu trīṇi guṇasthānāni mithyādṛṣṭiḥ sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭir asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭiś ca. samudghātagataḥ sayogakevalī ayogakevalī ca. siddhāḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ atītaguṇasthānāḥ. uktā satprarūpaṇā.
children.translated_text: § 44. By the thread of nutrition (<s>āhārānuvāda</s>): among those who take nourishment (<s>āhāraka</s>), [stages] from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>kevalī</s> exist. Among those without nourishment (<s>anāhāraka</s>): those in the state of transit between lives (<s>vigrahagatyāpanna</s>) have three <s>guṇasthānas</s>—<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>, <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, and <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>. Those who have entered the state of bodily emission (<s>samudghāta</s>) are <s>sayogakevalī</s> and <s>ayogakevalī</s>. The liberated souls (<s>siddha</s>), the supreme beings (<s>parameṣṭhin</s>), have transcended the <s>guṇasthānas</s>. Thus the existential analysis (<s>satprarūpaṇā</s>) has been stated.

children.text: § 45. saṃkhyāprarūpaṇocyate. sā dvividhā sāmānyena viśeṣeṇa ca. sāmānyena tāvad jīvā mithyādṛṣṭayo ’nantānantāḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭayo ’saṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ saṃyatāsaṃyatāś ca palyopmāsaṃkhyeyabhāgapramitāḥ. pramattasaṃyatāḥ koṭīpṛthaktvasaṃkhyāḥ. pṛthaktvam ity āgamasaṃjñā tisṝṇāṃ koṭīnāmam upari navānām adhaḥ.

apramattasaṃyatāḥ saṃkhyeyāḥ. catvāra upaśamakāḥ praveśena eko vā dvau vā trayo vā. utkarṣeṇa catuḥpañcāśat. svakālena samuditāḥ saṃkhyeyāḥ. catvāraḥ kṣapakā ayogakevalinaś ca praveśena eko vā dvau vā trayo vā. utkarṣeṇāṣṭottaraśatasaṃkhyāḥ. svakālena samuditāḥ saṃkhyeyāḥ. sayogakevalinaḥ praveśena eko vā dvau vā trayo vā. utkarṣeṇāṣṭottaraśatasaṃkhyāḥ. svakālena samuditāḥ śatasahasrapṛthaktvasaṃkhyāḥ.
children.translated_text: The <s>apramattasaṃyatas</s> are numerable (<s>saṃkhyeya</s>). The four subsiders, by entrance, are one, two, or three; at maximum, fifty-four; combined over their own time-period, they are numerable. The four destroyers and the <s>ayogakevalīs</s>, by entrance, are one, two, or three; at maximum, one hundred and eight; combined over their own time-period, they are numerable. The <s>sayogakevalīs</s>, by entrance, are one, two, or three; at maximum, one hundred and eight; combined over their own time-period, they are in the number of <s>pṛthaktva</s>-multiples of one hundred thousand.

§ 45. The numerical analysis (<s>saṃkhyāprarūpaṇā</s>) is now stated. It is twofold: general and specific. Generally: souls that are <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> (wrong believers) are infinitely infinite (<s>anantānanta</s>). The <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭis</s>, <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s>, <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭis</s>, and <s>saṃyatāsaṃyatas</s> are measured by an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> (ocean-measured time unit). The <s>pramattasaṃyatas</s> are in numbers of <s>koṭī</s>-multiples. '<s>Pṛthaktva</s>' is a scriptural term [referring to] above three <s>koṭīs</s> (tens of millions) and below nine.

children.text: § 46. viśeṣeṇa gatyanuvādena narakagatau prathamāyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ nārakā mithyādṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyāḥ śreṇayaḥ pratarāsaṃkhyeyabhāgapramitāḥ. dvitīyādiṣv ā saptamyā mithyādṛṣṭayaḥ śreṇyasaṃkhyeyabhāgapramitāḥ. sa cāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ asaṃkhyeyā yojanakoṭīkoṭyaḥ. sarvāsu pṛthivīṣu sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭayo ’samyatasamyagdṛṣṭayaś ca palyopmāsaṃkyeyabhḡapramitāḥ. tiryaggatau tiraścāṃ madhye mithyādṛṣṭayo ’nantānantāḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādayaḥ saṃyatāsamyatāntāḥ palyopamāsaṃkyeyabhāgapramitāḥ. manuṣyagatau manuṣyā mithyādṛṣṭayaḥ śreṇyasaṃkhyeyabhāgapramitāḥ. sa cāsamkhyeyabhāgaḥ asaṃkhyeyā yojanakoṭīkoṭyaḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādayaḥ saṃyatāsaṃyatāntāḥ saṃkhyeyāḥ. pramattādīnāṃ sāmānyoktā saṃkhyā. devagatau devā mithyādṛṣṭayo ’samkhyeyāḥ śreņayaḥ pratarāsaṃkhyeyabhāgapramitāḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgapramitāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 46. Specifically, by the thread of destiny (<s>gatyanuvāda</s>): in the hellish destiny, in the first earth [of hell], the hellish beings who are <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are innumerable, [measured as] rows innumerable-fraction-of-a-stratum in number. In the second through seventh [earths], the <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are innumerable-fraction-of-a-row in number. That innumerable fraction [equals] innumerable <s>koṭīkoṭī</s> (ten-million-times-ten-million) <s>yojanas</s>. In all the earths, the <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭis</s>, <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s>, and <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭis</s> are measured by an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>. In the animal destiny, among animals, <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are infinitely infinite. Those from <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s> are measured by an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>. In the human destiny, human <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are innumerable-fraction-of-a-row in number. That innumerable fraction [equals] innumerable <s>koṭīkoṭī yojanas</s>. Those from <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s> are numerable. For <s>pramattasaṃyatas</s> and above, the numbers are as stated generally. In the celestial destiny, celestial beings who are <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are innumerable, [measured as] rows innumerable-fraction-of-a-stratum in number. The <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭis</s>, <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s>, and <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭis</s> are measured by an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>.

children.text: § 47. indriyānuvādena ekendriyā mithyādṛṣṭayo ’nantānantāḥ. dvīndriyās trīndriyāś caturindriyā asaṃkhyeyāḥ śreṇayaḥ pratarāsaṃkhyeyabhāgamitāḥ.
pañcendriyeṣu mithyādṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyāḥ śreṇayaḥ pratarāsaṃkhyeyabhāgapramitāḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādayo ’yogakevalyantāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ.
children.translated_text: Among five-sensed beings, <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are innumerable, [measured as] rows innumerable-fraction-of-a-stratum in number. Those from <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>ayogakevalī</s> are in the numbers as stated generally.

§ 47. By the thread of sense-organs (<s>indriyānuvāda</s>): one-sensed <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are infinitely infinite. Two-sensed, three-sensed, and four-sensed beings are innumerable, [measured as] rows innumerable-fraction-of-a-stratum in number.

children.text: § 48. kāyānuvādena pṛthivīkāyikā apkāyikās tejaḥkāyikā vāyukāyikā asaṃkhyeyā lokāḥ. vanaspatikāyikāḥ anantānantāḥ. trasakāyikasaṃkhyā pañcendriyavat.
children.translated_text: § 48. By the thread of body-type (<s>kāyānuvāda</s>): earth-bodied (<s>pṛthivīkāyika</s>), water-bodied (<s>apkāyika</s>), fire-bodied (<s>tejaḥkāyika</s>), and air-bodied (<s>vāyukāyika</s>) beings are innumerable [in number of] worlds (<s>loka</s>). Plant-bodied beings (<s>vanaspatikāyika</s>) are infinitely infinite. The number of mobile beings (<s>trasakāyika</s>) is like that of five-sensed beings.

children.text: § 49. yogānuvādena manoyogino vāgyoginaś ca mithyādṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyāḥ śreṇayaḥ pratarāsaṃkhyeyabhāgapramitāḥ. kāyayogino mithyādṛṣṭayo ’nantānantāḥ. trayānām api yogināṃ sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādayaḥ saṃyatāsaṃyatāntāḥ palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgapramitāḥ. pramattasaṃyatādayaḥ sayogakevalyantāḥ saṃkhyeyāḥ. ayogakevalinaḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 49. By the thread of activity (<s>yogānuvāda</s>): mind-active (<s>manoyogin</s>) and speech-active (<s>vāgyogin</s>) <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are innumerable, [measured as] rows innumerable-fraction-of-a-stratum in number. Body-active (<s>kāyayogin</s>) <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are infinitely infinite. For all three types of active beings, those from <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s> are measured by an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>. Those from <s>pramattasaṃyata</s> up to <s>sayogakevalī</s> are numerable. <s>Ayogakevalīs</s> are in the numbers as stated generally.

children.text: § 50. vedānuvādena strīvedāḥ puṃvedāś ca mithyādṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyāḥ śreṇayaḥ pratarāsaṃkhyeyabhāgapramitāḥ. napuṃsakevedā mithyādṛṣṭayo ’nantānantāḥ. strīvedā napuṃsakavedāś ca sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādayaḥ saṃyatāsaṃyatāntāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. pramattasaṃyatādayo ’nivṛttibādarāntāḥ saṃkhyeyāḥ. puṃvedāḥ sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādayo nivṛttibādarāntāḥ sāmanyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. apagatavedā anivṛttibādarādayo ’yogakevalyantāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 50. By the thread of sex-determination (<s>vedānuvāda</s>): those with female sex-determination (<s>strīveda</s>) and male sex-determination (<s>puṃveda</s>) who are <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are innumerable, [measured as] rows innumerable-fraction-of-a-stratum in number. Those with neuter sex-determination (<s>napuṃsakaveda</s>) who are <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are infinitely infinite. Female and neuter [sex-determined souls] from <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s> are in the numbers as stated generally. Those from <s>pramattasaṃyata</s> up to <s>anivṛttibādara</s> are numerable. Male [sex-determined souls] from <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>anivṛttibādara</s> are in the numbers as stated generally. Those from whom sex-determination has departed, from <s>anivṛttibādara</s> up to <s>ayogakevalī</s>, are in the numbers as stated generally.

children.text: § 51. kaṣāyānuvādena krodhamānamāyāsu mithyādṛṣṭyādyaḥ saṃyatāsaṃyatāntāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. pramattasaṃyatādayo ’nivṛttibādarāntāḥ saṃkhyeyāḥ. lobhakaṣāyāṇāṃ ukta eva kramaḥ. ayaṃ tu viśeṣaḥ sūkṣmasāṃparāyasaṃyatāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. akaṣāyā upaśāntakaṣāyādayo ’yogakevalyantāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 51. By the thread of passions (<s>kaṣāyānuvāda</s>): in anger (<s>krodha</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), and deceit (<s>māyā</s>), those from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s> are in the numbers as stated generally. Those from <s>pramattasaṃyata</s> up to <s>anivṛttibādara</s> are numerable. For greed (<s>lobha</s>) passions, the order is the same as stated. But this is the distinction: the <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāyasaṃyatas</s> are in the numbers as stated generally. The passionless (<s>akaṣāya</s>), from <s>upaśāntakaṣāya</s> up to <s>ayogakevalī</s>, are in the numbers as stated generally.

children.text: § 52. jñānānuvādena matyajñāninaḥ śrutājñāninaś ca mithyādṛṣṭisāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. vibhaṅgajñānino mithyādṛṣṭayo ’saṃkyeyāḥ śreṇayaḥ pratarāsaṃkhyeyabhāgapramitāḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ palyopamāsaṃkheyabhāgapramitāḥ. matiśrutajñānino ’saṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādayaḥ kṣīṇakaṣāyāntāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. avadhijñānino ’saṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭisaṃyatāsaṃyatāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. pramattasaṃyatādayaḥ kṣīṇakaṣāyāntāḥ saṃkhyeyāḥ. manaḥparyayajñāninaḥ pramattasaṃyatādayaḥ kṣīṇakaṣāyāntāḥ saṃkhyeyāḥ. kevalajñāninaḥ sayogā ayogāś ca sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 52. By the thread of knowledge (<s>jñānānuvāda</s>): those with wrong sensory knowledge (<s>matyajñāna</s>) and wrong scriptural knowledge (<s>śrutājñāna</s>) who are <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> and <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> are in the numbers as stated generally. Those with clairvoyance (<s>vibhaṅgajñāna</s>) who are <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are innumerable, [measured as] rows innumerable-fraction-of-a-stratum in number. The <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭis</s> [with clairvoyance] are measured by an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>. Those with sensory and scriptural knowledge, from <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s>, are in the numbers as stated generally. Those with clairvoyant knowledge (<s>avadhijñāna</s>), the <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭis</s> and <s>saṃyatāsaṃyatas</s>, are in the numbers as stated generally. Those from <s>pramattasaṃyata</s> up to <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s> are numerable. Those with telepathic knowledge (<s>manaḥparyayajñāna</s>), from <s>pramattasaṃyata</s> up to <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s>, are numerable. The omniscient (<s>kevalajñāna</s>), both <s>sayoga</s> and <s>ayoga</s>, are in the numbers as stated generally.

children.text: § 53. saṃyamānuvādena sāmāyikacchedopasthāpanaśuddhisaṃyatāḥ pramattādayo ’nivṛttibādarāntāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. parihāraviśuddhisaṃyatāḥ pramattāś cāpramattāś ca saṃkhyeyāḥ. sūkṣmasāṃparāyaśuddhisaṃyatā yathākhyātavihāraśuddhisaṃyatāḥ saṃyatāsaṃyatā asaṃyatāś ca sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 53. By the thread of self-restraint (<s>saṃyamānuvāda</s>): those with <s>sāmāyika</s>, <s>chedopasthāpana</s>, and <s>śuddhi</s> self-restraint, from <s>pramatta</s> up to <s>anivṛttibādara</s>, are in the numbers as stated generally. Those with <s>parihāraviśuddhi</s> self-restraint, both <s>pramatta</s> and <s>apramatta</s>, are numerable. Those with <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāyaśuddhi</s> self-restraint, those with <s>yathākhyātavihāraśuddhi</s> self-restraint, the partially restrained (<s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>), and the unrestrained (<s>asaṃyata</s>) are in the numbers as stated generally.

children.text: § 54. darśanānuvādena cakṣurdarśanino mithyādṛṣṭayo ’saṃkheyāḥ śreṇayaḥ pratarāsaṃkheyabhāgapramitāḥ. acakṣurdarśanino mithyādṛṣṭayo ’nantānantāḥ. ubhaye ca sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādayaḥ kṣīṇakaṣāyāntāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. avadhidarśanino ’vadhijñānivat kevaladarśaninaḥ kevalajñānivat.
children.translated_text: § 54. By the thread of perception (<s>darśanānuvāda</s>): those with ocular perception (<s>cakṣurdarśana</s>) who are <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are innumerable, [measured as] rows innumerable-fraction-of-a-stratum in number. Those with non-ocular perception (<s>acakṣurdarśana</s>) who are <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are infinitely infinite. For both [types], those from <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s> are in the numbers as stated generally. Those with clairvoyant perception (<s>avadhidarśana</s>) are like those with clairvoyant knowledge. Those with omniscient perception (<s>kevaladarśana</s>) are like those with omniscient knowledge.

children.text: § 55. leśyānuvādena kṛṣṇalīlakāpotaleśyā mithyādṛṣṭyādayo ’saṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyantāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. tejaḥpadmaleśyā mithyādṛṣṭyādayaḥ saṃyatāsaṃyatāntāḥ strīvedavat. pramattāpramattasaṃyatāḥ saṃkhyeyāḥ. śuklaleśyā mithyādṛṣṭyādayaḥ saṃyatāsaṃyatāntāḥ palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgapramitāḥ. pramattāpramattasaṃyatāḥ saṃkyeyāḥ. apūrvakaraṇādayaḥ sayogakevalyantā aleśyāś ca sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 55. By the exposition according to <s>leśyā</s> (soul-coloring): those with <s>kṛṣṇa</s> (black), <s>nīla</s> (blue), and <s>kāpota</s> (grey) <s>leśyās</s>, from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong faith) up to <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> (unrestrained right believer), are of the generally stated number. Those with <s>tejas</s> (fiery) and <s>padma</s> (lotus) <s>leśyās</s>, from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s> (partially restrained), are like those with the feminine sex-passion (<s>strīveda</s>). The <s>pramatta</s> (negligent) and <s>apramatta-saṃyatas</s> (non-negligent restrained) are numerable. Those with <s>śukla</s> (white) <s>leśyā</s>, from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>, are measured by an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> (straw-simile time unit). The <s>pramatta</s> and <s>apramatta-saṃyatas</s> are numerable. Those from <s>apūrvakaraṇa</s> (unprecedented transformation) up to <s>sayoga-kevalin</s> (omniscient with activity), and those without <s>leśyā</s>, are of the generally stated number.

children.text: § 56. bhavyānuvādena bhavyeṣu mithyādṛṣṭyādayo ’yogakevalyantāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. abhavyā anantāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 56. By the exposition according to <s>bhavya</s> (capacity for liberation): among the <s>bhavyas</s>, from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>ayoga-kevalin</s> (omniscient without activity), they are of the generally stated number. The <s>abhavyas</s> (incapable of liberation) are infinite.

children.text: § 57. samyaktvānuvādena kṣāyikasamyagdṛṣṭiṣu asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ palyopa–māsaṃkheyabhāgapramitāḥ. saṃyatāsaṃyatādaya upaśāntakaṣāyāntāḥ saṃkheyāḥ. catvāraḥ kṣapakāḥ sayogakevalino ’yogakevalinaś ca sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. kṣāyopaśamikasamyagdṛṣṭiṣụ asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādayo ’pramattāntāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. aupaśamikasamyagdṛṣṭiṣu asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭisaṃyatāsaṃyatāḥ palyopmāsaṃkheyabhāgapramitāḥ. pramattāpramattasaṃyatāḥ saṃkheyāḥ. catvāra aupaśamikāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭayo mithyādṛṣṭayaś ca sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 57. By the exposition according to <s>samyaktva</s> (right faith): among those with <s>kṣāyika-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> (destructive right faith), the <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭis</s> are measured by an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>. From <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s> up to <s>upaśānta-kaṣāya</s> (quiescent passions), they are numerable. The four <s>kṣapakas</s> (destroyers of karma), the <s>sayoga-kevalins</s>, and the <s>ayoga-kevalins</s> are of the generally stated number. Among those with <s>kṣāyopaśamika-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> (destructive-subsidence right faith), from <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>apramatta</s> (non-negligent), they are of the generally stated number. Among those with <s>aupaśamika-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> (subsidence right faith), the <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s> are measured by an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>. The <s>pramatta</s> and <s>apramatta-saṃyatas</s> are numerable. The four <s>aupaśamikas</s> are of the generally stated number. The <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s> (those in the falling stage of right faith), <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s> (mixed faith), and <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> (wrong faith) are of the generally stated number.

children.text: § 58. saṃjñānuvādena saṃjñiṣu mithyādṛṣṭyādayaḥ kṣīṇakaṣāyāntāś cakṣurdarśanivat. asaṃjñino mithyādṛṣṭayo ’nantānantāḥ. tadubhayavyapadeśarahitāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 58. By the exposition according to <s>saṃjñā</s> (rationality): among the <s>saṃjñins</s> (rational beings), from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>kṣīṇa-kaṣāya</s> (destroyed passions), they are like those with visual perception (<s>cakṣurdarśana</s>). The <s>asaṃjñins</s> (non-rational beings) with wrong faith are infinitely infinite. Those devoid of the designation of either [rational or non-rational] are of the generally stated number.

children.text: § 59. āhārānuvādena āhārakeṣu mithyādṛṣṭyādayaḥ sayogakevalyantāḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. anāhārakeṣu mithyādṛṣṭisāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. sayogakevalinaḥ saṃkhyeyāḥ. ayogakevalinaḥ sāmānyoktasaṃkhyāḥ. saṃkhyā nirṇītā.
children.translated_text: § 59.
