By the exposition according to <s>āhāra</s> (nourishment): among the <s>āhārakas</s> (those who take nourishment), from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>sayoga-kevalin</s>, they are of the generally stated number. Among the <s>anāhārakas</s> (those without nourishment), <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s>, <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s>, and <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭis</s> are of the generally stated number. The <s>sayoga-kevalins</s> are numerable. The <s>ayoga-kevalins</s> are of the generally stated number. The determination of number is [thus] completed.

children.text: § 60. kṣetram ucyate. tad dvividhaṃ sāmānyena viśeṣeṇa ca. sāmānyena tāvad — mithyādṛṣṭīnāṃ sarvalokaḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādīnām ayogakevalyantānāṃ lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. sayogakevalināṃ lokasyāsaṃkyeyabhāgo ’saṃkyeyā bhāgāḥ sarvaloko vā.
children.translated_text: § 60. The spatial extent (<s>kṣetra</s>) is now stated. It is twofold: general and specific. Generally: for <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s>, [the spatial extent is] the entire universe (<s>sarvaloka</s>). For those from <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>ayoga-kevalin</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe. For <s>sayoga-kevalins</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe, or innumerable fractions [of the universe], or the entire universe.

children.text: § 61. viśeṣeṇa gatyanuvādena narakagatau sarvāsu pṛthivīṣu nārakāṇāṃ caturṣu guṇasthāneṣu lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. tiryaggatau tiraścāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādisaṃyatāsamyatāntānāṃ sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram. manuṣyagatau manuṣyāṇāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādyayogakevalyantānāṃ lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. sayogakevalināṃ sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram devagatau devānāṃ sarveṣāṃ caturṣu guṇasthāneṣu lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 61. Specifically, by the exposition according to <s>gati</s> (destiny): in the hellish destiny (<s>narakagati</s>), for <s>nārakas</s> (hellish beings) in all the earths, in the four <s>guṇasthānas</s> (spiritual stages), an innumerable fraction of the universe. In the animal destiny (<s>tiryaggati</s>), for animals from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>, the generally stated spatial extent. In the human destiny (<s>manuṣyagati</s>), for humans from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>ayoga-kevalin</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe. For <s>sayoga-kevalins</s>, the generally stated spatial extent. In the celestial destiny (<s>devagati</s>), for all celestial beings in the four <s>guṇasthānas</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe.

children.text: § 62. indriyānuvādena ekendriyāṇāṃ kṣetraṃ sarvalokaḥ. vikalendriyāṇāṃ lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. pañcendriyāṇāṃ manuṣyavat.
children.translated_text: § 62. By the exposition according to <s>indriya</s> (sense organs): for one-sensed beings, the spatial extent is the entire universe. For those with incomplete senses (<s>vikalendriya</s>), an innumerable fraction of the universe. For five-sensed beings, as for humans.

children.text: § 63. kāyānuvādena pṛthivīkāyādivanaspatikāyāntānāṃ sarvalokaḥ. trasakāyikānāṃ pañcendriyavat.
children.translated_text: § 63. By the exposition according to <s>kāya</s> (body-type): for those from the earth-body type up to the plant-body type, the entire universe. For mobile beings (<s>trasakāyika</s>), as for five-sensed beings.

children.text: § 64. yogānuvādena vāṅmanasayogināṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādisayogakevalyantānāṃ lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. kāyayoginām mithyādṛṣṭyādisayogakevalyantānām ayogakevalināṃ ca sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram.
children.translated_text: § 64. By the exposition according to <s>yoga</s> (activity): for those with speech-activity and mind-activity, from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>sayoga-kevalin</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe. For those with body-activity, from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>sayoga-kevalin</s> and <s>ayoga-kevalins</s>, the generally stated spatial extent.

children.text: § 65. vedānuvādena strīpuṃvedānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādyanivṛttibādarāntānāṃ lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. napuṃsakavedānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādyanivṛttibādarāntānām apagatavedānāṃ ca sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram.
children.translated_text: § 65. By the exposition according to <s>veda</s> (sex-passion): for those with feminine and masculine sex-passions, from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>anivṛtti-bādara</s> (gross non-retrogression), an innumerable fraction of the universe. For those with neuter sex-passion, from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>anivṛtti-bādara</s>, and for those free from sex-passion, the generally stated spatial extent.

children.text: § 66. kaṣāyānuvādena krodhamānamāyākaṣāyāṇāṃ lobhakaṣāyāṇāṃ ca mithyādṛṣṭyādyanivṛttibādarāntānāṃ sūkṣmasāṃparāyāṇām akaṣāyāṇāṃ ca sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram.
children.translated_text: § 66. By the exposition according to <s>kaṣāya</s> (passion): for those with the passions of anger (<s>krodha</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), deceit (<s>māyā</s>), and greed (<s>lobha</s>), from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>anivṛtti-bādara</s>, and for the <s>sūkṣma-sāṃparāyas</s> (subtle-passion souls) and those free from passions, the generally stated spatial extent.

children.text: § 67. jñānānuvādena matyajñāniśrutājñānināṃ mithyādṛṣṭisāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭīnāṃ sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram. vibhaṅgajñānināṃ mithyādṛṣṭisāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭīnāṃ lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. ābhinibodhikaśrutāvadhijñāninām asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādīnāṃ kṣīṇakaṣāyāntānāṃ manaḥparyayajñānināṃ ca pramattādīnāṃ kṣīṇakaṣāyāntānāṃ kevalajñānināṃ sayogānām ayogānāṃ ca sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram.
children.translated_text: § 67. By the exposition according to <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge): for those with wrong sensory knowledge (<s>matyajñāna</s>) and wrong scriptural knowledge (<s>śrutājñāna</s>), who are <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> and <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s>, the generally stated spatial extent. For those with <s>vibhaṅga-jñāna</s> (clairvoyance of wrong believers), who are <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> and <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe. For those with <s>ābhinibodhika</s> (sensory), <s>śruta</s> (scriptural), and <s>avadhi</s> (clairvoyant) knowledge, from <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>kṣīṇa-kaṣāya</s>, and for those with <s>manaḥparyaya-jñāna</s> (mind-reading knowledge), from <s>pramatta</s> up to <s>kṣīṇa-kaṣāya</s>, and for <s>kevala-jñānins</s> (omniscients)—both <s>sayoga</s> (with activity) and <s>ayoga</s> (without activity)—the generally stated spatial extent.

children.text: § 68. saṃyamānuvādena sāmāyikacchedopasthāpanāśuddhisaṃyatānāṃ caturṇāṃ parihāraviśuddhisaṃyatānāṃ pramattāpramattānāṃ sụkṣmasāṃparāyaśuddhisaṃyatānāṃ yathākhyātavihāraśuddhisaṃyatānāṃ caturṇāṃ saṃyatāsaṃyatānām asaṃyatānāṃ ca caturṇāṃ sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram.
children.translated_text: § 68. By the exposition according to <s>saṃyama</s> (restraint): for those with <s>sāmāyika</s> (equanimity), <s>chedopasthāpanā</s> (re-initiation), and <s>śuddhi-saṃyata</s> (pure restraint) of the four [types], for those with <s>parihāra-viśuddhi-saṃyata</s> (special-purity restraint) who are <s>pramatta</s> and <s>apramatta</s>, for the <s>sūkṣma-sāṃparāya</s> and <s>śuddhi-saṃyatas</s>, for the four [types of] <s>yathākhyāta-vihāra-śuddhi-saṃyatas</s> (ideal-conduct pure restraint), for the <s>saṃyatāsaṃyatas</s> (partially restrained), and for the four [types of] <s>asaṃyatas</s> (unrestrained)—the generally stated spatial extent.

children.text: § 69. darśanānuvādena cakṣurdarśanināṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādikṣīṇakaṣāyāntānāṃ lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. acakṣurdarśanināṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādikṣīṇakaṣāyāntānāṃ sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram. avadhidarśaninām avadhijñānivat. kevaladarśanināṃ kevalajñānivat.
children.translated_text: § 69. By the exposition according to <s>darśana</s> (perception/faith): for those with visual perception (<s>cakṣur-darśana</s>), from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>kṣīṇa-kaṣāya</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe. For those with non-visual perception (<s>acakṣur-darśana</s>), from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>kṣīṇa-kaṣāya</s>, the generally stated spatial extent. For those with <s>avadhi-darśana</s> (clairvoyant perception), as for those with <s>avadhi-jñāna</s> (clairvoyant knowledge). For those with <s>kevala-darśana</s> (omniscient perception), as for those with <s>kevala-jñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge).

children.text: § 70. leśyānuvādena kṛṣṇanīlakāpotaleśyānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyantānāṃ sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram. tejaḥpadmaleśyānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādyapramattāntānāṃ lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. śuklaleśyānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādikṣīṇakaṣāyāntānāṃ lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. sayogakevalinām aleśyānāṃ ca sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram.
children.translated_text: § 70. By the exposition according to <s>leśyā</s> (soul-coloring): for those with <s>kṛṣṇa</s> (black), <s>nīla</s> (blue), and <s>kāpota</s> (grey) <s>leśyās</s>, from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭi</s>, the generally stated spatial extent. For those with <s>tejas</s> (fiery) and <s>padma</s> (lotus) <s>leśyās</s>, from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>apramatta</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe. For those with <s>śukla</s> (white) <s>leśyā</s>, from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>kṣīṇa-kaṣāya</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe. For <s>sayoga-kevalins</s> and those without <s>leśyā</s>, the generally stated spatial extent.

children.text: § 71. bhavyānuvādena bhavyānāṃ caturdaśānāṃ sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram. abhavyānāṃ sarvalokaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 71. By the exposition according to <s>bhavya</s> (capacity for liberation): for <s>bhavyas</s> in the fourteen [<s>guṇasthānas</s>], the generally stated spatial extent. For <s>abhavyas</s>, the entire universe.

children.text: § 72. samyaktvānuvādena kṣāyikasamyagdṛṣṭīnām asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādyayogakevalyantānāṃ kṣāyopaśamikasamyagdṛṣṭīnām asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādyapramattāntānām aupaśamikasamyagdṛṣṭīnām asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādyupaśāntakaṣāyāntānāṃ sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭīnāṃ samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭīnāṃ mithyādṛṣṭīnāṃ ca sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram.
children.translated_text: § 72. By the exposition according to <s>samyaktva</s> (right faith): for those with <s>kṣāyika-samyagdṛṣṭi</s>, from <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>ayoga-kevalin</s>; for those with <s>kṣāyopaśamika-samyagdṛṣṭi</s>, from <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>apramatta</s>; for those with <s>aupaśamika-samyagdṛṣṭi</s>, from <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>upaśānta-kaṣāya</s>; for <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s>, <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s>, and <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s>—the generally stated spatial extent.

children.text: § 73. saṃjñānuvādena saṃjñināṃ caksurdarśanivat. asaṃjñināṃ sarvalokaḥ. tadubhayavyapadeśarahitānāṃ sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram.
children.translated_text: § 73. By the exposition according to <s>saṃjñā</s> (rationality): for <s>saṃjñins</s> (rational beings), as for those with visual perception. For <s>asaṃjñins</s> (non-rational beings), the entire universe. For those devoid of the designation of either, the generally stated spatial extent.

children.text: § 74. āhārānuvādena āhārakāṇāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādikṣīṇakaṣāyāntānāṃ sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetram. sayogakevalināṃ lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. anāhārakāṇāṃ mithyādṛṣṭisāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyayogakevalināṃ sāmānyoktaṃ kṣetraṃ. sayogakevalināṃ lokasyāsaṃkheyā bhāgāḥ sarvaloko vā. kṣetranirṇayaḥ kṛtaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 74. By the exposition according to <s>āhāra</s> (nourishment): for <s>āhārakas</s>, from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>kṣīṇa-kaṣāya</s>, the generally stated spatial extent. For <s>sayoga-kevalins</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe. For <s>anāhārakas</s>—<s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s>, <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s>, <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭis</s>, and <s>ayoga-kevalins</s>—the generally stated spatial extent. For <s>sayoga-kevalins</s>, innumerable fractions of the universe, or the entire universe. The determination of spatial extent is [thus] completed.

children.text: § 75. sparśanam ucyate. tad dvividhaṃ sāmānyena viśeṣeṇa ca. sāmānyena tāvan mithyādṛṣṭibhiḥ sarvalokaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ aṣṭau dvādaśa caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ aṣṭau caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. saṃyatāsaṃyatair lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ ṣaṭ caturdaśabhāgā vā desonāḥ. pramattasaṃyatādīnām ayogakevalyantānāṃ kṣetravatsparśanam.
children.translated_text: § 75. The range of contact (<s>sparśana</s>) is now stated. It is twofold: general and specific. Generally: <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> have contacted the entire universe. <s>Sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s> [have contacted] an innumerable fraction of the universe—eight, twelve, or fourteen parts, less a fraction. <s>Samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s> and <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭis</s> [have contacted] an innumerable fraction of the universe—eight or fourteen parts, less a fraction. <s>Saṃyatāsaṃyatas</s> [have contacted] an innumerable fraction of the universe—six or fourteen parts, less a fraction. For those from <s>pramatta-saṃyata</s> up to <s>ayoga-kevalin</s>, the range of contact is like the spatial extent.

children.text: § 76. viśeṣeṇa gatyanuvādena narakagatau prathamāyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ nārakaiś caturguṇasthānair lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ. dvitīyādiṣu prāksaptamyā mithyādṛṣṭisāsādanasamyagdṛṣtibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgāḥ eko dvau trayaḥ catvāraḥ pañca caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. saptamyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ mithyādṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkyeyabhāgaḥ ṣaṭ caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. śeṣais tribhir lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. tiryaggatau tiraścāṃ mithyādṛṣṭibhiḥ sarvalokaḥ spṛṣtaḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ sapta caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭisaṃyatāsaṃyatair lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ ṣaṭ caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. manuṣyagatau manuṣyair mithyādṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ sarvaloko vā spṛṣṭaḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣtibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ sapta caturdaśabhāgā vā desonāḥ. samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyādīnām ayogakevalyantānāṃ kṣetravatsparśanam. devagatau devair mithyādṛṣṭisāsādanasamyagdṛṣtibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ aṣṭau nava caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ aṣṭau caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 76. Specifically, by the exposition according to <s>gati</s> (destiny): in the hellish destiny, <s>nārakas</s> in the first earth, in the four <s>guṇasthānas</s>, have contacted an innumerable fraction of the universe. In the second through the sixth earths, <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> and <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s> have contacted innumerable fractions of the universe—one, two, three, four, or five of the fourteen parts, less a fraction. <s>Samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s> and <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭis</s> have contacted an innumerable fraction of the universe. In the seventh earth, <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> have contacted an innumerable fraction of the universe—six or fourteen parts, less a fraction. The remaining three [<s>guṇasthānas</s> there have contacted] an innumerable fraction of the universe. In the animal destiny, <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> animals have contacted the entire universe. <s>Sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s> have contacted an innumerable fraction of the universe—seven or fourteen parts, less a fraction. <s>Samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s> have contacted an innumerable fraction of the universe. <s>Asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭis</s> and <s>saṃyatāsaṃyatas</s> have contacted an innumerable fraction of the universe—six or fourteen parts, less a fraction. In the human destiny, <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> humans have contacted an innumerable fraction of the universe, or the entire universe. <s>Sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s> have contacted an innumerable fraction of the universe—seven or fourteen parts, less a fraction. For <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s> and higher up to <s>ayoga-kevalin</s>, the range of contact is like the spatial extent. In the celestial destiny, <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> and <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> celestials have contacted an innumerable fraction of the universe—eight, nine, or fourteen parts, less a fraction. <s>Samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s> and <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭis</s> have contacted an innumerable fraction of the universe—eight or fourteen parts, less a fraction.

children.text: § 77. indriyānuvādena ekendriyaiḥ sarvalokaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ. vikalendriyair lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ sarvaloko vā. pañcendriyeṣu mithyādṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ aṣṭau caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ sarvaloko vā. śeṣāṇāṃ sāmānyoktaṃ sparśanam.
children.translated_text: § 77. By the exposition according to <s>indriya</s> (sense organs): one-sensed beings have contacted the entire universe. Those with incomplete senses have contacted an innumerable fraction of the universe, or the entire universe. Among five-sensed beings, <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> have contacted an innumerable fraction of the universe—eight or fourteen parts, less a fraction—or the entire universe. For the rest, the generally stated range of contact [applies].

children.text: § 78. kāyānuvādena sthāvarakāyikaiḥ sarvalokaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ. trasakāyināṃ pañcendriyavat sparśanam.
children.translated_text: § 78. By the exposition according to <s>kāya</s> (body-type): immobile beings (<s>sthāvara-kāyikas</s>) have contacted the entire universe. For mobile beings (<s>trasakāyins</s>), the range of contact is as for five-sensed beings.

children.text: § 79. yogānuvādena vāṅmanasayogināṃ mithyādṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ aṣṭau caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ sarvaloko vā. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādīnāṃ kṣīṇakaṣāyāntānāṃ sāmānyoktaṃ sparśanam. sayogakevalināṃ lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. kāyayogināṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādīnāṃ sayogakevalyantānām ayogakevalināṃ ca sāmānyoktaṃ sparśanam.
children.translated_text: § 79. By the exposition according to <s>yoga</s> (activity): for those with speech-activity and mind-activity who are <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe—eight or fourteen parts, less a fraction—or the entire universe. For those from <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>kṣīṇa-kaṣāya</s>, the generally stated range of contact. For <s>sayoga-kevalins</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe. For those with body-activity, from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>sayoga-kevalin</s> and <s>ayoga-kevalins</s>, the generally stated range of contact.

children.text: § 80. vedānuvādena strīpuṃvedair mithyādṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ aṣṭau caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ sarvaloko vā. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭibhiḥ lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ aṣṭau nava caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyādyanivṛttibādarāntānāṃ sāmānyoktaṃ sparśanam. napuṃsakavedeṣu mithyādṛṣṭīnāṃ sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭīnāṃ ca sāmānyoktaṃ sparśanam. samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭisamyatāsaṃyatair lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ ṣaṭ caturdaśabhāgā vā deṡonāḥ. pramattādyanivṛttibādarāntānām apagatavedānāṃ ca sāmānyoktaṃ sparśanam.
children.translated_text: § 80. By the exposition according to <s>veda</s> (sex-passion): <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> with feminine and masculine sex-passions have contacted an innumerable fraction of the universe—eight or fourteen parts, less a fraction—or the entire universe. <s>Sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s> have contacted an innumerable fraction of the universe—eight, nine, or fourteen parts, less a fraction. For <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s> and higher up to <s>anivṛtti-bādara</s>, the generally stated range of contact. Among those with neuter sex-passion, for <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> and <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s>, the generally stated range of contact. For <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe. For <s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭis</s> and <s>saṃyatāsaṃyatas</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe—six or fourteen parts, less a fraction. For those from <s>pramatta</s> up to <s>anivṛtti-bādara</s>, and for those free from sex-passion, the generally stated range of contact.

children.text: § 81. kaṣāyānuvādena catuṣkaṣāyāṇām akaṣāyāṇāṃ ca sāmānyoktaṃ sparśanam.
children.translated_text: § 81. By the exposition according to <s>kaṣāya</s> (passion): for those with the four passions and for those free from passions, the generally stated range of contact.

children.text: § 82. jñānānuvādena matyajñāniśrutājñāninaṃ mithyādṛṣṭisāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭīnāṃ sāmānyoktaṃ sparśanam. vibhaṅgajñānināṃ mithyādṛṣṭīnāṃ lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ aṣṭau caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ sarvaloko vā. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭīnāṃ sāmānyoktaṃ sparśanam. ābhinibodhikaśrutāvadhimanaḥparyayakevalajñānināṃ sāmānyoktaṃ sparśanam.
children.translated_text: § 82. By the exposition according to <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge): for those with wrong sensory knowledge and wrong scriptural knowledge who are <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> and <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s>, the generally stated range of contact. For those with <s>vibhaṅga-jñāna</s> who are <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s>, an innumerable fraction of the universe—eight or fourteen parts, less a fraction—or the entire universe. For <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s>, the generally stated range of contact. For those with <s>ābhinibodhika</s>, <s>śruta</s>, <s>avadhi</s>, <s>manaḥparyaya</s>, and <s>kevala</s> knowledge, the generally stated range of contact.

children.text: § 83. saṃyamānuvādena saṃyatānāṃ sarveṣāṃ saṃyatāsaṃyatānām asaṃyatānāṃ ca sāmānyoktaṃ sparśanam.
children.translated_text: § 83. By the classification of self-restraint (<s>saṃyama</s>), the <s>sparśana</s> (spatial contact) as stated generally [applies] to all the restrained (<s>saṃyata</s>), the partially restrained (<s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>), and the unrestrained (<s>asaṃyata</s>).

children.text: § 84. darśanānuvādena cakṣurdarśanināṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādikṣīṇakaṣāyāntānāṃ pañcendriyavat. acakṣurdarśanināṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādikṣīṇakaṣāyāntānām adhikevaladarśanināṃ ca sāmānyoktaṃ sparśanam.
children.translated_text: § 84. By the classification of perception (<s>darśana</s>), for those possessing ocular perception (<s>cakṣurdarśana</s>), from those with wrong faith (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) to those with destroyed passions (<s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s>) — as for the five-sensed beings. For those possessing non-ocular perception, from those with wrong faith to those with destroyed passions, and for those possessing absolute perception (<s>kevaladarśana</s>) in addition — the <s>sparśana</s> is as stated generally.

children.text: § 85. leśyānuvādena kṛṣṇanīlakāpotaleśyair mithyādṛṣṭibhiḥ sarvalokaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ pañca catvāro dvau caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. tejoleśyair mithyādṛṣṭisāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ aṣṭau nava caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasaṃyagdṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ aṣṭau caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. saṃyatāsaṃyatair lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ adhyardha caturdaśa bhāgā vā deśonāḥ. pramattāpramattair lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. padmaleśyair mithyādṛṣṭyādyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyantair lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ aṣṭau caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. saṃyatāsaṃyatair lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ pañca caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. pramattāpramattair lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. śuklaleśyair mithyādṛṣṭyādisaṃyatāsamyatāntair lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ ṣaṭ caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. pramattādisayogakevalyantānām aleśyānāṃ ca sāmānyoktaṃ sparśanam.
children.translated_text: § 85. By the classification of <s>leśyā</s> (soul-coloration): by those with black (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>), blue (<s>nīla</s>), and grey (<s>kāpota</s>) <s>leśyās</s> who have wrong faith — the entire <s>loka</s> (cosmos) is touched. By those with right faith preceded by subsidence (<s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos, less than five, four, two, or fourteen parts respectively. By those with mixed right-and-wrong faith (<s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>) and unrestrained right faith (<s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos. By those with fiery (<s>tejo</s>) <s>leśyā</s> who have wrong faith and subsidence-right-faith — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos, less than eight, nine, or fourteen parts respectively. By those with mixed right-and-wrong faith and unrestrained right faith — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos, less than eight or fourteen parts. By the partially restrained — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos, less than one and a half or fourteen parts. By the vigilant and non-vigilant restraint — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos. By those with lotus (<s>padma</s>) <s>leśyā</s>, from wrong faith to unrestrained right faith — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos, less than eight or fourteen parts. By the partially restrained — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos, less than five or fourteen parts. By the vigilant and non-vigilant restraint — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos. By those with white (<s>śukla</s>) <s>leśyā</s>, from wrong faith to the partially restrained — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos, less than six or fourteen parts. For those from the vigilant to the omniscient-with-activity (<s>sayoga-kevalin</s>), and for those without <s>leśyā</s> — the <s>sparśana</s> is as stated generally.

children.text: § 86. bhavyānuvādena bhavyānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādyayogakevalyantānāṃ sāmānyoktaṃ sparśanam. abhavyaiḥ sarvalokaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 86. By the classification of capacity for liberation (<s>bhavya</s>): for the <s>bhavyas</s> (capable of liberation), from wrong faith to the motionless omniscient (<s>ayoga-kevalin</s>) — the <s>sparśana</s> is as stated generally. By the <s>abhavyas</s> (incapable of liberation) — the entire cosmos is touched.

children.text: § 87. samyaktvānuvādena kṣāyikasamyagdṛṣṭīnām asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādyayogakevalyantānāṃ sāmānyoktam. kiṃtu saṃyatāsaṃyatānāṃ lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. kṣāyopaśamikasamyagdṛṣṭīnāṃ sāmānyoktam. aupaśamikasamyaktvānām asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭīnāṃ sāmānyoktam. śeṣāṇāṃ lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyagmithyādṛṣṭimithyādṛṣṭīnāṃ sāmānyoktam.
children.translated_text: § 87. By the classification of right faith (<s>samyaktva</s>): for those with destructional right faith (<s>kṣāyika-samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), from unrestrained right faith to the motionless omniscient — as stated generally. However, for the partially restrained — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos. For those with destructional-subsidential right faith (<s>kṣāyopaśamika</s>) — as stated generally. For those with subsidential right faith (<s>aupaśamika</s>) who have unrestrained right faith — as stated generally. For the rest — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos. For those with subsidence-right-faith, mixed right-and-wrong faith, and wrong faith — as stated generally.

children.text: § 88. saṃjñānuvādena saṃjñināṃ caksurdarśanivat. asaṃjñibhiḥ sarvalokaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ. tadubhayavyapadeśarahitānāṃ sāmānyoktam.
children.translated_text: § 88. By the classification of rationality (<s>saṃjñā</s>): for the rational (<s>saṃjñin</s>) — as for those with ocular perception. By the irrational (<s>asaṃjñin</s>) — the entire cosmos is touched. For those without either designation — as stated generally.

children.text: § 89. āhārānuvādena āhārakāṇāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādikṣīṇakaṣāyāntānāṃ sāmānyoktam. sayogakevalināṃ lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. anāhārakeṣu mithyādṛṣṭibhiḥ sarvalokaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭibhir lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ ekādaśa caturdaśabhāgā vā deśonāḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭibhiḥ lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ ṣaṭ caturdaśa bhāgā vā deśonāḥ. sayogakevalināṃ lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgāḥ sarvaloko vā. ayogakevalināṃ lokasyāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. sparśanaṃ vyākhyātam.
children.translated_text: § 89. By the classification of nourishment (<s>āhāra</s>): for those who take nourishment, from wrong faith to destroyed passions — as stated generally. For the omniscient-with-activity — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos. Among non-nourishing beings: by those with wrong faith — the entire cosmos is touched. By those with subsidence-right-faith — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos, less than eleven or fourteen parts. By those with unrestrained right faith — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos, less than six or fourteen parts. For the omniscient-with-activity — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos, or the entire cosmos. For the motionless omniscient — an innumerable fraction of the cosmos. The [topic of] <s>sparśana</s> (spatial contact) has been explained.

children.text: § 90. kālaḥ prastūyate. sa dvividhaḥ — sāmānyena viśeṣeṇa ca. sāmānyena tāvad mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvāpekṣayā trayo bhaṅgāḥ. anādir aparyavasānaḥ anādiḥ saparyavasānaḥ sādiḥ saparyavasānaś ceti. tatra sādiḥ saparyavasāno jaghanyenāntarmuhūrttaḥ. utkarṣeṇārdhapudgalaparivartto deśonaḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa palyopamāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa ṣaḍāvalikāḥ. samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenāntarmuhūrttaḥ. utkarṣeṇa palyopamāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyaḥ utkṛṣṭaś cāntarmuhūrttaḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdrṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrttaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi sātirekāṇi. saṃyatāsaṃyatasya nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrttaḥ. utkarṣeṇa pūrvakoṭī deśonā. pramattāpramattayor nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇāntarmuhūrttaḥ. caturṇām upaśamakānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā ekajīvāpeksayā ca jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇāntarmuhūrttaḥ. caturṇāṃ kṣapakāṇām ayogakevalināṃ ca nānājīvāpekṣayā ekajīvāpekṣayā ca jaghanyaś cotkṛṣṭaś cāntarmuhūrttaḥ. sayogakevalināṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa pūrvakoṭī deśonā.
children.translated_text: § 90. <s>Kāla</s> (time-duration) is now discussed. It is twofold — general and specific. Generally: for one with wrong faith (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), with reference to many souls — all time. With reference to a single soul — three possibilities: beginningless and endless; beginningless but with an end; with a beginning and with an end. Among these, the one with a beginning and end is at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s> (fraction of 48 minutes); at maximum, a half <s>pudgala-parivarta</s> (matter-cycle) less a fraction. For one with subsidence-right-faith (<s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), with reference to many souls — at minimum one <s>samaya</s> (time-instant); at maximum, an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>. For a single soul — at minimum one <s>samaya</s>; at maximum, six <s>āvalikās</s>. For one with mixed right-and-wrong faith, with reference to many souls — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>. For a single soul — both minimum and maximum are an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>. For one with unrestrained right faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> (ocean-measured periods) and more. For the partially restrained, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, a <s>pūrvakoṭi</s> less a fraction. For the vigilant and non-vigilant, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum one <s>samaya</s>; at maximum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>. For the four subsiders (<s>upaśamaka</s>), with reference to many souls and a single soul — at minimum one <s>samaya</s>; at maximum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>. For the four destroyers (<s>kṣapaka</s>) and the motionless omniscient, with reference to many souls and a single soul — both minimum and maximum are an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>. For the omniscient-with-activity, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, a <s>pūrvakoṭi</s> less a fraction.

children.text: § 91. viśeṣeṇa gatyanuvādena narakagatau nārakeṣu saptasu pṛthivīṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa yathāsaṃkhyaṃ eka-tri-sapta-daśa-saptadaśa-dvāviṃśati-trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭeḥ samyagmithyādṛṣṭeś ca sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa ukta evotkṛṣṭo deśonaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 91. Specifically, by the classification of destiny (<s>gati</s>): in the hellish destiny, for hell-beings (<s>nāraka</s>) in the seven hells, for one with wrong faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, respectively one, three, seven, ten, seventeen, twenty-two, and thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s>. For one with subsidence-right-faith and mixed right-and-wrong faith — the time is as stated generally. For one with unrestrained right faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, the stated maximum less a fraction.

children.text: § 92. tiryaggatau tiraścāṃ mithyādṛṣṭīnāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇānantaḥ kālo ’saṃkhyeyāḥ pudgalaparivartāḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyagmithyādṛṣṭisaṃyatāsaṃyatānāṃ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trīṇi palyopamāni.
children.translated_text: § 92. In the animal destiny (<s>tiryaggati</s>): for animals with wrong faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, infinite time — innumerable <s>pudgala-parivarttas</s> (matter-cycles). For those with subsidence-right-faith, mixed right-and-wrong faith, and the partially restrained — the time is as stated generally. For one with unrestrained right faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, three <s>palyopamas</s>.

children.text: § 93. manuṣyagatau manuṣyeṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarseṇa trīṇi palyopamāni pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvair abhyadhikāni. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇāntarmuhūrtaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa ṣaḍāvalikāḥ. samyagmithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā ekajīvāpekṣayā ca jaghanyaś cotkṛṣṭaś cāntarmuhūrtaḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trīṇi palyopamāni sātirekāṇi. śeṣāṇāṃ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 93. In the human destiny (<s>manuṣyagati</s>): for humans with wrong faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, three <s>palyopamas</s> exceeded by several <s>pūrvakoṭi</s> units. For one with subsidence-right-faith, with reference to many souls — at minimum one <s>samaya</s>; at maximum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>. For a single soul — at minimum one <s>samaya</s>; at maximum six <s>āvalikās</s>. For one with mixed right-and-wrong faith, with reference to many souls and a single soul — both minimum and maximum are an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>. For one with unrestrained right faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, three <s>palyopamas</s> and more. For the rest — the time is as stated generally.

children.text: § 94. devagatau deveṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarseṇaikatriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭeḥ samyagmithyādṛṣṭeś ca sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarseṇa trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāni.
children.translated_text: § 94. In the divine destiny (<s>devagati</s>): for gods with wrong faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, thirty-one <s>sāgaropamas</s>. For those with subsidence-right-faith and mixed right-and-wrong faith — the time is as stated generally. For one with unrestrained right faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s>.

children.text: § 95. indriyānuvādena ekendriyāṇāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena kṣudrabhavagrahaṇaṃ. utkarṣeṇānantaḥ kālo ’saṃkheyāḥ pudgalaparivartāḥ. vikalendriyāṇāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena kṣudrabhavagrahaṇam. utkarṣeṇa saṃkheyāni varṣasahasrāṇi. pañcendriyeṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa sāgaropamasahasraṃ pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvair abhyadhikam. śeṣāṇāṃ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 95. By the classification of sense organs (<s>indriya</s>): for one-sensed beings, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum, the duration of a minor existence (<s>kṣudra-bhava</s>); at maximum, infinite time — innumerable <s>pudgala-parivarttas</s>. For beings with incomplete sense organs (<s>vikalendriya</s>), with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum, the duration of a minor existence; at maximum, numerable thousands of years. Among five-sensed beings, for one with wrong faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, a thousand <s>sāgaropamas</s> exceeded by several <s>pūrvakoṭi</s> units. For the rest — the time is as stated generally.

children.text: § 96. kāyānuvādena pṛthivyaptejovāyukāyikānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena kṣudrabhavagrahaṇam. utkarṣeṇāsaṃkhyeyā lokāḥ. vanaspatikāyikānām ekendriyavat. trasakāyikeṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa dve sagaropamasahasre pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvair abhyadhike. śeṣānāṃ pañcendriyavat.
children.translated_text: § 96. By the classification of body-type (<s>kāya</s>): for earth-, water-, fire-, and air-bodied beings, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum, the duration of a minor existence; at maximum, innumerable <s>lokas</s> (cosmic periods). For plant-bodied beings — as for one-sensed beings. Among mobile beings (<s>trasa</s>), for one with wrong faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, two thousand <s>sāgaropamas</s> exceeded by several <s>pūrvakoṭi</s> units. For the rest — as for five-sensed beings.

children.text: § 97. yogānuvādena vāṅmanasayogiṣu mithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭisaṃyatāsaṃyatapramattāpramattasayogakevalināṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇāntarmuhūrtaḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭeḥ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikasamayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇāntarmuhūrtaḥ. caturṇām upaśamakānāṃ kṣapakāṇāṃ ca nānājīvāpekṣayā ekajīvāpekṣayā ca jaghanyenaikasamayaḥ. utkarṣeṇāntarmuhūrtaḥ. kāyayogiṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenaikasamayaḥ. utkarṣeṇānantaḥ kālo ’saṃkhyeyāḥ pudgalaparivartāḥ. śeṣaṇāṃ manoyogivat. ayogānāṃ sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 97. By the classification of activity (<s>yoga</s>): among those with speech-activity and mind-activity, for those with wrong faith, unrestrained right faith, partial restraint, vigilant restraint, non-vigilant restraint, and the omniscient-with-activity, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum one <s>samaya</s>; at maximum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>. For one with subsidence-right-faith — the time is as stated generally. For one with mixed right-and-wrong faith, with reference to many souls — at minimum one <s>samaya</s>; at maximum, an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>. For a single soul — at minimum one <s>samaya</s>; at maximum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>. For the four subsiders and four destroyers, with reference to many souls and a single soul — at minimum one <s>samaya</s>; at maximum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>. Among those with body-activity, for one with wrong faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum one <s>samaya</s>; at maximum, infinite time — innumerable <s>pudgala-parivarttas</s>. For the rest — as for those with mind-activity. For those without activity — as stated generally.

children.text: § 98. vedānuvādena strīvedeṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa palyopamaśatapṛthaktvam. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādyanivṛttibādarāntānāṃ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. kintu asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvakālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa pañcapañcāśatpalyopamāni deśonāni. puṃvedeṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa sāgaropamaśatapṛthaktvam. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭādyanivṛttibādarāntānāṃ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. napuṃsakavedeṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇānantaḥ kālo ’saṃkhyeyāḥ pudgalaparivarttāḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭādyanivṛttibādarāntānāṃ sāmānyavat. kiṃtv asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi deśonāni. apagatavedānāṃ sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 98. By the classification of sex (<s>veda</s>): among those with feminine sex-passion (<s>strīveda</s>), for one with wrong faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, a hundred <s>palyopama</s> units. For those from subsidence-right-faith to the gross non-return stage (<s>anivṛtti-bādara</s>) — the time is as stated generally. However, for one with unrestrained right faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, fifty-five <s>palyopamas</s> less a fraction. Among those with masculine sex-passion (<s>puṃveda</s>), for one with wrong faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, a hundred <s>sāgaropama</s> units. For those from subsidence-right-faith to the gross non-return stage — the time is as stated generally. Among those with neuter sex-passion (<s>napuṃsakaveda</s>), for one with wrong faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, infinite time — innumerable <s>pudgala-parivarttas</s>. For those from subsidence-right-faith to the gross non-return stage — as stated generally. However, for one with unrestrained right faith, with reference to many souls — all time. For a single soul — at minimum an <s>antarmuhūrta</s>; at maximum, thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> less a fraction. For those without sex-passion — as stated generally.

children.text: § 99. kaṣāyānuvādena catuṣkaṣāyāṇāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādyapramattāntānāṃ manoyogivat. dvayor upaśamakayor dvayoḥ kṣapakayoḥ kevalalobhasya ca akaṣāyāṇāṃ ca sāmānyotaḥ kālaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 99. By the classification of passion (<s>kaṣāya</s>): for those with the four passions, from wrong faith to the non-vigilant restraint — as for those with mind-activity. For the two subsiders, the two destroyers, one with anger alone, and those without passions — the time is as stated generally.

children.text: § 100. jñānānuvādena matyajñāniśrutājñāniṣu mithyādṛṣṭisāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyoḥ sāmānyavat. vibhaṅgajñāniṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi deśonāni. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭeḥ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. ābhinibodhikaśrutāvadhimanaḥparyayakevalajñānināṃ ca sāmānyoktaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 100. By the exposition of knowledge (<s>jñānānuvāda</s>): for those with wrong sensory knowledge (<s>matyajñāna</s>) and wrong scriptural knowledge (<s>śrutājñāna</s>), the time for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong belief) and <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> (right belief in downfall) is as stated generally. For those with <s>vibhaṅgajñāna</s> (erroneous clairvoyant knowledge), the time of <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, is all time. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s> (48 minutes). At maximum, it is slightly less than thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> (ocean-measured periods). The time of <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> is as stated generally. For those possessing <s>ābhinibodhikajñāna</s> (sensory knowledge), <s>śrutajñāna</s> (scriptural knowledge), <s>avadhijñāna</s> (clairvoyant knowledge), <s>manaḥparyayajñāna</s> (mind-reading knowledge), and <s>kevalajñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge), the time is as stated generally.

children.text: § 101. saṃyamānuvādena sāmāyikacchedopasthāpanaparihāraviśuddhisūkṣmasāṃparāyayathākhyātaśuddhisaṃyatānāṃ saṃyatāsaṃyatānām asaṃyatānāṃ ca caturṇāṃ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 101. By the exposition of restraint (<s>saṃyamānuvāda</s>): for those with <s>sāmāyika</s> (equanimity), <s>chedopasthāpana</s> (re-initiation), <s>parihāraviśuddhi</s> (purificatory restraint), <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāya</s> (subtle passion), and <s>yathākhyāta</s> (perfect conduct) forms of purity-restraint, as well as for the partially restrained (<s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>) and the unrestrained (<s>asaṃyata</s>)—for [all] four, the time is as stated generally.

children.text: § 102. darśanānuvādena cakṣurdarśaniṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa dve sāgaropamasahasre. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādīnāṃ kṣīṇakaṣāyāntānāṃ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. acakṣurdarśaniṣu mithyādṛṣṭyādikṣīṇakaṣāyāntānāṃ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. avadhikevaladarśaninor avadhikevalajñānivat.
children.translated_text: § 102. By the exposition of perception (<s>darśanānuvāda</s>): for those with eye-perception (<s>cakṣurdarśana</s>), the time of <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, is all time. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is two thousand <s>sāgaropamas</s>. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and the rest up to <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s> (destroyed passions), the time is as stated generally. For those with non-eye-perception (<s>acakṣurdarśana</s>), for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> and the rest up to <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s>, the time is as stated generally. For those with clairvoyant perception (<s>avadhidarśana</s>) and omniscient perception (<s>kevaladarśana</s>), the time is as for those with <s>avadhijñāna</s> and <s>kevalajñāna</s>.

children.text: § 103. leśyānuvādena kṛṣṇanīlakāpotaleśyāsu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trayastriṃśatsaptadaśasaptasāgaropamāṇi sātirekāṇi. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyoḥ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trayastriṃśatsaptadaśasaptasāgaropamāṇi deśonāni. tejaḥpadmaleśyayor mithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa dve sāgaropame aṣṭādaśa ca sāgaropamāṇi sātirekāṇi. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyoḥ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. saṃyatāsaṃyatapramattāpramattānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarśeṇāntarmuhūrtaḥ. śuklaleśyānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇaikatriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi sātirekāṇi. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādisayogakevalyantānām aleśyānāṃ ca sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. kiṃ tu saṃyatāsaṃyatasya nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇāntarmuhūrtaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 103. By the exposition of <s>leśyā</s> (soul-coloration): for those with black (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>), blue (<s>nīla</s>), and grey (<s>kāpota</s>) <s>leśyās</s>, the time of <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, is all time. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is thirty-three, seventeen, and seven <s>sāgaropamas</s> respectively, with a remainder. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s> (mixed right-and-wrong belief), the time is as stated generally. For <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> (right-believer without restraint), with reference to many souls, it is all time. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is slightly less than thirty-three, seventeen, and seven <s>sāgaropamas</s>. For <s>tejas</s> (fiery) and <s>padma</s> (lotus) <s>leśyās</s>, for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> and <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, it is all time. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is two <s>sāgaropamas</s> and eighteen <s>sāgaropamas</s> respectively, with a remainder. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, the time is as stated generally. For the partially restrained (<s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>), the restrained with negligence (<s>pramatta</s>), and the restrained without negligence (<s>apramatta</s>), with reference to many souls, it is all time. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is one <s>samaya</s> (instant). At maximum, it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. For those with white (<s>śukla</s>) <s>leśyā</s>, for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, it is all time. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is thirty-one <s>sāgaropamas</s> with a remainder. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and the rest up to <s>sayogakevalin</s> (omniscient with activity), and for those without <s>leśyā</s>, the time is as stated generally. However, for the partially restrained, with reference to many souls, it is all time. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is one <s>samaya</s>. At maximum, it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>.

children.text: § 104. bhavyānuvādena bhavyeṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvāpekṣayā dvau bhaṅgau anādiḥ saparyavasānaḥ sādiḥ saparyavasānaś ca. tatra sādiḥ saparyavasāno jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇārddhapudgalaparivarto deśonaḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādyayogakevalyantānāṃ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. abhavyānām anādir aparyavasānaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 104. By the exposition of capacity for liberation (<s>bhavyānuvāda</s>): among the capable (<s>bhavya</s>), for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, it is all time. With reference to one soul, there are two alternatives: beginningless with an end, and with a beginning and with an end. Of these, the one with a beginning and with an end is, at minimum, less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is slightly less than half a <s>pudgalaparivarta</s> (cycle of matter). For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and the rest up to <s>ayogakevalin</s> (omniscient without activity), the time is as stated generally. For the incapable (<s>abhavya</s>), it is beginningless and endless.

children.text: § 105. samyaktvānuvādena kṣāyikasamyagdṛṣṭīnām asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭādyayogakevalyantānāṃ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. kṣāyopaśamikasamyagdṛṣṭīnāṃ caturṇāṃ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. aupaśamikasamyaktveṣu asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭisaṃyatāsaṃyator nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa palyopamāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyaś cotkṛṣṭaś cāntarmuhūrtaḥ. pramatāpramattayoś caturṇām upaśamakānāṃ ca nānājīvāpekṣayā ekajīvāpekṣayā ca jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇāntarmuhūrtaḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyaṅmithyādṛṣṭimithyādṛṣṭīnāṃ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 105. By the exposition of right belief (<s>samyaktvānuvāda</s>): for those with indestructible right belief (<s>kṣāyikasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>), from <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and the rest up to <s>ayogakevalin</s>, the time is as stated generally. For those with right belief born of destruction-cum-subsidence (<s>kṣāyopaśamikasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>), the time for [all] four is as stated generally. For those with right belief born of subsidence (<s>aupaśamikasamyaktva</s>), for <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>, with reference to many souls, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> (straw-measured period). With reference to one soul, at minimum and at maximum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. For the restrained with and without negligence (<s>pramatta</s> and <s>apramatta</s>), and for the four <s>upaśamaka</s> (subsidence-ladder) stages, with reference to many souls and with reference to one soul, at minimum it is one <s>samaya</s>. At maximum, it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, and <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>, the time is as stated generally.

children.text: § 106. saṃjñānuvādena saṃjñiṣu mithyādṛṣṭyādyanivṛttibādarāntānāṃ puṃvedavat. śeṣāṇām sāmānyoktaḥ. asaṃjñināṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena kṣudrabhavagrahaṇam. utkarṣenānantaḥ kalo ’saṃkhyeyāḥ pudgalaparivartāḥ. tadubhayavyapadeśarahitānāṃ sāmānyoktaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 106. By the exposition of rational faculty (<s>saṃjñānuvāda</s>): for rational beings (<s>saṃjñin</s>), for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> and the rest up to the stage ending with gross non-return (<s>anivṛttibādara</s>), the time is as for male sex-passion (<s>puṃveda</s>). For the remaining [stages], the time is as stated generally. For non-rational beings (<s>asaṃjñin</s>), with reference to many souls, it is all time. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is the minimum lifespan (<s>kṣudrabhavagrahaṇa</s>). At maximum, it is an infinite time, innumerable <s>pudgalaparivartāḥ</s> (cycles of matter). For those devoid of both designations, the time is as stated generally.

children.text: § 107. āhārānuvādena āhārakeṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghayenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇāṃgulāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ asaṃkheyāsaṃkheyā utsarpiṇyavasarpiṇyaḥ. śeṣāṇāṃ sāmānyoktaḥ kālaḥ. anāhārakeṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sarvaḥ kālaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ utkarṣeṇa trayaḥ samayāḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayāḥ jaghanenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇāvalikāyā asaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenaikaḥ samayāḥ. utkarṣeṇa dvau samayau. sayogakevalino nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyena trayaḥ samayāḥ. utkarṣeṇa saṃkheyāḥ samayāḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyaś cotkṛṣṭaś ca trayaḥ samayāḥ. ayogakevalināṃ sāmānyokataḥ kālaḥ. kālo varṇitaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 107. By the exposition of nourishment (<s>āhārānuvāda</s>): for those who take nourishment (<s>āhāraka</s>), for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, it is all time. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is an innumerable fraction of a finger-breadth [of time], innumerable times innumerable ascending and descending half-cycles (<s>utsarpiṇī-avasarpiṇī</s>). For the remaining [stages], the time is as stated generally. For those not taking nourishment (<s>anāhāraka</s>), for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, it is all time. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is one <s>samaya</s>. At maximum, it is three <s>samayas</s>. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, at minimum it is one <s>samaya</s>. At maximum, it is an innumerable fraction of an <s>āvalikā</s> (time unit). With reference to one soul, at minimum it is one <s>samaya</s>. At maximum, it is two <s>samayas</s>. For <s>sayogakevalin</s> (omniscient with activity), with reference to many souls, at minimum it is three <s>samayas</s>. At maximum, it is a numerable number of <s>samayas</s>. With reference to one soul, at minimum and at maximum it is three <s>samayas</s>. For <s>ayogakevalin</s> (omniscient without activity), the time is as stated generally. Thus, time has been described.

children.text: § 108. antaraṃ nirūpyate. vivakṣitasya guṇasya guṇāntarasaṃkrame sati punastatprāpteḥ prāṅmadhyam antaram. tad dvividhaṃ sāmānyena viśeṣaṇa ca. sāmānyena tāvad mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenārmuhūrtaḥ.

utkarṣeṇa dve ṣaṭṣaṣtī deśone sāgaropamāṇām. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭer antaraṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa palyopamāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. utkarṣeṇārddhapudgalaparivarto deśonaḥ. samyagmithyādṛṣṭer antaraṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sāsādanavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇārddhapudgalaparivarto deśonaḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭādyapramattāntānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇārddhapudgalaparivarto deśonaḥ. caturṇām upaśamakānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa varṣapṛthaktvam. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇārddhapudgalaparivarto deśonāḥ. caturṇāṃ kṣapakāṇām ayogakevalināṃ ca nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa ṣaṇmāsāḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. sayogakevalināṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā ekajīvāpekṣayā ca nāsty antaram.
children.translated_text: At maximum, it is slightly less than sixty-six <s>sāgaropamas</s>. The interval of <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, at minimum is one <s>samaya</s>. At maximum, it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>. At maximum, it is slightly less than half a <s>pudgalaparivarta</s>. The interval of <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, is as for <s>sāsādana</s>. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is slightly less than half a <s>pudgalaparivarta</s>. For <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and the rest up to <s>apramatta</s>, with reference to many souls, there is no interval. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is slightly less than half a <s>pudgalaparivarta</s>. For the four <s>upaśamaka</s> stages, with reference to many souls, at minimum it is one <s>samaya</s>. At maximum, it is one year minus a fraction. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is slightly less than half a <s>pudgalaparivarta</s>. For the four <s>kṣapaka</s> (destruction-ladder) stages and <s>ayogakevalin</s>, with reference to many souls, at minimum it is one <s>samaya</s>. At maximum, it is six months. With reference to one soul, there is no interval. For <s>sayogakevalin</s>, with reference to many souls and with reference to one soul, there is no interval.

§ 108. The interval (<s>antara</s>) is now examined. When there is a transition from the intended quality to another quality, the intervening period before re-attaining it is the interval. That is of two kinds: general and specific. Generally, for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, there is no interval. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>.

children.text: § 109. viśeṣeṇa gatyanuvādena narakagatau nārakāṇāṃ saptasu pṛthivīṣu mithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaraṃ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa eka-tri-sapta-daśa-saptadaśa-dvāviṃśati-trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi deśonāni. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgo ’ntarmuhūrtaś ca. utkarṣeṇa eka-tri-sapta-daśa-saptadaśa-dvāviṃśati-trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi deśonāni.
children.translated_text: § 109. Specifically, by the exposition of destinies (<s>gatyanuvāda</s>): in the hellish destiny (<s>narakagati</s>), for hell-beings (<s>nāraka</s>) in the seven earths, for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> and <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, there is no interval. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is slightly less than one, three, seven, ten, seventeen, twenty-two, and thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> [respectively for the seven hells]. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, at minimum it is one <s>samaya</s>. At maximum, it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> or less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is slightly less than one, three, seven, ten, seventeen, twenty-two, and thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> [respectively].

children.text: § 110. tiryaggatau tiraścāṃ mithyādrster nānājīvāpekeṣayā nasty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trīṇi palyopamāni deśonāni. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādīnāṃ caturṇāṃ sāmānyoktam antaram.
children.translated_text: § 110. In the animal destiny (<s>tiryaggati</s>): for animals (<s>tiryañc</s>), for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, there is no interval. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is slightly less than three <s>palyopamas</s>. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and the rest of the four [stages], the interval is as stated generally.

children.text: § 111. manuṣyagatau manuṣyāṇāṃ mithyādṛṣṭes tiryagvat. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyagmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgo ’ntarmuhūrtaś ca. utkarṣeṇa trīṇi palyopamāni pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvair abhyadhikāni. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trīṇi palyopamāni pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvair abhyadikāni. saṃyatāsaṃyatapramattāpramattānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā nasty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvāni. caturṇām upaśamakānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvāni. śeṣāṇāṃ sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 111. In the human destiny (<s>manuṣyagati</s>): for humans, the interval for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> is as for animals. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, it is as stated generally. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> or less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is three <s>palyopamas</s> increased by innumerable <s>pūrvakoṭi</s>-fold quantities. For <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, there is no interval. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is three <s>palyopamas</s> increased by innumerable <s>pūrvakoṭi</s>-fold quantities. For the partially restrained, the restrained with negligence, and the restrained without negligence, with reference to many souls, there is no interval. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is innumerable <s>pūrvakoṭi</s>-fold quantities. For the four <s>upaśamaka</s> stages, with reference to many souls, it is as stated generally. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is innumerable <s>pūrvakoṭi</s>-fold quantities. For the remaining [stages], it is as stated generally.

children.text: § 112. devagatau devānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyor nānājīāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa ekatriṃśatsāgaropmāṇi deśonāni. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyagmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena palyopamāsaṃkheyabhāgo ’ntarmuhūrtaś ca. utkarṣeṇaikatriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi deśonāni.
children.translated_text: § 112. In the celestial destiny (<s>devagati</s>): for gods (<s>deva</s>), for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> and <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, there is no interval. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is slightly less than thirty-one <s>sāgaropamas</s>. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, it is as stated generally. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> or less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is slightly less than thirty-one <s>sāgaropamas</s>.

children.text: § 113. indriyānuvādena ekendriyāṇāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvāpekṣayā jaghanyena kṣudrabhavagrahaṇam. utkarṣeṇa dve sāgaropamasahasre pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvair abhyadhike. vikalendriyāṇāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena kṣudrabhavagrahaṇam. utkarṣeṇānantaḥ kālo ’saṃkhyeyāḥ pudgalaparivartāḥ. evam indriyaṃ praty antaram uktam. guṇaṃ praty ubhayato ’pi nāsty antaram. pañcendriyeṣu mithyādṛṣṭeḥ sāmānyavat. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgo ’ntarmuhūrtaś ca. utkarseṇa sāgaropmasahasraṃ pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvair abhyadhikam. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādyapramattāntānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa sāgaropamasahasraṃ pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvair abhyadhikam. caturṇām upaśamakānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa sāgaropamasahasraṃ pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvair abhyadhikam. śeṣāṇāṃ sāmānyoktam.
children.translated_text: § 113. By the exposition of sense-organs (<s>indriyānuvāda</s>): for one-sensed beings (<s>ekendriya</s>), with reference to many souls, there is no interval. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is the minimum lifespan (<s>kṣudrabhavagrahaṇa</s>). At maximum, it is two thousand <s>sāgaropamas</s> increased by innumerable <s>pūrvakoṭi</s>-fold quantities. For beings with incomplete sense-organs (<s>vikalendriya</s>), with reference to many souls, there is no interval. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is the minimum lifespan. At maximum, it is an infinite time, innumerable <s>pudgalaparivartāḥ</s>. Thus, the interval with respect to the sense-organ [itself] has been stated. With respect to the quality [of the soul possessing it], from both perspectives, there is no interval. For five-sensed beings (<s>pañcendriya</s>), for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>, it is as stated generally. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with reference to many souls, it is as stated generally. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> or less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is one thousand <s>sāgaropamas</s> increased by innumerable <s>pūrvakoṭi</s>-fold quantities. For <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and the rest up to <s>apramatta</s>, with reference to many souls, there is no interval. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is one thousand <s>sāgaropamas</s> increased by innumerable <s>pūrvakoṭi</s>-fold quantities. For the four <s>upaśamaka</s> stages, with reference to many souls, it is as stated generally. With reference to one soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. At maximum, it is one thousand <s>sāgaropamas</s> increased by innumerable <s>pūrvakoṭi</s>-fold quantities. For the remaining [stages], it is as stated generally.

children.text: § 114. kāyānuvādena pṛthivyaptejovāyukāyikānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena kṣudrabhavagrahaṇam. utkarṣeṇānantaḥ kālo ’saṃkhyeyāḥ pudgalaparivartāḥ. vanaspatikāyikānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvāpekṣayā jaghanyena kṣudrabhavagrahaṇam. utkarṣeṇāsaṃkhyeyā lokāḥ. evaṃ kāyaṃ praty antaram uktam. guṇaṃ praty ubhayato ’pi nāsty antaram. trasakāyikeṣu mithyādṛṣṭeh sāmānyavat. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgo ’ntarmuhūrtaś ca. urkarṣeṇa dve sāgaropamasahasre pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvair abhyadhike. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādyapramattāntānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa dve sāgaropamasahasre pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvair abhyadhike. caturṇāṃ upaśamakānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa dve sāgaropamasahasre pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvair abhyadhike. śeṣāṇāṃ pañcendriyavat.
children.translated_text: § 114. By the supplementary perspective of body (<s>kāyānuvāda</s>): for the earth-bodied, water-bodied, fire-bodied, and air-bodied beings, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval. With respect to a single soul, at minimum it is one short lifetime (<s>kṣudrabhavagrahaṇa</s>); at maximum, infinite time and innumerable <s>pudgalaparivartās</s> (material cycles). For the plant-bodied (<s>vanaspatikāyika</s>) beings, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is one short lifetime; at maximum, innumerable <s>lokas</s> (worlds). Thus the interval with respect to body has been stated. With respect to quality (<s>guṇa</s>), in both cases there is no interval. Among the mobile beings (<s>trasakāyika</s>), for one of wrong faith (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), it is as stated generally. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> (one in the state of declining right faith) and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s> (one of mixed right and wrong faith), with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> and less than one <s>muhūrta</s> (<s>antarmuhūrta</s>); at maximum, two thousand <s>sāgaropamas</s> exceeded by a number of <s>pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvas</s>. For those ranging from <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> (the unrestrained right-believer) up to <s>apramatta</s> (the non-negligent), with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, two thousand <s>sāgaropamas</s> exceeded by a number of <s>pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvas</s>. For the four <s>upaśamakas</s> (those with subsided passions), with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, two thousand <s>sāgaropamas</s> exceeded by a number of <s>pūrvakoṭīpṛthaktvas</s>. For the rest, it is as for the five-sensed beings.

children.text: § 115. yogānuvādena kāyavāṅmanasayogināṃ mithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭisaṃyatāsaṃyatapramattāpramattasayogakevalināṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā ekajīvāpekṣayā ca nāsty antaram. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. caturṇām upaśamakānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. caturṇām kṣapakāṇām ayogakevalināṃ ca sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 115. By the supplementary perspective of activity (<s>yogānuvāda</s>): for those possessing bodily, vocal, and mental activity (<s>kāyavāṅmanasayoga</s>) — including those of wrong faith (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), the unrestrained right-believer (<s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>), the partially restrained (<s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>), the negligent (<s>pramatta</s>), the non-negligent (<s>apramatta</s>), and the omniscient with activity (<s>sayogakevalin</s>) — with respect to both multiple souls and a single soul, there is no interval. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, there is no interval. For the four <s>upaśamakas</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, there is no interval. For the four <s>kṣapakas</s> (those who have destroyed passions) and the omniscient without activity (<s>ayogakevalin</s>), it is as stated generally.

children.text: § 116. vedānuvādena strīvedeṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa pañcapañcāśatpalyopamāni deśonāni. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyagmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣaya sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgo ’ntarmuhūrtaś ca. utkarṣeṇa palyopamaśatapṛthaktvam. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādyapramattāntānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa palyopamaśatapṛthaktvam. dvayor upaśamakayor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa palyopamaśatapṛthaktvam. dvayoḥ kṣapakayor nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa varṣapṛthaktvam. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram.
children.translated_text: § 116. By the supplementary perspective of gender (<s>vedānuvāda</s>): among those with feminine gender (<s>strīveda</s>), for one of wrong faith (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, fifty-five <s>palyopamas</s> slightly less. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> and less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, one hundred <s>palyopama</s>-<s>pṛthaktvas</s>. For those ranging from <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>apramatta</s>, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, one hundred <s>palyopama</s>-<s>pṛthaktvas</s>. For two <s>upaśamakas</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, one hundred <s>palyopama</s>-<s>pṛthaktvas</s>. For two <s>kṣapakas</s>, with respect to multiple souls, at minimum it is one time-instant (<s>samaya</s>); at maximum, a <s>varṣapṛthaktva</s> (a number of years); with respect to a single soul, there is no interval.

children.text: § 117. puṃvedeṣu mithyādṛṣṭeḥ sāmānyavat. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyagmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena palyopmāsaṃkhyeyabhāgo ’ntarmuhūrtaś ca. utkarṣeṇa sāgaropamaśatapṛthaktvam. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādyapramattāntānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa sāgaropamaśatapṛthaktvam. dvayor upaśamakayor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa sāgaropamaśatapṛthaktvam. dvayoḥ kṣapakayor nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa saṃvatsaraḥ sātirekaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram.
children.translated_text: § 117. Among those with masculine gender (<s>puṃveda</s>), for one of wrong faith, it is as stated generally. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> and less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, one hundred <s>sāgaropama</s>-<s>pṛthaktvas</s>. For those ranging from <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>apramatta</s>, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, one hundred <s>sāgaropama</s>-<s>pṛthaktvas</s>. For two <s>upaśamakas</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, one hundred <s>sāgaropama</s>-<s>pṛthaktvas</s>. For two <s>kṣapakas</s>, with respect to multiple souls, at minimum it is one time-instant; at maximum, slightly more than one year; with respect to a single soul, there is no interval.

children.text: § 118. napuṃsakavedeṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi deśonāni. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭyādyanivṛttyupaśamakāntānāṃ sāmānyoktam. dvayoḥ kṣapakayoḥ strīvedavat. apagatavedeṣu anivṛttibādaropaśamakasūkṣmasāṃparāyopaśamakayor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyoktam. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyam utkṛṣṭaṃ cāntarmuhūrtaḥ. upaśāntakaṣāyasya nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. śeṣāṇāṃ sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 118. Among those with neuter gender (<s>napuṃsakaveda</s>), for one of wrong faith, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> slightly less. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>anivṛttyupaśamaka</s> (one with non-retreating subsidence), it is as stated generally. For two <s>kṣapakas</s>, it is as for feminine gender. Among those free from gender (<s>apagataveda</s>), for <s>anivṛttibādaropaśamaka</s> (one with non-retreating gross subsidence) and <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāyopaśamaka</s> (one with subtle mixed passions in subsidence), with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum and at maximum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. For <s>upaśāntakaṣāya</s> (one whose passions are subsided), with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, there is no interval. For the rest, it is as stated generally.

children.text: § 119. kaṣāyānuvādena krodhamānamāyālobhakaṣāyāṇāṃ mithyādṛṣṭādyanivṛttyupaśamakāntānāṃ manoyogivat. dvayoḥ kṣapakayor nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa saṃvatsaraḥ sātirekaḥ. kevalalobhasya sūkṣmasāṃparāyopaśamakasya nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. kṣapakasya tasya sāmānyavat. akaṣāyeṣu upaśāntakaṣāyasya nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. śeṣāṇāṃ trayāṇāṃ sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 119. By the supplementary perspective of passions (<s>kaṣāyānuvāda</s>): for the passions of anger (<s>krodha</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), deceit (<s>māyā</s>), and greed (<s>lobha</s>), from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>anivṛttyupaśamaka</s>, it is as for the mind-activity possessor (<s>manoyogin</s>). For two <s>kṣapakas</s>, with respect to multiple souls, at minimum it is one time-instant; at maximum, slightly more than one year. For the one with subtle mixed passions (<s>sūkṣmasāṃparāyopaśamaka</s>) possessing only greed (<s>kevalalobha</s>), with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, there is no interval. For the <s>kṣapaka</s> of that same [state], it is as stated generally. Among those free from passions (<s>akaṣāya</s>), for <s>upaśāntakaṣāya</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, there is no interval. For the remaining three, it is as stated generally.

children.text: § 120. jñānānuvādena matyajñānaśrutājñānavibhaṅgajñāniṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā ekajīvāpekṣayā ca nāsty antaram. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. ābhinibodhikaśrutāvadhijñāniṣu asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa pūrvakoṭī deśonā. saṃyatāsaṃyatasya nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa ṣaṭṣaṣṭisāgaropamāṇi sātirekāṇi. pramattāpramattayor nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarsena trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi sātirekāṇi. caturṇām upaśamakānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa ṣaṭṣaṣṭisāgaropamāṇi sātirekāṇi. caturṇāṃ kṣapakāṇāṃ sāmānyavat. kiṃ tu avadhijñāniṣu nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa varṣapṛthaktvam. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. manaḥparyayajñāniṣu pramattāpramattasaṃyatayor nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyam utkṛṣṭaṃ cāntarmuhūrtaḥ. caturṇāṃ upaśamakānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa pūrvakoṭī deśonā. caturṇāṃ kṣapakāṇām avadhijñānivat. dvayoḥ kevalajñāninoḥ sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 120. By the supplementary perspective of knowledge (<s>jñānānuvāda</s>): among those with <s>matyajñāna</s> (erroneous sensory knowledge), <s>śrutājñāna</s> (erroneous scriptural knowledge), and <s>vibhaṅgajñāna</s> (erroneous clairvoyance), for one of wrong faith, with respect to both multiple souls and a single soul, there is no interval. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, there is no interval.
