Among those with <s>ābhinibodhikajñāna</s> (sensory knowledge), <s>śrutajñāna</s> (scriptural knowledge), and <s>avadhijñāna</s> (clairvoyance), for <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, slightly less than a <s>pūrvakoṭī</s>. For <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, sixty-six <s>sāgaropamas</s> and more. For both <s>pramatta</s> and <s>apramatta</s>, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> and more. For four <s>upaśamakas</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, sixty-six <s>sāgaropamas</s> and more. For four <s>kṣapakas</s>, it is as stated generally. However, among those with clairvoyance (<s>avadhijñāna</s>), with respect to multiple souls, at minimum it is one time-instant; at maximum, a <s>varṣapṛthaktva</s>; with respect to a single soul, there is no interval. Among those with mind-reading knowledge (<s>manaḥparyayajñāna</s>), for the negligent and non-negligent restrained (<s>pramattāpramattasaṃyata</s>), with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum and at maximum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. For four <s>upaśamakas</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, slightly less than a <s>pūrvakoṭī</s>. For four <s>kṣapakas</s>, it is as for those with clairvoyance. For the two kinds of omniscient (<s>kevalajñānin</s>), it is as stated generally.

children.text: § 121. saṃyamānuvādena sāmāyikacchedopasthāpanaśuddhisaṃyateṣu pramattāpramattayor nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyam utkṛṣṭam cāntarmuhūrtaḥ. dvayor upaśamakayor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa pūrvakoṭī deśonā. dvayoḥ kṣapakayoḥ sāmānyavat. parihāraśuddhisaṃyateṣu pramattāpramattayor nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyam utkṛṣṭaṃ cāntarmuhūrtaḥ. sūkṣmasāmparāyaśuddhisaṃyateṣūpaśamakasya nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. tasyaiva kṣapakasya sāmānyavat. yathākhyāte akaṣāyavat. saṃyatāsaṃyatasya nānājīvāpekṣayā ekajīvāpekṣayā ca nāsty antaram. asaṃyateṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsy antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi deśonāni. śeṣāṇāṃ trayāṇām sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 121. By the supplementary perspective of restraint (<s>saṃyamānuvāda</s>): among those with <s>sāmāyika</s> (equanimous), <s>chedopasthāpana</s> (re-initiation), and <s>śuddhi</s> (pure) restraint, for both <s>pramatta</s> and <s>apramatta</s>, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum and at maximum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. For two <s>upaśamakas</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, slightly less than a <s>pūrvakoṭī</s>. For two <s>kṣapakas</s>, it is as stated generally. Among those with <s>parihāraśuddhi</s> (restraint with special purificatory practices), for both <s>pramatta</s> and <s>apramatta</s>, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum and at maximum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. Among those with <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāya</s> (subtle mixed passions) and <s>śuddhi</s> (pure) restraint, for the <s>upaśamaka</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, there is no interval. For the <s>kṣapaka</s> of that same [state], it is as stated generally. For the <s>yathākhyāta</s> (complete restraint), it is as for those free from passions. For <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s> (the partially restrained), with respect to both multiple souls and a single soul, there is no interval. Among the unrestrained (<s>asaṃyata</s>), for one of wrong faith, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> slightly less. For the remaining three, it is as stated generally.

children.text: § 122. darśanānuvādena cakṣurdarśaniṣu mithyādṛṣṭeḥ sāmānyavat. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyagmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena palyopamāsaṃkheyabhāgo ’ntarmuhūrtaś ca. utkarṣeṇa dve sāgaropamasahasre deśone. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādyapramattāntānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ utakrṣeṇa dve sāgaropamasahasre deśone. caturṇām upaśamakānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyoktam. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa dve sāgaropamasahasre deśone. caturṇāṃ kṣapakāṇāṃ sāmānyoktam. acakṣurdarśaniṣu mithyādṛṣṭyādikṣīṇakaṣāyāntānāṃ sāmānyoktam antaram. avadhidarśanino ’vadhijñānivat. kevaladarśaninaḥ kevalajñānivat.
children.translated_text: § 122. By the supplementary perspective of perception (<s>darśanānuvāda</s>): among those with visual perception (<s>cakṣurdarśana</s>), for one of wrong faith, it is as stated generally. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> and less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, two thousand <s>sāgaropamas</s> slightly less. For those ranging from <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>apramatta</s>, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, two thousand <s>sāgaropamas</s> slightly less. For four <s>upaśamakas</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, two thousand <s>sāgaropamas</s> slightly less. For four <s>kṣapakas</s>, it is as stated generally. Among those with non-visual perception (<s>acakṣurdarśana</s>), for those from <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> up to <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s> (one whose passions are destroyed), the interval is as stated generally. For those with clairvoyant perception (<s>avadhidarśana</s>), it is as for those with clairvoyant knowledge. For the omniscient perceiver (<s>kevaladarśanin</s>), it is as for the omniscient knower.

children.text: § 123. leśyānuvādena kṛṣṇalīlakāpotaleśyāsu mithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trayastriṃśatsaptadaśasaptasāgaropamāṇi deśonāni. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyagmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena palyopamāsaṃkheyabhāgo ’ntarmuhūrtaś ca. utkarṣeṇa trayastriṃśatsaptadaśasaptasāgaropamāṇi deśonāni.
children.translated_text: § 123. By the supplementary perspective of coloration (<s>leśyānuvāda</s>): among those with black (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>), dark-blue (<s>nīla</s>), and grey (<s>kāpota</s>) colorations, for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> and <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, thirty-three, seventeen, and seven <s>sāgaropamas</s> respectively, slightly less. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> and less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, thirty-three, seventeen, and seven <s>sāgaropamas</s> respectively, slightly less.

children.text: § 124. tejạhpadmaleśyayor mithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa dve sāgaropame aṣṭādaśa ca sāgaropamāṇi sātirekāṇi. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyagmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgo ’ntarmuhūrtaś ca. utkarṣeṇa dve sāgaropame aṣṭādaśa ca sāgaropamāṇi sātirekāṇi. saṃyatāsaṃyatapramattāpramattasaṃyatānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā ekajīvāpekṣayā ca nāsty antaram.
children.translated_text: § 124. Among those with fiery-red (<s>tejas</s>) and lotus-pink (<s>padma</s>) colorations, for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> and <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, two <s>sāgaropamas</s> and eighteen <s>sāgaropamas</s> and more. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> and less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, two <s>sāgaropamas</s> and eighteen <s>sāgaropamas</s> and more. For <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>, <s>pramatta</s>, and <s>apramattasaṃyata</s>, with respect to both multiple souls and a single soul, there is no interval.

children.text: § 125. śuklaleśyeṣu mithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇaikatriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi deṣonāni. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgo ’ntarmuhūrtaś ca. utkarṣeṇaikatriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi deśonāni. saṃyatāsaṃyatapramattasaṃyatos tejoleśyāvat. apramattasaṃyatsya nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyam utkṛṣṭaṃ cāntarmuhūrtaḥ. trayāṇām upaśamakānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyam utkṛṣṭaṃ cāntarmuhūrtaḥ. upaśāntakaṣāyasya nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. caturṇāṃ kṣapakāṇāṃ sayogakevalinām aleśyānāṃ ca sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 125. Among those with white coloration (<s>śuklaleśyā</s>), for <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> and <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, thirty-one <s>sāgaropamas</s> slightly less. For <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum it is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> and less than one <s>muhūrta</s>; at maximum, thirty-one <s>sāgaropamas</s> slightly less. For <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s> and <s>pramattasaṃyata</s>, it is as for the fiery-red coloration. For the <s>apramattasaṃyata</s>, with respect to multiple souls, there is no interval; with respect to a single soul, at minimum and at maximum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. For three <s>upaśamakas</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, at minimum and at maximum it is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. For <s>upaśāntakaṣāya</s>, with respect to multiple souls, it is as stated generally; with respect to a single soul, there is no interval. For four <s>kṣapakas</s>, the omniscient with activity (<s>sayogakevalin</s>), and those without coloration (<s>aleśya</s>), it is as stated generally.

children.text: § 126. bhavyānuvādena bhavyeṣu mithyādṛṣṭyādyayogakevalyantānāṃ sāmānyavat. abhavyānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā ekajīvāpekṣayā ca nāsty antaram.
children.translated_text: § 126. By way of the exposition of capacity (<s>bhavya</s>): for the capable, from those with wrong faith (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) through to those with <s>ayoga-kevalin</s> [status], it is as in the general [rule]. For the incapable (<s>abhavya</s>), there is no interval, whether considered from the standpoint of many souls or of a single soul.

children.text: § 127. samyaktvānuvādena kṣāyikasamyagdṛṣṭiṣv asamyatasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa pūrvakoṭī deśonā. saṃyatāsaṃyatapramattāpramattasaṃyatānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi sātirekāṇi. caturṇām upaśamakānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi sātirekāṇi. śeṣāṇāṃ sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 127. By way of the exposition of right faith (<s>samyaktva</s>): among those with <s>kṣāyika</s> (destructional) right faith — for the unrestrained right-believer (<s>asaṃyata-samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), from the standpoint of many souls, there is no interval. For a single soul, the minimum is a fraction of a <s>muhūrta</s>, the maximum is slightly less than a <s>pūrvakoṭi</s>. For the partially restrained (<s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>), the restrained-with-negligence (<s>pramatta</s>), and the restrained-without-negligence (<s>apramatta</s>), from the standpoint of many souls, there is no interval. For a single soul, the minimum is a fraction of a <s>muhūrta</s>, the maximum is thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> with some excess. For the four who are in the subsidence-ladder (<s>upaśamaka</s>), from the standpoint of many souls, it is as in the general [rule]. For a single soul, the minimum is a fraction of a <s>muhūrta</s>, the maximum is thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> with some excess. For the remaining [stages], it is as in the general [rule].

children.text: § 128. kṣāyopaśamikasamyagdṛṣṭiṣv asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa pūrvakoṭī deśonā. saṃyatāsaṃyatasya nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa ṣaṭṣaṣṭisāgaropamāṇi deśonāni. pramattāpramattasaṃyatayor nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi sātirekāṇi.
children.translated_text: § 128. Among those with <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s> (subsidence-cum-destructional) right faith: for the unrestrained right-believer, from the standpoint of many souls, there is no interval. For a single soul, the minimum is a fraction of a <s>muhūrta</s>, the maximum is slightly less than a <s>pūrvakoṭi</s>. For the partially restrained, from the standpoint of many souls, there is no interval. For a single soul, the minimum is a fraction of a <s>muhūrta</s>, the maximum is slightly less than sixty-six <s>sāgaropamas</s>. For the restrained-with-negligence and the restrained-without-negligence, from the standpoint of many souls, there is no interval. For a single soul, the minimum is a fraction of a <s>muhūrta</s>, the maximum is thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> with some excess.

children.text: § 129. aupaśamikasamyagdṛṣṭiṣv asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa sapta rātriṃdināni. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyaṃ utkṛṣṭaṃ cāntarmuhūrtaḥ. saṃyatāsaṃyatasya nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa caturdaśa rārtriṃdināni. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyam utkṛṣṭaṃ cāntarmuhūrtaḥ. pramattāpramattasaṃyatayor nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa paṃcadaśa rātriṃdināni. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyaṃ utkṛṣṭaṃ cāntarmuhūrtaḥ. trayāṇam upaśamakānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa varṣapṛthaktvam. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyam utkṛṣṭaṃ cāntarmuhūrtaḥ. upaśāntakaṣāyasya nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa palyopamāsaṃkheyabhāgaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā ekajīvāpekṣayā ca nāsty antaram.
children.translated_text: § 129. Among those with <s>aupaśamika</s> (subsidence-born) right faith: for the unrestrained right-believer, from the standpoint of many souls, the minimum is one <s>samaya</s> (instant), the maximum is seven days and nights. For a single soul, both the minimum and maximum are a fraction of a <s>muhūrta</s>. For the partially restrained, from the standpoint of many souls, the minimum is one instant, the maximum is fourteen days and nights. For a single soul, both the minimum and maximum are a fraction of a <s>muhūrta</s>.

children.text: § 130. saṃjñānuvādena saṃjñiṣu mithyādṛṣṭeḥ sāmānyavat. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgo ’ntarmuhūrtaś ca. utkarṣeṇa sāgaropamaśatapṛthaktvam. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādyapramattāntānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa sāgaropamaśatapṛthaktvam. caturṇām upaśamakānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇa sāgaropamaśatapṛthaktvam. caturṇāṃ kṣapakāṇāṃ sāmānyavat. asaṃjñināṃ nānājīvāpekṣayaikajīvāpekṣayā ca nāsty antaram. tadubhayavyapadeśarahitānāṃ sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 130. By way of the exposition of cognition-type (<s>saṃjñā</s>): among the rational beings (<s>saṃjñin</s>), for those with wrong faith, it is as in the general [rule]. For the <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> (downfall-right-believer) and the <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s> (mixed-faith), from the standpoint of many souls, it is as in the general [rule]. For a single soul, the minimum is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> plus a fraction of a <s>muhūrta</s>, the maximum is a hundred-and-some <s>sāgaropamas</s>. For those from the unrestrained right-believer through the restrained-without-negligence, from the standpoint of many souls, there is no interval. For a single soul, [continues as per general rules].

children.text: § 131. āhārānuvādena āhārakeṣu mithyādṛṣṭeḥ sāmānyavat. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣtisamyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyor nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyena palyopmāsaṃkhyeyabhāgo ’ntarmuhūrtaś ca. utkarśeṇāṅgulāsaṃkhyeyabhāgo ’saṃkhyeyāsaṃkhyeyā utsarpiṇyavasarpiṇyaḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyapramattāntānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā nāsty antaram. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarśeṇāṅgulāsaṃkhyeyabhāgo ’saṃkhyeyā utsarpiṇyavasarpiṇyaḥ. caturṇām upaśamakānāṃ nānājīvāpekṣayā sāmānyavat. ekajīvaṃ prati jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtaḥ. utkarṣeṇāṅgulāsaṃkhyeyabhāgo ’saṃkhyeyāsaṃkhyeyā utsarpiṇyavsarpiṇyaḥ. caturṇāṃ kṣapakāṇāṃ sayogakevalināṃ ca sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 131. By way of the exposition of nourishment (<s>āhāra</s>): among the nourishment-takers, for those with wrong faith, it is as in the general [rule]. For the <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, from the standpoint of many souls, it is as in the general [rule]. For a single soul, the minimum is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s> plus a fraction of a <s>muhūrta</s>, the maximum is an innumerable fraction of a finger-breadth [of time], [equaling] innumerable times innumerable ascending and descending half-cycles. For those from the unrestrained right-believer through the restrained-without-negligence, from the standpoint of many souls, there is no interval.

children.text: § 132. anāhārakeṣu mithyādṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā ekajīvāpekṣayā ca nāsty antaram. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭer nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣena māsapṛthaktvam. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. sayogakevalinaḥ nānājīvāpekṣayā jaganyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa varṣapṛthaktvam. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. ayogakevalinaḥ nānājīvāpekṣayā jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ. utkarṣeṇa ṣaṇmāsāḥ. ekajīvaṃ prati nāsty antaram. antaram avagatam.
children.translated_text: § 132. Among the non-nourishing beings: for those with wrong faith, from the standpoint of many souls and of a single soul, there is no interval. For the <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭi</s>, from the standpoint of many souls, the minimum is one instant, the maximum is an innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>. For a single soul, there is no interval. For the unrestrained right-believer, from the standpoint of many souls, the minimum is one instant, the maximum is slightly more than a month. For a single soul, [continues similarly].

children.text: § 133. bhāvo vibhāvyate. sa dvividhaḥ sāmānyena viśeṣeṇa ca. sāmānyena tavat mithyādṛṣṭir ity audayiko bhāvaḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭir iti pāriṇāmiko bhāvaḥ. samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭir iti kṣāyopaśamiko bhāvaḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭir iti aupaśamiko vā kṣāyiko vā kṣāyopaśamiko vā bhāvaḥ. asaṃyataḥ punar audayikena bhāvena. saṃyatāsaṃyataḥ pramattasaṃyato ’pramattasaṃyata iti kṣāyopaśamiko bhāvaḥ. caturṇām upaśamakānām aupaśamiko bhāvaḥ. caturṣu kṣapakeṣu sayogāyogakevalinoś ca kṣāyiko bhāvaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 133. <s>Bhāva</s> (state) is now analyzed. It is twofold: general and specific. In general terms: the one with wrong faith (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) — this is a state arising from the fruition of <s>karma</s> (<s>audayika bhāva</s>). The <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭi</s> (downfall-right-believer) — this is a transformational state (<s>pāriṇāmika bhāva</s>). The <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s> (mixed-faith) — this is a <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s> state. The unrestrained right-believer — this is either an <s>aupaśamika</s>, <s>kṣāyika</s>, or <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s> state. The unrestrained [quality] is further due to the <s>audayika</s> state [of conduct-deluding karma].

children.text: § 134. viśeṣeṇa gatyanuvādena narakagatau prathamāyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ nārakāṇāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyantānāṃ sāmānyavat. dvitīyādiṣv ā saptamyā mithyādṛṣṭisāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyaṅmithyādṛṣṭīnāṃ sāmānyavat. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭer aupaśamiko vā kṣāyopaśamiko vā bhāvaḥ. asaṃyataḥ punar audayikena bhāvena. tiryaggatau tiraścāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādisaṃyatāsaṃyatāntānāṃ sāmānyavat. manuṣyagatau manuṣyāṇāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādyayogakevalyantānāṃ sāmānyavat. devagatau devānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyantānāṃ sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 134. Specifically, by way of the exposition of states of existence (<s>gati</s>): in the hellish state, in the first earth, for hell-beings from those with wrong faith through the unrestrained right-believer, it is as in the general [rule]. In the second through seventh earths, for those with wrong faith, <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭi</s>, and <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>, it is as in the general [rule]. For the unrestrained right-believer, the state is either <s>aupaśamika</s> or <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s>. The unrestrained [quality] is further due to the <s>audayika</s> state.

children.text: § 135. indriyānuvādena ekendriyavikalendriyāṇām audayiko bhāvaḥ. pañcendriyeṣu mithyādṛṣṭyādyayogakevalyantānāṃ sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 135. By way of the exposition of sense-organs: for one-sensed and undeveloped-sensed beings, the state is <s>audayika</s>. Among five-sensed beings, for those from wrong faith through <s>ayoga-kevalin</s>, it is as in the general [rule].

children.text: § 136. kāyānuvādena sthāvarakāyikānām audayiko bhāvaḥ. trasakāyikānāṃ sāmānyam eva.
children.translated_text: § 136. By way of the exposition of body-types: for stationary-bodied beings (<s>sthāvarakāyika</s>), the state is <s>audayika</s>. For mobile-bodied beings (<s>trasakāyika</s>), it is as in the general [rule].

children.text: § 137. yogānuvādena kāyavāṅmanasayogināṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādisayogakevalyantānāṃ ca sāmānyam eva.
children.translated_text: § 137. By way of the exposition of <s>yoga</s> (activity): for those with bodily, verbal, and mental <s>yoga</s>, and for those from wrong faith through <s>sayoga-kevalin</s>, it is as in the general [rule].

children.text: § 138. vedānuvādena strīpunnapuṃsakavedānāṃ avedānāṃ ca sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 138. By way of the exposition of gender (<s>veda</s>): for those with female, male, and neuter gender, and for those without gender, it is as in the general [rule].

children.text: § 139. kaṣāyānuvādena krodhamānamāyālobhakaṣāyāṇām akaṣāyāṇāṃ ca sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 139. By way of the exposition of passions (<s>kaṣāya</s>): for those with the four passions — anger, pride, deceit, and greed — and for those without passions, it is as in the general [rule].

children.text: § 140. jñānānuvādena matyajñāniśrutājñānivibhaṅgajñānināṃ matiśrutāvadhimanaḥparyayakevalajñānināṃ ca sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 140. By way of the exposition of knowledge: for those with wrong sensory knowledge (<s>matyajñāna</s>), wrong scriptural knowledge (<s>śrutājñāna</s>), and wrong clairvoyance (<s>vibhaṅgajñāna</s>); and for those with [correct] sensory, scriptural, clairvoyant, mind-reading, and omniscient knowledge — it is as in the general [rule].

children.text: § 141 saṃyamānuvādena sarveṣāṃ saṃyatānāṃ saṃyatāsaṃyatānāṃ ca sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 141. By way of the exposition of restraint: for all the restrained, and for the partially restrained, it is as in the general [rule].

children.text: § 142. darśanānuvādena cakṣurdarśanācakṣurdarśanāvadhidarśanakevaladarśanināṃ sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 142. By way of the exposition of perception: for those with ocular, non-ocular, clairvoyant, and omniscient perception, it is as in the general [rule].

children.text: § 143. leśyānuvādena ṣaḍleśyāleśyānāṃ ca sāmanyavat.
children.translated_text: § 143. By way of the exposition of <s>leśyā</s> (soul-coloring): for those with the six <s>leśyās</s> and those without <s>leśyā</s>, it is as in the general [rule].

children.text: § 144. bhavyānuvādena bhavyānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādyayogakevalyantānāṃ sāmānyavat. abhavyānāṃ pāriṇāmiko bhāvaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 144. By way of the exposition of capacity: for the capable (<s>bhavya</s>), from those with wrong faith through <s>ayoga-kevalin</s>, it is as in the general [rule]. For the incapable (<s>abhavya</s>), the state is <s>pāriṇāmika</s> (transformational).

children.text: § 145. samyaktvānuvādena kṣāyikasamyagdṛṣṭiṣu asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭeḥ kṣāyiko bhāvaḥ. kṣāyikaṃ samyaktvam. asaṃyatatvam audayikena bhāvena. saṃyatāsaṃyatapramattāpramattasaṃyatānāṃ kṣāyopaśamiko bhāvaḥ. kṣāyikaṃ samyaktvam. caturṇām upaśamakānām aupaśamiko bhāvaḥ. kṣāyikaṃ samyaktvam. śeṣāṇāṃ sāmānyavat. kṣāyopaśamikasamyagdṛṣṭiṣu asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭeḥ kṣāyopaśamiko bhāvaḥ. kṣāyopaśamikaṃ samyaktvam. asaṃyataḥ punar audayikena bhāvena. saṃyatāsaṃyatapramattāpramattasaṃyatānāṃ kṣāyopaśamiko bhāvaḥ. kṣāyopaśamikaṃ samyaktvam. aupaśamikasamyagdṛṣṭiṣu asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭer aupaśamiko bhāvaḥ. aupaśamikaṃ samyaktvam. asaṃyataḥ punar audayikena bhāvena. saṃyatāsaṃyatapramattāpramattasaṃyatānāṃ kṣāyopaśamiko bhāvaḥ. aupaśamikaṃ samyaktvam. caturṇāṃ upaśamakānām aupaśamiko bhāvaḥ. aupaśamikaṃ samyaktvam. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭeḥ pāriṇāmiko bhāvaḥ. samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭeḥ kṣāyopaśmiko bhāvaḥ. mithyādṛṣṭer audayiko bhāvaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 145. By way of the exposition of right faith: among those with <s>kṣāyika</s> right faith — for the unrestrained right-believer, the state is <s>kṣāyika</s>: right faith is <s>kṣāyika</s>, while the unrestrained [quality] is due to the <s>audayika</s> state. For the partially restrained, restrained-with-negligence, and restrained-without-negligence, the state is <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s>, with <s>kṣāyika</s> right faith. For the four in the subsidence-ladder, the state is <s>aupaśamika</s>, with <s>kṣāyika</s> right faith. For the remaining [stages], it is as in the general [rule].

children.text: § 146. saṃjñānuvādena saṃjñināṃ sāmānyavat. asaṃjñinām audayiko bhāvaḥ. tadubhayavyapadeśarahitānāṃ sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 146. By way of the exposition of cognition-type: for the rational beings (<s>saṃjñin</s>), it is as in the general [rule]. For the non-rational (<s>asaṃjñin</s>), the state is <s>audayika</s>. For those designated as neither, it is as in the general [rule].

children.text: § 147. āhārānuvādena āhārakāṇām anāhārakāṇāṃ ca sāmānyavat. bhāvaḥ parisamāptaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 147. By way of the exposition of nourishment: for the nourishment-takers and the non-nourishing beings, it is as in the general [rule]. [The analysis of] <s>bhāva</s> (state) is completed.

children.text: § 148. alpabahutvam upavarṇyate. tad dvividhaṃ sāmānyena viśeṣeṇa ca. sāmānyena tāvat sarvataḥ stokāḥ traya upaśamakāḥ svaguṇasthānakāleṣu praveśena tulyasaṃkhyāḥ. upaśāntakaṣāyās tāvanta eva. trayaḥ kṣapakāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. kṣīṇakaṣāyavītarāgacchadmasthās tāvanta eva. sayogakevalino ’yogakevalinaś ca praveśena tulyasaṃkhyāḥ. sayogakevalinaḥ svakālena samuditāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. apramattasaṃyatāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. pramattasaṃyatāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. saṃyatāsaṃyatā asaṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. samyagmithyādṛṣṭayaḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. mithyādṛṣṭayo ’nantaguṇāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 148. <s>Alpabahutvam</s> (relative proportion) is now described. It is twofold: general and specific. In general terms: fewest of all are the three in the subsidence-ladder (<s>upaśamaka</s>), who are equal in number at the times of entry into their respective <s>guṇasthānas</s> (spiritual stages). The quiescence-of-passions (<s>upaśānta-kaṣāya</s>) souls are equally numerous. The three in the destruction-ladder (<s>kṣapaka</s>) are numerably more. The destroyed-passions (<s>kṣīṇa-kaṣāya</s>) and the passionless-non-omniscient (<s>vītarāga-chadmastha</s>) are equally numerous. The omniscient-with-activity (<s>sayoga-kevalin</s>) and omniscient-without-activity (<s>ayoga-kevalin</s>) [are counted next].

children.text: § 149. viśeṣeṇa gatyanuvādena narakagatau sarvāsu pṛthivīṣu nārakeṣu sarvataḥ stokāḥ sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ. samyagmithyādṛṣṭayaḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. mithyādṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. tiryaggatau tiraścāṃ sarvataḥ stokāḥ saṃyatāsaṃyatāḥ. itareṣāṃ sāmānyavat. manuṣyagatau manuṣyāṇām upaśamakādipramattasaṃyatāntānāṃ sāmānyavat. tataḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ saṃyatāsaṃyatāḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. samyagmithyādṛṣṭayaḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. mithyādṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. devagatau devānāṃ nārakavat.
children.translated_text: § 149. Specifically, by way of the exposition of states of existence: in the hellish state, in all earths, among hell-beings, fewest of all are the <s>sāsādana-samyagdṛṣṭis</s> (downfall-right-believers). The <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s> (mixed-faith) are numerably more. The unrestrained right-believers are innumerably more. Those with wrong faith are innumerably more [still]. In the animal state, among animals, fewest of all are the partially restrained. For the rest, it is as in the general [rule]. In the human state, [continues similarly].

children.text: § 150. indriyānuvādena ekendriyavikalendriyeṣu guṇasthānabhedo nāstīty alpabahutvābhāvaḥ. pañcendriyāṇāṃ sāmānyavat. ayaṃ tu viśeṣaḥ mithyādṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 150. By the thread of sense-organs (<s>indriya</s>): among one-sensed and incomplete-sensed beings, there is no distinction of <s>guṇasthānas</s> (spiritual stages), hence there is no few-and-many comparison. For five-sensed beings, [it is] as stated generally. But this is the distinction: the <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> (wrong believers) are innumerably many times [more].

children.text: § 151. kāyānuvādena sthāvarakāyeṣu guṇasthānabhedābhāvād alpabhahutvābhāvaḥ. traskāyikānāṃ pañcendriyavat.
children.translated_text: § 151. By the thread of body-type (<s>kāya</s>): among immobile-bodied beings (<s>sthāvarakāya</s>), since there is no distinction of <s>guṇasthānas</s>, there is no few-and-many comparison. For mobile beings (<s>trasakāyika</s>), [it is] as for five-sensed beings.

children.text: § 152. yogānuvādena vāṅmanasayogināṃ pañcendriyavat. kāyayogināṃ sāmānyavat. vedānuvādena strīpuṃvedānāṃ pañcendriyavat. napuṃsakavedānāṃ avedānāṃ ca sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 152. By the thread of activity (<s>yoga</s>): for speech-active (<s>vāgyogin</s>) and mind-active (<s>manoyogin</s>) beings, [it is] as for five-sensed beings. For body-active (<s>kāyayogin</s>) beings, [it is] as stated generally. By the thread of sex-determination (<s>veda</s>): for those with feminine and masculine sex-determination, [it is] as for five-sensed beings. For those with neuter sex-determination and those without sex-determination, [it is] as stated generally.

children.text: § 153. kaṣāyānuvādena krodhamānamāyākaṣāyāṇāṃ puṃvedavat. ayaṃ tu viśeṣaḥ mithyādṛṣṭayo ’nantaguṇāḥ. lobhakaṣāyāṇāṃ dvayor upaśamakayos tulyā saṃkhyā. kṣapakāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. sūkṣmasāṃparāyaśuddhyupaśamakasaṃyatā viśeṣādhikāḥ. sūkṣmasāṃparāyakṣapakāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. śeṣāṇām sāmānyavat.
children.translated_text: § 153. By the thread of passions (<s>kaṣāya</s>): for the passions of anger (<s>krodha</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), and deceit (<s>māyā</s>), [it is] as for those with masculine sex-determination. But this is the distinction: the <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are infinitely many times [more]. For the passion of greed (<s>lobha</s>): the two subsiders (<s>upaśamaka</s>) are equal in number; the destroyers (<s>kṣapaka</s>) are numerably many times [more]; those with <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāyaśuddhi</s> (subtle-passion pure) subsidence-restraint are slightly more; the <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāya</s> destroyers are numerably many times [more]. For the rest, [it is] as stated generally.

children.text: § 154. jñānānuvādena matyajñāniśrutājñāniṣu sarvataḥ stokāḥ sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ. mithyādṛṣṭayo ’nantaguṇāḥ. vibhaṅgajñāniṣu sarvataḥ stokāḥ sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ. mithyādṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. matiśrutāvadhijñāniṣu sarvataḥ stokāś catvāra upaśamakāś catvāraḥ kṣapakāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. apramattasaṃyatāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. pramattasaṃyatāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. saṃyatāsaṃyatāḥ asaṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ asaṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. manaḥparyayajñāniṣu sarvataḥ stokāś catvāra upaśamakāḥ. catvāraḥ kṣapakāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. apramattasaṃyatāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. pramattasaṃyatāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. kevalajñāniṣu ayogakevalibhyaḥ sayogakevalinaḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 154. By the thread of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>): among those with wrong sensory knowledge (<s>matyajñāna</s>) and wrong scriptural knowledge (<s>śrutājñāna</s>), fewest of all are the <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭis</s>; the <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are infinitely many times [more]. Among those with clairvoyance (<s>vibhaṅgajñāna</s>), fewest of all are the <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭis</s>; the <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are innumerably many times [more]. Among those with sensory, scriptural, and clairvoyant knowledge (<s>matiśrutāvadhijñāna</s>), fewest of all are the four subsiders and four destroyers, [who are] numerably many times [more]; the <s>apramattasaṃyatas</s> are numerably many times [more]; the <s>pramattasaṃyatas</s> are numerably many times [more]; the <s>saṃyatāsaṃyatas</s> (partially restrained) are innumerably many times [more]; the <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭis</s> are innumerably many times [more]. Among those with telepathic knowledge (<s>manaḥparyayajñāna</s>), fewest of all are the four subsiders; the four destroyers are numerably many times [more]; the <s>apramattasaṃyatas</s> are numerably many times [more]; the <s>pramattasaṃyatas</s> are numerably many times [more]. Among the omniscient (<s>kevalajñāna</s>), the <s>sayogakevalīs</s> are numerably many times more than the <s>ayogakevalīs</s>.

children.text: § 155. saṃyamānuvādena sāmāyikacchedopasthāpanāśuddhisaṃyateṣu dvayor upaśamakayos tulyā saṃkhyā. tataḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇau kṣapakau. apramattāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. pramattāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. parihāraśuddhisaṃyateṣu apramattebhyaḥ pramattāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. sūkṣmasaṃparāyaśuddhisaṃyateṣu upaśamakebhyaḥ kṣapakāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. yathākhyātavihāraśuddhisaṃyateṣu upaśāntakaṣāyebhyaḥ kṣīṇakaṣāyāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. ayogakevalinas tāvanta eva. sayogakevalinaḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. saṃyatāsaṃyatānāṃ nāsty alpabahutvam. asaṃyateṣu sarvataḥ stokāḥ sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ. samyaṅmityādṛṣṭayaḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭayayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. mityādṛṣṭayo ’nantaguṇāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 155. By the thread of self-restraint (<s>saṃyama</s>): among those with <s>sāmāyika</s>, <s>chedopasthāpana</s>, and <s>śuddhi</s> self-restraint, the two subsiders are equal in number; the two destroyers are numerably many times [more]; the <s>apramattas</s> are numerably many times [more]; the <s>pramattas</s> are numerably many times [more]. Among those with <s>parihāraśuddhi</s> self-restraint, the <s>pramattas</s> are numerably many times more than the <s>apramattas</s>. Among those with <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāyaśuddhi</s> self-restraint, the destroyers are numerably many times more than the subsiders. Among those with <s>yathākhyātavihāraśuddhi</s> self-restraint, the <s>kṣīṇakaṣāyas</s> are numerably many times more than the <s>upaśāntakaṣāyas</s>; the <s>ayogakevalīs</s> are exactly that many; the <s>sayogakevalīs</s> are numerably many times [more]. For the partially restrained (<s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>), there is no few-and-many comparison. Among the unrestrained (<s>asaṃyata</s>), fewest of all are the <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭis</s>; the <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s> are numerably many times [more]; the <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭis</s> are innumerably many times [more]; the <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are infinitely many times [more].

children.text: § 156. darśanānuvādena cakṣurdarśanināṃ manoyogivat. acakṣurdarśanināṃ kāyayogivat. avadhidarśaninām avadhijñānivat. kevaladarśanināṃ kevalajñānivat.
children.translated_text: § 156. By the thread of perception (<s>darśana</s>): for those with ocular perception (<s>cakṣurdarśana</s>), [it is] as for mind-active beings. For those with non-ocular perception (<s>acakṣurdarśana</s>), [it is] as for body-active beings. For those with clairvoyant perception (<s>avadhidarśana</s>), [it is] as for those with clairvoyant knowledge. For those with omniscient perception (<s>kevaladarśana</s>), [it is] as for those with omniscient knowledge.

children.text: § 157. leśyānuvādena kṛṣṇalīlakāpotaleśyānāṃ asaṃyatavat. tejaḥpadmaleśyānāṃ sarvataḥ stokā apramattāḥ. pramattāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. evam itareṣāṃ pañcendriyavat. śuklaleśyānāṃ sarvaḥ stokā upaśamakāḥ. kṣapakāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. sayogakevalinaḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. apramattasaṃyatāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. pramattasaṃyatāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. saṃyatāsaṃyatā asaṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. samyagmithyādṛṣṭayaḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. mithyādṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭayaḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 157. By the thread of coloring (<s>leśyā</s>): for those with black (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>), blue (<s>nīla</s>), and grey (<s>kāpota</s>) colorings, [it is] as for the unrestrained. For those with fiery (<s>tejas</s>) and lotus (<s>padma</s>) colorings, fewest of all are the <s>apramattas</s>; the <s>pramattas</s> are numerably many times [more]; for the rest, [it is] as for five-sensed beings. For those with white (<s>śukla</s>) coloring, fewest of all are the subsiders; the destroyers are numerably many times [more]; the <s>sayogakevalīs</s> are numerably many times [more]; the <s>apramattasaṃyatas</s> are numerably many times [more]; the <s>pramattasaṃyatas</s> are numerably many times [more]; the <s>saṃyatāsaṃyatas</s> are innumerably many times [more]; the <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭis</s> are innumerably many times [more]; the <s>samyaṅmithyādṛṣṭis</s> are numerably many times [more]; the <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are innumerably many times [more]; the <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭis</s> are numerably many times [more].

children.text: § 158. bhavyānuvādena bhavyānāṃ sāmānyavat. abhavyānāṃ nāsty alpabahutvam.
children.translated_text: § 158. By the thread of capacity for liberation (<s>bhavya</s>): for the capable (<s>bhavya</s>), [it is] as stated generally. For the incapable (<s>abhavya</s>), there is no few-and-many comparison.

children.text: § 159. samyaktvānuvādena kṣhāyikasamyagdṛṣṭiṣu sarvataḥ stokāś catvāra upaśamakāḥ. itareṣāṃ pramattāntānāṃ sāmānyavat. tataḥ saṃyatāsaṃyatāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. kṣāyopaśamikasamyagdṛṣṭiṣu sarvataḥ stokā apramattā. pramattāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. saṃyatāsaṃyatāḥ asaṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. aupaśamikasamyagdṛṣṭīnāṃ sarvataḥ stokāś catvāra upaśamakāḥ. apramattāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. pramattāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. saṃyatāsaṃyatāḥ asaṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. śeṣāṇāṃ nāsty alpabahutvam.
children.translated_text: § 159. By the thread of right faith (<s>samyaktva</s>): among those with destructive right faith (<s>kṣāyikasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>), fewest of all are the four subsiders; for the rest up to <s>pramatta</s>, [it is] as stated generally; then the <s>saṃyatāsaṃyatas</s> are numerably many times [more]; the <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭis</s> are innumerably many times [more]. Among those with destructive-subsidential right faith (<s>kṣāyopaśamika</s>), fewest of all are the <s>apramattas</s>; the <s>pramattas</s> are numerably many times [more]; the <s>saṃyatāsaṃyatas</s> are innumerably many times [more]; the <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭis</s> are innumerably many times [more]. Among those with subsidential right faith (<s>aupaśamika</s>), fewest of all are the four subsiders; the <s>apramattas</s> are numerably many times [more]; the <s>pramattas</s> are numerably many times [more]; the <s>saṃyatāsaṃyatas</s> are innumerably many times [more]; the <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭis</s> are innumerably many times [more]. For the rest, there is no few-and-many comparison.

children.text: § 160. saṃjñānuvādena saṃjñināṃ cakurdarśanivat. asaṃjñināṃ nāsty apabahutvam. tadubhayavyapadeśarahitānāṃ kevalajñānivat.
children.translated_text: § 160. By the thread of rationality (<s>saṃjñā</s>): for the rational (<s>saṃjñin</s>), [it is] as for those with ocular perception. For the irrational (<s>asaṃjñin</s>), there is no few-and-many comparison. For those beyond both designations, [it is] as for the omniscient.

children.text: § 161. āhārānuvādena āhārakāṇāṃ kāyayogivat. anāhārakāṇāṃ sarvataḥ stokāḥ sayogakevalinaḥ. ayogakevalinaḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭayo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. mithyādṛṣṭyo ’nantaguṇāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 161. By the thread of nourishment (<s>āhāra</s>): for those who take nourishment, [it is] as for body-active beings. Among those without nourishment, fewest of all are the <s>sayogakevalīs</s>; the <s>ayogakevalīs</s> are numerably many times [more]; the <s>sāsādanasamyagdṛṣṭis</s> are innumerably many times [more]; the <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭis</s> are innumerably many times [more]; the <s>mithyādṛṣṭis</s> are infinitely many times [more].

children.text: § 162. evaṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādīnāṃ gatyādiṣu mārgaṇā kṛtā sāmānyena. tatra sūkṣmabheda āgamāvirodhenānusartavyaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 162. Thus the investigation through the stations of inquiry beginning with destiny has been made for those with wrong faith etc. generally. Therein, the subtle distinctions should be pursued in accordance with scripture (<s>āgama</s>).

children.text: TAS 1.8 commentary §§ 33–162
§ 163. evaṃ samyagdarśanasyādāv uddiṣṭasya lakṣaṇotpattisvāmiviṣayanyāsādhigamopāyā nirdiṣṭāḥ. tatsaṃbandhena ca jīvādīnāṃ saṃjñāparimāṇādi nirdiṣṭam. tadantaraṃ samyagjñānaṃ vicārārham ity āha —
children.translated_text: § 163. Thus, for right faith (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), which was mentioned first, the definition, origin, possessor, scope, placement, and means of attainment have been specified. And in connection with it, the designation, measure, etc. of <s>jīva</s> and the rest have been specified. After that, right knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) is to be examined—thus he says—

children.text: matiśrutāvadhimanaḥparyayakevalāni jñānam ||
children.translated_text: Sensory knowledge (<s>mati</s>), scriptural knowledge (<s>śruta</s>), clairvoyant knowledge (<s>avadhi</s>), telepathic knowledge (<s>manaḥparyaya</s>), and omniscient knowledge (<s>kevala</s>)—these are knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). ||

children.text: § 164. jñānaśabdaḥ pratyekaṃ parisamāpyate. matijñānaṃ śrutajñānaṃ avadhijñānaṃ manaḥparyayajñānaṃ kevalajñānam iti. indriyair manasā ca yathā svam artho manyate anayā manute mananamātraṃ vā matiḥ. tadāvaraṇakarmakṣayopaśame sati nirūpyamāṇaṃ śrūyate anena tat śṛṇoti śravaṇamātraṃ vā śrutam. anayoḥ pratyāsannanirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvāt. tathā ca vakṣyate
śrutaṃ matipūrvam
children.translated_text: 'Scriptural knowledge (<s>śruta</s>) is preceded by sensory knowledge (<s>mati</s>).'

children.text: iti. avāgdhānād avacchinnaviṣayād vā avadhiḥ. parakīyamanogato ’rtho mana ity ucyate. sāhacaryāt tasya paryayaṇaṃ parigamanaṃ manaḥparyayaḥ. matijñānaprasaṅga iti cet; na; apekṣāmātratvāt. kṣayopaśamaśaktimātravijṛmbhitaṃ hi tatkevalaṃ svaparamanobhir vyapadiśyate. yathā abhre candramasaṃ paśyeti. bāhyenābhyantareṇa ca tapasā yadartham arthino mārgaṃ kevante sevante tatkevalam. asahāyam iti vā. tadante prāpyate iti ante kriyate. tasya pratyāsannatvāt tatsamīpe manaḥparyayagrahaṇam. kutaḥ pratyāsattiḥ. saṃyamaikādhikaraṇatvāt. tasya avadhir viprakṛṣṭaḥ. kutaḥ viprakṛṣṭāntaratvāt. pratyakṣāt parokṣaṃ pūrvam uktaṃ sugamatvāt. śrutaparicitānubhūtā hi matiśrutapaddhatiḥ sarveṇa prānigaṇena prāyaḥ prāpyate yataḥ. evam etat pañcavidhaṃ jñānam. tadbhedādayaś ca purastād vakṣyante.
children.translated_text: <s>Avadhi</s> (clairvoyance) is [so called] from limitation (<s>avāgdhāna</s>), or from having a delimited range. The content of another's mind is called <s>manas</s>; <s>manaḥparyaya</s> is the traversal, the comprehension, of that—by association [of proximity]. [Objection:] Would this not fall under sensory knowledge? No, because it involves merely a dependence [on the mind, not direct engagement]. For that [telepathic knowledge], produced by the mere power of subsidence-cum-destruction [of karma], is designated by one's own and another's mind [metaphorically]—just as [one says] 'he sees the moon through the clouds.' <s>Kevala</s> (omniscient knowledge) is that for the sake of whose object seekers pursue the path through external and internal austerities (<s>tapas</s>); or it is 'without companion' (i.e., independent). [Telepathic knowledge is] attained at its end; hence <s>manaḥparyaya</s> is placed near it because of its proximity [to omniscience]. Why the proximity? Because both share the same locus of self-restraint. <s>Avadhi</s> (clairvoyance) is [placed] farther away. Why? Because it is at a farther interval. Indirect knowledge (<s>parokṣa</s>) is stated before direct knowledge (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) because of its accessibility—for the path of sensory and scriptural knowledge, being familiar through study and experience, is generally attained by all living beings. Thus, this knowledge is fivefold. Its subdivisions etc. will be stated later.

§ 164. The word '<s>jñāna</s>' (knowledge) applies to each separately: sensory knowledge (<s>matijñāna</s>), scriptural knowledge (<s>śrutajñāna</s>), clairvoyant knowledge (<s>avadhijñāna</s>), telepathic knowledge (<s>manaḥparyayajñāna</s>), omniscient knowledge (<s>kevalajñāna</s>). <s>Mati</s> is that by which, through the senses and mind, an object is cognized as its own; or that by which one cognizes; or mere cognition. <s>Śruta</s> (scriptural knowledge) is that which, when the <s>karma</s> obstructing it is subsided or destroyed, is ascertained through hearing; or that through which one hears; or mere hearing. The mention of these two in proximity to each other is because they stand in the relation of effect and cause. As will be stated:

children.text: pramāṇanayair adhigamaḥ
children.translated_text: Comprehension (<s>adhigama</s>) is through valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) and standpoints (<s>naya</s>).

children.text: ity uktam. pramāṇaṃ ca keṣāṃcit jñānam abhimatam. keṣaṃcit saṃnikarṣaḥ keṣāṃcid indriyam iti. ato ’dhikṛtānāṃ eva matyādīnāṃ pramāṇatvakhyāpanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: This has been stated. And valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is regarded by some as knowledge itself, by some as contact (<s>saṃnikarṣa</s>), and by some as the sense-organ (<s>indriya</s>). Therefore, in order to proclaim that the very [five types of knowledge] under discussion—sensory knowledge etc.—are themselves the valid means of knowledge, he says—

children.text: tatpramāṇe ||
children.translated_text: Those [five types of knowledge] are the [two] valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). ||

children.text: § 166. tadvacanaṃ kim artham. pramāṇāntaraparikalpanānivṛttyartham. saṃnikarṣaḥ pramāṇam indriyaṃ pramāṇam iti kecit kalpayanti tannivṛttyarthaṃ tadity ucyate. tadeva matyādi pramāṇaṃ nānyad iti.
children.translated_text: § 166. What is the purpose of the word 'those' (<s>tad</s>)? For the purpose of preventing the fabrication of other valid means of knowledge. Since some fabricate 'contact is the valid means' or 'the sense-organ is the valid means,' to prevent that, 'those' is said—meaning: sensory knowledge etc. alone are valid means of knowledge, not anything else.

children.text: § 167. atha saṃnikarṣe pramāṇe sati indriye vā ko doṣaḥ? yadi saṃnikarṣaḥ pramāṇaṃ, sūkṣmavyavahitaviprakṛṣṭānām arthānām agrahaṇaprasaṅgaḥ. na hi te indriyaiḥ saṃnikṛṣyante. ataḥ sarvajñatvābhāvaḥ syāt. indriyam api yadi pramāṇaṃ sa eva doṣaḥ; alpaviṣayatvāt cakṣurādīnāṃ jñeyasya cāparimāṇatvāt.
children.translated_text: § 167. Now, what is the fault if contact (<s>saṃnikarṣa</s>) is the valid means, or if the sense-organ is? If contact is the valid means, then the consequence would be the non-apprehension of subtle, concealed, and remote objects, for they are not brought into contact with the sense-organs. Hence there would be an absence of omniscience. If the sense-organ is the valid means, the same fault [applies], since the eye etc. have limited range, while the objects of knowledge are unlimited.

children.text: § 168. sarvendriyasaṃnikarṣābhāvaś ca; cakṣurmanasoḥ prāpyakāritvābhāvāt. aprāpyakāritvaṃ ca uttaratra vakṣyate.
children.translated_text: § 168. And there is an absence of contact with all sense-organs—because the eye and mind do not operate through contact (<s>prāpyakāritva</s>). And the non-contact operation will be stated later.

children.text: § 169. yadi jñānaṃ pramāṇaṃ phalābhāvaḥ. adhigamo hi phalam iṣṭaṃ na bhāvāntaram. sa cet pramāṇaṃ, na tasyānyat phalaṃ bhavitum arhati. phalavatā ca pramāṇena bhavitavyam. saṃnikarṣe indriye vā pramāṇe sati adhigamaḥ phalam arthāntarabhūtaṃ yujyate iti. tad ayuktam. yadi saṃnikarṣaḥ pramāṇam arthādhigamaḥ phalaṃ, tasya dviṣṭhatvāt tatphalenādhigamenāpi dviṣṭhena bhavitavyam iti arthādīnām apy adhigamaḥ prāpnoti. ātmanaś cetanatvāt tatraiva samavāya iti cet. na; jñasvabhāvābhāve sarveṣām acetanatvāt. jñasvabhāvābhyupagame vā ātmanaḥ svamatavirodhaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: § 169. If knowledge is the valid means, [then objection:] there would be no result (<s>phala</s>). For comprehension (<s>adhigama</s>) is the desired result, not some separate entity. If that [comprehension] is itself the valid means, it cannot have any other result. And a valid means must have a result. When contact or the sense-organ is the valid means, then comprehension as a separate entity serving as the result is appropriate. [Reply:] That is unjust. If contact is the valid means and the comprehension of objects is the result, since contact resides in two [loci, the object and the knower], then its result, comprehension, would also have to reside in two loci—and hence even objects etc. would have comprehension [which is absurd]. [Objection:] Since the self has consciousness, [comprehension] would reside in the self alone through inherence? [Reply:] No—because in the absence of a knowing nature, all [selves] would be insentient. Or if one accepts the self's knowing nature, it would contradict one's own doctrine.

children.text: § 170. nanu coktaṃ jñāne pramāṇe sati phalābhāva iti. naiṣaḥ doṣaḥ; arthādhigame prītidarśanāt. jñasvabhāvasyātmanaḥ karmamalīmasasya karaṇālambanād arthaniścaye prītir ūpajāyate. sā phalam ity ucyate. upekṣā ajñānanāśo vā phalam. rāgadveṣayor apraṇidhānam upekṣā. andhakārakalpājñānanāśo vā phalam ity ucyate.
children.translated_text: § 170. [Objection:] But it was said that if knowledge is the valid means, there is no result. [Reply:] This is no fault, because satisfaction (<s>prīti</s>) is observed upon the comprehension of objects. For the self, whose nature is knowing but which is tainted by the impurity of <s>karma</s>, satisfaction arises upon ascertainment of objects through instruments and supports. That is called the result. Or equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) is the result, or the destruction of ignorance is the result. Equanimity is the non-engagement of attachment and aversion. Or the destruction of ignorance, which is like darkness, is called the result.

children.text: § 171. pramiṇoti pramīyate ’nena pramitimātraṃ vā pramāṇam. kim anena pramīyate. jīvādir arthaḥ. yadi jīvāder adhigame pramāṇaṃ pramāṇādhigame ca anyat pramāṇaṃ parikalpayItavyam. tathā saty anavasthā. nānavasthā pradīpavat. yathā ghaṭādīnāṃ prakāśane pradīpo hetuḥ svasvarūpaprakāśane ’pi sa eva, na prakāśāntaraṃ mṛgyaṃ tathā pramāṇam apīti avaśyaṃ caitad abhyupagantavyam. prameyavat pramāṇasya pramāṇāntaraparikalpanāyāṃ svādhigamābhāvāt smṛtyabhāvaḥ. tadabhāvād vyavahāralopaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: § 171. That by which one measures, or through which something is measured, or mere measurement—that is <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge). What is measured by it? Objects beginning with <s>jīva</s> (soul). [Objection:] If a [further] valid means is fabricated for the comprehension of the valid means [itself], then there would be infinite regress. [Reply:] There is no infinite regress—like a lamp. Just as a lamp is the cause of illuminating pots etc. and is also [the cause] of illuminating its own form—no other illumination need be sought—so too with the valid means; this must certainly be accepted. If, like the object of knowledge, another valid means is fabricated for the valid means, since [the valid means] would not be known [by itself], there would be no memory [of it]; and from that absence, conventional practice would cease.

children.text: § 172. vakṣyamānabhedāpekṣayā dvivacananirdeśaḥ. vakṣyate hi
ādye parokṣam, pratyakṣam anyad
children.translated_text: 'The first [two types] are indirect (<s>parokṣa</s>), the others are direct (<s>pratyakṣa</s>).'

children.text: iti sa ca dvivacananirdeśaḥ pramāṇāntarasaṃkhyānivṛttyarthaḥ.
children.translated_text: And that dual-number expression is for the purpose of preventing the enumeration of other valid means.
§ 172. The dual-number expression is with reference to the divisions that will be stated. For it will be said:

children.text: § 173. uktasya pañcavidhasya jñānasya pramāṇadvayāntaḥpātitve pratipādite pratyakṣānumānādipramāṇadvayakalpanānivṛttyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 173. Having established that the stated fivefold knowledge falls within the two valid means, in order to prevent the fabrication of [separate] valid means such as direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and inference (<s>anumāna</s>), he says—

children.text: ādye parokṣam ||
children.translated_text: The first [two types] are indirect (<s>parokṣa</s>). ||

children.text: § 174. ādiśabdaḥ prāthamyavacana. ādau bhavam ādyam. kathaṃ dvayoḥ prathamatvam? mukhyopacārakalpanayā. matijñānaṃ tāvan mukhyakalpanayā prathamam. śrutam api tasya pratyāsattyā prathamam ity upacaryate. dvivacananirdeśasāmarthyād gauṇasyāpi grahaṇam. ādyaṃ ca ādyaṃ ca ādye matiśrute ity arthaḥ. tadubhayam api parokṣaṃ pramāṇam ity abhisaṃbadhyate. kuto ’sya parokṣatvam. parāyattatatvāt
matijñānaṃ indriyānindriyanimittam
children.translated_text: <s>Mati-jñāna</s> (sensory knowledge) is caused by sense organs and the non-sense-organ [i.e., mind]

children.text: iti vakṣyate
children.translated_text: — thus it will be stated [later].

children.text: śrutam anindriyasya
children.translated_text: <s>Śruta</s> (scriptural knowledge) belongs to the non-sense-organ [i.e., mind]

children.text: iti ca. ataḥ parāṇīndriyāṇi manaś ca prakāśopadeśādi ca bāhyanimittaṃ pratītya tadāvaraṇakarmakṣayopaśamāpekṣasyātmano matiśrutam utpadyamānaṃ parokṣam ity ākhyāyate. ata upamānāgamādīnām atraivāntarbhāvaḥ.
children.translated_text: — thus also [it will be stated]. Therefore, depending on the external causes — the other sense organs (<s>indriya</s>), the mind (<s>manas</s>), and light, instruction, and the like as external conditions — <s>mati</s> (sensory knowledge) and <s>śruta</s> (scriptural knowledge), arising for the self whose dependence is on the subsidence and destruction of their respective obscuring <s>karmas</s>, are called <s>parokṣa</s> (indirect knowledge). Hence, analogy (<s>upamāna</s>), scripture (<s>āgama</s>), and the like are subsumed here.

§ 174. The word '<s>ādi</s>' (first) denotes priority. That which exists at the beginning is '<s>ādya</s>' (first). How can two [types] both be first? Through the distinction of primary and figurative designation. Sensory knowledge (<s>matijñāna</s>) is first by primary designation. Scriptural knowledge (<s>śruta</s>) too is figuratively called first due to its proximity to [sensory knowledge]. By the force of the dual-number expression, the secondary [type] is also included. '<s>Ādya</s>' and '<s>ādya</s>' [together form the dual] '<s>ādye</s>'—meaning <s>mati</s> and <s>śruta</s>. Both of these are to be connected as indirect (<s>parokṣa</s>) valid means of knowledge. Why is this indirect? Because it depends on others (<s>parāyattatva</s>).

children.text: § 175. abhihitalakṣaṇāt parokṣād itarasya sarvasya pratyakṣatvapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 175. In order to establish the <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct) nature of everything other than the <s>parokṣa</s> (indirect knowledge) whose definition has been stated, he says —

children.text: pratyakṣam anyat ||
children.translated_text: The other [knowledge] is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct). ||

children.text: § 176. akṣṇoti vyāpnoti jānātīty akṣa ātmā. tam eva prāptakṣayopaśamaṃ prakṣīṇāvaraṇaṃ vā pratiniyataṃ pratyakṣam. avadhidarśanaṃ kevaladarśanam api akṣam eva pratiniyatam atas tasyāpi grahaṇaṃ prāpnoti. naiṣa doṣaḥ; jñānam ity anuvartate, tena darśanasya vyudāsah. evam api vibhaṅgajñānam akṣam eva pratiniyatam ato ’syāpi grahaṇaṃ prāpnoti. samyagity adhikārāt tannivṛttiḥ. samyagity anuvartate tena jñānaṃ viśiṣyate tato vibhaṅgajñānasya nivṛttiḥ kṛtā. tad dhi mithyādarśanodayād viparītārthaviṣayam iti na samyak.
children.translated_text: § 176. '<s>Akṣa</s>' [means] the self, because it pervades (<s>akṣṇoti</s>), encompasses, and knows. That [knowledge] which pertains exclusively to that [self] which has attained the subsidence-and-destruction [of karmic obstruction] or whose obscuration has been completely destroyed, is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct). [Objection:] <s>Avadhidarśana</s> (clairvoyant perception) and <s>kevaladarśana</s> (absolute perception) also pertain exclusively to the <s>akṣa</s> (self); therefore, their inclusion [in pratyakṣa] would follow. [Reply:] This is no fault; the word '<s>jñāna</s>' (knowledge) carries over [from the earlier context], thereby excluding <s>darśana</s> (perception). [Objection:] Even so, <s>vibhaṅga-jñāna</s> (deceptive knowledge) also pertains exclusively to the <s>akṣa</s>; therefore, its inclusion would follow. [Reply:] Its exclusion [follows] from the governing topic of '<s>samyak</s>' (right). The word '<s>samyak</s>' carries over, thereby qualifying the knowledge; thus the exclusion of <s>vibhaṅga-jñāna</s> is accomplished. For that [deceptive knowledge], having objects that are the reverse [of reality] due to the arising of wrong faith (<s>mithyādarśana</s>), is not right (<s>samyak</s>).

children.text: § 177. syān matam indriyavyāpārajanitaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣaṃ vyatītendriyaviṣayavyāpāraṃ parokṣam ity etad avisaṃvādi lakṣaṇam abhyupagantavyam iti. tad ayuktam, āptasya pratyakṣajñānābhāvaprasaṅgāt yadi indriyanimittam eva jñānaṃ pratyakṣam iṣyate evaṃ sati āptasya pratyakṣajñānaṃ na syāt. na hi tasyendriyapūrvo ’rthādhigamaḥ. atha tasyāpi karaṇapūrvakam eva jñānaṃ kalpyate, tasyāsarvajñatvaṃ syāt. tasya mānasaṃ pratyakṣam iti cet; manaḥpraṇidhānapūrvakatvāt jñānasya sarvajñatvābhāva eva. āgamatas tatsiddhir iti cet. na; tasya pratyakṣajñānapūrvakatvāt.
children.translated_text: § 177. [Objection:] It may be held that knowledge generated by the operation of the sense organs is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct), and that which transcends the operation of the sense organs regarding objects is <s>parokṣa</s> (indirect) — this non-contradictory definition should be accepted. [Reply:] That is improper, because it would entail the absence of direct knowledge for the <s>āpta</s> (omniscient authority). If only knowledge caused by sense organs is accepted as <s>pratyakṣa</s>, then the <s>āpta</s> would have no direct knowledge, for his cognition of objects is not preceded by sense organs. If even for him knowledge preceded by instruments is postulated, then he would not be omniscient. [Objection:] His [knowledge] is mental <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception). [Reply:] Since knowledge would be preceded by mental application, omniscience would indeed be absent. [Objection:] Its establishment [comes] from scripture (<s>āgama</s>). [Reply:] No, because that [scripture] itself must be preceded by direct knowledge.

children.text: § 178. yogipratyakṣam anyaj jñānaṃ divyam apy astīti cet. na tasya pratyakṣatvaṃ; indriyanimittatvābhāvāt; akṣam akṣaṃ prati yad vartate tat pratyakṣam ity abhyupagamāt.
children.translated_text: § 178. [Objection:] There is another knowledge — <s>yogi-pratyakṣa</s> (yogic direct perception) — which is even divine. [Reply:] That does not have the nature of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception), because of the absence of sense-organ causation — given the acceptance that what operates toward each <s>akṣa</s> (sense organ) is <s>pratyakṣa</s>.

children.text: § 179. kiṃ ca sarvajñatvābhāvaḥ pratijñāhānir vā. asya yogino yaj jñānaṃ tat pratyarthavaśavarti vā syād anekārthagrāhi vā. yadi pratyarthavaśavarti, sarvajñatvam asya nāsti yoginaḥ, jñeyasyānantyāt. athānekārthagrāhi, yā pratijñā —
vijānāti na vijñānam ekam arthadvayaṃ yathā |
children.translated_text: 'A cognition does not know two objects,

children.text: ekam arthaṃ vijānāti na vijñānadvayam tathā |
children.translated_text: just as two cognitions do not know one object' —

children.text: sā hīyate.
children.translated_text: that [thesis] is contradicted.

§ 179. Moreover, either omniscience is absent, or the thesis is contradicted. The knowledge of this yogin is either confined to one object at a time, or grasps multiple objects. If it is confined to one object at a time, then this yogin does not have omniscience, due to the infinity of knowable objects. If it grasps multiple objects, then the thesis —

children.text: § 180. athavā
kṣaṇikāḥ sarvasaṃskārāḥ
children.translated_text: 'All conditioned things are momentary' —

children.text: iti pratijñā hīyate; anekakṣaṇa vṛttyekavijñānābhyupagamāt. anekārthagrahaṇaṃ hi krameṇeti. yugapad eveti cet. yo ’sya janmakṣaṇaḥ sa ātmalābhārtha eva. labhdātmalābhaṃ hi kiṃcit svakāryaṃ prati vyāpriyate. pradīpavad iti cet. tasyāpy anekakṣaṇaviṣayatāyāṃ satyām eva prakāśyaprakāśanābhyupagamāt. vikalpātītatvāt tasya śūnyatāprasaṅgaś ca.
children.translated_text: that thesis is contradicted, because of the acceptance of a single cognition operating across multiple moments. For the grasping of multiple objects is sequential, [they may say]. [But] if [it is] simultaneous, then the moment of its birth serves only the purpose of its own coming-into-being. For something that has attained its own existence then engages in its own function. [Objection:] Like a lamp. [Reply:] Even for that [lamp], the acceptance of illuminator and illuminated [applies] only when there is extension across multiple moments. And since it [the cognition] transcends conceptual construction, there would be the undesirable consequence of voidness.
§ 180. Alternatively,

children.text: § 181. abhihitobhayaprakārasya pramāṇasya ādiprakāraviśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 181. For the purpose of understanding the specific nature of the first type of the twofold valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) that has been stated, he says —

children.text: matiḥ smṛtiḥ saṃjñā cintābhinibodha ity anarthāntaram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mati</s> (sensory cognition), <s>smṛti</s> (memory), <s>saṃjñā</s> (recognition), <s>cintā</s> (reasoning), and <s>abhinibodha</s> (comprehension) — these are synonyms. ||

children.text: § 182. ādau uddiṣṭaṃ yaj jñānaṃ tasya paryāyaśabdā ete veditavyāḥ; matijñānāvaraṇakṣayopaśamāntaraṃganimittajanitopayogaviṣayatvād eteṣām śrutādiṣv apravṛtteś ca. mananaṃ matiḥ, smaraṇaṃ smṛtiḥ, saṃjñānaṃ saṃjñā, cintanaṃ cintā, abhinibodhanam abhinibodha iti. yathāsaṃbhavaṃ vigrahāntaraṃ vijñayam.
children.translated_text: § 182. These should be understood as synonym-words for the knowledge that was mentioned first. Because these are the objects of the active consciousness (<s>upayoga</s>) generated by the internal cause of the subsidence-and-destruction of <s>mati-jñāna</s> obscuring [karma], and because they do not apply to <s>śruta</s> (scriptural knowledge) and the rest. Reflecting is <s>mati</s>; remembering is <s>smṛti</s>; recognizing is <s>saṃjñā</s>; thinking is <s>cintā</s>; comprehending is <s>abhinibodha</s>. The alternative grammatical analyses should be understood as appropriate.

children.text: § 183. saty api prakṛtibhede rūḍhibalalābhāt paryāyaśabdatvam. yathā indraḥ śakraḥ purandara iti indanādikriyāhede ’pi śacīpater ekasyaiva saṃjñā. samabhirūḍhanayāpekṣayā teṣām arthāntarakalpanāyāṃ matyādiṣv api sa kramo vidyata eva. kiṃ tu matijñānāvaraṇakṣayopaśamanimittopayogaṃ nātivartanta iti ayam atrārtho vivakṣitaḥ. ‘iti’ śabdaḥ prakārāthaḥ evaṃ prakārā asya paryāyaśabdā iti. abhidheyārtho vā. matiḥ smṛtiḥ saṃjñā cintā abhinibodha ity etair yo ‘rtho ’bhidhīyate sa eka eva iti.
children.translated_text: § 183. Even though there is a difference in etymological derivation, they are synonyms due to the force of conventional usage — just as <s>Indra</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, and <s>Purandara</s> are designations of the one husband of <s>Śacī</s>, despite the difference in the derivational actions of 'ruling' etc. From the perspective of the <s>samabhirūḍha-naya</s> (the standpoint of strict synonymy), if one postulates distinct meanings for them, that method is indeed available for <s>mati</s> and the rest too. However, the intended meaning here is that they do not exceed the active consciousness caused by the subsidence-and-destruction of <s>mati-jñāna</s> obscuring [karma]. The word '<s>iti</s>' has the meaning of 'manner' — 'these are its synonym-words of such a manner.' Or it has the meaning of 'that which is expressed' — 'the meaning expressed by <s>mati</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>cintā</s>, and <s>abhinibodha</s> is one and the same.'

children.text: § 184. athāsyātmalābhe kiṃ nimittam ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 184. Now, what is the cause for its [mati-jñāna's] arising? To this he says —

children.text: tadindriyānindriyamittam ||
children.translated_text: That [mati-jñāna] is caused by sense organs and the non-sense-organ [mind]. ||

children.text: § 185. indatīti indra ātmā. tasya jñasvabhāvasya tadāvaraṇakṣayopaśame sati svayam arthān grahītum asamarthasya yad arthopalabdhiliṃgaṃ tad indrasya liṃgam indriyam ity ucyate. athavā līnam arthaṃ gamayatīti liṃgam. ātmanaḥ sūkṣmasyāstitvādhigame liṃgam indriyam. yathā iha dhūmo ’gneḥ. evam idaṃ sparśanādi karaṇaṃ nāsati kartary ātmani bhavitum arhatīti jñātur astitvaṃ gamyate. athavā indra iti nāmakarmocyate. tena sṛṣtam indriyam iti. tatsparśanādi uttaratra vakṣyate.
children.translated_text: § 185. '<s>Indra</s>' is the self, because it rules (<s>indati</s>). For that [self] whose nature is knowledge, when the subsidence-and-destruction of its [knowledge-]obscuring [karma] occurs, and which is by itself incapable of grasping objects, that which is the sign (<s>liṅga</s>) for the cognition of objects — that is called '<s>indriya</s>' (sense organ), the sign of <s>Indra</s> (the self). Alternatively, a '<s>liṅga</s>' is that which leads to the cognition of what is concealed. The <s>indriya</s> is the sign for the ascertainment of the existence of the subtle self — just as smoke [is the sign] of fire here. Thus, this instrument of touch and the like cannot exist without the self as agent; therefore, the existence of the knower is inferred. Alternatively, '<s>Indra</s>' refers to <s>nāma-karma</s> (name-determining karma). That which is produced by it is '<s>indriya</s>.' That — touch and the like — will be stated later.

children.text: § 186. anindriyaṃ manaḥ antaḥkaraṇam ity anarthāntaram. kathaṃ punar indriyapratiṣedhena indraliṃge eva manasi anindriyaśabdasya vṛtti. īṣadarthasya nañaḥ prayogāt. īṣadindriyam anindriyam iti. yathā anudarā kanyā iti. katham īṣadarthaḥ. imānīndriyāṇi pratiniyatadeśaviṣayāṇi kālāntarāvasthāyīni ca. na tathā manaḥ indrasya liṃgam api satpratiniyatadeśaviṣayaṃ kālāntarāvasthāyi ca.
children.translated_text: § 186. '<s>Anindriya</s>' (non-sense-organ) means <s>manas</s> (mind), <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner instrument) — these are synonyms. But how does the word '<s>anindriya</s>' apply to the mind, which is itself a sign (<s>liṅga</s>) of <s>Indra</s> (the self), through the negation of '<s>indriya</s>'? Because the negative prefix '<s>na</s>' is used in the sense of 'slightly.' '<s>Anindriya</s>' means 'slightly an <s>indriya</s>' — just as '<s>anudarā kanyā</s>' [means] 'a girl with a slight belly.' How is the meaning 'slightly' [justified]? These sense organs have specific spatial domains and do not endure beyond their own time. The mind, though a sign of <s>Indra</s> (the self), does not have a specific spatial domain nor does it endure beyond its time [in the same way].

children.text: § 187. tadantaḥkaraṇam iti cocyate. guṇadoṣavicārasmaraṇādivyāpare indriyānapekṣatvāc cakṣurādivad bahiranupabdheś ca antargataṃ karaṇam antaḥakaraṇam ity ucyate.
children.translated_text: § 187. It is also called '<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>' (inner instrument). Because in activities such as deliberating on merits and faults, remembering, and the like, it does not depend on the sense organs, and because it is not perceived externally like the eye and the rest, the instrument that is internal is called '<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>'.

children.text: § 188. tad iti kim artham. matijñānanirdeśārtham. nanu ca tadanantaraṃ ‘anantarasya vidhir vā bhavati pratiṣedho vā’ iti tasyaiva grahaṇaṃ bhavati. ihārtham uttarārthaṃ ca tad ity ucyate. yanmatyādiparyāyaśabdavācyaṃ jñānaṃ tadindriyānindriyanimittaṃ tadevāvagrahehāvāyadhāraṇā iti. itarathā hi prathamaṃ matyādiśabdavācyaṃ jñānam ity uktvā indriyānindriyanimittaṃ śrutam. tadevāvagrahehāvāyadhāraṇā ity aniṣṭam abhisaṃbadhyeta.
children.translated_text: § 188. What is the purpose of the word '<s>tad</s>' (that)? For the purpose of indicating <s>mati-jñāna</s>. [Objection:] But since what immediately follows receives either a prescription or a prohibition, the reference is to that [mati-jñāna] already. [Reply:] '<s>Tad</s>' is used for both the present and subsequent purposes. The knowledge that is denoted by the synonym-words <s>mati</s> and the rest — that is caused by sense organs and the non-sense-organ [mind], and that very [knowledge] is <s>avagraha</s>, <s>īhā</s>, <s>avāya</s>, and <s>dhāraṇā</s>. Otherwise, having first stated 'the knowledge denoted by the words <s>mati</s> and the rest,' [then] 'caused by sense organs and the non-sense-organ' would be understood. [Then] 'that very [knowledge] is <s>avagraha</s>, <s>īhā</s>, <s>avāya</s>, and <s>dhāraṇā</s>' — the undesired [referent] would be connected.

children.text: § 189. evaṃ nirjñātotpattinimittam anirṇītabhedam iti tadbhedapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 189. Thus, the cause of its arising has been ascertained but its divisions have not been determined; therefore, for the purpose of understanding its divisions, he says —

children.text: avagrahehāvāyadhāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Avagraha</s> (apprehension), <s>īhā</s> (speculation), <s>avāya</s> (judgment), and <s>dhāraṇā</s> (retention). ||

children.text: § 190. viṣayaviṣayisaṃnipātasamanantaram ādyaṃ grahaṇam avagrahaḥ. viṣayaviṣayisaṃnipāte sati darśanaṃ bhavati. tadanantaram arthagrahaṇam avagrahaḥ. yathā — cakṣuṣā śuklaṃ rūpam iti grahaṇam avagrahaḥ. avagrahagṛhīte ’rthe tadviśeṣākāṅkṣaṇam īhā. yathā śuklaṃ rūpaṃ kiṃ valākā patākā veti. viśeṣanirjñānād yāthātmyāvagamanam avāyaḥ. utpatananipatanapakṣavikṣepādibhir valākaiveyaṃ na patāketi. avetasya kālāntare ’vismaraṇakāraṇaṃ dhāraṇā. yathā saiveyaṃ balākā pūrvāhṇe yām aham adrākṣam iti. eṣām avagrahādīnām upanyāsakrama utpattikramakṛtaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 190. Immediately after the contact of the object and the cognizer, the initial grasping is <s>avagraha</s> (apprehension). When the contact of object and cognizer occurs, <s>darśana</s> (perception) arises. Immediately thereafter, the grasping of the object is <s>avagraha</s>. For example, the grasping through the eye that 'this is a white form' is <s>avagraha</s>. The desire to know the specific nature of the object grasped by <s>avagraha</s> is <s>īhā</s> (speculation) — for example, 'Is the white form a crane or a flag?' The ascertainment of the true nature through determining the specific [characteristics] is <s>avāya</s> (judgment) — [for example,] 'This is indeed a crane, not a flag, due to flying up, alighting, flapping of wings, and the like.' The cause of not forgetting at a later time what has been ascertained is <s>dhāraṇā</s> (retention) — for example, 'This is the very same crane that I saw in the forenoon.' The order of presentation of these — <s>avagraha</s> and the rest — is based on the order of arising.

children.text: § 191. uktānām avagrahādīnāṃ prabhedapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 191. For the purpose of understanding the subdivisions of the stated <s>avagraha</s> and the rest, he says —

children.text: bahubahuvidhakṣiprāniḥsṛtānuktadhruvāṇāṃ setarāṇām ||
children.translated_text: [The subdivisions are:] of the many (<s>bahu</s>), the manifold (<s>bahuvidha</s>), the quick (<s>kṣipra</s>), the unexpressed (<s>aniḥsṛta</s>), the unstated (<s>anukta</s>), and the steady (<s>dhruva</s>) — together with their opposites. ||

children.text: § 192. avagrahādayaḥ kriyāviśeṣāḥ prakṛtāḥ. tadapekṣo ’yaṃ karmanirdeśaḥ. bahvādīnāṃ setarāṇām iti. bahuśabdasya saṃkhyāvaipulyavācino grahaṇam aviśeṣāt. saṃkhyāvācī yathā, eko dvau bahava iti. vaipulyavācī yathā, bahur odano bahuḥ sūpa iti. vidhaśabdaḥ prakāravācī. kṣipragrahaṇam acirapratipattyartham. aniḥsṛtagrahaṇam asakalapudgalodgamārtham. anuktam abhiprāyeṇa grahaṇam. dhruvaṃ nirantaraṃ yathārthagrahaṇam. setaragrahaṇaṃ pratipakṣasaṃgrahārtham.
children.translated_text: § 192. <s>Avagraha</s> and the rest are specific cognitive activities under discussion. This statement of [their] properties (<s>karma</s>) is with reference to them. 'Of the many and the rest, together with their opposites.' The word '<s>bahu</s>' (many) is taken since it denotes both numerical plurality and abundance, without distinction. As denoting number: one, two, many. As denoting abundance: much rice, much soup. The word '<s>vidha</s>' (kind) denotes variety. '<s>Kṣipra</s>' (quick) is taken for the meaning of swift apprehension. '<s>Aniḥsṛta</s>' (unexpressed) is for the meaning of incomplete emergence of matter-particles. '<s>Anukta</s>' (unstated) means grasping based on one's own intention. '<s>Dhruva</s>' (steady) means continuous, accurate grasping. 'Together with their opposites' is for the purpose of including the counterparts.

children.text: § 193. bahūnām avagrahaḥ alpasyāvagrahaḥ bahuvidhasyāvagrahaḥ ekavidhasyāvagraḥ kṣipram avagrahaḥ cireṇāvagrahaḥ aniḥsṛtasyāvagrahaḥ niḥsṛtasyāvagrahaḥ anuktasyāvagrahaḥ uktasyāvagrahaḥ dhruvasyāvagrahaḥ adhruvasyāvagrahaś ceti avagraho dvādaśavikalpaḥ. evam īhādayo ’pi. ta ete pañcabhir indriyadvārair manasā ca pratyekaṃ pradurbhāvyante. tatra bahvavagrhādayaḥ matijñānāvaraṇakṣayopaśamaprakarṣāt prabhavanti netare iti. teṣām abhyarhitatvād ādau grahaṇaṃ kriyate.
children.translated_text: § 193. Apprehension of many, apprehension of few; apprehension of the manifold, apprehension of one kind; quick apprehension, slow apprehension; apprehension of the unexpressed, apprehension of the expressed; apprehension of the unstated, apprehension of the stated; steady apprehension, unsteady apprehension — thus <s>avagraha</s> is of twelve varieties. Similarly <s>īhā</s> and the rest also. These are manifested individually through the five sense-doors and the mind. Among these, the apprehension of many and the rest arise from the excellence of the subsidence-and-destruction of <s>mati-jñāna</s> obscuring [karma], not the others. Because they are more esteemed, they are mentioned first.

children.text: § 194. bahubahuvidhayoḥ kaḥ prativiśeṣaḥ; yāvatā bahuṣv api bahutvam asti bahuvidheṣv api bahutvam asti? ekaprakāranānāprakārakṛto viśeṣaḥ. uktaniḥsṛtayoḥ kaḥ prativiśeṣaḥ; yāvatā sakalaniḥsaraṇān niḥsṛtam. uktam apy evaṃ vidham eva? ayam asti viśeṣaḥ; anyopadeśapūrvakaṃ grahaṇam uktam. svata eva grahaṇaṃ niḥsṛtam.
children.translated_text: § 194. What is the distinction between 'many' (<s>bahu</s>) and 'manifold' (<s>bahuvidha</s>), since multiplicity exists in many and multiplicity exists in the manifold too? The distinction is made by [the difference between] one kind and many kinds. What is the distinction between 'stated' (<s>ukta</s>) and 'expressed' (<s>niḥsṛta</s>), since what is fully expressed is 'expressed,' and what is 'stated' is also of that nature? There is this distinction: grasping preceded by instruction from another is '<s>ukta</s>' (stated); grasping by oneself is '<s>niḥsṛta</s>' (expressed).

children.text: § 195. apareṣāṃ kṣipraniḥsṛta iti pāṭhaḥ. ta evaṃ varṇayanti śrotrendriyeṇa śabdam avagṛhyamāṇaṃ mayūrasya vā kurarasya veti kaścit pratipadyate. aparaḥ svarūpam evāsṛitya iti.
children.translated_text: § 195. Others have the reading '<s>kṣipra-niḥsṛta</s>' [as one compound]. They explain thus: when apprehending a sound through the ear, someone determines 'it is of a peacock or a <s>kurara</s> bird.' Another [determines it] relying on the form itself.

children.text: § 196. dhruvāvagrahasya dhāraṇāyāś ca kaḥ prativiśeṣaḥ? ucyate, kṣayopaśamaprāptikāle viśuddhapariṇāmasaṃtatyā prāptāt kṣayopaśamāt prathamasamaye yathāvagrahas tathaiva dvitīyādiṣv api samayeṣu nono nābhyadhika iti dhruvāvagraha ity ucyate. yadā punarviśuddhapariṇāmasya saṃkleśapariṇāmasya ca miśraṇāt kṣayopaśamo bhavati tata utpadyamāno ’vagrahaḥ kadācit bahūnāṃ kadācid alpasya kadācid bahuvidhasya kadācid ekavidhasya veti nyūnādhikabhāvād adhruvāvagraha ity ucyate. dharaṇā punargṛhītārthāvismaraṇakāraṇam iti mahad anayor antaram.
children.translated_text: § 196. What is the distinction between steady apprehension (<s>dhruvāvagraha</s>) and retention (<s>dhāraṇā</s>)? It is said: at the time of attaining subsidence-and-destruction, through a continuously pure mental disposition (<s>pariṇāma</s>), when the apprehension arising from the subsidence-and-destruction attained at the first moment continues the same in the second and subsequent moments — neither less nor more — that is called steady apprehension (<s>dhruvāvagraha</s>). But when, due to the mixture of pure and defiled dispositions, the subsidence-and-destruction produces an apprehension that is sometimes of many, sometimes of few, sometimes of many kinds, sometimes of one kind — having the nature of increase and decrease — that is called unsteady apprehension (<s>adhruvāvagraha</s>).
