Retention (<s>dhāraṇā</s>), on the other hand, is the cause of not forgetting what has been grasped — thus there is a great difference between the two.

children.text: § 197. yady avagrahādayo bahvādīnāṃ karmaṇām ākṣeptāraḥ, bahvādīni punarviśeṣaṇāni kasyety ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 197. If <s>avagraha</s> and the rest take on the properties of 'many' and the rest, then of what are 'many' and the rest qualifiers? — to this he says —

children.text: arthasya ||
children.translated_text: Of the object (<s>artha</s>). ||

children.text: § 198. cakṣurādiviṣayo ’rthaḥ. tasya bahvādiviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭasya avagrahādayo bhavantīty abhisaṃbandhaḥ kriyate. kim artham idam ucyate yāvatā bahvādir artha eva? satyam evam, kintu pravādiparikalpanānivṛttyarthaṃ ‘arthasya’ ity ucyate. kecit pravādino manyante rūpādayo guṇā eva indriyaiḥ saṃnikṛṣyante tenaiteṣām eva grahaṇam iti. tad ayuktam; na hi te rūpādayo guṇā amūrtā indriyasaṃnikarṣam āpadyante. na tarhi idānīm idaṃ bhavati ‘rūpaṃ mayā dṛṣṭaṃ, gandho vā ghrāta’ iti. bhavati ca. katham? iyarti paryāyāṃs tair vā ’ryata ity artho dravyaṃ, tasminn indriyaiḥ saṃnikṛṣṇyamāṇe tadavyatirekād rūpādiṣv api saṃvyavahāro yujyate.
children.translated_text: § 198. The object (<s>artha</s>) is the domain of the eye and other [sense organs]. The connection is made that <s>avagraha</s> (apprehension) and the other [stages of cognition] arise with respect to that [object] as qualified by the qualifications of 'many' etc. For what purpose is this stated, since 'many' and the rest already pertain to the object itself? True indeed, but the word 'of the object' (<s>arthasya</s>) is stated for the purpose of preventing the fabrications of opponents. Certain opponents maintain that qualities such as color and the like alone are brought into contact with the sense organs, and therefore only these are apprehended. That is untenable; for those qualities such as color and the like, being non-material (<s>amūrta</s>), cannot come into contact with the sense organs. [Objection:] Then this present experience would not occur: 'Color was seen by me,' or 'odor was smelled.' [Reply:] It does occur. How? That which moves through modifications, or through which [modifications] are moved—that is an <s>artha</s> (object), i.e., a substance (<s>dravya</s>). When the sense organs come into contact with that [substance], the conventional usage regarding color and the rest is also justified, due to their non-difference [from the substance].

children.text: § 199 kim ime avagrahādayaḥ sarvasyendriyānindriyasya bhavanti uta kaścid viṣayaviśeṣo ’stīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 199. Do these <s>avagraha</s> (apprehension) and the other [stages] occur for all [types of perception]—both sensory and non-sensory? Or is there a specific restriction regarding the objects? To this he says—

children.text: vyañjanasyāvagrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The apprehension (<s>avagraha</s>) [pertains to] the indistinct (<s>vyañjana</s>). ||

children.text: § 200. vyañjanam avyaktaṃ śabdādijātaṃ tasyāvagraho bhavati nehādayaḥ. kim artham idam? niyamārtham, avagraha eva nehādaya iti. sa tarhi evakāraḥ kartavyaḥ? na kartavyaḥ, ‘siddhe vidhir ārabhyamāno niyamārtha’ iti antareṇaivakāraṃ niyamārtho bhaviṣyati. nanu avagrahagrahaṇam ubhayatra tulyam tatra kiṃ kṛto ’yaṃ viśeṣaḥ? arthāvagrahavyañjanāvagrahayor vyaktāvyaktakṛto viśeṣaḥ. katham? abhinavaśarāvādrīkaraṇavat.
yathā jalakaṇadvitrāsiktaḥ sarāvo ’bhinavo nādrībhavati,
children.translated_text: Just as a new earthen vessel sprinkled with two or three drops of water does not become moist,

children.text: sa eva punaḥ punaḥ sicyamānaḥ śanais timyati, evaṃ śrotrādiṣv indriyeṣu śabdādipariṇatāḥ pudgalā dvitrādiṣu samayeṣu gṛhyamānā na vyaktībhavanti, punaḥ punar avagrahe sati vyaktībhavanti. ato vyaktagrahaṇāt prāgvyañjanāvagrahaḥ vyaktagrahaṇam arthāvagrahaḥ. tato ’vyaktāvagrahaṇād īhādayo na bhavanti.
children.translated_text: but the same vessel, when sprinkled again and again, gradually becomes saturated—similarly, in the sense organs such as the ear and the rest, the <s>pudgalas</s> (material particles) that have transformed into sound and the like, when apprehended in two, three, or more instants, do not become distinct; [but] when <s>avagraha</s> occurs again and again, they become distinct. Therefore, prior to the apprehension of the distinct, there is <s>vyañjanāvagraha</s> (apprehension of the indistinct); the apprehension of the distinct is <s>arthāvagraha</s> (apprehension of the object). Hence, from the [mere] indistinct apprehension, <s>īhā</s> (speculation) and the other [stages] do not arise.

§ 200. <s>Vyañjana</s> means the indistinct (<s>avyakta</s>)—the class of sounds and the like. Its <s>avagraha</s> (apprehension) occurs, but not <s>īhā</s> (speculation) and the other [stages]. For what purpose is this [stated]? For the purpose of restriction: [for the indistinct,] only <s>avagraha</s> occurs, not <s>īhā</s> and the rest. Then should the restrictive particle 'eva' (alone) be used? It need not be, because by the principle 'a prescriptive rule introduced when [the result] is already established serves the purpose of restriction,' even without the particle 'eva,' the restrictive meaning will follow. [Objection:] But the mention of <s>avagraha</s> is common to both [cases]; what then creates the distinction here? [Reply:] The distinction between <s>arthāvagraha</s> (apprehension of the distinct object) and <s>vyañjanāvagraha</s> (apprehension of the indistinct) is created by the clear and unclear [nature of the object]. How?

children.text: § 201. sarvendriyāṇām aviśeṣeṇa vyañjanāvagrahaprasaṅge yatrāsaṃbhavas tadarthapratiṣedam āha —
children.translated_text: § 201. Since <s>vyañjanāvagraha</s> (indistinct apprehension) would apply to all sense organs without distinction, he states the negation where it is impossible—

children.text: na cakṣuranindriyābhyām ||
children.translated_text: Not through the eye or the non-sensory [mind]. ||

children.text: § 202. cakṣuṣā anindriyena ca vyañjanāvagraho na bhavati. kutaḥ? aprāpyakāritvāt. yato ’prāptam artham avidikkaṃ yuktaṃ saṃnikarṣaviṣaye ’vasthitaṃ bāhyaprakāśābhivyaktam upalabhate cakṣuḥ manaś cāprāptam ity anayor vyañjanāvagraho nāsti.
children.translated_text: § 202. Through the eye and through the non-sensory [mind], <s>vyañjanāvagraha</s> (indistinct apprehension) does not occur. Why? Because they operate without contact (<s>aprāpyakāritva</s>). Since [the eye] apprehends an object that has not been reached and [even] one that is not in a [particular] direction, it is appropriate [to say it operates without contact].

children.text: § 203. cakṣuṣo ’prāpyakāritvaṃ katham adhyavasīyate? āgamato yuktitaś ca. āgamatas tāvat
children.translated_text: § 203. How is the non-contact operation (<s>aprāpyakāritva</s>) of the eye ascertained? Through scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and through reasoning (<s>yukti</s>). Through scripture, first:

children.text:
puṭṭhaṃ suṇodi saddaṃ apuṭṭhaṃ ceva passade rūaṃ |
	  gaṃdhaṃ rasaṃ ca phāsaṃ baddhaṃ puṭṭhaṃ viyāṇādi ||
children.translated_text: By contact it hears sound; without contact it sees form; odor, taste, and touch—the bound [soul] knows by contact. [Prakrit verse]

children.text: § 204. yuktitaś ca — aprāpyakāri cakṣuḥ, spṛṣṭānavagrahāt. yadi prāpyakāri syāt tvagindriyavat spṛṣṭam añjanaṃ gṛhṇīyāt, na tu gṛhṇāty ato manovadaprāpyakārīty avaseyam. tataś cakṣurmanasī varjayitvā śeṣāṇām indriyāṇāṃ vyañjanāvagrahaḥ. sarveṣām indriyānindriyāṇām arthāvagraha iti siddham.
children.translated_text: § 204. And through reasoning: the eye operates without contact, because it does not apprehend what is touched. If it operated by contact, like the tactile sense organ, it would apprehend the collyrium (<s>añjana</s>) that is in contact [with the eye].

children.text: § 205. āha nirdiṣṭaṃ matijñānaṃ lakṣaṇato vikalpataś ca; tadanantaram uddhiṣṭaṃ yat śrutaṃ tasyedānīṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vikalpaś ca vaktavya ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 205. He says: sensory knowledge (<s>matijñāna</s>) has been stated with regard to its definition and its varieties. Now, the definition and varieties of scriptural knowledge (<s>śrutajñāna</s>), which was mentioned next after that, [are to be stated]—

children.text: śrutaṃ matipūrvaṃ dvyanekadvādaśabhedam ||
children.translated_text: Scriptural knowledge (<s>śruta</s>) is preceded by sensory knowledge (<s>mati</s>) and has two, many, or twelve divisions. ||

children.text: § 206. śrutaśabdo ’yaṃ śravaṇam upādāya vyutpādito ’pi rūḍhivaśāt kasmiṃś cij jñānaviśeṣe vartate. yathā kuśalavanakarma pratītya vyutpādito ’pi kuśalaśabdo rūḍhivaśāt paryavadāte vartate. kaḥ punar asau jñānaviśeṣa iti? ata āha ‘śrutaṃ matipūrvam’ iti. śrutasya pramāṇatvaṃ pūrayatīti pūrvaṃ nimittaṃ kāraṇam ity anarthāntaram. matir nirdiṣṭā. matiḥ pūrvam asya matipūrvaṃ matikāraṇam ity arthaḥ. yadi matipūrvaṃ śrutaṃ tadapi matyātmakaṃ prāpnoti ‘kāraṇasadṛśaṃ hi loke kāryaṃ dṛṣṭam’ iti. naitad aikāntikam. daṇḍādikāraṇo ’yaṃ ghaṭo na daṇḍādyātmakaḥ. api ca sati tasmiṃs tadabhāvāt. saty api matijñāne bāhyaśrutajñānanimittasaṃnidhāne ’pi prabalaśrutāvaraṇodayasya śrutābhāvaḥ. śrutāvaraṇakṣayopaśamaprakarṣe tu sati śrutjañānam utpadyata iti matijñānaṃ nimttamātraṃ jñeyam.
children.translated_text: § 206. The word '<s>śruta</s>' (scriptural), though etymologically derived from <s>śravaṇa</s> (hearing), by conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>) applies to a particular kind of knowledge—just as the word '<s>kuśala</s>' (skillful) [is used conventionally despite its etymology]. And the word '<s>pūrva</s>' here means 'preceded by' or 'caused by.' The genitive case [in '<s>matipūrvam</s>'] should be construed as 'preceded by <s>mati</s>' or 'having <s>mati</s> as its cause.'

children.text: § 207. āha, śrutam anādinidhanam iṣyate. tasya matipūrvakatve tadabhavāḥ; ādimato ’ntavattvāt. tataś ca puruṣakṛtitvād aprāmāṇyam iti? naiṣa doṣaḥ; dravyādisāmānyārpaṇāt śrutam anādinidhanam iṣyate. na hi kenacit puruṣeṇa kvacit kadācit kathaṃcid utprekṣitam iti. teṣām eva viśeṣāpekṣayā ādir antaś ca saṃbhavatīti ‘matipūrvam’ ity ucyate. yathāṅkuro bījapūrvakaḥ sa ca saṃtānāpekṣayā anādinidhana iti. na cāpauruṣeyatvaṃ prāmāṇyakāraṇam; caurādyupadeśasyāsmaryamāṇakartṛkasya prāmāṇyaprasaṅgāt. anityasya ca pratyakṣādeḥ prāmāṇye ko virodhaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 207. [Objection:] Scriptural knowledge (<s>śruta</s>) is accepted as beginningless and endless. If it were preceded by sensory knowledge (<s>mati</s>), [those qualities] would not hold; since what has a beginning also has an end. And consequently, being man-made, it would not be authoritative (<s>pramāṇa</s>). [Reply:] This is not a fault. The precedence of <s>mati</s> refers to the experience of the individual soul—the scripture is experienced through sensory knowledge. But the scripture itself, in terms of its object-content, is beginningless.

children.text: § 208. āha, prathamasamyaktvotpattau yugapaj jñānapariṇāmān matipūrvakatvaṃ śrutasya nopapadyata iti? tad ayuktam; samyaktvasya tadapekṣatvāt. ātmalābhas tu kramavān iti matipūrvakatvavyāghātābhāvaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 208. [Objection:] At the time of the first arising of right faith (<s>samyaktva</s>), since the cognitive transformations [of mati and śruta] are simultaneous, the precedence of <s>mati</s> for <s>śruta</s> is not tenable? [Reply:] That is untenable; since even when arising simultaneously, the relation of cause and effect is established—like [the relation between] a lamp and its light.

children.text: § 209. āha, matipūrvaṃ śrutam ity etal lakṣaṇam avyāpi śrutapūrvam api śrutam iṣyate. tadyathā — śabdapariṇatapudgalaskandhād āhitavarṇapadavākyādibhāvāc cakṣurādiviṣayāc ca ādyaśrutaviṣayabhāvam āpannād avyabhicāriṇaḥ kṛtasaṃgītir jano ghaṭāj jaladhāraṇādi kāryaṃ saṃbandhyantaraṃ pratipadyate, dhūmāder vāgnyādidravyaṃ, tadā śrutāt śrutapratipattir iti? naiṣa doṣaḥ; tasyāpi matipūrvakatvam upacārataḥ. śrutam api kvacin matir ity upacaryate, matipūrvakatvād iti.
children.translated_text: § 209. [Objection:] The definition '<s>śruta</s> is preceded by <s>mati</s>' is too narrow (<s>avyāpti</s>), since <s>śruta</s> preceded by [another] <s>śruta</s> is also accepted. For example, the apprehension of <s>pudgalas</s> (material particles) transformed into sound—

children.text: § 210. bhedaśabdaḥ pratyekaṃ parisamāpyate — dvibhedam anekabhedaṃ dvādaśabhedam iti. dvi bhedaṃ tāvat — aṅgabāhyam aṅgapraviṣṭam iti. aṅgabāhyam anekavidhaṃ daśavaikālikottarādhyayanādi. aṅgapraviṣṭaṃ dvādaśavidham. tadyathā, ācāraḥ sūtrakṛtaṃ sthānaṃ samavāyaḥ vyākhyāprajñaptiḥ jñātṛdharmakathā upāsakādhyayanaṃ antakṛddaśaṃ anuttaraupapādikadaśaṃ praśnavyākaraṇaṃ vipākasūtraṃ dṛṣṭivāda iti. dṛṣṭivādaḥ pañcavidhaḥ — parikarma sūtraṃ prathamānuyogaḥ pūrvagataṃ cūlikā ceti. tatra pūrvagataṃ caturdaśavidham — utpādapūrvam agrāyaṇīyaṃ vīryānupravādam astināstipravādaṃ jñānapravādaṃ satyapravādam ātmapravādaṃ karmapravādaṃ pratyākhyānanāmadheyaṃ vidyānupravādaṃ kalyāṇanāmadheyaṃ prāṇāvāyaṃ kriyāviśālaṃ lokabindusāram iti. tadetat śrutaṃ dvibhedam anekabhedaṃ dvādaśabhedam iti.
children.translated_text: § 210. The word 'division' (<s>bheda</s>) applies to each [separately]: two divisions, many divisions, twelve divisions. First, the two divisions are: <s>aṅgabāhya</s> (outside the <s>aṅgas</s>/canonical limbs) and <s>aṅgapraviṣṭa</s> (within the <s>aṅgas</s>).

children.text: § 211. kiṃ kṛto ’yaṃ viśeṣaḥ? vaktṛviśeṣakṛtaḥ. trayo vaktāraḥ — sarvajñas tīrthakara itaro vā śrutakevalī ārātīyaś ceti. tatra sarvajñena paramarṣiṇā paramācintyakevalajñānavibhūtiviśeṣeṇa arthata āgama uddiṣṭaḥ. tasya pratyakṣadarśitvāt prakṣīṇadoṣatvāc ca prāmāṇyam. tasya sākṣāc chiṣyair buddhyatiśayarddhiyuktair gaṇadharaiḥ śrutakevalibhir anusmṛtagrantharacanam aṅgapūrvalakṣaṇam. tatpramāṇam; tatprāmāṇyāt. ārātīyair punar ācāryaiḥ kāladoṣāt saṃkṣiptāyurmatibalaśiṣyānugrahārthaṃ daśavaikālikādyupanibaddham. tatpramāṇam arthatas tadevedam iti kṣīrārṇavajalaṃ ghaṭagṛhītam iva.
children.translated_text: § 211. What creates this distinction? The distinction of the speaker. There are three speakers: the omniscient (<s>sarvajña</s>) [who is a] <s>Tīrthaṅkara</s>, or another [omniscient] who is a <s>śruta-kevalin</s> (one with complete scriptural knowledge), and an opponent (<s>ārātīya</s>).

children.text: § 212. vyākhyātaṃ parokṣam. pratyakṣam idānīṃ vaktavyam. tad dvedhā — deśapratyakṣaṃ sarvapratyakṣaṃ ca. deśapratyakṣam avadhimanaḥparyayajñāne. sarvapratyakṣaṃ kevalam. yady evam idam eva tāvad avidhijñānaṃ triḥprakārasya pratyakṣasyādyaṃ vyākriyatām ity atrocyate — dvividho ’vadhir bhavapratyayaḥ kṣayopaśamanimittaś ceti. tatra bhavapratyaya ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 212. Indirect knowledge (<s>parokṣa</s>) has been explained. Now direct knowledge (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is to be stated. It is twofold: partial direct knowledge (<s>deśa-pratyakṣa</s>) and complete direct knowledge (<s>sarva-pratyakṣa</s>). Partial direct knowledge is [further divided as]—

children.text: bhavapratyayo ’vadhir devanārakāṇām ||
children.translated_text: Clairvoyant knowledge (<s>avadhi</s>) arises from the condition of existence (<s>bhava-pratyaya</s>) for celestial and hellish beings. ||

children.text: § 213. bhava ity ucyate. ko bhavaḥ? āyurnāmakarmodayanimitta ātmanaḥ paryāyo bhavaḥ. pratyayaḥ kāraṇaṃ nimittam ity anarthāntaram. bhavaḥ pratyayo ’sya bhavapratyayo ’vadhir devanārakāṇāṃ veditavyaḥ. yady evaṃ tatra kṣayopaśamanimittatvaṃ na prāpnoti? naiṣa dośaḥ; tadāśrayāt tatsiddheh. bhavaṃ pratītya kṣayopaśamaḥ saṃjāyata iti kṛtvā bhavaḥ pradhānakāraṇam ity upadiśyate. yathā patatriṇo gamanam ākāśe bhavanimittam, na śikṣāguṇaviśeṣaḥ tathā devanārakāṇāṃ vrataniyamādyabhāve ’pi jāyata ‘iti bhavapratyayaḥ’ ity ucyate. itarathā hi bhavaḥ sādhāraṇa iti kṛtvā sarveṣām aviśeṣaḥ syāt. iṣyate ca tatrāvadheḥ prakarṣāprakarṣavṛttiḥ. ‘devanārakāṇām’ ity aviśeṣābhidhāne ’pi samyagdṛṣṭīnām eva grahaṇam. kutaḥ? avadhigrahaṇāt. mityādṛṣṭīnāṃ ca vibhaṅga ity ucyate. prakarṣāprakarṣavṛttiś ca āgamato vijñeyā.
children.translated_text: § 213. '<s>Bhava</s>' (existence/birth-state) is stated [in the sūtra]. What is <s>bhava</s>? <s>Bhava</s> is the modification of the self occasioned by the fruition of lifespan-determining (<s>āyus</s>), name-determining (<s>nāma</s>), and status-determining (<s>gotra</s>) <s>karmas</s>. '<s>Pratyaya</s>' means cause or condition—these are synonymous.

children.text: § 214. yadi bhavapratyayo ’vadhir devanārakāṇām, atha kṣayopaśamahetukaḥ keṣām ity āha —
children.translated_text: § 214. If clairvoyant knowledge (<s>avadhi</s>) arises from the condition of existence for celestials and hellish beings, then for whom does it arise from the cause of subsidence-cum-destruction (<s>kṣayopaśama</s>)? To this he says—

children.text: kṣayopaśamanimittaḥ ṣaḍvikalpaḥ śeṣāṇām ||
children.translated_text: That [clairvoyant knowledge] caused by subsidence-cum-destruction (<s>kṣayopaśama-nimitta</s>) is of six varieties, for the remaining [types of beings]. ||

children.text: § 215. avadhijñānāvaraṇasya deśaghātisparddhakānām udaye sati sarvaghātisparddhakānām udayābhāvaḥ kṣayaḥ teṣām evānudayaprāptānāṃ sadavasthā upaśamaḥ. tau nimittam asyeti kṣayopaśamanimittaḥ. sa śeṣāṇām veditavyaḥ. ke punaḥ śeṣāḥ. manuṣyās tiryañcaś ca. teṣv api yatra sāmarthyam asti tatraiva veditavyaḥ. na hy asaṃjñinām aparyāptakānāṃ ca tatsāmarthyam asti. saṃjñināṃ paryāptakānāṃ ca na sarveṣām. keṣāṃ tarhi? yathoktasamyagdarśanādinimttasaṃnidhāne sati śāntakṣīṇakarmaṇāṃ tasyopalabdhir bhavati. sarvasya kṣayopaśamanimittatve kṣayopaśam agrahaṇaṃ niyamārthaṃ kṣayopaśama eva nimittaṃ na bhava iti. sa eṣo ’vadhiḥ ṣaḍvikalpaḥ. kutaḥ? anugāmyananugāmivardhamānahīyamānāvasthitānavasthitabhedāt. kaścid avadhir bhāskaraprakāśavad gacchantam anugacchati. kaścin nānugacchati tatraivātipatati unmukhapraśnādeśipuruṣavacanavat. aparo ’vadhiḥ araṇinirmathanotpannaśuṣkaparṇopacīyamānendhananicayasamiddhapāvakavatsamyagdarśanādiguṇaviśuddhipariṇāmasaṃnidhānād yat -parimāṇa utpannas tato varddhate ā asaṃkhyeyalokebhyaḥ. aparo ’vadhiḥ paricchinnopādānasaṃtatyagniśikhāvatsamyagdarśanādiguṇahānisaṃkleśapariṇāmavṛddhiyogād yat- parimānā utpannas tato hīyate ā aṅgulasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgāt. itaro ’vadhiḥ samyagdarśanādiguṇāvasthānād yat parimāṇa utpannas tat primāṇā evāvasthiṣṭhate; na hīyate nāpi vardhate liṅgavat ā bhavakṣayād ā kevalajñānotpatter vā. anyo ’vadhiḥ samyagdarśanādiguṇavṛddhihāniyogād yatparimāṇa utpannas tato vardhate yāvad anena vardhitavyaṃ hīyate ca yāvad anena hātavyaṃ vāyuvegapreritajalormivat. evaṃ ṣaḍvikalpo ’vadhir bhavati.
children.translated_text: § 215. When the partial-destruction-competing (<s>deśaghātisparddhaka</s>) [karmic particles] of the obscuration of clairvoyant knowledge (<s>avadhijñānāvaraṇa</s>) are in operation, the non-operation of the total-destruction-competing (<s>sarvaghātisparddhaka</s>) particles is destruction (<s>kṣaya</s>); the stable state of those very [particles] that have attained non-operation is subsidence (<s>upaśama</s>). These two being its cause, it is called 'caused by destruction-cum-subsidence' (<s>kṣayopaśamanimitta</s>). This should be understood for the remaining [beings]. Who are the remaining? Humans and animals. Among them too, it should be understood only where the capacity exists. For non-rational beings (<s>asaṃjñin</s>) and beings with incomplete development (<s>aparyāptaka</s>) do not have that capacity. Nor do all rational beings with complete development. For whom then? When the conditions of right faith (<s>samyagdarśana</s>) etc. as described are present, the attainment of that [knowledge] occurs for those whose <s>karma</s> has been pacified or destroyed. The mention of 'destruction-cum-subsidence' when all [types] could be the cause is for the purpose of restriction: destruction-cum-subsidence alone is the cause, not [mere] existence. This <s>avadhi</s> (clairvoyant knowledge) is of six varieties. Why? Due to the distinctions of following (<s>anugāmin</s>), non-following (<s>ananugāmin</s>), increasing (<s>vardhamāna</s>), decreasing (<s>hīyamāna</s>), stable (<s>avasthita</s>), and unstable (<s>anavasthita</s>). Some clairvoyant knowledge follows the one who moves, like sunlight. Some does not follow but remains fixed in that place, like the words of a fortune-teller who speaks to one facing him. Another type of <s>avadhi</s>, like a fire kindled by friction that grows as dry leaves and fuel are added, increases from whatever extent it arises up to innumerable worlds, due to the proximity of purifying dispositions such as right faith etc. Another type, like a flame fed by limited fuel, decreases from whatever extent it arises down to an innumerable fraction of a finger-breadth, due to the growth of defiling dispositions and the decline of qualities such as right faith etc. Yet another type remains stable at whatever extent it arises, neither decreasing nor increasing, like a characteristic mark, until the end of the life or the arising of omniscient knowledge (<s>kevalajñāna</s>), due to the stability of qualities such as right faith etc. Another type increases as much as it should increase and decreases as much as it should decrease from whatever extent it arises, like a wave driven by the force of wind, due to the alternation of growth and decline of qualities such as right faith etc. Thus, <s>avadhi</s> is of six varieties.

children.text: § 216. evaṃ vyākhyātam avadhijñānaṃ, tadantaram idānīṃ manaḥparyayajñānaṃ vaktavyam. tasya bhedaḥ puraḥsaraṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vyācikhyāsur idam āha —
children.translated_text: § 216. Thus, clairvoyant knowledge (<s>avadhijñāna</s>) has been explained. Next, mind-reading knowledge (<s>manaḥparyayajñāna</s>) is to be described. Wishing to explain its definition preceded by its division, he says—

children.text: ṛjuvipulamatī manaḥparyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The straightforward (<s>ṛju</s>) and the extensive (<s>vipula</s>) [types of] cognition constitute mind-reading knowledge (<s>manaḥparyaya</s>). ||

children.text: § 217. ṛjvī nirvartitā praguṇā ca. kasmān nirvartitā? vākkāyamanaḥkṛtārthasya paramanogatasya vijñānāt. ṛjvī matir yasya so ’yaṃ ṛjumatiḥ. anirvartitā kuṭilā ca vipulā. kasmād anirvartitā? vākkāyamanaḥkṛtārthasya parakīyamanogatasya vijñānāt. vipulā matir yasya so ’yaṃ vipulamatiḥ. ṛjumatiś ca vipulamatiś ca ṛjuvipulamatī. ekasya matiśabdasya gatārthatvād aprayogaḥ. athavā ṛjuś ca vipulā ca ṛjuvipule. ṛjuvipule matī yayos tau ṛjuvipulamatī iti. sa eṣa manaḥparyayo dvividhaḥ ṛjumatir vipulamatir iti.
children.translated_text: § 217. '<s>Ṛjvī</s>' (straightforward) means accomplished and simple. Why accomplished? Because of the cognition of what is in another's mind by one who has accomplished the purposes of speech, body, and mind. One whose cognition is straightforward is the <s>ṛjumati</s> (straightforward-minded). '<s>Vipulā</s>' (extensive) means unaccomplished and crooked. Why unaccomplished? Because of the cognition of what is in another's mind by one who has [still] performed purposes through speech, body, and mind. One whose cognition is extensive is the <s>vipulamati</s> (extensive-minded). The straightforward-minded and the extensive-minded together are <s>ṛjuvipulamatī</s>. Since the word '<s>mati</s>' (cognition) would be redundant if used again, it is not repeated. Alternatively, '<s>ṛju</s>' and '<s>vipula</s>' [form the compound] '<s>ṛjuvipula</s>'; those whose two cognitions are straightforward and extensive are '<s>ṛjuvipulamatī</s>.' Thus, this <s>manaḥparyaya</s> is of two kinds: <s>ṛjumati</s> and <s>vipulamati</s>.

children.text: § 218. āha, ukto bhedaḥ, lakṣaṇam idānīṃ vaktavyam ity atrocyate — vīryāntarāyamanaḥparyayajñānāvaraṇakṣayopaśamāṅgopāṅganāmalābhāvaṣṭambhād ātmanaḥ parakīyamanaḥsaṃbandena labdhavṛttir upayogo manaḥparyayaḥ. matijñānaprasaṅga iti cet? uktottaraṃ purastāt. apekṣākāraṇaṃ mana iti. parakīyamanasi vyavasthito ’rthaḥ anena jñāyate ity etāvad atrāpekṣyate. tatra ṛjumatir manaḥparyayaḥ kālato jaghanyena jīvānām ātmanaś ca dvitrāṇi bhavagrahaṇāni, utkarṣeṇa saptāṣṭau gatyāgatyādibhiḥ prarūpayati. kṣetrato jaghanyena gavyūtipṛthaktvaṃ, utkarṣeṇa yojanapṛthaktvasyābhyantaraṃ, na bahiḥ. dvitīyaḥ kālato jaghanyena saptāṣṭau bhavagrahaṇāni, utkarṣeṇāsaṃkhyeyāni gatyāgatyādibhiḥ prarūpayati. kṣetrato jaghanyena yojanapṛthaktvaṃ, utkarṣeṇa mānuṣottaraśailasyābhyantaraṃ, na bahiḥ.
children.translated_text: § 218. He says: the division has been stated; the definition should now be given. To this it is said: the active consciousness (<s>upayoga</s>) that has obtained its function through connection with another's mind, arising from the destruction-cum-subsidence of energy-obstructing (<s>vīryāntarāya</s>) and mind-reading-knowledge-obscuring (<s>manaḥparyayajñānāvaraṇa</s>) [karmas], with the attainment of major and minor limbs, is mind-reading knowledge (<s>manaḥparyaya</s>). [Objection:] Would this not be a case of sensory knowledge (<s>matijñāna</s>)? [Reply:] This has been answered previously. The mind is the object of the cognitive relation. The meaning established in another's mind is cognized by this—only this much is required here. Of these, the <s>ṛjumati</s> type of <s>manaḥparyaya</s>, in terms of time, at minimum perceives the life-spans of [other] souls and one's own for two or three births; at maximum, it perceives seven or eight [births] through comings and goings etc. In terms of spatial range, at minimum it extends to a unit of <s>gavyūti</s> (about 2 miles); at maximum, it extends within a unit of <s>yojana</s> (about 8 miles), not beyond. The second [type, <s>vipulamati</s>], in terms of time, at minimum perceives seven or eight birth-spans; at maximum, it perceives innumerable [births] through comings and goings etc. In terms of spatial range, at minimum it extends to a unit of <s>yojana</s>; at maximum, it extends within the <s>Mānuṣottara</s> mountain, not beyond.

children.text: § 219. uktayor anayoḥ punar api viśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 219. For the purpose of further understanding the distinction between these two that have been stated, he says—

children.text: viśuddhyapratipātābhyāṃ tadviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The distinction between them is due to purity (<s>viśuddhi</s>) and non-falling (<s>apratipāta</s>). ||

children.text: § 220. tadāvaraṇakṣayopaśame sati ātmanaḥ prasādo viśuddhiḥ. pratipatanaṃ pratipātaḥ. na pratipātaḥ apratipātaḥ. upaśāntakaṣāyasya cāritramohodrekāt pracyutasaṃyamaśikharasya pratipāto bhavati. kṣīṇakaṣāyasya pratipātakāraṇābhāvād apratipātaḥ. viśuddhiś ca apratipātaś ca viśuddhyapratipātau. tābhyāṃ viśuddhyapratipātābhyām. tayor viśeṣas tadviśeṣaḥ. tatra viśuddhyā tāvat — ṛjumater vipulamatir dravyakṣetrakālabhāvair viśuddhataraḥ. katham? iha yaḥ kārmaṇadravyānantabhāgo ’ntyaḥ sarvāvadhinā jñātas tasya punar anantabhāgīkṛtasyāntyo bhāga ṛjumater viṣayaḥ. tasya ṛjumativiṣayasyānantabhāgīkṛtasyāntyo bhāgo vipulamater viṣayaḥ. anantasyānantabhedatvāt. dravyakṣetrakālato viśuddhir uktā. bhāvato viśuddhiḥ sūkṣmataradravyaviṣayatvād eva veditavyā, prakṛṣṭakṣayopaśamaviśuddhiyogāt. apratipātenāpi vipulamatir viśiṣṭaḥ; svāmināṃ pravardhamānacāritrodayatvāt. ṛjumatiḥ punaḥ pratipātī; svāmināṃ kaṣāyodrekād dhīyamānacāritrodayatvāt.
children.translated_text: § 220. When there is destruction-cum-subsidence of the relevant obscuring [<s>karma</s>], the clarity of the self is purity (<s>viśuddhi</s>). Falling down is <s>pratipāta</s>. Non-falling is <s>apratipāta</s>. For one whose passions have subsided (<s>upaśāntakaṣāya</s>), falling occurs due to the surge of conduct-deluding [<s>karma</s>], as one falls from the peak of restraint. For one whose passions have been destroyed (<s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s>), there is non-falling due to the absence of a cause for falling. Purity and non-falling together are <s>viśuddhyapratipāta</s>. By these two—purity and non-falling—their distinction is [established]. Regarding purity: the <s>vipulamati</s> is purer than the <s>ṛjumati</s> in terms of substance (<s>dravya</s>), space (<s>kṣetra</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), and disposition (<s>bhāva</s>). How? Here, the final innumerable fraction of <s>kārmaṇa</s> substance cognized by all forms of <s>avadhi</s>—of that, when further divided into innumerable parts, the final part is the object of <s>ṛjumati</s>. Of that <s>ṛjumati</s>'s object, when further divided into innumerable parts, the final part is the object of <s>vipulamati</s>—because the infinite can be infinitely subdivided. Purity in terms of substance, space, and time has been stated. Purity in terms of disposition should be understood from the fact that its object is subtler substance, due to the excellence of its destruction-cum-subsidence purity. In terms of non-falling too, <s>vipulamati</s> is superior, because its possessors have an increasing manifestation of conduct. But <s>ṛjumati</s> is subject to falling, because its possessors have a decreasing manifestation of conduct due to the surge of passions.

children.text: § 221. yady asya manaḥparyayasya pratyātmamayaṃ viśeṣaḥ, athānayor avadhimanaḥparyayayoḥ kuto viśeṣaḥ ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 221. If the distinction of this mind-reading knowledge is internal to each individual, then what is the distinction between <s>avadhi</s> (clairvoyant knowledge) and <s>manaḥparyaya</s> (mind-reading knowledge)? To this he says—

children.text: viśuddhikṣetrasvāmiviṣayebhyo ’vadhimanaḥparyayayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: The distinction between <s>avadhi</s> and <s>manaḥparyaya</s> is due to purity (<s>viśuddhi</s>), spatial range (<s>kṣetra</s>), possessor (<s>svāmin</s>), and object (<s>viṣaya</s>). ||

children.text: § 222. viśuddhiḥ prasādaḥ. kṣetraṃ yatrasthān bhāvān pratipadyate. svāmī prayoktā. viṣayo jñeyaḥ. tatrāvadher manaḥparyayo viśuddhataraḥ. kutaḥ? sūkṣmaviṣayatvāt. kṣetram uktam. viṣayo vakṣyate. svāmitvaṃ pratyutyate. prakṛṣṭacāritraguṇopeteṣu vartate pramattādiṣu kṣīṇakaṣayānteṣu. tatra cotpadyamānaḥ pravarddhamānacāritreṣu na hīyamānacāritreṣu. pravarddhamānacāritreṣu cotpadyamānaḥ saptavidhānyatamarddhiprāpteṣūpajāyate netareṣu. ṛddhiprāpteṣu keṣucin na sarveṣu. ity asyāyaṃ svāmiviśeṣo viśiṣṭasaṃyamagrahaṇaṃ vā vākye prakṛtam. avadhiḥ punaś cāturgatikeṣv iti svāmibhedād apy anayor viśeṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 222. Purity (<s>viśuddhi</s>) is clarity. The spatial range (<s>kṣetra</s>) is the area within which it cognizes entities. The possessor (<s>svāmin</s>) is the user. The object (<s>viṣaya</s>) is what is to be known. Of these, <s>manaḥparyaya</s> is purer than <s>avadhi</s>. Why? Because its object is subtler. The spatial range has been stated. The object will be stated. The possessor is now addressed. It [<s>manaḥparyaya</s>] operates among those endowed with excellent conduct-qualities, from the restrained with negligence (<s>pramatta</s>) and onwards up to those with destroyed passions (<s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s>). And when arising among them, it arises among those with increasing conduct, not among those with decreasing conduct. And when arising among those with increasing conduct, it arises among those who have attained one of the seven types of supernatural accomplishments (<s>ṛddhi</s>), not among others. Among those who have attained accomplishments, it arises in some, not in all. Thus, this is its distinction regarding the possessor—or the phrase 'distinguished restraint' is the principal [qualification] in the statement. <s>Avadhi</s>, however, exists among beings of all four destinies—thus the distinction between them is also due to difference of possessor.

children.text: § 223. idānīṃ kevalajñānalakṣaṇābhidhānaṃ prāptakālam. tadullaṅghya jñānāṃ viṣayanibandhaḥ parīkṣyate. kutaḥ? tasya ‘mohakṣayāj jñānadarśanāvaraṇāntarāyakṣayāc ca kevalam’ ity atra vakṣyamānatvāt. yady evam ādyayor eva tāvan matiśrutayor viṣayanibandha ucyatām ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 223. Now is the proper time for stating the definition of omniscient knowledge (<s>kevalajñāna</s>). Setting that aside, the object-scope of the [various] knowledges is examined [first]. Why? Because that [<s>kevalajñāna</s>] will be explained later in [the sūtra] 'From the destruction of delusion and the destruction of knowledge-obscuring, perception-obscuring, and obstructive [karmas comes] the absolute (<s>kevala</s>).' If so, let the object-scope of sensory and scriptural knowledge be stated first—to this he says—

children.text: matiśrutayor nibandho dravyesv asarvaparyāyeṣu ||
children.translated_text: The scope of sensory knowledge (<s>mati</s>) and scriptural knowledge (<s>śruta</s>) extends to substances in their non-total modes (<s>asarvaparyāya</s>). ||

children.text: § 224. nibandhanaṃ nibandhaḥ. kasya? viṣayasya. tadviṣayagrahaṇaṃ kartavyam? na kartavyam. prakṛtaṃ viṣayagrahaṇam. kva prakṛtam? ‘viśuddhikṣetrasvāmiviṣayebhyaḥ’ ity atra. atas tasyārthavaśād vibhaktipariṇāmo bhavatīti ‘viṣayasya’ ity abhisaṃbadhyate. ‘dravyeṣu’ iti bahuvacananirdeśaḥ sarveṣāṃ jīvadharmādharmakālākāśapudgalānāṃ saṃgrahārthaḥ. tadviśeṣaṇārthaṃ ‘asarvaparyāya’ grahaṇam. tāni dravyāṇi matiśrutayor viṣayabhāvam āpadyamānāni katipayair eva paryāyair viṣayabhāvam āskandanti na sarvaparyāyair anantair apīti. atrāha — dharmāstikāyādīny atīndriyaṇi teṣu matijñānaṃ na pravartate. ataḥ sarvadravyeṣu matijñānaṃ vartata ity ayuktam? naiṣa doṣaḥ; anindriyākhyaṃ karaṇam asti tadālambano noindriyāvaraṇakṣayopaśamalabdhipūrvaka upayogo ’vagrahādirūpaḥ pragevopajāyate. tatas tatpūrvaṃ śrutajñānaṃ tadviṣayeṣu svayogyeṣu vyāpriyate.
children.translated_text: § 224. '<s>Nibandhana</s>' is '<s>nibandha</s>' (scope/binding). Of what? Of the object (<s>viṣaya</s>). Should the word '<s>viṣaya</s>' be explicitly stated? It need not be, since '<s>viṣaya</s>' is already the topic under discussion. Where was it discussed? In [the sūtra] 'from purity, spatial range, possessor, and object.' Therefore, by force of meaning, the case-ending changes, and it connects as 'of the object.' The plural form 'in substances' (<s>dravyeṣu</s>) is for the purpose of including all [substances]: souls (<s>jīva</s>), the medium of motion (<s>dharma</s>), the medium of rest (<s>adharma</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), space (<s>ākāśa</s>), and matter (<s>pudgala</s>). The qualifier '<s>asarvaparyāya</s>' (not-all-modes) is used to qualify those [substances]: those substances, when becoming the objects of sensory and scriptural knowledge, become objects through only some modes, not through all their infinite modes. Here one objects: the medium of motion (<s>dharmāstikāya</s>) and others are supersensory; sensory knowledge does not operate regarding them. Therefore, it is improper to say sensory knowledge operates regarding all substances? This is no fault; there exists a sense-organ called non-sensory (<s>anindriya</s>), i.e. the mind, and the active consciousness in the form of apprehension (<s>avagraha</s>) etc., preceded by the attainment of destruction-cum-subsidence of the non-sensory obscuration, arises regarding its objects first. Then, scriptural knowledge preceded by that operates regarding its own suitable objects.

children.text: § 225. atha matiśrutayor anantaranirdeśārhasyāvadheḥ ko viṣayanibandha ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 225. Now, what is the object-scope of <s>avadhi</s> (clairvoyant knowledge), which deserves to be stated next after sensory and scriptural knowledge? To this he says—

children.text: rūpiṣv avadeḥ ||
children.translated_text: The scope of <s>avadhi</s> is in material entities (<s>rūpin</s>). ||

children.text: § 226. ‘viṣayanibandhaḥ’ ity anuvartate. ‘rūpiṣu’ ity anena pudgalāḥ pudgaladravyasaṃbandhāś ca jīvāḥ parigṛhyante. rūpiṣv evāvadher viṣayanibandho nārūpiṣv iti niyamaḥ kriyate. rūpiṣv api bhavan na sarvaparyāyeṣu, svayogyeṣv evety avadhāraṇārtham asarvaparyāyeṣv ity abhisaṃbadhyate.
children.translated_text: § 226. 'Object-scope' (<s>viṣayanibandha</s>) is carried forward [from the previous sūtra]. By the word '<s>rūpiṣu</s>' (in material entities), matter (<s>pudgala</s>) and souls (<s>jīva</s>) connected with material substance are included. The restriction is made that the object-scope of <s>avadhi</s> is only in material entities, not in non-material ones. Even among material entities, it does not extend to all modes, but only to those suitable to it—for this purpose of restriction, '<s>asarvaparyāyeṣu</s>' (not-in-all-modes) is connected.

children.text: § 227. atha tadanantaranirdeśabhājo manaḥparyayasya ko viṣayanibandha ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 227. Now, what is the object-scope of mind-reading knowledge (<s>manaḥparyaya</s>), which deserves to be stated next? To this he says—

children.text: tadanantabhāge manaḥparyayasya ||
children.translated_text: The scope of mind-reading knowledge (<s>manaḥparyaya</s>) is an infinitesimal fraction of that [<s>avadhi</s>'s scope]. ||

children.text: § 228. yad etad rūpi dravyaṃ sarvāvadhijñānaviṣayatvena samarthitaṃ tasyānantabhāgīkṛtasyaikasmin bhāge manaḥparyayaḥ pravartate.
children.translated_text: § 228. That material substance which has been established as the object of all forms of clairvoyant knowledge (<s>avadhi</s>)—when that is divided into infinite parts, mind-reading knowledge (<s>manaḥparyaya</s>) operates in one such part.

children.text: § 229. athānte yan nirdiṣṭaṃ kevalajñānaṃ tasya ko viṣayanibandha ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 229. Now, what is the object-scope of the omniscient knowledge (<s>kevalajñāna</s>) that was mentioned last? To this he says—

children.text: sarvadravyaparyāyeṣu kevalasya ||
children.translated_text: The scope of omniscient knowledge (<s>kevala</s>) extends to all substances and all modes (<s>sarvadravyaparyāyeṣu</s>). ||

children.text: § 230. dravyāṇi ca paryāyāś ca dravyaparyāyā iti itaretarayogalakṣaṇo dvandvaḥ. tadviśeṣaṇaṃ ‘sarva’ grahaṇaṃ pratyekam abhisaṃbadhyate, sarveṣu dravyeṣu sarveṣu paryāyeṣv iti. jīvadravyāṇi tāvad anantānantāni tato ’py anantānantāni pudgaladravyāṇi ca aṇuskandhabhedabhinnāni, dharmādharmākāśāni trīṇi, kālaś cāsaṃkhyeyas teṣāṃ paryāyāś ca trikālabhuvaḥ pratyekam anantānantās teṣu. dravyaṃ paryāyajātaṃ vā na kiṃcit kevalajñānasya viṣayabhāvam atikrāntam asti. aparimitamāhātmyaṃ hi tad iti jñāpanārthaṃ ‘sarvadravyaparyāyeṣu’ ity ucyate.
children.translated_text: § 230. Substances and modes together form the compound '<s>dravyaparyāya</s>' as a copulative (<s>dvandva</s>) compound characterized by mutual connection. The qualifier 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) connects with each separately: in all substances, in all modes. The soul-substances (<s>jīvadravya</s>) are innumerably infinite; even more innumerably infinite are the matter-substances (<s>pudgaladravya</s>), divided into atoms and aggregates; the media of motion and rest and space are three; and time is innumerable. Their modes, existing across the three times, are innumerably infinite for each. There is no substance or class of modes whatsoever that has transcended the object-status of omniscient knowledge. To indicate that its greatness is unlimited, it is said 'in all substances and modes.'

children.text: § 231. āha viṣayanibandho ’vadhṛto matyādīnām. idaṃ tu na nirjñātam ekasminn ātmani svanimittasaṃnidhānopajanitavṛttīni jñānāni yaugapadyena kati bhavantīty ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 231. He says: the object-scope has been ascertained for sensory knowledge and the rest. But this has not been determined: how many knowledges, whose functions have arisen through the presence of their respective causes, can exist simultaneously in one self? It is said—

children.text: ekādīni bhājyāni yugapad ekasminn ā caturbhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Beginning with one, [knowledges] are to be distributed simultaneously in one [self], up to four. ||

children.text: § 232. ekaśabdaḥ saṃkhyāvacī, ādiśabdo ’vayavavacanaḥ. eka ādir yeṣāṃ tāni imāny ekādīni. bhājyāni vibhaktavyāni. yaugapadyenaikasminn ātmani. ā kutaḥ? ā caturbhyaḥ. tadyathā ekaṃ tāvat kevalajñānaṃ, na tena sahānyāni kṣāyopaśamikāni yugapadavatiṣṭhante. dve matiśrute. trīṇi matiśrutāvadhijñānāni, matiśrutamanaḥparyayajñānāni vā. catvāri matiśrutāvadhimanaḥparyayajñānāni. na pañca santi, kevalasyāsahāyatvāt.
children.translated_text: § 232. The word 'one' (<s>eka</s>) denotes number; the word 'beginning' (<s>ādi</s>) denotes component parts. Those whose beginning is one—these are 'beginning with one' (<s>ekādīni</s>). 'To be distributed' (<s>bhājyāni</s>) means to be divided. Simultaneously in one self. From where? Up to four. That is: first, one—omniscient knowledge (<s>kevalajñāna</s>) alone; other [knowledges] born of destruction-cum-subsidence do not co-exist with it simultaneously. Two—sensory and scriptural knowledge (<s>mati</s> and <s>śruta</s>). Three—sensory, scriptural, and clairvoyant knowledge; or sensory, scriptural, and mind-reading knowledge. Four—sensory, scriptural, clairvoyant, and mind-reading knowledge. There are not five, because omniscient knowledge has no companion.

children.text: § 233. atha yathoktāni matyādīni jñānavyapadeśam eva labhante utānyathāpīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 233. Now, do the above-mentioned sensory knowledge etc. always receive the designation 'knowledge,' or can it be otherwise? To this he says—

children.text: matiśrutāvadhayo viparyayaś ca ||
children.translated_text: Sensory knowledge (<s>mati</s>), scriptural knowledge (<s>śruta</s>), and clairvoyant knowledge (<s>avadhi</s>) [can be valid knowledge]; and also their erroneous counterpart (<s>viparyaya</s>). ||

children.text: § 234. viparyayo mithyety arthaḥ. kutaḥ? samyagadhikārāt. ‘ca’ śabdah samuccayārthaḥ. viparyayaś ca samyak ceti. kutaḥ punar eṣāṃ viparyayaḥ? mithyādarśanena sahaikārthasamavāyāt sarajaskakaṭukālābugatadugdhavat. nanu ca tatrādhāradoṣād dugdasya rasaviparyayo bhavati. na ca tathā matyajñānādīnāṃ viṣayagrahaṇe viparyayaḥ. tathā hi, samyagdṛṣṭir yathā cakṣurādibhī rūpādīn upalabhate tathā mityādṛṣṭir api matyajñānena. yathā ca samyagdṛṣṭiḥ śrutena rūpādin jānāti nirūpayati ca tathā mithyādṛṣṭir api śrutājñānena. yathā cāvadhijñānena samyagdṛṣṭiḥ rūpiṇo ’rthānavagacchati tathā mithyādṛṣṭir vibhaṅgajñāneneti.
children.translated_text: § 234. The meaning of <s>viparyaya</s> (wrong [knowledge]) is <s>mithyā</s> (false). Why? Because of the context being right [knowledge, and 'wrong' is stated in contrast to it]. The word 'ca' is used in the sense of conjunction: 'wrong and right.' But why is there wrong [knowledge] in these [sensory knowledge, etc.]? Because of the co-inherence in a single object with wrong faith (<s>mithyādarśana</s>) — like milk that has entered a bitter gourd mixed with impurities [becomes tainted]. Objection: There, it is due to the defect of the container that the taste of the milk is perverted. But there is no such perversion in the apprehension of objects by wrong sensory knowledge and the like. For, just as one with right faith perceives forms and the like through the eyes and other senses, so too does one with wrong faith through wrong sensory knowledge. And just as one with right faith knows and ascertains forms and the like through scriptural knowledge, so too does one with wrong faith through wrong scriptural knowledge. And just as one with right faith comprehends material objects through clairvoyant knowledge, so too does one with wrong faith through wrong clairvoyance (<s>vibhaṅgajñāna</s>).

children.text: § 235. atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 235. To this, it is replied —

children.text: sadasator aviśeṣād yadṛcchopalabdher unmattavat ||
children.translated_text: Because of non-discrimination between the existent and the non-existent, [there is] random apprehension, like a madman.

children.text: § 236. sad vidyamānam asad avidyamānam ity arthaḥ. tayor aviśeṣeṇa yadṛchhayā upalabder viparyayo bhavati. kadācid rūpādi sad apy asad iti pratipadyate, asad api sad iti, kadācit sat sad eva, asad apy asad eveti mithyādarśanodayād adhyavasyati. yathā pittodayākulitabuddhir mātaraṃ bhāryeti, bhāryām api māteti manyate. yadṛcchayā yadāpi mātaraṃ mātaiveti bhāryam api bhāryeveti ca tadāpi na tatsamyagjñānam.

evaṃ matyādīnām api rūpādiṣu viparyayo veditavyaḥ. tathā hi, kaścin mityādarśanapariṇāma ātmany avasthito rūpādyupalabdhau satyām api kāraṇaviparyāsaṃ bhedābhedaviparyāsaṃ svarūpaviparyāsaṃ ca janayati.
children.translated_text: Thus, for sensory knowledge and the rest too, perversion with regard to forms and the like should be understood. For indeed, a certain transformation of wrong faith, established in the soul, even when there is apprehension of forms and the like, generates perversion of cause, perversion of identity-and-difference, and perversion of intrinsic nature.

§ 236. <s>Sat</s> means 'existing'; <s>asat</s> means 'non-existing' — this is the meaning. Through non-discrimination between these two, by random apprehension, there is perversion. Sometimes one cognizes form and the like, though existent, as non-existent; the non-existent too as existent. Sometimes one determines the existent as indeed existent, the non-existent as indeed non-existent — [yet even so] due to the arising of wrong faith, one ascertains [incorrectly]. Just as one whose intellect is agitated by the arising of bile considers his mother to be his wife, and his wife to be his mother. Even when he randomly considers his mother to be indeed his mother and his wife to be indeed his wife, even then it is not true right knowledge.

children.text: § 237. kāraṇaviparyāsas tāvad — rūpādīnām ekaṃ kāraṇam amūrtaṃ nityam iti kecit kalpayanti. apare pṛthivyādijātibhinnāḥ paramāṇavaś catustridvyeka guṇās tulyajātīyānāṃ kāryāṇām ārambhakā iti. anye varṇayanti — pṛthivyādīni catvāri bhūtāni, bhautikadharmā varṇagandharasasparśāḥ, eteṣāṃ samudāyo rūpaparamāṇur aṣṭaka ity ādi. itare varṇayanti — pṛthivyaptejovāyavaḥ kāṭhinyādidravatvādyuṣṇatvādīraṇatvādiguṇā jātibhinnāḥ paramāṇavaḥ kāryasyārambhakāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 237. First, perversion of cause (<s>kāraṇaviparyāsa</s>) — some imagine that the single cause of forms and the like is formless and eternal. Others [assert]: atoms differentiated by the classes of earth and the like, possessing four, three, two, or one quality, are the producers of effects belonging to the same class. Yet others describe: the four elements — earth, water, fire, and air — with the material properties of color, smell, taste, and touch; the aggregate of these is the form-atom, [composed of] eight [substances], and so on. Still others describe: earth, water, fire, and air are atoms differentiated by class, possessing qualities of hardness, fluidity, heat, and mobility respectively, and are the producers of effects.

children.text: § 238. bhedābhedaviparyāsaḥ kāraṇāt kāryam arthāntarabhūtam eveti anarthāntarabhūtam eveti ca parikalpanā.
children.translated_text: § 238. Perversion of identity-and-difference (<s>bhedābheda-viparyāsa</s>) is the construction that the effect is absolutely different from the cause, or absolutely non-different from it.

children.text: § 239. svarūpaviparyāso rūpādiyo nirvikalpāḥ santi na santy eva vā. tadākārapariṇataṃ vijñānam eva. na ca tadālambanaṃ vastu bāhyam iti. evam anyān api parikalpanābhedān dṛṣṭeṣṭaviruddhān mithyādarśanodayāt kalpayanti tatra ca śraddhānam utpādayanti. tatas tanmatyajñānaṃ śrutājñānam vibhaṅgajñānaṃ ca bhavati. samyagdarśanaṃ punas tatvārthādhigame śraddhānam utpādayati. tatas tanmatijñānaṃ śrutajñām avadhijñānānaṃ ca bhavati.
children.translated_text: § 239. Perversion of intrinsic nature (<s>svarūpa-viparyāsa</s>) [consists in views such as]: forms and the like are without determinate characteristics, or they do not exist at all; [they are] merely cognition transformed into those appearances, and there is no external object as their support. Thus, other varieties of false construction too, which are contrary to what is observed and accepted, should be understood as born from wrong faith [and thus constituting] wrong knowledge.

children.text: § 240. āha pramāṇaṃ dvi prakāraṃ varṇitam. pramāṇaikadeśāś ca nayās tadanantaroddeśabhājo nirdeṣṭavyā ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 240. He says: <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) has been described as twofold. And the <s>nayas</s> (standpoints), which are partial aspects of <s>pramāṇa</s>, are to be specified in the section immediately following — therefore he says:

children.text: naigamasaṃgrahavyavahārarjusūtraśabdasamabhirūḍhaivaṃbhūtā nayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>nayas</s> (standpoints) are: <s>naigama</s> (figurative), <s>saṃgraha</s> (synthetic), <s>vyavahāra</s> (analytic), <s>ṛjusūtra</s> (straightforward), <s>śabda</s> (verbal), <s>samabhirūḍha</s> (etymological), and <s>evaṃbhūta</s> (actuality).

children.text: § 241. eteṣāṃ sāmānyaviśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ vaktavyam. sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ tāvad vastuny anekāntātmany avirodhena hetvarpaṇāt sādhyaviśeṣasya yathātmyaprāpaṇapravaṇaḥ prayogo nayaḥ. sa dvedhā dravyārthikaḥ paryāyārthikaś ceti. dravyaṃ sāmānyam utsargaḥ anuvṛttir ity arthaḥ. tadviṣayo dravyārthikaḥ. paryāyo viśeṣo ’pavādo vyāvṛttir ity arthaḥ. tadviṣayaḥ paryāyārthikaḥ. tayor bhedā naigamādayaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 241. Their general and specific characteristics must be stated. The general characteristic first: a <s>naya</s> is the application inclined toward conveying the true nature of the particular object to be established, through the assignment of a reason, without contradiction, with respect to a thing that is of manifold nature (<s>anekānta</s>). It is twofold: <s>dravyārthika</s> (substance-oriented) and <s>paryāyārthika</s> (mode-oriented).

children.text: § 242. teṣāṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇam ucyate — anabhinirvṛttārthasaṃkalpamātragrāhī naigamaḥ. kaṃcit puruṣaṃ parigṛhītaparaśuṃ gacchantam avalokya kaścit pṛcchati kim arthaṃ bhavān gacchatīti. sa āha prastham ānetum iti. nāsau tadā prasthaparyāyaḥ saṃnihitaḥ. tadabhinirvṛttaye saṃkalpamātre prasthavyavhāraḥ. tathā edhodakādyāharaṇe vyāpriyamāṇaṃ kaścit pṛcchati kiṃ karoti bhavān iti. sa āha odanaṃ pacāmīti. na tadaudanaparyāyaḥ, saṃnihitaḥ, tadarthe vyāpāre sa prayujyate. evaṃ prakāro lokasaṃvyavahāraḥ anabhinirvṛttārthasaṃkalpamātraviṣayo naigamasya gocaraḥ.
children.translated_text: § 242. Their specific characteristics are stated: <s>Naigama</s> (figurative) is that which grasps mere intention regarding a purpose not yet accomplished. [Example:] Seeing a certain person going with an axe taken up, someone asks, 'For what purpose are you going, sir?' He replies, 'To fetch a <s>prastha</s> [measure of grain].'

children.text: § 243. svajātyavirodhenaikadhyam upānīya paryāyān ākrāntabhedān aviśeṣeṇa samastagrahaṇāt saṃgrahaḥ. sat, dravyaṃ, ghaṭa ity ādi. sad ity ukte sad iti vāgvijñanānupravṛttiliṅgānumitasattādhārabhūtānām aviśeṣeṇa sarveṣāṃ saṃgrahaḥ. dravyam ity ukte ’pi dravati gacchati tāṃs tān paryāyān ity upalakṣitānāṃ jīvājīvatadbhedaprabhedānāṃ saṃgrahaḥ. tathā ghaṭa ity ukte ’pi ghaṭabuddhyabhidhānānugamaliṅgānumitasakalārthasaṃgrahaḥ. evam prakāro ’nyo ’pi saṃgrahanayasya viṣayaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 243. <s>Saṃgraha</s> (synthetic) is the comprehensive grasping, without distinction, by bringing together modes — whose differences have been transcended — into unity, without contradiction to their own class. [Examples:] '<s>sat</s>' (existent), '<s>dravya</s>' (substance), '<s>ghaṭa</s>' (pot), and so on. When one says '<s>sat</s>,' entities that serve as the substratum of existence — inferred through the marks of verbal and cognitive engagement — [are all grasped].

children.text: § 244. saṃgrahanayākṣiptānām arthānāṃ vidhipūrvakam avaharaṇaṃ vyavahāraḥ. ko vidhiḥ? yaḥ saṃgrahagṛhīto ’rthas tadānupūrveṇaiva vyavahāraḥ pravartata ity ayaṃ vidhiḥ. tad yathā — sarvasaṃgraheṇa yat sattvaṃ gṛhītaṃ tac cānapekṣitaviśeṣaṃ nālaṃ saṃvyavahārāyeti vyavahāranaya āśrīyate. yat sat tad dravyaṃ guṇo veti. dravyeṇāpi saṃgrahākṣiptena jīvājīvaviśeṣānapekṣeṇa na śakyaḥ saṃvyavahāra iti jīvadravyam ajīvadravyam iti vā vyavahāra āśrīyate. jīvājīvāv api ca saṃgrahākṣiptau nālaṃ saṃvyavahārāyeti pratyekaṃ devanārakādir ghaṭādiś ca vyavahāreṇāśrīyate. evam ayaṃ nayas tāvad vartate yāvat punar nāsti vibhāgaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 244. <s>Vyavahāra</s> (analytic) is the methodical differentiation of objects that have been subsumed by the synthetic standpoint. What is the method? The method is this: an object grasped by the synthetic [standpoint] is differentiated through analysis in that very order. Thus, what is grasped by the all-comprehensive synthesis [is then broken down accordingly].

children.text: § 245. ṛjuṃ praguṇaṃ sūtrayati tan trayatīti ṛjusūtraḥ. pūrvāparāṃs trikālaviṣayān atiśayya vartamānakālaviṣayān ādatte atītānāgatayor vinaṣṭānutpannatvena vyavahārābhāvāt. tac ca vartamānaṃ samayamātram. tadviṣayaparyāyamātragrāhyam ṛjusūtraḥ. nanu saṃvyavahāralopaprasaṅga iti ced? na; asya nayasya viṣayamātrapradarśanaṃ kriyate. sarvanayasamūhasādhyo hi lokasaṃvyavahāraḥ.
children.translated_text: § 245. That which threads (<s>sūtrayati</s>) straightforwardly (<s>ṛju</s>), i.e., directly — that is <s>ṛjusūtra</s> (straightforward). Surpassing [objects] pertaining to past and future — the three times — it takes up [only] objects pertaining to the present time, because there is no practical usage regarding the past and future since they are destroyed and not yet arisen. And that present [is understood] from the [unit of] <s>samaya</s> (instant) [onwards].

children.text: § 246. liṅgasaṃkhyāsādhanādivyabhicāranivṛttiparaḥ śabdanayaḥ. tatra liṅgavyabhicāraḥ — puṣyas tārakā nakṣatram iti. saṃkhyāvyabhicṝaḥ — jalam āpaḥ, varṣā ṛtuḥ, āmrā vanam, varaṇā nagaram iti. sādhanavyabhicāraḥ — senā parvatam adhivasati. puruṣavyabhicāraḥ — ehi manye rathena yāsyasi, na hi yāsyasi, yātas te piteti. kālavyabhicāraḥ — viśvadṛśvā ’sya putro janitā. bhāvi kṛtyam āsīd iti. upagrahavyabhicāraḥ — saṃtiṣṭhate pratiṣṭhate viramaty uparamatīti. evaṃ prakāraṃ vyavahāramanyāyyaṃ manyate; anyārthasyānyārthena saṃbandhābhāvāt. lokasamayavirodha iti cet? virudhyatām. tattvam iha mīmāṃsyate, na bhaiṣajyam āturecchānuvarti.
children.translated_text: § 246. The <s>śabda-naya</s> (verbal standpoint) is concerned with preventing deviation of gender, number, causation, and the like. Therein, deviation of gender: <s>puṣya</s> [is masculine], <s>tārakā</s> [is feminine], <s>nakṣatra</s> [is neuter — yet all denote the same star]. Deviation of number: <s>jalam</s> (water, singular), <s>āpaḥ</s> (waters, plural); <s>varṣā</s> (rain, singular), <s>ṛtu</s> (season); <s>āmrā</s> (mango trees), <s>vanam</s> (forest); <s>varaṇā</s> (trees), <s>nagaram</s> (city). [Further deviations of] causation [are also addressed].

children.text: § 247. nānārthaśamabhirohaṇāt samabhirūḍhaḥ. yato nānārthān samatīty aikam artham ābhimukhyena rūḍhaḥ samabhirūḍhaḥ. gaur ity ayaṃ śabdo vāgādiṣv artheṣu vartamānaḥ paśāv abhirūḍhaḥ. athavā arthagatyarthaḥ śabdaprayogaḥ. tatraikasyārthasyaikena gatārthatvāt paryāyaśabdaprayogo ’narthakaḥ. śabdabhedāś ced asti arthabhedenāpy avaśyaṃ bhavitavyam iti. nānārthasamabhirohaṇāt samabhirūḍhaḥ. indanād indraḥ śakanāc chakraḥ pūrdāranāt puradara

ity evaṃ sarvatra. athavā yo yatrābhirūḍhaḥ sa tatra sametyābhimukhenārohaṇāt samabhirūḍhaḥ. yathā kva bhavān āste? ātmanīti. kutaḥ? vastv antare vṛttyabhāvāt. yady anyasyānyatra vṛttiḥ syāt, jñānādīnāṃ rūpādīnāṃ cākaśe vṛttiḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: thus everywhere. Alternatively, that which is established somewhere — it, having approached there, ascends facing [that meaning] — hence <s>samabhirūḍha</s>. For example: 'Where does the venerable one abide?' 'In the self.' Why? Because there is no activity in any other thing. If there were the activity of one in another, [then] knowledge and the like [would abide elsewhere].

§ 247. <s>Samabhirūḍha</s> (etymological) is [defined as] ascending equally to one of many meanings. Since, having passed over the many meanings, it is established (<s>rūḍha</s>) directly facing one meaning — [it is called] <s>samabhirūḍha</s>. The word <s>go</s> (cow), which is applicable to speech and other objects, is established [specifically] in the sense of 'bovine animal.' Alternatively, by the derivation of meaning —

children.text: § 248. yenātmanā bhūtas tenaivādhyavasāyayatīti evaṃbhūtaḥ. svābhipretakriyāpariṇatikṣaṇe eva sa śabdo yukto nānyadeti. yadaivendati tadaivendro nābhiṣecako na pūjaka iti. yadaiva gacchati tadaiva gaur na sthito na śayita iti. athavā yenātmanā yena jñānena bhūtaḥ pariṇatas tenaivādhyavasāyayati. yathendrāgnijñānapariṇata ātmaivendro ’gniś ceti.
children.translated_text: § 248. <s>Evaṃbhūta</s> (actuality) means: one determines [a thing] only by the aspect by which it is [actually functioning] thus. A word is appropriate only at the moment of transformation into the activity intended by it, and not otherwise. Only when [<s>Indra</s>] 'exercises sovereignty' (<s>indati</s>) is he [truly] <s>Indra</s> — not when he is being consecrated or worshipped. Only when [the cow] 'goes' (<s>gacchati</s>) is it [truly] a <s>go</s> (cow).

children.text: § 249. uktā naigamādayo nayāḥ. uttarottarasūkṣmaviṣayatvād eṣāṃ kramaḥ pūrvapūrvahetukatvāc ca. evam ete nayāḥ pūrvapūrvaviruddhamahāviṣayā uttarottarānukūlālpaviṣayā dravyasyānantaśakteḥ pratiśakti vibhidyamānā bahuvikalpā jāyante. ta ete guṇapradhānatayā parasparatantrāḥ samyagdarśanahetavaḥ puruṣārthakriyāsādhanasāmarthyāt tantvādaya iva yathopāyaṃ viniveśyamānāḥ paṭādisaṃjñāḥ svatantrāś cāsamarthāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 249. The <s>nayas</s> beginning with <s>naigama</s> have been stated. Their order [follows] because each successive one has a subtler domain, and because each former one is the cause of [the next]. Thus these <s>nayas</s>, whose earlier members have a large domain contradicting [more refined perspectives] and whose later members have a small domain in agreement [with finer distinctions], may [each] express a [particular] power among the infinite powers of a substance.

children.text: § 250. tantvādaya iveti viṣama upanyāsaḥ. tantvādayo nirapekṣā api kāṃcid arthamātrāṃ janayanti. bhavati hi kaścit pratyekaṃ tantus tvaktrāṇe samarthaḥ. ekaś ca balvajo bandhane samarthaḥ. ime punar nayā nirapekṣāḥ santo na kāṃcid api samyagdarśanamātrāṃ prādur bhāvayantīti? naiṣa doṣaḥ; abhihitānavabodhāt. abhihitam artham anavabudhya pareṇedam upālabhyate. etad uktaṃ, nirapekṣeṣu tantvādiṣu paṭādikāryaṃ nāstīti. yat tu tenopadarśitaṃ na tat paṭādikāryam. kiṃ tarhi? kevalaṃ tantvādikāryam. tantvādikaryam api tantvādyavayaveṣu nirapekṣeṣu nāsty eva ity asmatpakṣasiddhir eva. atha tantvādiṣu paṭādikāryaṃ śaktyapekṣayā astīty ucyate. nayeṣv api nirapekṣeṣu buddhyabhidhānarūpeṣu kāraṇavaśāt samyagdarśanahetutvavipariṇatisadbhāvāt. śaktyātmanāstitvam iti sāmyam evopanyāsasya.
children.translated_text: § 250. The illustration 'like threads and the like' is an imprecise analogy. Threads and the like, even independently, produce some effect. For indeed, a single thread is capable of protecting the skin, and a single rope-blade is capable of binding. But these [<s>nayas</s>], [taken independently], do not [yield valid knowledge].

children.text: iti tattvārthavṛttau sarvārthasiddhisaṃjñāyāṃ prathamo ’dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter of the <s>Tattvārthavṛtti</s> named <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>.

children.text: atha dvitīyo ’dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins the second chapter.

children.text: § 251. āha, samyagdarśanasya viṣayabhāvenopadiṣṭeṣu jīvādiṣv ādāv upanyas tasya jīvasya kiṃ svatattvam ity ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 251. He says: Among the <s>jīva</s> and the rest, which have been taught as the objects of right faith — the <s>jīva</s> being presented first — what is its own essential nature? It is said:

children.text: aupaśamikakṣāyikau bhāvau miśraś ca jīvasya svatattvam audayikapāriṇāmikau ca ||
children.translated_text: The <s>aupaśamika</s> (subsidence-born) and <s>kṣāyika</s> (destructional) states, and the mixed (<s>miśra</s>) [i.e., <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s>] — these are the own essential nature of the <s>jīva</s> (soul); also the <s>audayika</s> (arising from karmic fruition) and <s>pāriṇāmika</s> (transformational) [states].

children.text: § 252. ātmani karmaṇaḥ svaśakteḥ kāraṇavaśād anudbhūtir upaśamaḥ. yathā katakādidravyasaṃbandhād ambhasi paṃkasya upaśamaḥ. kṣaya ātyantikī nivṛttiḥ. yathā tasminn evāmbhasi śucibhājanāntarasaṃkrānte paṃkasyātyantābhāvaḥ. ubhayātmako miśraḥ. yathā tasminn evāmbhasi katakādidravyasaṃbandhāt paṃkasya kṣīṇākṣīṇavṛttiḥ. dravyādinimittavaśāt karmaṇāṃ phalaprāptir udayaḥ. dravyātmalābhamātrahetukaḥ pariṇāmaḥ. upaśamaḥ prayojanam asyety aupaśamikaḥ. evaṃ kṣāyikaḥ kṣāyopaśamikaḥ audayikaḥ pariṇāmikaś ca. ta ete pañca bhāvā asādharaṇā jīvasya svatattvam ity ucyante.
children.translated_text: § 252. <s>Upaśama</s> (subsidence) is the non-manifestation of the power of <s>karma</s> in the self, due to causal conditions—just as the settling of mud in water by contact with the clearing-nut (<s>kataka</s>) and similar substances. <s>Kṣaya</s> (destruction) is the absolute cessation—just as the complete absence of mud in that same water when transferred to a clean vessel. <s>Miśra</s> (mixed) is of both natures—just as in that same water, through contact with the clearing-nut, the mud's activity is partly destroyed and partly not. <s>Udaya</s> (fruition) is the attainment of the fruit of <s>karmas</s> due to conditions of substance and the like. <s>Pariṇāma</s> (inherent modification) is caused merely by the acquisition of the substance-nature of the self. That whose purpose is <s>upaśama</s> is <s>aupaśamika</s> (subsidence-born). Similarly, <s>kṣāyika</s> (destruction-born), <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s> (destruction-cum-subsidence-born), <s>audayika</s> (fruition-born), and <s>pāriṇāmika</s> (inherent-modification-born). These five <s>bhāvas</s> (states), being distinctive [to the soul], are called the own nature (<s>svatattvam</s>) of the <s>jīva</s> (soul).

children.text: § 253. samyagdarśanasya prakṛtatvāt tasya triṣu vikalpeṣu aupaśamikam ādau labhyata iti tasyādau grahaṇaṃ kriyate. tadanantaraṃ kṣāyikagrahaṇam; tasya pratiyogitvāt saṃsāry apekṣayā dravyatas tato ’saṃkyeyaguṇatvāc ca. tata uttaraṃ miśragrahaṇam; tadubhayātmakatvāt tato ’saṃkyeyaguṇatvāc ca. teṣāṃ sarveṣām anantaguṇatvād audayikapāriṇāmikagrahaṇam ante kriyate. atra dvandanirdeśaḥ kartavyaḥ — aupaśamikakṣāyikamiśraudayikapāriṇāmikā iti. tathā sati dviḥ ‘ca’ śabdo na kartavyo bhavati. naiva śaṅkyam; anyaguṇāpekṣayā iti pratīyate. vākye punaḥ sati ‘ca’ sabdena prakṛtobhayānukarṣaḥ kṛto bhavati. tarhi kṣāyopaśamikagrahaṇam eva kartavyam iti cet. na; gauravāt. miśragrahaṇaṃ madhye kriyate ubhayāpekṣārtham. bhavyasya aupaśamikakṣāyikau bhāvau. miśraḥ punar abhavyasyāpi bhavati, audayikapāriṇāmikābhyāṃ saha bhavyasyāpīti. bhāvāpekṣayā talliṅgasaṃkhyāprasaṅgaḥ svatattvasyeti cet? na; upāttaliṃgasaṃkhyatvāt. tadbhāvas tattvam. svaṃ tattvaṃ svatattvam iti.
children.translated_text: § 253. Since right faith (<s>samyagdarśana</s>) is the topic under discussion, among its three varieties, the <s>aupaśamika</s> (subsidence-born) is obtained first—therefore it is mentioned first. Next comes the mention of <s>kṣāyika</s> (destruction-born), since it is its counterpart, and from the perspective of transmigrating beings it is innumerably more in terms of substance-standpoint. Then the mention of <s>miśra</s> (mixed), since it is of both natures and is innumerably more than that. Since all of these are infinitely more, the mention of <s>audayika</s> and <s>pāriṇāmika</s> comes at the end. Here, a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound) construction should be used: <s>aupaśamika-kṣāyika-miśra-audayika-pāriṇāmika</s>. In that case, the particle '<s>ca</s>' need not be used twice. There should be no doubt [about the reading]; it is understood as 'with respect to other qualities.' But in a sentence, through the particle '<s>ca</s>', the inclusion of both [previously discussed items] is accomplished. [Objection:] Then should the term <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s> alone be used? [Reply:] No, because of prolixity. The term <s>miśra</s> (mixed) is placed in the middle for the purpose of relating to both. A <s>bhavya</s> (capable of liberation) soul has the <s>aupaśamika</s> and <s>kṣāyika</s> states. But <s>miśra</s> exists also for the <s>abhavya</s> (incapable of liberation), and also for the <s>bhavya</s> together with <s>audayika</s> and <s>pāriṇāmika</s>. [Objection:] From the standpoint of states, there should be the gender and number of those [states], since [the sūtra says] 'own nature'? [Reply:] No, because the gender and number adopted [in the sūtra] prevail. The state of that (<s>tad-bhāva</s>) is <s>tattva</s> (reality). One's own <s>tattva</s> is <s>svatattvam</s>.

children.text: § 254. atrāha tasyaikasyātmano ye bhāvā aupaśamkādayas te kiṃ bhedavanta utābhedā iti. attrocyate, bhedavantaḥ. yady evaṃ, bhedā ucyantām ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 254. Here one asks: those states of the one self such as <s>aupaśamika</s> and the rest—are they differentiated or undifferentiated? Here it is said: they are differentiated. If so, let the divisions be stated—thus he says—

children.text: dvinavāṣṭādaśaikaviṃśatitribhedā yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: Two, nine, eighteen, twenty-one, and three divisions, respectively. ||

children.text: § 255. dvyādīnāṃ saṃkhyāśabdānāṃ kṛtadvandvānāṃ bhedaśabdena saha svapadārthe ’nyapadārthe vā vṛttir veditavyā. dvau ca nava ca aṣṭādaśa ca ekaviṃśatiś ca trayaś ca dvinavāṣṭādaśaikaviṃśatitrayaḥ. te ca te bhedās ca, ta eva bhedā yeṣām iti vā vṛttir dvinavāṣṭādaśaikaviṃśatitribhedā ity. yadā svapadārthe vṛttis tadā aupaśamikādīnā bhāvānāṃ dvinavāṣṭādaśaikaviṃśatitrrayo bhedā ity abhisaṃbandhaḥ kriyate; arthavaśād vibhaktipariṇāma iti. yadānyapadārthe vṛttis tadā nirdiṣṭavibhaktyantā evābhisaṃbadhyante, aupaśamikādayo bhāvā dvinavāṣṭādaśaikaviṃśatitribhedā iti. ‘yathākrama’ vacanam yathāsaṃkhyapratipattyārtham. aupaśamiko dvibhedaḥ. kṣāyiko navabhedaḥ. miśro ’ṣṭādaśabhedaḥ. audayika ekaviṃśatibhedaḥ. pāriṇāmikas tribhedaḥ iti.
children.translated_text: § 255. The number-words 'two' and the rest, when compounded in a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound) with the word '<s>bheda</s>' (division), should be understood as operating either in their own meaning or in the meaning of another word. 'Two and nine and eighteen and twenty-one and three'—these are to be connected with the five states respectively.

children.text: § 256. yady evam aupaśamikasya kau dvau bhedāv ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 256. If so, what are the two divisions of the <s>aupaśamika</s> (subsidence-born state)? To this he says—

children.text: samyaktvacāritre ||
children.translated_text: Right faith (<s>samyaktva</s>) and right conduct (<s>cāritra</s>). ||

children.text: § 257. vyākhyātalakṣaṇe samyaktvacāritre. aupaśamikatvaṃ katham iti cet? ucyate — cāritramoho dvividaḥ kaṣāyavedanīyo nokaṣāyavedanīyaś ceti. tatra kaṣāyavedanīyasya bhedā anantānubandhinaḥ krodhamānamāyālobhāś catvāraḥ. darśanamohasya trayo bhedāḥ samyaktvaṃ mithyātvaṃ samyagmithyātvam iti. āsāṃ saptānāṃ pakṛtīnāmupaśamād aupaśamikaṃ samyaktvam.
children.translated_text: § 257. [These are] right faith and right conduct, whose definitions have been explained. How is the <s>aupaśamika</s> nature [of these]? It is said: conduct-deluding [<s>karma</s>] is twofold: <s>kaṣāya-vedanīya</s> (passion-experiencing) and <s>nokaṣāya-vedanīya</s> (quasi-passion-experiencing).

children.text: § 258. anādimithyādṛṣṭer bhavyasya karmodayāpāditakāluṣye sati kutas tadupaśamaḥ? kālalabdhyādinimittatvāt. tatra kālalabdhis tāvat — karmāviṣṭa ātmā bhavyaḥ kāle ’rddhapudgalaparivarttanākhye ’vaśiṣṭe prathamasamyaktvagrahaṇasya yogyo bhavati nādhike iti. iyam ekā kālalabdhiḥ. aparā karmasthitikā kālalabdhiḥ. utkṛṣṭasthitikeṣu karmasu jaghanyasthitikeṣu ca prathamasamyaktvalābho na bhavati. kva tarhi bhavati? antaḥkoṭīkoṭīsāgaropamasthitikeṣu karmasu bandham āpadhyamāneṣu viśuddhapariṇāmavaśāt satkarmasu ca tataḥ saṃkheyasāgaropamasahasronāyām antaḥkoṭīkoṭīsāgaropamasthitau sthāpiteṣu prathamasamyaktvayogyo bhavati. aparā kālalabdhir bhavāpekṣayā. bhavyaḥ pañcendriyaḥ saṃjñī paryāptikaḥ sarvaviśuddhaḥ prathamasamyaktvam utpādayati. ‘ādi’ śabdena jātismaraṇādiḥ parigṛhyate.
children.translated_text: § 258. For a <s>bhavya</s> soul with beginningless wrong faith (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), whose [soul-nature] is clouded by the fruition of <s>karma</s>—whence comes the subsidence of that [<s>karma</s>]? Because of causal conditions such as <s>kāla-labdhi</s> (temporal attainment) and others. Among these, <s>kāla-labdhi</s> first: the self, free from <s>karma</s>'s control—

children.text: § 259. kṛtsnasya mohanīyasyopaśamād aupaśamikaṃ cāritram. tatra samyaktvasyādau vacanaṃ; tatpūrvakatvāc cāritrasya.
children.translated_text: § 259. From the subsidence of the entire <s>mohanīya</s> (deluding) <s>karma</s>, [arises] <s>aupaśamika</s> conduct. Therein, right faith is mentioned first, since conduct is preceded by it.

children.text: § 260. yaḥ kṣāyiko bhāvo navavidha uddiṣṭas tasya bhedasvarūpapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 260. The <s>kṣāyika</s> (destruction-born) state has been stated as ninefold. To explain the nature of its divisions, he says—

children.text: jñānadarśanadānalābhabhogopabhogavīryāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), perception (<s>darśana</s>), giving (<s>dāna</s>), gain (<s>lābha</s>), enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>), re-enjoyment (<s>upabhoga</s>), and power (<s>vīrya</s>)—and [right faith and right conduct]. ||

children.text: § 261. ‘ca’ śabdaḥ samyaktvacāritrānukarṣaṇārthaḥ. jñānāvaraṇasyātyantakṣāyāt kevalajñānaṃ kṣāyikaṃ tathā kevaladarśanam. dānāntarāyasyātyantakṣayād anantaprāṇigaṇānugrahakaraṃ kṣāyikam abhayadānam. lābhāntarāyasyāśeṣasya nirāsāt parityaktakavalāhārakriyāṇāṃ kevalināṃ yataḥ śarīrabalādhānahetavo ’nyam anujāsādhāraṇāḥ paramaśubhāḥ sukṣmāḥ anantāḥ pratisamayaṃ pudgalāḥ saṃbandham upayānti sa kṣāyiko lābhaḥ. kṛtsnasya bhogāntarāyasya tirobhāvād āvirbhūto ’tiśayavān ananto bhogaḥ kṣāyikaḥ. yataḥ kusumavṛṣṭyādayo viśeṣāḥ prādurbhavanti. niravaśeṣasyopabhogāntarāyasya pralayāt prādurbhūto ’nanta upabhogaḥ kṣāyikaḥ. yataḥ siṃhāsanacāmaracchatrayādayo vibhūtayaḥ. vīryāntarāyasya karmaṇo ’tyantakṣayād āvirbhūtam anantavīryaṃ kṣāyikam. pūrvoktānāṃ saptānāṃ prakṛtīnām atyantakṣayāt kṣāyikaṃ samyaktvam. cāritram api tathā. yadi kṣāyikadānādibhāvakṛtam abhayadānādi, siddheṣv api tatprasaṅgaḥ? naiṣa doṣaḥ; śarīranāmatīrthakaranāmakarmodayādyapekṣatvāt. teṣāṃ tadabhāve tadaprasaṃgaḥ. kathaṃ tarhi teṣāṃ siddheṣu vṛttiḥ? paramānandāvyābādharūpeṇaiva teṣāṃ tatra vṛttiḥ. kevalajñānarūpeṇānantavīryavṛttivat.
children.translated_text: § 261. The particle '<s>ca</s>' is for the purpose of including right faith (<s>samyaktva</s>) and right conduct (<s>cāritra</s>) [mentioned earlier]. From the absolute destruction of knowledge-obscuring [<s>karma</s>], <s>kevala-jñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge) arises as <s>kṣāyika</s>; similarly, <s>kevala-darśana</s> (omniscient perception). From the absolute destruction of the <s>dāna-antarāya</s> (giving-obstructing karma), the unobstructed [capacity for] giving arises.

children.text: § 262. ya uktaḥ kṣāyopaśamiko bhāvo ’ṣṭādaśavikalpas tadbhedanirūpaṇārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 262. The <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s> (destruction-cum-subsidence-born) state has been stated as of eighteen varieties. To explain its divisions, he says—

children.text: jñānājñānadarśanalabdhayaś catustritripañcabhedāḥ samyaktvacāritrasaṃyamāsaṃyamāś ca ||
children.translated_text: Knowledge, wrong-knowledge, perception, and attainments—of four, three, three, and five divisions [respectively]; and right faith, right conduct, and partial restraint-cum-non-restraint. ||

children.text: § 263. catvāraś ca trayaś ca trayaś ca pañca ca catustritripañca. te bhedāḥ yāsāṃ tāścatustritripañcabhedāḥ. yathākramam ity anuvartate. tenābhisaṃbandhāc caturādibhir jñānādīny abhisaṃbadhyante. catvāri jñānāni, trīṇy ajñānāni, trīṇi darśanāni, pañca labdhaya iti. sarvaghātisparddhakānām udayakṣayāt teṣām eva sadupaśamād deśaghātisparddhakānām udaye kṣāyopaśamiko bhāvo bhavati. tatra jñānādīnāṃ vṛttiḥ svāvaraṇāntarāyakṣayopaśamād vyākhyātavyā. ‘samyaktva’ grahaṇena vedakasamyaktvaṃ gṛhyate. anantānubandhikaṣāyacatuṣtayasya mithyātvasamyaṅmithyātvayoś codayakṣayāt sadupaśamāc ca samyaktvasya deśaghātisparddhakasyodaye tattvārthaśraddhānaṃ kṣayopaśamikaṃ samyaktvam. anantānubandhyapratyākhyānapratyākhyānadvādaśakaṣāyodayakṣayāt sadupaśamāc ca saṃjvalanakaṣāyacatuṣṭayānyatamadeśaghātisparddhakodaye nokaṣāyanavakasya yathāsaṃbhavodaye ca nivṛttipariṇāma ātmanaḥ kṣāyopaśamikaṃ cāritram. anantānubandhyapratyākhyānakaṣāyāṣṭakodakṣayāt
sadupaśamāc ca pratyākhyānakaṣāyodaye saṃjvalanakaṣāyasya deśaghātisparddhakodaye nokaṣāyanavakasya yathāsaṃbhavodaye ca viratāviratapariṇāmaḥ kṣāyopaśamikaḥ saṃyamāsaṃyama ity ākhyāyate.
children.translated_text: And from the subsidence of the [complete] right-conduct-deluding <s>karma</s>, when the partial-renunciation passions are in fruition and the flaming passions are in partial-destruction-partial-competition fruition, and the nine quasi-passions are in fruition as applicable—the modification of partial restraint-cum-non-restraint is <s>kṣāyopaśamika</s>.

§ 263. 'Four and three and three and five'—<s>catustritripañca</s>. Those are the divisions of which—those are 'of four, three, three, and five divisions.' The phrase 'respectively' (<s>yathākramam</s>) continues [from the previous sūtra]. Through the connection with that—

children.text: § 264. ya ekaviṃśativikalpa audayiko bhāva uddiṣṭas tasya bhedasaṃjñāsaṃkīrtanārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 264. The <s>audayika</s> (fruition-born) state has been stated as of twenty-one varieties. To declare the names of its divisions, this is said—

children.text: gatikaṣāyaliṅgamithyādarśanājñānāsaṃyatāsiddhaleśyāś catuścatustryekaikaikaikaṣaḍbhedāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Destiny (<s>gati</s>), passion (<s>kaṣāya</s>), sex (<s>liṅga</s>), wrong perception (<s>mithyādarśana</s>), wrong knowledge (<s>ajñāna</s>), non-restraint (<s>asaṃyata</s>), non-attainment (<s>asiddha</s>), and soul-coloring (<s>leśyā</s>)—of four, four, three, one, one, one, one, and six divisions [respectively]. ||

children.text: § 265. yathākramam ity anuvartate, tenābhisaṃbandhād gatiś caturbhedā, narakagatis tiryagatir manuṣyagtir devagatir iti. tatra narakagatināmakarmodayān nārako bhāvo bhavatīti narakagatir audayikī. evam itaratrāpi. kaṣāyaś caturbhedaḥ, krodho māno māyā lobha iti. tatra krodhanirvartanasya karmaṇa udayāt krodhaḥ audayikaḥ. evam itaratrāpi. liṅgaṃ tribhedaṃ, srtīvedaḥ puṃvedo napuṃsakaveda iti. strīvedakarmaṇa udayāt strīveda audayikaḥ. evam itaratrāpi. mithyādarśanam ekabhedam. mityādarśanakarmaṇa udayāt tattvārthāśraddhānapariṇāmo mithyādarśanam audayikam. jñānāvaraṇakarmaṇa udayāt padārthānavabodho bhavati tadajñānam audayikam. cāritramohasya sarvaghātisparddhakasyodayād asaṃyata audayikaḥ. karmodayasāmānyāpekṣo ’siddha audayikaḥ. leśyā dvividhā, dravyaleśyā bhāvaleśyā ceti. jīvabhāvādhikārād dravyaleśyā nādhikṛtā. bhāvaleśyā kaṣāyodayarañjitā yogapravṛttir iti kṛtvā audayikīty ucyate. sā ṣaḍvidhā — kṛṣṇaleśyā nīlaleśyā kāpotaleśyā tejoleśyā padmaleśyā śuklaleśyā ceti.
children.translated_text: § 265. 'Respectively' continues [from before]; through the connection with that, destiny (<s>gati</s>) is fourfold: hellish destiny (<s>narakagati</s>), animal destiny (<s>tiryaggati</s>), human destiny (<s>manuṣyagati</s>), and celestial destiny (<s>devagati</s>). Among these, the hellish destiny is the modification of the self occasioned by the fruition of the hellish-lifespan-determining <s>karma</s>—

children.text: § 266. nanu ca upaśāntkaṣāye kṣīṇakaṣāye sayogakevalini ca śuklaleśyā ’stīty āgamaḥ. tatra kaṣāyānurañjanābhāvād audayikatvaṃ nopapadyate. naiṣa doṣaḥ; pūrvabhāvaprajñāpananayāpekṣayā yāsau yogapravṛttiḥ kaṣāyānurañjitā saivety upacārād audayikīty ucyate. tadabhāvād ayogakevalyaleśya iti niścīyate.
children.translated_text: § 266. [Objection:] But scripture states that <s>śukla-leśyā</s> (white soul-coloring) exists in the quiescent-passion stage, the destroyed-passion stage, and in the omniscient-with-activity stage. In those cases, due to the absence of coloring by passions, the designation '<s>audayika</s>' (fruition-born) is untenable. [Reply:] This is not a defect—

children.text: § 267. yaḥ pāriṇāmiko bhāvas tribheda uktas tadbhedasvarūpapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 267. The <s>pāriṇāmika</s> (inherent-modification-born) state has been stated as threefold. To explain the nature of its divisions, he says—

children.text: jīvabhavyābhavyatvāni ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jīvatva</s> (soul-hood), <s>bhavyatva</s> (capacity for liberation), and <s>abhavyatva</s> (incapacity for liberation)—and [these are the three]. ||

children.text: § 268. jīvatvaṃ bhavyatvam abhavyatvam iti trayo bhāvāḥ pāriṇāmikā anyadravyāsādhāraṇā ātmano veditavyāḥ. kutaḥ punar eṣāṃ pāriṇāmikatvam. karmodayopaśamakṣayakṣayopaśamānapekṣitvāt. jīvatvaṃ caitanyam ity arthaḥ. samyagdarśanādibhāvena bhaviṣyatīti bhavyaḥ. tadviparīto ’bhavyaḥ. ta ete trayo bhāvā jīvasya pāriṇāmikā.
children.translated_text: Section 268. <s>Jīvatva</s> (soul-nature), <s>bhavyatva</s> (capacity for liberation), and <s>abhavyatva</s> (incapacity for liberation) — these three dispositions are innate (<s>pāriṇāmika</s>), unique to the soul and not shared with other substances. Why are they innate? Because they do not depend on the rise, subsidence, destruction, or destruction-cum-subsidence of <s>karma</s>. <s>Jīvatva</s> means consciousness — this is the meaning. One who will attain the state of right faith and so forth is <s>bhavya</s> (capable of liberation). The opposite of that is <s>abhavya</s> (incapable of liberation). These three dispositions of the soul are innate.

children.text: § 269. nanu cāstitvanityatvapradeśavattvādayo ’pi bhāvāḥ pāriṇāmikāḥ santi, teṣām iha grahaṇaṃ kartavyam. na kartavyam; kṛtam eva. katham? ‘ca’ śabdena samuccitatvāt. yady evaṃ traya iti saṃkhyā virudhyate. na virudhyate, asādharaṇā jīvasya bhāvāḥ pāriṇāmikās traya eva. astitvādayaḥ punar jīvājīvaviṣayatvāt sādhāraṇā iti ‘ca’ śabdena pṛthaggṛhyante. āha, aupaśmikādibhāvānupapattir amūrtatvād ātmanaḥ karmabandhāpekṣā hi te bhāvāḥ. na cāmūrteḥ karmaṇāṃ bandho yujyata iti. tan na; anekāntāt. nāyam ekāntaḥ amūrtir evātmeti. karmabandhaparyāyāpekṣayā tadāveśāt syān mūrtaḥ. śuddhasvarūpāpekṣayā syād amūrtaḥ. yady evaṃ karmabandhāveśād asyaikatve saty avivekaḥ prāpnoti. naiṣa doṣaḥ; bandhaṃ pratyekatve saty api lakṣaṇabhedād asya nānātvam avasīyate. uktaṃ ca —
baṃdhaṃ paḍi eyattaṃ lakkhaṇado havai tassa ṇāṇattaṃ |
children.translated_text: Even though there is oneness with respect to bondage, its distinctness is [established] through defining characteristics;

children.text: tamhā amuttibhāvo ṇeyaṃto hoi jīvassa ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, the formless nature of the soul should be understood [accordingly].

children.text: iti |
children.translated_text: Thus.

Section 269. One objects: existence (<s>astitva</s>), permanence (<s>nityatva</s>), having spatial units (<s>pradeśavattva</s>), and so forth are also innate dispositions — should they not be included here? No, they need not be; it is already done. How? Because they are conjoined by the word 'ca' (and). If so, the number 'three' would be contradicted.
