It is not contradicted, for the innate dispositions unique to the soul are exactly three. <s>Astitva</s> and the rest, however, being common to both <s>jīva</s> (soul) and <s>ajīva</s> (non-soul), are separately included by the word 'ca.' One objects: the dispositions such as <s>aupaśamika</s> (quiescent) and others are impossible because the soul is formless (<s>amūrta</s>); those dispositions depend on karmic bondage, and bondage of <s>karma</s> with what is formless is not possible. That is not so; because of non-absolutism (<s>anekānta</s>). This is not an absolute [truth] that the soul is only formless. From the standpoint of karmic bondage and its associated states, it may be considered corporeal (<s>mūrta</s>) due to the interpenetration of karma. From the standpoint of its pure nature, it may be considered formless. If so, then due to the interpenetration of karmic bondage, there would be non-distinction [between soul and karma] when they are one. This is not a fault; for even though there is oneness with respect to bondage, the distinctness [of the soul] is ascertained through difference of defining characteristics. And it has been said —

children.text: § 270.yady evaṃ tadeva lakṣaṇam ucyatāṃ yena nānātvam avasīyate ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: Section 270. If so, then let that very defining characteristic by which distinctness is ascertained be stated — therefore he says —

children.text: upayogo lakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Upayoga</s> (active consciousness) is the defining characteristic.

children.text: § 271. ubhayanimittavaśād utpadyamānaś caitanyānuvidhāyī pariṇāma upayogaḥ. tena bandhaṃ pratyekatve saty apy ātmā lakṣyate suvarṇarajatayor bandhaṃ pratyekatve saty api varṇādibhedavat.
children.translated_text: Section 271. <s>Upayoga</s> is a transformation conforming to consciousness, arising due to both types of causes. By it, the soul is distinguished even when there is oneness with respect to bondage — just as gold and silver are distinguished by differences in color and other properties even when bonded together.

children.text: § 272. tadbhedapradarśanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 272. In order to show the divisions of that [<s>upayoga</s>], he says —

children.text: sa dvividho ’ṣṭacaturbhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It [<s>upayoga</s>] is twofold, with eight and four subdivisions.

children.text: § 273. sa upayogo dvividhaḥ — jñānopayogo darśanopayogaś ceti. jñānopayogo ’ṣṭabhedaḥ — matijñānaṃ śrutajñānaṃ avadhijñānaṃ manaḥparyayajñānaṃ kevalajñānaṃ matyajñānaṃ śrutājñānaṃ vibhaṅgajñānaṃ ceti. darśanopayogaś caturvidhaḥ — cakṣurdarśanam acakṣurdarśanam avadhidarśanaṃ kevaldarśanaṃ ceti. tayo kathaṃ bhedaḥ? sākārānakārabhedāt. sākāraṃ jñānam anākāraṃ darśanam iti. tacchadmastheṣu krameṇa vartate. nirāvaraṇeṣu yugapat pūrvakālabhāvino ’pi darśanāj jñānasya prāgupanyāsaḥ; abhyarhitatvāt. samyagjñānaprakaraṇāt pūrvaṃ pañcavidho jñānopayogo vyākhyātaḥ. iha punar upayogagrahaṇād viparyayo ’pi gṛhyate ity aṣṭavidha iti ucyate.
children.translated_text: Section 273. <s>Upayoga</s> is twofold: <s>jñānopayoga</s> (cognitive consciousness) and <s>darśanopayoga</s> (perceptive consciousness). <s>Jñānopayoga</s> is of eight kinds: <s>matijñāna</s> (sensory knowledge), <s>śrutajñāna</s> (scriptural knowledge), <s>avadhijñāna</s> (clairvoyant knowledge), <s>manaḥparyayajñāna</s> (mind-reading knowledge), <s>kevalajñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge), <s>matyajñāna</s> (erroneous sensory knowledge), <s>śrutājñāna</s> (erroneous scriptural knowledge), and <s>vibhaṅgajñāna</s> (erroneous clairvoyant knowledge). <s>Darśanopayoga</s> is fourfold: <s>cakṣurdarśana</s> (visual perception), <s>acakṣurdarśana</s> (non-visual perception), <s>avadhidarśana</s> (clairvoyant perception), and <s>kevaladarśana</s> (omniscient perception). How are they differentiated? By the distinction of determinate and indeterminate [cognition]. Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is determinate (<s>sākāra</s>); perception (<s>darśana</s>) is indeterminate (<s>anākāra</s>). In those whose knowledge is obscured (<s>chadmastha</s>), these operate sequentially. In those without obscuration, they operate simultaneously; though perception precedes knowledge in time, knowledge is mentioned first because it is more highly valued. In the context of right knowledge, the five types of <s>jñānopayoga</s> were previously explained. Here, however, since [the term] <s>upayoga</s> is used [broadly], erroneous cognition is also included — hence it is said to be eightfold.

children.text: § 274. yathoktenānenābhihitapariṇāmena sarvātmasādhāraneṇopayogena ye upalakṣitā upayoginas te dvividhāḥ —
children.translated_text: Section 274. Those who are characterized by this above-described <s>upayoga</s> — the transformation common to all souls — are of two kinds:

children.text: saṃsāriṇo muktāś ca ||
children.translated_text: Worldly beings (<s>saṃsārin</s>) and liberated ones (<s>mukta</s>).

children.text: § 275. saṃsaraṇaṃ saṃsāraḥ parivartaṇam ity arthaḥ. sa eṣām asti te saṃsāriṇaḥ. tatparivartanaṃ pañcavidham — dravyaparivartanaṃ kṣetraparivartanaṃ kālaparivartanaṃ bhavaparivartanaṃ bhāvaparivartanaṃ ceti. tatra dravyaparivartanaṃ dvividham — nokarmadravyaparivartanaṃ karmadravyaparivartanaṃ ceti. tatra nokarmadravyaparivartanaṃ nāma trayāṇāṃ śarīrāṇāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ paryāptīnāṃ ca yogyā ye pudgalā ekena jīvena ekasmin samaye gṛhītāḥ snigdharūkṣavarṇagandhādibhis tīvramandamadhyamabhāvena ca yathāvasthitā dvitīyādiṣu samayeṣu nirjīrṇā agṛhītān anantavārān atītya miśrakāṃś cānantavārān atītya madhye gṛhītāṃś cānantavārān atītya ta eva tenaiva prakāṛeṇa tasyaiva jīvasya norkarmabhāvam āpadyante yāvat tāvat samuditaṃ nokarmadravyaparivartanam. karmadravyaparivartanaṃ ucyate — ekasmin samaye ekena jīvenāṣṭavidhakarmabhāvena ye gṛhītāḥ pudgalāḥ samayādhikām āvalikām atītya dvitīyādiṣu samayeṣu nirjīrṇāḥ, pūrvoktenaiva krameṇa ta eva tenaiva prakāreṇa tasya jīvasya karmabhāvam āpadyante yāvat tāvat karmadravyaparivartanam. uktaṃ ca —
children.translated_text: Section 275. <s>Saṃsāra</s> means wandering, i.e., revolving — this is the meaning. Those who have it are <s>saṃsārins</s> (worldly beings). That revolving is fivefold: revolution of substance (<s>dravyaparivartana</s>), revolution of space (<s>kṣetraparivartana</s>), revolution of time (<s>kālaparivartana</s>), revolution of existence (<s>bhavaparivartana</s>), and revolution of state (<s>bhāvaparivartana</s>). Of these, revolution of substance is twofold: revolution of non-karmic substance (<s>nokarmadravyaparivartana</s>) and revolution of karmic substance (<s>karmadravyaparivartana</s>). Of these, revolution of non-karmic substance means: the material particles (<s>pudgalas</s>) suitable for the three types of bodies and six types of completions (<s>paryāptis</s>), which were taken by one soul at one moment, possessing smooth and rough [qualities], colors, smells, and so forth, in their respective intense, mild, and moderate states — when, in subsequent moments, being undigested, they pass beyond those not taken infinitely many times, and pass beyond those mixed infinitely many times, and pass beyond those taken in between infinitely many times, those very same [particles] in the very same manner attain the state of non-karmic matter for that same soul — the totality of this constitutes the revolution of non-karmic substance. The revolution of karmic substance is as follows: the material particles taken by one soul at one moment in the form of eight types of <s>karma</s>, passing beyond the measure of one <s>āvalikā</s> plus one time-instant, being undigested in subsequent moments, in the very same manner described above attain the state of karmic matter for that soul — the totality of this constitutes the revolution of karmic substance. And it has been said —

children.text:
savve vi puggalā khalu kamaso bhuttujjhiyā ya jīveṇa |
	  asaiṃ aṇaṃtakhutto puggalapariyaṭṭasaṃsāre ||

§ 276. kṣetraparivartanam ucyate — sūkṣmanigodajīvo ’paryāptikaḥ sarvajaghanyapradeśaśarīro lokasyāṣṭamadhyapradeśān svaśarīramadhye kṛtvotpannaḥ kṣudrabhavagrahaṇaṃ jīvitvā mṛtaḥ. sa eva punas tenaivāvaghāhena dvir utpannas tathā tris tathā catur ity evaṃ yāvad ghanāṃgulasyāsaṃkheyabhāgapramitākāśapradeśās tāvat kṛtvas tatraiva janitvā punar ekaikapradeśādhikabhāvena sarvo loka ātmano jamakṣetrabhāvam upanīto bhavati yāvat tāvat kṣetraparivartanam. uktaṃ ca —
children.translated_text: Section 276. The revolution of space is as follows: a subtle <s>nigoda</s> soul, undeveloped (<s>aparyāptika</s>), possessing a body of the smallest number of spatial units, is born having placed eight middle spatial units of the universe within its body. Having lived for the shortest lifespan, it dies. That same [soul] is born again twice with the same bodily extent, then three times, then four, and so on, as many times as there are spatial units in an uncountable fraction of a cubic <s>aṅgula</s> — being born that many times in that same place, then with each subsequent [birth] occupying one additional spatial unit, the entire universe becomes its birth-territory — the totality of this constitutes the revolution of space. And it has been said —

children.text:
“savvam hi loyakhette kamaso taṃ ṇatthi jam ṇa uppaṇṇaṃ |
	  ogāhaṇāe bahuso paribhamido khetttasaṃsāre ||
children.translated_text: In the entire field of the universe, there is no place where it has not been successively born; with [varying] bodily extent, it has revolved many times in the revolution of space.
Indeed, all material particles (<s>pudgalas</s>) have been successively enjoyed and abandoned by the soul, infinitely many times, in the revolution of material substance in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: § 277. kālaparivartanam ucyate — utsarpiṇyāḥ prathamasamaye jātaḥ kaścij jīvaḥ svāyuṣaḥ parisamāptau mṛtaḥ. sa eva punar dvitīyāyā utsarpiṇyā dvitīyasamaye jātaḥ svāyuṣaḥ kṣayān mṛtaḥ. sa eva punas tṛtīyāyā utsarpiṇyās tṛtīyasamaye jātaḥ. evam anena krameṇotsarpiṇī parisamāptā. tathāvasarpiṇī ca. evaṃ janmanair antaryam uktam. maraṇasyāpi nairantaryaṃ tathaiva grāhyam. etāvat kālaparivartanam. uktaṃ ca —
children.translated_text: Section 277. The revolution of time is as follows: a certain soul born at the first moment of an ascending cycle (<s>utsarpiṇī</s>) dies upon completion of its lifespan. That same [soul] is born again at the second moment of the second <s>utsarpiṇī</s> and dies at the expiry of its lifespan. That same [soul] is born at the third moment of the third <s>utsarpiṇī</s>. In this manner, the <s>utsarpiṇī</s> is completed. Likewise, the descending cycle (<s>avasarpiṇī</s>). Thus, the uninterrupted [succession] of births has been stated. The uninterrupted [succession] of deaths is to be understood in the same way. This constitutes the revolution of time. And it has been said —

children.text:
ussappiṇiavasappiṇisamayāvaliyāsu ṇiravasesāsu |
	  jādo mudo ya bahuso bhamaṇeṇa du kālasaṃsāre ||
children.translated_text: Born and died many times in every moment and <s>āvalikā</s> of the ascending and descending cycles without remainder, through wandering in the revolution of time.

children.text: § 278. bhavaparivartanam ucyate — narakagatau sarvajaghanyam āyurdaśavarṣasahasrāṇi. tenāyuṣā tatrotpannaḥ punaḥ paribhramya tenaivāyuṣā jātaḥ. evaṃ daśavarṣasahasrāṇāṃ yāvantaḥ samayās tāvat kṛtvas tatraiva jāto mṛtaḥ. punar ekaikasamayādhikabhāvena trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi parisamāpitāni. tataḥ pracyutya tiryaggatāv antarmuhūrtāyuḥ samutpannaḥ. pūrvoktenaiva krameṇa trīṇi palyopamāni tena parisamāpitāni. evaṃ manuṣyagatau ca. devagatau ca nārakavat. ayaṃ tu viśeṣaḥ — ekatriṃśatsāgaropamāṇi parisamāpitāni yāvat tāvad bhavaparivartanam. uktaṃ ca —
children.translated_text: Section 278. The revolution of existence is as follows: in the hellish destiny, the minimum lifespan is ten thousand years. Having been born there with that lifespan, [the soul] wanders again and is born with that same lifespan. Thus, as many time-instants as there are in ten thousand years, that many times it is born and dies there. Then, with each subsequent [birth] having one additional time-instant [of lifespan], thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> are completed. Then, having departed from there, it is born in the animal destiny with a lifespan of less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. In the same manner as before, three <s>palyopamas</s> are completed by it. Likewise in the human destiny. And in the celestial destiny, as in the hellish one. But there is this difference: thirty-one <s>sāgaropamas</s> are completed — the totality of this constitutes the revolution of existence. And it has been said —

children.text:
ṇirayādijahaṇṇādisu jāva du uvarillayā du gevajjā |
	  micchattasaṃsideṇa du bahuso vi bhavaṭṭhidī bhamidā ||
children.translated_text: From the minimum in the hellish and other [destinies], up to the maximum lifespans of their respective classes, through adherence to wrong faith, the states of existence have been revolved through many times.

children.text: § 279. bhāvaparivartanam ucyate — pañcendriyaḥ saṃjñī paryāptako mithyādṛṣṭiḥ kaścij jīvaḥ sa sarvajaghanyāṃ svayogyāṃ jñānāvaraṇaprakṛteḥ sthitim antaḥkoṭīkoṭīsaṃjñikām āpadyate. tasya kaṣāyādhyavasāyasthānānyasaṃkhyeyalokapramitāni ṣaṭsthānapatitāni tatsthitiyogyāni bhavanti. tatra sarvajaghanyakaṣāyādhyavasāyasthānanimittāny anubhāgādhyavasāyasthānāny asaṃkhyeyalokapramitāni bhavanti. evaṃ sarvajaghanyāṃ sthitiṃ sarvajaghanyaṃ ca kaṣāyādhyavasāyasthānaṃ sarvajaghanyam evānubhāgabandhasthānam āskandatas tadyogyaṃ sarvajaghanyaṃ yogasthānaṃ bhavati. teṣām eva sthitikaṣāyānubhāgasthānānāṃ dvitīyam asaṃkhyeyabhāgavṛddhiyuktaṃ yogasthānaṃ bhavati. evaṃ ca tritīyādiṣu catuḥsthānapatitāni śreṇyasaṃkhyeyabhāgapramitāni yogasthānāni bhavanti. tathā tām eva sthitiṃ tad eva kaṣāyādhyavasāyasthānaṃ ca pratipadyamānasya dvitīyam anubhavādhyavasāyasthānaṃ bhavati. tasya ca yogasthānāni pūrvavadveditavyāni. evaṃ tritīyādiṣv api anubhavādhyavasāyasthāneṣu ā asaṃkhyeyalokaparisamāpteḥ. evaṃ tām eva sthitim āpadyamānasya dvitīyaṃ kaṣāyādhyavasāyasthānaṃ bhavati. tasyāpy anubhavādhyavasāyasthānāni yogasthānāni ca pūrvavadveditavyāni. evaṃ tritīyādiṣv api kaṣāyādhyavasāyasthāneṣu ā asaṃkyeyalokaparisamāpter vṛddhikramo veditavyaḥ. uktāyā jaghanyāyāḥ sthiteḥ samayādhikāyāḥ kaṣāyādisthānāni pūrvavat. evaṃ samayādhikakrameṇa ā utkṛṣṭasthites triṃśatsāgaropamakoṭīkoṭīparimitāyāḥ kaṣāyādisthānāni veditavyāni. anantabhāgavṛddhiḥ asaṃkhyeyabhāgavṛddhiḥ saṃkhyeyabhāgavṛddhiḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇavṛddhiḥ asaṃkhyeyaguṇavṛddhiḥ anantaguṇavṛddhiḥ imāni ṣaṭ vṛddhisthānāni. hānir api tathaiva. anantabhāgavṛddhyanantaguṇavṛddhirahitāni catvāri sthānāni. evaṃ sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ mūlaprakṛtīnām uttaraprakṛtīnāṃ ca parivatanakramo veditavyaḥ. tadetat sarvaṃ samuditaṃ bhāvaparivartanam. uktam ca —
children.translated_text: Section 279. The revolution of state is as follows: a certain soul, five-sensed, possessing mind (<s>saṃjñin</s>), fully developed (<s>paryāptaka</s>), of wrong faith (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), attains the minimum duration appropriate to it of the <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring) <s>karma</s> type, designated as <s>koṭīkoṭi</s> within. Its passion-disposition-stations (<s>kaṣāyādhyavasāyasthānas</s>), measured as an uncountable number of universe-spaces, fall into six stations and are suitable for that duration. Among these, the experience-disposition-stations (<s>anubhāgādhyavasāyasthānas</s>) caused by the lowest passion-disposition-station are measured as an uncountable number of universe-spaces. Thus, ascending to the lowest duration, the lowest passion-disposition-station, and the lowest experience-bondage-station, there is the lowest activity-station (<s>yogasthāna</s>) suitable for it. The second activity-station is endowed with an increase by an uncountable fraction of those same duration, passion, and experience stations. Likewise, from the third onward, the activity-stations, falling into four stations, are measured as an uncountable fraction of a row. Similarly, for one attaining that same duration and that same passion-disposition-station, there is a second experience-disposition-station, and its activity-stations are to be understood as before. Likewise for the third and subsequent experience-disposition-stations, up to the completion of uncountable universe-spaces. Similarly, for one attaining that same duration, there is a second passion-disposition-station, and its experience-disposition-stations and activity-stations are to be understood as before. Likewise for the third and subsequent passion-disposition-stations, the order of increase is to be understood up to the completion of uncountable universe-spaces. For the next duration beyond the stated minimum, increased by one time-instant, the passion and other stations are as before. Thus, with successive increase by one time-instant, up to the maximum duration measured as thirty <s>sāgaropama</s> <s>koṭīkoṭis</s>, the passion and other stations are to be understood. The six stations of increase are: increase by an infinite fraction, increase by an uncountable fraction, increase by a countable fraction, increase by a countable multiple, increase by an uncountable multiple, and increase by an infinite multiple. Decrease is likewise. Four stations, excluding increase by infinite fraction and increase by infinite multiple. Thus, the order of revolution of all the root-types and sub-types of all <s>karmas</s> is to be understood. All of this together constitutes the revolution of state. And it has been said —

children.text:
savvā payaḍiṭṭhidīo aṇubhāgapadesabaṃdhaṭhāṇāṇi |
	  micchattasaṃsideṇa ya bhamidā puṇa bhāvasaṃsāre ||
children.translated_text: All the type-durations, experience-stations, spatial-unit-bondage-stations, through adherence to wrong faith, have been revolved again in the revolution of states.

children.text: § 280.  uktāt pañcavidhāt saṃsārān nivṛttā ye te muktāḥ. saṃsāriṇāṃ pragupādānaṃ tatpūrvakatvān muktavyapadeśasya.
children.translated_text: Section 280. Those who have ceased from the fivefold <s>saṃsāra</s> described above are the liberated ones (<s>muktas</s>). The worldly beings are mentioned first because the designation of the liberated presupposes [prior worldly existence].

children.text: § 281. ya ete saṃsāriṇas te dvividhāḥ —
children.translated_text: Section 281. These worldly beings are of two kinds —

children.text: samanaskāmanaskāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those with mind (<s>samanaska</s>) and those without mind (<s>amanaska</s>).

children.text: § 282. mano dvitīdham — dravyamano bhāvamanaś ceti. tatra pudgalavipākikarmodayāpekṣaṃ dravyamanaḥ. vīryāntarāyanoindriyāvaraṇakṣayopaśamāpekṣā ātmano viśuddhir bhāvamanaḥ. tena manasā saha vartanta iti samanaskāḥ. na vidyate mano yeṣāṃ ta ime amanaskāḥ. evaṃ manaso bhāvābhāvābhyāṃ samsāriṇo dvividhā vibhajyante. samanaskāś cāmanaskāś ca samanaskāmanaskā iti. abhyarhitatvāt samanaskaśabdasya pūrvanipātaḥ. katham abhyarhitatvam? guṇadoṣavicārakatvāt.
children.translated_text: Section 282. Mind (<s>manas</s>) is twofold: material mind (<s>dravyamanas</s>) and psychic mind (<s>bhāvamanas</s>). Of these, <s>dravyamanas</s> depends on the fruition of matter-producing (<s>pudgalavipāki</s>) <s>karma</s>. The purification of the soul dependent on the destruction-cum-subsidence of energy-obstructing (<s>vīryāntarāya</s>) and sensory-obstructing (<s>indriyāvaraṇa</s>) karmas is <s>bhāvamanas</s>. Those who exist with that mind are <s>samanaskas</s> (those with mind). Those in whom mind is absent are <s>amanaskas</s> (those without mind). Thus, by the presence and absence of mind, worldly beings are divided into two kinds: those with mind and those without mind — <s>samanaskāmanaskāḥ</s>. The word <s>samanaska</s> is placed first because it is more highly valued. Why is it more highly valued? Because it has the capacity to discriminate between virtues and faults.

children.text: § 283. punar api saṃsāriṇāṃ bhedapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 283. Again, in order to understand the classification of worldly beings, he says —

children.text: saṃsāriṇas trasasthāvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Worldly beings are <s>trasa</s> (mobile) and <s>sthāvara</s> (immobile).

children.text: § 284. ‘saṃsāri’ grahaṇam anarthakam; prakṛtatvāt. kva prakṛtam? ‘saṃsāriṇo muktaś ca’ iti. nānarthakam, pūrvāpekṣārtham, ye uktāḥ samanaskā amanaskās te saṃsāriṇa iti. yadi hi pūrvasya viśeṣạṇaṃ na syāt, samanaskāmanaskagrahaṇaṃ saṃsāriṇo muktāś cety anena yathāsaṃkhyam abhisaṃbadhyeta. evaṃ ca kṛtvā ‘saṃsāri’ grahaṇam adau kriyamāṇam upapannaṃ bhavati. tatpūrvāpekṣaṃ saduttarārtham api bhavati. te saṃsāriṇo dvividhāḥ — trasāḥ sthāvarā iti. trasanāmakarmodayavaśīkṛtās trasā. sthāvaranāmakarmodayavaśavartinaḥ sthāvarāḥ. trasyantīti trasāḥ, sthānaśīlāḥ sthāvara iti cet? na; āgamavirodhāt. āgame hi kāyānuvādena trasā dvīndriyād ārabhya ā ayogakevalina iti. tasmān na calanācalanāpekṣaṃ trasasthāvaratvam. karmodayāpekṣam eva. trasagrahaṇam ādau kriyate; alpāctaratvād abhyarhitatvāc ca. sarvopayogasambhavād abhyarhitatvam.
children.translated_text: § 284. The inclusion of the word '<s>saṃsārin</s>' (transmigrating being) is purposeless, since it is already the topic. Where was it established? In [the sūtra:] 'transmigrating and liberated.' [Reply:] It is not purposeless; it is for the purpose of connecting with the preceding [discussion], [meaning:] those who were described as rational (<s>samanaska</s>) and non-rational (<s>amanaska</s>) are transmigrating beings. For if it were not a qualifier of the preceding, the terms 'rational' and 'non-rational' would be connected sequentially with [the sūtra] 'transmigrating and liberated.' And thus, the inclusion of '<s>saṃsārin</s>' placed at the beginning becomes justified. It also serves a subsequent purpose with reference to the preceding: those transmigrating beings are of two kinds—mobile (<s>trasa</s>) and immobile (<s>sthāvara</s>). Those governed by the fruition of mobile-body-determining <s>karma</s> (<s>trasanāmakarma</s>) are mobile. Those governed by the fruition of immobile-body-determining <s>karma</s> are immobile. [Objection:] 'Those that move are mobile (<s>trasa</s>), those stationary by nature are immobile (<s>sthāvara</s>)'? [Reply:] No, because that would contradict scripture. For in scripture, by the thread of body-type (<s>kāyānuvāda</s>), mobile beings [are defined as] from two-sensed beings up to the motionless omniscient (<s>ayogakevalin</s>). Therefore, the distinction of mobile and immobile does not depend on motion and non-motion, but on the fruition of <s>karma</s> alone. The term 'mobile' is placed first because of its being of lesser extent and more honored. Its being more honored is because all types of active consciousness (<s>upayoga</s>) are possible [in it].

children.text: § 285. ekendriyāṇām atibahuvaktavyābhāvād ullaṅghyānupūrvīṃ sthāvarabhedapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 285. Since for one-sensed beings there is not much to be stated, he skips the sequence and says [the following] for the purpose of understanding the divisions of immobile beings—

children.text: pṛthivyaptejovāyuvanaspatayaḥ sthāvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Earth, water, fire, air, and plants—these are the immobile (<s>sthāvara</s>) [beings]. ||

children.text: § 286. sthāvaranāmakarmabhedāḥ pṛthivīkāyādayaḥ santi. tadudayanimittā jīveṣu pṛthivyādayaḥ saṃjñā veditavyāḥ. prathanādiprakṛtiniṣpannā api rūḍhivaśāt prathanādyanapekṣā vartante. eṣāṃ pṛthivyādīnām ārṣe cāturvidhyam uktaṃ pratyekam. tatkatham iti cet? ucyate — pṛthivī pṛthivīkāyaḥ pṛthivīkāyikaḥ pṛthivījīva ity ādi. tatra acetanā vaiśrasikapariṇāmanirvṛttā kāṭhinyaguṇātmikā pṛthivī. acetanatvād asaty api pṛthivīkāyanāmakarmodaye prathanakriyopalakṣitaiveyam. athavā pṛthivīti sāmānyam; uttaratraye ’pi sadbhāvāt. kāyaḥ śarīram. pṛthivīkāyikajīvaparityaktaḥ pṛthivīkāyo mṛtamanuṣyādikāyavat. pṛthivīkāyo ’syāstīti pṛthivīkāyikaḥ. tatkāyasaṃbandhavaśīkṛta ātmā. samavāptapṛthivīkāyanāmakarmodayaḥ kārmaṇakāyayogastho yo na tāvat pṛthivīṃ kāyatvena gṛhṇāti sa pṛthivījīvaḥ. evam abādiṣv api yojyam. ete mañcavidhāḥ prāṇinaḥ sthāvarāḥ.
kati punar eṣāṃ prāṇāḥ? catvāraḥ — sparśanendriyaprāṇāḥ kāyabalaprāṇāḥ ucchvāsaniśvāsaprāṇaḥ āyuḥprānaś ceti.
children.translated_text: How many vital forces (<s>prāṇa</s>) do these [immobile beings] have? Four: the vital force of the sense of touch (<s>sparśanendriyaprāṇa</s>), the vital force of bodily strength (<s>kāyabalaprāṇa</s>), the vital force of respiration (<s>ucchvāsaniśvāsaprāṇa</s>), and the vital force of lifespan (<s>āyuḥprāṇa</s>).

§ 286. The earth-bodied (<s>pṛthivīkāya</s>) and others exist as divisions of the immobile-body-determining <s>karma</s>. The designations 'earth' etc. in [connection with] souls should be understood as occasioned by the fruition of that [karma]. Though they are also produced by the natural process of spreading etc., they function by conventional usage without reference to spreading etc. The fourfold [designation] of each of these—earth etc.—is stated in the scriptures. How? It is said: <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth), <s>pṛthivīkāya</s> (earth-body), <s>pṛthivīkāyika</s> (earth-bodied), <s>pṛthivījīva</s> (earth-soul). Among these, <s>pṛthivī</s> is the insentient [substance], produced by the natural transformation [of matter], whose essential quality is hardness. Being insentient, even without the fruition of earth-body-determining <s>karma</s>, it is identified by the activity of spreading. Or, '<s>pṛthivī</s>' is the general [category], since it also exists in the latter three. '<s>Kāya</s>' means body. <s>Pṛthivīkāya</s> is [the earth body] abandoned by the earth-bodied soul—like the body of a dead human etc. <s>Pṛthivīkāyika</s> is one who possesses an earth body—a self governed by the connection with that body. <s>Pṛthivījīva</s> is one who has attained the fruition of earth-body-determining <s>karma</s> and, being in the state of <s>kārmaṇa</s> (karmic) body-activity, has not yet grasped earth as a body. The same should be applied to water etc. These five types of beings are the immobile ones.

children.text: § 287. atha trasāḥ ke te, ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 287. Now, who are the mobile (<s>trasa</s>) beings? To this it is said—

children.text: dvīndriyādayas trasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Two-sensed beings and beyond are mobile (<s>trasa</s>). ||

children.text: § 288. dve indriye yasya so ’yaṃ dvīndriyaḥ. dvīndriṣa ādir yeyāṃ te dvīndriyādayaḥ.

‘ādi’ śabdo vyavasthāvācī. kva vyavasthitāḥ? āgame. katham? dvīndriyas trīndriyaś caturindriyaḥ pañcendriyaś ceti. tadguṇasaṃvijñānavṛttigrahaṇād dvīndriyasyāpy antarbhāvaḥ. kati punar eṣāṃ prāṇāh? dvīndriyasya tāvat ṣaṭ prāṇāḥ, pūrvoktā eva rasanavākprāṇādhikāḥ. trīndriyasya sapta ta eva ghrāṇaprāṇādhikāḥ. caturindriyasyāṣṭau ta eva cakṣuḥprāṇādhikāḥ. pañcendriyasya tiraśco ’saṃjñino nava ta eva śrotraprāṇādhikāḥ. saṃjñino daśa ta eva manobalaprāṇādhikāḥ.
children.translated_text: The word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.) denotes a definite [set]. Where is it defined? In scripture. How? Two-sensed, three-sensed, four-sensed, and five-sensed. With the [previously stated] qualities [of the immobile beings], these [mobile beings too share them].
§ 288. One who has two senses is a two-sensed being (<s>dvīndriya</s>). Those beginning with the two-sensed are the 'two-sensed and beyond' (<s>dvīndriyādaya</s>).

children.text: § 289. ‘ādi’ śabdena nirdiṣṭānām anirjñātasaṃkhyānām iyattāvadhāraṇaṃ karttavyām ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 289. Since the exact number of those indicated by the word '<s>ādi</s>' is not yet known, in order to determine their extent, he says—

children.text: pañcendriyāṇi ||
children.translated_text: There are five sense organs (<s>indriya</s>). ||

children.text: § 290. ‘indriya’ śabdo vyākhyātārthaḥ. ‘pañca’ grahaṇam avadhāraṇārtham, paṃcaiva nādhikasaṃkhyānīti. karmendriyāṇāṃ vāgādinām iha grahaṇaṃ kartavyam? na kartavyam; upayogaprakaraṇāt. upayogasādhanānām iha grahaṇaṃ, na kriyāsādhanānām; anavasthānāc ca. kriyāsādhanānām aṅgopāṅganāmakarmanivartitānāṃ sarveṣām api kriyāsādhanatvam astīti na paṃcaiva karmendriyāṇi.
children.translated_text: § 290. The word '<s>indriya</s>' has already been explained. The word 'five' is for the purpose of delimitation—meaning five only, not of greater number. The motor organs (<s>karmendriya</s>) such as speech (<s>vāk</s>) etc. are not accepted [as separate sense organs in Jain philosophy]; therefore they are not included here.

children.text: § 291. teṣām antarbhedapradarśanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 291. In order to show the internal divisions of these [sense organs], he says—

children.text: dvividhāni ||
children.translated_text: [They are] of two kinds. ||

children.text: § 292. ‘vidha’ śabdaḥ prakāravācī. dvau vidhau yeṣāṃ tāni dvividhāni, dviprakārāṇīty arthaḥ. kau punas tau dvau prakārau? dravyendriyaṃ bhāvendriyam iti.
children.translated_text: § 292. The word '<s>vidha</s>' means 'type.' Those having two types are 'of two kinds' (<s>dvividha</s>), meaning of two varieties. What then are those two varieties?

children.text: § 293. tatra dravyendriyasvarūpapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 293. In order to present the essential nature of the physical sense organ (<s>dravyendriya</s>), he says—

children.text: nirvṛttyupakaraṇo dravyendriyam ||
children.translated_text: The structure (<s>nirvṛtti</s>) and the instrument (<s>upakaraṇa</s>) [together constitute] the physical sense organ (<s>dravyendriya</s>). ||

children.text: § 294. nirvartyate ity nirvṛttiḥ. kena nirvartyate? karmanā. sā dvividhā; bāhyābhyantarabhedāt. utsedhāṅgulāsaṃkhyeyabhāgapramitānāṃ śuddhānām ātmapradeśānāṃ pratiniyatacakṣurādīndriyasaṃsthānenāvasthitānāṃ vṛttir ābhyantarā nirvṛttiḥ. teṣv ātmapradeśeṣv indriyavyapadeśabhākṣu yaḥ pratiniyatasaṃsthāno nāmakarmodayāpāditāvasthāviśeṣaḥ pudgalapracayaḥ sā bāhyā nirvṛttiḥ. yena nirvṛtter upakāraḥ kriyate tadupakaraṇam. pūrvavat tadapi dvividham. tatrābhyantaraṃ kṛṣṇaśuklamaṇḍalaṃ, bāhyam akṣipatrapakṣmadvayādi. evaṃ śeṣeṣv apīndriyeṣu jñeyam.
children.translated_text: § 294. That which is constructed is the structure (<s>nirvṛtti</s>). By what is it constructed? By <s>karma</s>. It is twofold, due to the distinction of external and internal. [The external is of] an innumerable fraction of a finger-breadth in height

children.text: § 295. bhāvendriyam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 295. The dispositional sense organ (<s>bhāvendriya</s>) is stated—

children.text: labdhyupayogau bhāvendriyam ||
children.translated_text: Attainment (<s>labdhi</s>) and active consciousness (<s>upayoga</s>) [together constitute] the dispositional sense organ (<s>bhāvendriya</s>). ||

children.text: § 296. lambhanaṃ labdhiḥ. kā punar asau? jñānāvaraṇakarmakṣayopaśamaviśeṣaḥ. yat saṃnidhānād ātmā dravyendriyanirvṛttiṃ prati vyāpriyate tan nimitta ātmanaḥ pariṇāma upayogaḥ. tadubhaye bhāvenindriyam. indriyaphalam upayogaḥ, tasya katham indriyatvam? kāraṇadharmasya kārye darśanāt. yathā ghaṭākārapariṇataṃ vijñānaṃ ghaṭa iti. svārthasya tatra mukhyatvāc ca. indrasya liṅgam indriyam iti yaḥ svārthaḥ sa upayoge mukhyaḥ, ‘upayogalakṣaṇo jīva’ iti vacanāt. ata upayogasyendriyatvaṃ nyāyyaṃ.
children.translated_text: § 296. The obtaining is attainment (<s>labdhi</s>). What is that? It is the specific subsidence-cum-destruction of knowledge-obscuring <s>karma</s>. In the presence of which, the self [performs] the construction of the physical sense organ

children.text: § 297. uktānām indriyāṇāṃ saṃjñānupūrvīpratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 297. In order to teach the names and sequence of the stated sense organs, he says—

children.text: sparśanarasanaghrāṇacakṣuḥśrotrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Touch, taste, smell, sight, and hearing. ||

children.text: § 298. loke indriyāṇāṃ pāratantryavivakṣā dṛśyate. anenākṣaṇā suṣṭhu paśyāmi, anena karṇena suṣṭhu śṛṇomīti. tataḥ pāratantryāt sparśanādīnāṃ karaṇatvam. vīryāntarāyamatijñānāvaraṇakṣayopaśamāṅgopāṅganāmalābhāvaṣṭambhād ātmanā spṛśyate ’neneti sparśanam. rasyate ’neneti rasanam. ghrāyate ’neneti ghrāṇam. cakṣer anekārthatvād darśanārthavivakṣāyāṃ caṣṭe arthān paśyaty aneneti cakṣuḥ. śrūyate ’neneti śrotram. svātantryavivakṣā ca dṛśyate. idaṃ me akṣi suṣṭhu paśyati. ayaṃ me karṇaḥ suṣṭhu śṛṇoti. tataḥ sparśanādīnāṃ kartari niṣpattiḥ. spṛśatīti sparśanam. rasatīti rasanam. jighratīti ghrāṇam. caṣṭe iti cakṣuḥ. śṛṇotīti śrotram. eṣāṃ nirdeśakramaḥ ekaikavṛddhikramaprajñāpanārthaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 298. In the world, the dependence of the sense organs is observed: 'With this eye I see well,' 'With this ear I hear well.' Therefore, due to the intention of dependence,

children.text: § 299. teṣām indriyāṇāṃ viṣayapradarśanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 299. In order to show the objects of those sense organs, he says—

children.text: sparśarasagandhavarṇaśabdās tadarthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Touch, taste, smell, color, and sound are their objects. ||

children.text: § 300. dravyaparyāyayoḥ prādhānyavivakṣāyāṃ karmabhāvasādhanatvaṃ sparśādiśabdānāṃ veditavyam. dravyaprādhānyavivakṣāyāṃ karmanirdeśaḥ. spṛśyata iti sparśaḥ. rasyata iti rasaḥ. gandhyata iti gandhaḥ. varṇyata iti varṇaḥ. śabdyata iti śabdaḥ. paryāyaprādhānyavivakṣāyāṃ bhāvanirdeśaḥ. sparśanaṃ sparśaḥ. rasanaṃ rasaḥ. gandhanaṃ gandhaḥ. varṇanaṃ varṇaḥ. śabdanaṃ śabda iti. eṣāṃ krama indriyakrameṇaiva vyākhyātaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 300. When the priority of substance or mode is intended, the instrumental function of the words 'touch' etc. should be understood. When the priority of substance is intended,

children.text: § 301. atrāha, yat tāvan mano ’navasthānād indriyaṃ na bhavatīti pratyākhyātaṃ tat kim upayogasyopakāri uta neti. tad apy upakāryeva. tena vinendriyāṇāṃ viṣayeṣu svaprayojanavṛttyabhāvāt. kiñcāsyaiṣāṃ sahakāritvamātram eva prayojanam utānyad apīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 301. Here one says: That which was rejected—that the mind (<s>manas</s>) is not a sense organ because of its instability—does it or does it not assist active consciousness (<s>upayoga</s>)? That too

children.text: śrutam anindriyasya ||
children.translated_text: Scriptural [knowledge pertains] to the non-sensory. ||

children.text: § 302. śrutajñānaviśayo ’rthaḥ śrutam. sa viṣayo ’nindriyasya; pariprāptaśrutajñānāvaraṇakṣayopaśamasyātmanaḥ śrutārthe ’nindriyālambanajñānapravṛtteḥ. athavā śrutajñānaṃ śrutam, tadanindriyasyārthaḥ prayojanam iti yāvat. svātantryasādhyam idaṃ prayojanam anindriyasya.
children.translated_text: § 302. The object within the range of scriptural knowledge (<s>śrutajñāna</s>) is <s>śruta</s>. That object pertains to the non-sensory—to the self that has attained the subsidence-cum-destruction of scriptural-knowledge-obscuring [karma], [perceiving] scriptural objects

children.text: § 303. uktānām indriyānāṃ pratiniyataviṣayāṇāṃ svāmitvanirdeśe kartavye yat prathamaṃ gṛhītaṃ sparśanaṃ tasya tāvat svāmitvāvadhāraṇārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 303. When the ownership of the stated sense organs, which have fixed objects, is to be indicated—for that which was first grasped, touch, its ownership is stated first—

children.text: vanaspatyantānām ekam ||
children.translated_text: One [sense organ belongs] to [beings] up to and including plants (<s>vanaspati</s>). ||

children.text: § 304. ekaṃ prathamam ity arthaḥ. kiṃ tat? sparśanam. tat keṣām? pṛthivyādīnāṃ vanaspatyantānāṃ veditavyam. tasyotpattikāraṇam ucyate — vīryāntarāyasparśanendriyāvaraṇakṣayopaśame sati śeṣendriyasarvaghātispardhakodaye ca śarīranāmalābhāvaṣṭambhe ekendriyajātinamodayavaśartitāyāṃ ca satyāṃ sparśanam ekam indriyam āvirbhavati.
children.translated_text: § 304. 'One' means the first—that is the meaning. What is that? Touch. To whom does it belong? It should be understood as belonging to earth-bodied beings etc., up to and including plant-bodied beings. Its production

children.text: § 305. itareṣām indriyāṇāṃ svāmitvapradarśanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 305. In order to show the ownership of the remaining sense organs, he says—

children.text: kṛimipipīlakābhramaramanuṣyādinām ekaikavṛddhāni ||
children.translated_text: [Sense organs] increase by one each for worms, ants, bees, humans, and the like. ||

children.text: § 306. ‘ekaikam’ iti vīpsāyāṃ dvitvam. ekaikena vṛddhāni ekaikavṛddhāni. kṛimim ādiṃ kṛtvā, sparśanādhikārāt sparśanam ādiṃ kṛtvā ekaikavṛddhānīty abhisaṃbandhaḥ kriyate. ‘ādi’ śabdaḥ pratyekaṃ parisamāpyate. kṛmyādīnāṃ sparśanaṃ rasanādhikam, pipīlikādīnāṃ sparśanarasane ghrāṇadhike, bhramarādīnāṃ sparśanarasanaghrāṇāni cakṣuradhkāni, manuṣyādīnāṃ tāny eva śrotrādhikānīti yathāsaṃkhyenābhisaṃbandho vyākhyātaḥ. teṣāṃ niṣpattiḥ sparśnotpatyā vyākhyātā uttarottarasarvaghātispardhakodayena.
children.translated_text: § 306. The repetition '<s>ekaika</s>' (one each) is for distribution. 'Increased by one each' means '<s>ekaikavṛddha</s>.' Taking worms as the beginning, and since the context is touch,

children.text: § 307. evam eteṣu saṃsāriṣu dvibhedeṣu indriyabhedāt pañcavidheṣu ye pañcendriyās tadbhedasyānuktasya pratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 307. Thus, among these transmigrating beings of two divisions, who are fivefold through the distinction of sense organs, those that are five-sensed—for the purpose of presenting their [further] division which has not yet been stated—he says—

children.text: saṃjñinaḥ samanaskāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rational (<s>saṃjñin</s>) are those possessing mind (<s>samanaska</s>). ||

children.text: § 308. mano vyākhyātam. saha tena ye vartante te samanaskāḥ. saṃjñina ity ucyante. pāriśeṣyād itare saṃsāriṇaḥ prāṇino ’saṃjñina iti siddham. nanu ca saṃjñina ity anenaiva gatārthatvāt samanaskā iti viśeṣaṇam anarthakam. yato manovyāpāro hitāhitaprāptiparihāraparīkṣā. saṃjñāpi saiveti. naitad yuktam, saṃjñāśabdārthavyabhicārāt. saṃjñā nāmety ucyate. tadvantaḥ saṃjñina iti sarveṣām atiprasaṅgaḥ. saṃjñā jñānam iti cet; sarveṣām prāṇiṇāṃ jñānātmakatvād atiprasaṅgaḥ. āhārādiviṣayābhilāṣaḥ saṃjñeti cet. tulyam. tasmāt samanaskā ity ucyate. evaṃ ca kṛtvā garbhāṇḍajamūrcchitasuṣuptyādyavasthāsu hitāhitaparīkṣābhāve’ pi manaḥsaṃnidhānāt saṃjñitvam upapannaṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text: § 308. <s>Manas</s> (mind) has been explained. Those who exist together with it are called <s>samanaska</s> (possessing mind); they are called <s>saṃjñin</s> (rational). By elimination, the other transmigrating living beings are established as <s>asaṃjñin</s> (non-rational). [Objection:] Since the meaning is already conveyed by '<s>saṃjñin</s>' alone, the qualification '<s>samanaska</s>' is purposeless — because the activity of the mind is the examination of what is beneficial and harmful, and <s>saṃjñā</s> is the same thing. [Reply:] This is not correct, because the meaning of the word '<s>saṃjñā</s>' is variable. '<s>Saṃjñā</s>' is said to mean 'name'; those possessing it are '<s>saṃjñins</s>' — this would over-extend to all. [Objection:] If <s>saṃjñā</s> means knowledge? [Reply:] Since all living beings are of the nature of knowledge, there would be over-extension. [Objection:] If <s>saṃjñā</s> means the desire for food and the like? [Reply:] The same [over-extension applies]. Therefore, '<s>samanaska</s>' (possessing mind) is said. And by this reasoning, even in states such as the embryonic, egg-born, spontaneously-generated, and deep-sleep states, despite the absence of examination of what is beneficial and harmful, the status of being <s>saṃjñin</s> is justified due to the proximity of the mind.

children.text: § 309. yadi hitāhitādiviṣayaparispandaḥ prāṇināṃ manaḥpraṇidhānapūrvakaḥ. athābhi–navaśarīragrahaṇaṃ pratyāgūrṇasya viśīrṇapūrvamūrter nirmanaskasya yatkarma tatkuta ity ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 309. If the activity of living beings regarding beneficial and harmful objects and the like is preceded by the application of mind, then how does the soul whose previous body has disintegrated and which is without mind perform the action of taking up a new body? — to this it is said —

children.text: vigrahagatau karmayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the transit to [a new] body (<s>vigrahagati</s>), there is activity caused by <s>karma</s>. ||

children.text: § 310. vigraho dehaḥ. vigrahārthā gatir vigrahagatiḥ. athavā viruddho graho vigraho vyāghātaḥ. karmādāne ’pi nokarmapudgalādānanirodha ity arthaḥ. vigraheṇa gatir vigrahagatiḥ. sarvaśarīraprarohaṇabījabhūtaṃ kārmaṇaṃ śarīraṃ karmety ucyate. yogo vāṅmanasakāyavargaṇānimitta ātmapradeśaparispandaḥ. karmaṇā kṛto yogaḥ karmayogo vigrahagatau bhavatīty arthaḥ. tena karmādānaṃ deśāntarasaṃkramaś ca bhavati.
children.translated_text: § 310. '<s>Vigraha</s>' means the body. Movement for the purpose of [acquiring] a body is <s>vigrahagati</s> (transit to a body). Alternatively, '<s>vigraha</s>' means obstruction — a contrary grasping, an impediment. The meaning is: even in the taking up of <s>karma</s>, there is no cessation of the intake of <s>karma-pudgalas</s> (karmic matter-particles). Movement with obstruction is <s>vigrahagati</s>. The <s>kārmaṇa</s> (karmic) body, which is the seed for the sprouting of all [other] bodies, is called '<s>karma</s>.' <s>Yoga</s> (activity) is the vibration of the spatial units of the self caused by the clusters of speech, mind, and body. The activity effected by <s>karma</s> is <s>karmayoga</s>, which exists in <s>vigrahagati</s> — this is the meaning. Thereby, the intake of <s>karma</s> and the transition to another location occur.

children.text: § 311. āha jīvapudgalānāṃ gatim āskandatāṃ deśāntarasaṃkramaḥ kim ākāśapradeśakramavṛtyā bhavati, utāviśeṣeṇety ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 311. He asks: does the transition to another location of souls and matter-particles that are moving occur through the sequential traversal of space-points, or without distinction? — to this he says —

children.text: anuśreṇi gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Movement is along a row (<s>anuśreṇi</s>). ||

children.text: § 312. lokamadhyād ārabhya ūrdhvam adhas tiryak ca ākāśāpradeśānāṃ kramasaṃniviṣṭānāṃ paṅktiḥ śreṇiḥ ity ucyate. ‘anu’ śabdasyānupurvyeṇa vṛttiḥ.

śreṇer ānupūrvyeṇānuśreṇīti jīvānāṃ pudgalānāṃ ca gatir bhavatīty arthaḥ. anadhikṛtānāṃ pudglānāṃ kathaṃ grahaṇam iti cet. gatigrahaṇāt. yadi jīvānām eva gatir iṣṭā syād gatigrahaṇam anarthakam; adhikārāt tatsiddheḥ. uttaratra jīvagrahaṇāc ca pudgalasaṃpratyayaḥ. nanu candrādīnāṃ jyotiṣkāṇāṃ merupradakṣiṇākāle vidyādharādīnāṃ ca viśreṇigatir api dṛśyate, tatra kim ucyate, ‘anuśreṇi gatiḥ’ iti. kāladeśaniyamo ’tra veditavyaḥ. tatra kālaniyamas tāvaj jīvānāṃ maraṇakāle bhavāntarasaṃkrame muktānāṃ cordhvagamanakāle anuśreṇy eva gatiḥ. deśaniyamo ’pi ūrdhvalokād adho gatiḥ, adho lokād ūrdhvagatiḥ, tiryaglokād adho gatir ūrdhvā vā tatrānuśreṇy eva. pudgalānāṃ ca yā lokāntaprāpiṇī sā niyamād anuśreṇy eva. itarā gatir bhajanīya.
children.translated_text: Following the row in order is '<s>anuśreṇi</s>' — the movement of souls and matter-particles occurs thus, this is the meaning. [Objection:] How is the inclusion of matter-particles, which are not the subject under discussion? [Reply:] From the mention of 'movement' (<s>gati</s>). If movement were intended for souls alone, the mention of 'movement' would be purposeless, since that is already established from the topic. And from the mention of '<s>jīva</s>' (soul) in the subsequent [sūtra], the implication of matter-particles [here] is understood. [Objection:] But the movement of luminaries like the moon and the like going around <s>Meru</s>, and of <s>Vidyādharas</s> and the like, is seen to be across rows (<s>viśreṇi</s>); what is to be said there, [given that] 'movement is along a row'? [Reply:] A restriction of time and place should be understood here. The time restriction is: for souls, at the time of death, in the transition to another existence, and for the liberated in their upward movement — the movement is strictly along a row. The place restriction is also: movement downward from the upper cosmos, upward from the lower cosmos, and downward or upward from the transverse cosmos — there it is strictly along a row. And for matter-particles, that [movement] which reaches the boundary of the cosmos is necessarily along a row. Other movement is variable.

§ 312. Starting from the middle of the cosmos, going upward, downward, and sideways, the row of space-points arranged in sequence is called a <s>śreṇi</s> (row). The word '<s>anu</s>' means 'following in order.'

children.text: § 313. punar api gativiśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 313. For understanding yet another distinction of movement, he says —

children.text: avigrahā jīvasya ||
children.translated_text: The movement of the soul is without obstruction (<s>avigrahā</s>). ||

children.text: § 314. vigraho vyāghātaḥ kauṭilyam ity arthaḥ. sa yasyāṃ na vidyate ’sāv avigrahā gatiḥ. kasya? jīvasya. kīdṛśasya? muktasya. kathaṃ gamyate muktasyeti? uttarasūtre saṃsārigrahaṇād iha muktasyeti vijñāyate. nanu ca ‘anuśreṇi gatiḥ’ ity anenaiva śreṇyantarasaṃkramābhāvo vyākhyātaḥ. nārtho ’nena. pūrvasūtre viśreṇi gatir api kvacid astīti jñāpanārtham idaṃ vacanam. nanu tatraiva deśakālaniyama uktaḥ. na; atas tatsiddheḥ.
children.translated_text: § 314. '<s>Vigraha</s>' means obstruction, crookedness — this is the meaning. That [movement] in which it [obstruction] does not exist is unobstructed movement (<s>avigrahā gati</s>). Of whom? Of the soul. Of what kind? Of the liberated. How is it known that it means the liberated? From the mention of 'transmigrating' (<s>saṃsārin</s>) in the subsequent sūtra, it is understood that here the liberated is meant. [Objection:] But the absence of crossing between rows was already explained by 'movement is along a row'; this [sūtra] is unnecessary. [Reply:] This statement is for the purpose of indicating that in the previous sūtra, movement across rows also exists in some cases. [Objection:] But the time-and-place restriction was already stated there. [Reply:] No; because this [sūtra] establishes that [restriction].

children.text: § 315. yady asaṅgasyātmano ’pratibandhena gatir ālokāntād avadhṛtakālā pratijñāyate, sadehasya punar gatiḥ kiṃ pratibandhinī uta muktātmavad ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 315. If the unobstructed movement of the disembodied self, reaching up to the boundary of the non-cosmos, is affirmed for a definite time, then is the movement of the embodied [soul] obstructed, or is it like that of the liberated self? — to this he says —

children.text: vigrahavatī ca saṃsāriṇaḥ prāk caturbhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And [the movement] of the transmigrating [soul] is with obstruction (<s>vigrahavatī</s>), prior to the fourth [instant]. ||

children.text: § 316. kālāvadhāraṇārthaṃ ‘prāk caturbhyaḥ’ ity ucyate. ‘prāg’ ity vacanaṃ maryādārtham, caturthāt samayāt prag vigrahavatī gatir bhavati na caturthe iti. kuta iti cet? sarvotkṛṣṭavigrahanimittaniṣkuṭakṣetre utpitsuḥ prāṇī niṣkuṭakṣetrānupūrvyanuśreṇyabhāvādiṣu gatyabhāve niṣkuṭakṣetraprāpaṇanimittāṃ trivigrahāṃ gatim ārabhate nordhvām; tathāvidhopapādakṣetrābhāvāt. ‘ca’ śabdaḥ samuccayārthaḥ. vigrahavatī cāvigrahā ceti.
children.translated_text: § 316. 'Prior to the fourth' is stated for the purpose of fixing the time. The word '<s>prāk</s>' (prior) has the sense of a limit: prior to the fourth instant, the movement is with obstruction; not at the fourth. Why? A living being desiring to arise in the rebirth-field [corresponding to] the maximum obstruction, in the absence of a row along the path to the rebirth-field, when movement is impossible, undertakes a movement with three obstructions directed at reaching the rebirth-field, but not upward, because there is no rebirth-field of that kind [upward]. The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) has a connective meaning: both with obstruction and without obstruction.

children.text: § 317. vigrahavatyā gateḥ kālo ’vadhṛtaḥ. avigrahāyāḥ kiyān kāla ity ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 317. The time of movement with obstruction has been fixed. What is the time of movement without obstruction? — it is said —

children.text: ekasamayā ’vigrahā ||
children.translated_text: The unobstructed [movement] takes one instant (<s>ekasamayā</s>). ||

children.text: § 318. ekaḥ samayo yasyāḥ sā ekasamayā. na vidyate vigraho yasyāḥ sā avigrahā. gatimatāṃ hi jīvapudgalānām avyāghātenaikasamayikī gatir ālokāntād apīti.
children.translated_text: § 318. That which has one <s>samaya</s> (instant) is '<s>ekasamayā</s>.' That in which there is no obstruction is '<s>avigrahā</s>.' For the movement of souls and matter-particles that are in motion, occurring without impediment in a single instant — [this applies] even up to the boundary of the cosmos.

children.text: § 319. anādikarmabandhasaṃtatau mithyādarśanādipratyayavaśāt karmāṇyād adāno vigrahagatāv atyāhārakaḥ prasaktas tato niyamārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 319. In the continuum of beginningless <s>karma</s>-bondage, when a soul taking up <s>karmas</s> under the influence of wrong faith and the like and moving in transit to a body becomes involved in excessive intake, for the purpose of restricting [this], this is said —

children.text: ekaṃ dvau trīn vā ’nahārakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One, two, or three [instants is the soul] without intake (<s>anāhāraka</s>). ||

children.text: § 320. adhikārāt samayābhisaṃbandhaḥ. ‘vā’ śabdo vikalpārthaḥ. vikalpaś ca yathecchātisargaḥ. ekaṃ vā dvau vā trīn vā samayān anāhārako bhavitīty arthaḥ. trayāṇāṃ śarīrāṇāṃ ṣaṣṇām paryāptīnāṃ yogyapudgalagrahaṇam āhāraḥ.
tadabhāvād anāhārakaḥ. karmādānaṃ hi nirantaraṃ kārmaṇaśarīrasadbhāve. upapādakṣetraṃ prati ṛjvyāṃ gatau āhārakaḥ. itareṣu triṣu samayeṣu anāhārakaḥ.
children.translated_text: Due to the absence of that [intake], [the soul] is <s>anāhāraka</s> (without intake). For the intake of <s>karma</s> is continuous when the <s>kārmaṇa</s> (karmic) body exists. When moving in a straight line toward the rebirth-field, [the soul] takes intake. In the remaining three instants, [it is] without intake.

§ 320. By the governing topic, the connection is with <s>samaya</s> (instants). The word '<s>vā</s>' (or) has the sense of alternatives. And the alternative is an unrestricted option. The meaning is: for one, two, or three instants, [the soul] is without intake. The intake of matter-particles suitable for three bodies and six completions is <s>āhāra</s> (intake).

children.text: § 321. evaṃ gacchato ’bhinavamūrtyantaranirvṛttiprakārapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 321. For the purpose of explaining the manner of the formation of a new body for one thus moving, he says —

children.text: saṃmūrcchanagarbhopapādā janma ||
children.translated_text: Birth is [of three kinds:] <s>saṃmūrcchana</s> (spontaneous generation), <s>garbha</s> (womb-birth), and <s>upapāda</s> (apparitional birth). ||

children.text: § 322. triṣu lokeṣūrdhvam adhas tiryak ca dehasya samantato mūrcchanaṃ saṃmūrcchanaṃ avayavaprakalpanam. striyā udare śukraśoṇitayor garaṇaṃ miśraṇaṃ garbhaḥ. mātrupabhuktāhāragaraṇād vā garbhaḥ. upetya padyate ’sminn iti upapādaḥ. devanārakotpattisthānaviśeṣasaṃjñā. ete trayaḥ saṃsāriṇām jīvānāṃ janmaprakārāḥ śubhāśubhapariṇāmanimittakarmabhedavipākakṛtāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 322. The coalescence of the body on all sides — upward, downward, and sideways — in the three worlds, the formation of parts, is <s>saṃmūrcchana</s> (spontaneous generation). The conception — the mixing of semen and blood in a woman's womb — is <s>garbha</s> (womb-birth). Or <s>garbha</s> is [also] from the conception through the food consumed by the mother. <s>Upapāda</s> (apparitional birth) — so called because one arrives and is born there — is the special designation for the birthplace of gods and hell-beings. These three are the modes of birth for transmigrating souls, caused by the fruition of distinct <s>karmas</s> produced by auspicious and inauspicious mental dispositions.

children.text: § 323. athādhikṛtasya saṃsāraviṣayopabhogopalabdhyadhiṣṭhānapravaṇasya janmano yogivikalpā vaktavyā ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 323. Now, the various conditions of the womb (<s>yoni</s>) must be stated for the birth that has been discussed, which inclines toward obtaining the means and substrate for experiencing the objects of <s>saṃsāra</s> — to this he says —

children.text: sacittaśītasaṃvṛtāh setarā miśrāś caikaśas tadyonaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sentient (<s>sacittā</s>), cold (<s>śītā</s>), covered (<s>saṃvṛtā</s>), together with their opposites (<s>setarā</s>), and mixed (<s>miśrā</s>) — singly; these are the types of womb (<s>yoni</s>). ||

children.text: § 324. ātmanaś caitanyaviśeṣapariṇāmaś cittam. saha cittena vartata iti sacittaḥ. śīta iti sparśaviśeṣaḥ; śuklādivad ubhayavacanatvād tadyuktaṃ dravyam apy āha. samyagvṛtaḥ saṃvṛtaḥ. saṃvṛta iti durupalakṣyapradeśa ucyate. saha itarair vartanta iti setarāḥ. sapratipakṣā ity arthaḥ. ke punar itare? acittoṣṇavivṛtāḥ. ubhayātmako miśraḥ. sacittācittaḥ śītoṣṇaḥ saṃvṛtavivṛta iti. ‘ca’ śabdaḥ samuccayārthaḥ miśrāś ca yonayo bhavantīti. itarathā hi pūvoktānām eva viśeṣaṇaṃ syāt. ‘ekaśaḥ’ iti vīpsārthaḥ. tasya grahaṇaṃ kramamiśrapratipattyarthaṃ. yathaivaṃ vijñāyeta — sacittaś ca acittaś ca, śītaś ca uṣṇaś ca, saṃvṛtaś ca vivṛtaś ceti. maivaṃ vijñāyi — sacittaś ca śītaś cety ādi. ‘tadgrahaṇaṃ’ janmaprakārapratinirdeśārtham. teṣāṃ saṃmūrcchanādīnāṃ janmanāṃ yonaya iti. ta ete nava yonayo veditavyāḥ. yonijanmanor aviśeṣa iti cet? na; ādhārādheyabhedāt tadbhedaḥ. ta ete sacittādayo yonaya ādhārāḥ. ādheyā janmaprakārāḥ. yataḥ sacittādiyonyadhiṣṭhāne ātmā saṃmūrcchanādinā janmanā śarīrāhārendriyādiyogyān pudgalān upādatte. devanārakā acittayonayaḥ. teṣām hi yonir upapādadeśapudgalapracayo ’cittaḥ. garbhajā miśrayonayaḥ. teṣāṃ hi mātur udare śukraśoṇitam acittam, tadātmanā cittavatā miśraṇān miśrayoniḥ. saṃmūrcchanajās trivikalpayonayaḥ. kecit sacittayonayaḥ. anye acittayonayaḥ. apare miśrayonayaḥ. sacittayonayaḥ sādhāraṇaśarīrāḥ. kutaḥ? paraparāśrayatvāt. itare acittayonayo miśrayonayaś ca. śītoṣṇayonayo devanārakāḥ. teṣāṃ hi upapādasthānāni kānicic chītāni kānicid uṣṇānīti. uṣṇayonayas taijaskāyikāḥ. itare trivikalpayonayaḥ. kecic chītayonayaḥ. kecid uṣṇayonayaḥ apare miśrayonaya iti. devanārakaikendriyāḥ saṃvṛtayonayaḥ. vikalendriyā vivṛtayonayaḥ. garbhajāḥ miśrayonayaḥ. tadbhedāś caturaśītiśatasahasrasaṃkhyā āgamato veditavyāḥ. uktaṃ ca —
ṇiccidaradhādu satta ya taru dasa viyaliṃdiesu chacceva |
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] Earth-bodied seven hundred thousand, plants ten [hundred thousand], beings with incomplete senses six hundred thousand each,

children.text: suraṇirayatiriya cauro coddasa maṇue sadasahassā ||
children.translated_text: gods, hell-beings, and animals four [hundred thousand each], humans fourteen hundred thousand.

§ 324. <s>Citta</s> (sentience) is the specific modification of the consciousness of the self. That which exists together with <s>citta</s> is <s>sacittā</s> (sentient). '<s>Śīta</s>' (cold) is a specific type of touch; like 'white' and the like, since the word is used in both senses, it also refers to the substance possessing it. '<s>Saṃvṛta</s>' (covered) means well-enclosed; it denotes a location that is difficult to perceive. Those that exist with the others are '<s>setarā</s>' (together with their opposites) — meaning 'with their counterparts.' And what are the others? Non-sentient (<s>acitta</s>), hot (<s>uṣṇa</s>), and open (<s>vivṛta</s>). That which has the nature of both is '<s>miśra</s>' (mixed): sentient-and-non-sentient, cold-and-hot, covered-and-open. The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) has a connective meaning: mixed ones are also types of womb. Otherwise, they would be merely qualifications of the previously stated [types]. '<s>Ekaśaḥ</s>' (singly) has a distributive meaning. Its mention is for understanding the sequential and mixed [application]. Thus it should be understood: sentient and non-sentient; cold and hot; covered and open. It should not be understood as: sentient and cold, etc. The word '<s>tad</s>' (that) is for the purpose of indicating the mode of birth: those — of <s>saṃmūrcchana</s> and the rest — are the types of birth, [and their] wombs. These should be understood as nine types of womb. [Objection:] If there is no difference between womb (<s>yoni</s>) and birth (<s>janma</s>)? [Reply:] No; because of the difference between container and contained, there is a distinction. These — sentient and the rest — as wombs are the containers. The modes of birth are the contained. Because in a substrate of a sentient womb and the like, the self, through birth by spontaneous generation and the like, takes up matter-particles suitable for body, food, sense organs, and the like. Gods and hell-beings have non-sentient wombs, for their womb — the aggregate of matter-particles at the place of apparitional birth — is non-sentient. The womb-born have mixed wombs, for in the mother's womb, the semen and blood are non-sentient, and since there is mixing with the self that is sentient, the womb is mixed. The spontaneously generated have three types of wombs: some have sentient wombs, others have non-sentient wombs, and others have mixed wombs. Those with sentient wombs are those sharing a common body. Why? Because of mutual dependence. The others have non-sentient or mixed wombs. Gods and hell-beings have cold and hot wombs, for some of their places of apparitional birth are cold and some are hot. Fire-bodied beings have hot wombs. The rest have three types of wombs: some have cold wombs, some hot, and others mixed. Gods, hell-beings, and one-sensed beings have covered wombs. Beings with incomplete sense organs have open wombs. The womb-born have mixed wombs. Their subdivisions — numbering eighty-four hundred thousand — should be known from scripture. And it has been said —

children.text: § 325. evam etasmin navayonibhedasaṃkaṭe trividhajanmani sarvaprāṇabhṛtām aniyamena prasakte tadavadhāraṇārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 325. Thus, when all living beings are indiscriminately involved in the threefold birth within the complex of nine types of womb, for the purpose of determining [which birth belongs to whom], he says —

children.text: jarāyujāṇḍajapotānāṃ garbhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Womb-birth (<s>garbha</s>) belongs to the viviparous (<s>jarāyuja</s>), oviparous (<s>aṇḍaja</s>), and fledglings (<s>pota</s>). ||

children.text: § 326. yaj jālavatprāṇiparivaraṇaṃ vitatamāṃsaśoṇitaṃ taj jarāyuḥ. yan nakhatvaksadṛśam upāttakāṭhinyaṃ śukraśoṇitaparivaraṇaṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ tad aṇḍam. kiṃcit parivaraṇam antareṇa paripūrṇāvayavo yoninirgatamātra eva parispandādisāmarthyopetaḥ potaḥ. jarāyau jātā jarāyujāḥ. aṇḍe jātā aṇḍajāḥ. jarāyujāś ca aṇḍajāś ca potāś ca jarāyujāṇḍajapotā garbhayonayaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 326. That which is a net-like covering of the living being, consisting of extended flesh and blood, is the <s>jarāyu</s> (placental membrane). That which resembles a nail or skin, having acquired hardness, a round covering of semen and blood, is the <s>aṇḍa</s> (egg). That [being] which, without any covering, is born with fully formed parts and is endowed with the capacity for movement and the like immediately upon emerging from the womb, is a <s>pota</s> (fledgling). Those born in a <s>jarāyu</s> are <s>jarāyuja</s> (viviparous). Those born from an <s>aṇḍa</s> are <s>aṇḍaja</s> (oviparous). The viviparous, oviparous, and fledglings have womb-birth as their mode.

children.text: § 327. yady amīṣāṃ jarāyujāṇḍajapotānāṃ garbho ’vadhriyate, athopapādaḥ keṣāṃ bhavatīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 327. If womb-birth is confined to the viviparous, oviparous, and fledglings, then for whom does apparitional birth (<s>upapāda</s>) occur? — to this he says —

children.text: devanārakāṇām upapādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Apparitional birth (<s>upapāda</s>) belongs to gods and hell-beings. ||

children.text: devānāṃ nārakāṇām copapādo janma veditavyam.
children.translated_text: The birth of gods and hell-beings should be understood as apparitional.

children.text: § 328. athānyeṣāṃ kiṃ janmety ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 328. Now, what is the birth of the rest? — to this he says —

children.text: śeṣāṇāṃ saṃmūrcchanam ||
children.translated_text: Spontaneous generation (<s>saṃmūrcchana</s>) belongs to the rest. ||

children.text: § 329. garbhajebhya aupapādikebhyaś cānye śeṣāḥ. saṃmūrcchanaṃ janmeti. ete trayo ’pi yogā niyamārthāḥ. ubhayato niyamaś ca draṣṭavyaḥ. jarāyujāṇḍajapotānām eva garbhaḥ. garbha eva ca jarāyujāṇḍajapotānām. devanārakāṇām evopapādaḥ. upapāda eva ca devanārakāṇām. śeṣāṇām eva saṃmūrcchanam. saṃmūrcchanam eva śeṣāṇām iti.
children.translated_text: § 329. The rest are those other than the womb-born and the apparitionally born. Their birth is spontaneous generation. These three combinations are for the purpose of restriction. And the restriction should be understood from both sides: womb-birth belongs only to the viviparous, oviparous, and fledglings; and the viviparous, oviparous, and fledglings have only womb-birth. Apparitional birth belongs only to gods and hell-beings; and gods and hell-beings have only apparitional birth. Spontaneous generation belongs only to the rest; and the rest have only spontaneous generation.

children.text: § 330. teṣāṃ punaḥ saṃsāriṇāṃ trividhajanmanāmāhitabahuvikalpanavayonibhedānāṃ śubhāśubhanāmakarmavipākanirvartitāni bandhaphalānubhavanādhiṣṭhānāni śarīrāṇi kānīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 330. Now, what are the bodies — the substrates for experiencing the fruits of bondage, produced by the fruition of auspicious and inauspicious <s>nāma-karma</s> (name-determining karma) — of those transmigrating beings who have the threefold birth, the manifold nine types of womb? — to this he says —

children.text: audārikavaikriyikāhārakataijasakārmaṇāni śarīrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: The bodies are: <s>audārika</s> (gross), <s>vaikriyika</s> (transformable), <s>āhāraka</s> (assimilative), <s>taijasa</s> (fiery), and <s>kārmaṇa</s> (karmic). ||

children.text: § 331. viśiṣṭanāmakarmodayāpāditavṛttīni śīryanta iti śarīrāṇi. audārikādiprakṛtiviśeṣodayaprāptavṛttīni audārikādīni. udāraṃ sthūlam. udāre bhavaṃ udāraṃ prayojanam asyeti vā, audārikam. aṣṭaguṇaiśvaryayogād ekānekāṇumahac charīravidhikaraṇaṃ vikriyā, sā prayojanam asyeti vaikriyikam. sūkṣmapadārthanirjñānārtham asaṃyamaparijihīrṣayā vā pramattasaṃyatenāhriyate nirvartyate tad ity āhārakam. yat tejor nimittaṃ tejasi vā bhavaṃ tat taijasam. karmaṇāṃ kāryaṃ kārmaṇam. sarveṣāṃ karmanimittattve ’pi rūḍhivaśāt viśiṣṭaviṣaye vṛttir avaseyā.
children.translated_text: § 331. Bodies are so called because they decay (<s>śīryante</s>), their functions being brought about by the fruition of specific name-<s>karmas</s>. The <s>audārika</s> (gross) and the others are [bodies] whose functions are obtained through the fruition of the specific subtypes of the <s>audārika</s> and other [body-name karma] classes. <s>Udāra</s> means 'gross'; that which is related to the gross, or that whose purpose is gross — that is <s>audārika</s>. <s>Vikriyā</s> (transformation) is the ability to modify one's body — making it single, multiple, atomic, or huge — through the <s>yoga</s> of the eightfold supernatural powers; that whose purpose is this [transformation] is <s>vaikriyika</s> (transformable). That which is drawn out and fashioned by a restrained-with-negligence [monk] for the purpose of ascertaining subtle matters or out of a desire to protect his restraint is <s>āhāraka</s> (projectable). That which has <s>tejas</s> (luminous energy) as its cause or which exists in <s>tejas</s> is <s>taijasa</s> (luminous). That which is the product of <s>karmas</s> is <s>kārmaṇa</s> (karmic). Even though all [bodies] are caused by <s>karma</s>, due to conventional usage, the application [of this term] should be understood in the specific [karmic body] sense.

children.text: § 332. yathaudārikasyendriyair upalabdhis tathetareṣāṃ kasmān na bhavatīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 332. Just as the <s>audārika</s> (gross body) is perceived by the senses, why is it not so for the others? To this he says —

children.text: paraṃ paraṃ sūkṣmam ||
children.translated_text: Each successive one is subtler.

children.text: § 333. ‘para’ śabdasyānekārthavṛttitve ’pi vivakṣāto vyavasthārthagatiḥ. pṛthagbhūtānāṃ śarīrāṇāṃ sūkṣmaguṇena vīpsānirdeśaḥ kriyate paramparam iti. audārikaṃ sthūlam, tataḥ sūkṣmaṃ vaikriyikam, tataḥ sūkṣmam āhārakaṃ tataḥ sūkṣmaṃ taijasam, taijasāt kārmaṇaṃ sūkṣmam iti.
children.translated_text: § 333. Although the word '<s>para</s>' has multiple meanings, from the intended [context] the relevant meaning is understood. The repetitive statement '<s>paramparam</s>' (each successive one) is made with the qualifier of subtlety regarding the bodies taken separately. The <s>audārika</s> is gross; subtler than that is the <s>vaikriyika</s>; subtler than that is the <s>āhāraka</s>; subtler than that is the <s>taijasa</s>; and subtler than the <s>taijasa</s> is the <s>kārmaṇa</s>.

children.text: § 334. yadi paramparaṃ sūkṣmam, pradeśato ’pi nyūnaṃ paramparaṃ hīnam iti viparītapratipattinivṛttyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 334. If each successive one is subtler, then each successive one should also be smaller in space-points — to prevent this wrong inference, he says —

children.text: pradeśato ’samkhyeyaguṇaṃ prāktaijasāt ||
children.translated_text: In space-points, [each is] innumerably greater, up to the <s>taijasa</s>.

children.text: § 335. pradiśyanta iti pradeśāḥ paramāṇavaḥ. saṃkhyām atīto ’saṃkhyeyaḥ. asaṃkhyeyo guṇo ’sya tad idam asaṃkhyeyaguṇam. kutaḥ? pradeśataḥ. nāvagāhataḥ. paramparam ity anuvṛtter ā kārmaṇāt prasaṅge tannivṛttyartham āha prāktaijasād iti. audārikād asaṃkhyeyaguṇapradeśaṃ vaikriyikam. vaikriyikād asaṃkhyeyaguṇapradeśam āhārakam iti. ko guṇakāraḥ. palyopamāsaṃkhyeyabhāgaḥ. yady evam, paramparaṃ mahāparimāṇaṃ prāpnoti? naivam; bandhaviśeṣāt parimāṇabhedābhāvas tūlanicayāyaḥpiṇḍavat.
children.translated_text: § 335. Space-points (<s>pradeśa</s>) are atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>) — so called because they are 'pointed out.' That which has exceeded enumeration is <s>asaṃkhyeya</s> (innumerable). That which has an innumerable multiplier — that is 'innumerably greater.' From what? From [the standpoint of] space-points, not from [the standpoint of] spatial extent. Since the continuation of 'each successive one' would [otherwise] extend up to the <s>kārmaṇa</s>, to prevent that he says 'up to the <s>taijasa</s>.' The <s>vaikriyika</s> has innumerably more space-points than the <s>audārika</s>; the <s>āhāraka</s> has innumerably more space-points than the <s>vaikriyika</s>. What is the multiplier? An innumerable fraction of a <s>palyopama</s>. If so, wouldn't each successive one reach an enormous size? Not so; due to the specific mode of binding, there is no difference in size — like a heap of cotton [compressed into] a ball.

children.text: § 336. athottarayoḥ kiṃ samapradeśatvam utāsti kaścid viśeṣa ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 336. Now, for the latter two [bodies], is there equality of space-points, or is there some distinction? To this he says —

children.text: anantaguṇe pare ||
children.translated_text: The latter two are infinitely greater [in space-points].

children.text: § 337. pradeśata ity anuvartate, tenaivam abhisaṃbandhaḥ kriyate — āhārakāt taijasaṃ pradeśato ’nantaguṇam, taijasāt kārmaṇaṃ pradeśato ’nantaguṇam iti. ko guṇakāraḥ? abhavyānām anantaguṇaḥ siddhānām anantabhāgaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 337. 'In space-points' continues [from before]; thus the connection is made: the <s>taijasa</s> is infinitely greater in space-points than the <s>āhāraka</s>; the <s>kārmaṇa</s> is infinitely greater in space-points than the <s>taijasa</s>. What is the multiplier? For the incapable (<s>abhavya</s>), an infinite multiple; for the liberated (<s>siddha</s>), an infinite fraction.

children.text: § 338. tatraitat syāc chalyakavanmūrtimaddravyopacitatvāt saṃsāriṇo jīvasyābhipretagatinirodhaprasaṅga iti? tan na; kiṃ kāraṇam. yasmād ubhe apy ete —
children.translated_text: § 338. Here this [objection] might arise: since the transmigrating soul is constituted by material substance possessing form, like a porcupine [enclosed in its quills], there would be the undesirable consequence that its movement to the desired destiny would be obstructed? No, that is not so. Why? Because both of these —

children.text: apratīghate ||
children.translated_text: [are] non-obstructive.

children.text: § 339. mūrtimato mūrtyantareṇa vyāghātaḥ pratīghātaḥ. sa nāsty anayor ity apratīghāte; sūkṣmapariṇāmāt ayaḥpiṇḍe tejo ’nupraveśavattaijasakārmaṇayor nāsti vajrapaṭalādiṣu vyāghātaḥ. nanu ca vaikriyikāhārakayor api nāsti pratīghātaḥ? sarvatrāpratīghāto ’tra vivakṣitaḥ. yathā taijasakārmaṇāyor ā lokāntāt sarvatra nāsti pratīghātaḥ, na tathā vaikriyikāhārakayoḥ.
children.translated_text: § 339. For material entities, obstruction (<s>pratīghāta</s>) occurs through other material entities. That does not exist for these two — hence they are 'non-obstructive.' Due to their subtle transformation, just as luminous energy (<s>tejas</s>) enters an iron ball, there is no obstruction for the <s>taijasa</s> and <s>kārmaṇa</s> bodies even in diamond surfaces and the like. Objection: But for the <s>vaikriyika</s> and <s>āhāraka</s> too, there is no obstruction? [Reply:] What is intended here is non-obstruction everywhere. Just as for the <s>taijasa</s> and <s>kārmaṇa</s> there is no obstruction anywhere up to the boundary of the universe — the same is not true for the <s>vaikriyika</s> and <s>āhāraka</s>.

children.text: § 340. āha kim etāvān eva viśeṣa uta kaścid anyo ’apy astīty āha —
children.translated_text: § 340. He asks: Is this the only distinctive feature, or is there yet another? He says —

children.text: anādisaṃbandhe ca ||
children.translated_text: And [they have] a beginningless connection.

children.text: § 341. ‘ca’ śabdo vikalpārthaḥ. anādisaṃbandhe sādisaṃbandhe ceti. kāryakāraṇabhāvasaṃtatyā anādisaṃbandhe, viśeṣāpekṣayā sādisaṃbandhe ca bījavṛkṣavat. yathaudārikavaikriyikāhārakāṇi jīvasya kadācit kāni, na tathā taijasakārmaṇe. nityasaṃbandhinī hi te ā saṃsārakṣayāt.
children.translated_text: § 341. The particle '<s>ca</s>' is used in the sense of alternatives: both 'beginningless connection' and 'connection with a beginning.' Through the continuity of the cause-effect relationship, [the connection is] beginningless; from the standpoint of the particular, it has a beginning — like a seed and a tree. Just as the <s>audārika</s>, <s>vaikriyika</s>, and <s>āhāraka</s> [bodies] belong to the soul only sometimes, not so the <s>taijasa</s> and <s>kārmaṇa</s>. For these two are permanently connected [with the soul] until the destruction of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration).

children.text: § 342. ta ete taijasakārmaṇe kiṃ kasyacid eva bhavata utāviśeṣeṇety ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 342. Do these <s>taijasa</s> and <s>kārmaṇa</s> [bodies] belong only to some [souls], or to all without distinction? To this he says —

children.text: sarvasya ||
children.translated_text: [They belong] to all.

children.text: § 343. ‘sarva’ śabdo niravaśeṣavācī. niravaśeṣasya saṃsāriṇo jīvasya te dve api śarīre bhavata ity arhaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 343. The word '<s>sarva</s>' (all) denotes 'without exception.' The meaning is: both these bodies belong to every transmigrating soul without exception.

children.text: § 344. aviśeṣābhidhānāt tair audārikādibhiḥ sarvasya saṃsāriṇo yaugapadyena saṃbandhaprasaṃge saṃbhaviśarīrapradarśanārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 344. Since the statement is without distinction, there would be the undesirable consequence that all transmigrating [souls] are connected simultaneously with the <s>audārika</s> and other [bodies] along with those [<s>taijasa</s> and <s>kārmaṇa</s>] — to show which bodies are possible [together], this is said —

children.text: tadādīni bhājyāni yugapad ekasyā caturbhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Beginning with those [<s>taijasa</s> and <s>kārmaṇa</s>], [bodies] are to be classified as [occurring] simultaneously for one [soul], up to four.

children.text: § 345. ‘tad’ śabdaḥ prakṛtataijasakārmaṇapratinirdeśārthaḥ. te taijasakārmaṇe ādir yeṣāṃ tāni tadādini. bhājyāni vikalpyāni. ā kutaḥ? āṃ caturbhyaḥ. yugapad ekasyātmanaḥ. kasyācid dve taijasakārmaṇe. aparasya trīṇi audārikataijasakārmaṇāni vaikriyikataijasakārmaṇāni vā. anyasya catvāri audārikāhārakataijasakārmaṇānīti vibhāgaḥ kriyate.
children.translated_text: § 345. The word '<s>tad</s>' (that) refers back to the <s>taijasa</s> and <s>kārmaṇa</s> under discussion. Those which begin with them are '<s>tadādini</s>.' 'To be classified' means 'to be distinguished.' Up to what? Up to four. Simultaneously, for a single self: some have two — the <s>taijasa</s> and <s>kārmaṇa</s>. Another has three — <s>audārika</s>, <s>taijasa</s>, and <s>kārmaṇa</s>, or <s>vaikriyika</s>, <s>taijasa</s>, and <s>kārmaṇa</s>. Yet another has four — <s>audārika</s>, <s>āhāraka</s>, <s>taijasa</s>, and <s>kārmaṇa</s> — thus the classification is made.

children.text: § 346. punar api teṣāṃ viśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 346. To further determine distinctions among them, he says —

children.text: nirupabhogam antyam ||
children.translated_text: The last one is without enjoyment (<s>nirupabhoga</s>).

children.text: § 347. ante bhavam antyam. kiṃ tat? kārmaṇam. indriyapraṇālikayā śabdādīnām upalabdhir upabhogaḥ. tadabhāvān nirupabhogam. vigrahagatau satyām api indriyalabdhau dravyendriyanirvṛttyabhāvāc chabdādyupabhogābhāva iti. nanu taijasam api nirupabhogam tatra kim ucyate nirupabhogam antyam iti? taijasaṃ śarīraṃ yoganimittam api na bhavati, tato ’syopabhogavicāre ’nadhikāraḥ.
children.translated_text: § 347. That which is at the end is 'the last.' What is that? The <s>kārmaṇa</s>. Enjoyment (<s>upabhoga</s>) is the apprehension of sound and the like through the channel of the senses. Due to its absence, [the kārmaṇa body is] 'without enjoyment.' Even though in the state of transit (<s>vigrahagatau</s>) there may be sense-faculties [in potential], due to the absence of the formation of material sense-organs, there is no enjoyment of sound and the like. Objection: The <s>taijasa</s> body too is without enjoyment — so why say 'the last one is without enjoyment'? [Reply:] The <s>taijasa</s> body does not arise even as a cause of <s>yoga</s> (bodily activity), and therefore has no standing in the discussion of enjoyment.

children.text: § 348. evaṃ tatroktalakṣaṇeṣu janmasu amūni śarīrāṇi prādurbhāvam āpadyamānāni kim aviśeṣeṇa bhavanti, uta kaścid asti prativiśeṣa ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 348. Thus, these bodies, manifesting in the births described with their characteristics — do they arise without distinction, or is there some specific [mode]? To this he says —

children.text: garbhasaṃmūrcchanajam ādyam ||
children.translated_text: The first [body] is born from the womb or from spontaneous generation (<s>saṃmūrcchana</s>).

children.text: § 349. sūtrakramāpekṣayā ādau bhavam ādyam. audārikam ity arthaḥ. yad garbhajaṃ yac ca saṃmūrcchanajaṃ tat sarvam audārikaṃ draṣṭavyam.
children.translated_text: § 349. 'First' means 'first in the order of the sūtras' — the meaning is the <s>audārika</s> body. Whatever is womb-born and whatever is spontaneously generated — all that should be understood as <s>audārika</s>.

children.text: § 350. tadantaraṃ yan nirdiṣṭaṃ tat kasmin janmanīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 350. The one mentioned next after that — in which type of birth [does it occur]? To this he says —

children.text: aupapādikaṃ vaikriyikam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>vaikriyika</s> [body arises in beings of] spontaneous generation (<s>aupapādika</s>).

children.text: § 351. upapāde bhavam aupapādikam, tatsarvaṃ vaikriyikaṃ veditavyam.
children.translated_text: § 351. <s>Aupapādika</s> means 'arising through spontaneous generation (<s>upapāda</s>).' All of that should be known as <s>vaikriyika</s>.

children.text: § 352. yady aupapādikaṃ vaikriyikam, anaupapādikasya vaikriyikatvābhāva ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 352. If the <s>aupapādika</s> [birth] is [associated with] the <s>vaikriyika</s> [body], then one not born by <s>aupapādika</s> [birth] would lack <s>vaikriyika</s> [capacity] — to this he says —

children.text: labdhipratyayaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And [the <s>vaikriyika</s> may also be] one whose cause is [supernatural] attainment (<s>labdhi</s>).

children.text: § 353. ‘ca’ śabdena vaikriyikam abhisaṃbadhyate. tapoviśeṣād ṛddhiprāptir labdhiḥ. labdhiḥ pratyayaḥ kāraṇam asya labdhipratyayam. vaikriyikaṃ labdhipratyayaṃ ca bhavatīty abhisaṃbadhyate.
children.translated_text: § 353. The particle '<s>ca</s>' connects with '<s>vaikriyika</s>.' <s>Labdhi</s> is the acquisition of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) through special austerities. That whose cause (<s>pratyaya</s>) is <s>labdhi</s> is '<s>labdhi-pratyaya</s>.' It is connected [with the previous] as: 'the <s>vaikriyika</s> [body] also arises from <s>labdhi</s> as its cause.'

children.text: § 354. kim etad eva labdhyapekṣam utānyad apy astīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 354. Is only this [<s>vaikriyika</s>] dependent on [supernatural] attainment, or is there another? To this he says —

children.text: taijasam api ||
children.translated_text: The <s>taijasa</s> also.

children.text: § 355. ‘api’ śabdena labdhipratyayam abhisaṃbadhyate. taijasam api labdhipratyayaṃ bhavatīti
children.translated_text: § 355. The particle '<s>api</s>' connects with '<s>labdhi-pratyaya</s>.' The <s>taijasa</s> [body] too arises from <s>labdhi</s> as its cause.

children.text: § 356. vaikriyikānantaraṃ yad upadiṣṭaṃ tasya svarūpanirdhāraṇārthaṃ svāminirdeśārthaṃ cāha —
children.translated_text: § 356. To determine the intrinsic nature and to specify the possessor of what was taught immediately after the <s>vaikriyika</s>, he says —

children.text: śubhaṃ viśuddham avyāghāti cāhārakaṃ pramattasaṃyatasyaiva ||
children.translated_text: The <s>āhāraka</s> (projectable body) is auspicious (<s>śubha</s>), pure (<s>viśuddha</s>), non-obstructive (<s>avyāghāti</s>), and belongs only to the restrained-with-negligence (<s>pramatta-saṃyata</s>).

children.text: § 357. śubhakāraṇatvāc chubhavyapadeśaḥ. śubhakarmaṇa āhārakakāyayogasya kāraṇatvāc chubham ity ucyate annasya prāṇavyapadeśavat. viśuddhakāryatvād viśuddhavyapadeśaḥ. viśuddhasya puṇyakarmaṇaḥ aśabalasya niravadyasya kāryatvād viśuddham ity ucyate tantūnāṃ kārpāsavyapadeśavat. ubhayato vyāghātābhāvād avyāghāti. na hy āhārakaśarīreṇānyasya vyāghātaḥ. nāpy anyenāhārakasyeti. tasya prayojanasamucyārthaḥ  ‘ca’ śabdaḥ kriyate.

tad yathā — kadācil labdhiviśeṣasadbhāvajñāpanārthaṃ kadācit sūkṣmapadārthanirdhāraṇārthaṃ saṃyamaparipālanārthaṃ ca. āhārakam iti prāguktasya pratyāmnāyaḥ. yadāhārakaśarīraṃ nirvartayitum ārabhate tadā pramatto bhavatīti ‘pramattasaṃyatasya’ ity ucyate. iṣṭato ’vadhāraṇārthaṃ ‘eva’kāropādānam. yathaivaṃ vijñāyeta pramattasaṃyatasyaivāhārakaṃ nānyasyeti. maivaṃ vijñāyi pramattasaṃyatasyāhārakam eveti. mā bhūd audārikādinivṛttir iti.
children.translated_text: Thus — sometimes for the purpose of making known the existence of a special attainment, sometimes for the purpose of ascertaining subtle matters, and for the purpose of safeguarding one's restraint. '<s>Āhāraka</s>' is a restatement of what was said before.
