When one begins to fashion the <s>āhāraka</s> body, at that time one becomes negligent (<s>pramatta</s>) — therefore it is said 'of the restrained-with-negligence.' The word '<s>eva</s>' (only) is used for the purpose of restrictive determination from the desired [standpoint]: this should be understood as — 'the <s>āhāraka</s> belongs only to the restrained-with-negligence, not to another.' It should not be understood as: 'the restrained-with-negligence has only the <s>āhāraka</s> [and no other body]' — lest [one think] the <s>audārika</s> and other [bodies] are excluded.

§ 357. It is designated '<s>śubha</s>' (auspicious) because of being caused by auspicious [karma]: since the <s>āhāraka-kāya-yoga</s> (projectable-body activity) is caused by auspicious <s>karma</s>, it is called <s>śubha</s> — like rice being designated as 'life' (<s>prāṇa</s>). It is designated '<s>viśuddha</s>' (pure) because of being the effect of a pure [cause]: since it is the effect of pure merit-<s>karma</s>, which is unmixed and faultless, it is called <s>viśuddha</s> — like threads being designated as 'cotton.' It is 'non-obstructive' (<s>avyāghāti</s>) because of the absence of obstruction from both sides: for the <s>āhāraka</s> body does not obstruct another, nor does another obstruct the <s>āhāraka</s>. The particle '<s>ca</s>' is used for indicating its purposes jointly.

children.text: § 358. evaṃ vibhaktāni śarīrāṇi bibhratāṃ saṃsāriṇāṃ pratigati kiṃ triliṅgasaṃnidhānaṃ uta liṅganiyamaḥ kaścid astīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 358. When transmigrating beings bearing these differentiated bodies [are considered] — for each state of existence, is there the presence of all three genders, or is there some restriction of gender? To this he says —

children.text: nārakasaṃmūrcchino napuṃsakāni ||
children.translated_text: Hell-beings and the spontaneously-generated are neuter (<s>napuṃsaka</s>).

children.text: § 359. nārakāṇi vakṣyante. narakeṣu bhavā nārakāḥ. saṃmūrcchanaṃ saṃmūrcchaḥ sa yeṣām asti te saṃmūrcchinaḥ. nārakāś ca saṃmūrcchinaś ca nārakasaṃmūrcchinaḥ. cāritramohavikalpanokaṣāyabhedasya napuṃsakavedasyāśubhanāmnaś codayān na striyo na pumāṃsa iti napuṃsakāni bhavanti. nārakasaṃmūrcchino napuṃsakāny eveti niyamaḥ. tatra hi strīpuṃsaviṣayamanojñaśabdagandharūparasasparśasaṃbandhanimittā svalpāpi sukhamātrā nāsti.
children.translated_text: § 359. 'Hell-beings' (<s>nārakāḥ</s>) will be described [later]. Those born in hells are <s>nārakas</s>. <s>Saṃmūrcchana</s> (spontaneous generation) is that which those who possess it — the <s>saṃmūrcchins</s>. '<s>Nāraka-saṃmūrcchins</s>' is a copulative compound: hell-beings and the spontaneously-generated. Due to the fruition of the neuter gender (<s>napuṃsaka-veda</s>), a variety of conduct-deluding <s>karma</s>, a subtype of quasi-passion, and an inauspicious name-<s>karma</s> — they are neither women nor men, hence they are neuter. The restriction is: hell-beings and the spontaneously-generated are neuter only. For in those [states], there is not even a trace of pleasure arising from the connection with pleasing sounds, smells, forms, tastes, and touches that relate to the female and male [domains].

children.text: § 360. yady evam avaghriyate, arthād āpannam etad uktebhyo ’nye saṃsāriṇas triliṅgā iti yatrātyantaṃ napuṃsakaliṅgasyābhāvas tatpratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 360. If so, it is implied that transmigrating beings other than those mentioned are of all three genders. To explain [the case] where there is an absolute absence of the neuter gender, he says —

children.text: na devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Not the gods.

children.text: § 361. straiṇaṃ pauṃsnaṃ ca yan niratiśayasukhaṃ śubhagatināmodayāpekṣaṃ tad devā anubhavantīti na teṣu napuṃsakāni santi.
children.translated_text: § 361. Gods experience the unsurpassed pleasure — both feminine and masculine [in nature] — that depends on the fruition of auspicious destiny and name [karmas]. Therefore, neuter [gender] does not exist among them.

children.text: § 362. athetare kiyal liṅgā ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 362. Now, the others — how many genders do they have? To this he says —

children.text: śeṣās trivedāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The remaining [beings] have all three genders (<s>triveda</s>).

children.text: § 363. trayo vedā yeṣāṃ te trivedāḥ. ke punas te vedāḥ? strītvaṃ puṃstvaṃ napuṃsakatvam iti. kathaṃ teṣāṃ siddhiḥ? vedyata iti vedaḥ. liṃgam ity arthaḥ. tad dvividhaṃ dravyaliṃgaṃ bhāvaliṃgaṃ ceti. dravyaliṃgaṃ yonimehanādi nāmakarmodayanirvartitam. nokaṣāyodayāpāditavṛtti bhāvaliṃgam. strīvedodayāt styāyastyasyāṃ garbha iti strī. puṃvedodayāt sūte janayatyapatyam iti pumān. napuṃsakavedodayāt tadubhayaśaktivikalaṃ napuṃsakam. rūḍhiśabdāś caite. rūḍhiṣu ca kriyā vyutpattyarthaṃ ca. yathā gacchatīti gaur iti. itarathā hi garbhadhāraṇādikriyāprādhānye bālavṛddhānāṃ tiryaṅmanuṣyāṇāṃ devānāṃ kārmaṇakāyayogasthānāṃ ca tadabhāvāt strītvādivyapadeśo na syāt. ta ete trayo vedāḥ śeṣāṇāṃ garbhajānāṃ bhavanti.
children.translated_text: § 363. Those who have three <s>vedas</s> (genders) are <s>trivedas</s>. What then are those <s>vedas</s>? Femaleness (<s>strītva</s>), maleness (<s>puṃstva</s>), and neuter-ness (<s>napuṃsakatva</s>). How are they established? That which is experienced (<s>vedyate</s>) is <s>veda</s>; the meaning is 'gender' (<s>liṅga</s>). It is twofold: material gender (<s>dravya-liṅga</s>) and dispositional gender (<s>bhāva-liṅga</s>). Material gender — the womb, genitals, and so on — is produced by the fruition of name-<s>karma</s>. Dispositional gender is a function brought about by the fruition of quasi-passion (<s>nokaṣāya</s>). From the fruition of female-gender [karma]: 'she conceives; in her is the embryo' — [thus she is called] a woman (<s>strī</s>). From the fruition of male-gender [karma]: 'he begets, he produces offspring' — [thus he is called] a man (<s>pumān</s>). From the fruition of neuter-gender [karma]: one lacking the capacity of both — [is called] neuter (<s>napuṃsaka</s>). These are conventional words (<s>rūḍhi-śabda</s>). In conventional [usage], the etymological meaning is [expressed through] action. Just as '<s>go</s>' (cow) [means] 'that which goes.' Otherwise — if the activity of bearing an embryo and so on were predominant — then children, the elderly, animals, humans, gods, and those in the state of the karmic body would lack the designation of femaleness and so on, since those [activities] are absent [in them]. These three genders belong to the remaining [beings], i.e., the womb-born.

children.text: § 364. ya ime janmayoniśarīraliṃgasaṃbandhāhitaviśeṣāḥ prāṇino nirdiśyante devādayo vicitradharmādharmavaśīkṛtāś catasṛṣu gatiṣu śarīrāṇi dhārayantas te kiṃ yathākālam upabhuktāyuṣo mūrtyantarāṇy āskandanti utāyathākālam apīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 364. These beings — specified by differences of birth, origin, body, and gender — these gods and others, subject to the varied forces of merit and demerit, bearing bodies in the four states of existence: do they, when their lifespan is exhausted in due time, proceed to another embodiment, or even before due time? To this he says —

children.text: aupapādikacaramottamadehāsaṃkhyeyavarṣāyuṣo ’napavartyāyuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who are spontaneously born (<s>aupapādika</s>), in their final and highest body, with innumerable years of lifespan, [and] whose lifespan is not subject to curtailment.

children.text: § 365. aupapādikā vyākhyātā devanārakā iti. caramaśabdo ’ntyavācī. uttama utkṛṣṭaḥ. carama uttamo deho yeṣāṃ te caramottamadehāḥ. parītasaṃsārās tajjanmanirvāṇārhā ity arthaḥ. asaṃkhyeyam atītasaṃkhyānam upamāpramāṇena palyādinā gamyam āyur yeṣāṃ ta ime asaṃkhyeyavarṣāyuṣas tiryaṅmanuṣyā uttarakurvādiṣu prasūtāḥ. aupapādikāś ca caramottamadehāś ca asaṃkhyeyavarṣāyuṣaś ca aupapādikacaramottamadehāsaṃkhyeyavarṣāyuṣaḥ. bāhyasyopaghātanimittasya viṣaśastrādeḥ sati saṃnidhāne hrasvaṃ bhavatīty apavartyam. apavartyam āyur yeṣāṃ ta ime apavartyāyuṣaḥ. na apavartyāyuṣaḥ anapavartyāyuṣaḥ. na hy eṣām aupapādikādīnāṃ bāhyanimittavaśād āyur apavartyate, ity ayaṃ niyamaḥ. itareṣām aniyamaḥ. caramasya dehasyotkṛṣṭatvapradarśanārtham uttamagrahaṇaṃ nārthāntaraviśeṣo ’sti. ‘caramadehā’ iti vā pāṭhaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 365. The spontaneously-born (<s>aupapādika</s>) have been explained as gods and hell-beings. The word '<s>carama</s>' means 'final.' '<s>Uttama</s>' means 'supreme.' Those whose final body is the supreme body are '<s>caramottamadeha</s>' (those with the ultimate final body)—meaning those whose <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) is nearing its end, who are worthy of attaining <s>nirvāṇa</s> in that very birth. Those whose lifespan is innumerable, i.e., beyond enumerable numbers, measurable by the standard of a <s>palyopama</s> (straw-measured period) and the like, are animals and humans born in <s>Uttarakuru</s> and similar regions. Those who are spontaneously-born, and those with the ultimate final body, and those with innumerable years of lifespan—[are designated as] <s>aupapādikacaramottamadehāsaṃkhyeyavarṣāyuṣaḥ</s>. That which becomes shortened due to the proximity of an external destructive cause such as poison, weapons, and the like is called '<s>apavartyam</s>' (curtailable). Those whose lifespan is curtailable are '<s>apavartyāyuṣaḥ</s>.' Those whose lifespan is not curtailable are '<s>anapavartyāyuṣaḥ</s>' (non-curtailable). For indeed, the lifespan of the spontaneously-born and others is not curtailed due to external causes—this is the restriction. For the others, there is no restriction. The term '<s>uttama</s>' (supreme) is used to indicate the supreme nature of the final body; it does not denote a different meaning. Alternatively, the reading is simply '<s>caramadeha</s>' (final body).

children.text: iti tattvārthavṛttau sarvārthasiddhisaṃjñikāyāṃ dvitīyo ’dhyāyaḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter of the <s>Tattvārthavṛtti</s> named <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>. ||2||

children.text: atha tṛtīyo ’dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins the third chapter.

children.text: § 366. ‘bhavapratyayo ’vadhir devanārakāṇām’ ity evam ādiṣu nārakāḥ śrutās tataḥ pṛcchati ke te nārakā iti. tatpratipādanārthaṃ tadadhikaraṇanirdeśaḥ kriyate —
children.translated_text: § 366. In [sūtras] such as 'Clairvoyant knowledge arises spontaneously for gods and hell-beings,' hell-beings (<s>nāraka</s>) have been mentioned. Therefore one asks: who are these hell-beings? For the purpose of explaining that, their abode is described—

children.text: ratnaśarkarāvālukāpaṅkadhūmatamomahātamaḥprabhā bhūmayo ghanāmbuvātākāśaprathiṣṭhāḥ saptādho ’dhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ratnaprabhā</s> (Jewel-luster), <s>Śarkarāprabhā</s> (Gravel-luster), <s>Vālukāprabhā</s> (Sand-luster), <s>Paṅkaprabhā</s> (Mud-luster), <s>Dhūmaprabhā</s> (Smoke-luster), <s>Tamaḥprabhā</s> (Darkness-luster), and <s>Mahātamaḥprabhā</s> (Great-darkness-luster)—these are the seven earths, resting on dense [matter], water, wind, and space, one below the other. ||

children.text: § 367. ratnaṃ ca śarkarā ca vālukā ca paṅkaś ca dhūmaś ca tamaś ca mahātamaś ca ratnaśarkarāvālukāpaṅkadhūmatamomahātamāṃsi. ‘prabhā’ śabdaḥ pratyekaṃ parisamāpyate. sāhacaryāt tācchabdyam. citrādiratnaprabhāsahacaritā bhūmiḥ ratnaprabhā, śarkarāprabhāsahacaritā bhūmiḥ śarkarāprabhā, vālukāprabhāsahacaritā bhūmir vālukāprabhā, paṅkaprabhāsahacaritā bhūmiḥ pańkaprabhā, dhūmaprabhāsahacaritā bhūmir dhūmaprabhā, tamaḥprabhāsahacaritā bhūmis tamaḥprabhā, mahātamaḥprabhāsahacaritā bhūmir mahātamaḥprabhā iti. etāḥ saṃjñā anenopāyena vyutpādyante. ‘bhūmi’ grahaṇam adhikaraṇaviśeṣapratipattyartham. yathā svargapaṭalāni bhūmim anāśritya vyavasthitāni na tathā nārakāvāsāḥ. kiṃ tarhi. bhūmim āśritā iti. āsāṃ bhūmīnāmālmbananirjñānārthaṃ ghanāmbuvātādigrahaṇaṃ kriyate. ghanāmbu ca vātaś ca ākāśaṃ ca ghanāmbuvātākāśāni. tani pratiṣṭhā āśrayo yāsāṃ tā ghanāmbuvātākāśapratiṣṭhāḥ. sarvā etā bhūmayo ghanodadhivalayapratiṣṭhāḥ. ghanodadhivalayaṃ ghanavātavalayapratiṣṭham. ghanavātavalayaṃ tanuvātavalayapratiṣṭham. tanuvātavalayam ākāśapratiṣṭham. ākāśam ātmapratiṣṭham, tasyaivādhārādheyatvāt. trīṇy apy etāni valayāni pratyekaṃ viṃśatiyojanasahasrabāhulyāni. ‘sapta’ grhaṇaṃ saṃkhyāntaranivṛttyartham. sapta bhūmayo nāṣṭau na nava ceti. ‘adho ’dhaḥ’ vacanaṃ tiryakpracayanivṛttyartham.
children.translated_text: § 367. Jewel, gravel, sand, mud, smoke, darkness, and great darkness—these are <s>Ratnaśarkarāvālukāpaṅkadhūmatamomahātamas</s>. The word '<s>prabhā</s>' (luster) completes each one individually. The designation is by association. The earth accompanied by the luster of variegated jewels and the like is <s>Ratnaprabhā</s>; the earth accompanied by the luster of gravel is <s>Śarkarāprabhā</s>; the earth accompanied by the luster of sand is <s>Vālukāprabhā</s>; the earth accompanied by the luster of mud is <s>Paṅkaprabhā</s>; the earth accompanied by the luster of smoke is <s>Dhūmaprabhā</s>; the earth accompanied by the luster of darkness is <s>Tamaḥprabhā</s>; the earth accompanied by the luster of great darkness is <s>Mahātamaḥprabhā</s>—thus these designations are derived by this method. The word '<s>bhūmi</s>' (earth) is for the purpose of understanding the specific nature of the substratum. Unlike the celestial planes, which are established without depending on an earth, the abodes of hell-beings are dependent on an earth. The terms '<s>ghana</s>' (dense [matter]), '<s>ambu</s>' (water), '<s>vāta</s>' (wind), and '<s>ākāśa</s>' (space) are employed for understanding the support of these earths. Dense water, wind, and space—these are '<s>ghanāmbuvātākāśa</s>.' Those whose support (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) is those—they are '<s>ghanāmbuvātākāśapratiṣṭhā</s>.' All these earths rest upon the dense ocean-ring. The dense ocean-ring rests upon the dense wind-ring. The dense wind-ring rests upon the thin wind-ring. The thin wind-ring rests upon space. Space rests upon itself, since it is its own support and supported. All three of these rings are each twenty thousand <s>yojanas</s> in thickness. The word 'seven' is for the purpose of excluding other numbers: seven earths, not eight and not nine. The phrase 'one below the other' is for the purpose of excluding horizontal arrangement.

children.text: § 368. kiṃ tā bhūmayo nārakāṇāṃ sarvatrāvāsā āhosvit kvacit kvacid iti prannirdhāraṇārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 368. Are those earths abodes for hell-beings everywhere, or only in certain places? To ascertain this, he says—

children.text: tāsu triṃśatpañcaviṃśatipañcadaśadaśatripañconaikanarakaśatasahasrāṇi paṃca caiva yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: In those [earths], there are thirty, twenty-five, fifteen, ten, three, [one less than one, i.e.,] ninety-five, and five hundred-thousands of hells, respectively, in order. ||

children.text: § 369. tāsu ratnaprabhādiṣu bhūmiṣu narakāṇy anena saṃkhyāyante yathākramam. ratnaprabhāyāṃ triṃśannarakaśatasahasrāṇi, śarkarāprabhāyāṃ pañcaviṃśatir narakaśatasahasrāṇi, vālukāprabhāyāṃ pañcadaśa narakaśatasahasrāṇi, paṃkaprabhāyāṃ daśa narakaśatasahasrāṇi, dhūmaprabhāyāṃ trīṇi narakaśatasahasrāṇi, tamaḥprabhāyāṃ pañconam ekaṃ narakaśatasahasraṃ, mahātamaḥprabhāyāṃ pañca narakāni. ratnaprabhāyāṃ narakaprastārās trayodaśa. tato ’dha ā saptamyā dvau dvau narakaprastārau hīnau. itaro viśeṣo lokānuyogato veditavyaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 369. In those earths beginning with <s>Ratnaprabhā</s>, the hells are enumerated in order: in <s>Ratnaprabhā</s>, thirty hundred-thousands (three million) of hells; in <s>Śarkarāprabhā</s>, twenty-five hundred-thousands; in <s>Vālukāprabhā</s>, fifteen hundred-thousands; in <s>Paṅkaprabhā</s>, ten hundred-thousands; in <s>Dhūmaprabhā</s>, three hundred-thousands; in <s>Tamaḥprabhā</s>, ninety-five thousand (one hundred-thousand less five thousand); in <s>Mahātamaḥprabhā</s>, five hells. In <s>Ratnaprabhā</s>, there are thirteen tiers of hells. Below that, down to the seventh [earth], two tiers fewer in each successive [earth]. The remaining details should be understood from <s>Lokānuyoga</s> (cosmological treatise).

children.text: § 370. atha tāsu bhūmiṣu nārakānāṃ kaḥ prativiśeṣa ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 370. Now, what are the specific characteristics of hell-beings in those earths? To this he says—

children.text: nārakā nityāśubhataraleśyāpariṇāmadehavedanāvikriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hell-beings (<s>nāraka</s>) are characterized by constantly worsening soul-coloration (<s>leśyā</s>), dispositions (<s>pariṇāma</s>), body (<s>deha</s>), sensation (<s>vedanā</s>), and transformative power (<s>vikriyā</s>). ||

children.text: § 371. leśyādayo vyākhyātārthāḥ. aśubhatarā iti prakarṣanirdeśaḥ tiryaggativiṣayāśubhaleśyādyapekṣayā adho ’dhaḥ svagatyapekṣayā ca veditavyaḥ. ‘nitya’ śabda ābhīkṣṇyavacanaḥ. nityam aśubhatarā leśyādayo yeṣāṃ te nityāśubhataraleśyāpariṇāmadehavedanāvikriyā nārakāḥ. prathamādvitīyayoḥ kāpotī leśyā, tṛtīyāyam upariṣṭāt kāpotī adho nīlā, caturthyāṃ nīlā, pañcamyām upari nīlā adhaḥ kṛṣṇā, ṣaṣṭhyāṃ kṛṣṇā, saptamyāṃ paramakṛṣṇā. svāyuḥpramāṇāvadhṛtā dravyaleśyā uktāḥ. bhāvaleśyāsu antarmuhūrtaparivartinyaḥ. pariṇāmāḥ sparśarasagandhavarṇaśabdāḥ kṣetraviśeṣanimittavaśād atiduḥkhahetavo ’śubhatarā. dehāś ca teṣām aśubhanāmakarmodayād atyantāśubhatarā vikṛtākṛtayo huṇḍasaṃsthānā durdarśanāḥ. teṣām utsedhaḥ prathamāyāṃ sapta dhanūṃṣi trayo hastāḥ ṣaḍaṃgulayaḥ. adho ’dho — dviguṇadviguṇa utsedhaḥ. abhyantarāsadvedyodaye sati anādipāriṇāmikaśītoṣṇabāhyanimittajanitā atitīvrā vedanā bhavanti nārakāṇām. prathamādvitīyātṛtīyācaturthīṣu uṣṇavedanāny eva narakāṇi. pañcamyām upari uṣṇavedene dve narakaśatasahasre. adhaḥ śītavedanam ekaṃ śatasahasram. ṣaṣṭhīsaptamyoḥ śītavedanāny eva. śubhaṃ vikariṣyāma iti aśubhataram eva vikurvanti, sukhahetūn utpādayāma iti duḥkhahetūn evotpādayanti. ta ete bhāvā adho ’dho ’śutarā veditavyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 371. <s>Leśyā</s> and the rest have already been explained. The term 'worsening' (<s>aśubhatara</s>) indicates an intensification, to be understood in comparison with the inauspicious <s>leśyā</s> etc. pertaining to the animal destiny, and [also] in comparison with [the levels] within their own destiny, progressively downward. The word '<s>nitya</s>' (constant) denotes frequency. Those whose <s>leśyā</s>, dispositions, body, sensation, and transformative power are constantly worsening are the hell-beings. In the first and second [earths], the <s>leśyā</s> is grey (<s>kāpotī</s>); in the third, grey above and blue (<s>nīlā</s>) below; in the fourth, blue; in the fifth, blue above and black (<s>kṛṣṇā</s>) below; in the sixth, black; in the seventh, supremely black. The material <s>leśyās</s> (<s>dravyaleśyā</s>) are bounded by their own lifespans as stated. The dispositional <s>leśyās</s> (<s>bhāvaleśyā</s>) alternate within less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. The dispositions (<s>pariṇāma</s>)—touch, taste, smell, color, and sound—are extremely inauspicious, causing extreme suffering, due to the particular spatial conditions. Their bodies too, due to the fruition of inauspicious name-determining <s>karma</s>, are extremely inauspicious, of deformed shape, with <s>huṇḍa</s> (asymmetric) bodily form, terrible to behold. Their height in the first [earth] is seven bows, three cubits, and six finger-breadths. Downward, the height doubles with each successive [earth]. When the fruition of inner unpleasant sensation-experiencing [<s>karma</s>] occurs, there arise extremely intense sensations for the hell-beings, generated by beginningless natural cold and heat and external causes. In the first, second, third, and fourth [earths], the hells have only hot sensations. In the fifth, above there are two hundred-thousands of hells with hot sensation, and below one hundred-thousand with cold sensation. In the sixth and seventh, the hells have only cold sensations. When they wish 'let us transform into something auspicious,' they transform into something even more inauspicious; when they think 'let us produce causes of happiness,' they produce only causes of suffering. These conditions should be understood as progressively worse downward.

children.text: § 372. kim eteṣāṃ nārakāṇāṃ śītoṣṇajanitam eva duḥkham utānyathāpi bhavatīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 372. Is the suffering of these hell-beings caused only by cold and heat, or is there also other [suffering]? To this he says—

children.text: parasparodīritaduḥkhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They suffer torments inflicted by one another (<s>parasparodīritaduḥkha</s>). ||

children.text: § 373. kathaṃ parasparodīrītaduḥkhatvam? nārakāḥ bhavapratyayenāvadhinā mithyādarśanodayād vibhaṅgavyapadeśabhājā ca dūrād eva duḥkhahetūn avagamyotpannaduḥkhāḥ pratyāsattau parasparālokanāc ca prajvalitakopāgnayaḥ pūrvabhavānusmaraṇāc cātitīvrānubaddhavairāś ca śvaśṛgālādivatsvābhighāte pravartamānāḥ svavikriyākṛtāsivāsīparaśubhiṇḍimālaśaktitomarakuntāyodhanādibhir āyudhaiḥ svakaracaraṇadaśanaiś ca chedanabhedanatakṣaṇadaṃśanādibhiḥ parasparasyātitīvraṃ duḥkham utpādayanti.
children.translated_text: § 373. How are they tormented by one another? The hell-beings, through birth-determined (<s>bhavapratyaya</s>) clairvoyant knowledge (<s>avadhi</s>) and through wrong perception's fruition—which is designated as <s>vibhaṅga</s> (erroneous clairvoyance)—perceive causes of suffering even from afar and become afflicted. Upon proximity, through mutual sight, the fire of their anger blazes forth; and through the remembrance of previous births, they harbor extremely intense and persistent enmity. Engaging in mutual attack like dogs and jackals, with weapons such as swords, axes, hatchets, maces, garlands of iron balls, spears, lances, javelins, and battle-implements created by their own transformative power (<s>vikriyā</s>), and with their own hands, feet, and teeth, through cutting, piercing, chiseling, biting, and the like, they produce extremely intense suffering for one another.

children.text: § 374. kim etāvān eva duḥkhotpattikāraṇaprakāra utānyo ’pi kaścid astīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 374. Is this the only manner of producing suffering, or is there yet another? To this he says—

children.text: saṃkliṣṭāsurodīritaduḥkhāś ca prāk caturthyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They also suffer torments inflicted by malevolent <s>asuras</s> (demons), [but only] before the fourth [earth]. ||

children.text: § 375. devagatināmakarmavikalpasyāsuratvasaṃvartanasya karmaṇa udayād asyanti parān ity asurāḥ. pūrvajanmani bhāvitenātitīvreṇa saṃkleśapariṇāmena yad upārjitaṃ pāpakarma tasyodayāt satataṃ kliṣṭāḥ saṃkliṣṭāḥ, saṃvikliṣṭā asurāḥ saṃvikliṣṭāsurāḥ. saṃkliṣṭā iti viśeṣaṇān na sarve asurā nārakāṇāṃ duḥkham utpādayanti. kiṃ tarhi? ambāvarīṣādaya eva kecaneti. avadhipradarśanārthaṃ ‘prak caturthyāḥ’ iti viśeṣaṇam. upari tisṛṣu pṛthvīṣu saṃkliṣṭāsurā bādhāhetavo nātaḥ param iti pradarśanārtham. ‘ca’ śabdaḥ pūrvoktaduḥkhahetusamuccayārthaḥ. sutatptāyorasapāyananiṣṭaptāyastambhāliṅganakūṭaśālmalyārohaṇāvataraṇāyoghanābhighātavāsīkṣuratakṣaṇakṣārataptatailāvasecanāyaḥkumbhīpākāmbarīṣabharjanavaitaraṇīmajjanayantraniṣpīḍanādibhir nārakāṇāṃ duḥkham utpādayanti. evaṃ chedanabhedanādibhiḥ śakalīkṛtamūrtīnām api teṣāṃ na maraṇam akāle bhavati. kutaḥ? anapavartyāyuṣkatvāt.
children.translated_text: § 375. Those who hurl (<s>asyanti</s>) others are <s>asuras</s> (demons), due to the fruition of the <s>karma</s>-variety of the celestial-destiny-name called '<s>asuratva</s>' (demonhood). Those who are constantly afflicted due to the fruition of sinful <s>karma</s> accumulated through extremely intense defiling dispositions in previous births are '<s>saṃkliṣṭa</s>' (intensely afflicted); <s>saṃkliṣṭa asuras</s> are '<s>saṃkliṣṭāsuras</s>.' The qualifier '<s>saṃkliṣṭa</s>' indicates that not all <s>asuras</s> produce suffering for hell-beings—but rather only certain ones such as <s>Ambāvarīṣa</s> and others. The qualifier 'before the fourth' is to indicate the limit: the malevolent <s>asuras</s> cause harm in the upper three earths, not beyond that. The particle '<s>ca</s>' is for the purpose of aggregating with the previously stated causes of suffering. They produce suffering for the hell-beings through [tortures such as]: immersion in supremely heated alkaline liquid, embracing red-hot iron pillars, climbing up and down thorny <s>Śālmalī</s> trees, being struck with dense blows, being planed with chisels and razors, being drenched with alkaline solution and boiling oil, being cooked in iron cauldrons, being roasted on spits, being submerged in the river <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>, being crushed in presses, and other [torments]. Even though their bodies are broken to pieces by such cutting and piercing, they do not die prematurely. Why? Because their lifespan is non-curtailable (<s>anapavartyāyuṣka</s>).

children.text: § 376. yady evaṃ, tad eva tāvad ucyatāṃ nārakāṇām āyuḥparimāṇam ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 376. If so, then let the measure of the hell-beings' lifespan be stated first—to this he says—

children.text: teṣv ekatrisaptadaśasaptadaśadvāviṃśatitrayāstriṃśatsāgaropamā sattvānāṃ parā sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In those [earths], the maximum lifespan (<s>parā sthiti</s>) of beings is one, three, seven, ten, seventeen, twenty-two, and thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> (ocean-measured periods), respectively. ||

children.text: § 377. yathākramam ity anuvartate. teṣu narakeṣu bhūmikrameṇa yathāsaṃkhyam ekādayaḥ sthitayo ’bhisaṃbadhyante. ratnaprabhāyām utkṛṣṭā sthitir ekasāgaropamā. śarkarāprabhāyāṃ trisāgaropamā. vālukāprabhāyāṃ saptasāgaropamā. paṃkaḥprabhāyāṃ daśasāgaropamā. dhūmaprabhāyāṃ saptadaśasāgaropamā. tamaḥprabhāyāṃ dvāviṃśatisāgaropamā. mahātamaḥprabhāyāṃ trayāstriṃśatsāgaropamā iti. parā utkṛṣṭety arthaḥ. ‘sattvānām’ iti vacanaṃ bhūminivṛttyartham. bhūmiṣu sattvānām iyaṃ sthitiḥ, na bhūmīnām iti.
children.translated_text: § 377. 'Respectively' (<s>yathākramam</s>) continues [from before]. In those hells, the lifespans beginning with one [<s>sāgaropama</s>] are connected in the order of the earths. In <s>Ratnaprabhā</s>, the maximum lifespan is one <s>sāgaropama</s>; in <s>Śarkarāprabhā</s>, three <s>sāgaropamas</s>; in <s>Vālukāprabhā</s>, seven <s>sāgaropamas</s>; in <s>Paṅkaprabhā</s>, ten <s>sāgaropamas</s>; in <s>Dhūmaprabhā</s>, seventeen <s>sāgaropamas</s>; in <s>Tamaḥprabhā</s>, twenty-two <s>sāgaropamas</s>; in <s>Mahātamaḥprabhā</s>, thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s>. '<s>Parā</s>' means 'maximum'—this is the meaning. The word '<s>sattvānām</s>' (of beings) is for the purpose of differentiating from the earths: this is the lifespan of beings in the earths, not of the earths themselves.

children.text: § 378. uktaḥ saptabhūmivistīrṇo ’dholokaḥ. idānīṃ tiryagloko vaktavyaḥ. kathaṃ punas tiryaglokaḥ. yatho ’saṃkhyeyāḥ svayaṃbhūramaṇaparyantās tiryakpracayaviśeṣeṇāvasthitā dvīpasamudrās tatas tiryagloka iti. ke punas tiryagvyavasthitā ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 378. The lower world (<s>adholoka</s>), extending through seven earths, has been described. Now the middle world (<s>tiryagloka</s>) is to be described. What constitutes the middle world? Since innumerable islands and oceans are arranged in a specific transverse pattern extending up to <s>Svayaṃbhūramaṇa</s>, it is called the middle world. Who then are arranged transversely? To this he says—

children.text: jambūdvīpalavaṇodādayaḥ śubhanāmāno dvīpasamudrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> and <s>Lavaṇoda</s> (Salt Ocean) and the rest—these are the islands and oceans with auspicious names. ||

children.text: § 379. jambūdvīpādayo dvīpāḥ. lavaṇodādayaḥ samudrāḥ. yāni loke śubhāni nāmāni tan nāmānas te. tad yathā — jambūdvīpo dvīpaḥ. lavaṇodaḥ samudraḥ. dhātakīkhaṇḍo dvīpaḥ. kālodaḥ samudraḥ. puṣkaravaro dvīpaḥ. puṣkaravaraḥ samudraḥ. vāruṇīvaro dvīpaḥ. vāruṇīvaraḥ samudraḥ. kṣīravaro dvīpaḥ. kṣīravaraḥ samudraḥ. ghṛtavaro dvīpaḥ. ghṛtavaraḥ samudraḥ. ikṣuvaro dvīpaḥ. ikṣuvaraḥ samudraḥ. nandīśvaravaro dvīpaḥ. nandīśvaravaraḥ samudraḥ. aruṇavaro dvīpaḥ. aruṇavaraḥ samudraḥ. ity evam asaṃkhyeyā dvīpasamudrāḥ svayambhūramaṇaparyantā veditavyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 379. The islands beginning with <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>. The oceans beginning with <s>Lavaṇoda</s> (Salt Ocean). Those whose names are auspicious names known in the world—they are those. Namely: <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> is an island; <s>Lavaṇoda</s> is an ocean; <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s> is an island; <s>Kāloda</s> is an ocean; <s>Puṣkaravara</s> is an island; <s>Puṣkaravara</s> is an ocean; <s>Vāruṇīvara</s> is an island; <s>Vāruṇīvara</s> is an ocean; <s>Kṣīravara</s> is an island; <s>Kṣīravara</s> is an ocean; <s>Ghṛtavara</s> is an island; <s>Ghṛtavara</s> is an ocean; <s>Ikṣuvara</s> is an island; <s>Ikṣuvara</s> is an ocean; <s>Nandīśvaravara</s> is an island; <s>Nandīśvaravara</s> is an ocean; <s>Aruṇavara</s> is an island; <s>Aruṇavara</s> is an ocean. Thus, innumerable islands and oceans extending up to <s>Svayaṃbhūramaṇa</s> should be understood.

children.text: § 380. amīṣāṃ viṣkambhasaṃniveśasaṃsthānaviśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 380. For the purpose of understanding the specific diameter, arrangement, and shape of these, he says—

children.text: dvir dvir viskambhāḥ pūrvapūrvaparikṣepiṇo valayākṛtayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their diameters are each double [the preceding], each encircling the previous one, ring-shaped. ||

children.text: § 381. dvir dvir iti vīpsābhyāvṛttivacanaṃ viṣkambhadviguṇatvavyārpttham.

ādyasya dvīpasya yo viṣkambhaḥ tad dviguṇaviṣkambho lavaṇajaladhiḥ. taddviguṇaviṣkambho dvitīyo dvīpaḥ. taddviguṇaviṣkambho dvitīyo jaladhir iti. dvir dvir viṣkambho yeṣāṃ te dvir dvir viṣkambhāḥ. pūrvapūrvaparikṣepivacanaṃ grāmanagarādivadviniveśo mā vijñāyīti. valayākṛtivacanaṃ caturasrādisaṃsthānāntaranivṛttyartham.
children.translated_text: The diameter of the salt ocean (<s>Lavaṇa-jaladhi</s>) is twice the diameter of the first continent. The diameter of the second continent is twice that [of the ocean]. The diameter of the second ocean is twice that [of the second continent]—and so on. 'Twice-twice the diameter' means each has double the diameter of the previous one. The statement about 'encircling the preceding one' is to indicate that the arrangement is like that of villages and cities [i.e., concentric]. The statement about 'ring-shaped' (<s>valayākṛti</s>) is for the purpose of excluding other forms such as square and the like.
§ 381. 'Each double' (<s>dvir dvir</s>) is a repetitive expression indicating that the diameter doubles [each time].

children.text: § 382. atrāha, jambūdvīpasya pradeśasaṃsthānaviṣkambhā vaktavyās tanmūlatvāditaraviṣkambhādivijñānasyety ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 382. Here one says: the spatial units (<s>pradeśa</s>), form, and diameter of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> should be stated, since the knowledge of other diameters and the like is based on that. Thus it is said—

children.text: tanmadhye merunābhir vṛtto yojanaśatasahasraviṣkambho jambūdvīpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the midst of those, <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, with <s>Meru</s> as its navel, is circular, with a diameter of one hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. ||

children.text: § 383. teṣāṃ madhye tanmadhye. keṣām? pūrvoktānāṃ dvīpasamudrāṇām. nābhir iva nābhiḥ. merur nābhir yasya sa merunābhiḥ. vṛtta ādityamaṇḍalopamānaḥ. śatānāṃ sahasraṃ śatasahasram. yojanānāṃ śatasahasraṃ yojanaśatasahasraṃ. yojanaśatasahasraṃ viṣkambho yasya so ’yaṃ yojanaśatasahasraviṣkambhaḥ. ko ’sau? jambūdvīpaḥ. kathaṃ jambūdvīpaḥ? jambūvṛkṣopalakṣitatvāt. uttarakurūṇāṃ madhye jambūvṛkṣo ’nādinidhanaḥ pṛthivīpariṇāmo ’kṛtrimaḥ saparivāras tadupalakṣito ’yaṃ dvīpaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 383. 'In the midst of those' (<s>tanmadhye</s>)—in the middle of whom? Of the previously mentioned continents and oceans. 'Navel' (<s>nābhi</s>) is used figuratively, like a navel. That which has <s>Meru</s> as its navel is <s>Merunābhi</s>. 'Circular' (<s>vṛtta</s>) means comparable to the disc of the sun. A hundred thousands is a <s>śatasahasra</s>. A <s>śatasahasra</s> of <s>yojanas</s> is a <s>yojana-śatasahasra</s>. That which has a diameter of one hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> is <s>yojana-śatasahasra-viṣkambha</s>. What is it? <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>. Why '<s>Jambūdvīpa</s>'? Because it is characterized by the <s>Jambū</s> tree. In the middle of <s>Uttarakuru</s>, there stands the <s>Jambū</s> tree, beginningless and endless, a natural transformation of the earth, uncreated, with its retinue—this continent is characterized by it.

children.text: § 384. tatra jambūdvīpe ṣaḍabhiḥ kalaparvatair vibhaktāni sapta kṣetrāṇi kāni tānīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 384. In that <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, seven regions are divided by six mountain ranges (<s>kulaparvatā</s>). What are those? To this he says—

children.text: bharatahaimavataharivideharamyakahairaṇyavatairāvatavarṣāḥ kṣetraṇi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Haimavata</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Videha</s>, <s>Ramyaka</s>, <s>Hairaṇyavata</s>, and <s>Airāvata</s>—these are the <s>varṣas</s> (regions), i.e., the fields (<s>kṣetrāṇi</s>). ||

children.text: § 385. bharatādayaḥ saṃjñā anādikālapravṛttā amimittāḥ.

tatra bharatavarṣaḥ kva saṃniviṣṭaḥ? dakṣiṇadigbhāge himavato ’dres trayāṇāṃ samudrāṇāṃ madhye āropitacāpākāro bharatavarsaḥ. vijayārddhena gaṅgāsindhubhyāṃ ca vibhaktaḥ sa ṣaṭkhaṇḍaḥ. kṣudrahimavantam uttareṇa dakṣiṇena mahāhimavantaṃ pūrvāparasamudrayor madhye haimavatavarṣaḥ. niṣadhasya dakṣiṇato mahāhimavata uttarataḥ pūrvāparasamudrayor antarāle harivarṣaḥ. niṣadhasyottarān nīlato dakṣiṇataḥ pūrvāparasamudrayor antare videhasya saṃniveśo draṣṭavyaḥ. nīlata uttarāt (d) rukmiṇo dakṣiṇāt pūrvāparasamudrayor madhye ramyakavarṣaḥ. rukmiṇa uttarāc chikhariṇo dakṣiṇāt pūrvāparasamudrayor madhye saṃniveśī hairaṇyavatavarṣaḥ. śikhariṇa uttaratas trayāṇāṃ samudrāṇāṃ madhye airāvatavarṣaḥ. vijayārddhena raktāraktodābhyāṃ ca vibhaktaḥ sa ṣaṭkhaṇḍaḥ.
children.translated_text: Where is <s>Bharatavarṣa</s> situated? In the southern region, between <s>Himavat</s> mountain and three oceans, <s>Bharatavarṣa</s> has the form of a bow placed [with its ends] on [the mountain].
§ 385. The names <s>Bharata</s> and the rest are of beginningless usage and without [ascertainable] cause.

children.text: § 386. ṣaṭ kulaparvatā ity uktaṃ ke punas te kathaṃ vā vyavasthitā ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 386. Six mountain ranges (<s>kulaparvatā</s>) have been mentioned. What are they and how are they arranged? To this he says—

children.text: tadvibhājinaḥ pūrvāparāyatā himavanmahāhimavanniṣadhanīlarukmiśikhariṇo varṣadharaparvatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The watershed mountains (<s>varṣadhara-parvatāḥ</s>) that divide those [regions], extending from east to west, are <s>Himavat</s>, <s>Mahāhimavat</s>, <s>Niṣadha</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Rukmin</s>, and <s>Śikharin</s>. ||

children.text: § 387. tāni kṣetrāṇi vibhajanta ity evaṃ śīlās tadvibhājinaḥ. pūrvāparāyatā iti pūrvāparakoṭibhyāṃ lavaṇajaladhisparśina ity arthaḥ. himavadādayo ’nādikālapravṛttā animittasaṃjñā varṣavibhāgahetutvād varṣadharaparvatā ity ucyante. tatra kva himavān? bharatasya haimavatasya ca sīmani vyavasthitaḥ. kṣudrahimavān yojanaśatocchrāyaḥ. haimavatasya harivarṣasya ca vibhāgakaro mahāhimavān dviyojanaśatocchrāyaḥ. videhasya dakṣiṇato harivarṣasyottarato niṣadho nāma parvataś caturyojanaśatocchrāyaḥ. uttare trayo ’pi parvatāḥ svavarṣavibhājino vyākhyātāḥ. ucchrāyaś ca teṣāṃ catvāri dve ekaṃ ca yojanaśataṃ veditavyam. sarveṣāṃ parvatānām ucchrāyasya caturbhāgo ’vagāhaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 387. Those that divide those regions—such is their nature—hence '<s>tadvibhājinaḥ</s>' (dividers of those). 'Extending from east to west' means touching the salt ocean at their eastern and western ends.

children.text: § 388. tesāṃ varṇaviśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 388. For the purpose of understanding the specific colors of those [mountains], he says—

children.text: hemārjunatapanīyavaiḍūryarajatahemamayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are made of gold, silver, refined gold (<s>tapanīya</s>), <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (cat's eye gem), silver, and gold, respectively. ||

children.text: § 389. ta ete himavadādayaḥ parvatā hemādimayā viditavyā yathākramam. hemamayo himavān cīnapaṭṭavarṇaḥ. arjunamayo mahāhimavān śuklavarṇaḥ. tapanīyamayo niṣadhas taruṇādityavarṇaḥ. vaiḍūryamayo nīlo māyuragrīvābhaḥ. rajatamayo rukmī śuklaḥ. hemamayaḥ śikharo cīnapaṭṭavarṇaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 389. These mountains beginning with <s>Himavat</s> should be understood as made of gold and the rest, respectively. <s>Himavat</s> is made of gold, of the color of Chinese silk. <s>Mahāhimavat</s> is made of silver, white in color.

children.text: § 390. punar api tadviśeṣaṇārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 390. Further, to characterize them, he says—

children.text: maṇivicitrapārśvā upari mūle ca tulyavistārāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their sides are variegated with gems, and they are of equal width at the top and base. ||

children.text: § 391. nānavarṇaprabhādiguṇopetair maṇibhir vicitrāṇi pārśvāṇi yeṣāṃ te maṇivicitrapārśvāḥ. aniṣṭasaṃsthānasya nivṛttyartham uparyādivacanaṃ kriyate. ‘ca’ śabdo madhyasamuccayārthaḥ. ya eṣāṃ mūle vistāraḥ sa upari madhye ca tulyaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 391. Those whose sides are variegated with gems possessing qualities such as various colors and radiances—they are '<s>maṇi-vicitra-pārśvāḥ</s>' (having gem-variegated sides). The statement about 'equal width at top and base' is for the purpose of excluding undesirable forms.

children.text: § 392. teṣāṃ madhye labdhāspadā hradā ucyante —
children.translated_text: § 392. The lakes situated in their midst are stated—

children.text: padmamahāpadmatigiñchakesarimahāpuṇḍarīkapuṇḍarīkā hradās teṣām upari ||
children.translated_text: <s>Padma</s>, <s>Mahāpadma</s>, <s>Tigiñcha</s>, <s>Kesarin</s>, <s>Mahāpuṇḍarīka</s>, and <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>—these are the lakes, upon those [mountains]. ||

children.text: § 393. padmo mahāpadmas tigiñchaḥ kesarī mahāpuṇḍarīkaḥ puṇḍarīka iti teṣāṃ himavadādīnām upari yathākramam ete hradā veditavyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 393. <s>Padma</s>, <s>Mahāpadma</s>, <s>Tigiñcha</s>, <s>Kesarin</s>, <s>Mahāpuṇḍarīka</s>, and <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>—these lakes should be understood as situated upon those [mountains] beginning with <s>Himavat</s>, in order.

children.text: § 394. tatrādyasya saṃsthānaviśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 394. For the purpose of understanding the specific form of the first [lake], he says—

children.text: prathamo yojanasahasrāyāmas tadarddhaviṣkambho hradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The first lake is one thousand <s>yojanas</s> in length and half that in width. ||

children.text: § 395. prākpratyag yojanasahasrāyām udagavāk pañcayojanaśatavistāro vajramayatalo vividhamaṇikanakavicitritataṭaḥ padmanāmāhradaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 395. One thousand <s>yojanas</s> in the east-west [direction], five hundred <s>yojanas</s> in width in the north-south [direction], with a bed made of diamond (<s>vajra</s>), its banks variegated with various gems and gold—this is the lake named <s>Padma</s>.

children.text: § 396. tasyāvagāhapraklṛptyartham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 396. For the purpose of determining its depth, this is stated—

children.text: daśayojanāvagāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its depth is ten <s>yojanas</s>. ||

children.text: § 397. avagāho ’dhaḥ praveśo nimnatā. daśayojanāny avagāho ’sya daśayojanāvagāhaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 397. Depth (<s>avagāha</s>) means downward penetration, depression. That whose depth is ten <s>yojanas</s> is '<s>daśa-yojanāvagāha</s>'.

children.text: § 398. tanmadye kim —
children.translated_text: § 398. In its middle, what [is there]?

children.text: tanmadhye yojanaṃ puṣkaram ||
children.translated_text: In its middle is a lotus (<s>puṣkara</s>) of one <s>yojana</s>. ||

children.text: § 399. yojanapramāṇam yojanam, krośāyāmapatratvāt krośadvayaviṣkambhakarṇikatvāc ca yojanāyāmaviṣkambham. jalatalāt krośadvayocchrāyanālaṃ yāvad bahulapatrapracayaṃ puṣkaram avagantavyam.
children.translated_text: § 399. 'Of one <s>yojana</s> in measure' means one <s>yojana</s>—because its petals are one <s>krośa</s> in length and its pericarp is two <s>krośas</s> in diameter, [the total is] one <s>yojana</s> in length and diameter. [Its height] above the water surface is two <s>krośas</s>.

children.text: § 400. itareṣāṃ hradānāṃ puṣkarāṇāṃ cāyāmādinirjñānārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 400. For the purpose of knowing the dimensions of the other lakes and lotuses, he says—

children.text: taddviguṇadviguṇā hrdāḥ puṣkarāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: The lakes and lotuses are successively double-double [in size]. ||

children.text: § 401. sa ca tacca te, tayor dviguṇā dviguṇās taddviguṇadviguṇā iti dvitvaṃ vyāptijñā–panārtham. kena dviguṇāḥ? āyāmādinā. padmahradasya dviguṇāyāmaviṣkambhāvagāho mahāpadmo hradaḥ. tasya dviguṇāyāmaviṣkambhāvagāhas tigiñcho hradaḥ. puṣkarāṇi ca. kiṃ? dviguṇāni dviguṇānīty abhisaṃbadhyate.
children.translated_text: § 401. 'That and that'—of those; 'double-double'—the repetition is for conveying universality. Double in what respect? In length and other dimensions. The lake <s>Padma</s>—

children.text: § 402. tannivāsinīnāṃ devīnāṃ saṃjñājīvitaparivārapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 402. For the purpose of explaining the names, lifespan, and retinue of the goddesses dwelling in those [lotuses], he says—

children.text: tannivāsinyo devyaḥ śrīhrīdhṛtikīrtibuddhilakṣmyaḥ palyopamasthitayaḥ sasāmānikapariṣatkāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The goddesses dwelling in those [lotuses] are <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Hrī</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>, <s>Kīrti</s>, <s>Buddhi</s>, and <s>Lakṣmī</s>; their lifespan is one <s>palyopama</s>; they have their own councils (<s>sāmānika</s>) and retinues (<s>pariṣat</s>). ||

children.text: § 403. teṣu puṣkareṣu karṇikāmadhyadeśaniveśinaḥ śaradvimalapūrṇacandradyutiharāḥ krośāyāmāḥ krośārddhaviṣkambhā deśonakrośotsedāḥ prāsādāḥ. teṣu nivasantīty evaṃ śīlās tannivāsinyaḥ, devyaḥ śrīhrīdhṛtikīrtibuddhilakṣmīsaṃjñikās teṣu padmādiṣu yathākramaṃ veditavyāḥ. ‘palyopamasthitayaḥ’ ity anenāyuṣaḥ pramānam uktam. samāne sthāne bhavāḥ sāmānikāḥ. sāmānikāś ca pariṣadaś ca sāmānikapariṣadaḥ. saha sāmānikapariṣadbhir vartanta iti sasāmānikapariṣatkāḥ. tasya padmasya parivārapadmeṣu prāsādānām upari sāmānikāḥ pariṣadaś ca vasanti.
children.translated_text: § 403. Established in the central area of the pericarps of those lotuses, having the radiance of the full autumn moon's unblemished luster, one <s>krośa</s> in length, half a <s>krośa</s> in width, slightly less than one <s>krośa</s> in height—

children.text: § 404. yakābhiḥ saridbhis tāni kṣetrāṇi pravibhaktāni tā ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 404. The rivers by which those regions are divided are stated—

children.text: gaṅgāsindhurohidrohitāsyāhariddharikāntāsītāsītodānārīnarakāntāsuvarṇarūpyakūlāraktāraktodāḥ saritas tanmadhyagāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Sindhu</s>, <s>Rohit</s>, <s>Rohitāsyā</s>, <s>Harit</s>, <s>Harikāntā</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Sītodā</s>, <s>Nārī</s>, <s>Narakāntā</s>, <s>Suvarṇarūpyakūlā</s>, <s>Raktā</s>, <s>Raktodā</s>—these are the rivers flowing through the middle of those [regions]. ||

children.text: § 405. sarito na vāpyaḥ. tāḥ kim antarā uta samīpā iti? āha — tanmadhyagāḥ teṣāṃ kṣetrāṇām madhyaṃ tanmadhyam. tanmadhyaṃ tanmadhyena vā gacchatīti tanmadhyagāḥ. ekatra sarvāsāṃ prasaṃganivṛttyarthaṃ digviśeṣapratipattyarthaṃ cāha —
children.translated_text: § 405. [They are] rivers, not ponds. Are they distant or close [to each other]? He says: '<s>tanmadhyagāḥ</s>'—flowing through the middle of those regions. The middle of those regions is '<s>tanmadhya</s>.'

children.text: dvayor dvayoḥ pūrvāḥ pūrvagāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of each pair, the first ones flow eastward. ||

children.text: § 406. dvayor dvayoḥ saritor ekaikaṃ kṣetraṃ viṣaya iti vākyaśeṣābhisaṃbandhād ekatra sarvāsāṃ prasaṃganivṛttiḥ kṛtā. ‘pūvaḥ pūrvagāḥ’ iti vacanaṃ digviśeṣapratipattyartham. tatra pūrvā yāḥ saritas tāḥ pūrvagāḥ. pūrvajaladhiṃ gacchantīti pūrvagāḥ. kim apekṣaṃ pūrvatvam? sūtranirdeśāpekṣam. yady evaṃ gaṅgāsindhvādayaḥ sapta pūvagā iti prāptam? naiṣa doṣaḥ; dvayor dvayor ity abhisaṃbandhāt. dvayor dvayoḥ pūvāḥ pūrvagā iti veditavyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 406. Since the connection with the rest of the sentence [indicates] that each pair of rivers has one region as its domain, the unwanted consequence that all [rivers] would be in one [region] is prevented. 'The first ones flow eastward'—

children.text: § 407. itarāsaṃ digvibhāgapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 407. For the purpose of understanding the directional division of the remaining [rivers], he says—

children.text: śeṣāstv aparagāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The remaining ones, however, flow westward. ||

children.text: § 408. dvayor dvayor yā avaśiṣṭās tā aparagāḥ pratyetavyāḥ. aparasamudraṃ gacchantīty aparagāḥ. tatra padmahradaprabhavā pūrvatoraṇadvāranirgatā gaṅgā. aparatoraṇadvāranirgatā sindhuḥ. udīcyatoraṇadvāranirgatā rohitāsyā. mahāpadmahradaprabhavā avācyatoraṇadvāranirgatā rohit. udīcyatoraṇadvāranirgatā harikāntā. tigiñchahradaprabhavā dakṣiṇatoraṇadvāranirgatā harit. udīcyatoraṇadvāranirgatā sītodā. kesarihradaprabhavā avācyatoraṇadvāranirgatā sītā. udīcyatoraṇadvāranirgatā narakāntā. mahāpuṇḍarīkahradaprabhavā dakṣiṇatoraṇadvāranirgatā nārī. udīcyatoraṇadvāranirgatā rūpyakūlā. puṇḍarīkahradaprabhavā avācyatoraṇadvāranirgatā suvarṇakūlā. pūrvatoraṇadvāranirgatā raktā. pratīcyatoraṇadvāranirgatā raktodā.
children.translated_text: § 408. Of each pair, those that remain are to be understood as flowing westward (<s>aparagāḥ</s>)—'<s>aparagāḥ</s>' means 'going toward the western ocean.' Among these, [the river] originating from Lake <s>Padma</s> flows eastward—

children.text: § 409. tāsāṃ parivārapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 409. For the purpose of explaining the retinue of those [rivers], he says—

children.text: caturdaśanadīsahasraparivṛtā gaṅgāsindhvādayo nadyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rivers <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Sindhu</s>, and the rest are each attended by fourteen thousand rivers. ||

children.text: § 410. kim arthaṃ ‘gaṅgāsindhvādi’ grahanaṃ kriyate? nadīgrahṇārtham. prakṛtās tā abhisaṃbhadyante? naivaṃ śaṃkyam; ‘anantarasya vidhir vā bhavati pratiṣedho vā’ iti aparagāṇām eva grahaṇaṃ syāt. gaṅgādigrahaṇam evāstīti cet? pūrvagāṇām eva grahaṇaṃ syāt. ata ubhayīnāṃ grahaṇārthaṃ ‘gaṅgāsindhvādi’ grahaṇaṃ kriyate. ‘nadī’ grahaṇaṃ dviguṇā dviguṇā ity abhisaṃbandhārtham, gaṅgā caturdaśanadīsahasraparivṛtā. sindhur api. evam uttarā api nadyaḥ pratikṣetraṃ taddviguṇadviguṇā bhavanti; ā videhāntāt. tata uttarā arddhārddhahīnāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 410. For what purpose is the mention of '<s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Sindhu</s>, etc.' made? For the purpose of [specifying] 'rivers.' Are the ones under discussion connected [by this]? There should be no such doubt; 'when the immediately preceding [is available]'—

children.text: § 411. uktānāṃ kṣetrāṇāṃ viṣkambhapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 411. For the purpose of understanding the widths of the stated regions, he says—

children.text: bharataḥ ṣaḍviṃśapañcayojanaśatavistāraḥ ṣaṭ caikonaviṃśatibhāgā yojanasya ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> is five hundred and twenty-six <s>yojanas</s> in width, and six-nineteenths of a <s>yojana</s>. ||

children.text: § 412. ṣaḍadhikā viṃśatiḥ ṣaḍviṃśatiḥ. ṣaḍviṃśatir adhikā yeṣu tāni ṣaḍviṃśāni. ṣaḍviṃśāni pañcayojanaśatāni vistāro yasya ṣaḍviṃśapañcayojanaśatavistāro bharataḥ. kim etāvān eva? na; ity āha ṣaṭ caikonaviṃśatibhāgā yojanasya vistāro ’syety abhisaṃbadhyate.
children.translated_text: § 412. Twenty plus six is twenty-six. Those in which twenty-six [units] are in excess are '<s>ṣaḍviṃśa</s>' (twenty-six [units] over). <s>Bharata</s>, whose breadth is twenty-six times five hundred <s>yojanas</s>. Is it exactly this much? No; hence he says: six and nineteen parts of a <s>yojana</s> in breadth—this is to be connected [with the preceding].

children.text: § 413. itareṣāṃ viṣkambhaviśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 413. In order to present the specific breadths of the others, he says—

children.text: taddviguṇadviguṇavistārā varṣadharavarṣā videhāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The mountain ranges (<s>varṣadhara</s>) and regions (<s>varṣa</s>) up to <s>Videha</s> have breadths that are successively double. ||

children.text: § 414. tato bharatād dviguṇo dviguṇo vistāro yesāṃ ta ime taddviguṇadviguṇavistārāḥ. ke te varṣadharavarṣāḥ. kiṃ sarve? na; ity āha videhāntā iti.
children.translated_text: § 414. Those whose breadth is double and double of that of <s>Bharata</s> are 'of successively doubled breadth.' Who are they? The mountain ranges and regions. All of them? No; hence he says: 'up to <s>Videha</s>.'

children.text: § 415. athottareṣāṃ katham ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 415. Now, how about the northern ones? To this he says—

children.text: uttarā dakṣiṇatulyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The northern ones are equal to the southern. ||

children.text: § 416. uttarā airāvatādayo nīlāntā bharatādibhir dakṣiṇais tulyā draṣṭavyāḥ. atītasya sarvasyāyaṃ viśeṣo veditavyaḥ. tena hradapuṣkarādīnāṃ tulyatā yojyā.
children.translated_text: § 416. The northern ones—<s>Airāvata</s> etc. up to <s>Nīla</s>—should be seen as equal to the southern ones—<s>Bharata</s> etc. This distinction should be understood for the entire [series] that has been described. Thereby, the equality of the lakes, <s>Puṣkara</s> etc. should also be applied.

children.text: § 417. attrāha, uktesu bharatādiṣu kṣetreṣu manuṣyāṇāṃ kiṃ tulyo ’nubhavādiḥ, āho svid asti kaścit prativiśeṣa ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 417. Here one asks: In the stated regions such as <s>Bharata</s> etc., do the humans have the same experience etc., or is there some difference? To this it is said—

children.text: bharatairāvatayor vṛddhihrāsau ṣaṭsamayābhyām utsarpiṇyavasarpiṇībhyām ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Bharata</s> and <s>Airāvata</s>, increase and decrease [occur] through the six time-periods of the ascending (<s>utsarpiṇī</s>) and descending (<s>avasarpiṇī</s>) [cycles]. ||

children.text: § 418. vṛddhiś ca hrāsaś ca vṛddhihrāsau. kābhyām? ṣaṭsamayābhyām utsarpiṇyavasarpiṇībhyām. kayoḥ? bharatairāvatayoḥ. na tayoḥ kṣetrayor vṛddhihrāsau staḥ; asaṃbhavāt. tatsthānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ vṛddhihrāsāu bhavataḥ. athavādhikaraṇanirdeśaḥ. bharate airāvate ca manuṣyāṇāṃ vṛddhihrāsāv iti. kiṃ kṛtau vṛddhihrāsau? anubhavāyuḥpramāṇādikṛtau. anubhava upabhogaḥ, āyurjīvitaparimāṇam, pramāṇaṃ śarīrotsedha ity evam ādibhir vṛddhihrāsau manuṣyāṇāṃ bhavataḥ. kiṃ hetukau punas tau? kālahetukau. sa ca kālo dvividhaḥ — utsarpiṇī avasarpiṇī ceti. tadbhedāḥ pratyekaṃ ṣaṭ. anvarthasaṃjñe caite. anubhavādibhir utsarpaṇaśīlā utsarpiṇī. tair evāvasarpaṇaṣīlā avasarpiṇī. tatrāvasarpiṇī ṣaḍvidhā — suṣamasuṣamā suṣamā suṣamaduṣṣamā duṣṣamasuṣamā duṣṣamā atiduṣṣamā ceti. utsarpiṇyapi atiduṣṣamādyā suṣamasuṣamāntā ṣaṭvidhaiva bhavati. avasarpiṇyāḥ parimāṇaṃ daśasāgaropamakoṭīkoṭyaḥ. utsarpiṇyā api tāvatya eva. sobhayī kalpa ity ākhyāte. tatra suṣamasuṣamā catasraḥ sāgaropamakoṭīkoṭyaḥ. tadādau manuṣyā uttarakurumanuṣyatulyāḥ. tataḥ krameṇa hānau satyāṃ suṣamā bhavati tisraḥ sāgaropamakoṭīkoṭyaḥ. tadādau manuṣyā harivarṣamanuṣyasamāḥ. tataḥ krameṇa hānau satyāṃ suṣamaduṣṣamā bhavati dve sāgaropamakoṭīkoṭyau. tadādau manuṣyā haimavatakamanuṣyasamāḥ. tataḥ krameṇa hānau satyāṃ duṣṣamasuṣamā bhavati ekasāgaropamakoṭīkoṭī dvi catvāriṃśadvarṣasahasronā. tadadau manuṣyā videhajanatulyā bhavanti. tataḥ krameṇa hānau satyāṃ duṣṣamā bhavati ekoviṃśativarṣasahasrāṇi. tataḥ krameṇa hanau satyām atiduṣṣamā bhavati ekaviṃśativarṣasahasrāṇi. evam utsarpiṇy api viparītakramā veditavyā.
children.translated_text: § 418. Increase and decrease are '<s>vṛddhihrāsa</s>.' Through what? Through the six time-periods of the ascending and descending [cycles]. Of what? Of <s>Bharata</s> and <s>Airāvata</s>. There is no increase and decrease of those regions themselves, since that is impossible. The increase and decrease belong to the humans residing there. Or it is a statement of the locus: in <s>Bharata</s> and <s>Airāvata</s>, the increase and decrease of humans [occur]. In respect of what are the increase and decrease? In respect of experience, lifespan, bodily measure, etc. Experience means enjoyment; lifespan means the duration of life; measure means bodily height—by these and similar [factors], increase and decrease of humans occur. And what is their cause? Time is their cause. And that time is twofold: the ascending cycle (<s>utsarpiṇī</s>) and the descending cycle (<s>avasarpiṇī</s>). The divisions of each are six. And these are self-explanatory in name. The ascending [cycle] is that in which experience etc. tend to ascend. The descending [cycle] is that in which they tend to descend. Among these, the descending cycle is sixfold: <s>suṣamasuṣamā</s> (extremely happy), <s>suṣamā</s> (happy), <s>suṣamaduṣṣamā</s> (happy-unhappy), <s>duṣṣamasuṣamā</s> (unhappy-happy), <s>duṣṣamā</s> (unhappy), and <s>atiduṣṣamā</s> (extremely unhappy). The ascending cycle too, beginning with <s>atiduṣṣamā</s> and ending with <s>suṣamasuṣamā</s>, is likewise sixfold. The duration of the descending cycle is ten <s>koṭīkoṭī</s> (ten million times ten million) <s>sāgaropamas</s> (ocean-measured periods). The ascending cycle is also of the same duration. Both together constitute what is called a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle). Therein, <s>suṣamasuṣamā</s> lasts four <s>koṭīkoṭī sāgaropamas</s>. At its beginning, humans are like the humans of <s>Uttarakuru</s>. Then, as gradual decline occurs, <s>suṣamā</s> lasts three <s>koṭīkoṭī sāgaropamas</s>. At its beginning, humans are like the humans of <s>Harivarṣa</s>. Then, as gradual decline occurs, <s>suṣamaduṣṣamā</s> lasts two <s>koṭīkoṭī sāgaropamas</s>. At its beginning, humans are like the humans of <s>Haimavataka</s>. Then, as gradual decline occurs, <s>duṣṣamasuṣamā</s> lasts one <s>koṭīkoṭī sāgaropama</s> less forty-two thousand years. At its beginning, humans are like the people of <s>Videha</s>. Then, as gradual decline occurs, <s>duṣṣamā</s> lasts twenty-one thousand years. Then, as gradual decline occurs, <s>atiduṣṣamā</s> lasts twenty-one thousand years. The ascending cycle should be understood in the reverse order.

children.text: § 419. athetarāsu bhūmiṣu kāvasthety ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 419. Now, what is the condition in the other regions? To this he says—

children.text: tābhyām aparā bhūmayo ’vasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The other regions apart from those two are stable (<s>avasthita</s>). ||

children.text: § 420. tābhyāṃ bharatairāvatābhyām aparā bhūmayo ’vasthitā bhavanti. na hi tatrotsarpiṇyavasarpiṇyau staḥ.
children.translated_text: § 420. The regions other than <s>Bharata</s> and <s>Airāvata</s> are stable. For there are no ascending and descending cycles in those [regions].

children.text: § 421. kiṃ tāsu bhūmiṣu manuṣyās tulyāyuṣa āho svit kaścid asti prativiśeṣa ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 421. Are the humans in those regions of equal lifespan, or is there some difference? To this he says—

children.text: ekadvitripalopamasthitayo haimavatakahārivarṣakadaivakuravakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those of <s>Haimavataka</s>, <s>Hārivarṣaka</s>, and <s>Daivakuravaka</s> have lifespans of one, two, and three <s>palyopamas</s> respectively. ||

children.text: § 422. haimavate bhavā haimavatakā ity evaṃ ‘vuñi’ sati manuṣyasaṃpratyayo bhavati. evam uttarayor api. haimavatakādayas trayaḥ. ekādayas trayaḥ. tatra yathāsaṃkhyam abhisaṃbandhaḥ kriyate. ekapalyopamasthitayo haimavatakāḥ. dvipalyopamasthitayo hārivarṣakāḥ. tripalyopamasthitayo daivakuravakā iti. tatra pañcasu haimavateṣu suṣamaduṣṣamā sadāvasthitā. tatra manuṣyā ekapalyopamāyuṣo dvidhanuḥsahasrocchratāś caturthabhaktāhārā nīlotpalavarṇāḥ. pañcasu harivarṣeṣu suṣamā sadāvasthitā. tatra manuṣyā dvipalyopamāyuś cāpasahasrotsedhāḥ ṣaṣṭhabhaktāhārāḥ śaṃkhavarṇāḥ. pañcasu devakuruṣu suṣamasuṣamā sadāvasthitā. tatra manuṣyās tripalyopamāyuṣaḥ ṣaḍdhanuḥsahasrocchrāyā aṣṭamabhaktāhārāḥ kanakavarṇā.
children.translated_text: § 422. Those born in <s>Haimavata</s> are <s>Haimavataka</s>—when the suffix '<s>vuñ</s>' is applied, the understanding of 'human' arises. Similarly for the other two. The three [regions] beginning with <s>Haimavataka</s>. The three [lifespans] beginning with 'one.' Among these, the connection is made sequentially: the <s>Haimavatakas</s> have a lifespan of one <s>palyopama</s>; the <s>Hārivarṣakas</s> have a lifespan of two <s>palyopamas</s>; the <s>Daivakuravakas</s> have a lifespan of three <s>palyopamas</s>. Among the five <s>Haimavata</s> [regions], the <s>suṣamaduṣṣamā</s> age perpetually prevails. There, humans have a lifespan of one <s>palyopama</s>, a height of two thousand bows, eat at every fourth meal-time, and are blue-lotus colored. In the five <s>Harivarṣa</s> [regions], the <s>suṣamā</s> age perpetually prevails. There, humans have a lifespan of two <s>palyopamas</s>, a height of one thousand bows, eat at every sixth meal-time, and are conch-white colored. In the five <s>Devakuru</s> [regions], the <s>suṣamasuṣamā</s> age perpetually prevails. There, humans have a lifespan of three <s>palyopamas</s>, a height of six thousand bows, eat at every eighth meal-time, and are gold-colored.

children.text: § 423. athottareṣu kāvasthety ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 423. Now, what is the condition in the northern ones? To this he says—

children.text: tathottarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The northern ones are likewise. ||

children.text: § 424. yathā dakṣiṇā vyākhyāthās tathaivottarā veditavyāḥ. hairanyavatakā haimavatakais tulyāḥ. rāmyakā hārivarṣakais tulyāḥ. daivakuravakair auttarakuruvakāḥ samākhyātāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 424. Just as the southern ones have been explained, so too the northern ones should be understood. The <s>Hairaṇyavatakas</s> are equal to the <s>Haimavatakas</s>. The <s>Rāmyakas</s> are equal to the <s>Hārivarṣakas</s>. The <s>Auttarakuravakas</s> are declared equal to the <s>Daivakuravakas</s>.

children.text: § 425. atha videheṣv avasthiteṣu kā sthitir ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 425. Now, what is the lifespan of those situated in the <s>Videha</s> [regions]? To this it is said—

children.text: videheṣu saṃkhyeyakālāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Videhas</s>, [humans have] numerable (<s>saṃkhyeya</s>) lifespans. ||

children.text: § 426. sarveṣu videheṣu saṃkhyeyakālā manuṣyāḥ. tatra kālaḥ suṣamaduṣṣamāntopamaḥ sadāvasthitaḥ. manuṣyāś ca pañcadhanuḥśatotsedhāḥ. nityāhārāḥ. utkarṣeṇaikapūrvakoṭīsthitikāḥ. jaghanyenāntarmuhūrtāyuṣaḥ. tasyāś ca saṃbandhe gāthāṃ paṭhanti —
puvassa du parimāṇaṃ sadariṃ khalu koḍisadasahassāiṃ |
children.translated_text: The measure of a <s>pūrva</s> is indeed a hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s>,

children.text: chapaṇṇaṃ ca sahassā boddhavvā vāsakoḍīṇaṃ ||
children.translated_text: and fifty-six thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of years should be understood. ||

§ 426. In all the <s>Videhas</s>, humans have numerable lifespans. There, the age resembles the end of the <s>suṣamaduṣṣamā</s> period, and is perpetually stable. Humans are five hundred bows in height, take nourishment daily, have at maximum a lifespan of one <s>pūrvakoṭī</s>, and at minimum a lifespan of less than one <s>antarmuhūrta</s>. And in connection with that [pūrva], they recite the verse—

children.text: § 427. ukto bharatasya viṣkambhaḥ. punaḥ prakārāntareṇa tatpratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 427. The breadth of <s>Bharata</s> has been stated. In order to present it again by another method, he says—

children.text: bharatasya viṣkambho jambūdvīpasya navatiśatabhāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The breadth of <s>Bharata</s> is one-nine-hundredth of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>. ||

children.text: § 428. jambūdvīpaviṣkambhasya yojanaśatasahasrasya navatiśatabhāgīkṛtasyaiko bhāgo bharatasya viṣkambhaḥ. sa pūrvokta eva. uktaṃ jambūdvīpaṃ parivṛtya vedikā sthitā, tataḥ paro lavaṇodaḥ samudro dviyojanaśatasahasravalayaviṣkambhaḥ. tataḥ paro dhātakīkhaṇḍo dvīpaś caturyojanaśatasahasravalayaviṣkambhaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 428. Of the breadth of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, which is one hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>, one part when divided into nine hundred—that is the breadth of <s>Bharata</s>. That is the same as stated before. It has been stated that a rampart (<s>vedikā</s>) surrounds <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>; beyond that is the <s>Lavaṇoda</s> (salt-water) ocean, with a ring-breadth of two hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. Beyond that is the continent of <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s>, with a ring-breadth of four hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>.

children.text: § 429. tatra varṣādīnāṃ saṃkhyādividhipratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 429. In order to present the number of regions etc. there, he says—

children.text: dvir dhātakīkhaṇḍe ||
children.translated_text: Twice [as many] in <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s>. ||

children.text: § 430. bharatādīnāṃ dravyāṇām ihābhyāvrttir vivakṣitā. atra kathaṃ suc? adhyāhriyamānakriyābhyāvṛttidyotanārthaḥ suc. yathā dvistāvān ayaṃ prāsado mīyata iti. evaṃ dvir dhātakīkhaṇḍe bharatādayo mīyante iti. tad yathā — dvābhyām iṣvākāraparvatābhyāṃ dakṣiṇottarāyatābhyāṃ lavaṇodakālodavedikāspṛṣṭakoṭibhyāṃ vibhakto dhātakīkhaṇḍaḥ pūrvāpara iti. tatra pūrvasya aparasya ca madhye dvau mandarau. tayor ubhayato bharatādīni kṣetrāṇi himavadādayaś ca varṣadharaparvatāḥ. evaṃ dvau bharatau dvau himavantau ity evam ādi saṃkhyānaṃ dviguṇaṃ veditavyam. jambūdvīpahimavadādīnāṃ varṣadharāṇāṃ yo viṣkambhas taddviguṇo dhātakīkhaṇḍe himavadādīnāṃ varṣadharāṇām. varṣadharāś cakrāravadavasthitāḥ. aravivarasaṃsthānāni kṣetrāṇi. jambūdvīpe yatra jambūvṛkṣaḥ sthitaḥ tatra dhātakīkhaṇḍe dhātkīvṛkṣaḥ saparivāraḥ. tadyogād dhātakīkhaṇḍa iti dvīpasya nāma pratītam. tatparikṣepī kālodaḥ samudraḥ ṭaṃkacchinnatīrthaḥ aṣṭayojanaśatasahasravalayavikambhaḥ.
kālodaparikṣepī puṣkaradvīpaḥ ṣodaśayojanaśatasahasravalayaviṣkambhaḥ.
children.translated_text: Encircling <s>Kāloda</s> is the <s>Puṣkara</s> continent, with a ring-breadth of sixteen hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>.

§ 430. The doubling (<s>āvṛtti</s>) of the substances such as <s>Bharata</s> etc. is intended here. How is the [suffix] '<s>suc</s>' [applied] here? The '<s>suc</s>' serves to indicate the repetition of the action to be supplied. Just as [one says] 'this palace is measured as twice as large,' so too 'in <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s>, <s>Bharata</s> etc. are measured twice.' That is as follows: <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s> is divided into eastern and western [halves] by two bow-shaped mountains extending from south to north, whose tips touch the ramparts of <s>Lavaṇoda</s> and <s>Kāloda</s> [oceans]. In the middle of both the eastern and western [halves] are two <s>Mandara</s> [mountains]. On both sides of each are the regions such as <s>Bharata</s> etc. and the mountain ranges such as <s>Himavat</s> etc. Thus, two <s>Bharatas</s>, two <s>Himavats</s>—and so on, the enumeration should be understood as doubled. The breadths of the mountain ranges such as <s>Himavat</s> etc. in <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s> are double those in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>. The mountain ranges are positioned like the spokes of a wheel. The regions are in the shape of the spaces between spokes. Where the <s>Jambū</s> tree stands in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, there in <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s> stands the <s>Dhātakī</s> tree with its retinue. From that, the name of the continent as <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s> is established. Its enclosing [ocean] is the <s>Kāloda</s> ocean, with smooth-cut banks, having a ring-breadth of eight hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>.

children.text: § 431. tatra dvīpāmbhonidhiviṣkambhadviguṇapariklṛptivaddhātakīkhaṇḍavarṣādidviguṇavṛddhiprasaṃge viśeṣāvadhāraṇārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 431. Since, just as the breadths of continents and oceans are stipulated as doubling, there might be the presumption that the regions etc. of <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s> also double [in the same way], he says [the following] for the purpose of specifying the distinction—

children.text: puṣkarārddhe ca ||
children.translated_text: And in half of <s>Puṣkara</s>. ||

children.text: § 432. kim. dvir ity anuvartate. kim apekṣā dvir āvṛttiḥ? jambūdīpabharatahimavadādyapekṣayaiva.

kutaḥ? vyākhyānataḥ. yathā dhātakīkhaṇḍe himavadādīnāṃ viṣkambhas tathā puṣkarārdhe himavadādīnāṃ viṣkambho dviguṇa iti vyākhyāyate. nāmāni tāny eva, iṣvākarau mandarau ca pūrvavat. yatra jambūvṛkṣas tatra puṣkaraṃ saparivāram. tata eva tasya dvipasya nāma rūḍhaṃ puṣkaradvīpa iti. atha kathaṃ puṣkarārddhasaṃjñā. mānuṣottaraśailena vibhaktārdhatvāt puṣkarārdhasaṃjñā.
children.translated_text: Why? From the explanation. Just as the breadth of <s>Himavat</s> etc. in <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s>, so too in half of <s>Puṣkara</s>, the breadth of <s>Himavat</s> etc. is explained as doubled. The names are the same; the bow-shaped [mountains] and the <s>Mandaras</s> are as before. Where the <s>Jambū</s> tree [stands in Jambūdvīpa], there is a <s>Puṣkara</s> [lotus] with its retinue. From that, the name of the continent as <s>Puṣkaradvīpa</s> is established. Now, how [does one get] the designation 'half of <s>Puṣkara</s>'? Because it is divided into halves by the <s>Mānuṣottara</s> mountain, the designation 'half of <s>Puṣkara</s>' [applies].
§ 432. What? 'Twice' continues [from the previous sūtra]. With reference to what is the doubling? With reference to <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Himavat</s>, etc. of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> itself.

children.text: § 433. atrāha kim arthaṃ jambūdvīpahimavadādisaṃkhyā dvir āvṛttā puṣḳarārdhe kathyate, na punaḥ kṛtsna eva puṣkaradvīpe. ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 433. Here one asks: Why is the enumeration of <s>Himavat</s> etc. of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> said to be doubled in half of <s>Puṣkara</s>, rather than in the whole of <s>Puṣkaradvīpa</s>? To this it is said—

children.text: prāṅ mānuṣottarān manuṣyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Humans [exist] only on this side of <s>Mānuṣottara</s> [mountain]. ||

children.text: § 434. puṣkaradvīpabahumadhyadeśabhāgī valayavṛtto mānuṣottaro nāma śailaḥ. tasmāt prāgeva manuṣyā na bahir iti. tato na bahiḥ pūrvoktakṣetravibhāgo ’sti. nāsmād uttaraṃ kadācid api vidyādharā ṛddhiprāptā api manuṣya gacchanti anyatropapādasamudghātābhyām. tato ’syānvarthasaṃjñā. evaṃ jambūdvīpādiṣv ardhatṛtīyeṣu dvīpeṣu dvayoś ca samudrayor manuṣyā veditavyāḥ. te dvividhāḥ —
children.translated_text: § 434. The mountain called <s>Mānuṣottara</s>, ring-shaped, occupies a large portion of the middle region of <s>Puṣkaradvīpa</s>. Only on this side of it are humans, not beyond. Therefore, beyond it there is no division of regions as described earlier. Not even <s>Vidyādharas</s> (celestial beings) who have attained supernatural powers ever go beyond this [mountain] as humans—except through [special modes of] rebirth and bodily emission (<s>samudghāta</s>). Hence, the name [<s>Mānuṣottara</s>, 'beyond which there are no humans'] is self-explanatory. Thus, in the two-and-a-half continents beginning with <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> and in the two oceans, humans should be understood [to exist]. They are of two kinds—

children.text: āryā mlecchāś ca ||
children.translated_text: The civilized (<s>ārya</s>) and the barbarians (<s>mleccha</s>). ||

children.text: § 435. guṇair guṇavadbhir vā aryanta ity āryāḥ. te dvividhā ṛddhiprāptāryā anṛddhiprāptāryāś ceti. anṛddhiprāptāryāḥ paṃcavidhāḥ kṣetrāryā jātyāryāḥ karmāryāś cāritrāryā darśanāryāś ceti. ṛddhiprāptāryāḥ saptavidhāḥ; buddhivikriyātapobalauṣadharasākṣīṇabhedāt. mlecchā dvividhāḥ — antardvīpajāḥ karmabhūmijāś ceti. tatrāntardvīpā lavaṇodadher abhyantare pārśve ’ṣṭāsu dikṣv aṣṭau. tadantareṣu cāṣṭau. himavacchikhariṇor ubhayoś ca vijayārddhayor anteṣv aṣṭau. tatra dikṣu dvīpā vedikāyās tiryak pañcayojanaśatāni praviśya bhavanti. vidikṣv antareṣu ca dvīpāḥ pañcāśatpañcayojanaśateṣu gateṣu bhavanti. śailānteṣu dvīpāḥ ṣaḍyojanaśateṣu gateṣu bhavanti. dikṣu dvīpāḥ śatayojanavistārāḥ. vidikṣv antareṣu ca dvīpās tadardhaviṣkambhāḥ. śailānteṣu pañcaviṃśatiyojanavistārāḥ. tatra pūrvasyāṃ diśy ekorukāḥ. aparasyāṃ diśi lāṅgūlinaḥ. uttarasyāṃ diśy abhāṣakāḥ. dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi viṣāṇinaḥ. śaśakarṇaśaṣkulīkarṇaprāvaraṇakarṇalambakarṇāḥ vidikṣu. aśvasiṃhaśvamahiṣavarāhavyāghrakākakapimukhā antareṣu. meghamukhavidyunmukhāḥ śikhariṇa ubhayor antayoḥ. matsyamukhakālamukhā himavata ubhayor antayoḥ. hastimukhādarśamukhā uttaravijayārdhasyobhayor antayoḥ. gomukhameṣamukhā dakṣiṇavijayārdhasyobhayor antayoḥ. ekorukā mṛdāhārā guhāvāsinaḥ. śeṣāḥ puṣpaphalāhārā vṛkṣavāsinaḥ. sarve te palyopamāyuṣaḥ. te caturviṃśatir api dvīpā jalatalād ekayojanotsedhāḥ. lavaṇodadher bāhyapārśve ’py evaṃ caturviṃśatidvīpā vijñātavyāḥ. tathā kālode ’pi veditavyāḥ. ta ete ’ntardvīpajā mlecchāḥ. karmabhūmijāś ca śakayavanaśabarapulindādayaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 435. Those who are honored (<s>aryante</s>) by virtues or by virtuous persons are <s>Āryas</s> (noble ones). They are twofold: those who have attained <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural powers) and those who have not. Those without <s>ṛddhi</s> are fivefold: <s>kṣetrāryā</s> (noble by region), <s>jātyāryā</s> (noble by birth), <s>karmāryā</s> (noble by action), <s>cāritrāryā</s> (noble by conduct), and <s>darśanāryā</s> (noble by faith). Those who have attained <s>ṛddhi</s> are sevenfold: by the distinction of intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), transformation (<s>vikriyā</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), power (<s>bala</s>), medicine (<s>auṣadha</s>), essence (<s>rasa</s>), and indestructibility (<s>akṣīṇa</s>). The <s>Mlecchas</s> (barbarians) are twofold: those born on intermediate islands (<s>antardvīpajāḥ</s>) and those born in the lands of action (<s>karmabhūmijāḥ</s>). Among these, the intermediate islands are within the inner shore of the salt ocean—eight in the eight directions, and eight in the intermediate directions. At the extremities of both <s>Himavat</s> and <s>Śikharin</s>, and of both <s>Vijayārdhas</s>, there are eight. The islands in the cardinal directions are situated five hundred <s>yojanas</s> sideways from the rim. Islands in the intermediate and other directions are situated at five hundred and fifty <s>yojanas</s>. Islands at mountain-ends are situated at six hundred <s>yojanas</s>. Islands in the cardinal directions are one hundred <s>yojanas</s> wide. Islands in the intermediate and other directions are half that in width. Those at mountain-ends are twenty-five <s>yojanas</s> wide. Among these: in the east, the <s>Ekorukas</s> (one-thighed); in the west, the <s>Lāṅgūlins</s> (tailed); in the north, the <s>Abhāṣakas</s> (speechless); in the south, the <s>Viṣāṇins</s> (horned). In the intermediate directions: <s>Śaśakarṇa</s>, <s>Śaṣkulīkarṇa</s>, <s>Prāvaraṇakarṇa</s>, and <s>Lambakarṇa</s> (hare-eared, shell-eared, cloth-eared, and drooping-eared). In the other [intermediate directions]: horse-faced, lion-faced, dog-faced, buffalo-faced, boar-faced, tiger-faced, crow-faced, and monkey-faced. At both ends of <s>Śikharin</s>: cloud-faced and lightning-faced. At both ends of <s>Himavat</s>: fish-faced and black-faced. At both ends of the northern <s>Vijayārdha</s>: elephant-faced and mirror-faced. At both ends of the southern <s>Vijayārdha</s>: cow-faced and ram-faced. The <s>Ekorukas</s> eat clay and dwell in caves. The rest eat flowers and fruits and dwell in trees. All of them have a lifespan of one <s>palyopama</s>. All twenty-four islands rise one <s>yojana</s> above the water level. On the outer shore of the salt ocean too, twenty-four islands should be understood in the same manner. Likewise in the <s>Kāloda</s> ocean too. These are the <s>Mlecchas</s> born on intermediate islands. Those born in the lands of action include the <s>Śakas</s>, <s>Yavanas</s>, <s>Śabaras</s>, <s>Pulindas</s>, and others.

children.text: § 436. kāḥ punaḥ karmabhūmaya ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 436. What then are the lands of action (<s>karmabhūmi</s>)? To this he says—

children.text: bharatairāvatavidehāḥ karmabhūmayo ’nyatra devakurūttarakurubhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Airāvata</s>, and <s>Videha</s> are the lands of action (<s>karmabhūmi</s>), excluding <s>Devakuru</s> and <s>Uttarakuru</s>. ||

children.text: § 437. bharatā airāvatā videhāś ca paṃca, paṃca, etāḥ karmabhūmaya iti vyapadiśyante. tatra ‘videha’ grahaṇād devakurūttarakurugrahaṇe prasakte tatpratiṣedhārtham āha — ‘anyatra devakurūttarakurubhyaḥ’ iti. ‘anyatra’ śabdo varjanārthaḥ. devakurava uttarakuravo haimavato harivarṣo ramyako hairanyavato ’ntardvīpāś ca bhogabhūmaya iti vyapadiśyante. atha kathaṃ karmabhūmitvam? śubhāśubhalakṣaṇasya karmaṇo ’dhiṣṭhānatvāt. nanu sarvaṃ lokatritayaṃ karmaṇo ’dhiṣṭhānam eva. tata evaṃ prakarṣagatir vijñāsyate, prakarṣeṇa yatkarmaṇo ’dhiṣṭhānam iti. tatrāśubhakarmaṇas tāvat saptamanarakaprāpaṇasya bharatādiṣv evārjanam, śubhasya ca sarvārthasiddhyādisthānaviśeṣaprāpaṇasya karmaṇa upārjanaṃ tatraiva, kṛṣyādilakṣaṇasya ṣaḍvidhasya karmaṇaḥ pātradānādisahitasya tatraivārambhāt karmabhūmivyapadeśo veditavyaḥ. itarāstu daśavidhakalpavṛkṣakaspitabhogānubhavanaviṣayatvād bhogabhūmaya iti vyapadiśyante.
children.translated_text: § 437. The <s>Bharatas</s>, <s>Airāvatas</s>, and <s>Videhas</s>—five, five [each]—these are designated as the lands of action (<s>karmabhūmi</s>). Since the mention of '<s>Videha</s>' would include <s>Devakuru</s> and <s>Uttarakuru</s>, for the purpose of excluding them, he says: 'excluding <s>Devakuru</s> and <s>Uttarakuru</s>.' The word '<s>anyatra</s>' (excluding) is for the purpose of exclusion. <s>Devakuru</s>, <s>Uttarakuru</s>, <s>Haimavata</s>, <s>Harivarṣa</s>, <s>Ramyaka</s>, <s>Hairaṇyavata</s>, and the intermediate islands are designated as lands of enjoyment (<s>bhogabhūmi</s>). But how is the designation 'land of action' [justified]? Because it is the locus of <s>karma</s> characterized as auspicious and inauspicious. [Objection:] But the entire triple world is the locus of <s>karma</s>. [Reply:] Therefore, the meaning should be understood as 'in the highest degree': that which is pre-eminently the locus of <s>karma</s>. For indeed, the earning of inauspicious <s>karma</s> that leads to the seventh hell is possible only in <s>Bharata</s> and the rest; and the earning of auspicious <s>karma</s> that leads to special abodes like <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s> is also possible only there; and since the sixfold <s>karma</s> characterized by agriculture and the like, together with charitable giving and so forth, is undertaken only there—the designation 'land of action' should be understood. The others, however, are designated as lands of enjoyment (<s>bhogabhūmi</s>) because they are the domain of enjoyment nourished by ten types of wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpavṛkṣa</s>).

children.text: § 438. uktāsu bhūmiṣu manuṣyāṇāṃ sthitiparicchedārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 438. For the purpose of determining the lifespan of humans in the stated lands, he says—

children.text: nṛsthitī parāvare tripalyopamāntarmuhūrte ||
children.translated_text: The maximum and minimum lifespans of humans are three <s>palyopamas</s> and less than one <s>muhūrta</s> (48 minutes), [respectively]. ||

children.text: § 439. trīṇi palyopamāni yasyāḥ sā tripalyopamā. antargato muhūrto yasyāḥ sā antarmuhūrtā. yathāsaṃkhyenābhisaṃbandhaḥ. manuṣyāṇāṃ parā utkṛṣṭā sthitis tripalyopamā. aparā jaghanyā antarmuhūrtā. madhye anekavikalpāḥ. tatra palyaṃ trividham — vyavahārapalyam uddhārapalyam addhāpalyam iti. anvarthasaṃjñā etāḥ. ādyaṃ vyavahārapalyam ity ucyate; uttarapalyadvayavyavahārabījatvāt. nānena kiṃcit paricchedyam astīti. dvitīyam uddhārapalyam. tata uddhṛtair lomakacchedair dvīpasamudrāḥ saṃkhyāyanta iti. tṛtīyam addhāpalyam. addhā kālasthitir ity arthaḥ. tatrādyasya pramāṇaṃ kathyate, tatparicchedanārthatvāt. tad yathā — pramāṇāṅgulaparimitayojanaviṣkambhāyāmāvagāhāni trīṇi palyāni kuśūlā ity arthaḥ. ekādisaptāntāhorātrajātāvivālāgrāṇi tāvac chinnāni yāvad dvitīyaṃ kartaricchedaṃ nāvāpnuvanti, tādṛśair lomacchedaiḥ paripūrṇaṃ ghanīkṛtaṃ vyavahārapalyam ity ucyate. tato varṣaśate varṣaśate gate ekaikalomāpakarṣaṇavidhinā yāvatā kālena tadriktaṃ bhavet tāvān kālo vyavahārapalyopamākhyaḥ. tair eva lomacchedaiḥ pratyekam asaṃkhyeyavarṣakoṭīsamayamātracchinnais tatpūrṇam uddhārapalyam. tataḥ samaye samaye ekaikasmin romacchede ’pakṛṣyamāṇe yāvatā kālena tadriktaṃ bhavati tāvan kāla uddhārapalyopmākhyaḥ. eṣām uddhārapalyānāṃ daśakoṭīkoṭya ekam uddhārasāgaropamam. ardhatṛtīyoddhārasāgaropamānāṃ yāvanto romacchedās tāvanto dvīpasamudrāḥ. punar uddhārapalyaromacchedair varṣaśatasamayamātracchinnaiḥ pūrṇam addhāpalyam. tataḥ samaye samaye ekaikasmin romacchede ’pakṛṣyamāṇe yāvatā kālena tadriktaṃ bhavati tāvān kālo ’ddhāpalyopmākhyaḥ. eṣām addhāpalyānāṃ daśakoṭīkoṭya ekam addhāsāgaropamam. daśāddhāsāgaropamakoṭīkoṭya ekāvasarpiṇī. tāvaty evotsarpiṇī. anenāddhāpalyena nārakatairyagyonijānāṃ devamanuṣyāṇāṃ ca karmasthitir bhavasthitir āyuḥsthitiḥ kāyasthitiś ca paricchettavyā. uktā ca saṃgrahagāthā —
children.translated_text: § 439. That which has three <s>palyopamas</s> is '<s>tripalyopamā</s>.' That which has a <s>muhūrta</s> contained within it is '<s>antarmuhūrtā</s>' (less than a <s>muhūrta</s>). The connection is according to the respective numbers. The maximum (<s>parā</s>) lifespan of humans is three <s>palyopamas</s>. The minimum (<s>aparā</s>) is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. In between, there are many varieties. Now, <s>palya</s> (straw-measure) is threefold: <s>vyavahāra-palya</s> (conventional), <s>uddhāra-palya</s> (extraction), and <s>addhā-palya</s> (temporal). These names are self-explanatory. The first is called <s>vyavahāra-palya</s> because it is the seed of conventional usage for the other two <s>palyas</s>. Nothing is actually measured by it. The second is <s>uddhāra-palya</s>; continents and oceans are counted by the hair-tips extracted from it. The third is <s>addhā-palya</s>; <s>addhā</s> means temporal duration. Of the first, the measure is stated, for the purpose of determining [the others]. It is as follows: three pits of dimensions [equal to one <s>yojana</s> each] in diameter, length, and depth, measured by the standard digit (<s>pramāṇāṅgula</s>)—that is the meaning. Hair-tips cut from [the hair of babies] born on the first through the seventh day-and-night, cut so fine that they cannot receive a second scissor-cut—when the [pit] is filled with such hair-tips and packed solid, it is called a <s>vyavahāra-palya</s>. The time during which [the pit] becomes empty by the procedure of removing one hair-tip every hundred years—that duration of time is called a <s>vyavahāra-palyopama</s> (straw-simile). Those same hair-tips, each cut into pieces lasting innumerable crores of years per instant, filling [a pit]—that is the <s>uddhāra-palya</s>. The time during which [the pit] becomes empty by removing one hair-tip per instant—that duration is called an <s>uddhāra-palyopama</s>. Ten crore crores of these <s>uddhāra-palyas</s> make one <s>uddhāra-sāgaropama</s> (ocean-simile). The number of continents and oceans equals the number of hair-tips in two-and-a-half <s>uddhāra-sāgaropamas</s>. Again, filling [a pit] with <s>uddhāra-palya</s> hair-tips, each cut into hundred-year-instant pieces—that is the <s>addhā-palya</s>.
