The time during which [the pit] becomes empty by removing one hair-tip per instant—that duration is called an <s>addhā-palyopama</s>. Ten crore crores of these <s>addhā-palyas</s> make one <s>addhā-sāgaropama</s>. Ten crore crores of <s>addhā-sāgaropamas</s> make one descending cycle (<s>avasarpiṇī</s>). The ascending cycle (<s>utsarpiṇī</s>) is of equal duration. By this <s>addhā-palya</s>, the <s>karma</s>-duration, existence-duration, lifespan, and body-duration of hellish beings, animals, celestials, and humans are to be measured. And a summary verse has been stated:

children.text:
vavahāruddhāraddhā pallā tiṇṇeva hoṃti boddhavvā |
	  saṃkhā dīva-samuddā kammaṭṭhidi vaṇṇidā tadie ||
children.translated_text: The <s>vyavahāra</s>, <s>uddhāra</s>, and <s>addhā</s> <s>palyas</s>—these three alone should be understood; the enumeration of continents and oceans, and <s>karma</s>-duration have been described from those. [Prakrit verse]

children.text: § 440. yathaivete utkṛṣṭajaghanye sthitī nṛṇāṃ tataiva —
children.translated_text: § 440. Just as these are the maximum and minimum lifespans for humans, so also—

children.text: tiryagyonijānāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: For those born in the animal destiny (<s>tiryagyoni</s>) [they are the same]. ||

children.text: § 441. tiraścāṃ yonis tiryagyoniḥ. tiryaggatināmakarmodayāpāditaṃ janmety arthaḥ. tiryagyonau jātās tiryagyonijāḥ. teṣāṃ tiryagyonijānām utkrṣṭā bhavasthitis tripalyopamā. jaghanyā antarmuhūrtā. madhye ’nekavikalpāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 441. The womb of animals is '<s>tiryagyoni</s>.' The meaning is: birth brought about by the fruition of the lifespan-determining <s>karma</s> of the animal destiny. Those born in the animal womb are <s>tiryagyonija</s>. The maximum existence-duration of those animals is three <s>palyopamas</s>. The minimum is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. In between, there are many varieties.

children.text: iti tattvārthavṛttau sarvārthasiddhisaṃjñikāyāṃ tṛitīyo ’dhyāyaḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter of the <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>, the commentary on the <s>Tattvārthasūtra</s>. || 3 ||

children.text: atha caturtho ’dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, the fourth chapter.

children.text: § 442. ‘bhavapratyayo ’vadhir devanārakāṇām’ ity evam ādiṣv asakṛd devaśabda uktas tatra na jñāyate ke devāḥ katividhā iti tannirṇayārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 442. The word 'celestial' (<s>deva</s>) has been used repeatedly in statements such as 'clairvoyant knowledge arises from the condition of existence for celestials and hellish beings' and so forth. Since it is not known who the celestials are and how many types there are, for the purpose of determining that, he says—

children.text: devāś caturṇikāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The celestials (<s>devas</s>) are of four orders (<s>nikāyas</s>). ||

children.text: § 443. devagatināmakarmodaye saty abhyantare hetau bāhyavibhūtir viśeṣaiḥ dvīpādrisamudrādipradeśeṣu yatheṣṭaṃ dīvyanti krīḍantīti devāḥ. ihaikavacananirdeśo yuktaḥ ‘devāś caturṇikāyāḥ’ iti. sa jātyabhidhānāt bahūnāṃ pratipādako bhavati. bahutvanirdeśas tadantargatabhedapratipattyarthaḥ. indrasāmānikādayo bahavo bhedāḥ santi sthityādikṛtāś ca tatsūcanārthaḥ. devagatināmakarmodayasya svakarmaviśeṣāpāditabhedasya sāmarthyān nicīyanta iti nikāyāḥ saṃghatā ity arthaḥ. catvāro nikāyā yeṣāṃ te caturṇikāyāḥ. ke punas te? bhavanavāsino vyantarā jyotiṣkā vaimānikāś ceti.
children.translated_text: § 443. When the fruition of the celestial-destiny lifespan-determining <s>karma</s> occurs as an internal cause, they sport (<s>dīvyanti</s>) and play as they please with external splendors in the regions of continents, mountains, oceans, and the like—hence '<s>devas</s>' (celestials). Here the use of the singular [in the sūtra] is appropriate: 'the celestials are of four orders.' Since it denotes a class, it conveys many [individuals]. The plural [in the commentary] is for the purpose of indicating the divisions contained within. There are many divisions such as <s>Indra</s>, <s>Sāmānika</s>, and so forth, and those based on lifespan, etc.—this is to indicate those. Those who are heaped together (<s>nicīyante</s>) by the potency of the specific <s>karmas</s> that have brought about distinctions in the fruition of the celestial-destiny lifespan-determining <s>karma</s> are '<s>nikāyas</s>' (orders/groups). Those having four orders are '<s>caturnikāyas</s>.' What are they? <s>Bhavanavāsins</s> (mansion-dwellers), <s>Vyantaras</s> (intermediary celestials), <s>Jyotiṣkas</s> (stellar celestials), and <s>Vaimānikas</s> (celestial-vehicle dwellers).

children.text: § 444. teṣāṃ leśyāvadhāranārtham ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 444. For the purpose of determining their <s>leśyās</s> (soul-colorings), it is said—

children.text: āditas triṣu pītāntaleśyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The first three [orders] have <s>leśyās</s> ending with yellow (<s>pīta</s>). ||

children.text: § 445. ‘ādita’ ity ucyate, ante madhye anyathā vā grahaṇaṃ mā vijñāyīti. ādau āditaḥ. dvayor ekasya ca nivṛttyarthaṃ ‘tri’ grahaṇaṃ kriyate. atha caturṇṇāṃ nivṛttyarthaṃ kasmān na bhavati? ‘āditaḥ’ iti vacanāt. ṣaḍleśyā uktāḥ. tatra catasṛṇāṃ leśyānāṃ grahaṇārthaṃ ‘pītānta’ grahaṇaṃ kriyate. pītaṃ teja ity arthaḥ. pītā ante yāsāṃ tāḥ pītāntāḥ. pītāntā leśyā yeṣām te pītāntaleśyāḥ. etad uktaṃ bhavati — āditas triṣu nikāyeṣu bhavanavāsivyantarajyotiṣkanāmasu devānāṃ kṛṣṇā nīlā kāpotā pīteti catasro leśyā bhavanti.
children.translated_text: § 445. The word '<s>ādita</s>' (from the beginning) is used lest the mention be understood as [referring to] the end, middle, or otherwise. '<s>Ādau</s>' means from the beginning. The word '<s>tri</s>' (three) is used for the purpose of excluding two or one. But why not for excluding four? Because of the statement '<s>ādita</s>' (from the beginning). Six <s>leśyās</s> have been mentioned. Among them, the mention of '<s>pītānta</s>' (ending with yellow) is for the purpose of including four <s>leśyās</s>. '<s>Pīta</s>' means fiery (<s>tejas</s>). Those whose end is <s>pīta</s> are '<s>pītānta</s>.' Those having <s>leśyās</s> ending with <s>pīta</s> are '<s>pītānta-leśyā</s>.' What is being said is this: in the first three orders—<s>Bhavanavāsins</s>, <s>Vyantaras</s>, and <s>Jyotiṣkas</s>—the celestials have four <s>leśyās</s>: black (<s>kṛṣṇā</s>), blue (<s>nīlā</s>), grey (<s>kāpotā</s>), and yellow (<s>pītā</s>).

children.text: § 446. teṣāṃ nikāyānām antarvikalpapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 446. For the purpose of explaining the internal varieties of those orders, he says—

children.text: daśāṣṭapaṃcadvādaśavikalpāḥ kalpopapannaparyantāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are of ten, eight, five, and twelve varieties, extending up to the <s>kalpopapanna</s> (those born in the celestial realms). ||

children.text: § 447. caturṇṇāṃ devanikāyānāṃ daśādibhiḥ saṃkhyāśabdair yathāsaṃkhyam abhisaṃbandho veditavyaḥ. daśavikalpā bhavanavāsinaḥ. aṣṭavikalpā vyantarāḥ. pañcavikalpā jyotiṣkāḥ. dvādaśavikalpā vaimānikā iti. sarvavaimānikānāṃ dvādaśavikalpāntaḥpātitve prasakte graiveyakādinivṛttyarthaṃ viśeṣaṇam upādīyate ‘kalpopapannaparyantāḥ’ iti. atha kathaṃ kalpasaṃjñā? indrādayaḥ prakārā daśa eteṣu kalpyanta iti kalpāḥ. bhavanavāsiṣu tatkalpanāsaṃbhave ’pi rūḍhivaśād vaimānikeṣv eva vartate kalpaśabdaḥ. kalpeṣūpapannā kalpopapannāḥ.
kalpopapannāḥ paryantā yeṣāṃ te kalpopapannaparyantāḥ.
children.translated_text: Those whose limit is the <s>kalpopapannas</s> are '<s>kalpopapanna-paryantāḥ</s>'.

§ 447. The connection of the number-words 'ten' etc. with the four celestial orders should be understood respectively. The <s>Bhavanavāsins</s> are of ten varieties. The <s>Vyantaras</s> are of eight varieties. The <s>Jyotiṣkas</s> are of five varieties. The <s>Vaimānikas</s> are of twelve varieties. Since all <s>Vaimānikas</s> would be included within the twelve varieties, the qualifier '<s>kalpopapanna-paryantāḥ</s>' (extending up to those born in the celestial realms) is added for the purpose of excluding the <s>Graiveyaka</s> and higher [celestials]. Now, how does the designation '<s>kalpa</s>' [apply]? The ten categories beginning with <s>Indra</s> are arranged (<s>kalpyante</s>) in these—hence '<s>kalpas</s>.' Although this arrangement is not possible among the <s>Bhavanavāsins</s>, by conventional usage the word '<s>kalpa</s>' applies only to the <s>Vaimānikas</s>. Those born in the <s>kalpas</s> are '<s>kalpopapanna</s>'.

children.text: § 448. punar api tadviśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 448. For further understanding of the specific [divisions], he says—

children.text: indrasāmānikatrāyastriṃśapāriṣadātmarakṣalokapālānīka--prakīrṇakābhiyogyakilbiṣikāś caikaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, <s>Sāmānika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Pāriṣada</s>, <s>Ātmarakṣa</s>, <s>Lokapāla</s>, <s>Anīka</s>, <s>Prakīrṇaka</s>, <s>Ābhiyogya</s>, and <s>Kilbiṣika</s>—each [order has these] individually. ||

children.text: § 449. anyadevāsādhāraṇāṇimādiguṇayogād indantīti indrāḥ. ājñaiśvaryavarjitaṃ yatsthānāyurvīryaparivārabhogopabhogādi tatsamānaṃ, tasmin samāne bhavāḥ sāmānikā mahattarāḥ pitṛgurūpādhyāyatulyāḥ. mantripurohitasthāniyās trāyastriṃśāḥ. trayastriṃśad eva trāyastriṃśāḥ. vayasyapīṭhamardasadṛśāḥ pariṣadi bhavāḥ pariṣadāḥ. ātmarakṣāḥ śirorakṣopamānāḥ. arthacarā rakṣakasamāna lokapālāḥ. lokaṃ pālayantīti lokapālāḥ. padātyādīni sapta anīkāni daṇḍasthānīyāni. prakīrṇakāḥ paurajānapadakalpāḥ. ābhiyogyā dāsasamānā vāhanādikarmaṇi pravṛttāḥ. antevāsisthānīyāḥ kilbiṣikāḥ. kilbiṣaṃ pāpaṃ yeṣām astīti kilbiṣikāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 449. Those who sport (<s>indanti</s>) through the possession of qualities such as <s>aṇimā</s> (atomic size) and others, which are not shared by other celestials, are <s>Indras</s>. <s>Sāmānikas</s> are the great ones equal [to <s>Indra</s>] in position, lifespan, power, retinue, enjoyment, and re-enjoyment, but lacking command and sovereignty—comparable to parents, elders, and teachers. The <s>Trāyastriṃśas</s> (thirty-three) occupy the position of ministers and chaplains; they are exactly thirty-three. <s>Pāriṣadas</s> are members of the assembly, comparable to companions and courtiers. <s>Ātmarakṣas</s> (bodyguards) are comparable to head-guards. <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-protectors), comparable to envoys and sentinels, protect the world—hence '<s>lokapālas</s>.' The seven <s>Anīkas</s> (army divisions), from infantry onward, occupy the position of military commanders. <s>Prakīrṇakas</s> (common ones) are comparable to citizens and villagers. <s>Ābhiyogyas</s> (servants) are comparable to slaves, engaged in duties such as serving as vehicles. <s>Kilbiṣikas</s> (sinful ones) occupy the position of resident students; they are those who have sin (<s>kilbiṣa</s>).

children.text: § 450. ekaikasya nikāyasya ekaśa ete indrādayo daśa vikalpāś caturṣu nikāyeṣūtsargeṇa prasaktās tato ’pavādārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 450. Since these ten divisions from <s>Indra</s> onward, belonging to each order, are applicable to all four orders as a general rule, for the purpose of stating the exceptions, he says—

children.text: trāyastriṃśalokapālavarjyā vyantarajyotiṣkāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Vyantaras</s> and <s>Jyotiṣkas</s> lack the <s>Trāyastriṃśas</s> and <s>Lokapālas</s>. ||

children.text: § 451. vyantareṣu jyotiṣkeṣu ca trāyastriṃśāṃl lokapālāṃś ca varjayitvā itare ’ṣtau vikalpā draṣṭavyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 451. Among the <s>Vyantaras</s> and <s>Jyotiṣkas</s>, excluding the <s>Trāyastriṃśas</s> and <s>Lokapālas</s>, the remaining eight divisions should be observed.

children.text: § 452. atha teṣu nikāyeṣu kim ekaika indra utānyaḥ pratiniyamaḥ kaścid astīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 452. Now, in those classes [of gods], is there one <s>Indra</s> (chief) for each, or is there some other fixed arrangement? — to this he says —

children.text: pūrvayor dvīndrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The first two [classes] have two <s>Indras</s> each. ||

children.text: § 453. pūrvayor nikāyayor bhavanavāsivyantaranikāyayoḥ. kathaṃ dvitīyasya pūrvatvam? sāmīpyāt pūrvatvam upacaryoktam. ‘dvindrāḥ’ iti antarnītavīpsārthaḥ. dvau dvau indrau yeṣāṃ te dvīndrā iti. yathā saptaparṇo ’ṣṭāpada iti. tad yathā — bhavanavāsiṣu tāvad asurakumārāṇāṃ dvāv indrau camaro vairocanaś ca. nāgakumārāṇāṃ dharaṇo bhūtānandaś ca. vidyutkumārāṇāṃ harisiṃho harikāntaś ca. suparṇakumārāṇāṃ veṇudevo veṇudhārī ca. agnikumārāṇāṃ agniśikho ’gnimāṇavaś ca. vātakumārāṇāṃ vailambaḥ prabhañjanaś ca. stanitakumārāṇāṃ sughoṣo mahāghoṣaś ca. udadhikumārāṇāṃ jalakānto jalaprabhaś ca. dvīpakumārāṇāṃ pūrṇo vasiṣṭhaś ca. dikkumārāṇāṃ amitagatir amitavāhanaś ceti. vyantareṣv api kinnarāṇāṃ dvāv īndrau kinnaraḥ kimpuruṣaś ca. kimpuruṣāṇāṃ satpuruṣo mahāpuruṣaś ca. mahoragāṇāṃ matikāyo mahākāyaś ca.
gandharvāṇāṃ gītaratir gītayaśaś ca. yakṣāṇāṃ pūrṇabhadro maṇibhadraś ca. rākṣasānāṃ bhīmo mahābhīmaś ca. bhūtānāṃ pratirūpo ’pratirūpaś ca. piśācānāṃ kālo mahākālaś ca.
children.translated_text: The <s>Gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians) — <s>Gītarati</s> and <s>Gītayaśas</s>. The <s>Yakṣas</s> — <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s> and <s>Maṇibhadra</s>. The <s>Rākṣasas</s> (demons) — <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Mahābhīma</s>. The <s>Bhūtas</s> (spirits) — <s>Pratirūpa</s> and <s>Apratirūpa</s>. The <s>Piśācas</s> (ghouls) — <s>Kāla</s> and <s>Mahākāla</s>.

§ 453. 'The first two classes' means the <s>Bhavanavāsin</s> (mansion-dwelling) and <s>Vyantara</s> (peripatetic) classes. How is the second [class] called 'prior'? The term 'prior' is used figuratively due to proximity. '<s>Dvīndrāḥ</s>' (two Indras) has an implied distributive sense — 'those who have two Indras each.' Like [the compounds] '<s>saptaparṇa</s>' (seven-leaved) and '<s>aṣṭāpada</s>' (eight-footed). That is: among the <s>Bhavanavāsins</s>, the <s>Asurakumāras</s> (demon-princes) have two <s>Indras</s> — <s>Camara</s> and <s>Vairocana</s>. The <s>Nāgakumāras</s> (serpent-princes) — <s>Dharaṇa</s> and <s>Bhūtānanda</s>. The <s>Vidyutkumāras</s> (lightning-princes) — <s>Harisiṃha</s> and <s>Harikānta</s>. The <s>Suparṇakumāras</s> (eagle-princes) — <s>Veṇudeva</s> and <s>Veṇudhārin</s>. The <s>Agnikumāras</s> (fire-princes) — <s>Agniśikha</s> and <s>Agnimāṇava</s>. The <s>Vātakumāras</s> (wind-princes) — <s>Vailamba</s> and <s>Prabhañjana</s>. The <s>Stanitakumāras</s> (thunder-princes) — <s>Sughoṣa</s> and <s>Mahāghoṣa</s>. The <s>Udadhikumāras</s> (ocean-princes) — <s>Jalakānta</s> and <s>Jalaprabha</s>. The <s>Dvīpakumāras</s> (island-princes) — <s>Pūrṇa</s> and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>. The <s>Dikkumāras</s> (direction-princes) — <s>Amitagati</s> and <s>Amitavāhana</s>. Among the <s>Vyantaras</s> too, the <s>Kinnaras</s> have two <s>Indras</s> — <s>Kinnara</s> and <s>Kimpuruṣa</s>. The <s>Kimpuruṣas</s> — <s>Satpuruṣa</s> and <s>Mahāpuruṣa</s>. The <s>Mahoragas</s> (great serpents) — <s>Matikāya</s> and <s>Mahākāya</s>.

children.text: § 454. athaiṣāṃ devānāṃ sukhaṃ kīdṛśam ity ukte sukhāvabodhanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 454. Now, what is the nature of the pleasure of these gods? — for the understanding of [their] pleasure, he says —

children.text: kāyapravīcārā ā aiśānāt ||
children.translated_text: Physical sexual intercourse (<s>kāya-pravīcāra</s>) [extends] up to [the heaven of] <s>Aiśāna</s>. ||

children.text: § 455. pravīcāro maithunopasevanam. kāyena pravīcāro yeṣāṃ te kāyapravīcārāḥ. āṅ abhividhyarthaḥ. asaṃhitayā nirdeśaḥ asaṃdehārthaḥ. ete bhavanavāsyādaya aiśānāntāḥ saṃkliṣṭakarmatvān manuṣyavat strīviṣayasukham anubhavantīty arthaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 455. '<s>Pravīcāra</s>' means sexual enjoyment. Those whose <s>pravīcāra</s> is through the body are '<s>kāya-pravīcārāḥ</s>.' The prefix '<s>ā</s>' has an inclusive sense. The use of the non-compound form is for the purpose of avoiding ambiguity. These [gods], from the <s>Bhavanavāsins</s> onward up to [and including] the <s>Aiśāna</s> [heaven], due to the intensity of their <s>karma</s>, experience pleasure related to women just like humans — this is the meaning.

children.text: § 456. avadhigrahaṇād itareṣāṃ sukhavibhāge ’nirjñāte tatpratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 456. Since the distinction in the pleasure of the remaining [gods] beyond the stated limit is not yet ascertained, for the purpose of explaining that, he says —

children.text: śeṣāḥ sparśarūpaśabdamanaḥ pravīcārāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rest [experience pleasure through] touch, form, sound, and mental intercourse (<s>sparśa-rūpa-śabda-manaḥ-pravīcārāḥ</s>). ||

children.text: § 457. uktāvaśiṣṭagrahaṇārthaṃ ‘śeṣa’ grahaṇam. ke punar uktāvaśiṣṭāḥ? kalpavāsinaḥ. sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca śabdaś ca manaś ca sparśarūpaśabdamanāṃsi, teṣu pravīcāro yeṣāṃ te sparśarūpaśabdamanaḥpravīcārāḥ. kathaṃ abhisaṃbandhaḥ? ārṣāvirodhena. kutaḥ punaḥ ‘pravīcāra’ grahaṇam? iṣṭasaṃpratyayārtham iti. kaḥ punar iṣṭo ’bhisaṃbandhaḥ? ārṣāvirodhī — sānatkumāramāhendrayor devā devāṅganāṅgasparśamātrād eva parāṃ prītim upalabhante, tathā devyo ’pi. brahmabrahmottaralāntavakāpiṣṭheṣu devā divyāṅganānāṃ śṛṅgārākāravilāsacaturamanojñaveṣarūpāvalokanamātrād eva paramasukham āpnuvanti. śukramahāśukraśatārasahasrāreṣu devā devavanitānāṃ madhurasaṃgītamṛduhasitalalitakathitabhūṣaṇaravaśravaṇamātrād eva parāṃ prītimāskandanti. ānataprāṇatāraṇācyutakalpeṣu devā svāṅganāmanaḥsaṃkalpamātrād eva paraṃ sukham āpnuvanti.
children.translated_text: § 457. The word '<s>śeṣa</s>' (rest) is for the purpose of including the remainder after those already stated. Who are the rest after those stated? The <s>Kalpavāsins</s> (heaven-dwellers). Touch, form, sound, and mind — in these [the gods] have their <s>pravīcāra</s> (pleasure); they are '<s>sparśa-rūpa-śabda-manaḥ-pravīcārāḥ</s>.' How is the connection [between these and particular heavens to be understood]? In accordance with scripture, without contradiction. Why then is '<s>pravīcāra</s>' (intercourse) mentioned? For the purpose of communicating the desired connection. What is the desired connection? That which is consistent with scripture: the gods of <s>Sānatkumāra</s> and <s>Māhendra</s> [heavens] obtain supreme delight merely from the touch of the limbs of divine women; likewise do the goddesses. In <s>Brahma</s>, <s>Brahmottara</s>, <s>Lāntava</s>, and <s>Kāpiṣṭha</s> [heavens], the gods attain supreme pleasure merely from beholding the charming, amorous, graceful, and lovely forms and appearances of divine women. In <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Mahāśukra</s>, <s>Śatāra</s>, and <s>Sahasrāra</s> [heavens], the gods attain supreme delight merely from hearing the sweet singing, gentle laughter, charming conversation, and tinkling of ornaments of divine women. In <s>Ānata</s>, <s>Prāṇata</s>, <s>Āraṇa</s>, and <s>Acyuta</s> <s>kalpas</s> (heavens), the gods attain supreme pleasure merely from the mental conception of their own women.

children.text: § 458. athottareṣāṃ kiṃ prakāraṃ sukham ity ukte tanniścayārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 458. Now, what kind of pleasure do those above [these heavens] have? — for the purpose of ascertaining that, he says —

children.text: pare ’pravīcārāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those beyond are without intercourse (<s>apravīcārāḥ</s>). ||

children.text: § 459. ‘para’ grahaṇam itarāśeṣasaṃgrahārtham. ‘apravīcāra’ grahaṇaṃ paramasukhapratipattyartham. pravīcāro hi vedanāpratikāraḥ. tadbhāve teṣāṃ paramasukham anavarataṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text: § 459. The word '<s>para</s>' (beyond) is for the purpose of including all the remaining [gods]. The word '<s>apravīcāra</s>' (without intercourse) is for the purpose of conveying [their] supreme pleasure. For <s>pravīcāra</s> is the remedy for [the agitation of] sensation (<s>vedanā</s>). In the absence of that [agitation], their supreme pleasure exists uninterruptedly.

children.text: § 460. uktā ye ādinikāyadevā daśavikalpā iti teṣāṃ sāmānyaviśeṣasaṃjñāvijñāpanārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 460. The gods of the first class have been stated to be of ten varieties; for the purpose of explaining their general and specific designations, this is said —

children.text: bhavanavāsino ’suranāgavidyutsuparṇāgnivātastanitodadhidvīpadikkumārāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhavanavāsins</s> (mansion-dwellers) are: <s>Asura</s>, <s>Nāga</s>, <s>Vidyut</s> (lightning), <s>Suparṇa</s> (eagle), <s>Agni</s> (fire), <s>Vāta</s> (wind), <s>Stanita</s> (thunder), <s>Udadhi</s> (ocean), <s>Dvīpa</s> (island), and <s>Dik</s> (direction) <s>kumāras</s> (princes). ||

children.text: § 461. bhavaneṣu vasantīty evaṃśīlā bhavanavāsinaḥ. ādinikāyasyeyaṃ sāmānyasaṃjñā. asurādayo viśeṣasaṃjñā viśiṣṭanāmakarmodayāpāditavṛttayaḥ sarveṣāṃ devānām avasthitavayaḥsvabhāvatve ’pi veṣabhūṣāyudhayānavāhanakrīḍanādikumaravad eṣām ābhāsata iti bhavanavāsiṣu kumāravyapadeśo rūḍhaḥ. sa pratyekaṃ parisamāpyate asurakumārā ity evam ādi. kva teṣāṃ bhavanānīti cet. ucyate — ratnaprabhāyāḥ paṃkabahulabhāge ’surakumārāṇāṃ bhavanāni. kharapṛthivībhāge upary adhaś ca ekaikayojanasahasraṃ varjayitvā śeṣanavānāṃ kumārāṇām āvāsāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 461. Those who dwell in mansions — such is their nature — are '<s>Bhavanavāsins</s>.' This is the general designation of the first class. <s>Asura</s> and the rest are the specific designations, their modes of existence being produced by the arising of specific <s>nāma-karma</s> (name-determining karma). Though all gods are of fixed age and nature, their appearance resembles that of princes in attire, ornaments, weapons, vehicles, mounts, and play — hence the conventional designation '<s>kumāra</s>' (prince) is established among the <s>Bhavanavāsins</s>. It is completed individually: '<s>Asurakumāras</s>' and so forth. Where are their mansions? It is said: in the muddy part of the <s>Ratnaprabhā</s> [hell], the mansions of the <s>Asurakumāras</s> [are located]. In the hard-earth part, excluding one thousand <s>yojanas</s> each above and below, the dwelling places of the remaining <s>kumāras</s> [are found].

children.text: § 462. dvitīyanikāyasya sāmānyaviśeṣasaṃjñāvadhāraṇārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 462. For the purpose of ascertaining the general and specific designations of the second class, he says —

children.text: vyantarāḥ kiṃnarakiṃpuruṣamahoragagandharvayakṣarākṣasabhūtapiśācāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Vyantaras</s> (peripatetics) are: <s>Kinnara</s>, <s>Kimpuruṣa</s>, <s>Mahoraga</s>, <s>Gandharva</s>, <s>Yakṣa</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, <s>Bhūta</s>, and <s>Piśāca</s>. ||

children.text: § 463. vividhadeśāntarāṇi yeṣāṃ nivāsās te ‘vyantarāḥ’ ity anvarthā sāmānyasaṃjñeyam aṣṭānām api vikalpānām. teṣāṃ vyantarāṇām aṣṭau vikalpāḥ kiṃnarādayo veditavyā nāmakarmodayaviśeṣāpāditāḥ. kva punas teṣām āvāsa iti cet. ucyate — asmāj jambūdvīpād asaṃkhyeyān dvīpasamudrān atītya upariṣṭe kharapṛthivībhāge saptānāṃ vyantarāṇām āvāsāḥ. rākṣasānāṃ paṅkabahulabhāge.
children.translated_text: § 463. Those whose dwellings are in various different places are '<s>Vyantaras</s>' — this meaningful general designation applies to all eight varieties. The eight varieties of <s>Vyantaras</s> — <s>Kinnara</s> and the rest — should be understood as produced by the specific arising of <s>nāma-karma</s>. Where then are their dwellings? It is said: beyond innumerable continents and oceans from this <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, above, in the hard-earth part, the dwellings of the seven [kinds of] <s>Vyantaras</s> are located. The <s>Rākṣasas</s>' [dwellings] are in the muddy part.

children.text: § 464. tṛtīyasya nikāyasya sāmānyaviśeṣasaṃjñāsaṃkīrtanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 464. For the purpose of stating the general and specific designations of the third class, he says —

children.text: jyotiṣkāḥ sūryācandramasau grahanakṣatraprakīrṇakatārakāś ca ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Jyotiṣkas</s> (luminaries) are: the suns (<s>Sūrya</s>) and moons (<s>Candramas</s>), planets (<s>graha</s>), constellations (<s>nakṣatra</s>), and scattered stars (<s>prakīrṇa-katārakā</s>). ||

children.text: § 465. jyotis svabhāvatvād eṣāṃ pañcānām api ‘jyotiṣkāḥ’ iti sāmānyasaṃjñā anvarthā. sūryādayas tadviśeṣasaṃjñā nāmakarmodayapratyayāḥ. ‘sūryācandramasau’ iti pṛthaggrahaṇaṃ prādhānyakhyāpanārtham. kiṃ kṛtaṃ punaḥ prādhānyam? prabhāvādikṛtam. kva punas teṣām āvāsāḥ? ity attrocyate, asmāt samād bhūmibhāgād ūrdhvaṃ saptayojanaśatāni navatyuttarāṇi utpatya sarvajyotiṣām adhobhāgavinyastās tārakāś caranti. tato daśayojanāny utpatya sūryaś caranti. tato ’śītiyojanāny utpatya candramaso bhramanti. tataś catvāri yojanāny utpatya nakṣatrāṇi. tataś catvāri yojanāny utpatya budhāḥ. tatas trīṇi yojanāny utpatya śukrāḥ. tatas trīṇi yojanāny utpatya bṛhaspatayaḥ. tatas trīṇi yojanāny utpatyāṃgārakāḥ. tatas trīṇi yojanāny utpatya śanaiś carāś caranti. sa eṣa jyotir gaṇagocaro nabho ’vakāśo daśādhikayojanaśatabahalas tiryagsaṃkhyātadvīpasamudrapramāṇo ghanodadhiparyantaḥ. uktam ca.
ṇauduttarasattasayā dasasīdī cadugaṃ tiyacaukkaṃ |
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] Ninety-seven hundred, ten, eighty, four, four,

children.text: tārāravisasirikkhā buhabhaggavaguruaṃgirārasaṇī ||
children.translated_text: stars, sun, moon, constellations, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, Mars, and Saturn.

§ 465. Because all five have luminosity as their nature, the general designation '<s>Jyotiṣkas</s>' is meaningful. <s>Sūrya</s> and the rest are their specific designations, caused by the arising of <s>nāma-karma</s>. The separate mention of '<s>sūryā-candramasau</s>' (suns and moons) is for the purpose of indicating their preeminence. What makes them preeminent? Their radiance and the like. Where then are their dwellings? It is said here: rising seven hundred and ninety <s>yojanas</s> upward from this level ground, the stars of all luminaries move, placed at the lower level. Rising ten <s>yojanas</s> from there, the suns move. Rising eighty <s>yojanas</s> from there, the moons revolve. Rising four <s>yojanas</s> from there, the constellations. Rising four <s>yojanas</s> from there, the Mercuries. Rising three <s>yojanas</s> from there, the Venuses. Rising three <s>yojanas</s> from there, the Jupiters. Rising three <s>yojanas</s> from there, the Marses. Rising three <s>yojanas</s> from there, the Saturns revolve. This celestial space, the domain of the host of luminaries, is one hundred and ten <s>yojanas</s> thick, extends transversely across numerable continents and oceans, and reaches up to the dense ocean. And it has been said:

children.text: § 466. jyotiṣkāṇāṃ gativiśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 466. For the purpose of understanding the specific movement of the luminaries, he says —

children.text: merupradakṣiṇā nityagatayo nṛloke ||
children.translated_text: They move perpetually clockwise around <s>Meru</s>, in the human world. ||

children.text: § 467. meroḥ pradakṣiṇā merupradakṣiṇā. ‘merupradakṣiṇāḥ’ iti vacanaṃ gativiśeṣapratipattyarthaṃ viparītā gatir mā vijñāyīti. ‘nityagatayaḥ’ iti viśeṣaṇam anuparatakriyāpratipādanārtham. ‘nṛloka’ grahaṇaṃ viṣayārtham. ardhatṛtīyeṣu dvīpeṣu dvayoś ca samudrayor jyotiṣkā nityagatayo nānyatreti. jyotiṣkavimānānāṃ gatihetvabhāvāt tadvṛttyabhāva iti cet. na; asiddhatvāt, gatiratābhiyogyadevaprerita gatipariṇāmāt karmavipākasya vaicitryāt. teṣāṃ hi gatimukhenaiva karma vipacyata iti. ekādaśabhir yojanaśatair ekaviṃśair merum aprāpya jyotiṣkāḥ pradakṣiṇaś caranti.
children.translated_text: § 467. Clockwise around <s>Meru</s> is '<s>merupradakṣiṇā</s>.' The statement '<s>merupradakṣiṇāḥ</s>' is for the purpose of understanding the specific direction of movement — lest counter-clockwise movement be understood. '<s>Nityagatayaḥ</s>' (perpetually moving) is a qualifier for conveying their unceasing activity. The mention of '<s>nṛloka</s>' (human world) specifies the domain: the luminaries move perpetually in two-and-a-half continents and two oceans, not elsewhere. [Objection:] Since there is no cause of movement for the celestial vehicles, there would be no [such] movement. [Reply:] No; because that is not established — due to the transformation of movement [occurring] from the deities who are impelled [by karma] and who are suited to vehicles of movement, and due to the variety of karmic fruition. For their <s>karma</s> ripens through the very medium of movement. The luminaries revolve clockwise at eleven hundred and twenty-one <s>yojanas</s> [distance] from <s>Meru</s>, without reaching it.

children.text: § 468. gatimajjyotisaṃbandhena vyavahārakālapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 468. For the purpose of understanding conventional time in connection with the moving luminaries, he says —

children.text: tatkṛtaḥ kālavibhāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The division of time is effected by them. ||

children.text: § 469. ‘tad’ grahaṇaṃ gatimajjyotiḥpratinirdeśārtham. na kevalayā gatyā nāpi kevalair jyotirbhiḥ kālaḥ paricchadyate;

anupalabdher aparivartanāc ca. kālo dvividho vyāvahāriko mukhyaś ca. vyāvahārikaḥ kālavibhāgas tatkṛtaḥ samayāvalikādiḥ kriyāviśeṣaparicchinno ’nyasyāparicchinnasya paricchedahetuḥ. mukhyo ’nyo vakṣamāṇalakṣaṇaḥ.
children.translated_text: because [without both] there is non-apprehension and non-recurrence. Time is twofold: conventional (<s>vyāvahārika</s>) and primary (<s>mukhya</s>). The conventional division of time — effected by them — beginning with <s>samaya</s> (instant) and <s>āvalikā</s>, is delimited by specific activities and serves as the means of delimiting what is otherwise undelimited. The primary [time] is of a different nature, whose definition will be stated [later].
§ 469. The word '<s>tad</s>' (that/them) indicates the moving luminaries. Time is not measured by movement alone, nor by luminaries alone;

children.text: § 470. itaratra jyotiṣām avasthānapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 470. For the purpose of explaining the position of the luminaries elsewhere [outside the human world], he says —

children.text: bahir avasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are stationed outside. ||

children.text: § 471. ‘bahiḥ’ ity ucyate. kuto bahiḥ? nṛlokāt. katham avagamyate? arthavaśād vibhaktipariṇāmo bhavati. nanu ca nṛloke ‘nityagati’ vacanād anyatrāvasthānaṃ jyotiṣkāṇāṃ siddham. ato bahir avasthitā iti vacanam anarthakam iti. tan na; kiṃ kāraṇam? nṛlokād anyatra hi jyotiṣām astitvam avasthānāṃ cāsiddham. atas tadubhayasiddhyarthaṃ bahir avasthitā ity ucyate. viparītagatinivṛttyarthaṃ kādācitkagatinivṛttyarthaṃ ca sūtram ārabdham.
children.translated_text: § 471. 'Outside' is said. Outside of what? Of the human world. How is this understood? Due to the force of meaning, a case-ending transformation occurs. [Objection:] But since 'perpetually moving in the human world' was stated, the stationing of luminaries elsewhere is already established; therefore the statement 'stationed outside' is purposeless. [Reply:] Not so. Why? Because the existence and stationing of luminaries elsewhere than the human world was not yet established. Therefore, for the establishment of both, 'stationed outside' is said. The sūtra was begun for the purpose of excluding counter-direction movement and occasional movement.

children.text: § 472. turīyasya nikāyasya sāmānyasaṃjñāsaṃkīrtanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 472. For the purpose of stating the general designation of the fourth class, he says —

children.text: vaimānikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaimānikas</s> (celestial mansion-dwellers). ||

children.text: § 473. ‘vaimānika’ grahaṇam adhikārārtham. ita uttaraṃ ye vakṣyante teṣāṃ vaimānikasaṃpratyayo yathā syād iti adhikāraḥ kriyate. viśeṣeṇātmasthān sukṛtino mānayantīti vimānāni. vimāneṣu bhavā vaimānikāḥ. tāni vimānāni trividhāni — indrakaśreṇīpuṣpaprakīrṇakabhedena. tatra indrakavimānāni indravanmadye ’vasthitāni. teṣāṃ catasṛṣu dikṣu ākāśapradeśaśreṇivadavasthānāt śreṇivimānāni. vidikṣu prakīrṇapuṣpavadavasthānāt puṣpaprakīrṇakāni.
children.translated_text: § 473. The word '<s>Vaimānika</s>' is for the purpose of [establishing] a governing topic. Those who will be stated hereafter — [the topic is established] so that they may be understood as <s>Vaimānikas</s>. '<s>Vimānas</s>' (celestial mansions) are so called because they specially honor the meritorious [souls] dwelling in them. Those born in <s>vimānas</s> are <s>Vaimānikas</s>. Those <s>vimānas</s> are of three kinds — differentiated as <s>Indraka</s> (Indra-like), <s>Śreṇī</s> (row), and <s>Puṣpaprakīrṇaka</s> (flower-scattered). Among these, <s>Indraka</s> mansions are situated in the center, like <s>Indra</s>. Those stationed on all four sides like rows of space-points are <s>Śreṇi</s> mansions. Those stationed in the intermediate directions like scattered flowers are <s>Puṣpaprakīrṇakas</s>.

children.text: § 474. teṣāṃ vaimānikānāṃ bhedāvabodhanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 474. For the purpose of understanding the divisions of the <s>Vaimānikas</s>, he says —

children.text: kalpopapannāḥ kalpātītāś ca ||
children.translated_text: They are <s>Kalpopapanna</s> (born in <s>kalpas</s>) and <s>Kalpātīta</s> (beyond <s>kalpas</s>). ||

children.text: § 475. kalpeṣūpannāḥ kalpopapannāḥ — kalpātītāḥ kalpātītāś ceti dvividhā vaimānikāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 475. Those born in the <s>kalpas</s> (heavens) are <s>Kalpopapanna</s>; the <s>Kalpātītas</s> are beyond the <s>kalpas</s> — thus the <s>Vaimānikas</s> are twofold.

children.text: § 476. teṣām avasthānaviśeṣanirjñānārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 476. For the purpose of ascertaining the specific arrangement of their position, he says —

children.text: upary upari ||
children.translated_text: One above the other (<s>upary upari</s>). ||

children.text: § 477. kim artham idam ucyate. tiryagavasthitipratiṣedhārtham ucyate. na jyotiṣkavattiryagavasthitāḥ. na vyantaravadasamāvasthitayaḥ. ‘upary upari’ ity ucyante. ke te? kalpāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 477. For what purpose is this said? For the purpose of excluding a transverse arrangement. They are not arranged transversely like the luminaries, nor are they unevenly positioned like the <s>Vyantaras</s>. 'One above the other' is said. Who are they? The <s>kalpas</s> (heavens).

children.text: § 478. yady evaṃ, kiyatsu kalpavimāneṣu te devā bhavantīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 478. If so, in how many heavenly mansions do those gods exist? — to this he says —

children.text: saudharmaiśānasānatkumāramāhendrabrahmabrahmottaralāntavakāpiṣṭhaśukramahāśukraśatārasahasrāreṣv ānataprāṇatayor āraṇācyutayor navasu graiveyakeṣu vijayavaijayantajayantāparājiteṣu sarvārthasiddhau ca ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Saudharma</s>, <s>Aiśāna</s>, <s>Sānatkumāra</s>, <s>Māhendra</s>, <s>Brahma</s>, <s>Brahmottara</s>, <s>Lāntava</s>, <s>Kāpiṣṭha</s>, <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Mahāśukra</s>, <s>Śatāra</s>, <s>Sahasrāra</s>; in <s>Ānata</s> and <s>Prāṇata</s>; in <s>Āraṇa</s> and <s>Acyuta</s>; in the nine <s>Graiveyakas</s>; in <s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Vaijayanta</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, and <s>Aparājita</s>; and in <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>. ||

children.text: § 479. katham eṣāṃ saudharmādiśabdānāṃ kalpābhidhānam? cāturārthikenāṇā svabhāvato vā kalpasyābhidhānaṃ bhavati. atha katham indrābhidhānam? svabhāvataḥ sāhacaryād vā. tat katham iti cet? ucyate — sudharmā nāma sabhā, sā ’sminn astīti saudharmaḥ kalpaḥ.
tad asminn astīti
children.translated_text: 'That exists in this' —

children.text: aṇ. tatkalpasāhacaryād indro ’pi saudharmaḥ. īśāno nāma indraḥ svabhāvataḥ. īśānasya nivāsaḥ kalpa aiśānaḥ.
children.translated_text: [The suffix] <s>aṇ</s> [is applied in the derivation]. Due to association with that <s>kalpa</s> (heaven), the <s>Indra</s> too is called <s>Saudharma</s>. <s>Īśāna</s> is the name of an <s>Indra</s> by nature. The abode of <s>Īśāna</s> is the heaven called <s>Aiśāna</s>.

children.text: tasya nivāsaḥ
children.translated_text: 'His abode'

children.text: ity aṇ. tatsāhacaryād indro ’py aiśānaḥ. sanatkumāro nāma indraḥ svabhāvataḥ.
children.translated_text: [takes the suffix] <s>aṇ</s>. Due to association with that, the <s>Indra</s> too is <s>Aiśāna</s>. <s>Sanatkumāra</s> is the name of an <s>Indra</s> by nature.

children.text: tasya nivāsaḥ
children.translated_text: 'His abode'

children.text: ity aṇ. sānatkumāraḥ kalpaḥ. tatsāhacaryād indro ’pi sānatkumāraḥ. mahendro nāmendraḥ svabhāvataḥ. tasya nivāsaḥ kalpo māhendraḥ. tatsāhacaryād indro ’pi māhendraḥ. evam uttaratrāpi yojyam. āgamāpekṣayā vyavasthā bhavatīti ‘upary upari’ ity anena dvayor dvayor abhisaṃbandho veditavyaḥ. prathamo saudharmaiśānakalpau, tayor upari sānatkumāramāhendrau, tayor upari brahmalokabrahmottarau, tayor upari lāntavakāpiṣṭau, tayor upari śukramahāśukrau, tayor upari śatārasāhasrārau, tayor upari ānataprāṇatau, tayor upari āraṇācyutau. adha upari ca pratyekam indrasaṃbandho veditavyaḥ. madhye tu pratidvayam. saudharmaiśānasānatkumāramāhendrāṇāṃ caturṇāṃ catvāra indrāḥ. brahmalokabrahmottarayor eko brahmā nāma. lāntavakāpiṣṭhayor eko lāntavākhyaḥ. śukramahāśukrayor ekaḥ śukrasaṃjñaḥ. śatārasahasrārayor ekaḥ śatāranāmā. ānataprāṇatāraṇācyutānāṃ caturṇṇāṃ catvāraḥ. evaṃ kalpavāsināṃ dvādaśa indrā bhavanti. jambūdvīpe mahāmandaro yojanasahasrāvagāho navanavatiyojanasahasrocchrāyaḥ. tasyādhastād adholokaḥ. bāhalyena tatpramāṇas tiryakprasṛtas tiryaglokaḥ. tasyopariṣṭād ūrdvalokaḥ. merucūlikā catvāriṃśad yojanocchrāyā. tasyā upari keśāntaramātre vyavasthitam ṛjuvimānam indrakaṃ saudharmasya. sarvam anyal lokānuyogād veditavyam. ‘navasu graiveyakeṣu’ iti navaśabdasya pṛthagvacanaṃ kim artham? anyāny api navavimānāni anudiśasaṃjñakāni santīti jñāpanārtham. tenānudiśānāṃ grahaṇaṃ veditavyam.
children.translated_text: [takes the suffix] <s>aṇ</s>. The <s>kalpa</s> is <s>Sānatkumāra</s>. Due to association with that, the <s>Indra</s> too is <s>Sānatkumāra</s>. <s>Mahendra</s> is an <s>Indra</s> by nature. His abode, the <s>kalpa</s>, is <s>Māhendra</s>. Due to association with that, the <s>Indra</s> too is <s>Māhendra</s>. The same applies for the higher ones. Since the arrangement follows scripture, from the expression 'successively higher,' the connection should be understood as pairs of two. The first pair is the <s>Saudharma</s> and <s>Aiśāna kalpas</s>; above them, <s>Sānatkumāra</s> and <s>Māhendra</s>; above them, <s>Brahmaloka</s> and <s>Brahmottara</s>; above them, <s>Lāntava</s> and <s>Kāpiṣṭha</s>; above them, <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Mahāśukra</s>; above them, <s>Śatāra</s> and <s>Sahasrāra</s>; above them, <s>Ānata</s> and <s>Prāṇata</s>; above them, <s>Āraṇa</s> and <s>Acyuta</s>. The lower and upper [of each pair] should each be understood as having its own <s>Indra</s>. But in the middle [pairs], it is one [<s>Indra</s>] per pair. The four [kalpas] — <s>Saudharma</s>, <s>Aiśāna</s>, <s>Sānatkumāra</s>, and <s>Māhendra</s> — have four <s>Indras</s>. For <s>Brahmaloka</s> and <s>Brahmottara</s>, there is one [<s>Indra</s>] called <s>Brahmā</s>. For <s>Lāntava</s> and <s>Kāpiṣṭha</s>, one called <s>Lāntava</s>. For <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Mahāśukra</s>, one called <s>Śukra</s>. For <s>Śatāra</s> and <s>Sahasrāra</s>, one called <s>Śatāra</s>. For the four — <s>Ānata</s>, <s>Prāṇata</s>, <s>Āraṇa</s>, and <s>Acyuta</s> — there are four [<s>Indras</s>]. Thus there are twelve <s>Indras</s> among the <s>kalpa</s>-dwelling [gods]. In <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, the great <s>Mandara</s> [mountain] descends one thousand <s>yojanas</s> [below the surface] and rises ninety-nine thousand <s>yojanas</s> [in height]. Below it is the lower world. Equal in extent to that, extending horizontally, is the middle world. Above that is the upper world. The <s>Merucūlikā</s> (peak of <s>Meru</s>) rises forty <s>yojanas</s>. Above it, at a hair's breadth distance, stands the upright mansion (<s>ṛju-vimāna</s>) called <s>Indraka</s>, belonging to <s>Saudharma</s>. All other [details] should be known from the <s>Lokānuyoga</s> (cosmological treatise). What is the purpose of the separate mention of 'nine' in 'in the nine <s>Graiveyakas</s>'? To indicate that there also exist nine other mansions called <s>Anudiśa</s>. Thereby, the inclusion of the <s>Anudiśas</s> should be understood.

§ 479. How do these words — <s>Saudharma</s> and the rest — come to designate <s>kalpas</s> (heavens)? Through [the principle of] fourfold [naming], or the designation of the <s>kalpa</s> arises from its nature. But how does the designation of the <s>Indra</s> [arise]? From its nature, or from association. How so? It is said: there is an assembly hall named <s>Sudharmā</s>; that exists in this — hence the <s>Saudharma</s> heaven.

children.text: § 480. eṣām adhikṛtānāṃ vaimānikāṃ parasparato viśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 480. To understand the mutual distinctions among these <s>Vaimānika</s> gods that have been discussed, he says —

children.text: sthitiprabhāvasukhadyutileśyāviśuddhīndriyāvadhiviṣayato ’dhikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are superior in lifespan (<s>sthiti</s>), supernatural power (<s>prabhāva</s>), bliss (<s>sukha</s>), radiance (<s>dyuti</s>), purity of soul-coloring (<s>leśyā-viśuddhi</s>), and the range of senses and clairvoyance (<s>indriya-avadhi-viṣaya</s>).

children.text: § 481. svopāttasyāyuṣa udayāt tasmin bhave śarīreṇa sahāvasthānaṃ sthitiḥ. śāpānugrahaśaktiḥ prabhāvaḥ. sukham indriyārthānubhavaḥ. śarīravasanābharaṇādidīptiḥ dyutiḥ. leśyā uktā. leśyāyā viśuddhir leśyāviśuddhiḥ. indriyāṇām avadheś ca indriyāvadhiviṣayaḥ. tebhyas tair vā ’dhikā iti tasiḥ. upary upari pratikalpaṃ pratiprastāram ca vaimānikāḥ sthityādibhir adhikā ity arthaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 481. <s>Sthiti</s> (lifespan) is the duration of abiding with a body in that existence, due to the fruition of one's acquired lifespan-determining <s>karma</s>. <s>Prabhāva</s> (supernatural power) is the capacity for cursing and blessing. <s>Sukha</s> (bliss) is the experience of sense-objects. <s>Dyuti</s> (radiance) is the luster of the body, garments, ornaments, and so forth. <s>Leśyā</s> (soul-coloring) has been explained. <s>Leśyā-viśuddhi</s> is the purity of the soul-coloring. <s>Indriya-avadhi-viṣaya</s> is the range of the senses and of clairvoyance. 'Superior to those, by those' — [the suffix] <s>tasi</s> [is used]. The meaning is: the <s>Vaimānika</s> gods are successively superior in lifespan and the other [attributes], for each <s>kalpa</s> and each tier upward.

children.text: § 482. yathā sthityādibhir upary upary adhikā evaṃ gatyādhibhir apīty atiprasaṃge tannivṛttyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 482. Just as they are successively superior in lifespan and the like, they might also be so in movement and the like — to prevent this over-extension, he says —

children.text: gatiśarīraparigrahābhimānato hīnāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are inferior in movement (<s>gati</s>), body-size (<s>śarīra</s>), possessions (<s>parigraha</s>), and pride (<s>abhimāna</s>).

children.text: § 483. deśād deśāntaraprāptihetur gatiḥ. śarīraṃ vaikriyikam uktam. lobhakaṣāyodayād viṣayeṣu saṅgaḥ parigrahaḥ. mānakaṣāyād utpanno ’haṃkāro ’bhimānaḥ. etair gatyādibhir upary upari hīnāḥ. deśāntaraviṣayakrīḍāratiprakarṣābhāvād upary upari gatihīnāḥ. śarīraṃ saudharmaiśānayor devānāṃ saptāratnipramāṇam. sānatkumāramāhendrayoḥ ṣaḍaratnipramāṇam. brahmalokabrahmottaralāntavakāpiṣṭheṣu pañcāratnipramāṇam. śukramahāśukraśatārasahasrāreṣu caturaratnipramāṇam. ānataprāṇatayor arddhacaturthāratnipramāṇam. āraṇācyutayos tryaratnipramāṇam. adho graiveyakeṣu arddhatṛtīyāratnipramāṇam. madhyagraiveyakeṣv aratnidvayapramāṇam. uparimagraiveyakeṣu anudiśavimānakeṣu ca adhyarddhāratnipramāṇam. anuttareṣv aratnipramāṇam. parigrahaś ca vimānaparicchadādir upary upari hīnaḥ. abhimānaś copary upari tanukaṣāyatvād dhīnaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 483. <s>Gati</s> (movement) is the cause of reaching from one place to another. <s>Śarīra</s> (body) is the <s>vaikriyika</s> (transformable body), as described. <s>Parigraha</s> (possessions) is the attachment to sense-objects arising from the fruition of greed-passion (<s>lobha-kaṣāya</s>). <s>Abhimāna</s> (pride) is the ego arising from pride-passion (<s>māna-kaṣāya</s>). In these — movement and the rest — they are successively inferior upward. They are successively inferior in movement upward because of the absence of the excellence of play and delight pertaining to other regions. The body of the gods of <s>Saudharma</s> and <s>Aiśāna</s> is seven <s>aratnis</s> (cubits) in size; of <s>Sānatkumāra</s> and <s>Māhendra</s>, six <s>aratnis</s>; of <s>Brahmaloka</s>, <s>Brahmottara</s>, <s>Lāntava</s>, and <s>Kāpiṣṭha</s>, five <s>aratnis</s>; of <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Mahāśukra</s>, <s>Śatāra</s>, and <s>Sahasrāra</s>, four <s>aratnis</s>; of <s>Ānata</s> and <s>Prāṇata</s>, three and a half <s>aratnis</s>; of <s>Āraṇa</s> and <s>Acyuta</s>, three <s>aratnis</s>; in the lower <s>Graiveyakas</s>, two and a half <s>aratnis</s>; in the middle <s>Graiveyakas</s>, two <s>aratnis</s>; in the upper <s>Graiveyakas</s> and the <s>Anudiśa</s> mansions, one and a half <s>aratnis</s>; in the <s>Anuttara</s> [mansions], one <s>aratni</s>. Possessions — such as the furnishings of the celestial mansions — are successively lesser upward. Pride too is successively lesser upward, due to the thinning of passions.

children.text: § 484. purastāt triṣu nikāyeṣu devānāṃ leśyāvidhir uktaḥ. idānīṃ vaimānikeṣu leśyāvidhipratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 484. Earlier, the arrangement of <s>leśyā</s> (soul-coloring) was stated for the gods of the three [lower] classes. Now, to understand the arrangement of <s>leśyā</s> among the <s>Vaimānika</s> gods, he says —

children.text: pītapadmaśuklaleśyā dvitriśeṣeṣu ||
children.translated_text: Yellow (<s>pīta</s>), lotus-pink (<s>padma</s>), and white (<s>śukla</s>) <s>leśyās</s> [prevail] in [groups of] two, three, and the remaining [kalpas].

children.text: § 485. pītā ca padmā ca śuklā ca tāḥ pītapadmaśuklāḥ. pītapadmaśuklā leśyā yeṣāṃ te pītapadmaśuklaleśyāḥ. kathaṃ hrasvatvam. autarapadikam. yathā —
drutāyāṃ taparakaraṇe madhyamavilambitayor upasaṃkhyānam
children.translated_text: 'In rapid [recitation], the making of [the intervocalic consonant as] <s>tapara</s> [i.e., lightly articulated]; and the enumeration of the middle and slow [varieties].'

children.text: iti. athavā pītaś ca padmaś ca śuklaś ca pītapadmaśuklā varṇavanto ’rthāḥ. teṣām iva leśyā yeṣāṃ te pītapadmaśuklaleśyāḥ. tatra kasya kā leśyā iti. attrocyate — saudharmaiśānayoḥ pītaleśyāḥ. sānatkumāramāhendrayoḥ pītapadmaleśyāḥ. brahmalokabrahmottaralāntavakāpiṣṭheṣu padmaleśyāḥ. śukramahāśukraśatārasahasrāreṣu padmaśuklaleśyāḥ. ānatādiṣu śuklaleśyāḥ. tatrāpy anudiśān uttareṣu paramaśuklaleśyāḥ. sūtre ’nabhihitaṃ kathaṃ miśragrahaṇam? sāhacaryāl lokavat. tad yathā — chatriṇo gacchanti iti acchatriṣu chatravyavahāraḥ. evam ihāpi miśrayor anyataragrahaṇaṃ bhavati. ayam arthaḥ sūtrataḥ kathaṃ gamyate iti cet. ucyate — evam abhisaṃbandhaḥ kriyate, dvayoḥ kalpayugalayoḥ pītaleśyā; sānatkumāramāhendrayoḥ padmaleśyāyā avivakṣātaḥ. brahmalokādiṣu triṣu kalpayugaleṣu padmaleśyā; śukramahāśukrayoḥ śuklaleśyāyā avivakṣātaḥ. śeṣeṣu śatārādiṣu śuklaleśyāyā; padmaleśyāyā avivakṣātaḥ. iti nāsti doṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: Alternatively: yellow, lotus-pink, and white are colored objects; those whose <s>leśyā</s> is like theirs are <s>pīta-padma-śukla-leśyāḥ</s>. Now, which <s>leśyā</s> belongs to whom? To this it is said: In <s>Saudharma</s> and <s>Aiśāna</s>, the <s>leśyā</s> is yellow (<s>pīta</s>). In <s>Sānatkumāra</s> and <s>Māhendra</s>, yellow and lotus-pink. In <s>Brahmaloka</s>, <s>Brahmottara</s>, <s>Lāntava</s>, and <s>Kāpiṣṭha</s>, lotus-pink. In <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Mahāśukra</s>, <s>Śatāra</s>, and <s>Sahasrāra</s>, lotus-pink and white. In <s>Ānata</s> and above, white. And therein, in the <s>Anudiśa</s> and the higher [mansions], the <s>leśyā</s> is supremely white. How is the mixed [assignment] understood from the <s>sūtra</s>, which does not explicitly state it? Through association, as in common usage. Just as [in the statement] 'those with umbrellas go,' the [term] 'umbrella' applies even to those without umbrellas. Similarly here, the mention of one also includes the other [in the mixed pairs]. How is this meaning derived from the <s>sūtra</s>? It is said: the connection is made thus — for two <s>kalpa</s>-pairs, yellow <s>leśyā</s>; for <s>Sānatkumāra</s> and <s>Māhendra</s>, lotus-pink is not intended [to be excluded]. For the three <s>kalpa</s>-pairs beginning with <s>Brahmaloka</s>, lotus-pink <s>leśyā</s>; for <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Mahāśukra</s>, white is not intended [to be excluded]. For the remaining ones beginning with <s>Śatāra</s>, white <s>leśyā</s>; lotus-pink is not intended [to be excluded]. Thus there is no defect.

§ 485. Yellow, lotus-pink, and white — these are <s>pīta-padma-śukla</s>. Those who have yellow, lotus-pink, and white <s>leśyā</s> are <s>pīta-padma-śukla-leśyāḥ</s>. How is the shortening [of the compound explained]? It is an <s>Autarapadika</s> (final-member) compound. As [the rule states]:

children.text: § 486. āha kalpopapannā ity uktaṃ tattredaṃ na jñāyate ke kalpā ity attrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 486. He says: '<s>Kalpopapanna</s>' (born in a <s>kalpa</s>) has been stated; but it is not known which are the <s>kalpas</s>. To this it is said —

children.text: prāggraiveyakebhyaḥ kalpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>kalpas</s> are [those] below the <s>Graiveyakas</s>.

children.text: § 487. idaṃ na jñāyate ita ārabhya kalpā bhavantīti saudharmādigrahaṇam anuvartate. tenāyam artho labhyate — saudharmādayaḥ prāggraiveyakebhyaḥ kalpā iti. pāriśeṣyāditare kalpātītā iti.
children.translated_text: § 487. It is not known from where the <s>kalpas</s> begin — the mention of '<s>Saudharma</s> and the rest' continues. Thus this meaning is obtained: '<s>Saudharma</s> and the rest, up to the <s>Graiveyakas</s>, are the <s>kalpas</s>.' By residual inference, the others are '<s>kalpātīta</s>' (beyond the <s>kalpas</s>).

children.text: § 488. laukāntikā devā vaimānikāḥ santaḥ kva gṛhyante? kalpopapanneṣu. katham iti ced ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 488. The <s>Laukāntika</s> gods, being <s>Vaimānika</s>, where are they classified? Among the <s>kalpopapanna</s> (heaven-born). If asked how, it is said —

children.text: brahmalokālayā laukāntikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Laukāntika</s> [gods] have their abode in <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: § 489. etya tasmin līyanta iti ālaya āvāsaḥ. brahmaloka ālayo yeṣām te brahmalokālayā laukāntikā devā veditavyāḥ. yady evaṃ sarveṣāṃ brahmalokālayānāṃ devānāṃ laukāntikatvaṃ prasaktam. anvarthasaṃjñāgrahaṇād adoṣaḥ. brahmaloko lokaḥ, tasyānto lokāntaḥ, tasmin bhavā laukāntikā iti na sarveṣāṃ grahaṇam. teṣām hi vimānāni brahmalokasyānteṣu sthitāni. athavā janmajarāmaraṇākīrṇo lokaḥ saṃsāraḥ, tasyānto lokāntaḥ. lokānte bhavā laukāntikāḥ. te sarve parītasaṃsārāḥ, tataś cyutā ekaṃ garbhāvāsaṃ prāpya parinirvāsyantīti.
children.translated_text: § 489. '<s>Ālaya</s>' means abode — [the place] where, having arrived, they reside. Those whose abode is <s>Brahmaloka</s> are '<s>Brahmalokālaya</s>' — the <s>Laukāntika</s> gods should be understood thus. If so, all gods whose abode is <s>Brahmaloka</s> would be <s>Laukāntikas</s>? There is no defect, because the term is taken as a meaningful name (<s>anvarthasaṃjñā</s>). <s>Brahmaloka</s> is a '<s>loka</s>' (world); its end is '<s>lokānta</s>'; those who dwell at the end of the world are <s>Laukāntikas</s> — so not all are included. For their mansions are situated at the extremities of <s>Brahmaloka</s>. Alternatively, '<s>loka</s>' means <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), which is filled with birth, old age, and death; its end is '<s>lokānta</s>.' Those who exist at the end of the world [of transmigration] are <s>Laukāntikas</s>. They have all completed their [rounds of] transmigration; having fallen from there and attaining one [more] womb-existence, they will attain final liberation (<s>parinirvāṇa</s>).

children.text: § 490. teṣāṃ sāmānyenopadiṣṭānāṃ bhedadarśanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 490. To show the divisions of those [<s>Laukāntikas</s>] who have been generally described, he says —

children.text: sārasvatādityavahnyaruṇagardatoyatuṣitāvyābādhāriṣṭāś ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sārasvata</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Vahni</s>, <s>Aruṇa</s>, <s>Gardatoya</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Avyābādha</s>, and <s>Ariṣṭa</s> — and [others].

children.text: § 491. kva ime sārasvatādayaḥ? aṣṭāsv api pūrvottarādiṣu dikṣu yathākramam ete sārasvatādayo devagaṇā veditavyāḥ. tad yathā — pūrvottarakoṇe sārasvatavimānam, pūrvasyāṃ diśi ādityavimānam, pūrvadakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi vahnivimānam, dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi aruṇavimānam, dakṣiṇāparakoṇe gardatoyavimānam, aparasyāṃ diśi tuṣitavimānam, uttarāparasyāṃ diśi avyābādhavimānam, uttarsyāṃ diśi ariṣṭavimānam. ‘ca’ śabdasamuccitās teṣām antareṣu dvau devagaṇau. tad yathā — sārasvatādityāntare agnyābhasūryābhāḥ. ādityasya ca vahneś cāntare candrābhasatyābhāḥ. vahnyaruṇāntarāle śreyaskarakṣemaṃkarāḥ. aruṇagardatoyāntarāle vṛṣabheṣṭakāmacārāḥ gardatoyatuṣitamadhye nirmāṇarajodigantarakṣitāḥ. tuṣitāvyābādhamadhye ātmarakṣitasarvarakṣitāḥ. avyābādhāriṣṭāntarāle marudvasavaḥ. ariṣṭasārasvatāntarāle aśvaviśvāḥ. sarve ete svatantrāḥ; hīnādhikatvābhāvāt, viṣayarativirahād devarṣayaḥ, itareṣāṃ devānām arcanīyāḥ, caturdaśapūrvadharāḥ tīrthakaraniṣkramaṇapratibodhanaparā veditavyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 491. Where are these <s>Sārasvata</s> and the rest? In the eight directions — northeast and so on — these divine groups from <s>Sārasvata</s> onward should be understood in order. Thus: in the northeast corner is the <s>Sārasvata</s> mansion; in the eastern direction, the <s>Āditya</s> mansion; in the southeast, the <s>Vahni</s> mansion; in the southern direction, the <s>Aruṇa</s> mansion; in the southwest corner, the <s>Gardatoya</s> mansion; in the western direction, the <s>Tuṣita</s> mansion; in the northwest, the <s>Avyābādha</s> mansion; in the northern direction, the <s>Ariṣṭa</s> mansion. The particle '<s>ca</s>' includes [additional] groups between them — two divine groups between each. Thus: between <s>Sārasvata</s> and <s>Āditya</s> are <s>Agnyābha</s> and <s>Sūryābha</s>; between <s>Āditya</s> and <s>Vahni</s> are <s>Candrābha</s> and <s>Satyābha</s>; between <s>Vahni</s> and <s>Aruṇa</s> are <s>Śreyaskara</s> and <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>; between <s>Aruṇa</s> and <s>Gardatoya</s> are <s>Vṛṣabha</s> and <s>Iṣṭakāmacāra</s>; between <s>Gardatoya</s> and <s>Tuṣita</s> are <s>Nirmāṇa</s>, <s>Rajas</s>, and <s>Digantarakṣita</s>; between <s>Tuṣita</s> and <s>Avyābādha</s> are <s>Ātmarakṣita</s> and <s>Sarvarakṣita</s>; between <s>Avyābādha</s> and <s>Ariṣṭa</s> are <s>Marut</s> and <s>Vasu</s>; between <s>Ariṣṭa</s> and <s>Sārasvata</s> are <s>Aśva</s> and <s>Viśva</s>. All of these are independent [of one another]; since there is no superiority or inferiority among them, and since they are free from attachment to sense-pleasures, they are [like] divine sages (<s>devarṣi</s>), worthy of worship by other gods, knowers of the fourteen <s>Pūrvas</s> (ancient texts), and devoted to the renunciation, awakening, and [teaching] of <s>Tīrthaṅkaras</s>.

children.text: § 492. āha, uktā laukāntikās tataś cyutā ekaṃ garbhavāsam avāpya nirvāsyantīty uktāḥ. kim evam anyesv api nirvāṇaprāptikālavibhāgo vidyate. ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 492. He says: The <s>Laukāntikas</s> have been described — [it was said that] having fallen from there and attaining one womb-existence, they will attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Is there similarly a division of the time of attaining <s>nirvāṇa</s> for others too? To this he says —

children.text: vijayādiṣu dvicaramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In [the mansions of] <s>Vijaya</s> and the like, [the beings have] two final [bodies].

children.text: § 493. ‘ādi’ śabdaḥ prakārārthe vartate, tena vijayavaijantajayantāparājitānudiśavimānānām iṣṭānāṃ grahaṇaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati. kaḥ punar atra prakāraḥ. ahamindratve sati samyagdṛṣṭyupapādaḥ. sarvārthasiddhiprasaṅga iti cet. na; tesāṃ paramotkṛṣṭatvāt, anvarthasaṇjñāta ekacaramatvasiddheh. caramatvaṃ dehasya manuṣyabhavāpekṣayā. dvau caramau dehau yeṣām te dvicaramāḥ. vijayādibhyaś cyutā apratipatitasamyaktvā manuṣyeṣūtpadya saṃyamam ārādya punar vijayādiṣūtpadya tataś cyutāḥ punar manuṣyabhavam avāpya siddyantīti dvicaramadehatvam.
children.translated_text: § 493. The word '<s>ādi</s>' (and the like) is used in the sense of 'variety'; thereby the inclusion of the desired [mansions] — <s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Vaijayanta</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, <s>Aparājita</s>, and the <s>Anudiśa</s> mansions — is accomplished. What then is the 'variety'? [It is:] being born with right faith through spontaneous generation while having the status of an <s>Ahamindra</s>. [Objection:] This should [also] apply to <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>? No, because those [in <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>] are supremely exalted, and since the meaningful name establishes that they have [only] one final [body]. 'Final' refers to the body, in relation to human existence. Those who have two final bodies are '<s>dvicarama</s>.' Having fallen from <s>Vijaya</s> and the like without losing their right faith, they are born among humans, undertake restraint, then are born again in <s>Vijaya</s> and the like, and having fallen from there, again attaining human existence, they achieve liberation (<s>siddhi</s>) — thus they have two final bodies.

children.text: § 494. āha, jivasyāudayikeṣu bhāveṣu tiryagyonigatir audayakīty uktaṃ, punaś ca sthitau ‘tiryagyonijānāṃ ca’ iti. tatra na jñāyate ke tiryagyonayaḥ. ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 494. He says: Among the <s>audayika</s> (fruition-born) states of the soul, the animal-origin destiny (<s>tiryagyoni-gati</s>) was mentioned as <s>audayika</s>, and again in the context of duration, 'of those born from animal origins.' But it is not known who the animal-origin [beings] are. To this it is said —

children.text: aupapādikamanuṣyebhyaḥ śeṣās tiryagyonayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those other than spontaneously-generated beings and humans are <s>tiryagyonis</s> (animal-origin beings).

children.text: § 495. aupapādikā uktā devanārakāḥ. manuṣyāś ca nirdiṣṭāḥ ‘prāṅmānuṣottarān manuṣyāh’ iti. ebhyo ’nye saṃsāriṇo jīvāḥ śeṣās te tiryagyonayo veditavyāḥ. teṣāṃ tiraścāṃ devādīnām iva kṣetravibhāgaḥ punar nirdeṣṭavyaḥ? sarvalokavyāpitvāt tesāṃ kṣetravibhāgo noktaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 495. The <s>aupapādikas</s> (spontaneously-generated) have been described — they are gods and hell-beings. Humans too have been specified: 'humans [exist] before [i.e., south of] the northern <s>Mānuṣottara</s> [mountain].' The remaining transmigrating souls other than these should be understood as <s>tiryagyonis</s>. Should a territorial division of those animals be stated, as for gods and others? Since they pervade the entire universe, their territorial division is not stated.

children.text: § 496. āha, sthitir uktā nārakāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ tiraścāṃ ca. devānāṃ noktā. tasyāṃ vyaktavyāyām ādāv uddiṣṭānāṃ bhavanavāsināṃ sthitipratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 496. He says: The lifespan has been stated for hell-beings, humans, and animals. It has not been stated for gods. When that [lifespan] needs to be explained, to establish the lifespan of the <s>Bhavanavāsī</s> (mansion-dwelling) gods mentioned first, he says —

children.text: sthitir asuranāgasuparṇadvīpaśeṣāṇāṃ sāgaropamatripalyopmārddhahīnamitā  ||
children.translated_text: The lifespan of <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Suparṇas</s>, <s>Dvīpas</s>, and the remaining [classes] is measured as [one] <s>sāgaropama</s> diminished by half of three <s>palyopamas</s>.

children.text: § 497. asurādīnāṃ sāgaropmādibhir yathākramam atrābhisaṃbandho veditavyaḥ. iyaṃ sthitir utkṛṣṭā jaghanyāpy uttaratra vakṣyate. tad yathā asurāṇāṃ sāgaropamā sthitiḥ. nāgānāṃ tripalyopamāni sthitiḥ. suparṇānāṃ arddhatṛtīyāni. dvīpānām dve. śeṣāṇāṃ ṣaṇṇām adhyarddhapalyopamam.
children.translated_text: § 497. The connection of the <s>Asuras</s> and others with <s>sāgaropamas</s> (ocean-measured periods) and so forth should be understood here in sequence. This is the maximum lifespan; the minimum will also be stated later. That is: the lifespan of the <s>Asuras</s> is one <s>sāgaropama</s>. The lifespan of the <s>Nāgas</s> is three <s>palyopamas</s>. That of the <s>Suparṇas</s> is two and a half. That of the <s>Dvīpas</s> is two. For the remaining six, it is one and a half <s>palyopamas</s>.

children.text: § 498. adyadevanikāyasthityabhidhānād anantaraṃ vyantarajyotiṣkasthitivacane kramaprāpte sati tadullaṅghya vaimānikānāṃ sthitir ucyate. kutaḥ? tayor uttaratra laghunopāyena sthitivacanāt. teṣu cādāv uddiṣṭayo kalpayoḥ sthitividhānārtham aha —
children.translated_text: § 498. Having stated the lifespans of the first class of deities, when it was the turn to state the lifespans of the <s>Vyantaras</s> and <s>Jyotiṣkas</s> in sequence, passing over them, the lifespan of the <s>Vaimānikas</s> (celestial beings with aerial vehicles) is stated. Why? Because the lifespans of those two will be stated later by a brief method. And among these, in order to establish the lifespan for the first two <s>kalpas</s> (heavenly realms) mentioned, he says —

children.text: saudharmaiśānayoḥ sāgaropame adhike ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Saudharma</s> and <s>Aiśāna</s>, <s>sāgaropamas</s> with excess.

children.text: § 499. ‘sāgaropame’ iti dvivacananirdeśād dvitvagatiḥ. ‘adhike’ ity ayam adhikāraḥ. ā kutaḥ? ā sahasrārāt. idaṃ tu kuto jñāyate? uttaratra ‘tu’ śabdagrahaṇāt. tena saudharmaiśānayor devānāṃ dve sāgaropame sātireke pratyetvaye.
children.translated_text: § 499. Since '<s>sāgaropame</s>' is stated in the dual number, the number understood is two. 'With excess' is the governing term. Up to what point? Up to <s>Sahasrāra</s>. But how is this known? From the use of the word 'tu' (but) in the subsequent <s>sūtra</s>. Thus, the lifespan of the gods in <s>Saudharma</s> and <s>Aiśāna</s> is two <s>sāgaropamas</s> with some excess, in each case.

children.text: § 500. uttarayoḥ sthitiviśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 500. In order to establish the specific lifespan of the next two, he says —

children.text: sānatkumāramāhendrayoḥ sapta ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Sānatkumāra</s> and <s>Māhendra</s>, seven.

children.text: § 501. anayoḥ kalpayor devānāṃ saptasāgaropamāṇi sādhikāni utkṛṣṭā sthitiḥ.
children.translated_text: § 501. The maximum lifespan of the gods in these two <s>kalpas</s> is seven <s>sāgaropamas</s> with excess.

children.text: § 502. brahmalokādiṣv acyutāvasāneṣu sthitiviśeṣapratipattyartham āha
children.translated_text: § 502. In order to establish the specific lifespans in <s>Brahmaloka</s> and the subsequent realms up to <s>Acyuta</s>, he says —

children.text: trisaptanavaikādaśatrayodaśapañcadaśabhir adhikāni tu ||
children.translated_text: With excess of three, seven, nine, eleven, thirteen, and fifteen respectively, but —

children.text: § 503. ‘sapta’ grahaṇaṃ prakṛtam. tasyeha tryādibhir nirdiṣṭair abhisaṃbandho veditavyaḥ. sapta tribhir adhikāni, sapta saptabhir adhikānīty ādiḥ. dvayor dvayor abhisaṃbandho veditavyaḥ. ‘tu’ śabdo viśeṣaṇārthaḥ. kiṃ viśinaṣṭi? ‘adhika’ śabdo ’nuvartamānaś caturbhir abhisaṃbadhyate nottarābhyām ity ayam artho viśiṣyate. tenāyam artho bhavati — brahmalokabrahmottarayor daśasāgaropamāṇi sādhikāni. lāntavakāpiṣṭhayoś caturdaśasāgaropamāṇi sādhikāni. śukramahāśukrayoḥ ṣoḍaśasāgaropamāṇi sādhikāni. śatārasahasrārayor aṣṭādaśasāgaropamāṇi sādhikāni. ānataprāṇatayor viṃśatisāgaropamāṇi. āraṇācyutayor dvāviṃśatisāgaropamāṇi.
children.translated_text: § 503. The term 'seven' is carried forward from the previous context. Its connection here should be understood with the numbers three and so forth as specified. Seven plus three with excess, seven plus seven with excess, and so on. The connection should be understood for pairs of two. The word 'tu' (but) serves as a qualifier. What does it qualify? The meaning qualified is that the word 'excess' which continues applies to the first four pairs but not to the last two. Thus the meaning is: for <s>Brahmaloka</s> and <s>Brahmottara</s>, ten <s>sāgaropamas</s> with excess; for <s>Lāntava</s> and <s>Kāpiṣṭha</s>, fourteen <s>sāgaropamas</s> with excess; for <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Mahāśukra</s>, sixteen <s>sāgaropamas</s> with excess; for <s>Śatāra</s> and <s>Sahasrāra</s>, eighteen <s>sāgaropamas</s> with excess; for <s>Ānata</s> and <s>Prāṇata</s>, twenty <s>sāgaropamas</s>; for <s>Āraṇa</s> and <s>Acyuta</s>, twenty-two <s>sāgaropamas</s>.

children.text: § 504. tata ūrdhvaṃ sthitiviśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 504. In order to establish the specific lifespans above that, he says —

children.text: āraṇācyutād ūrdhvam ekaikena navasu graiveyakeṣu vijayādiṣu sarvārthasiddhau ca ||
children.translated_text: Above <s>Āraṇa</s>-<s>Acyuta</s>, increasing by one each in the nine <s>Graiveyakas</s>, in <s>Vijaya</s> and the rest, and in <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>.

children.text: § 505. ‘adhika’ grahaṇam anuvartate. tenehābhisaṃbandho veditavyaḥ. ekaikenādhikānīti. ‘nava’ grahaṇaṃ kim artham? pratyekam ekaikam adhikam iti jñāpanārtham. itarathā hi graiveyakeṣv ekam evādhikaṃ syāt. vijayādiṣv iti ‘ādi’ śabdasya prakārārthatvād anudiśānām api grahaṇam. sarvārthasiddhes tu pṛthaggrahaṇaṃ jaghanyābhāvapratipādanārtham. tenāyam arthaḥ, adhograiveyakeṣu prathame trayoviṃśatiḥ, dvitīye caturviṃśatiḥ, tṛtīye pañcaviṃśatiḥ. madhyamagraiveyakeṣu prathame ṣaḍviṃśatiḥ dvitīye saptaviṃśatiḥ tṛtīye ’ṣṭāviṃśatiḥ. uparimagraiveyakeṣu prathame ekonatriṃśad dvitīye triṃśat tṛtīye ekatriṃśat. anudiśavimāneṣu dvātriṃśat. vijayādiṣu trayas triṃśat sāgaropamāṇy utkṛṣṭā sthitiḥ. sarvārthasiddhau trayas triṃśad eveti.
children.translated_text: § 505. The term 'excess' continues and should be understood in connection here — with excess of one each. What is the purpose of the term 'nine'? To indicate that one is added separately for each. Otherwise, there would be only one addition for all the <s>Graiveyakas</s> collectively. 'In <s>Vijaya</s> and the rest' — since the word 'ādi' (and the rest) indicates things of the same kind, the <s>Anudiśa</s> heavens are also included. The separate mention of <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s> is to indicate the absence of a minimum lifespan there. Thus the meaning is: in the lower <s>Graiveyakas</s>, the first has twenty-three, the second twenty-four, the third twenty-five; in the middle <s>Graiveyakas</s>, the first has twenty-six, the second twenty-seven, the third twenty-eight; in the upper <s>Graiveyakas</s>, the first has twenty-nine, the second thirty, the third thirty-one; in the <s>Anudiśa</s> heavens, thirty-two; in <s>Vijaya</s> and the rest, thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> as the maximum lifespan; in <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>, it is exactly thirty-three.

children.text: § 506. nirdiṣṭotkṛṣṭasthitikeṣu deveṣu jaghanyasthitipratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 506. In order to establish the minimum lifespan for the gods whose maximum lifespans have been stated, he says —

children.text: aparā palyopamam adhikam ||
children.translated_text: The minimum is a <s>palyopama</s> with excess.

children.text: § 507. palyopamaṃ vyākhyātam. aparā jaghanyā sthitiḥ. palyopamaṃ sādhikam. keṣām? saudharmaiśānīyānām. kathaṃ gamyate? ‘parataḥ parataḥ’ ity uttaratra vakṣyamāṇātvāt.
children.translated_text: § 507. <s>Palyopama</s> has been explained. The minimum lifespan is a <s>palyopama</s> with excess. For whom? For those of <s>Saudharma</s> and <s>Aiśāna</s>. How is this understood? Because it will be stated later 'from the next higher, from the next higher.'

children.text: § 508. tata ūrdhvaṃ jaghanyasthitipratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 508. In order to establish the minimum lifespan above that, he says —

children.text: parataḥ parataḥ pūrvāpūrvā ’nantarā ||
children.translated_text: From the next higher, from the next higher, the preceding maximum in succession.

children.text: § 509. parasmin deśe parataḥ. vīpsāyāṃ dvitvam. ‘pūrva’ śabdasyāpi. ‘adhika’ grahaṇam anuvartate. tenaivam abhisaṃbandhaḥ kriyate — saudharmaiśānayor dve sāgaropame sādhike ukte, te sādhike sānatkumāramāhendrayor jaghanyā sthitiḥ. sānatkumāramāhendrayoḥ parā sthitiḥ saptasāgaropamāṇi sādhikāni, tāni sādhikāni brahmabrahmottarayor jaghanyā sthitir ity ādi.
children.translated_text: § 509. 'From the next higher' means in the next region; the repetition indicates distributive application. The word 'preceding' is also repeated. The term 'excess' continues. Thus the connection is made as follows: for <s>Saudharma</s> and <s>Aiśāna</s>, two <s>sāgaropamas</s> with excess have been stated as the maximum; that same amount with excess is the minimum lifespan in <s>Sānatkumāra</s> and <s>Māhendra</s>. The maximum lifespan in <s>Sānatkumāra</s> and <s>Māhendra</s> is seven <s>sāgaropamas</s> with excess; that same amount with excess is the minimum lifespan in <s>Brahma</s> and <s>Brahmottara</s>, and so on.

children.text: § 510. nārakāṇām utkṛṣṭā sthitir uktā. jaghanyāṃ sūtre ’nupāttām aprakṛtām api laghunopāyena pratipādayitum icchann āha —
children.translated_text: § 510. The maximum lifespan of hell-beings has been stated. Wishing to establish the minimum lifespan, which though not under discussion in the <s>sūtra</s>, can be taught by a brief method, he says —

children.text: nārakāṇāṃ ca dvitīyādiṣu ||
children.translated_text: And for hell-beings, in the second and subsequent ones.

children.text: § 511. ‘ca’ śabdaḥ kim arthaḥ? prakṛtasamuccayārthaḥ. kiṃ ca prakṛtam? ‘parataḥ parataḥ pūrvāpūrvā ’nantarā’ aparā sthitir iti. tenāyam artho labhyate — ratnaprabhāyāṃ nārakāṇāṃ parā sthitir ekaṃ sāgaropamam. sā śarkarāprabhāyām jaghanyā. śarkarāprabhāyām utkṛṣṭā sthitis trīṇi sāgaropamāṇi. sā vālukāprabhāyāṃ jaghanyety ādi.
children.translated_text: § 511. What is the purpose of the word 'ca' (and)? It serves to conjoin with what is under discussion. What is under discussion? 'From the next higher, from the next higher, the preceding maximum in succession' as the minimum lifespan. Thus the meaning obtained is: the maximum lifespan of hell-beings in <s>Ratnaprabhā</s> is one <s>sāgaropama</s>; that becomes the minimum in <s>Śarkarāprabhā</s>. The maximum lifespan in <s>Śarkarāprabhā</s> is three <s>sāgaropamas</s>; that becomes the minimum in <s>Vālukāprabhā</s>, and so on.

children.text: § 512. evaṃ dvitīyādiṣu jaghanyā sthitir uktā. prathamāyāṃ kā jaghanyeti tatpradarśanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 512. Thus the minimum lifespan in the second and subsequent hells has been stated. What is the minimum in the first? To show that, he says —

children.text: daśavarṣasahasrāṇi prathamāyām ||
children.translated_text: Ten thousand years in the first.

children.text: § 513. aparā sthitir ity anuvartate. ratnaprabhāyāṃ daśavarṣasahasrāṇi aparā sthitir veditavyā.
children.translated_text: § 513. The term 'minimum lifespan' continues. The minimum lifespan in <s>Ratnaprabhā</s> should be understood as ten thousand years.

children.text: § 514. atha bhavanavāsināṃ kā jaghanyā sthitir ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 514. Now, what is the minimum lifespan of the <s>Bhavanavāsins</s> (residential gods)? To this he says —

children.text: bhavaneṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: And in the residences.

children.text: § 515. ‘ca’ śabda kim arthaḥ?
prakṛtasamuccayārthaḥ. tena bhavanavāsināṃ aparā sthitir daśavarṣasahasrāṇīty abhisaṃbadhyate.
children.translated_text: It serves to conjoin with what is under discussion. Thus it is connected as: the minimum lifespan of the <s>Bhavanavāsins</s> is ten thousand years.
§ 515. What is the purpose of the word 'ca' (and)?

children.text: § 516. vyantarāṇāṃ tarhi kā jaghanyā sthitir ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 516. Then what is the minimum lifespan of the <s>Vyantaras</s> (peripatetic gods)? To this he says —

children.text: vyantarāṇāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And of the <s>Vyantaras</s>.

children.text: § 517. ‘ca’ śabdaḥ prakṛtasamuccayārthaḥ. tena vyantarāṇāṃ aparā sthitir daśavarṣasahasrāṇīty avagamyate.
children.translated_text: § 517. The word 'ca' (and) serves to conjoin with what is under discussion. Thus it is understood that the minimum lifespan of the <s>Vyantaras</s> is ten thousand years.

children.text: § 518. athaiṣāṃ parā sthitiḥ kā ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 518. Now, what is their maximum lifespan? To this it is said —

children.text: parā palyopamam adhikam ||
children.translated_text: The maximum is a <s>palyopama</s> with excess.

children.text: § 519. parā utkṛṣtā sthitir vyantarāṇāṃ palyopamam adhikam.
children.translated_text: § 519. The maximum lifespan of the <s>Vyantaras</s> is a <s>palyopama</s> with excess.

children.text: § 520. idānīṃ jyotiṣkāṇāṃ parā sthitir vaktavyety ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 520. Now, the maximum lifespan of the <s>Jyotiṣkas</s> (stellar gods) needs to be stated, and so he says —

children.text: jyotiṣkāṇāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And of the <s>Jyotiṣkas</s>.

children.text: § 521. ‘ca’ śabdaḥ prakṛtasamuccayārthaḥ. tenaivam abhisaṃbandhaḥ. jyotiṣkāṇāṃ parā sthitiḥ palyopamam adhikam iti.
children.translated_text: § 521. The word 'ca' (and) serves to conjoin with what is under discussion. Thus the connection is: the maximum lifespan of the <s>Jyotiṣkas</s> is a <s>palyopama</s> with excess.

children.text: § 522. athāparā kiyatīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 522. Now, how much is the minimum? To this he says —

children.text: tadaṣṭabhāgo ’parā ||
children.translated_text: One-eighth of that is the minimum.

children.text: § 523. tasya palyopamasyāṣṭabhāgo jyotiṣkāṇāṃ aparā sthitir ity arthaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 523. One-eighth of that <s>palyopama</s> is the minimum lifespan of the <s>Jyotiṣkas</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: § 524. atha laukāntikānāṃ viśeṣoktānāṃ sthitiviśeṣo noktaḥ. sa kiyān ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 524. Now, the specific lifespan of the <s>Laukāntikas</s> (world-end gods), who have been specifically mentioned, has not been stated. How much is it? To this it is said —

children.text: laukāntikānām aṣṭau sāgaropamāṇi sarveṣām ||
children.translated_text: For the <s>Laukāntikas</s>, eight <s>sāgaropamas</s> for all of them.

children.text: § 525. aviśiṣṭāḥ sarve te śuklaleśyāḥ pañcahastotsedhaśarīrāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 525. They are all alike — all having <s>śuklaleśyā</s> (white soul-coloration), with bodies five <s>hastas</s> (cubits) in height.

children.text: iti tattvārthavṛttau sarvārthasiddhisaṃjñikāyāṃ caturtho ’dhyāyaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter of the <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>, the commentary on the <s>Tattvārthasūtra</s>. || 4 ||

children.text: atha pañcamo ’dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins the fifth chapter.

children.text: § 526. idānīṃ samyagdarśanasya viṣayabhāvenopakṣipteṣu jīvādiṣu jīvapadārtho vyākhyātaḥ. athājīvapadārtho vicāraprāptasya saṃjñābhedasaṃkīrtanārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 526. Now, among <s>jīva</s> (soul) and other categories introduced as objects of right faith, the <s>jīva</s> category has been explained. Now, in order to state the classification of names for the <s>ajīva</s> (non-soul) category, which is next in order of investigation, this is said —

children.text: ajīvakāyā dharmādharmākāśapudgalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>ajīva</s> (non-soul) categories are <s>dharma</s> (medium of motion), <s>adharma</s> (medium of rest), <s>ākāśa</s> (space), and <s>pudgala</s> (matter).

children.text: § 527. ‘kāya’ śabdaḥ śarīre vyutpāditaḥ. ihopacārād adhyāropyate. kuta upacāraḥ? yathā śarīraṃ pudgaladravyapracayātmakaṃ tathā dharmādiṣv api pradeśpracāyāpekṣayā kāyā iva kāyā iti. ajīvāś ca te kāyāś ca ajīvakāyāḥ
viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyeṇeti
children.translated_text: the qualifier being compounded with the qualified —

children.text: vṛttiḥ. nanu ca nīlotpalādiṣu vyabhicāre sati viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyayogaḥ. ihāpi vyabhicārayogo ’sti. ajīvaśabdo ’kāye kāle ’pi vartate, kāyo ’pi jīve. kim arthaḥ kāyaśabdaḥ? pradeśabahutvajñāpanārthaḥ. dharmādīnāṃ pradeśā bahava iti. nanu ca ‘asaṃkhyeyāḥ pradeśā dharmādharmaikajīvānām’ ity anenaiva pradeśabahutvaṃ jñāpitam. satyam idam. paraṃ kintv asmin vidhau sati tadavadhāraṇaṃ vijñāyate, asaṃkhyeyāḥ pradeśā na saṃkhyeyā nāpy anantā iti. kālasya pradeśapracayābhāvajñāpanārthaṃ ca iha ‘kāya’ grahaṇam. kālo vakṣyate. tasya pradeśapratiṣedhārthaṃ iha ‘kāya’ grahaṇam. yathā ’ṇoḥ pradeśamatratvād dvitīyādayo ’sya pradeśā na santīty apradeśo ’ṇuḥ, tathā kālaparamāṇur apy ekapradeśatvād apradeśa iti. teṣāṃ dharmādīnāṃ ‘ajīva’ iti sāmānyasaṃjñā jīvalakṣanābhāvamukhena pravṛttā. ‘dharmādharmākāśapudgalāḥ’ iti viśeṣasaṃjñāḥ sāmayikyaḥ.
children.translated_text: this is the grammatical formation. But is there not a deviation as in cases like 'blue lotus' and the like, where a qualifier-qualified relation holds? Here too such deviation exists. The word '<s>ajīva</s>' also applies to <s>kāla</s> (time), which is not a <s>kāya</s>, and '<s>kāya</s>' also applies to <s>jīva</s> (soul). What is the purpose of the word '<s>kāya</s>'? To indicate multiplicity of spatial points — that <s>dharma</s> and the rest have many <s>pradeśas</s> (spatial points). But is not the multiplicity of spatial points already indicated by the statement 'the <s>pradeśas</s> of <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and individual <s>jīva</s> are innumerable'? True, this is so. However, given this rule, the precise determination is understood — that the <s>pradeśas</s> are innumerable, neither countable nor infinite. And the term '<s>kāya</s>' is used here to indicate the absence of an aggregation of spatial points in <s>kāla</s> (time). <s>Kāla</s> will be discussed later. The term '<s>kāya</s>' is used here to negate spatial points for it. Just as an <s>aṇu</s> (atom), being of the measure of a single spatial point, has no second or further spatial points and is therefore without spatial extension, so too a <s>kāla-paramāṇu</s> (time-atom), being of a single spatial point, is without spatial extension. The general designation '<s>ajīva</s>' (non-soul) for <s>dharma</s> and the rest is applied by way of the absence of the defining characteristics of <s>jīva</s> (soul). '<s>Dharmādharmākāśapudgalāḥ</s>' — these are specific designations that are conventional.

§ 527. The word '<s>kāya</s>' (body) is etymologically derived in the sense of a physical body. Here it is metaphorically applied through figurative usage. Whence the figurative usage? Just as a physical body consists of an aggregation of material substances (<s>pudgala-dravya</s>), so also with respect to <s>dharma</s> and the rest, by analogy with the aggregation of spatial points (<s>pradeśas</s>), they are called '<s>kāyas</s>' as if they were bodies. '<s>Ajīvakāyāḥ</s>' — they are non-souls and they are bodies, hence non-soul bodies,

children.text: § 528. atrāha, ‘sarvadravyaparyāyeṣu kevalasya’ ity evam ādiṣu dravyāny uktāni, kāni tānīty ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 528. Here one asks: substances have been mentioned in passages such as 'of all substances and modes, the omniscient one...' and so forth — what are those? It is said —

children.text: dravyāṇi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dravyāṇi</s> (Substances).
