children.text: § 529. yathā svaṃ paryāyair drūyante dravanti vā tāni iti dravyāṇi. dravyatvayogād dravyam iti cet. na; ubhayāsiddeḥ. yathā daṇḍadaṇḍinor yogo bhavati pṛthaksiddhayoḥ, na ca tathā dravyadravyatve pṛthaksiddhe staḥ. yady apṛthaksiddhayor api yogaḥ syād ākāśakusumasya prakṛtapruṣasya dvitīyaśirasaś ca yogaḥ syād iti. atha pṛhtaksiddhir abhupagamyate, dravyatvakalpanā nirarthikā. guṇasamudāyo dravyam iti cet? tatrāpi guṇānāṃ samudāyasya ca bhedābhāve tadvyapadeśo nopapadyate. bhedābhyupagame ca pūrvokta eva doṣaḥ. nanu guṇān dravanti guṇair vā drūyanta iti vigrahe ’pi sa eva doṣa iti cet? na; kathaṃcid bhedābhedopapattes tadvyapadeśasiddhiḥ. vyatirekeṇānupalabdher abhedaḥ saṃjñālakṣaṇaprayojanādibhedād bheda iti. prakṛtā dharmādayo bahavas tatsāmānādhikaraṇyād bahutvanirdeśaḥ. syād etat saṃkhyānuvṛttivatpulliṅgānuvṛttir api prāpnoti. naiṣa doṣaḥ; āviṣṭaliṅgāḥ śabdā na kadācil liṅgaṃ vyabhicaranti. ato dharmādayo dravyāṇi bhavantīti.
children.translated_text: § 529. They are called <s>dravyāṇi</s> (substances) because they are characterized (<s>drūyante</s>) by their own modes (<s>paryāyas</s>), or because they flow (<s>dravanti</s>). If one objects that something is a substance because it possesses substance-ness (<s>dravyatva</s>) — no, because both terms are unestablished. Just as the relation between a stick and the stick-bearer requires two independently established entities, substance and substance-ness are not independently established as two things. If one argues that a relation can hold between non-independently established things, then there would be a relation between a sky-flower and a naturally hornless person, or a second head — which is absurd. If, however, their independent existence is accepted, then positing substance-ness becomes pointless. If one says substance is an aggregate of qualities — even there, if there is no difference between the qualities and their aggregate, the designation cannot be justified. And if a difference is accepted, the very same objection stated earlier applies. If one objects that the same fault arises with the etymological analysis 'they characterize qualities' or 'they are characterized by qualities' — no, because the designation is justified through the intelligibility of simultaneous difference and non-difference. Non-difference, because they are not apprehended as separate; difference, because of distinctions in name, definition, purpose, and so forth. The entities under discussion — <s>dharma</s> and the rest — are many, and the plural is used because of their co-referentiality. One might suggest that just as number agreement carries over, so should masculine gender agreement. This is not a fault; words with inherent grammatical gender never deviate from that gender. Therefore, <s>dharma</s> and the rest are <s>dravyāṇi</s> (substances).

children.text: § 530. anantaratvāc caturṇām eva dravyavyapadeśaprasaṃge ’dhyāropaṇārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 530. Since there is a risk that only four would be designated as substances due to their immediate proximity, this is said for the purpose of including additional ones —

children.text: jīvāś ca ||
children.translated_text: And <s>jīvas</s> (souls) also.

children.text: § 531. ‘jīva’ śabdo vyākhyātārthaḥ. bahutvanirdeśo vyākhyātabhedapratipattyarthaḥ. ‘ca’ śabdaḥ dravyasaṃjñānukarṣaṇārthaḥ jīvāś ca dravyāṇīti. evam etāni vakṣyamāṇena kālena saha ṣaḍ dravyāṇi bhavanti. nanu dravyasya lakṣaṇaṃ vakṣyate ‘guṇaparyayavad dravyam’ iti. tallakṣaṇayogād dharmādīnāṃ dravyavyapadeśo bhavati, nārthaḥ parigaṇanena? parigaṇanam avadhāraṇārtham. tenānyavādiparikalpitānāṃ pṛthivyādīnāṃ nivṛttiḥ kṛtā bhavati. katham? pṛthivyaptejovāyumanāṃsi pudgaladravye ’ntarbhavanti; rūparasagandhasparśavatvāt. vāyumanaso rūpādiyogābhava iti cet? na; vāyus tāvad rūpādimān; sparśatvād ghaṭādivat. cakṣurādikaraṇagrāhyatvābhāvād rūpādyabhāva iti cet? na; paramāṇvādiṣv atiprasaṅgaḥ syāt. āpo gandhavatyaḥ; sparśavatvāt pṛthivīvat. tejo ’pi rasagandhavad; rūpavattvāt tadvad eva. mano ’pi dvividhaṃ dravyamano bhāvamanaś ceti. tatra bhāvamano jñānam; tasya jīvaguṇatvād ātmany antarbhāvaḥ. dravyamanaś ca rūpādiyogāt pudgaladravyavikāraḥ. rūpādivan manaḥ; jñānopayogakaraṇatvāc cakṣurindriyavat. nanu amūrte ’pi śabde jñānopayogakaraṇatvadarśanād vyabhicārī hetur iti cet? na; tasya paudgalikatvān mūrtimattvopapatteḥ. nanu yathā paramāṇūnāṃ rūpādimatkāryadarśanād rūpādimattvaṃ na tathā vāyumanaso rūpādisatkāryaṃ dṛṣyate iti cet? na; teṣām api tadupapatteḥ. sarveṣāṃ paramāṇūnāṃ sarvarūpādimatkāryatvaprāptiyogatvābhyupagamāt. na ca kecit pārthivādijātiviśeṣayuktāḥ paramāṇavaḥ santi; jātisaṃkareṇārambhadarśanāt. diśo ’py ākāśe ’ntarbhāvaḥ, ādityodayādyapekṣayā ākāśapradeśapaṅktiṣu ita idam iti vyavahāropapatteḥ.
children.translated_text: § 531. The word '<s>jīva</s>' has already been explained. The plural number is for the purpose of understanding the divisions [already] explained. The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) serves to connect the term '<s>dravya</s>' (substance): '<s>jīvas</s> too are substances.' Thus, these, together with time (<s>kāla</s>) which will be mentioned [later], make six substances. [Objection:] But the definition of substance will be stated: 'that which possesses qualities and modes is substance.' By the applicability of that definition, <s>Dharma</s> etc. would be called substances—what need is there for enumeration? [Reply:] The enumeration is for the purpose of delimitation. By it, the [elements] fabricated by other schools—earth, water, etc.—are excluded. How? Earth, water, fire, air, and mind are included within the substance of <s>pudgala</s> (matter), because they possess color, taste, smell, and touch. [Objection:] Air and mind lack color etc.? [Reply:] No. Air, for its part, possesses color etc., because it has touch—like a pot. [Objection:] The absence of color etc. [in air and mind] is due to the absence of apprehension by the eye and other sense-organs? [Reply:] No, because that argument would overextend to atoms etc. [as well]. Water possesses smell, because it has touch—like earth. Fire too possesses taste and smell, because it possesses color—just like that [earth]. Mind too is twofold: physical mind (<s>dravyamanas</s>) and dispositional mind (<s>bhāvamanas</s>). Among these, the dispositional mind is knowledge; since it is a quality of the soul, it is included within the soul. And the physical mind, possessing color etc., is a modification of the substance <s>pudgala</s>. [Objection:] Mind is like color etc.? [Reply:] Because it is the instrument of knowledge-consciousness—like the eye-organ. [Objection:] Since the status of being an instrument of knowledge is observed even in sound, which is formless, the reason [given] is inconclusive? [Reply:] No, because sound too, being material (<s>paudgalika</s>), is appropriately possessed of form. [Objection:] Just as atoms are known to have form because their effects have color etc., so too of air and mind no such effects with color etc. are observed? [Reply:] No, because that is possible for them too, since it is accepted that all atoms have the capacity to produce effects possessing all [types of] color etc. And there are no atoms possessing specific species-characteristics such as 'earthen' etc., because [atoms of] mixed species are observed to combine [in production]. Directions too are included within space (<s>ākāśa</s>), because, with reference to the sunrise etc., the conventional usage 'this is here' is possible with regard to the rows of spatial units of space.

children.text: § 532. uktānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ viśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 532. In order to understand the specific [nature] of the stated substances, he says—

children.text: nityāvasthitāny arūpāṇi ||
children.translated_text: They are eternal, stable, and formless. ||

children.text: § 533. nityaṃ dhruvam ity arthaḥ. ‘ner dhruve tyaḥ’ iti niṣpāditatvāt. dharmādīni dravyāṇi gatihetutvādiviśeṣalakṣaṇadravyārthādeśād astitvādisāmānyalakṣaṇadravyārthādeśāc ca kadācid api na vyayantīti nityāni. vakṣyate hi ‘tadbhāvāvyayaṃ nityam’ iti. iyattā ’vyabhicārād avasthitāni. dharmādīni ṣaḍ api dravyāṇi kadācid api ṣaḍ iti iyattvaṃ nātivartante. tato ’vasthitānīty ucyante. na vidyate rūpam eṣām ity arūpāṇi, rūpapratiṣedhe tatsahacāriṇāṃ rasādīnām api pratiṣedaḥ. tena arūpāṇy amūrtānīty arthaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 533. '<s>Nitya</s>' means permanent. Because it is derived [from the root <s>nī</s>] with the suffix '<s>tya</s>' in the sense of 'permanent.' The substances <s>Dharma</s> etc. never perish, whether understood as substances characterized by their specific functions such as being the cause of motion etc., or as substances characterized by their general properties such as existence etc.—hence they are 'eternal.' For it will be stated: 'That whose being does not perish is eternal.' They are 'stable' (<s>avasthita</s>) because their number does not deviate. The six substances <s>Dharma</s> etc. never exceed the number 'six'—hence they are called 'stable.' 'Formless' (<s>arūpa</s>) means those that lack form (<s>rūpa</s>); and in denying form, the qualities that accompany it—taste, smell, etc.—are also denied. Therefore, 'formless' means 'incorporeal' (<s>amūrta</s>).

children.text: § 534. yathā sarveṣāṃ dravyāṇāṃ ‘nityāvasthitāni’ ity etat sādhāraṇaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ prāptaṃ tathā pudgalānām api arūpitvaṃ prāptam, atas tadapavādārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 534. Just as the common characteristic 'eternal and stable' applies to all substances, so too formlessness would apply to <s>pudgalas</s> (matter) as well; therefore, to state the exception, he says—

children.text: rūpiṇaḥ pudgalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pudgalas</s> (material particles) are possessed of form. ||

children.text: § 535. rūpaṃ mūrtir ity arthaḥ. kā mūrtiḥ? rūpādisaṃsthānapariṇāmo mūrtiḥ. rūpam eṣām astīti rūpiṇaḥ. mūrtimanta ity arthaḥ. athavā rūpam iti guṇaviśeṣavacanaśabdaḥ. tadeṣām astīti rūpiṇaḥ. rasādyagrahaṇam iti cet? na; tadavinābhāvāt tadantarbhāvaḥ. ‘pudgalāḥ’ iti bahuvacanaṃ bhedapratipādanārtham. bhinnā hi pudgalāḥ; skandhaparamāṇubhedāt. tadvikalpa upariṣṭād vakṣyate. yadi pradhānavad arūpitvam ekatvaṃ ceṣṭaṃ syāt, viśvarūpakāryadarśanavirodhaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: § 535. '<s>Rūpa</s>' means '<s>mūrti</s>' (corporeal form). What is <s>mūrti</s>? The configuration consisting of color etc. is <s>mūrti</s>. Those that possess form are '<s>rūpin</s>,' meaning 'corporeal.' Or, '<s>rūpa</s>' is a word denoting a specific quality. Those that possess it are '<s>rūpin</s>.' [Objection:] Taste etc. are not mentioned? [Reply:] No, because they are invariably concomitant [with form], they are included. '<s>Pudgalas</s>' in the plural is for the purpose of indicating divisions. For <s>pudgalas</s> are different—due to the division into aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) and atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>). Their varieties will be stated later. If, like <s>Pradhāna</s> [of the Sāṅkhya system], formlessness and oneness were held [for matter], there would be a contradiction with the observed variety of worldly effects.

children.text: § 536. āha, kiṃ pudgalavad dharmādīny api dravyāṇi pratyekaṃ bhinnānīty atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 536. One asks: Are the substances <s>Dharma</s> etc. also individually multiple, like <s>pudgala</s>? To this it is said—

children.text: ā ākāśād ekadravyāṇi ||
children.translated_text: [Each is] a single substance, up to and including space (<s>ākāśa</s>). ||

children.text: § 537. ‘āṅ’ ayam abhividhyarthaḥ. sautrīm ānupūrvīm āsṛtyaitad uktam. tena dharmā ’dharmākāśāni gṛhyante. ‘eka’ śabdaḥ saṃkhyāvacanaḥ. tena dravyaṃ viśiṣyate, ekaṃ dravyaṃ ekadravyam iti. yady evaṃ bahuvacanam ayuktam? dharmādyapekṣayā bahutvasiddhir bhavati. nanu ekasyānekārthapratyāyanaśaktiyogād ekaikam ity astu, laghutvād. ‘dravya’ grahaṇam anarthakam? (satyam;) tathāpi dravyāpekṣayā ekatvakhyāpanārthaṃ dravyagrahaṇam. kṣetrabhāvādyapekṣayā asaṃkhyeyatvānantatvavikalpasyeṣṭatvān na jīvapudgalavad eṣāṃ bahutvam ity etad anena khyāpyate.
children.translated_text: § 537. The particle '<s>ā</s>' here means 'including.' Following the order of the <s>sūtras</s>, this is stated [thus]. Thereby, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Adharma</s>, and <s>Ākāśa</s> are included. The word '<s>eka</s>' (one) denotes number. By it, 'substance' is qualified: one substance is '<s>ekadravya</s>.' [Objection:] If so, the plural [in the sūtra] is inappropriate? [Reply:] The plurality is established with reference to <s>Dharma</s> etc. [taken together]. [Objection:] Since one [thing] has the capacity to convey multiple meanings, let it be '<s>ekaika</s>' (one each)—more concise? And the word 'substance' would be purposeless? [Reply:] (True;) nonetheless, the word 'substance' is [included] for the purpose of indicating oneness with reference to substance. Since the alternatives of innumerable and infinite [numbers] are acceptable with reference to spatial location etc., this [sūtra] proclaims that these [substances] do not have plurality like <s>jīva</s> and <s>pudgala</s>.

children.text: § 538. adhikṛtānām eva ekadravyāṇāṃ viśeṣapratipattyartham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 538. In order to understand the specific [nature] of these very single-substance [entities] under discussion, this is said—

children.text: niṣkriyāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: And they are without activity (<s>niṣkriya</s>). ||

children.text: § 539. ubhayanimittavaśād utpadyamānaḥ paryāyo dravyasya deśāntaraprāptihetuḥ kriyā. tasyā niṣkrāntāni niṣkriyāṇi. atra codyate — dharmādīni dravyāṇi yadi niṣkriyāṇi tatas teṣām utpādo na bavet. kriyāpūrvako hi ghaṭādīnām utpādo dṛṣṭaḥ. utpādābhāvāc ca vyayābhāva iti. ataḥ sarvadravyāṇām utpādāditritayakalpanāvyāghāta iti. tan na; kiṃ kāraṇam? anyathopapatteḥ. kriyānimittotpādābhāve ’py eṣāṃ dharmādīnām anyathotpādaḥ kalpyate. tad yathā — dvividha utpādaḥ — svanimittaḥ parapratyayaś ca. svanimittas tāvad anantānām agurulaghuguṇānām āgamaprāmāṇyād abhupagamyamānānāṃ ṣaṭ sthānapatitayā vṛddhyā hānyā ca pravartamānānāṃ svabhāvād eteṣām utpādo vyayaś ca. parapratyayo ’pi aśvādigatisthityavagāhanahetutvāt kṣaṇe kṣaṇe teṣāṃ bhedāt taddhetutvam api bhinnam iti parapratyayāpekṣa utpādo vināśaś ca vyavahriyate. nanu yadi niṣkriyāṇi dharmādīni, jīvapudgalānāṃ gatyādihetutvaṃ nopapadyate. jalādīni hi kriyāvanti matsyādīnāṃ gatyādinimittāni dṛṣṭānīti? naiṣa doṣaḥ; balādhānanimittatvāc cakṣurvat. yathā rūpopalabdhau cakṣur nimittam iti na vyākṣiptamanaskasyāpi bhavati. adhikṛtānāṃ dharmādharmākāśānāṃ niṣkriyatve ’bhyupagate jīvapudgalānāṃ sakriyatvam arthād āpannam. kālasyāpi sakriyatvam iti cet? na; anadhikārāt. ata evāsāv etaiḥ saha nādhikriyate.
children.translated_text: § 539. Activity (<s>kriyā</s>) is a mode arising from both types of causes, which is the cause of a substance's reaching another location. Those from which [activity] has departed are 'without activity' (<s>niṣkriya</s>). Here an objection is raised: If the substances <s>Dharma</s> etc. are without activity, then they would have no origination. For origination of pots etc. is observed to be preceded by activity. And from the absence of origination, there would be absence of destruction too. Therefore, the threefold [scheme of] origination etc. for all substances would be contradicted. [Reply:] That is not [so]. Why? Because of [the possibility of] alternative explanation. Even in the absence of activity-caused origination, the origination of <s>Dharma</s> etc. is conceived of differently. Namely: origination is of two kinds—self-caused (<s>svanimiita</s>) and other-dependent (<s>parapratyaya</s>). Self-caused, first: since the innumerable qualities of 'neither heavy nor light' (<s>agurulaghu</s>), accepted on the authority of scripture, progress through increase and decrease falling into six categories—the origination and destruction of these [substances] is from their own nature. Other-dependent also: since [these substances] are the cause of the motion, stability, and spatial extension of horses etc., and since their [causal role] differs at every moment because [the effects] change, origination and destruction dependent on external factors is also conventionally stated. [Objection:] If <s>Dharma</s> etc. are without activity, their being causes of motion etc. for <s>jīvas</s> and <s>pudgalas</s> is not possible. For water etc., which possess activity, are observed as the causes of the motion etc. of fish etc. [Reply:] This is not a fault, because [they are] a contributing condition—like the eye. Just as the eye is a condition for the apprehension of form but does not [cause perception] even in one whose mind is distracted [so too Dharma etc. are conditions, not active agents]. When the non-activity of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Adharma</s>, and <s>Ākāśa</s> under discussion is accepted, the activity of <s>jīvas</s> and <s>pudgalas</s> is consequentially established. [Objection:] Time (<s>kāla</s>) too has activity? [Reply:] No, because it is not under discussion here. For this very reason, it is not taken up together with these [three substances].

children.text: § 540. ajīvakāyā ity atra kāyagrahaṇena pradeśāstitvamātraṃ nirjñātaṃ na tv iyattāvadhāritā pradeśānām atas tannirdhāraṇārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 540. In '<s>ajīvakāya</s>' (non-soul bodies), the word '<s>kāya</s>' (body) establishes only the existence of spatial units (<s>pradeśa</s>), but the exact number of spatial units is not determined; therefore, for the purpose of determining that, this is said—

children.text: asaṃkhyeyāḥ pradeśā dharmādharmaikajīvānām ||
children.translated_text: The spatial units (<s>pradeśa</s>) of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Adharma</s>, and a single <s>jīva</s> (soul) are innumerable (<s>asaṃkhyeya</s>). ||

children.text: § 541. saṃkhyām atītā asaṃkhyeyāḥ. asaṃkhyeyās trividhaḥ — jaghanya utkṛṣṭo ’jaghanyotkṛṣṭaś ceti. tatrehājaghanyotkṛṣṭāsaṃkhyeyaḥ parigṛhyate. pradiśyanta iti pradeśāḥ. vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇaḥ paramāṇuḥ sa yāvati kṣetre vyavatiṣṭhate sa pradeśa iti vyavahriyate. dharmādharmaikajīvās tulyāsamkhyeyapradeśāḥ. tatra dharmādharmo niṣkriyau lokākāśaṃ vyāpya sthitau. jīvas tāvat pradeśo ’pi san saṃharaṇavisarpaṇasvabhāvatvāt karmanirvartitaṃ śarīram aṇu mahad vā ’dhitiṣṭhaṃs tāvad avagāhya vartate. yadā tu lokapūraṇaṃ bhavati tadā mandarasyādhaś citravajrapaṭalamadhye jīvasyāṣṭau madhyapradeśā vyavatiṣṭhante. itare pradeśā ūrdhvam adhas tiryak ca kṛtsnaṃ lokākāśaṃ vyaśnuvate.
children.translated_text: § 541. Those that surpass enumeration are 'innumerable.' The innumerable is threefold: minimum, maximum, and intermediate. Here, the intermediate innumerable is intended. '<s>Pradeśas</s>' are that which is indicated. The atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>), whose definition will be given [later]—the space in which it occupies is conventionally called a '<s>pradeśa</s>' (spatial unit). <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Adharma</s>, and a single <s>jīva</s> have the same innumerable number of spatial units. Among these, <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Adharma</s>, being without activity, pervade the entire cosmic space (<s>lokākāśa</s>) and remain [there]. A <s>jīva</s>, though possessing [innumerable] spatial units, by its nature of contraction and expansion, occupying the body—whether small or large—produced by <s>karma</s>, extends through that much [space]. But when the filling of the entire cosmos occurs, then below <s>Mandara</s> [mountain], in the middle of the <s>Citravajra</s> stratum, eight middle spatial units of the <s>jīva</s> are positioned, while the remaining spatial units extend upward, downward, and sideways throughout the entire cosmic space.

children.text: § 542. athākāśaya kati pradeśā ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 542. Now, how many spatial units does space (<s>ākāśa</s>) have? To this he says—

children.text: ākāśasyānantāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those of space are infinite (<s>ananta</s>). ||

children.text: § 543. avidyamāno ’nto yeṣāṃ te anantāḥ. ke? pradeśāḥ. kasya? ākāśasya. pūrvavad asyāpi pradeśakalpanā ’vaseyā.
children.translated_text: § 543. Those whose end is not found are 'infinite.' What [are infinite]? The spatial units. Of what? Of space. The conception of spatial units for this [space] too should be understood as before.

children.text: § 544. uktam amūrtānāṃ pradeśaparimāṇam. idānīṃ mūrtānāṃ pudgalānāṃ pradeśaparimāṇaṃ nirjñātavyam ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 544. The spatial extent of the incorporeal [substances] has been stated. Now the spatial extent of the corporeal <s>pudgalas</s> (matter) is to be ascertained; therefore he says—

children.text: saṃkhyeyā ’saṃkhyeyāś ca pudgalānām ||
children.translated_text: The [spatial units] of <s>pudgalas</s> are numerable (<s>saṃkhyeya</s>) and innumerable (<s>asaṃkhyeya</s>). ||

children.text: § 545. ‘ca’ śabdād anantaś cety anukṛṣyate. kasyacit pudgaladravyasya dvyaṇukādeḥ saṃkhyeyāḥ pradeśāḥ kasyacid asaṃkhyeyā anantāś ca. anantānantopasaṃkhyānam iti cet. na; anantasāmānyāt. anantapramāṇaṃ trividham uktam parītānantaṃ yuktānantam anantānantaṃ ceti. tatsarvam anantasāmānyena gṛhyate. syād etat asaṃkhyāt apradeśo lokaḥ anantapradeśasyānantānantapradeśasya ca skandasyādhikaraṇam iti virodhas tato nānantyam iti? naiṣa doṣaḥ; sūkṣmapariṇāmāvagāhanaśaktiyogāt. paramāṇvādayo hi sūkṣmabhāvena pariṇatā ekaikasminn apy ākāśapradeśe ’nantānantā avatiṣṭhante, avagāhanaśaktiś caiṣām avyāhatāsti. tasmād ekasminn api pradeśe anantānantānām avasthānaṃ na virudhyate.
children.translated_text: § 545. By the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), 'infinite' (<s>ananta</s>) is also drawn in. Some material substance, such as a dyad (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>) etc., has numerable spatial units; some has innumerable; and [some has] infinite. [Objection:] The sub-varieties of infinite should also be enumerated? [Reply:] No, because [they are included] under the general [category of] 'infinite.' The infinite measure has been stated as threefold: bounded infinite (<s>parītānanta</s>), combined infinite (<s>yuktānanta</s>), and infinitely infinite (<s>anantānanta</s>). All of these are included under the general term 'infinite.' [Objection:] There might be a contradiction: the cosmos, having innumerable spatial units, serves as the locus of an aggregate having infinite or infinitely infinite spatial units? [Reply:] This is not a fault, because of the capacity for subtle transformation and spatial interpenetration. For atoms etc., transformed into a subtle state, infinitely infinite [in number] occupy even a single spatial unit of space, and their capacity for interpenetration remains unobstructed. Therefore, the coexistence of infinitely infinite [atoms] even in a single spatial unit is not contradictory.

children.text: § 546. ‘pudgalānām ity aviśeṣavacanāt paramāṇor api pradeśavattvaprasaṃge tatpratiṣedhārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 546. Since the unqualified statement '<s>pudgalas</s>' [having spatial units] might entail that even an atom (<s>aṇu</s>) has spatial units, for the purpose of denying that, he says—

children.text: nāṇoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Not of the atom (<s>aṇu</s>). ||

children.text: § 547. aṇoḥ ‘pradeśā na santi’ śti vākyaśeṣaḥ.

kuto na santīti cet? pradeśamātratvāt. yathā ākāśapradeśasyaikasya pradeśabhedābhāvād apradeśatvam evam aṇor api pradeśamātratvāt pradeśabhedābhāvaḥ. kiṃ ca tato ’lpaparimāṇābhāvāt. na hy aṇor alpīyānanyo ’sti, yato ’sya pradeśā bhidyeran.
children.translated_text: Why does it have none? Because it is itself a mere spatial unit. Just as a single spatial unit of space has no subdivision of spatial units due to being [itself] a mere spatial unit, so too, the atom, being a mere spatial unit, has no subdivision of spatial units. Moreover, because there is nothing of lesser extent than it. For there is nothing smaller than the atom by which its spatial units could be divided.
§ 547. 'The atom has no spatial units'—this is the completion of the sentence.

children.text: § 548. eṣām avadhṛtapradeśānāṃ dharmādīnām ādhārapratipattyartham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 548. In order to understand the substratum of these substances whose spatial units have been determined—<s>Dharma</s> etc.—this is said—

children.text: lokākāśe ’vagāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their interpenetration (<s>avagāha</s>) is in cosmic space (<s>lokākāśa</s>). ||

children.text: § 549. uktānāṃ dharmādīnāṃ dravyāṇāṃ lokākāśe ’vagāho na bāhir ity arthaḥ. yadi dharmādīnāṃ lokākāśam ādhāraḥ, ākāśasya ka ādhāra iti? ākāśasya nāsty anya ādhāraḥ. svapratiṣṭham ākāśam. yady ākāśaṃ svapratiṣtiṣṭham; dharmādīny api svapratiṣtiṣṭhāny eva. atha dharmādīnāṃ anya ādhāraḥ kalpyate, ākāśasyāpy anya ādhāra kalpyaḥ. tathā saty anavasthāprasaṅga ity cet? naiṣa doṣaḥ; nākāśad anyad adhikaparimāṇaṃ dravyam asti yatrākāśaṃ sthitam ity ucyate. sarvato ’nantaṃ hi tat. dharmādīnāṃ punar adhikaraṇam ākāśam ity ucyate vyavahāranayavaśāt. evambhūtanayāpekṣayā tu sarvāṇi dravyāṇi svapratiṣtiṣṭhāny eva. tathā coktam,
kva bhavān āste. ātmani
children.translated_text: 'Where do you dwell?' 'In the self.'

children.text: iti. dharmādīni lokākāśān na bahiḥ santīty etāvad atrādhārādheyakalpanāsādhyaṃ phalam. nanu ca loke pūrvottarakālabhāvinām ādhārādheyabhāvo dṛṣto yathā kuṇḍe badarādīnām. na tathā ”kāśaṃ pūrvaṃ dharmādīny uttarakālabhāvīni; ato vyavahāranayāpekṣayā ’pi ādhārādheyakalpanān upapattir iti? naiṣa doṣaḥ, yugpadbhāvinām api ādhārādheyabhāvo dṛśyate. ghaṭe rūpādayaḥ śarīre hastādaya iti. loka ity ucyate. ko lokaḥ? dharmādharmādīni dravyāṇi yatra lokyante sa loka iti. adhikaraṇasādhano ghañ. ākāśaṃ dvidhā vibhaktaṃ — lokākāśam alokākāśaṃ ceti. loka uktaḥ. sa yatra tal lokākāśam. tato bahiḥ sarvato ’nantam alokākāśam. lokālokavibhāgaś ca dharmādharmās̄tikāyasadbhāvāsadbhāvād vijñeyaḥ. asati hi tasmin dharmāstikāye jīvapudgalānāṃ gatiniyamahetvabhāvād vibhāgo na syāt. asati cādharmāstikāye sthiter āśrayanimittābhāvāt sthiter abhāvo lokālokavibhagābhāvo vā syāt. tasmād ubhayasadbhāvāsadbhāvāl lokālokavibhāgasiddhiḥ.
children.translated_text: Thus, the result to be accomplished here by the conception of container and contained is merely this: <s>dharma</s> (medium of motion) and the rest do not exist outside the cosmic space (<s>lokākāśa</s>). [Objection:] But in the world, the container-contained relation is observed between things existing at earlier and later times, as with berries in a pot. Is not <s>ākāśa</s> (space) prior and <s>dharma</s> and the rest later in time—so that even from the standpoint of conventional usage (<s>vyavahāra-naya</s>), the conception of container-contained is untenable? [Reply:] This is no defect, since the container-contained relation is also observed among things existing simultaneously—as color and the like in a pot, or hands and the like in a body. '<s>Loka</s>' (universe) is stated. What is <s>loka</s>? That wherein substances such as <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and the rest are found (<s>lokyante</s>)—that is <s>loka</s>. The suffix '<s>ghañ</s>' denotes the locus. Space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is divided into two: cosmic space (<s>lokākāśa</s>) and trans-cosmic space (<s>alokākāśa</s>). The universe has been described. Where that [universe] is—that is cosmic space. Beyond that, on all sides, infinitely, is trans-cosmic space. The division between the cosmic and trans-cosmic is to be understood from the presence and absence of the <s>dharmāstikāya</s> (medium-of-motion aggregate) and <s>adharmāstikāya</s> (medium-of-rest aggregate). For in the absence of the <s>dharmāstikāya</s>, there would be no cause for the regulation of the motion of souls and <s>pudgalas</s> (matter), so no division would be possible. And in the absence of the <s>adharmāstikāya</s>, since the efficient cause of rest would be lacking, there would be no rest, or no division between cosmic and trans-cosmic [space]. Therefore, from the presence and absence of both, the division of cosmic and trans-cosmic [space] is established.

§ 549. The interpenetration of the stated substances <s>Dharma</s> etc. is in cosmic space, not outside—that is the meaning. [Objection:] If cosmic space is the substratum of <s>Dharma</s> etc., what is the substratum of space? [Reply:] Space has no other substratum. Space is self-established. [Objection:] If space is self-established, then <s>Dharma</s> etc. too are self-established. Or, if another substratum is fabricated for <s>Dharma</s> etc., then another substratum must be fabricated for space too, leading to infinite regress? [Reply:] This is not a fault. There is no substance of greater extent than space in which space could be said to be situated. For it [space] is infinite in all directions. But for <s>Dharma</s> etc., space is said to be the locus—by the conventional standpoint (<s>vyavahāranaya</s>). From the standpoint of 'the thing as it is' (<s>evambhūtanaya</s>), however, all substances are self-established. As it has been said:

children.text: § 550. tatrāvadhriyamāṇānām avasthānabhedasaṃbhavād viśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 550. Since there is the possibility of differences in position among those [substances] being determined, for the purpose of specific understanding, he says—

children.text: dharmādharmayoḥ kṛtsne ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (medium of motion) and <s>Adharma</s> (medium of rest) [pervade] the entire [cosmic space]. ||

children.text: § 551. kṛtsnavacanam aśeṣavyāptipradarśanārtham. agāre ’sthito ghaṭa iti yathā tathā dharmādharmayor lokākāśe ’vagāho na bhavati. kiṃ tarhi? kṛtsne tilesu tailavad iti. anyonyapradeśapraveśavyāghātābhāvaḥ avagāhanaśaktiyogād veditavyaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 551. The word 'entire' (<s>kṛtsna</s>) is for the purpose of showing complete pervasion without remainder. The pervasion of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> in cosmic space is not like a pot placed in a room. Rather, [it is] in the entirety, like oil in sesame seeds. The absence of obstruction from mutual penetration of spatial points (<s>pradeśa</s>) is to be understood as due to the possession of the power of interpenetration.

children.text: § 552. ato viparītānāṃ mūrtimatām apradeśasaṃkhyeyāsaṃkhyeyānantapradeśānāṃ pudgalānām avagāhaviśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 552. For the purpose of understanding the specific pervasion of <s>pudgalas</s> (matter-aggregates), which are the opposite [of the formless substances]—being corporeal, having no spatial points, or numerable, innumerable, or infinite spatial points—he says—

children.text: ekapradeśādiṣu bhājyaḥ pudgalānām ||
children.translated_text: The pervasion of <s>pudgalas</s> (matter) is to be divided among [spaces of] one spatial point and more. ||

children.text: § 553. ekaḥ pradeśa ekapradeśaḥ. ekapradeśa ādir yeṣāṃ ta ime ekapradeśādayaḥ. teṣu pudgalānām avagāho bhājyo vikalpyaḥ.
avayavena vigrahaḥ samudāyaḥ samāsārthaḥ
children.translated_text: The analysis is by parts; the collection is the meaning of the compound.

children.text: iti ekapradeśo ’pi gṛhyate. tad yathā — ekasminn akāśapradeśe paramāṇor avagāhaḥ. dvayor ekatrobhayatra ca baddhayor abaddhayoś ca. trayāṇām apy ekatra dvayos triṣu ca baddhānām abaddhānāṃ ca. evaṃ saṃkhyeyāsaṃkhyeyānantapradeśānāṃ skandhānām ekasaṃkhyeyāsaṃkhyeyapradeśeṣu lokākāśe ’vasthānaṃ pratyetavyam. nanu yuktaṃ tāvad amūrttayor dharmādharmayor ekatrāvirodhenāvarodha iti. mūrtimatāṃ pudgalānāṃ katham? ity atrocyate — avagāhanasvabhāvatvāt sūkṣmapariṇāmāc ca mūrtimatām apy avagāho na virudhyate ekāpavarake anekadīpaprakāśāvasthānavat. āgamaprāmāṇyāc ca tathā ’dhyavaseyam. tad uktam —
children.translated_text: Thus, even one spatial point is included. For example: in one spatial point of space, there is the pervasion of a <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom). Of two [atoms], bound or unbound, in one or both [spatial points]—

§ 553. One spatial point is '<s>ekapradeśa</s>.' Those whose beginning is one spatial point are '<s>ekapradeśādi</s>.' In those [spaces], the pervasion of <s>pudgalas</s> is to be divided, i.e., analyzed.

children.text:
ogāḍhagāḍhaṇicio puggalakāehi savvado logo |
	  suhumehiṃ bādarehiṃ aṇaṃtāṇaṃtehiṃ vivahehiṃ ||
§ 554. atha jīvānāṃ katham avagāhanam ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 554. Now, how is the pervasion of <s>jīvas</s> (souls)? To this it is said—

children.text: asaṃkhyeyabhāgādiṣu jīvānām ||
children.translated_text: The [pervasion] of <s>jīvas</s> (souls) is in innumerable fractions and more [of cosmic space]. ||

children.text: § 555. ‘lokākāśe’ity anuvartate. tasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgīkṛtasyaiko bhāgo ’saṃkhyeyabhāga ity ucyate. sa ādir yeṣāṃ te ’saṃkhyeyabhāgādayaḥ. teṣu jīvānām avagāho veditavyaḥ. tad yathā — ekasminn asaṃkhyeyabhāge eko jīvo ’vatiṣṭhate. evaṃ dvitricaturādiṣv api asaṃkhyeyabhāgeṣu ā sarvalokād avagāhaḥ pratyetavyaḥ. nānājīvānāṃ tu sarvaloka eva. yady ekasminn asaṃkhyeyabhāge eko jīvo ’vatiṣṭhate, kathaṃ dravyapramāṇenānantānanto jīvarāśiḥ saśarīro ’vatiṣṭhate lokākāśe? sūkṣmabādarabhedād avasthānaṃ pratyetavyam. bādarās tāvat sapratighātaśarīrāḥ. sūkṣmās tu saśarīrā api sūkṣmabhāvād evaikanigodajīvāvagāhye ’pi pradeśe sādhāraṇaśarīrā anantānantā vasanti. na te paraspareṇa bādaraiś ca vyāhanyanta iti nāsty avagāhavirodhaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 555. '<s>Lokākāśa</s>' (cosmic space) is supplied [from the previous sūtra]. When the [cosmic space] is divided into innumerable parts, one such part is called an 'innumerable fraction' (<s>asaṃkhyeya-bhāga</s>). That is the beginning of which—those are '<s>asaṃkhyeya-bhāgādi</s>'.

children.text: § 556. atrāha lokākāśatulyapradeśa ekajīva ity uktam, tasya kathaṃ lokasyāsaṃkhyeyabhāgādiṣu vṛttiḥ. nanu sarvalokavyāptyaiva bhavitavyam ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 556. Here one objects: it has been said that a single <s>jīva</s> (soul) has spatial points equal to [the entire] cosmic space. How then can it exist in an innumerable fraction and the like of the cosmic space? [Reply:] Is not the all-pervading-the-entire-universe [status of the soul understood] only at certain times—

children.text: pradeśasaṃhāravisarpābhyāṃ pradīpavat ||
children.translated_text: Through the contraction and expansion of spatial points, like a lamp. ||

children.text: § 557. amūrtasvabhāvasyātmano ’nādibandhaṃ pratyekatvāt kathaṃcin mūrtatāṃ vibhrataḥ kārmaṇaśarīravaśān mahad aṇu ca śarīram adhitiṣṭhatas tadvaśāt pradeśasaṃharaṇavisarpaṇasvabhāvasya tāvat pramāṇatāyāṃ satyām asaṃkhyeyabhāgādiṣu vṛttir upapadyate, pradīpavat. yathā nirāvaraṇavyomapradeśe ’navadhṛtaprakāśaparimāṇasya pradīpasya śarāvamaṇikāpavarakādyāvaraṇavaśāt tatparimāṇateti. atrāha dharmādīnām anyonyapradeśānupraveśāt saṃkare sati, ekatvaṃ prāpnotīti? tan na; parasparam atyantasaṃśleṣe saty api svabhāvaṃ na jahati. uktam ca —
children.translated_text: § 557. The self (<s>ātman</s>), whose essential nature is non-material (<s>amūrta</s>), bearing a kind of materiality due to the <s>kārmaṇa-śarīra</s> (karmic body) from beginningless bondage, assumes both a large and a small body—

children.text:
“aṇṇoṇṇaṃ pavisaṃtā diṃtā ogāsamaṇṇamaṇṇassa |
	  melaṃtā vi ya ṇiccaṃ sagasabbhāvaṃ ṇa jahaṃti |
children.translated_text: Mutually interpenetrating, giving space to each other, and always meeting together, they do not abandon their own essential nature. [Prakrit verse]
The universe is densely packed on all sides by <s>pudgala</s>-bodies—subtle and gross, in infinite-infinite combinations. [Prakrit verse]

children.text: § 558. yady evaṃ dharmādīnāṃ svabhāvabheda ucyatām ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 558. If so, let the essential nature-difference of <s>dharma</s> and the rest be stated—thus he says—

children.text: gatisthityupagrahau dharmādharmayor upakāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The assistance (<s>upakāra</s>) of <s>dharma</s> (medium of motion) and <s>adharma</s> (medium of rest) consists in [facilitating] motion, rest, and support. ||

children.text: § 559. deśāntaraprāptihetur gatiḥ. tadviparītā sthitiḥ. upagṛhyata ity upagrahaḥ. gatiś ca sthitiś ca gatisthitī. gatisthitī eva upagrahau gatisthityupagrahau. dharmādharmayor iti kartṛnirdeśaḥ. upakriyata ity upakāraḥ. kaḥ punar asau? gatyupagrahaḥ sthityupagrahaś ca. yady evaṃ dvitvanirdeśaḥ prāpnoti. naiṣa doṣaḥ; sāmānyena vyutpāditaḥ śabda upāttasaṃkhyaḥ śabdāntarasaṃbandhe saty api na pūrvopāttāṃ saṃkhyāṃ jahāti. yathā —
sādhoḥ kāryaṃ tapaḥśrute
children.translated_text: The action of the virtuous is austerity and learning.

children.text: iti. etad uktaṃ bhavati — gatipariṇāmināṃ jīvapudgalānāṃ gatyupagrahe kartavye dharmāstikāyaḥ sādhāraṇāśrayo jalavanmatsyagamane. tathā sthitipariṇāmināṃ jīvapudgalānāṃ sthityupagrahe kartavye adharmāstikāyaḥ sādhāraṇāśrayaḥ pṛthivīdhatur ivāśvādisthitāv iti. nanu ca ‘upagraha’ vacanam anarthakam ‘upakāraḥ’ ity evaṃ siddhatvāt. ‘gatisthitī dharmādharmayor upakāraḥ’ iti. naiṣa doṣaḥ; yathāsaṃkhyanivṛttyarthaṃ ‘upagraha’ vacanam. dharmādharmayor gatisthityoś ca yathāsaṃkhyaṃ bhavati, evaṃ jīvapudgalānāṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ prāpnoti dharmasyopakāro jīvānāṃ gatiḥ adharmasyopakāraḥ pudgalānāṃ sthitir iti. tannivṛttyartham upagrahavacanaṃ kriyate. āha dharmādharmayor ya upakāraḥ sa ākāśasya yuktaḥ; sarvagatvād iti cet? tad ayuktam; tasyānyopakārasadbhāvāt. sarveṣāṃ dharmādīnāṃ dravyāṇām avagāhanaṃ tatprayojanam. ekasyānekaprayojanakalpanāyāṃ lokālokavibhāgābhāvaḥ. bhūmijalādiny eva tatprayojanasamarthāni nārtho dharmādharmābhyām iti cet? na; sādhāraṇāśraya iti viśiṣyoktatvāt. anekakāraṇasādhyatvāc caikasya kāryasya. tulyabalatvāt tayor gatisthitipratibandha iti cet? na; aprerakatvāt. anupalabdher na tau staḥ kharaviṣāṇavad iti cet? na; sarvapravādyavipratipatteḥ. sarve hi pravādinaḥ pratyakṣāpratyakṣānarthān abhivāñchanti. asmān prati hetor asiddheś ca. sarvajñena niratiśayapratyakṣajñānacakṣuṣā dharmādayaḥ sarve upalabhyante. tadupadeśāc ca śrutajñānibhir api.
children.translated_text: What is being said is this: in providing assistance for motion to <s>jīvas</s> and <s>pudgalas</s> that have the disposition for motion, the <s>dharmāstikāya</s> is a common support, like water for fish—

§ 559. Motion (<s>gati</s>) is the cause of reaching another place. Rest (<s>sthiti</s>) is the opposite of that. That which supports is support (<s>upagraha</s>). Motion and rest [together] are '<s>gati-sthiti</s>.'

children.text: § 560. atrāha, yady atīndriyayor dharmādharmayor upakārasaṃbandhenāstitvam avadhriyate, tadanantaram uddiṣṭasya nabhaso ’tīndriyasyādhigame ka upakāra ity ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 560. Here one objects: if the existence of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, which are beyond the senses, is ascertained through their relation of assistance, then what is the assistance of space (<s>ākāśa</s>), which was mentioned next? To this—

children.text: ākāśasyāvagāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The assistance of <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is [providing] room for pervasion (<s>avagāha</s>). ||

children.text: § 561. ‘upakāraḥ’ ity anuvartate. jīvapudgalādīnāṃ avagāhinām avakāśadānam avagāha ākāśasyopakāro veditavyaḥ. āha, jīvapudgalānāṃ kriyāvatām avagāhinām avakāśadānaṃ yuktam. dharmāstikāyādayaḥ punar niṣkriyā nityasaṃbandhās teṣāṃ katham avagāha iti cet? na; upacāratas tatsiddheḥ. yathā gamanābhāve ’pi ‘sarvagatam ākāśam’ ity ucyate; sarvatra sadbhāvāt, evaṃ dharmādharmāv api avagāha kriyābhāve ’pi sarvatra vyāptidarśanād avagāhināv ity upacaryete.

āha yady avakāśadānam asya svabhāvo vajrādibhir loṣṭādīnāṃ bhittyādibhir gavādīnāṃ ca vyāghāto na prāpnoti. dṛśyate ca vyāghātaḥ. tasmād asyāvakāśadānaṃ hīyate iti. naiṣa doṣaḥ; vajraloṣṭādīnāṃ sthūlānāṃ parasparavyāghāta iti nāsyāvakāśadānasāmarthyaṃ hīyate; tatrāvagāhinām eva vyāghātāt. vajrādayaḥ punaḥ sthūlatvāt parasparaṃ pratyavakāśadānaṃ kurvantīti nāsāv ākāśadoṣaḥ. ye khalu pudgalāḥ sūkṣmās te parasparaṃ pratyavakāśadānaṃ kurvanti. yady evaṃ nedam ākāśasyāsādhāraṇaṃ lakṣaṇam; itareṣām api tatsadbhāvād iti? tan na; sarvapadārthānāṃ sādhāraṇāvagāhanahetutvam asyāsādhāraṇaṃ lakṣaṇam iti nāsti doṣaḥ. alokākāśe tadbhāvād abhāva iti cet? na; svabhāvāparityāgāt.
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If providing room is its essential nature, then the obstruction of clods of earth by diamonds, of cattle by walls, and the like should not occur. But obstruction is indeed observed. [Reply:] Providing room is [the function] of <s>ākāśa</s> alone. But obstruction is caused by <s>pudgalas</s> (matter) themselves, through their own resistance—not by <s>ākāśa</s>.

§ 561. 'Assistance' (<s>upakāra</s>) is supplied [from the previous sūtra]. The assistance of <s>ākāśa</s> should be understood as providing room (<s>avakāśa-dāna</s>) for <s>jīvas</s>, <s>pudgalas</s>, and others that pervade [space]. [Objection:] [If so, why do] <s>jīvas</s>, <s>pudgalas</s>—

children.text: § 562. ukta ākāśasyopakāraḥ. atha tadanantaroddiṣṭānāṃ pudgalānāṃ ka upakāra ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 562. The assistance of <s>ākāśa</s> has been stated. Now, what is the assistance of <s>pudgalas</s> (matter), which were mentioned next? To this it is said—

children.text: śarīravāṅmanaḥprāṇāpānāh pudgalānām ||
children.translated_text: Body, speech, mind, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), and <s>apāna</s> (outgoing breath) [are the assistance] of <s>pudgalas</s>. ||

children.text: § 563. idam ayuktam vartate. kim atrāyuktam? pudgalānāṃ ka upakāra ity paripraśne pudgalānāṃ lakṣaṇam ucyate; śarīrādīni pudgalamayānīti? naitad ayuktam; pudgalānāṃ lakṣaṇam uttaratra vakṣyate. idaṃ tu jīvān prati pudgalānām upakārapratipādanārtham eveti upakāraprakaraṇe ucyate. śarīrāṇy uktāni. audārikādīni saukṣmyād apratyakṣāṇi. tadudayāpāditavṛttīny upacayaśarīrāṇi kānicit pratyakṣāṇi kānicid apratyakṣāṇi. eteṣāṃ kāraṇabhūtāni karmāny api śarīragrahaṇena gṛhyante. etāni paudgalikānīti kṛtvā jīvānām upakāre pudgalāḥ pravartante. syān mataṃ kārmaṇam apaudgalikam; anākāratvād. ākāravatāṃ hi audārikādīni paudagalikatvaṃ yuktam iti? tan na; tad api paudagalikam eva; tadvipākasya mūrtimatsambandhanimittatvāt. dṛśyate hi vrīhyādīnām udakādidravyasaṃbandhaprāpitaparipākānāṃ paudagalikatvaṃ. tathā kārmaṇam api guḍakaṇṭakādimūrtimaddravyopanipāte sati vipacyamānatvāt paudagalikaṃ ity avaseyam. vāg dvividham — dravyavāg bhāvavāg iti. tatra bhāvavāk tāvad vīryāntarāyamatiśrutajñānāvaraṇakṣayopaśamāṅgopāṅganāmalābhanimittatvāt paudagalikī. tadabhāve tadvṛttyabhāvāt. tatsāmarthyopetena kriyāvatātmanā preryamāṇāḥ pudgalā vāktvena vipariṇamanta iti dravyavāg api paudgalikī; śrotendriyaviṣayatvāt. itarendriyaviṣayā kasmān na bhavati. tadgrahaṇāyogyatvāt. ghrāṇagrāhye gandhadravye rasādyanupalabdhivat. amūrtā vāg iti cet? na; mūrtimadgrahaṇāvarodhavyāghātābhibhavādidarśanān mūrtimattvasiddheḥ. mano dvividhaṃ dravyamano bhāvamanaś ceti. bhāvamanas tāval labdhyupayogalakṣaṇaṃ pudgalāvalambanatvāt paudagalikam. dravyamanaś ca, jñānāvaraṇavīryāntarāyakṣayopaśamāṅgopāṅganāmalābhapratyayā guṇadoṣavicārasmaraṇādipranidhānābhimukhasyātmano ’nugrāhakāḥ pudgalā manas tv ena pariṇatā iti paudagalikam. kaścid āha mano dravyāntaraṃ rūpādipariṇāmarahitam aṇumātraṃ tasya paudagalikatvaṃ ayuktam iti? tad ayuktam. katham? ucyate — tadindriyeṇātmanā ca saṃbaddhaṃ vā syād asaṃbaddham vā. yady asaṃbaddham, tannātmana upakārakaṃ bhavitum arhati indriyasya ca sācivyaṃ na karoti. atha saṃbaddham, ekasmin pradeśe saṃbaddhaṃ sat tad aṇu itareṣu pradeśeṣu upakāraṃ na kuryāt. adṛṣṭavaśād asya alātacakravatparibhramaṇam iti cet. na; tatsāmarthyābhāvāt. amūrtasyātmano niṣkriyasyādṛṣṭo guṇaḥ, sa niṣkriyaḥ sann anyatra kriyārambhe na samarthaḥ. dṛṣṭo hi vāyudravyaviśeṣaḥ kriyāvān sparśavān prāptavanaspatau parispandahetus tadviparītalakṣaṇaś cāyam iti kriyāhetutvābhāvaḥ. vīryāntrāyajñānāvaraṇakṣayopaśamāṅgopāṅganāmodayāpekṣiṇātmanā udasyamānaḥ koṣṭhyo vāyur ucchvāsalakṣaṇaḥ prāṇa ity ucyate. tenaivātmanā bāhyo vāyur abhyantarīkriyamāṇo niḥsvāsalakṣaṇo ’pāna ity ākhyāyate. evaṃ tāv apy ātmānugrāhiṇau; jīvitahetutvāt. teṣāṃ manaḥprāṇāpānānāṃ mūrtimattvam avaseyam. kutaḥ? mūrtimadbhiḥ pratighātādidarśanāt. pratibhayahetubhir aśanipātādibhir manasaḥ pratighāto dṛśyate. surādibhiś cābhibhavaḥ. hastatalapaṭādibhir āsyasaṃvaraṇāt prāṇāpānayoḥ pratighāta upalabhyate. śleṣmaṇā cābhibhavaḥ. na cāmūrtasya mūrtimadbhir abhighātādayaḥ syuḥ. ata evātmāstitvasiddhiḥ. yathā yantrapratimāceṣṭitaṃ prayoktur astitvaṃ gamayati tathā prāṇāpānādikarmāpi kriyāvantam ātmānaṃ sādhayati.
children.translated_text: § 563. This is inappropriate, [one objects]. What is inappropriate here? When the question is 'What is the benefit of <s>pudgalas</s> (matter-particles)?', the definition of <s>pudgalas</s> is being stated — [namely] that bodies and the like are made of <s>pudgala</s>? This is not inappropriate; the definition of <s>pudgala</s> will be stated later. But this is stated in the context of benefit, for the purpose of establishing the benefit of <s>pudgalas</s> to <s>jīvas</s> (souls). Bodies have been described. The <s>audārika</s> and other [bodies] are imperceptible due to their subtlety. The accretion-bodies (<s>upacaya-śarīra</s>), whose functions are brought about by the fruition of [body-name karma], are in some cases perceptible and in some cases imperceptible. <s>Karmas</s>, which are the cause of these [bodies], are also included by the mention of 'body.' These are <s>paudgalika</s> (material), and thus <s>pudgalas</s> function for the benefit of <s>jīvas</s>. [Objection:] One might think the <s>kārmaṇa</s> (karmic body) is non-material, since it is formless. For it seems reasonable that only the <s>audārika</s> and other [bodies] that have form are material. [Reply:] Not so; it too is material, because the fruition of that [karmic body] is caused by contact with material [embodied] entities. For we observe that rice and the like, whose ripening is brought about by contact with water and other material substances, are material. Similarly, the <s>kārmaṇa</s> [body] too, since it ripens upon the encounter with material substances like molasses, thorns, and the like, should be understood as material. Speech (<s>vāk</s>) is twofold: <s>dravya-vāk</s> (material speech) and <s>bhāva-vāk</s> (dispositional speech). Of these, <s>bhāva-vāk</s> is material because it is caused by the attainment of limbs, secondary limbs, and name-[karma], through the destruction-cum-subsidence of the energy-obstructing, sensory-knowledge-obscuring, and scriptural-knowledge-obscuring [karmas]. In their absence, its function would be absent. <s>Dravya-vāk</s> too is material, because <s>pudgalas</s>, impelled by the active self endowed with that capacity, transform into [the nature of] speech — and because it is the object of the auditory sense-organ. [Objection:] Why is it not the object of the other sense-organs? [Reply:] Because it is not fit to be grasped by them — just as taste and the like are not apprehended in an odor-substance grasped by the olfactory [organ]. [Objection:] Speech is formless? [Reply:] No; its material nature is established from the observation that it is grasped by, resisted by, obstructed by, and overpowered by material entities. Mind (<s>manas</s>) is twofold: <s>dravya-manas</s> (material mind) and <s>bhāva-manas</s> (dispositional mind). <s>Bhāva-manas</s> is material because it has the nature of attainment and cognitive engagement, and because it depends on <s>pudgalas</s>. <s>Dravya-manas</s> too [is material], because <s>pudgalas</s> — which are the auxiliaries of the self that is inclined toward deliberation such as the examination of virtues and faults, recollection, and the like, [arising] from the attainment of limbs, secondary limbs, and name-[karma] through the destruction-cum-subsidence of knowledge-obscuring and energy-obstructing [karmas] — transform into the nature of mind. [Objection:] Someone says: mind is a separate substance, devoid of transformation into form and the like, atomic in size — its materiality is unjustified? [Reply:] That is unjustified. How? It is said: by that sense-organ and by the self, the connection [is established].

children.text: § 564. kim etāvān eva pudgalakṛta upakāra āhosvid anyo ’py astīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 564. Is this the only benefit rendered by <s>pudgala</s>, or is there yet another? To this he says —

children.text: sukhadhuḥkhajīvitamaraṇopagrahāś ca ||
children.translated_text: And also pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), life (<s>jīvita</s>), death (<s>maraṇa</s>), and [various] supports (<s>upagraha</s>).

children.text: § 565. sadasadvedyodaye ’ntaraṅgahetau sati bāhyadravyādiparipākanimittavāśād utpadyamānaḥ prītiparitāparūpaḥ pariṇāmaḥ sukhaduḥkham ity ākhyāyate. bhavadhāranakāraṇāyurākhyakarmodayāt bhavasthitim ādadhānasya jīvasya pūrvoktaprāṇāpānakriyāviśeṣāvyucchedo jīvitam ity ucyate. taducchedo maraṇam. etani sukhādīni jīvasya pudgalakṛta upakāraḥ; mūrtimaddhetusaṃnidhāne sati tadutpatteḥ. upakārādhikārāt ‘upagraha’ vacanam anarthakam? nānarthakam. svopagrahapradarśanārtham idam. pudgalānāṃ pudgalakṛta upakāra iti. tad yathā — kāṃsyādīnāṃ bhasmādibhir jalādīnāṃ katakādibhir ayaḥprabhṛtīnām udakādibhir upakāraḥ kriyate. ‘ca’ śabdaḥ kim arthaḥ? samuccayārthaḥ. anyo ’pi pudgalakṛta upakāro ’stīti samuccīyate. yathā śarīrāṇi evaṃ caksurādinīndriyāṇy apīti.
children.translated_text: § 565. When the internal cause — the fruition of [karma] to be experienced as pleasant or unpleasant — is present, the transformation in the form of joy and distress that arises due to the ripening of external substances and the like is called pleasure and pain (<s>sukha-duḥkha</s>).

children.text: § 566. evam ādyam ajīvakṛtam upakāraṃ pradarśya jīvakṛtopakārapradarśanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 566. Having thus shown the first benefit rendered by non-living [matter], to show the benefit rendered by [other] living beings, he says —

children.text: parasparopagraho jīvānām ||
children.translated_text: The mutual assistance of <s>jīvas</s> (souls) [is established].

children.text: § 567. ‘paraspara’ śabdaḥ karmavyatihāre vartate. karmavyatihāraś ca kriyāvyatihāraḥ. parasparasyopagrahaḥ parasparopagrahaḥ. jīvānām upakāraḥ. kaḥ punar asau? svāmī bhṛtyaḥ, ācāryaḥ śiṣyaḥ, ity evam ādibhāvena vṛttiḥ parasparopagrahaḥ. svāmī tāvad vittatyāgādinā bhṛtyānām upakare vartate. bhṛtyāś ca hitapratipādanenāhitapratiṣedhena ca. ācārya ubhayalokaphalapradopadeśadarśanena tadupadeśavihitakriyānuṣṭhāpanena ca śiṣyāṇām anugrahe vartate. śiṣyā api tadanukūlyavṛttyā ācāryāṇām. upakārādhikāre punaḥ ‘upagraha’ vacanaṃ kim artham? pūrvoktasukhādicatuṣṭayapradarśanārthaṃ punaḥ ‘upagraha’ vacanaṃ kriyate. sukhādīny api jīvānāṃ jīvakṛta upakāra iti.
children.translated_text: § 567. The word '<s>paraspara</s>' (mutual) is used in the sense of reciprocal action (<s>karma-vyatihāra</s>). And reciprocal action means reciprocal activity. The mutual assistance (<s>parasparopagraha</s>) is the benefit of <s>jīvas</s>. What kind of benefit? [The benefit is that] through instruction in <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and the like, those endowed with right faith, knowledge, and conduct assist one another — as a lamp illuminates other lamps.

children.text: § 568. āha, yady avaśyaṃ satopakāriṇā bhavitavyam; saṃś ca kālo ’bhimatas tasya ka upakāra ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 568. He says: If one must necessarily be a benefactor of the existent [beings], and if time (<s>kāla</s>) is accepted as an existent [category], what is its benefit? To this it is said —

children.text: vartanāpariṇāmakriyāḥ paratvāparatve ca kālasya ||
children.translated_text: Continuity (<s>vartanā</s>), transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>), and activity (<s>kriyā</s>) [are the functions of time]; and [it provides] the [distinctions of] priority (<s>paratva</s>) and posteriority (<s>aparatva</s>).

children.text: § 569. vṛtter ṇijatantāt karmaṇi bhāve vā yuṭi strīliṃge vartaneti bhavati. vartyate vartanamātraṃ vā vartanā iti. dharmādīnāṃ dravyāṇāṃ svaparyāyanivṛttiṃ prati svātmanaiva vartamānānāṃ bāhyopagrahād vinā tadvṛttyabhāvāt tatpravartanopalakṣitaḥ kāla iti kṛtvā vartanā kālasyopakāraḥ. ko nij arthaḥ? vartate dravyaparyāyas tasya vartayitā kālaḥ. yady evaṃ kālasya kriyāvattvaṃ prāpnoti. yathā śiṣyo ’dhīte, upādhyāyo ’dhyāpayatīti? naiṣa doṣaḥ; nimittamātre ’pi hetukartṛ vyapadeśo dṛṣṭaḥ. yathā
kārīṣo ’gnir adhyāpayati
children.translated_text: 'Cow-dung fire cooks [things]'

children.text: . evaṃ kālasya hetukartṛtā. sa kathaṃ kāla ity avasīyate? samayādīnāṃ kriyāviśeṣāṇāṃ samayādibhir nirvartyamānānāṃ ca pākādīnāṃ samayaḥ pāka ity evam ādi svasaṃjñārūḍhisadbhāve ’pi samayaḥ kālaḥ odanapākaḥ kāla iti adhyāropyamāṇaḥ kālavyapadeśas tadvyapadeśanimittasya kālasyāstitvaṃ gamayati. kutaḥ? gauṇasya mukhyāpekṣatvāt. dravyasya paryāyo dharmāntaranivṛttidharmāntaropajananarūpaḥ aparispandātmakaḥ pariṇāmaḥ. jīvasya krodhādiḥ, pudgalasya varṇādiḥ. dharmādharmākāśānām agurulaghuguṇavṛddhihānikṛtaḥ. kriyā parispandātmikā. sā dvividhā; prāyogikavaisrasikabhedāt. tatra prāyogikī śakaṭādīnām, vaisrasikī meghādīnām. paratvāparatve kṣetrakṛte kālakṛte ca staḥ. tatra kālopakāraprakaraṇāt kālakṛte gṛhyete. ta ete vartanādaya upakārāḥ kālasyāstitvaṃ gamayanti. nanu ‘vartanā’ grahaṇam evāstu, tadbhedāḥ pariṇāmādayas teṣāṃ pṛthaggrahaṇam anarthakam? nānarthakam; kāladvayasūchanārthatvat prapañcasya. kālo hi dvividhaḥ paramārthakālo vyavahārakālaś ca. paramārthakālo vartanālakṣaṇaḥ. pariṇāmādilakṣaṇo vyavahārakālaḥ. anyena paricchinnaḥ anyasya paricchedahetuḥ kriyāviśeṣaḥ kāla iti vyavahriyate. sa tridhā vyavatiṣṭhate — bhūto vartamāno bhaviṣyann iti. tatra paramārthakāle kālavyapadeśo mukhyaḥ. bhūtādivyapadeśo gauṇaḥ. vyavahārakāle bhūtādivyapadeśo mukhyaḥ. kālavyapadeśo gauṇaḥ; kriyāvaddravyāpekṣatvāt kālakṛtatvāc ca. atrāha, dharmādharmākāśapudgalajīvakālānām upakārā uktāḥ. lakṣaṇaṃ coktam ‘upayogo lakṣaṇam’ ity evam ādi. pudgalānāṃ nu sāmānyalakṣaṇam uktam ‘ajīvakāyāḥ’ iti. viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ noktam. tat kim ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: — thus time has the role of auxiliary cause. How is it ascertained to be time? Because [we say] 'an instant is a cooking' — i.e., the instant is [identified with] the particular activities such as cooking and the like that are accomplished by instants and other [time-units].

§ 569. From the causal stem '<s>vṛt</s>' with <s>ṇic</s> (causative), [with the suffix] <s>yut</s> in the feminine, it becomes <s>vartanā</s>. It means: 'causing to continue' or 'mere continuation.' The non-disrupted continuation of the own modes of substances such as <s>dharma</s> and the rest [is <s>vartanā</s>].

children.text: sparśarasagandhavarṇavantaḥ pudgalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pudgalas</s> (matter-particles) possess touch (<s>sparśa</s>), taste (<s>rasa</s>), smell (<s>gandha</s>), and color (<s>varṇa</s>).

children.text: § 570. sprśyate sparśanamātraṃ vā sparśaḥ. so ’ṣṭavidhaḥ; mṛdukaṭhinagurulaghuśītoṣṇasnigdharūkṣabhedāt. rasyate rasanamātraṃ vā rasaḥ. sa pañcavidhaḥ; tiktāmlakaṭukamadhurakaṣāyabhedāt. gandhyate gandhanamātraṃ vā gandhaḥ. sa dvedhā; surabhir asurabhir iti. varṇyate varṇanamātraṃ vā varṇaḥ. sa pañcavidhaḥ; kṛṣṇalīlapītaśuklalohitabhedāt. ta ete mūlabhedāḥ pratyekaṃ saṃkheyāsaṃkhyeyānantabhedāś ca bhavanti. sparśaś ca rasaś ca gandhaś ca varṇaś ca sparśarasagandhavarṇās ta eteṣāṃ santīti sparśarasagandhavarṇavanta iti. nityayoge matunirdeśaḥ. yathā kṣīriṇo nyagrodhā iti. nanu ca rūpiṇaḥ pudgalā ity atra pudgalānāṃ rūpavattvam uktaṃ tadavinābhāvinaś ca rasādayas tatraiva parigṛhītā iti vyākhyātaṃ tasmāt tenaiva pudgalānāṃ rūpādimattvasiddheḥ sūtram idam anarthakam iti? naiṣa doṣaḥ; ‘nityāvasthitāny arūpāṇi’ ity atra dharmādīnāṃ nityatvādinirūpaṇena pudgalānām arūpitvaprasaṃge tadapākaraṇārthaṃ taduktam. idaṃ tu teṣām svarūpaviśeṣapratipattyartham ucyate.
children.translated_text: § 570. <s>Sparśa</s> (touch) is that which is touched, or mere touching. It is eightfold: soft, hard, heavy, light, cold, hot, smooth, and rough. <s>Rasa</s> (taste) is that which is tasted, or mere tasting. It is fivefold: pungent, bitter, astringent, sour, and sweet. <s>Gandha</s> (smell) is that which is smelled, or mere smelling. It is twofold: fragrant and foul. <s>Varṇa</s> (color) is that which is colored, or mere coloring. It is fivefold: black, blue, red, yellow, and white. One <s>sparśa</s>, one <s>rasa</s>, one <s>gandha</s>, and one <s>varṇa</s> — these are the minimum. Five <s>sparśas</s>, five <s>rasas</s>, two <s>gandhas</s>, and five <s>varṇas</s> — these are the maximum. [Objection:] All eight <s>sparśas</s> should be the maximum. [Reply:] No; because soft-hard, heavy-light, cold-hot, and smooth-rough are mutually contradictory. Just as blackness and whiteness cannot exist simultaneously in one place, so soft and hard [cannot coexist] — thus there should be no doubt.

children.text: § 571. avaśiṣṭapudgalavikārapratippattyartam idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 571. To understand the remaining modifications of <s>pudgala</s>, this is stated —

children.text: śabdabandhasaukṣmyasthaulyasaṃsthānabhedatamaśchāyātapodyotavantaś ca ||
children.translated_text: And [<s>pudgalas</s> (matter)] possess <s>śabda</s> (sound), <s>bandha</s> (binding), <s>saukṣmya</s> (subtlety), <s>sthaulya</s> (grossness), <s>saṃsthāna</s> (shape), <s>bheda</s> (division), <s>tamas</s> (darkness), <s>chāyā</s> (shadow), <s>ātapa</s> (sunlight), and <s>udyota</s> (luminosity).

children.text: § 572. śabdo dvividhaḥ bhāṣālakṣaṇo viparītaś ceti. bhāṣālakṣaṇo dvividhaḥ — sākṣaro ’nakṣaraś ceti. akṣarīkṛtaḥ śāstrābhivyañjakaḥ saṃskṛtaviparītabhedād āryamlecchavyavahārahetuḥ. anakṣarātmako dvīndriyādīnām atiśayajñānasvarūpapratipādanahetuḥ. sa eṣa sarvaḥ prāyogikaḥ. abhāṣātmako dvividhaḥ prāyogiko vaisrasikaś ceti. vaisrasiko valāhakādiprabhavaḥ. prāyogikaś caturdhā, tatavitataghanasauṣirabhedāt. tatra carmatanananimittaḥ puṣkarabherīdardurādiprabhavas tataḥ. tantrīkṛtavīṇāsughoṣādisamudbhavo vitataḥ. tālaghaṇṭālālanādyabhighātajo ghanaḥ. vaṃśaśaṃkhādinimittaḥ sauṣiraḥ. bandho dvividhaḥ–vaisrasikaḥ prāyogikaś ca. puruṣaprayogānapekṣo vaisrasikaḥ. tad yathā–snigdharūkṣatvaguṇanimitto vidyudulkājaladhārāgnīndradhanurādivṣayaḥ. puruṣaprayoganimittaḥ prāyogikaḥ ajīvaviṣayo jīvājīvaviṣayaś ceti dvidhā bhinnaḥ. tatrājīvaviṣayo jatukāṣṭhādilakṣaṇaḥ. jīvājīvaviṣayaḥ karmanokarmabandhaḥ. saukṣmyaṃ dvividhaṃ — antyam āpekṣikaṃ ca. tatrāntyaṃ paramāṇūnāṃ. āpekṣikaṃ vilvāmalakabadarādīnām. sthaulyam api dvividham antyam āpekṣikaṃ ceti. tatrāntyaṃ jagadvyāpini mahāskandhe. āpekṣikam badarāmalakavilvatālādiṣu. saṃsthānam ākṛtiḥ. tad dvividham — itthaṃlakṣaṇam anitthaṃlakṣaṇaṃ ceti. vṛttatryasracaturasrāyataparimaṇḍalādīnām itthaṃlakṣaṇam. ato ’nyan meghādīnāṃ saṃsthānam anekavidham ittham idam iti nirūpaṇābhāvād anitthaṃlakṣaṇam. bhedāḥ ṣoḍhā; utkaracūrṇakhaṇḍacūrṇikāpratarāṇucaṭanavikalpāt. tatrotkaraḥ kāṣṭhādīnāṃ karapatrādibhir utkaraṇam. cūrṇo yavagodhūmādīnāṃ saktukaṇikādiḥ. khaṇḍo ghaṭādīnāṃ kapālaśarkarādiḥ. cūrṇikā māṣamudgādīnām. prataro ’bhrapaṭalādīnām. aṇucaṭanaṃ san taptāyaḥ piṇḍādiṣu ayoghanādibhir abhihanyamāneṣu sphuliṅganirgamaḥ. tamo dṛṣṭipratibandhakāraṇaṃ prakāśavirodhi. chāyā prakāśāvaraṇanimittā. sā dvedhā — varṇādivikārapariņatā pratibimbhamātrātmikā ceti. ātapa ādityādinimitta uṣṇaprakāśalakṣaṇaḥ. udyotaś candramaṇikhadyotādiprabhavaḥ prakāśaḥ. ta ete śabdādayaḥ pudgaladravyavikārāḥ. ta eṣāṃ santīti śabdabandhasaukṣmyasthaulyasaṃsthānabhedatamaśchāyātapodyotavantaḥ. pudgalā ity abhisaṃbadyate. ‘ca’ śabdena nodanābhighātādayaḥ pudgalapariṇāmā āgame prasiddhāḥ samuccīyante.
children.translated_text: § 572. <s>Śabda</s> (sound) is of two kinds: that which has the character of language and that which is the opposite. That which has the character of language is of two kinds — with syllables and without syllables. That which is formed into syllables, being expressive of treatises, is the cause of the transactions of the <s>Āryas</s> and <s>Mlecchas</s>, through the distinction of <s>Saṃskṛta</s> and its opposite. That which is without syllables is the cause of conveying the nature of extraordinary knowledge for two-sensed beings and above. All of this is produced by effort. That which is not of the nature of language is of two kinds — produced by effort and spontaneous. The spontaneous arises from clouds and the like. That produced by effort is fourfold, due to the distinction of <s>tata</s> (stretched-skin), <s>vitata</s> (stringed), <s>ghana</s> (solid), and <s>sauṣira</s> (hollow). Among these, <s>tata</s> is caused by the stretching of skin, produced from drums such as <s>puṣkara</s>, <s>bherī</s>, and <s>dardura</s>. <s>Vitata</s> arises from stringed instruments such as <s>vīṇā</s> and <s>sughoṣa</s>. <s>Ghana</s> is produced by striking cymbals, bells, gongs, and the like. <s>Sauṣira</s> is caused by flutes, conches, and the like. <s>Bandha</s> (binding) is of two kinds — spontaneous and produced by effort. That which does not depend on human effort is spontaneous, such as that caused by the qualities of smoothness and roughness, having as its domain lightning, meteors, streams of water, fire, rainbows, and the like. That caused by human effort is <s>prāyogika</s>, which is divided into two: pertaining to non-living matter alone, and pertaining to both living and non-living. Of these, that pertaining to non-living matter is exemplified by lac, wood, and the like. That pertaining to both living and non-living is the binding of <s>karma</s> and <s>nokarma</s>. <s>Saukṣmya</s> (subtlety) is of two kinds — ultimate and relative. The ultimate belongs to <s>paramāṇus</s> (atoms). The relative belongs to wood-apples, myrobalans, jujubes, and the like. <s>Sthaulya</s> (grossness) is also of two kinds — ultimate and relative. The ultimate belongs to the great aggregate that pervades the universe. The relative belongs to jujubes, myrobalans, wood-apples, palm trees, and the like. <s>Saṃsthāna</s> (shape) is configuration. It is of two kinds — definable and indefinable. The definable includes circular, triangular, quadrilateral, elongated, spherical, and so forth. Other than these, the shape of clouds and the like, being of many kinds and impossible to determine as 'it is thus,' is indefinable. <s>Bheda</s> (division) is sixfold: by the varieties of sawing, grinding, breaking, splitting, slicing, and splintering. Among these, sawing is the cutting of wood and the like with saws and similar tools. Grinding is the production of flour and meal from barley, wheat, and the like. Breaking is the shattering of pots and the like into potsherds and gravel. Splitting pertains to black gram, mung beans, and the like. Slicing pertains to layers of clouds and the like. Splintering is the emission of sparks when heated iron lumps and the like are struck with iron hammers and similar implements. <s>Tamas</s> (darkness) is the cause of obstruction to vision and is opposed to light. <s>Chāyā</s> (shadow) is caused by the obstruction of light. It is of two kinds — that which transforms into color and so forth, and that which is merely a reflection. <s>Ātapa</s> (sunlight) is caused by the sun and the like, characterized by heat and light. <s>Udyota</s> (luminosity) is the light produced from the moon, gems, fireflies, and the like. These — sound and the rest — are modifications of the substance <s>pudgala</s> (matter). They possess these, hence [they are called] possessing sound, binding, subtlety, grossness, shape, division, darkness, shadow, sunlight, and luminosity. The word '<s>pudgala</s>' is to be connected [from the previous sūtra]. By the word 'and,' <s>nodanā</s> (impulse), <s>abhighāta</s> (impact), and other modifications of <s>pudgala</s> that are well-known in the <s>Āgama</s> are included.

children.text: § 573. uktānāṃ pudgalānāṃ bhedapradarśanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 573. In order to show the divisions of the aforementioned <s>pudgalas</s> (matter), [the author] states —

children.text: aṇavaḥ skhandāś ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aṇus</s> (atoms) and <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates).

children.text: § 574. pradeśamātrabhāvisparśādiparyāyaprasavasāmarthyenāṇyante śabdyanta ity aṇavaḥ. saukṣmyād ātmādaya ātmamadhyā ātmāntāś ca. uktaṃ ca —
attādi attamajjhaṃ attaṃtaṃ ṇeva iṃdiye gejjhaṃ |
children.translated_text: Having itself as beginning, itself as middle, and itself as end, not graspable by the senses,

children.text: jaṃ davvaṃ avibhāgī taṃ paramāṇuṃ viāṇāhi ||
children.translated_text: that substance which is indivisible — know that to be the <s>paramāṇu</s> (ultimate atom).

children.text: sthūlabhāvena grahaṇanikṣepaṇādivyāpāraskandhanāt skandhā iti saṃjñāyante. rūḍhau kriyā kvacit satī upalakṣaṇatvenāśrīyate iti grahaṇādivyāpārāyogyeṣv api dvyaṇukādiṣu skandhākhyā pravartate. anantabhedā api pudgalā aṇujātyā skandhajātyā ca dvaividhyam āpadyamānāḥ sarve gṛhyanta iti tajjātyādhārānantabhedasaṃsūcanārthaṃ bahuvacanaṃ kriyate. aṇavaḥ skandā iti bhedābhidhānaṃ pūrvoktasūtradvayabhedasaṃbandhanārtham. sparśarasagandhavarṇavanto ’ṇavaḥ. skandhāh punaḥ śabdabandhasaukṣmyasthaulyasaṃsthānabhedatamaśchāyātapodyotavantaś ca sparśādimantaś ceti.
children.translated_text: They are designated as <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) because of the activity of grasping, depositing, and so forth in their gross state. In established usage, an action that sometimes exists is taken as a characterizing mark, and therefore the designation '<s>skandha</s>' applies even to dyads and the like that are incapable of being grasped. Though <s>pudgalas</s> (matter) have infinite divisions, all are comprehended under the twofold classification of the atomic kind and the aggregate kind; hence the plural is used to indicate the infinite divisions based on those kinds. The statement of division as '<s>aṇus</s>' and '<s>skandhas</s>' serves to connect with the distinction made in the two preceding <s>sūtras</s>. <s>Aṇus</s> (atoms) possess touch, taste, smell, and color. <s>Skandhas</s> (aggregates), moreover, possess sound, binding, subtlety, grossness, shape, division, darkness, shadow, sunlight, and luminosity, as well as touch and the rest.

§ 574. They are called <s>aṇus</s> (atoms) because they are sounded forth — that is, made known — by virtue of their capacity for the production of modes such as touch, which exist in a single spatial point. Due to their subtlety, they have themselves as their beginning, themselves as their middle, and themselves as their end. And it has been said —

children.text: § 575. āha, kim eṣāṃ pudgalānām aṇuskandhalakṣaṇaḥ pariṇāmo ’nādir uta ādimān ity ucyate. sa khalūtpattimattvād ādimān pratijñāyate. yady evaṃ tasmād abhidhīyatāṃ kasmān nimittād utpadyanta iti. tatra skandhānāṃ tāvad utpattihetupratipādanārtham ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 575. One asks: is this transformation of <s>pudgalas</s> (matter) into atoms and aggregates beginningless, or does it have a beginning? It is maintained to have a beginning, since it is subject to origination. If so, then let it be stated from what cause they originate. To explain the cause of origination of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), [the author] states —

children.text: bhedasaṃghātebhya utpadyante ||
children.translated_text: They originate from division and combination.

children.text: § 576. saṃghātānāṃ dvitayanimittavaśād vidāraṇam bhedaḥ. pṛthagbhūtānām ekatvāpattiḥ saṃghātaḥ. nanu ca dvitvād dvivacanena bhavitavyam. bahuvacananirdeśas tritayasaṃgrahārthaḥ. bhedāt saṃghātād bhedasaṃghātābhyām ca utpadyanta iti. tad yathā — dvayoḥ paramāṇvoḥ saṃghātād dvipradeśaḥ skandha utpadyate. dvipradeśasyāṇoś ca trayāṇām vā aṇūnāṃ saṃghātāt tripradeśaḥ. dvayor dvipradeśayos tripradeśasyāṇoś ca caturṇāṃ vā aṇūnāṃ saṃghātāc catuḥpradeśaḥ. evaṃ saṃkheyāsaṃkhyeyānantānām anantānantānāṃ ca saṃghātāt tāvat pradeśaḥ. eṣām eva bhedāt tāvad dvipradeśaparyantāḥ skandhā utpadyante. evaṃ bhedasaṃghātābhyām ekasamayikābhyāṃ dvipradeśādayaḥ skandhā utpadyante. anyato bhedenānyasya saṃghāteneti. evaṃ skandhānām utpattihetur uktaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 576. <s>Bheda</s> (division) is the splitting of combinations due to the force of two causes. <s>Saṃghāta</s> (combination) is the coming together into unity of separate entities. Now, since there are two [causes], a dual number should have been used. The use of the plural is for the purpose of including a third [possibility]. They originate from division, from combination, and from both division and combination. For example: from the combination of two <s>paramāṇus</s> (atoms), an aggregate of two spatial points originates. From the combination of a two-point aggregate with an atom, or of three atoms, a three-point [aggregate] arises. From the combination of two two-point aggregates, or of a three-point aggregate with an atom, or of four atoms, a four-point [aggregate] arises. In this way, from the combination of countable, uncountable, infinite, and infinitely infinite [atoms], aggregates of that many spatial points [arise]. From the division of these same, aggregates down to two spatial points originate. Thus, from both division and combination occurring simultaneously, aggregates of two spatial points and more originate — by division of one and combination with another. Thus the cause of origination of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) has been stated.

children.text: § 577. aṇor utpattihetupradarśanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 577. In order to show the cause of origination of the <s>aṇu</s> (atom), [the author] states —

children.text: bhedād aṇuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>aṇu</s> (atom) [arises] from division.

children.text: siddhe vidhir ārabhyamāṇo niyamārtho bhavati.
children.translated_text: A positive rule stated where the result is already established serves the purpose of restriction.

children.text: aṇor utpattir bhedād eva, na saṃghātān nāpi bhedasaṃghātābhyām iti.
children.translated_text: The origination of an <s>aṇu</s> (atom) is from division alone — not from combination, nor from both division and combination.

children.text: § 579. āha, saṃghātād eva skandhānām ātmalābhe siddhe bhedasaṃghātagrahaṇam anarthakam iti tadgrahaṇaprayojanapratipādanārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 579. One objects: since the origination of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) from combination alone is already established, the mention of both division and combination is purposeless. To explain the purpose of that mention, [the author] states —

children.text: bhedasaṃghātābhyāṃ cākṣuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through division and combination, [an aggregate becomes] visible.

children.text: § 580. anantānantapramāṇusamudayaniṣpādyo ’pi kaścic cākṣuṣaḥ kaścid acākṣuṣaḥ. tatra yo ’cākṣuṣaḥ sa kathaṃ cākṣuṣo bhavatīti ced ucyate — bhedasaṃghātābhyāṃ cākṣuṣaḥ. na bhedād iti. kātropapattir iti cet? brūmaḥ; sūkṣmapariṇāmasya skandhasya bhede saukṣmyāparityāgād acākṣuṣatvam eva. saukṣmyapariṇataḥ punar aparaḥ saty api tadbhede ’nyasaṃghātāntarasaṃyogāt saukṣmyapariṇamoparame sthaulyotpattau cākṣuṣo bhavati.
children.translated_text: § 580. Even an aggregate composed of infinitely infinite <s>paramāṇus</s> (atoms) may be either visible or invisible. If one asks how that which is invisible becomes visible, the answer is: through division and combination it becomes visible — not through division alone. Where is this applicable? We say: when an aggregate in a subtle state is divided, since it does not abandon its subtlety, it remains invisible. But when another aggregate, though in a subtle state, upon being divided and combined with a different aggregate, ceases its subtle modification and grossness arises, it becomes visible.

children.text: § 581. āha, dharmādīnām dravyāṇāṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇāny uktāni, sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ noktam, tadvaktavyam. ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 581. One asks: the specific characteristics of substances such as <s>dharma</s> and the rest have been stated, but the general characteristic has not been stated; that should be stated. [The author] states —

children.text: sad dravyalakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Existence is the defining characteristic of substance.

children.text: § 582. yat sat tad dravyam ity arthaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 582. The meaning is: whatever exists, that is <s>dravya</s> (substance).

children.text: § 583. yady evaṃ tad eva tāvad vaktavyaṃ kiṃ sat. ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 583. If so, then first of all this should be stated: what is existence? Therefore [the author] states —

children.text: utpādavyayadhrauvyayuktaṃ sat ||
children.translated_text: That which is endowed with origination, decay, and permanence is existent.

children.text: § 584. cetanasyācetanasya vā dravyasya svāṃ jātim ajahata ubhayanimittavaśād bhāvāntarāvāptir utpādanam utpādaḥ mṛtpiṇḍasya ghaṭaparyāyavat. tathā pūrvabhāvavigamanaṃ vyayaḥ. yathā ghaṭotpattau piṇḍākṛte. anādipāriṇāmikasvabhāvena vyayodayābhāvād dhruvati sthirībhavatīti dhruvaḥ. dhruvasya bhāvaḥ karma vā dhrauvyam. yathā mṛtpiṇḍaghaṭādyavasthāsu mṛdādyanvayaḥ. tair utpādavyayadhrauvyair yuktaṃ utpādavyayadhrauvyayuktaṃ sad iti.

āha, bhede sati yuktaśabdo dṛṣṭaḥ. yathā daṇḍena yukto devadatta iti. tathā sati teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ tair yuktasya dravyasya cābhāvaḥ prāpnoti? naiṣa doṣaḥ; abhede ’pi kathaṃcid bhedanayāpekṣayā yuktaśabdo dṛṣṭaḥ. yathā sārayuktaḥ sthambha iti. tathā sati teṣām avinābhāvāt sadvyapadeśo yuktaḥ. samādhivacano vā yuktaśabdaḥ. yuktaḥ samāhitas tadātmaka ity arthaḥ. utpādavyayadhrauvyayuktaṃ sat utpādavyayadhrauvyātmakam iti yāvat. etad uktaṃ bhavati — utpādādīni dravyasya lakṣaṇāni. dravyaṃ lakṣyam. tatra paryāyārthikanayāpekṣayā parasparato dravyāc cārthāntarabhāvaḥ. dravyārthikanayāpekṣayā vyatirekeṇānupalabdher anarthāntarabhāvaḥ. iti lakṣyalakṣaṇabhāvasiddhiḥ.
children.translated_text: One objects: the word 'endowed' (<s>yukta</s>) is seen [used] where there is difference, as in '<s>Devadatta</s> endowed with a staff.' If so, then the three [attributes] and the substance endowed with them would be [entirely] separate — which would entail their non-existence [as intrinsic properties]. This is no fault; the word 'endowed' is also seen where there is [essential] non-difference, by taking recourse to the standpoint that distinguishes, as in 'a pillar endowed with substance.' If so, then since they are inseparable, the designation 'existent' is appropriate. Alternatively, the word 'endowed' (<s>yukta</s>) means 'concentrated' — that is, composed of, having that nature. 'Endowed with origination, decay, and permanence' means having origination, decay, and permanence as its very nature. What is meant is this: origination and the rest are the characteristics of substance; substance is what is characterized. From the standpoint of the <s>paryāyārthika naya</s> (modal viewpoint), they are mutually distinct and distinct from the substance. From the standpoint of the <s>dravyārthika naya</s> (substantive viewpoint), since they cannot be apprehended in separation, they are non-different. Thus the relationship of characterized and characteristic is established.

§ 584. For a substance, whether sentient or insentient, <s>utpāda</s> (origination) is the attainment of a different state due to the force of both [causes], without abandoning its own class — like a lump of clay [attaining] the mode of a pot. Likewise, <s>vyaya</s> (decay) is the departure from the previous state, as the form of the lump [departs] upon the origination of the pot. Due to its beginningless, transformative nature, because there is no [absolute] destruction or [absolute] origination, it endures — becomes stable — this is <s>dhruva</s> (permanence). The state or nature of what is permanent is <s>dhrauvya</s> (permanence). Just as clay and the like persist through the states of lump, pot, and so forth. That which is endowed with origination, decay, and permanence — [that is] <s>sat</s> (existent).

children.text: § 585. āha ‘nityāvasthitāny arūpāṇi’ ity uktaṃ tatra na jñāyate kiṃ nityam ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 585. One asks: it was stated that [<s>dharma</s> and the rest are] 'eternal, stable, and formless' — there it is not known what is meant by eternal. Therefore [the author] states —

children.text: tadbhāvāvyayaṃ nityam ||
children.translated_text: That which does not lose its own nature is eternal.

children.text: § 586. ‘tadbhāvaḥ’ ity ucyate. kas tadbhāvaḥ? pratyabhijñānahetutā. tad evedam iti smaraṇaṃ pratyabhijñānam. tad akasmān na bhavatīti yo ’sya hetuḥ sa tadbhāvaḥ. bhavanaṃ bhāvaḥ. tasya bhāvas tadbhāvaḥ. yenātmanā prāgdṛṣṭaṃ vastu tenaivātmanā punar api bhāvāt tad evedam iti pratyabhijñāyate. yady atyantanirodho ’bhinavaprādurbhāvamātram eva vā syāt tataḥ smaraṇānupapattiḥ. tadadhīno lokasaṃvyavahāro virudhyate. tatas tadabhāvenāvyayaṃ tadbhāvāvyayaṃ nityam iti niścīyate. tat tu kathaṃcid veditavyam. sarvathā nityatve anyathābhāvābhāvāt saṃsāratadvinivṛttikāraṇaprakriyāvirodhaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: § 586. '<s>Tadbhāva</s>' (its own nature) is spoken of. What is this own nature? It is being the cause of recognition. 'This is the very same thing' — such recollection is recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>). That does not arise without cause; what is its cause is '<s>tadbhāva</s>' (its own nature). Becoming is <s>bhāva</s>; the state of that is <s>tadbhāva</s>. Because the object previously perceived is perceived again with the very same nature, it is recognized as 'this is the very same thing.' If there were complete annihilation or merely a fresh appearance, then recollection would be impossible. The worldly transactions dependent on that would be contradicted. Therefore, that which does not lose that [nature] — that which is without loss of its own nature — is ascertained to be eternal. But this should be understood in a qualified sense. If it were eternal in every respect, then since there would be no change whatsoever, there would be a contradiction with the process of <s>saṃsāra</s> and its cessation.

children.text: § 587. nanu idam eva viruddhaṃ tad eva nityaṃ tad evānityam iti. yadi nityaṃ vyayodayābhāvād anityatāvyāghātaḥ. athānityam eva sthityabhāvān nityatāvyāghāta iti? naitad viruddham. kutaḥ —
children.translated_text: § 587. Now, is this not contradictory — that the very same thing is both eternal and non-eternal? If it is eternal, then due to the absence of decay and origination, non-eternality would be contradicted. If it is simply non-eternal, then due to the absence of persistence, eternality would be contradicted. This is not contradictory. Why? —

children.text: arpitānarpitasiddheḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of the establishment through the focused and the non-focused [viewpoints].

children.text: § 588. anekāntātmakasya vastunaḥ prayojanavaśād yasya kasyacid dharmasya vivakṣayā prāpitaṃ prādhānyam arpitam upanītam iti yāvat. tadviparītam anarpitam. prayojanābhāvāt sato ’py avivakṣā bhavatīty upasarjanībhūtam anarpitam ity ucyate. arpitaṃ cānarpitaṃ cārpitānanarpite. tābhyāṃ siddher arpitānanarpitasiddher nāsti virodhaḥ. tad yathā — ekasya devadattasya pitā putro bhrātā bhāgineya ity evam ādayaḥ saṃbandhā janakatvajanyatvādinimittā na virudhyante; arpaṇābhedāt. putrāpekṣayā pitā, pitrapekṣayā putra ity evam ādiḥ. tathā dravyam api sāmānyārpaṇayā nityam, viśeṣārpaṇayānityam iti nāsti virodhaḥ. tau ca sāmānyaviśeṣau kathaṃcid bhedābhedābhyāṃ vyavahārahetū bhavataḥ.
children.translated_text: § 588. For a reality that has a manifold nature, when by reason of a [particular] purpose the prominence of some property is intended, that is <s>arpita</s> (focused) — brought to the fore. The opposite is <s>anarpita</s> (non-focused). Due to the absence of purpose, even though [a property] exists, there is non-intention regarding it — thus what has become subordinate is called <s>anarpita</s>. Both the focused and the non-focused together are <s>arpitānarpita</s>. Because of the establishment through these two — through the establishment of the focused and the non-focused — there is no contradiction.
