For example, one and the same <s>Devadatta</s> has the relationships of father, son, brother, nephew, and so forth, caused by the conditions of being a progenitor, being produced, and the like — and these do not contradict each other, because of the non-difference of the focusing. In relation to his son, he is a father; in relation to his father, he is a son — and so forth. Likewise, a substance too is eternal when focused on from the standpoint of the universal, and non-eternal when focused on from the standpoint of the particular — thus there is no contradiction. And those two — the universal and the particular — are in some sense both different and non-different, and serve as the basis of conventional usage.

children.text: § 589. atrāha, sato ’nekanayavyavahāratantratvāt upapannā bhedasaṃghātebhyaḥ satāṃ skandhātmanotpattiḥ. idaṃ tu saṃdigdham, kiṃ saṃghātaḥ saṃyogād eva dvyaṇukādilakṣaṇo bhavati, uta kaścid viśeṣo ’vadhriyata iti? ucyate, ‘sati saṃyoge bandhād ekatvapariṇāmātmakāt saṃghāto niṣpadyate. yady evam idam ucyatāṃ, kuto nu khalu pudgalajātyaparityāge saṃyoge ca sati bhavati keṣāṃcid bandho ’nyeṣāṃ ca neti? ucyate, yasmāt teṣāṃ pudgalātmāviśeṣe ’py anantaparyāyāṇāṃ parasparavilakṣaṇapariṇāmād āhitasāmartyād bhavanpratītaḥ —
children.translated_text: § 589. Here one says: Since [reality], by virtue of being governed by the convention of multiple standpoints (<s>naya</s>), allows for the origination of aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) from the combination and division of existing [entities]—this is established. But this is uncertain: does the aggregate arise from mere conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) alone, in the form of dyads (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>) etc., or is some specific [factor] determined [to be necessary]? It is said: 'Given conjunction, from bonding (<s>bandha</s>)—whose nature is the transformation into unity—the aggregate is produced.' If so, let this be stated: Why is it that, when the nature of <s>pudgala</s> (matter) is not abandoned and conjunction exists, bonding occurs for some [particles] but not for others? It is said: Because, even though these <s>pudgalas</s> do not differ in their nature, being possessed of infinite modes and having acquired the capacity [for bonding] through their mutually distinct transformations, [bonding] is understood [to occur]—

children.text: snigdharūkṣatvād bandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Bonding (<s>bandha</s>) is due to oiliness (<s>snigdha</s>) and dryness (<s>rūkṣa</s>). ||

children.text: § 590. bāhyābhyantarakāraṇavaśāt snehaparyāyāvirbhāvāt snihyate smeti snigdhaḥ. tathā rūkṣaṇād rūkṣaḥ. snigdhaś ca rūkṣaś ca snigdharūkṣau. tayor bhāvaḥ snigdharūkṣatvam. snigdhatvaṃ cikkaṇaguṇalakṣaṇaḥ paryāyaḥ. tadviparītapariṇāmo rūkṣatvam. ‘snigdharūkṣatvāt’ iti hetunirdeśaḥ. tatkṛto bandho dvyaṇukādipariṇāmaḥ. dvayoḥ snigdharūkṣayor aṇvoḥ parasparaśleṣalakṣaṇe bandhe sati dvyaṇukaskandho bhavati. evaṃ saṃkhyeyāsaṃkheyānantapradeśaḥ skandho yojyaḥ. tatra snehaguṇa ekadvitricatuḥ saṃkhyeyāsaṃkheyānantavikalpaḥ. tathā rūkṣaguṇo ’pi. tadguṇāḥ paramāṇavaḥ santi. yathā toyājāgomahiṣyuṣṭrīkṣīraghṛteṣu snehaguṇaḥ prakarṣāprakarśeṇa pravartate. pāṃśukaṇikāśarkarādiṣu ca rūkṣaguṇo dṛṣṭaḥ. tathā paramāṇuṣv api snigdharūkṣaguṇayor vṛttiḥ prakarṣāprakarśeṇānumīyate.
children.translated_text: § 590. Due to the influence of external and internal causes, from the manifestation of the mode of oiliness, [a particle] 'becomes oily'—hence it is 'oily' (<s>snigdha</s>). Likewise, from drying, [it is] 'dry' (<s>rūkṣa</s>). Oily and dry together are '<s>snigdharūkṣa</s>.' Their state is '<s>snigdharūkṣatva</s>' (oiliness and dryness). Oiliness is a mode characterized by the quality of smoothness (<s>cikkaṇa</s>). The opposite transformation is dryness (<s>rūkṣatva</s>). '<s>Snigdharūkṣatvāt</s>' is a statement of the cause. The bonding caused by that is the transformation into dyads (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>) etc. When two atoms, [one] oily and [one] dry, undergo bonding—characterized by mutual adhesion—a dyadic aggregate (<s>dvyaṇukaskandha</s>) arises. Similarly, aggregates of numerable, innumerable, and infinite spatial units should be understood. Among these, the quality of oiliness admits varieties of one, two, three, four, numerable, innumerable, and infinite [degrees]. Likewise the quality of dryness. Atoms possess these qualities. Just as in the milks and ghees of cows, she-buffaloes, and camels, the quality of oiliness operates in greater and lesser degrees; and in dust particles, grains of sand, etc., the quality of dryness is observed—so too in atoms, the operation of the qualities of oiliness and dryness in greater and lesser degrees is inferred.

children.text: § 591. snigdharūkṣatvaguṇanimitte bandhe aviśeṣeṇa prasakte aniṣṭaguṇanivṛttyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 591. Since bonding caused by the qualities of oiliness and dryness, without qualification, would apply [universally], in order to exclude undesired [cases], he says—

children.text: na jaghanyaguṇānām ||
children.translated_text: Not for those of the lowest degree of quality. ||

children.text: § 592. jaghanyo nikṛṣṭaḥ. guṇo bhāgaḥ. jaghanyo guṇo yeṣām te jaghanyaguṇāḥ. teṣāṃ jaghanyaguṇānāṃ nāsti bandhaḥ. tad yathā — ekaguṇasnigdhasyaikaguṇasnigdhena dvyādisaṃkhyeyāsaṃkheyānantaguṇasnigdhena vā nāsti bandhaḥ. tasyaivaikaguṇasnigdhasya ekaguṇarūkṣeṇa dvyādisaṃkhyeyāsaṃkheyānantaguṇarūkśeṇa vā nāsti bandhaḥ. tathā ekaguṇarūkṣasyāpi yojyam iti.
children.translated_text: § 592. '<s>Jaghanya</s>' means lowest. '<s>Guṇa</s>' means degree. Those whose degree is the lowest are 'of the lowest degree.' For those of the lowest degree, there is no bonding. Namely: for one of one-degree oiliness, there is no bonding with [another of] one-degree oiliness, nor with [one of] two or more degrees up to numerable, innumerable, or infinite degrees of oiliness. Likewise, for that same one of one-degree oiliness, there is no bonding with [one of] one-degree dryness, nor with two or more degrees up to infinite degrees of dryness. The same should be applied for one of one-degree dryness.

children.text: § 593. etau jaghanyaguṇasnigdharūkṣau varjayitvā anyeṣāṃ snigdhānāṃ rūkṣāṇāṃ ca paraspareṇa bandho bhavatīty aviśeṣeṇa prasaṃge tatrāpi pratiṣedhaviṣayakhyāpanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 593. Excluding these two of lowest-degree oiliness and dryness, the bonding of the remaining oily and dry [particles] with each other occurs. [But there is a question of] whether equals bond—

children.text: guṇasāmye sadṛśānām ||
children.translated_text: When the degrees are equal, [bonding occurs] between those of the same kind. ||

children.text: § 594. ‘sadṛśa’ grahaṇaṃ tulyajatīyasaṃpratyayārtham. ‘guṇasāmya’ grahaṇaṃ tulyabhāgasaṃpratyayārtham. etad uktaṃ bhavati — dviguṇasnigdhānāṃ dviguṇarūkṣaiḥ triguṇasnigdhānāṃ dviguṇarūkṣaiḥ dviguṇasnigdhānāṃ dviguṇasnigdhaiḥ dviguṇarūkṣāṇāṃ dviguṇarūkṣaiś caityevam ādiṣu nāsti bandha iti. yady evaṃ ‘sadṛśa’ grahaṇaṃ kim artham? guṇavaiṣamye sadṛśānām api bandhapratipattyarthaṃ ‘sadṛśa’ grahaṇaṃ kriyate.
children.translated_text: § 594. The inclusion of '<s>sadṛśa</s>' (similar) is for the purpose of understanding 'of the same class.' The inclusion of '<s>guṇasāmya</s>' (equality of degrees) is for the purpose of understanding 'of the same degree.' [When both conditions hold, bonding occurs.]

children.text: § 595. ato viṣamaguṇānāṃ tulyajātīyānām atulyajātīyānām cāniyamena bandhaprasaktau iṣṭārthasaṃpratyayārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 595. Therefore, when bonding would apply without restriction for those of unequal degrees, whether of the same or different class, for the purpose of establishing the intended meaning, he says—

children.text: dvyadhikādiguṇānāṃ tu ||
children.translated_text: But for those with two or more degrees in excess. ||

children.text: § 596. dvābhyāṃ guṇābhyām adhiko dvyadhikaḥ. kaḥ punar asau? caturguṇaḥ. ‘ādi’ śabdaḥ prakārārthaḥ. kaḥ punar asau prakāraḥ? dvyadhikatā. tena pañcaguṇādīnāṃ sampratyayo na bhavati. tena dvyadhikādiguṇānāṃ tulyajātīyānām atulyajātīyānām ca bandha ukto bhavati netareṣām. tad yathā — dviguṇasnigdhasya paramāṇor ekaguṇasnigdhena dviguṇasnigdhena triguṇasnigdhena vā nāsti bandhaḥ. caturguṇasnigdhena punar asti bandhaḥ. tasyaiva punar dviguṇasnigdhasya pañcaguṇasnigdhena ṣaṭsaptāṣṭasaṃkhyeyānantaguṇasnigdhena vā bandho nāsti. evaṃ triguṇasnighdasya pañcaguṇasnigdhena bandho ’sti. śeṣaiḥ pūrvottariar na bhavati. caturguṇasnigdhasya ṣaḍguṇasnigdhenāsti bandhaḥ. śeṣaiḥ pūrvottarair nāsti. evaṃ śeṣeṣv api yojyaḥ. tathā dviguṇarūkṣasya ekadvitriguṇarūkṣair nāsti bandhaḥ. caturguṇarūkṣeṇa tv asti bandhaḥ. tasyaiva dviguṇarūkṣasya pañcaguṇarūkṣādibhir uttariar nāsti bandhaḥ. evaṃ triguṇarūkṣādīnām api dviguṇādhikair bandho yojyaḥ. evaṃ bhinnajātīyeṣv pi yojyaḥ. uktaṃ ca —
ṇiddhassa ṇiddhe ṇa durādhieṇa lukkhassa lukkheṇa durādhieṇa |
children.translated_text: [In Prākrit:] 'Of an oily one with an oily one—not by excess; of a dry one with a dry one—not by excess;

children.text: ṇiddhassa lukkheṇa havei baṃdho jahaṇṇavajjo visame same vā |
children.translated_text: of an oily one with a dry one, bonding occurs, excluding the lowest, whether in unequal or equal [degrees].'

children.text: ‘tu’ śabdo viśeṣaṇārthaḥ. pratiṣedhaṃ vyāvartayati bandhaṃ ca viśeṣayati.
children.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) serves as a qualifier. It excludes the prohibition [stated earlier] and qualifies the bonding.
§ 596. One that is in excess by two degrees is '<s>dvyadhika</s>' (two-excess). Which is that? One of four degrees. The word '<s>ādi</s>' denotes varieties.

children.text: § 597. kim artham adhikaguṇaviṣayo bandho vyākhyāto na samaguṇaviṣaya ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 597. Why is bonding explained with reference to excess degrees and not with reference to equal degrees? To this he says—

children.text: bandhe ’dhikau pariṇāmikau ca ||
children.translated_text: In bonding, the two [that bond] are dominant and subject to transformation (<s>pāriṇāmika</s>). ||

children.text: § 598. adhikārād ‘guṇa’ śabdaḥ saṃbadyate. adhikaguṇāv adhikāv iti. bhāvāntarāpādanaṃ pāriṇāmikatvaṃ klinnaguḍavat. yathā klinno guḍo ’dhikamadhurarasaḥ parītānāṃ reṇvādīnāṃ svaguṇāpādanāt pāriṇāmikaḥ. tathānyo ’py adhikaguṇa alpīyasaḥ pāriṇāmika iti kṛtvā dviguṇādisnigdharūkṣasya caturguṇādisnigdharūkṣaḥ pāriṇāmiko bhavati. tataḥ pūrvāvasthāpracyavanapūrvakaṃ tārtīyikam avasthāntaraṃ prādurbhavatīty ekatvam upapadyate. itarathā hi śuklakṛṣṇatantuvat saṃyoge saty apy apāriṇāmikatvāt sarvaṃ viviktarūpeṇaivāvatiṣṭheta. uktena vidhinā bandhe punaḥ sati jñānāvaraṇādīnāṃ karmaṇāṃ triṃśatsāgaropamakoṭikoṭyādisthitir upapanna bhavati.
children.translated_text: § 598. By context, the word '<s>guṇa</s>' (degree) is connected: 'those with excess degrees are dominant.' Transformation into another state is transformative nature (<s>pāriṇāmikatva</s>).

children.text: § 599. ‘utpādavyayadhrauvyayuktaṃ sat’ iti dravyalakṣaṇam uktaṃ punar apareṇa prakāreṇa dravyalakṣaṇapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 599. The definition of substance (<s>dravya</s>) as 'that which is characterized by origination, destruction, and permanence is existent (<s>sat</s>)' has been stated. Now, another definition of substance is given by a different method—

children.text: guṇaparyayavad dravyam ||
children.translated_text: That which possesses qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) and modes (<s>paryāya</s>) is substance (<s>dravya</s>). ||

children.text: § 600. guṇāś ca paryayāś ca guṇaparyayāḥ. te ’sya santīti guṇaparyayavad dravyam. atra mator utpattāv ukta eva samādhiḥ, kathaṃcid bhedopapatter iti. ke guṇāḥ ke paryāyāḥ? anvayino guṇā vyatirekiṇaḥ paryāyāḥ. ubhayair upetaṃ dravyam iti. uktaṃ ca —
guṇa idi davvavihāṇaṃ davvavikāro hi pajjavo bhaṇido |
children.translated_text: [In Prākrit:] 'A quality is that which constitutes the nature of substance; the modification of substance is declared to be a mode.',

children.text: tehi aṇūṇaṃ davvaṃ ajudapasiddhaṃ have ṇiccaṃ ||
children.translated_text: 'By them, substance, inseparable [from them], is indeed eternal.' ||

children.text:
iti
	  etad uktaṃ bhavati, dravyaṃ dravyāntarād yena viśiṣyate sa guṇaḥ. tena hi tad dravyaṃ vidhīyate. asati tasmin dravyasaṃkaraprasṅgaḥ syāt. tad yathā — jīvaḥ pudgalādibhyo jñānādibhir guṇair viśiṣyate, pudgalādayaś ca rūpādibhiḥ. tataś cāviśeṣe saṃkaraḥ syāt. tataḥ sāmānyāpekṣayā anvayino jñānādayo jīvasya guṇāḥ pudgalādīnāṃ ca rūpādayaḥ. teṣāṃ vikārā viśeṣātmanā bhidyamānāḥ paryāyāḥ. ghaṭajñānaṃ paṭajñānaṃ krodho māno gandho varṇas tīvro manda ity evam ādayaḥ. tebhyo ’nyatvaṃ kathaṃcid āpadyamānaḥ samudāyo dravyavyapadeśabhāk. yadi hi sarvathā samudāyo ’narthāntarabhūta eva syāt sarvābhāvaḥ syāt. tad yathā — parasparavilakṣaṇānāṃ samudāye sati ekānarthāntarabhāvāt samudāyasya sarvābhāvaḥ parasparato ’rthāntarabhūtatvāt. yadi idaṃ rūpaṃ tasmād arthāntarabhūtā rasādayaḥ. tataḥ samudāyo ’narthāntarabhūtaḥ. yaś ca rasādibhyo ’rthantarabhūtād rūpād anarthāntarabhūtaḥ samudāyaḥ sa kathaṃ rasādibhyo ’rthāntarabhūto na bhavet. tataś ca rūpamātraṃ samudāyaḥ prasaktaḥ. na caikaṃ rūpaṃ samudāyo bhavitum arhati. tataḥ samudāyābhāvaḥ. samudāyābhāvāc ca tadanarthāntarabhūtānāṃ samudāyinām apy abhāva iti sarvābhāvaḥ. evaṃ rasādiṣv api yojyam. tasmāt samudāyam icchatā kathaṃcid arthāntarabhāva eṣitavyaḥ.
children.translated_text: This has been said: A quality (<s>guṇa</s>) is that by which a substance is distinguished from another substance. For by it, that substance is characterized
§ 600. Qualities and modes together are '<s>guṇaparyāyas</s>.' That which has them is a substance possessing qualities and modes. Here, from the root <s>mat</s> meaning 'to possess,'

children.text: § 601. uktānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ lakṣaṇanirdeśāt tadviṣaya eva dravyādhyavasāye prasakte anuktadravyasaṃsūcanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 601. Since the definition has been given for the stated substances, and since determination as substance would apply only to those, in order to hint at the unstated substance, he says—

children.text: kālaś ca ||
children.translated_text: And time (<s>kāla</s>) [is also a substance]. ||

children.text: § 602. kim? ‘dravyam’ iti vyākyaśeṣạḥ. kataḥ?

tallakṣaṇopetatvāt. dvividhaṃ lakṣaṇam uktam — ‘utpādavyayadhrauvyayuktaṃ sat’ ‘guṇaparyayavad dravyam’ iti ca. tadubhayaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kālasya vidyate. tad yathā — dhrauvyaṃ tāvat kālasya svapratyayaṃ svabhāvavyavasthānāt. vyayodayau parapratyayau, agurulaghuguṇavṛddhihāny apekṣayā svapratyayau ca. tathā guṇā api kālasya sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇarūpāḥ santi. tatrāsādhāraṇo vartanāhetutvam, sādhāraṇāś cācetanatvāmūrtatvasūkṣmatvāgurulaghutvādayaḥ. paryāyaś ca dravyotpādalakṣaṇā yojyāḥ. tasmād dviprakāralakṣaṇopetatvād ākāśādivat kālasya dravyatvaṃ siddham. tasyāstitvaliṃgaṃ dharmādivad vyākhyātam ‘vartanālakṣaṇaḥ kālaḥ’ iti. nanu kim artham ayaṃ kālaḥ pṛthag ucyate. yatraiva dharmādaya uktās tatraivāyam api vaktavyaḥ ‘ajīvakāyā dharmādharmākāśakālapudgalāḥ’ iti. naivaṃ śaṅkhyam; tatroddeśe sati kāyatvam asya syāt. neṣyate ca mukyopacārapradeśapracayakalpanābhāvāt. dharmādīnaṃ tāvan mukyapradeśapracaya uktaḥ ‘asaṃkhyeyāḥ pradeśāḥ’ ity evam ādinā. aṇor apy ekapradeśasya pūrvottarabhāvaprajñāpananayāpekṣayopacārakalpanayā pradeśapracaya uktaḥ. kālasya punar dvedhāpi pradeśapracayakalpanā nāstīty akāyatvam. api ca tatra pāṭhe ‘niṣkriyāṇi ca’ ity atra dharmādīnām ākāśāntānāṃ niṣkriyatve pratipādite itareṣāṃ jīvapudgalānāṃ sakriyatvaprāptivat kālasyāpi sakriyatvaṃ syāt. athākāśāt prākkāla uddiśyeta. tan na; ‘ā ākāśād ekadravyāṇi’ ity ekadravyatvam asya syāt. tasmāt pṛthag iha kāloddeśaḥ kriyate. anekadravyatve sati kim asya pramāṇam. lokākāśasya yāvantaḥ pradeśās tāvantaḥ kālāṇavo niṣkriyāḥ. ekaikākāśapradeśe ekaikavṛttyā lokaṃ vyāpya vyavasthitāḥ. uktaṃ ca —
children.translated_text: Because it possesses the stated characteristics. The twofold definition has been given: 'that characterized by origination, destruction, and permanence is existent' and 'that which possesses qualities and modes is substance.'

children.text: logāgāsapadese ekkekke je ṭṭhiyā hu ekkakkā |
children.translated_text: [In Prākrit:] 'Those that stand individually, one each, in every spatial unit of the cosmos,

children.text: rayaṇāṇaṃ rāsīviva te kālāṇū muṇeyavvā ||
children.translated_text: like heaps of gems—they should be understood as the atoms of time (<s>kālāṇu</s>).' ||

children.text: rūpādiguṇavirahād amūrtāḥ.
children.translated_text: Due to the absence of qualities such as color (<s>rūpa</s>) etc., [they are] formless (<s>amūrta</s>).
§ 602. What [is time]? 'A substance'—this completes the sentence. How?

children.text: § 603. vartanālakṣaṇasya mukhyasya kālasya pramāṇam uktam. pariṇāmādigamyasya vyavahārakālasya kiṃ pramānam ity ata idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 603. The measure of primary time (<s>kāla</s>), characterized by continuity (<s>vartanā</s>), has been stated. What is the measure of conventional time (<s>vyavahāra-kāla</s>), which is understood through transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) and the like? — to this it is said —

children.text: so ’nantasamayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It [time] consists of infinite instants (<s>ananta-samaya</s>). ||

children.text: § 604. sāmpratikasyaikasamayikatve ’pi atīta anāgatāś ca samayā anantā iti kṛtvā ‘anantasamayaḥ’ ity ucyate. athavā mukhyasyaiva kālasya pramāṇāvadhāraraṇārtham idam ucyate. anantaparyāyavartanāhetutvād eko ’pi kālāṇur ananta ity upacaryate. samayaḥ punaḥ paramaniruddhaḥ kālāṃśas tatpracayaviśeṣa āvalikādir avagantavyaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 604. Although the present is a single instant (<s>ekasamayika</s>), since the past and future instants are infinite, it is said to consist of 'infinite instants.' Alternatively, this is stated for the purpose of determining the measure of primary time itself. Because it is the cause of the occurrence of infinite modes (<s>paryāya</s>), even a single time-atom (<s>kālāṇu</s>) is conventionally designated as 'infinite.' Furthermore, <s>samaya</s> (instant) is the most minute indivisible portion of time; its specific accumulations — <s>āvalikā</s> and the rest — should be understood.

children.text: § 605. āha guṇaparyayavad dravyam ity uktaṃ tatra ke guṇā ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 605. He asks: it was said that a substance (<s>dravya</s>) possesses qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) and modes (<s>paryāya</s>); in that regard, what are the qualities? — to this it is said —

children.text: dravyāśrayā nirguṇā guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) have substance as their substratum and are themselves without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>). ||

children.text: § 606. dravyam āśrayo yeṣāṃ te dravyāśrayāḥ. niṣkrāntā guṇebhyo nirguṇāḥ. evam ubhayalakṣanopetā guṇā iti. ‘nirguṇāḥ’ iti viśeṣaṇaṃ dvyaṇukādinivṛttyartham. tāny api hi kāraṇabhūtaparamāṇudravyāśrayāṇi guṇavanti tu tasmāt ‘nirguṇāḥ’ iti viśeṣaṇāt tāni nivarttitāni bhavanti. nanu paryāyā api ghaṭasaṃsthānādayo dravyāśrayā nirguṇaś ca, teṣām api guṇatvaṃ prāpnoti. ‘dravyāśrayāḥ’ iti vacanāt ‘nityaṃ dravyam āśritya vartante ye’ te guṇā iti viśeṣāt paryāyā nivartitā bhavanti. te hi kādācitkā iti.
children.translated_text: § 606. Those whose substratum is substance are 'substance-dependent' (<s>dravyāśraya</s>). Those that have departed from [further] qualities are 'without qualities' (<s>nirguṇa</s>). Thus, [entities] possessing both characteristics are qualities. The qualifier '<s>nirguṇa</s>' (without qualities) is for the purpose of excluding dyads (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>) and the like. For those too are dependent on the substance of the constituent atoms as their cause, and they possess qualities; therefore, by the qualifier '<s>nirguṇa</s>,' they are excluded. [Objection:] But modes (<s>paryāya</s>) too — such as the configuration of a pot and the like — are substance-dependent and without [further] qualities; so their being [counted as] qualities would follow. [Reply:] From the statement 'substance-dependent,' [the meaning is:] 'those that always exist depending on the substance' are qualities — by this specification, modes are excluded. For they [modes] are occasional (<s>kādācitkā</s>).

children.text: § 607. asakṛt ‘pariṇāma’ śabda uktaḥ. tasya ko ’rtha iti praśne uttaram āha —
children.translated_text: § 607. The word '<s>pariṇāma</s>' (transformation) has been used repeatedly. When asked what its meaning is, he replies —

children.text: tadbhāvaḥ pariṇāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its [substance's] own-nature-becoming (<s>tadbhāva</s>) is <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation). ||

children.text: § 608. athavā guṇā dravyād arthāntarabhūtā iti keṣāṃcid darśanaṃ tat kiṃ bhavato ’bhimatam. na; ity āha — yady api kathaṃcid vyapadeśādibhedahetvapekṣayā dravyād anye, tathāpi tadavyatirekāt tatpariṇāmāc ca nānye. yady evaṃ sa ucyatāṃ kaḥ pariṇāma iti. tanniścayārtham idam ucyate — dharmādīni dravyāṇi yenātmanā bhavanti sa tadbhāvas tattvaṃ pariṇāma iti ākhyāyate. sa dvividho ’nādir ādimāṃś ca. tatrānadir dharmādīnāṃ gatyupagrahādiḥ sāmānyāpekṣayā. sa evādimāṃś ca bhavati viśeṣāpekṣayā iti.
children.translated_text: § 608. Alternatively, some hold the view that qualities are entities distinct from substance — is that your accepted position? No — he says: although in some sense, with reference to the grounds of distinction such as designation and the like, [qualities] are other than substance, nevertheless, due to non-separation from it and due to being its transformation, they are not [ultimately] other. If so, let that which is called transformation be stated — what is it? For the purpose of ascertaining that, this is said: the nature (<s>tattvam</s>) by which substances such as <s>Dharma</s> and the rest exist — that own-nature-becoming (<s>tadbhāva</s>) is called <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation). It is twofold: beginningless and having-a-beginning. Of these, the beginningless [transformation] is [the function of] facilitating motion and the like of <s>Dharma</s> and the rest, from the standpoint of the general. That very same [transformation] also has a beginning, from the standpoint of the particular.

children.text: iti tattvārthavṛttau sarvārthasiddhisaṃjñikāyāṃ paṃcamo ’dhyāyaḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the <s>Tattvārthavṛtti</s> named <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>. || 5 ||

children.text: atha ṣaṣṭho ’dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now the sixth chapter.

children.text: § 609. āha, ajīvapadārtho vyākhyātaḥ. idāniṃ tadanantaroddeśabhāgāsravapadārtho vyākhyeya iti tatas tatprasiddhyartham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 609. He says: the non-living category (<s>ajīva-padārtha</s>) has been explained. Now the category of influx (<s>āsrava</s>), which is the next in the enumeration after that, is to be explained — therefore, for the purpose of establishing that, this is said —

children.text: kāyavāṅmanaḥkarma yogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yoga</s> (activity) is the activity of body, speech, and mind. ||

children.text: § 610. kāyādayaḥ śabdā vyākhyātārthāḥ. karma kriyā ity anarthāntaram. kāyavāṅmanasāṃ karma kāyavāṅmanaḥkarma yoga ity ākhyāyate. ātmapradeśaparispando yogaḥ. sa nimittabhedāt tridhā bhidyate. kāyayogo vāgyogo manoyoga iti. tad yathā — vīryāntarāyakṣayopaśamasadbhāve sati audārikādisaptavidhakāyavargaṇānyatamālambanāpekṣa ātmapradeśaparispandaḥ kāyayogaḥ. śarīranāmakarmodayāpāditavāgvargaṇālambane sati vīryāntarāyamatyakṣarādyāvaraṇakṣayopaśamāpāditābhyantaravāglabdhisāṃnidhye vākparināmābhimukhasyātmanaḥ pradeśaparispando vāgyogaḥ. abyantaravīryāntarāyanoindriyāvaraṇakṣayopaśamātmakamanolabdhisaṃnidhāne bāhyanimittamanovargaṇālambane ca sati manaḥpariṇāmābhimukhasyātmapradeśaparispando manoyogaḥ. kṣaye ’pi trividhavargaṇāpekṣaḥ sayogakevalina ātmapradeśaparispando yogo veditavyaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 610. The words 'body' (<s>kāya</s>) and the rest have already been explained. <s>Karma</s> (action) and <s>kriyā</s> (activity) are synonyms. The activity of body, speech, and mind is called <s>kāya-vāṅ-manaḥ-karma</s>, [which is] designated as <s>yoga</s>. <s>Yoga</s> is the vibration of the spatial units of the self (<s>ātma-pradeśa-parispanda</s>). It is divided into three due to the difference in its instrumental causes: <s>kāya-yoga</s> (bodily activity), <s>vāg-yoga</s> (verbal activity), and <s>mano-yoga</s> (mental activity). Namely: when the subsidence-cum-destruction of energy-obstructing [karma] (<s>vīryāntarāya</s>) exists, the vibration of the spatial units of the self, dependent on any one of the seven types of body-clusters (<s>audārika</s> etc.), is <s>kāya-yoga</s>. When there is dependence on the speech-cluster (<s>vāg-vargaṇā</s>) produced by the rise of body-name-determining karma (<s>śarīra-nāma-karma</s>), and when, through the subsidence-cum-destruction of the energy-obstructing and <s>mati</s>-and-letter-obscuring [karmas], the internal speech-capacity (<s>vāg-labdhi</s>) is proximately present, the vibration of the spatial units of the self inclined toward vocal transformation is <s>vāg-yoga</s>. When the internal mind-capacity (<s>mano-labdhi</s>), consisting of the subsidence-cum-destruction of energy-obstructing and non-sensory-obstructing [karmas], is proximately present, and when there is dependence on the external causal mind-cluster (<s>mano-vargaṇā</s>), the vibration of the spatial units of the self inclined toward mental transformation is <s>mano-yoga</s>. Even in the case of destruction [of obstructing karmas], the vibration of the spatial units of the self of one possessing <s>yoga</s> with omniscience (<s>sayoga-kevalin</s>), dependent on the threefold cluster, should be understood as <s>yoga</s>.

children.text: § 611. āha, abhyupemaḥ āhitatraividhyakriyo yoga iti. prakṛta idānīṃ nirdiśyatām kiṃ lakṣaṇa āsrava ity ucyate. yo ’yaṃ yogaśabdābhideyaḥ saṃsāriṇa puruṣasya —
children.translated_text: § 611. He says: we accept that <s>yoga</s> is the threefold activity as described. Now let it be stated what is currently under discussion — what is the definition of <s>āsrava</s> (influx)? It is said: this very thing denoted by the word '<s>yoga</s>,' belonging to the transmigrating soul —

children.text: sa āsravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That [yoga] is <s>āsrava</s> (influx [of karma]). ||

children.text: § 612. yathā sarassalilāvāhidvāraṃ tadāsravakāraṇatvād āsrava ity ākhyāyate tathā yogapraṇālikayā ātmanaḥ karma āsravatīti yoga āsrava iti vyapadeśam arhati.
children.translated_text: § 612. Just as the channel for carrying the water of a lake is called '<s>āsrava</s>' (influx) because it is the cause of the inflow of that [water], so too, through the channel of <s>yoga</s>, <s>karma</s> flows into the self — therefore <s>yoga</s> deserves the designation '<s>āsrava</s>'.

children.text: § 613. āha, karma dvividhaṃ puṇyaṃ pāpaṃ ceti. tasya kim aviśeṣeṇa yoga āsravahetur āhosvid asti kaścit prativiśeṣa ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 613. He asks: <s>karma</s> is twofold — <s>puṇya</s> (merit) and <s>pāpa</s> (demerit). Is <s>yoga</s> indiscriminately the cause of the influx of both, or is there some specific distinction? — to this it is said —

children.text: śubhaḥ puṇyasyāśubhaḥ pāpasya ||
children.translated_text: The auspicious (<s>śubha</s>) [yoga is the cause of influx] of merit (<s>puṇya</s>); the inauspicious (<s>aśubha</s>), of demerit (<s>pāpa</s>). ||

children.text: § 614. kaḥ śubho yogaḥ ko vā aśubhaḥ. prāṇātipātādattādānamaithunādir aśubhaḥ kāyayogaḥ. anṛtabhāṣaṇaparuṣāsabhyavacanādir aśubho vāgyogaḥ. vadhacintanerṣyāsūyādir aśubho manoyogaḥ. tato viparītaḥ śubhaḥ. kathaṃ yogasya śubhāśubhatvam. śubhapariṇāmanirvṛtto yogaḥ śubhaḥ. aśubhapariṇāmanirvṛttaś cāśubhaḥ. na punaḥ śubhāśubhakarmakāraṇatvena. yady evam ucyate śubhayoga eva na syāt, śubhayogasyāpi jñānāvaraṇādibandhahetutvābhyupagamāt. punāty ātmānaṃ pūyate ’neneti vā puṇyam. tat sadvedyādi. pāti rakṣati ātmānaṃ śubhād iti pāpam. tad asadvedyādi.
children.translated_text: § 614. What is auspicious <s>yoga</s> and what is inauspicious? Violence against living beings (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>), taking what is not given (<s>adattādāna</s>), sexual misconduct (<s>maithuna</s>), and the like constitute inauspicious bodily activity (<s>kāya-yoga</s>). Speaking falsehood (<s>anṛta-bhāṣaṇa</s>), harsh and improper speech (<s>paruṣāsabhya-vacana</s>), and the like constitute inauspicious verbal activity (<s>vāg-yoga</s>). Contemplation of killing (<s>vadha-cintā</s>), jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), fault-finding (<s>asūyā</s>), and the like constitute inauspicious mental activity (<s>mano-yoga</s>). Their opposite is auspicious. How can <s>yoga</s> be auspicious or inauspicious? <s>Yoga</s> produced by an auspicious mental disposition (<s>pariṇāma</s>) is auspicious; that produced by an inauspicious disposition is inauspicious — but not by being the cause of auspicious or inauspicious <s>karma</s>. [Objection:] If so, auspicious <s>yoga</s> would not exist at all, since even auspicious <s>yoga</s> is accepted as a cause of bondage of knowledge-obscuring and other [karmas]. [Reply:] <s>Puṇya</s> (merit) — that which purifies the self, or by which [the self] is purified — is pleasant-feeling [karma] (<s>sadvedya</s>) and the like. <s>Pāpa</s> (demerit) — that which protects [i.e., keeps] the self from the auspicious — is unpleasant-feeling [karma] (<s>asadvedya</s>) and the like.

children.text: § 615. āha kim ayam āsravaḥ sarvasaṃsāriṇām samānaphalārambhahetur āhosvit kaścid asti prativiśeṣa ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 615. He asks: is this <s>āsrava</s> (influx) a cause producing equal results for all transmigrating beings, or is there some specific distinction? — to this it is said —

children.text: sakaṣāyākaṣāyayoḥ sāṃparāyikeryāpathayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of the one with passions (<s>sakaṣāya</s>) and the one without passions (<s>akaṣāya</s>), [the influx is respectively] <s>sāṃparāyika</s> (worldly-cycle-related) and <s>īryāpatha</s> (path-of-movement-related). ||

children.text: § 616. svāmibhedād āsravabhedaḥ. svāminau dvau sakaṣāyo ’kaṣāyaś cati. kaṣāyaḥ krodhādiḥ. kaṣāya iva kaṣāyaḥ. kaḥ upamārthaḥ. yathā kaṣāyo naiyagrodhādiḥ śleṣahetus tathā krodhādir apy ātmanaḥ karmaśleṣahetutvāt kaṣāya iva kaṣāya ity ucyate. saha kaṣāyeṇa vartata iti sakaṣāyaḥ. na vidyate kaṣāyo yasyety akaṣāyaḥ. sakaṣāyaś cākaṣāyaś ca sakaṣāyākaṣāyau tayoḥ sakaṣāyākaṣāyayoḥ. saṃparāyaḥ saṃsāraḥ tatprayojanaṃ karma sāmparāyikam. īraṇam īryā yogo gatir ity arthaḥ. taddvārakaṃ karma īryāpatham. sāṃparāyikaṃ ca īryāpathaṃ ca sāmparāyikeryāpathe. tayoḥ sāmparāyikeryāpathayoḥ. yathāsaṃkhyam abhisaṃbandhaḥ sakaṣāyasyātmano mithyādṛṣṭyādeḥ sāṃparāyikasya karmaṇa āsravo bhavati. akaṣāyasya upaśāntakaṣāyāder īryāpathasya karmaṇa āsravo bhavati.
children.translated_text: § 616. From the difference of possessors, [there is] difference of <s>āsrava</s>. The two possessors are: one with passions and one without passions. <s>Kaṣāya</s> (passion) is anger (<s>krodha</s>) and the like. '<s>Kaṣāya</s> like <s>kaṣāya</s>' [i.e., passion is like an astringent]. What is the point of comparison? Just as the astringent (<s>kaṣāya</s>) of the banyan tree and the like is a cause of adhesion, so too anger and the like, being the cause of the adhesion of <s>karma</s> to the self, are called '<s>kaṣāya</s>' (passions) by analogy. One who exists together with <s>kaṣāya</s> is '<s>sakaṣāya</s>' (with passions). One in whom <s>kaṣāya</s> does not exist is '<s>akaṣāya</s>' (without passions). '<s>Sakaṣāya</s>' and '<s>akaṣāya</s>' [together form] '<s>sakaṣāyākaṣāyau</s>'; of those two — '<s>sakaṣāyākaṣāyayoḥ</s>.' '<s>Saṃparāya</s>' means <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly cycle); <s>karma</s> serving its purpose is '<s>sāṃparāyika</s>' (worldly-cycle-related). Movement (<s>īraṇa</s>) is '<s>īryā</s>,' meaning <s>yoga</s> (activity) or motion (<s>gati</s>). <s>Karma</s> [acquired] through that channel is '<s>īryāpatha</s>' (path-of-movement-related). '<s>Sāṃparāyika</s>' and '<s>īryāpatha</s>' [together form] '<s>sāṃparāyikeryāpathe</s>'; of those two — '<s>sāṃparāyikeryāpathayoḥ</s>.' The correlation is sequential: for the self with passions — one of wrong faith (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) and the like — there is influx of <s>sāṃparāyika</s> karma. For the self without passions — one whose passions are pacified (<s>upaśānta-kaṣāya</s>) and the like — there is influx of <s>īryāpatha</s> karma.

children.text: § 617. ādāv uddiṣṭasyāsravasya bhedapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 617. For the purpose of explaining the subdivisions of the <s>āsrava</s> initially enumerated, he says —

children.text: indriyakaṣāyāvratakriyāḥ pañcacatuḥpañcapañcaviṃśatisaṃkhyāḥ pūrvasya bhedāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sense organs (<s>indriya</s>), passions (<s>kaṣāya</s>), non-restraints (<s>avrata</s>), and activities (<s>kriyā</s>) — numbering five, four, five, and twenty-five — are the subdivisions of the former [sāṃparāyika āsrava]. ||

children.text: § 618. atra indriyādīnāṃ paṃcādibhir yathāsaṃkhyam abhisaṃbandho veditavyaḥ, indriyāṇi paṃca. catvāraḥ kaṣāyāḥ. pañcāvratāni. pañcaviṃśatiḥ kriyā iti. tatra pañcendriyāṇi sparśanādīny uktāni. catvāraḥ kaśāyāḥ krodhādayaḥ. pañcāvratāni prāṇavyaparopaṇādīni vakṣyate. pañcaviṃśatiḥ kriyā ucyante — caityagurupravacanapūjādilakṣaṇā samyaktvavardhanī kriyā samyaktvakriyā. anyadevatāstavanādirūpā mithyātvahetukī pravṛttir mithyātvakriyā. gamanāgamanādipravartanaṃ kāyādibhiḥ prayogakriyā. saṃyatasya sataḥ aviratiṃ pratyābhimukhyaṃ samādānakriyā. īryāpathanimitteryāpathakriyā. tā etāḥ pañca kriyā. krodhāveśāt prādoṣikī kriyā. praduṣṭasya sato ’bhyudyamaḥ kāyikī kriyā. hiṃsopakaraṇādānādhikaraṇikī kriyā. duḥkotpattitantratvāt pāritāpikī kriyā. āyurindriyabalocchvāsaniḥśvāsaprāṇānāṃ viyogakaraṇāt prānātipātikī kriyā. tā etāḥ pañca kriyāḥ. rāgārdrīkṛtatvāt pramādino ramaṇīyarūpālokanābhiprāyo darśanakriyā. pramādavaśāt spṛṣṭavyasaṃcetanānubandhaḥ sparśanakriyā. apūrvādhikaraṇotpādanāt prātyayikī kriyā. srtīpuruṣapaśusampātideśe ’ntarmalotsargakaraṇaṃ samantānupātakriyā. apramṛṣṭādṛṣṭabhūmau kāyādinikṣepo ’nābhogakriyā. tā etāḥ pañca kriyā. yāṃ pareṇa nirvartyāṃ kriyāṃ svayaṃ karoti sā svahastakriyā. pāpādānādipravṛttiviśeṣābhyanujñānaṃ nisargakriyā. parācaritasāvadyādiprakāśanaṃ vidāraṇakriyā. yathoktām ājñām āvaśyakādiṣu cāritramohodayāt kartum aśaknuvato ’nyathāprarūpaṇad ājñāvyāpādikī kriyā. śāṭhyālasyābhyāṃ pravacanopadiṣṭavidhikartavyatānādaro ’nākāṅkṣakriyā. tā etāḥ pañca kriyā. chedanabhedanaviśasanādikriyāparatvam anyena vārambhe kriyamāṇe praharṣaḥ prārambhakriyā. parigrahāvināśārthā pārigrāhikī kriyā. jñānadarśanādiṣu nikṛtir vañcanaṃ māyākriyā. anyaṃ mithyādarśanakriyākaraṇakāraṇāviṣṭaṃ praśaṃsādibhir dṛḍhayati yathā sādhu karoṣīti sā mithyādarśanakriyā. saṃyamaghātikarmodayavaśād anivṛttir apratyākhyānakriyā. tā etāḥ pañca kriyāḥ. samuditāḥ pañcaviṃśatikriyāḥ. etānīndriyādīni kāryakāraṇabhedād bhedam āpadyamānāni sāṃparāyikasya karmaṇa āśravadvārāṇi bhavanti.
children.translated_text: § 618. Here, the correlation of sense organs and the rest with five and the rest should be understood sequentially: the sense organs are five; the passions are four; the non-restraints are five; the activities are twenty-five. Among these, the five sense organs — touch and the rest — have been stated. The four passions are anger (<s>krodha</s>) and the rest. The five non-restraints are violence against living beings (<s>prāṇa-vyaparopaṇa</s>) and the rest — [which] will be stated [later]. The twenty-five activities are enumerated: (1) <s>samyaktva-kriyā</s> — activity that increases right faith, characterized by worship of <s>caityas</s>, teachers, and scriptures; (2) <s>mithyātva-kriyā</s> — engagement motivated by wrong faith, such as praising other deities; (3) <s>prayoga-kriyā</s> — initiation of movement such as going and coming through body and the like; (4) <s>samādāna-kriyā</s> — the inclination toward non-restraint on the part of one who is restrained; (5) <s>īryāpatha-kriyā</s> — activity occasioned by movement along a path. These are the first five activities. (6) <s>prādoṣikī kriyā</s> — activity arising from an outburst of anger; (7) <s>kāyikī kriyā</s> — the exertion of one who is enraged; (8) <s>ādhikaraṇikī kriyā</s> — taking up instruments of violence; (9) <s>pāritāpikī kriyā</s> — [activity] that is instrumental in producing suffering; (10) <s>prāṇātipātikī kriyā</s> — [activity] that causes the separation of vitality, sense organs, strength, respiration, and life-breaths. These are the second five activities. (11) <s>darśana-kriyā</s> — the intention of one who is heedless and softened by passion to gaze at beautiful forms; (12) <s>sparśana-kriyā</s> — the pursuit of tactile sensations due to heedlessness; (13) <s>prātyayikī kriyā</s> — [activity] that produces unprecedented substrata [for karma]; (14) <s>samantānupāta-kriyā</s> — discharging bodily waste in places frequented by women, men, and animals; (15) <s>anābhoga-kriyā</s> — placing one's body and the like on ground that is unexamined and unseen. These are the third five activities. (16) <s>svahasta-kriyā</s> — performing oneself an action that should be performed by another; (17) <s>nisarga-kriyā</s> — sanctioning engagement in sinful actions such as giving [harmful things] and the like; (18) <s>vidāraṇa-kriyā</s> — revealing another's sinful deeds and the like; (19) <s>ājñā-vyāpādikī kriyā</s> — misrepresenting prescribed duties such as obligatory rites, when one is unable to perform them as instructed due to the rise of conduct-deluding [karma]; (20) <s>anākāṅkṣa-kriyā</s> — disregard for the duties prescribed by scripture, due to deceit and laziness. These are the fourth five activities. (21) <s>prārambha-kriyā</s> — rejoicing when another undertakes violent acts such as cutting, splitting, slaughtering, and the like; (22) <s>pārigrāhikī kriyā</s> — [activity] for the purpose of preserving possessions; (23) <s>māyā-kriyā</s> — deception and fraud regarding knowledge, perception, and the like; (24) <s>mithyādarśana-kriyā</s> — strengthening another who is possessed by wrong-faith-generating activity through praise and the like, as in 'you are doing well'; (25) <s>apratyākhyāna-kriyā</s> — non-renunciation due to the rise of restraint-destroying <s>karma</s>. These are the fifth five activities. Together, [they constitute] the twenty-five activities. These — sense organs and the rest — undergoing differentiation through the distinction of cause and effect, become the channels of influx of <s>sāṃparāyika</s> karma.

children.text: § 619. atrāha, yogatrayasya sarvātmakāryatvāt sarveṣāṃ saṃsāriṇāṃ sādhāraṇaḥ, tato bandhaphalānubhavanaṃ pratyaviśeṣa ity atrocyate — naitad evam. yasmāt saty api pratyātmasaṃbhave teṣāṃ jīvapariṇāmebhyo ’nantavikalpebhyo viśeṣo ’bhyanujñāyate katham iti ced ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 619. Here one objects: since the threefold <s>yoga</s> is common to all activities of the self, it is common to all transmigrating beings; therefore, there should be no distinction in the experience of the fruits of bondage — to this it is said: this is not so. Because, even though [yoga] potentially exists in every self, a distinction is recognized from the infinite varieties of the mental dispositions (<s>pariṇāma</s>) of souls. If asked how, it is said —

children.text: tīvramandajñātājñātabhāvādhikaraṇavīryaviśeṣebhyas tadviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The distinction of that [āsrava] arises from the distinctions of intensity (<s>tīvra</s>), mildness (<s>manda</s>), the known (<s>jñāta</s>), the unknown (<s>ajñāta</s>), disposition (<s>bhāva</s>), substratum (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), and potency (<s>vīrya</s>). ||

children.text: § 620. bāhyābhyantarahetūdīraṇavaśād udriktaḥ pariṇāmas tīvraḥ. tadviparīto mandaḥ. ayaṃ prāṇī mayā hantavya iti jñātvā pravṛttir jñātam ity ucyate. madāt pramādād vānavabudhya pravṛttir ajñātam. adhikriyante ’sminn arthā ity adhikaraṇaṃ dravyam ity arthaḥ. dravyasya svaśaktiviśeṣo vīryam. bhāvaśabdaḥ pratyekaṃ parisamāpyate — tīvrabhāvo mandabhāva ity ādiḥ. etebhyas tasyāsravasya viśeṣo bhavati. kāraṇabhedād dhi kāryabheda iti.
children.translated_text: § 620. A mental disposition (<s>pariṇāma</s>) that is intensified due to the arousal of external and internal causes is '<s>tīvra</s>' (intense). Its opposite is '<s>manda</s>' (mild). Engagement after knowing 'this living being is to be killed by me' is called '<s>jñāta</s>' (known). Engagement without awareness, due to intoxication or heedlessness, is '<s>ajñāta</s>' (unknown). That in which things are employed is '<s>adhikaraṇa</s>' (substratum) — meaning a [material] substance. The specific capacity (<s>śakti-viśeṣa</s>) of a substance is '<s>vīrya</s>' (potency). The word '<s>bhāva</s>' (disposition) is to be applied to each individually — 'intense-disposition,' 'mild-disposition,' and so on. From these [factors], the distinction of that <s>āsrava</s> arises. For from the difference of causes, [there is] difference of effects.

children.text: § 621. atrāha, adhikaraṇam uktam, tatsvarūpam anirjñātam atas taducyatām iti. tatra bhedapratipādanadvārenādhikaraṇasvarūpanirjñānārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 621. Here one says: the substratum (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) has been mentioned, but its nature has not been ascertained; therefore let that be stated. For the purpose of ascertaining the nature of the substratum through indicating its subdivisions, he says —

children.text: adhikaraṇaṃ jīvājīvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The substrata (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) are <s>jīvas</s> (souls) and <s>ajīvas</s> (non-living things). ||

children.text: § 622. uktalakṣaṇā jīvājīvāḥ. yady uktalakṣaṇāḥ punarvacanaṃ kiṃ artham? adhikaraṇaviśeṣajñāpanārthaṃ punarvacanaṃ. jīvājīvā adhikaraṇam ity ayaṃ viśeṣo jñāpayitavya iti. kaḥ punar asau? hiṃsādyupakaraṇabhāva iti. syād etan mūlapadārthayor dvitvāj jīvājīvāv iti dvivacanaṃ nyāyaprāptam iti. tan na, paryāyāṇām adhikaraṇatvāt. yena kenacit paryāyeṇa viśiṣṭaṃ dravyam adhikaraṇam, na sāmānyam iti bahuvacanaṃ kṛtam. jīvājīvā adhikaraṇaṃ kasya? āsravasyeti. arthavaśād abhisaṃbandho bhavati.
children.translated_text: § 622. <s>Jīvas</s> (living beings) and <s>ajīvas</s> (non-living substances) have the characteristics already stated. If their characteristics have already been stated, what is the purpose of repeating them? The repetition is for the purpose of indicating a particular substratum. The specific point to be conveyed is that <s>jīvas</s> and <s>ajīvas</s> are the substratum. What then is that specific point? That they serve as the instrumental basis for <s>hiṃsā</s> (violence) and other activities. One might object that since the two fundamental categories are only two, the dual number 'jīvājīvau' would be grammatically correct. That is not so, because the modes serve as the substratum. A substance qualified by any particular mode is the substratum, not the universal — hence the plural is used. Of what are <s>jīvas</s> and <s>ajīvas</s> the substratum? Of <s>āsrava</s> (karmic influx). The connection is established by the force of meaning.

children.text: § 623. tatra jīvādhikaraṇabhedapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 623. In order to explain the varieties of the <s>jīva</s>-substratum, he says —

children.text: ādyaṃ saṃrambhasamārambhārambhayogakṛtakāritānumatakaṣāyaviśeṣais tris tris triś catuś caikaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The first (<s>jīva</s>-substratum <s>āsrava</s>) is differentiated by the specific varieties of <s>saṃrambha</s> (mental impetus), <s>samārambha</s> (preparation), <s>ārambha</s> (undertaking), <s>yoga</s> (activity), <s>kṛta</s> (done by oneself), <s>kārita</s> (caused to be done), <s>anumata</s> (approved), and <s>kaṣāya</s> (passion) — three, three, three, and four, each taken singly.

children.text: § 624. prāṇavyaparopaṇādiṣu pramādavataḥ prayatnāveśaḥ saṃrambhaḥ. sādhanasamabhyāsīkaraṇaṃ samārambhaḥ prakrama ārambhaḥ. ‘yoga’ śabdo vyākhyātārthaḥ. kṛtavacanaṃ svātantryapratipattyārtham. kāritābhidhānaṃ paraprayogāpekṣam. anumataśabdaḥ prayojakasya mānasapariṇāmapradarśanārthaḥ. abhihitalakṣaṇāḥ kaṣāyāḥ krodhādayaḥ. viśiṣyate ’rtho ’rthāntarād iti viśeṣaḥ. sa pratyekam abhisaṃbadhyate — saṃrambhaviśeṣaḥ samārambhaviśeṣa ity ādi. ādyaṃ jīvādhikaraṇam etair viśeṣaiḥ ‘bhidyate’ iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. ete catvāraḥ sujantās tryādiśabdā yathākramam abhisaṃbadhyante — saṃrambhasamārambhārambhās trayaḥ, yogās trayaḥ, kṛtakāritānumatās trayaḥ, kaṣāyāś catvāra iti. eteṣāṃ gaṇanābhyāvṛttiḥ sucā dyotyate. ekaśa iti vīpsānirdeśaḥ. ekaikaṃ tryādīn bhedān nayed ity arthaḥ. yad yathā

— krodhakṛtakāyasaṃrambhaḥ mānakṛtakāyasaṃrambhaḥ māyākṛtakāyasaṃrambhaḥ lobhakṛtakāyasaṃrambhaḥ krodhakāritakāyasaṃrambhaḥ mānakāritakāyasaṃrambhaḥ māyakāritakāyasaṃrambhaḥ lobhakāritakāyasaṃrambhaḥ krodhānumatakāyasaṃrambhaḥ mānānumatakāyasaṃrambhaḥ māyānumatakāyasaṃrambhaḥ lobhānumatakāysaṃrambhaś ceti dvādaśadhā kāyasaṃrambhaḥ. evaṃ vāgyoge manoyoge ca dvādaśadhā saṃrambhaḥ. ta ete saṃpiṇḍitāh ṣaṭtriṃśat, tathā samārambhā api ṣaṭtriṃśat, ārambhā api ṣaṭtriṃśat. ete saṃpiṇḍitā jīvādhikaraṇāsravabhedā aṣṭottaraśatasaṃkhyāḥ saṃbhavanti. ‘ca’ śabdo ’nantānubandyapratyākhyānapratyākhyānasaṃjvalanakaśāyabhedakṛtāntarbhedasamuccyārthaḥ.
children.translated_text: — <s>krodha</s>-<s>kṛta</s>-<s>kāya</s>-<s>saṃrambha</s> (bodily impetus done through anger), <s>māna</s>-<s>kṛta</s>-<s>kāya</s>-<s>saṃrambha</s> (bodily impetus done through pride), <s>māyā</s>-<s>kṛta</s>-<s>kāya</s>-<s>saṃrambha</s> (bodily impetus done through deceit), <s>lobha</s>-<s>kṛta</s>-<s>kāya</s>-<s>saṃrambha</s> (bodily impetus done through greed), <s>krodha</s>-<s>kārita</s>-<s>kāya</s>-<s>saṃrambha</s> (bodily impetus caused through anger), <s>māna</s>-<s>kārita</s>-<s>kāya</s>-<s>saṃrambha</s> (bodily impetus caused through pride), <s>māyā</s>-<s>kārita</s>-<s>kāya</s>-<s>saṃrambha</s> (bodily impetus caused through deceit), <s>lobha</s>-<s>kārita</s>-<s>kāya</s>-<s>saṃrambha</s> (bodily impetus caused through greed), <s>krodha</s>-<s>anumata</s>-<s>kāya</s>-<s>saṃrambha</s> (bodily impetus approved through anger), <s>māna</s>-<s>anumata</s>-<s>kāya</s>-<s>saṃrambha</s> (bodily impetus approved through pride), <s>māyā</s>-<s>anumata</s>-<s>kāya</s>-<s>saṃrambha</s> (bodily impetus approved through deceit), and <s>lobha</s>-<s>anumata</s>-<s>kāya</s>-<s>saṃrambha</s> (bodily impetus approved through greed) — thus <s>kāya</s>-<s>saṃrambha</s> (bodily impetus) is of twelve kinds. Similarly, with <s>vāgyoga</s> (vocal activity) and <s>manoyoga</s> (mental activity), <s>saṃrambha</s> is also of twelve kinds each. These combined together amount to thirty-six; likewise <s>samārambha</s> (preparation) is also thirty-six, and <s>ārambha</s> (undertaking) is also thirty-six. These combined together yield one hundred and eight varieties of <s>jīva</s>-substratum <s>āsrava</s> (karmic influx). The word 'ca' (and) serves to include the sub-varieties arising from the divisions of <s>kaṣāya</s> into <s>anantānubandhin</s> (infinitely binding), <s>apratyākhyāna</s> (non-renunciation), <s>pratyākhyāna</s> (partial renunciation), and <s>saṃjvalana</s> (smoldering) passions.

§ 624. <s>Saṃrambha</s> is the onset of effort with heedlessness in acts such as depriving others of life. <s>Samārambha</s> is the preparation of the means. <s>Ārambha</s> is the actual commencement. The word '<s>yoga</s>' has its meaning already explained. The word '<s>kṛta</s>' (self-done) is for conveying independent action. The term '<s>kārita</s>' (caused to be done) implies dependence on another's agency. The word '<s>anumata</s>' (approved) is for showing the mental disposition of the instigator. The <s>kaṣāyas</s> (passions) with the characteristics already described are <s>krodha</s> (anger) and the rest. A <s>viśeṣa</s> (specific variety) is that which distinguishes one meaning from another. It is connected with each individually — specific variety of <s>saṃrambha</s>, specific variety of <s>samārambha</s>, and so on. The first, namely the <s>jīva</s>-substratum, 'is differentiated' by these specific varieties — this is the completion of the sentence. These four terms ending in numeral suffixes — three and so forth — are connected in order: <s>saṃrambha</s>, <s>samārambha</s>, and <s>ārambha</s> are three; <s>yogas</s> are three; <s>kṛta</s>, <s>kārita</s>, and <s>anumata</s> are three; <s>kaṣāyas</s> are four. The repetition of the enumeration is indicated by the word 'ca' (and). '<s>Ekaśaḥ</s>' is a distributive expression. The meaning is that each one should be multiplied by the three and other divisions. How this works:

children.text: § 625. parasyājīvādhikaraṇasya bhedapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 625. In order to explain the varieties of the other, namely the <s>ajīva</s>-substratum, he says —

children.text: nirvartanānikṣepasaṃyoganisargā dvicaturdvitribhedāḥ param ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nirvartanā</s> (production), <s>nikṣepa</s> (placement), <s>saṃyoga</s> (combination), and <s>nisarga</s> (emission) have two, four, two, and three sub-varieties respectively — this pertains to the latter (<s>ajīva</s>-substratum).

children.text: § 626. nirvartyata iti nirvartanā niṣpādanā. nikṣipyata iti nikṣepaḥ sthāpanā. saṃyujyate iti saṃyogo miśrīkṛtam. nisṛjyata iti nisargaḥ pravartanam. ete dvyādibhir yathākramam abhisaṃbadhyante — nirvartanā dvibhedā nikṣepaś caturbhedaḥ saṃyogo dvibhedaḥ nisargas tribheda iti. ta ete bhedā ajīvādhikaraṇasya veditavyāḥ. paravacanam anarthakam, pūrvasūtre ādyam iti vacanād idam avaśiṣṭārthaṃ bhavatīti. nānarthakam. anyārthaḥ paraśabdaḥ. saṃrambhādibhyo ’nyāni nirvarttanādīni.

itarathā hi nirvartanādīnām ātmapariṇāmasadbhāvāj jīvādhikaraṇavikalpā eveti vijñāyeta. nirvatanādhikaraṇaṃ dvividhaṃ mūlaguṇanirvatanādhikaraṇam uttraraguṇanirvatanādhikaraṇaṃ ceti. tatra mūlaguṇanirvatanaṃ pañcavidham, śarīravāṅmanaḥprāṇāpānāś ca. uttraraguṇanirvartanaṃ kāṣṭhapustacitrakarmādi. nikṣepaś caturvidhaḥ apratyavekṣitanikṣepādhikaraṇaṃ duḥpramṛṣṭanikṣepādhikaraṇaṃ sahasānikṣepādhikaraṇam anābhoganikṣepādhikaraṇaṃ ceti. nisargas trividhaḥ — kāyanisargādhikaraṇaṃ vāgnisargādhikaraṇaṃ manonisargādhikaraṇaṃ ceti.
children.translated_text: Otherwise, since <s>nirvartanā</s> and the rest can exist as transformations of the self, they would be understood as varieties of the <s>jīva</s>-substratum alone. The <s>nirvartanā</s>-substratum is of two kinds: the substratum of production of fundamental qualities and the substratum of production of secondary qualities. Among these, production of fundamental qualities is fivefold: body, speech, mind, <s>prāṇa</s> (inhalation), and <s>apāna</s> (exhalation). Production of secondary qualities includes woodwork, painting, artwork, and the like. <s>Nikṣepa</s> (placement) is fourfold: the substratum of careless placement, the substratum of poorly cleaned placement, the substratum of hasty placement, and the substratum of inattentive placement. <s>Nisarga</s> (emission) is threefold: the substratum of bodily emission, the substratum of vocal emission, and the substratum of mental emission.

§ 626. That which is produced is <s>nirvartanā</s>, meaning fabrication. That which is placed is <s>nikṣepa</s>, meaning depositing. That which is combined is <s>saṃyoga</s>, meaning mixing. That which is released is <s>nisarga</s>, meaning setting forth. These are connected with two and other numbers in order: <s>nirvartanā</s> has two sub-varieties, <s>nikṣepa</s> has four sub-varieties, <s>saṃyoga</s> has two sub-varieties, and <s>nisarga</s> has three sub-varieties. These are the varieties to be understood as belonging to the <s>ajīva</s>-substratum. The word 'para' (latter) might seem redundant, since the word 'ādya' (first) in the previous <s>sūtra</s> implies that this pertains to the remainder. It is not redundant; the word 'para' has a different purpose — it indicates that <s>nirvartanā</s> and the rest are different from <s>saṃrambha</s> and the rest.

children.text: § 627. uktaḥ sāmānyena karmāsravabhedaḥ. idānīṃ karmaviśeṣāsravabhedo vaktavyaḥ. tasmin vaktavye ādyayor jñānadarśanāvaraṇayor āsravabhedapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 627. The varieties of karmic <s>āsrava</s> (influx) have been stated in general. Now the <s>āsrava</s> varieties for specific karmas are to be stated. To explain the varieties of <s>āsrava</s> for the first two, namely <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring) and <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s> (perception-obscuring) karmas, he says —

children.text: tatpradoṣanihnavamātsaryāntarāyāsādanopaghātā jñānadarśanāvaraṇayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Defamation of these, concealment, envy, obstruction, undermining, and injuring — these are the causes of <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring) and <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s> (perception-obscuring) karmas.

children.text: § 628. tattvajñanasya mokṣasādhanasya kīrtane kṛte kasyācid anabhivyāharataḥ antaḥpaiśunyapariṇāmaḥ pradoṣaḥ. kutaś citkāraṇān nāsti na vedmīty ādi jñānasya vyapalapanaṃ nihnavaḥ. kutaścit kāraṇād bhāvitam api vijñanaṃ dānārham api yato na dīyate tan mātsaryam. jñānavyavacchedakaraṇam antarāyaḥ. kāyena vācā ca paraprakāśyajñānasya varjanam āsādanam. praśastajñānadūṣaṇam upaghātaḥ. āsādanam eveti cet? sato jñānasya vinayapradānādiguṇakīrtanānuṣṭhānam āsādanam. upaghātas tu jñānam ajñānam eveti jñānanāśābhiprāyaḥ. iti anayor ayaṃ bhedaḥ. ‘’tat’ śabdena jñānadarśanayoḥ pratinirderśaḥ kriyate. kathaṃ punar aprakṛtayor anirdiṣṭayos tac chabdena parāmarśaḥ kartuṃ śakyaḥ? praśnāpekṣayā. jñānadarśanāvaraṇayoḥ ka āsrava iti praśne kṛte tadapekṣayā tac chabdo jñānadarśane pratinirdiśati. etena jñānadarśanavatsu tatsādhaneṣu ca pradoṣādayo yojyāḥ; tannimittatvāt. ta ete jñānadarśanāvaraṇayor āsravahetavaḥ. ekakāraṇasādhyasya kāryasyānekasya darśanāt tulye ’pi pradoṣādau jñānarśanāvaraṇāsravasiddhiḥ.
athavā viṣayabhedād āsravabhedaḥ. jñānaviṣayāḥ pradoṣādayo jñānāvaraṇasya. darśanaviṣayāḥ pradoṣādayo darśanāvaraṇasyeti.
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the difference in <s>āsrava</s> is due to the difference in object. <s>Pradoṣa</s> (defamation) and the rest directed toward knowledge cause <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring karma); <s>pradoṣa</s> and the rest directed toward perception cause <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s> (perception-obscuring karma).

§ 628. <s>Pradoṣa</s> (defamation) is the internal disposition of malice toward someone who does not openly express it when the true knowledge that is the means to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) is praised. <s>Nihnava</s> (concealment) is the denial of knowledge, saying 'it does not exist' or 'I do not know' for some reason. <s>Mātsarya</s> (envy) is the attitude by which knowledge, even when cultivated and worthy of being shared, is not given for some reason. <s>Antarāya</s> (obstruction) is causing interruption of knowledge. <s>Āsādana</s> (undermining) is the prohibition, by body or speech, of knowledge that is being imparted to others. <s>Upaghāta</s> (injuring) is the disparagement of excellent knowledge. If one objects that <s>āsādana</s> alone suffices? <s>Āsādana</s> is the practice of disparaging the virtues such as humility and generosity of existing knowledge. <s>Upaghāta</s>, however, is the intention to destroy knowledge, declaring that knowledge is actually ignorance — this is the difference between the two. The word 'tat' (that) refers back to knowledge and perception. How can the word 'tat' refer to things not under discussion and not previously mentioned? By reference to the implied question. When the question arises 'What is the <s>āsrava</s> of <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> and <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s>?', the word 'tat' refers to knowledge and perception in relation to that question. By this, <s>pradoṣa</s> (defamation) and the rest should be applied to those who possess knowledge and perception and to the means of attaining them, since they are the causes thereof. These are the causes of <s>āsrava</s> for <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> and <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s> karmas. Since effects produced by a single cause are observed to be multiple, the <s>āsrava</s> for both <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> and <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s> is established even though <s>pradoṣa</s> and the rest are the same.

children.text: § 629. yathānayoḥ karmaprakṛtyor āsravabhedās tathā —
children.translated_text: § 629. Just as the varieties of <s>āsrava</s> have been stated for these two <s>karma</s>-types, similarly —

children.text: duḥkhaśokatāpākrandanavadhaparidevanāny ātmaparobhayasthāny asadvedyasya ||
children.translated_text: Suffering, grief, anguish, lamentation, killing, and wailing — whether pertaining to oneself, others, or both — are the causes of <s>asadvedya</s> (unpleasant feeling-producing karma).

children.text: § 630. pīḍālakṣaṇaḥ pariṇāmo duḥkham. anugrāhakasaṃbandhavicchede vaiklavyaviśeṣaḥ śokaḥ. parivādādinimittād āvilāntaḥkaraṇasya tīvrānuśayas tāpaḥ. paritāpajātāśrupātapracuravipralāpādibhir vyaktakrandanam ākrandanam. āyurindriyabalaprāṇaviyogakaraṇaṃ vadhaḥ. saṃkleśapariṇāmāvalambanaṃ guṇasmaraṇānukīrtanapūrvakaṃ svaparānugrahābhilāṣaviṣayam anukampāpracuraṃ rodanaṃ paridevanam. nanu ca śokādīnāṃ duḥkhaviśeṣatvād duḥkhagrahaṇam evāstu? satyam evam; tathāpi katipayaviśeṣapratipādanena duḥkhajātyanuvidhānaṃ kriyate. yathā gaur ity ukte anirjñāte viśeṣe tatpratipādanārthaṃ khaṇḍamuṇḍakṛṣṇaśuklādyupādānaṃ kriyate tathā duḥkhaviṣayāsrvāsaṃkhyeyalokabhedasaṃbhavād duḥkham ity ukte viśeṣānirjñānāt katipayaviśeṣanirdeśena tadviśeṣapratipattiḥ kriyate. tāny etāni duḥkhādīni krodhādyāveśād ātmasthāni bhavanti parasthāny ubhayasthāni ca. etāni sarvāṇy asadvedyāsravakāraṇāni veditavyāni. atra codyate — yadi duḥkhādīny ātmaparobhayasthāny asadvedyāsravanimittāni, kim artham ārhataiḥ keśaluñcanānaśanātapasthānādīni duḥkhanimittāny āsthīyante pareṣu ca pratipādyante iti? naiṣa doṣaḥ — antarańgakrodhādyāveśapūrvakāṇi duḥkhādīny asadvedyāsravanimittānīti viśeṣyoktatvāt. yathā kasyacid bhiṣajaḥ paramakaruṇāśasya niḥśalyasya saṃyatasyopari gaṇḍaṃ pāṭayato duḥkhahetutve saty api na pāpabandho bāhyanimittamātrād eva bhavati. evaṃ saṃsāraviṣayamahāduḥkhād udvignasya bhikṣos tannivṛttyupāyaṃ prati samāhitamanaskasya śāstravihite karmaṇi pravartamānasya saṃkleśapariṇāmābhāvād duḥkhanimittatve saty api na pāpabandhaḥ. uktaṃ ca —
children.translated_text: § 630. <s>Duḥkha</s> (suffering) is a mental state characterized by pain. <s>Śoka</s> (grief) is a particular kind of bewilderment arising from separation from a beneficial connection. <s>Tāpa</s> (anguish) is an intense remorse of one whose inner being is agitated due to reproach and similar causes. <s>Ākrandana</s> (lamentation) is crying out loudly, manifested through tears born of distress, profuse incoherent utterances, and the like. <s>Vadha</s> (killing) is causing the separation of life-span, sense-organs, strength, and vital breaths. <s>Paridevana</s> (wailing) is weeping full of compassion, preceded by recollection and recounting of virtues, having as its object the desire for the welfare of oneself and others, and rooted in afflictive mental states. If one objects that since grief and the rest are merely specific forms of suffering, the term suffering alone should suffice? True indeed; nevertheless, by specifying certain particular forms, the entire range of suffering is indicated. Just as when the word 'cow' is spoken and the specific type is unknown, terms like 'hornless,' 'polled,' 'black,' 'white,' etc. are employed to specify, similarly, since the <s>āsrava</s> pertaining to suffering can exist in innumerable varieties across the universe, and since the specific types are not known merely by saying 'suffering,' a few specific types are mentioned to facilitate understanding of those varieties. These sufferings and the rest, due to the influence of <s>krodha</s> (anger) and other passions, may pertain to oneself, to others, or to both. All of these should be understood as causes of <s>asadvedya</s> (unpleasant feeling-producing) <s>āsrava</s>. Here an objection is raised: if suffering and the rest pertaining to oneself, others, or both are the causes of <s>asadvedya</s> <s>āsrava</s>, then why do the <s>Arhats</s> (Jain saints) undertake acts that cause suffering such as pulling out hair, fasting, and standing in the heat, and also teach these to others? This is no fault — because the qualification is stated that suffering and the rest preceded by the inner influence of <s>krodha</s> (anger) and other passions are causes of <s>asadvedya</s> <s>āsrava</s>. Just as a physician who is supremely compassionate, free from inner affliction, and self-restrained, though causing suffering when lancing a boil, does not incur sinful bondage merely from the external cause alone, similarly, a monk who is distressed by the great suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), whose mind is concentrated on the means of its cessation, and who engages in actions prescribed by scripture, does not incur sinful bondage despite the presence of suffering, due to the absence of afflictive mental states. And it has been said —

children.text:
na duḥkhaṃ na sukhaṃ yadvad dhetur dṛṣṭaś cikitsite |
	  cikitsāyāṃ tu yuktasya syād duḥkham athavā sukham ||
	  na duḥkhaṃ na sukhaṃ tadvad dhetur mokṣasya sādhane |
	  mokṣopāye tu yuktasya syād duḥkham athavā sukham ||
children.translated_text: Just as neither suffering nor happiness is seen as the cause in medical treatment, but for one engaged in treatment there may be suffering or happiness; similarly, neither suffering nor happiness is the cause in the practice leading to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), but for one engaged in the means of liberation there may be suffering or happiness.

children.text: § 631. uktā asadvedyāsravahetavaḥ. sadvedyasya punaḥ ke ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 631. The causes of <s>asadvedya</s> (unpleasant feeling-producing) <s>āsrava</s> have been stated. Now, what are the causes of <s>sadvedya</s> (pleasant feeling-producing karma)? This is answered here —

children.text: bhūtavratyanukampādānasarāgasaṃyamādiyogaḥ kṣāntiḥ śaucam iti sadvedyasya ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūtavratyanukampā</s> (compassion toward living beings and those observing vows), <s>dāna</s> (charity), <s>sarāgasaṃyama</s> (restraint with residual attachment) and the like, <s>yoga</s> (meditation), <s>kṣānti</s> (forbearance), and <s>śauca</s> (purity) — these and such are the causes of <s>sadvedya</s> (pleasant feeling-producing karma).

children.text: § 632. tāsu tāsu gatiṣu karmodayavaśād bhavantīti bhūtāni prāṇina ity arthaḥ. vratāny ahiṃsādīni vakṣyante, tadvanto vratinaḥ. te dvividhāḥ. āgāraṃ prati nivṛttautsukyāḥ. saṃyatāḥ gṛhiṇaś ca saṃyatāsaṃyatāḥ. anugrahārdrīkṛtacetasaḥ parapīḍām ātmasthām iva kurvato ’nukampanam anukampā. bhūteṣu vratiṣu cānukampā bhūtavratyanukampā. parānugrahabuddhyā svasyātisarjanaṃ dānam. saṃsārakāraṇavinivṛttiṃ pratyāgūrṇo ’kṣīṇāśayaḥ sarāga ity ucyate. prāṇīnidriyeṣv aśubhapravṛtter viratiḥ saṃyamaḥ. sarāgasya saṃyama sarāgo vā saṃyamaḥ sarāgasaṃyamaḥ.

‘ādi’-śabdena saṃyamāsaṃyamākāmanirjarābālatapo ’nurodhaḥ. yogaḥ samādhiḥ samyakpraṇidhānam ity arthaḥ. bhūtavratyanukampādānasarāgasaṃyamādīnāṃ yogo bhūtavratyanukampādānasarāgasaṃyamādiyogaḥ. krodhādinivṛttiḥ kṣāntiḥ. lobhaprakārāṇām uparamaḥ śaucam. ‘iti’ śabdaḥ prakārārthaḥ. ke te punas te prakārāḥ. arhatpūjākaraṇatatparatābālavṛddhatapasvivaiyāvṛttyādayaḥ. ‘bhūta’ grahaṇāt siddhe ‘vrati’ grahaṇaṃ tadviṣayānukampāprādhānyakhyāpanārtham. ta ete sadvedyasyāsravā jñeyāḥ.
children.translated_text: The word 'ādi' (and the like) includes <s>saṃyamāsaṃyama</s> (partial restraint), <s>ākāmanirjarā</s> (involuntary karmic dissipation), <s>bālatapas</s> (austerity of the uninitiated), and <s>anurodha</s> (compliance). <s>Yoga</s> means <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), that is, right concentration — this is the meaning. The <s>yoga</s> (meditation) practiced together with compassion toward beings and ascetics, charity, restraint with attachment, and so forth is called <s>bhūtavratyanukampādānasarāgasaṃyamādiyoga</s>. <s>Kṣānti</s> (forbearance) is the cessation of <s>krodha</s> (anger) and other passions. <s>Śauca</s> (purity) is the cessation of forms of <s>lobha</s> (greed). The word 'iti' indicates 'and such kinds.' What then are those kinds? Worship of the <s>Arhats</s> (omniscient ones), devotion to them, service to the young, the elderly, and ascetics, and similar acts. Although the term '<s>bhūta</s>' (living beings) already covers ascetics, the separate mention of '<s>vratin</s>' (those observing vows) is to emphasize the primacy of compassion directed specifically toward them. These should be known as the causes of <s>āsrava</s> for <s>sadvedya</s> (pleasant feeling-producing karma).

§ 632. <s>Bhūtas</s> (living beings) are <s>prāṇins</s> (sentient creatures) who exist in various states of existence due to the fruition of <s>karma</s> — this is the meaning. <s>Vratas</s> (vows) such as <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence) and the rest will be described later; those who observe them are <s>vratins</s> (ascetics). They are of two kinds: those who have turned away from worldly attachment toward home — the fully restrained (<s>saṃyatas</s>) — and householders who are partially restrained (<s>saṃyatāsaṃyatas</s>). <s>Anukampā</s> (compassion) is the sympathetic feeling of one whose heart is softened by grace, who regards the suffering of others as if it were one's own. <s>Bhūtavratyanukampā</s> is compassion toward living beings and toward those observing vows. <s>Dāna</s> (charity) is the giving away of one's own possessions with the intention of benefiting others. One who is turned back from the causes of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) but whose dispositions are not yet exhausted is called <s>sarāga</s> (one with residual attachment). <s>Saṃyama</s> (restraint) is abstention from harmful activity in the five senses. The restraint of one with residual attachment, or restraint that itself has residual attachment, is <s>sarāgasaṃyama</s>.

children.text: § 633. atha tadantaroddeśabhājo mohasyāsravahetau vaktavye tadbhedasya darśanamohasyāsravahetupratipādanārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 633. Now, since the causes of <s>āsrava</s> for <s>moha</s> (delusion), which shares in the intermediate enumeration, are to be stated, this is said for the purpose of explaining the causes of <s>āsrava</s> for its sub-variety, <s>darśanamoha</s> (perception-deluding karma) —

children.text: kevaliśrutasaṃghadharmadevāvarṇavādo darśanamohasya ||
children.translated_text: Speaking ill of the <s>Kevali</s> (omniscient one), the scriptures, the <s>saṃgha</s> (community of monks), the <s>dharma</s> (doctrine), and the <s>devas</s> (celestial beings) — this is the cause of <s>darśanamoha</s> (perception-deluding karma).

children.text: § 634. nirāvaraṇajñānāḥ kevalinaḥ. tadupadiṣṭaṃ buddhyatiśayarddhiyuktagaṇadharānusmṛtaṃ grantharacanaṃ śrutaṃ bhavati. ratnatrayopetaḥ śramaṇagaṇaḥ saṃghaḥ. ahiṃsālakṣaṇas tadāgamadeśito dharmaḥ. devāś caturṇikāya uktāḥ. guṇavatsu mahatsu asadbhūtadoṣodbhāvanam avarṇavādaḥ. eteṣv avarṇavādo darśanamohasyāsravahetuḥ. kavalābhyavahārajīvinaḥ kevalina ity evam ādi vacanaṃ kevalinām avarṇavādaḥ. māṃsabhakṣaṇādyanavadyābhidhānaṃ śrutāvarṇavādaḥ. śūdratvāśucitvādyāvirbhāvanaṃ saṃghāvarṇavādaḥ. jinopadiṣṭo dharmo nirguṇas tadupasevino ye te cāsurā bhaviṣyantīty evam ādy abhidhānaṃ dharmāvarṇavādaḥ. surāmāṃsopasevādyāghoṣaṇaṃ devāvarṇavādaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 634. <s>Kevalins</s> (omniscients) are those possessing unveiling knowledge. <s>Śruta</s> (scripture) consists of the compositions of texts remembered by the <s>Gaṇadharas</s> (chief disciples) endowed with exceptional intellect and supernatural power, as instructed by them [the <s>Kevalins</s>]. <s>Saṃgha</s> (congregation) is the community of monks endowed with the three jewels (<s>ratnatraya</s>). <s>Dharma</s> (religion) is characterized by non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), as taught by their scripture. <s>Devas</s> (celestials) are of four orders as stated. <s>Avarṇavāda</s> (defamation) is the fabrication of nonexistent faults in those great beings who possess virtues. Defamation of these is the cause of influx of faith-deluding [<s>karma</s>]. Saying things like '<s>Kevalins</s> sustain themselves by morsel-food' is defamation of the <s>Kevalins</s>. Calling meat-eating and the like blameless is defamation of scripture. Manifesting [false attributions of] low caste, impurity, and the like is defamation of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. Saying 'the religion taught by the <s>Jina</s> is without merit, and those who practice it will become <s>Asuras</s>' and such things is defamation of <s>Dharma</s>. Proclaiming [that the gods engage in] wine-drinking, meat-eating, and the like is defamation of the <s>Devas</s>.

children.text: § 635. dvitīyasya mohasyāsravabhedapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 635. For the purpose of explaining the divisions of influx of the second type of delusion, he says—

children.text: kaṣāyodayāt tīvrapariṇāmaś cāritramohasya ||
children.translated_text: Intense inclination arising from the fruition of passions (<s>kaṣāya</s>) is [the influx] of conduct-deluding [<s>karma</s>]. ||

children.text: § 636. kaṣāyā uktāḥ. udayo vipākaḥ. kaṣāyāṇām udayāt tīvrapariṇāmaś cāritramohasyāsravo veditavyaḥ. tatra svaparakaṣāyotpādanaṃ tapasvijanavṛttadūṣaṇaṃ saṃkliṣṭaliṅgavratadhāraṇādiḥ kaṣāyavedanīyasyāsravaḥ. saddharmopahasanadīnātihāsakandarpopahāsabahuvipralāpopahāsaśīlatādir hāsyavedanīyasya. vicitrakrīḍanaparatāvrataśīlārucyādiḥ rativedanīyasya. parāratiprādurbhāvanarativināśanapāpāśīlasaṃsargādiḥ arativedanīyasya. svaśokotpādanaparaśokaplutābhinandanādiḥ śokavedanīyasya. svabhayapariṇāmaparabhayotpādanādir bhayavedanīyasya. kuśalakriyācārajugupsāparivādaśīlatvādir jugupsāvedanīyasya. alīkābhidhāyitātisaṃdhānaparatvapararandhraprekṣitvapravṛddharāgādiḥ strīvedanīyasya. stokakrodhānutsukatvasvadārasaṃtoṣādiḥ puṃvedanīyasya. pracurakaṣāyāguhyendriyavyaparopaṇaparāṅganāvaskandādir napuṃsakavedanīyasya.
children.translated_text: § 636. The <s>kaṣāyas</s> (passions) have been stated. Fruition (<s>udaya</s>) means ripening. The influx of conduct-deluding [<s>karma</s>] should be understood as the intense inclination arising from the fruition of passions. Among these: generating passions in oneself and others, corrupting the conduct of ascetics, wearing the marks and vows of an impure [ascetic] life, and the like—this is the influx of passion-experiencing [<s>karma</s>]. Ridiculing the true religion, excessive laughter, amorous sport, mockery, and propensity for much idle talk—this is [the influx] of laughter-experiencing [<s>karma</s>]. Attachment to various amusements, distaste for vows and moral conduct—this is [the influx] of pleasure-experiencing [<s>karma</s>]. Generating displeasure in others, destroying [others'] delight, association with sinful conduct—this is [the influx] of displeasure-experiencing [<s>karma</s>]. Producing grief in oneself, rejoicing at another's grief—this is [the influx] of grief-experiencing [<s>karma</s>]. The inclination toward one's own fear, generating fear in others—this is [the influx] of fear-experiencing [<s>karma</s>]. Disgust toward virtuous practices and conduct, propensity for slander—this is [the influx] of disgust-experiencing [<s>karma</s>]. Speaking falsehood, excessive scheming, prying into others' faults, intensified attachment—this is [the influx] of feminine-sex-passion-experiencing [<s>karma</s>]. Mild anger, lack of eagerness, contentment with one's own wife—this is [the influx] of masculine-sex-passion-experiencing [<s>karma</s>]. Abundant passions, concealed genital manipulation, assault on others' wives—this is [the influx] of neuter-sex-passion-experiencing [<s>karma</s>].

children.text: § 637. nirdiṣṭo mohanīyasyāsravabhedaḥ. idānīṃ tadanantaranirdiṣṭasyāyuṣa āsravahetau vaktavye ādyasya niyatakālaparipākasyāyuṣaḥ kāraṇapradarśanārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 637. The divisions of the influx of deluding [<s>karma</s>] have been stated. Now, regarding the cause of influx of lifespan-determining [<s>karma</s>], which was mentioned next, for the purpose of showing the cause of the first [type of] lifespan, which matures at a fixed time, this is said—

children.text: bahvārambhaparigrahatvaṃ nārakasyāyuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Abundance of occupation and possessiveness [is the cause of influx] of hellish lifespan (<s>nāraka-āyus</s>). ||

children.text: § 638. ārambhaḥ prāṇipīḍāhetur vyāpāraḥ. mamedaṃ buddhilakṣaṇaḥ parigrahaḥ. ārambhāś ca parigrahāś ca ārambhaparigrahāḥ. bahava ārambhaparigrahā yasya sa bahvārambhaparigrahaḥ. tasya bhāvo bahvārambhaparigrahatvam. hiṃsādikrūrakarmājasrapravartanaparasvaharaṇaviṣayātigṛddhikṛṣṇaleśyābhijātaraudradhyānamaraṇakālatādilakṣaṇo nārakasyāyuṣa āsravo bhavati.
children.translated_text: § 638. Occupation (<s>ārambha</s>) is activity that causes harm to living beings. Possessiveness (<s>parigraha</s>) is characterized by the notion 'this is mine.' Occupations and possessivenesses are '<s>ārambha-parigraha</s>.' One who has abundant occupations and possessivenesses is '<s>bahvārambha-parigraha</s>.' His state is 'abundance of occupation and possessiveness.' The influx of hellish lifespan is characterized by: constantly engaging in cruel actions such as violence, stealing others' property, excessive greed for sense-objects, being of black <s>leśyā</s> (soul-coloring), practicing fierce meditation (<s>raudra-dhyāna</s>), and [the state at the] time of death, and so forth.

children.text: § 639. āha, ukto nārakasyāyuṣa āsravaḥ. tairyagyonasyedānīṃ vaktavya ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 639. He says: the influx of hellish lifespan has been stated. Now the [influx] of animal lifespan is to be stated—to this it is said—

children.text: māyā tairyagyonasya ||
children.translated_text: Deceit (<s>māyā</s>) [is the cause of influx] of animal [lifespan]. ||

children.text: § 640. cāritramohakarmaviśeṣasyodayād āvirbhūta ātmanaḥ kuṭilabhāvo māyā nikṛtiḥ tairyagyonasyāyuṣa āsravo veditavyaḥ. tatprapañco mithyātvopetadharmadeśanā niḥśīlatātisaṃdhānapriyatā nīlakāpotaleśyārtadhyānamaraṇakālatādiḥ.
children.translated_text: § 640. <s>Māyā</s> (deceit) is the crooked disposition of the self manifested from the fruition of a particular conduct-deluding <s>karma</s>—deception—this should be understood as the influx of animal lifespan. Its elaboration: teaching religion while possessing wrong faith, propensity for duplicity and dishonesty, blue or grey <s>leśyā</s>, sorrowful meditation (<s>ārta-dhyāna</s>), and [the state at the] time of death, and so forth.

children.text: § 641. āha, vyākhyātas tairyagyonasyāyuṣa āsravaḥ. idānīṃ mānuṣasyāyuṣuḥ ko hetur ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 641. He says: the influx of animal lifespan has been explained. Now, what is the cause of human lifespan? To this it is said—

children.text: alpārambhaparigrahatvaṃ mānuṣasya ||
children.translated_text: Scarcity of occupation and possessiveness [is the cause of influx] of human [lifespan]. ||

children.text: § 642. nārakāyur āsravo vyākhyātaḥ. tadviparīto mānuṣasyāyuṣa iti saṃkṣepaḥ. tadvyāsaḥ — vinītasvabhāvaḥ prakṛtibhadratā praguṇavyavahāratā tanukaṣāyatvaṃ maraṇakālāsaṃkleśatādiḥ.
children.translated_text: § 642. The influx of hellish lifespan has been explained. The opposite of that is [the influx] of human lifespan—in brief. Its elaboration: having a disciplined nature, innate goodness, straightforward conduct, mild passions, and freedom from distress at the time of death, and so forth.

children.text: § 643. kim etāvān eva mānuṣasyāyuṣa āsrava ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 643. Is this alone the influx of human lifespan? To this it is said—

children.text: svabhāvamārdavaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And natural gentleness (<s>svabhāva-mārdava</s>). ||

children.text: § 644. mṛdor bhāvo mārdavam. svabhāvena mārdavaṃ svabhāvamārdavaṃ. upadeśānapekṣam ity arthaḥ. etad api mānuṣasyāyuṣa āsravaḥ. pṛthagyogakaraṇaṃ kim artham? uttarārtham, devāyuṣa āsravo ’yam api yathā syāt.
children.translated_text: § 644. The quality of being soft (<s>mṛdu</s>) is '<s>mārdava</s>' (gentleness). Gentleness by nature is 'natural gentleness'—meaning: not dependent on instruction. This too is the influx of human lifespan. Why is a separate formulation made? For the purpose of what follows—so that this may also be [understood as] an influx of celestial lifespan.

children.text: § 645. kim etad eva dvitīyaṃ mānuṣasyāsravaḥ? na; ity ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 645. Is this alone the second [cause of] influx for human [lifespan]? No; it is said—

children.text: niśśīlavratatvaṃ ca sarveṣām ||
children.translated_text: And the state of being without [true] moral conduct and vows (<s>niḥśīla-vratatva</s>) [is the influx] for all [lifespans]. ||

children.text: § 646. ‘ca’ śabdo ’dhikṛtasamucyayārthaḥ.

alpārambhaparigrahatvaṃ ca niḥśīlavratatvaṃ ca. śīlāni ca vratāni ca śīlavratāni tāni vakṣyate. niṣkrāntaḥ śīlavratebhyo niḥśīlavrataḥ. tasya bhāvo niḥśīlavratatvam. ‘sarveṣāṃ’ grahaṇaṃ sakalāyurāsravapratipattyartham. kiṃ devāyuṣo ’pi bhavati? satyam, bhavati bhogabhūmijāpekṣayā.
children.translated_text: Scarcity of occupation and possessiveness, and the state of being without moral conduct and vows. Moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) and vows (<s>vrata</s>) are '<s>śīla-vratas</s>'—these will be explained. One who has departed from moral conduct and vows is '<s>niḥśīlavrata</s>.' His state is '<s>niḥśīlavratatva</s>.' The mention of 'for all' (<s>sarveṣām</s>) is for the purpose of including [this as a cause of influx for] all lifespans. Does it apply even to celestial lifespan? Yes, it does—with reference to those born in the lands of enjoyment (<s>bhogabhūmi</s>).
§ 646. The particle '<s>ca</s>' (and) is for the purpose of cumulative inclusion with what has been established.

children.text: § 647. atha caturthasyāyuṣaḥ ka āsrava ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 647. Now, what is the influx of the fourth [type of] lifespan? To this it is said—

children.text: sarāgasaṃyamasaṃyamāsaṃyamākāmanirjarābālatapāṃsi daivasya ||
children.translated_text: Restraint with attachment (<s>sarāga-saṃyama</s>), partial restraint-cum-non-restraint (<s>saṃyamāsaṃyama</s>), involuntary austerity (<s>akāma-nirjarā</s>), and childish austerity (<s>bāla-tapas</s>) [are the causes of influx] of celestial [lifespan]. ||

children.text: § 648. sarāgasaṃyamaḥ saṃyamāsaṃyamaś ca vyākhyātau. akāmanirjarā akāmaś cārakanirodhabandhanabaddheṣu kṣuttṛṣṇānirodhabrahmacaryabhūśayyāmaladhāraṇaparitāpādiḥ. akāmena nirjarā akāmanirjarā. bālatapo mithyādarśanopetam anupāyakāyakleśapracuraṃ nikṛtibahulavratadhāraṇam. tāny etani daivasyāyuṣa āsravahetavo veditavyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 648. Restraint with attachment (<s>sarāga-saṃyama</s>) and partial restraint-cum-non-restraint (<s>saṃyamāsaṃyama</s>) have been explained. Involuntary austerity (<s>akāma-nirjarā</s>): among those who are involuntarily subjected to imprisonment, bondage, suppression of hunger and thirst, celibacy, sleeping on the ground, bearing filth, and affliction—the shedding [of <s>karma</s>] that is involuntary (<s>akāma</s>) is '<s>akāma-nirjarā</s>.' Childish austerity (<s>bāla-tapas</s>) is the observance of vows attended by wrong faith, abundant bodily mortification without proper method, and full of deceit. These are to be understood as the causes of influx of celestial lifespan.

children.text: § 649. kim etāvan eva daivasyāyuṣa āsravaḥ. nety āha —
children.translated_text: § 649. Is this alone the influx of celestial lifespan? No, he says—

children.text: samyaktvam ca ||
children.translated_text: And right faith (<s>samyaktva</s>). ||
