children.text: § 650. kim? daivasyāyuṣa āsrava ity anuvartate. aviśeṣābhidhāne ’pi saudharmādiviśeṣagatiḥ. kutaḥ? pṛthakkaraṇāt. yady evam, pūrvasūtre, ukta āsravavidhir aviśeṣeṇa prasaktaḥ tena sarāgasaṃyamasaṃyamāsaṃyamāv api bhavanavāsyādyāyuṣa āsravau prāpnutaḥ. naiṣa doṣaḥ; samyaktvābhāve sati tadvyapadeśābhāvāt tadubhayam apy atrāntarbhavati.
children.translated_text: § 650. What? [It is] the influx of celestial lifespan—this is supplied. Even though stated without specification, the specific reference to <s>Saudharma</s> and higher [celestial realms] is understood. Why? Because of separate formulation. If so, the influx-procedure stated in the previous <s>sūtra</s>, being applicable without specification, would entail that restraint with attachment and partial restraint-cum-non-restraint also become influxes of <s>Bhavanavāsi</s> and other [lower celestial] lifespans. This is no defect; in the absence of right faith, there being no designation of those [higher celestial categories], both of those [i.e., the causes in the previous sūtra] are included here [for the lower celestials].

children.text: § 651. āyuṣo ’nantaram uddiṣṭasya nāmna āsravavidhau vaktavye, tatrāśubhānāmna āsravapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 651. After lifespan, for the purpose of understanding the influx of name-determining [<s>karma</s>], which was mentioned next, he says regarding the influx of inauspicious name-determining [<s>karma</s>]—

children.text: yogavakratā visaṃvādanaṃ cāśubhasya nāmnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Crookedness of activity (<s>yoga-vakratā</s>) and deception (<s>visaṃvādana</s>) [are the causes of influx] of inauspicious name-determining [<s>karma</s>]. ||

children.text: § 652. yogas triprakāro vyākhyātaḥ. tasya vakratā kauṭilyam. visaṃvādanam anyathāpravartanam. nanu ca nārthabhedaḥ. yogavakrataivānyathāpravartanam? satyam evam etat — svagatā yogavakratety ucyate. paragataṃ visaṃvādanam. samyagabhyudayaniḥśreyasārthāsu kriyāsu pravartamānam anyaṃ tadviparītakāyavāṅmanobhir visaṃvādayati maivaṃ kārṣīr evam kurvīti. etad ubhayam aśubhanāmakarmāsravakāraṇaṃ veditavyam. ‘ca’ śabdena mithyādarśanapaiśunyāsthiracittatākūṭamānatulākaraṇaparanindātmapraśaṃsādiḥ samuccīyate.
children.translated_text: § 652. Activity (<s>yoga</s>) has been explained as threefold. Its crookedness (<s>vakratā</s>) is dishonesty. Deception (<s>visaṃvādana</s>) is acting otherwise [than one professes]. [Objection:] But there is no difference in meaning—crookedness of activity is itself acting otherwise? [Reply:] True indeed; but crookedness of activity is said with reference to oneself. Deception is with reference to another—misleading another who is engaged in proper activities for spiritual uplift and liberation by body, speech, and mind [saying]: 'Don't do this, do that.' Both of these should be understood as causes of influx of inauspicious name-determining <s>karma</s>. By the particle '<s>ca</s>' (and), the following are also included: wrong faith, tale-bearing, mental instability, using false weights and measures, slandering others, praising oneself, and the like.

children.text: § 653. atha śubhanāmakarmaṇaḥ ka āsrava ity atra ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 653. Now, what is the influx of auspicious name-determining <s>karma</s>? To this it is said—

children.text: tadviparītaṃ śubhasya ||
children.translated_text: The opposite of that [is the influx] of the auspicious [name-determining <s>karma</s>]. ||

children.text: § 654. kāyavāṅmanasām ṛjutvam avisaṃvādanaṃ ca tadviparītam. ‘ca’ śabdena samuccitasya ca viparītaṃ grāhyam. dhārmikadarśanasaṃbhramasadbhāvopanayanasaṃsaraṇabhīrutāpramādavarjanādiḥ. tadetac chubhanāmakarmāsravakāraṇaṃ veditavyam.
children.translated_text: § 654. Straightness of body, speech, and mind, and non-deception—these are the opposite. By the particle '<s>ca</s>' (and), the opposite of what was cumulatively included [before] should also be taken: religious outlook, agitation [at seeing religious practices], bringing forth good qualities, fear of transmigration, avoidance of negligence, and the like. These should be understood as the causes of influx of auspicious name-determining <s>karma</s>.

children.text: § 655. āha kim etāvān eva śubhanāmna āsravavidhir uta kaścid asti prativiśeṣa ity atrocyate — yad idaṃ tīrthakaranāmakarmānantānupamaprabhāvam acintyavibhūtiviśeṣakāraṇaṃ trailokyavijayakaraṃ tasyāsravavidhiviśeṣo ’stīti. yady evam ucyatām ke tasyāsravaḥ. ity ata idam ārabhyate —
children.translated_text: § 655. He says: is this alone the influx-procedure for auspicious name-determining [<s>karma</s>], or is there some specific [additional influx]? To this it is said: there exists this name-determining <s>karma</s> of the <s>Tīrthaṅkara</s> (ford-maker), of infinite, incomparable power, the cause of inconceivable extraordinary splendor, conquering the triple world—for this, there is a specific influx-procedure. If so, let the influx [causes] be stated. Therefore this is begun—

children.text: darśanaviśuddhir vinayasampannatā śīlavrateṣv anatīcāro ’bhīkṣṇajñānopayogasaṃvegau śaktitas tyāgatapasī sādhusamādhir vaiyāvṛttyakaraṇam arhadācāryabahuśrutapravacanabhaktir āvaśyakāparihāṇir mārgaprabhāvanā pravacanavatsalatvam iti tīrthakaratvasya ||
children.translated_text: Purity of faith (<s>darśana-viśuddhi</s>), perfection of reverence (<s>vinaya-sampannatā</s>), faultless observance of moral conduct and vows (<s>śīla-vrateṣv anatīcāra</s>), constant engagement in knowledge (<s>abhīkṣṇa-jñānopayoga</s>), spiritual ardor (<s>saṃvega</s>), giving and austerity according to one's capacity (<s>śaktitas tyāga-tapas</s>), supporting monks in difficulty (<s>sādhu-samādhi</s>), rendering service (<s>vaiyāvṛttya-karaṇa</s>), devotion to the <s>Arhat</s>, the <s>Ācārya</s>, the learned (<s>bahuśruta</s>), and the teaching (<s>pravacana</s>), non-neglect of the essential duties (<s>āvaśyakāparihāṇi</s>), propagation of the path (<s>mārga-prabhāvanā</s>), and affection for the teaching (<s>pravacana-vatsalatva</s>)—these [are the causes of influx] of <s>Tīrthaṅkara</s> [name-determining <s>karma</s>]. ||

children.text: § 656. jinena bhagavatārhatparameṣṭhinopadiṣṭe nirgranthalakṣaṇe mokṣavartmani rucir darśanaviśuddhiḥ prāguktalakṣaṇā. tasyā aṣṭāv aṅgāni niśśaṅkitatvaṃ niḥkāṅkṣitā vicikitsāvirahatā amūḍhadṛṣṭitā upabṛṃhaṇaṃ sthitīkaraṇaṃ vātsalyaṃ prabhāvanaṃ ceti. samyagjñānādiṣu mokṣamārgeṣu tatsādhaneṣu ca gurvādiṣu svayogyavṛttyā satkāra ādaro vinayas tena saṃpannatā vinayasaṃpannatā. ahiṃsādiṣu vrateṣu tatpratipālanārtheṣu ca krodhavarjanādiṣu śīleṣu niravadyā vṛttiḥ śīlavrateṣv anatīcāraḥ. jīvādipadārthasvatattvaviṣaye samyagjñāne nityaṃ yuktatā abhīkṣaṇajñānopayogaḥ. saṃsāraduḥkhān nityabhīrutā saṃvegaḥ. tyāgo dānam. tat trividham — āhāradānam abhayadānaṃ jñādānaṃ ceti. tacchaktito yathāvidhi prayujyamānaṃ tyāga ity ucyate. anigūhitavīryasya mārgāvirodhi kāyakleśas tapaḥ. yathā bhāṇḍāgāre dahane samutthite tatpraśamanam anuṣṭhīyate bahūpakāratvāt tathānekavrataśīlasamṛddhasya munes tapasaḥ kutaścit pratyūhe samupasthite tatsaṃdhāraṇaṃ samādhiḥ. guṇavadduḥkhopanipāte niravadyena vidhinā tadapaharaṇaṃ vaiyāvṛttyam. arhadācāryeṣu bahuśruteṣu pravacane ca bhāvaviśuddhiyukto ’nurāgo bhaktiḥ. ṣaṇṇām āvaśyakakriyāṇāṃ yathākālaṃ pravartanam āvaśyakāparihāṇiḥ. jñānatapodānajinapūjāvidhinā dharmaprakāśanaṃ mārgaprabhāvanā. vatse dhenuvatsadharmaṇi snehaḥ pravacanavatsalatvam. tāny etāni ṣodaṣakāraṇāni samyagbhāvyamānāni vyastāni ca tīrthakaranāmakarmāsrvakāraṇāni pratyetavyāni.
children.translated_text: § 656. Purity of faith (<s>darśana-viśuddhi</s>) is delight in the path to liberation characterized by the <s>Nirgrantha</s> [teaching], as taught by the blessed Lord <s>Arhat Parameṣṭhin</s> (the <s>Jina</s>)—with the previously stated definition. Its eight limbs are: freedom from suspicion (<s>niśśaṅkitatva</s>), freedom from expectation (<s>niḥkāṅkṣitā</s>), freedom from disgust (<s>vicikitsā-virahitā</s>), undeluded vision (<s>amūḍha-dṛṣṭitā</s>), nourishment (<s>upabṛṃhaṇa</s>), stabilization (<s>sthitīkaraṇa</s>), affection (<s>vātsalya</s>), and propagation (<s>prabhāvana</s>). Reverence (<s>vinaya</s>) is the respectful honor shown through one's proper conduct toward the paths to liberation—right knowledge and the like—and their instruments—teachers and the like. Being endowed with that reverence is 'perfection of reverence.' Faultless conduct in the vows of non-violence and the like, and in the moral practices such as avoidance of anger that serve to protect those [vows], is 'faultless observance of moral conduct and vows.' Constant engagement in right knowledge regarding the true nature of the categories such as <s>jīva</s> (soul) and the like is 'constant engagement in knowledge.' Perpetual fear of the sufferings of transmigration (<s>saṃsāra</s>) is 'spiritual ardor' (<s>saṃvega</s>). Giving (<s>tyāga</s>) is donation. It is threefold: giving food (<s>āhāra-dāna</s>), giving freedom from fear (<s>abhaya-dāna</s>), and giving knowledge (<s>jñāna-dāna</s>). That [giving], practiced according to one's capacity and in proper manner, is called '<s>tyāga</s>.' Bodily mortification that does not conceal one's power and does not contradict the path is austerity (<s>tapas</s>). Just as when a fire breaks out in a treasury, extinguishing it is undertaken because of its great utility—so too, for a monk rich in many vows and moral practices, when some obstacle arises, maintaining [those practices] is '<s>samādhi</s>' (supporting in difficulty). Removing the suffering of a virtuous person by blameless means is 'rendering service' (<s>vaiyāvṛttya</s>). Affection accompanied by purity of disposition toward the <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Ācāryas</s>, the learned, and the teaching is 'devotion' (<s>bhakti</s>). Performing the six essential duties (<s>āvaśyaka-kriyā</s>) at the proper time is 'non-neglect of essential duties.' Illuminating religion through the means of knowledge, austerity, giving, and worship of the <s>Jina</s> is 'propagation of the path.' Affection like that of a cow for her calf is 'affection for the teaching' (<s>pravacana-vatsalatva</s>). These sixteen causes, properly cultivated both collectively and individually, should be understood as the causes of influx of <s>Tīrthaṅkara</s> name-determining <s>karma</s>.

children.text: § 657. idānīṃ nāmāsravābhidhānānantaraṃ gotrāsrave vaktavye sati nīcairgotrasyāsravavidhānārtham idam āha —
children.translated_text: § 657. Now, after the statement of the influx of name-determining [<s>karma</s>], when the influx of status-determining (<s>gotra</s>) [<s>karma</s>] is to be stated, he says regarding the influx of low-status-determining [<s>karma</s>]—

children.text: parātmanindāpraśaṃse sadasatguṇocchādanodbhāvane ca nīcairgotrasya ||
children.translated_text: Slandering others, praising oneself, concealing the good qualities [of others], and proclaiming the bad qualities [of others]—these [are the causes of influx] of low status-determining (<s>nīcairgotra</s>) [<s>karma</s>]. ||

children.text: § 658. tathyasya vātathyasya vā doṣasyodbhāvanaṃ prati icchā nindā. guṇodbhāvanābhiprāyaḥ praśaṃsā. yathāsaṃkhyam abhisaṃbandhaḥ — paranindā ātmapraśaṃseti. pratibandhakahetusaṃnidhāne sati anudbhūtavṛttitā anāvirbhāva ucchādanam. pratibandhakābhāve prakāśavṛttitā udbhāvanam. atrāpi ca yathākramam abhisaṃbandhaḥ — sadguṇocchādanam asadguṇodbhāvanam iti. tāny etāni nīcairgotrasyāsravakāraṇāni veditavyāni.
children.translated_text: § 658. The desire to bring forth a fault—whether true or untrue—[in another] is slander (<s>nindā</s>). [The desire] intended to bring forth virtues [in oneself] is praise (<s>praśaṃsā</s>). The connection is in order: 'slandering others' and 'praising oneself.' Non-manifestation when a revealing cause is present—concealment (<s>ucchādana</s>). Manifestation when there is no obstruction—proclamation (<s>udbhāvana</s>). Here too, the connection is in order: 'concealing good qualities' and 'proclaiming bad qualities.' These should be understood as the causes of influx of low status-determining [<s>karma</s>].

children.text: § 659. athoccairgotrasya ka āsravavidhir atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 659. Now, what is the influx-procedure for high status-determining [<s>karma</s>]? To this it is said—

children.text: tadviparyayo nīcair vṛttyanutsekau cottarasya ||
children.translated_text: The opposite of that, together with humble conduct and absence of pride, [is the influx] of the latter [high status-determining <s>karma</s>]. ||

children.text: § 660. ‘tat’ ity anena pratyāsatter nīcairgotrasyāsravaḥ pratinirdiśyate. anyena prakāreṇa vṛttir viparyayaḥ. tasya viparyayas tadviparyayaḥ. kaḥ punar asau viparyayaḥ? ātmanindā, parapraśaṃsā, sadguṇodbhāvanam asadguṇocchādanaṃ ca. guṇotkṛṣṭeṣu vinayenāvanatir nīcair vṛttiḥ. vijñānādibhir utkṛṣṭasyāpi satas tatkṛtamadaviraho ’nahaṃkāratānutsekaḥ. tāny etāny uttarasyoccair gotrasyāsravakāraṇāni bhavanti.
children.translated_text: § 660. By the word 'tat' (that), due to proximity, the influx (<s>āsrava</s>) of low-status-determining karma (<s>nīcair-gotra</s>) is indicated. 'Reverse conduct' (<s>viparyaya</s>) means behaving in another manner. What is that reverse? Self-deprecation, praising others, displaying [one's own] good qualities [only to flaunt them], and concealing [others'] faults. Bowing humbly to those superior in virtues is low behavior (<s>nīcair-vṛtti</s>). The absence of pride arising from superiority in knowledge and the like — freedom from ego, non-arrogance — these are the causes of the influx of the opposite, i.e., the high-status-determining karma (<s>uccair-gotra</s>).

children.text: § 661. atha gotrānantaram uddiṣṭasyāntarāyasya ka āsrava ity ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 661. Now, after <s>gotra</s> (status-determining karma), what is the influx of <s>antarāya</s> (obstructing karma), which was listed next? It is said —

children.text: vighnakaraṇam antarāyasya ||
children.translated_text: The causing of obstruction (<s>vighna-karaṇa</s>) is [the influx] of <s>antarāya</s> (obstructing karma).

children.text: § 662. dānādīny uktāni ‘dānalābhabhogopahogavīryāṇi ca’ ity atra. teṣāṃ vihananaṃ vighnaḥ. vighnasya karaṇaṃ vighnakaraṇam antarāyasyāsravavidhir veditavyaḥ. atra codyate — tatpradoṣanihnavādayo jñānadarśanāvaraṇādīnāṃ pratiniyatā āsravahetavo varṇitāḥ, kiṃ te pratiniyatajñānāvaraṇādyāsravahetava eva utāviśeṣeṇeti. yadi pratiniyatajñānāvaraṇādyāsravahetavaḥ eva, āgamavirodhaḥ prasajyate. āgame hi sapta karmāṇi āyurvarjyāni pratikṣaṇaṃ yugapad āsravantīty uktam. tadvirodhaḥ syāt. athāviśeṣeṇa āsravahetavo viśeṣanirdeśo na yukta iti? atrocyate — yady api tatpradoṣādibhir jñānāvaraṇādīnāṃ sarvāsāṃ karmaprakṛtīnāṃ pradeśabandhaniyamo nāsti, tathāpy anubhāganiyamahetutvena tatpradoṣanihnavādayo vibhājyante.
children.translated_text: § 662. Giving and the rest have been mentioned in '<s>dāna-lābha-bhoga-upabhoga-vīryāṇi ca</s>' (giving, gain, enjoyment, re-enjoyment, and power). The impeding of these is obstruction (<s>vighna</s>). The causing of obstruction is the method of influx of <s>antarāya</s> karma. Here an objection is raised: The causes of influx have been described as specifically assigned — disparagement of [right knowledge] and the like as causes for the influx of knowledge-obscuring karma and the rest. Are these causes of influx specifically assigned to knowledge-obscuring karma and the rest, or are they non-specific? If they are specifically assigned, there would be a contradiction with scripture. For in scripture it is said that seven karmas, excluding lifespan, flow in simultaneously at every instant. That would be contradicted. If they are non-specific, then the specific description would be unjustified? To this it is said: Although there is no restriction on the binding of karmic spatial points to all karmic species — knowledge-obscuring and the rest — through disparagement and the like, nevertheless, disparagement, concealment, and the like are classified as causes of the intensity of binding for [the respective karmas].

children.text: iti tattvārthavṛttau sarvārthasiddhisaṃjñikāyāṃ ṣaṣṭho ’dhyāyaḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth chapter of the <s>Tattvārthavṛtti</s> named <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>. ||6||

children.text: atha saptamo ’dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins the seventh chapter.

children.text: § 663. āsravapadārtho vyākhyātaḥ. tatprārambhakāle evoktaṃ ‘śubhaḥ puṇyasya’ iti tatsāmānyenoktam. tadviśeṣapratipattyarthaṃ kaḥ punaḥ śubha ity ukte idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 663. The category of <s>āsrava</s> (influx) has been explained. At the very beginning of that [discussion], it was said '<s>śubhaḥ puṇyasya</s>' (the auspicious [influx is that] of merit) — that was stated in general terms. To understand its specific nature: what is 'auspicious'? To this it is said —

children.text: hiṃsānṛtasteyābrahmaparigrahebhyo viratir vratam ||
children.translated_text: Abstention from violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>), falsehood (<s>anṛta</s>), theft (<s>steya</s>), unchastity (<s>abrahma</s>), and possessiveness (<s>parigraha</s>) is a vow (<s>vrata</s>).

children.text: § 664. ‘pramattayogāt prāṇavyaparopaṇaṃ hiṃsā’ ity evam ādibhiḥ sūtrair hiṃsādayo nirdekṣyante. tebhyo viramaṇaṃ viratir vratam ity ucyate. vratam abhisandhikṛto niyamaḥ, idaṃ kartavyam idaṃ na kartavyam iti vā. nanu ca hiṃsādayaḥ pariṇāmaviśeṣā adhruvāḥ, kathaṃ teṣām apādānatvam ucyate? buddhyapāye dhruvatvavivakṣopapatteḥ. yathā dharmād viramatīty atra ya eṣa manuṣyaḥ saṃbhinnabuddhiḥ sa paśyati — duṣkaro dharmaḥ, phalaṃ cāsya śraddhāmātragamyam iti sa buddhyā saṃprāpya nivartate. evam ihāpi ya eva manuṣyaḥ prekṣāpūrvakārī sa paśyati — ya ete hiṃsādayaḥ pariṇāmās te pāpahetavaḥ. pāpakarmaṇi pravartamānān janān ihaiva rājāno daṇḍayanti paratra ca duḥkham āpnuvantīti sa buddhyā saprāpya nivartate. tato buddhyā dhruvatvavivakṣopapatter apādānanatvaṃ yuktam. ‘virati’ śabdaḥ pratyekaṃ parisamāpyate hiṃsāyā viratiḥ anṛtād viratir ity evam ādi. tatra ahiṃsāvratam ādau kriyate pradhānatvāt. satyādīni hi tatparipālanārthāni sasyasya vṛtiparikṣepavat. sarvasāvadyanivṛttilakṣaṇasāmāyikāpekṣayā ekaṃ vrataṃ, tadeva chedopasthāpanāpekṣayā pañcavidham ihocyate. nanu ca asya vratasyāsravahetutvam anupapannaṃ saṃvarahetuṣv antarbhāvāt. saṃvarahetavo vakṣyante guptisamityādayaḥ. tatra daśavidhe dharme saṃyame vā vratānām antarbhāva iti? naiṣa doṣaḥ; tatra saṃvaro nivṛttilakṣaṇo vakṣyate. pravṛttiś cātra dṛśyate; hiṃsānṛtādattādānādiparityāge ahiṃsāsatyavacanadattādānādikriyāpratīteḥ guptyādisaṃvaraparikarmatvāc ca. vrateṣu hi kṛtaparikarmā sādhuḥ sukhena saṃvaraṃ karotīti tataḥ pṛthaktvenopadeśaḥ kriyate. nanu ca ṣaṣṭham aṇuvratam asti rātribhojanaviramaṇaṃ tadihopasaṃkhyātavyam? na; bhāvanāsv antarbhāvāt. ahiṃsāvratabhāvanā hi vakṣyante. tatra ālokitapānabhojanabhāvanā kāryeti.
children.translated_text: § 664. Violence and the rest will be defined by sūtras such as '<s>pramattayogāt prāṇavyaparopaṇaṃ hiṃsā</s>' (violence is the depriving of vital forces through negligent activity). The desisting from these is abstention (<s>virati</s>), which is called a vow (<s>vrata</s>). A vow is a deliberate commitment: 'this is to be done, this is not to be done.' [Objection:] But violence and the rest are specific mental modifications that are impermanent — how can they be [treated as] the source from which one desists? [Reply:] Because the intention to regard [them as] permanent is justified when [considering] the cessation of the intellect [that leads to them]. Just as [in the statement] 'he desists from <s>dharma</s> (righteousness)' — here, the person of confused understanding sees that <s>dharma</s> is difficult and its fruit is grasped only through faith, and so, having intellectually grasped [this], he turns away. So too here: the person who acts with deliberation sees that these transformations — violence and the like — are causes of sin; that people engaged in sinful actions are punished here by kings and attain suffering hereafter; and so, having intellectually grasped [this], he turns away. Therefore, the source-role [of hiṃsā etc.] is justified through the intention to regard [them] as permanent by way of the intellect. The word '<s>virati</s>' (abstention) is individually completed: 'abstention from violence,' 'abstention from falsehood,' and so on. Among these, the non-violence vow is stated first because of its pre-eminence. For truthfulness and the rest serve to protect it, like a fence around a crop. Viewed from the perspective of <s>sāmāyika</s> (equanimity) — characterized by the cessation of all harmful [activities] — the vow is one; that same [vow], viewed from the perspective of <s>chedopasthāpanā</s> (re-initiation), is said here to be fivefold. [Objection:] The characterization of this vow as a cause of influx is unjustified, since it should be included among the causes of <s>saṃvara</s> (stoppage). The causes of <s>saṃvara</s> will be described — <s>gupti</s> (restraint of activity), <s>samiti</s> (carefulness), and the like. The vows should be included there, within the tenfold <s>dharma</s> or within restraint. [Reply:] This is not a defect; <s>saṃvara</s> will be described there as characterized by cessation. But here, activity is observed: in the abandoning of violence, falsehood, and taking what is not given, the activities of non-violence, truthful speech, and accepting what is given are understood — and because [vows are] a preparatory discipline for <s>saṃvara</s> through <s>gupti</s> and the like. For one who has undergone the preparatory discipline of vows easily accomplishes <s>saṃvara</s> — therefore they are taught separately. [Objection:] But is there not a sixth minor vow — abstention from eating at night — which should be mentioned here? [Reply:] No, because it is included among the contemplations (<s>bhāvanā</s>). For the contemplations of the non-violence vow will be described; and therein, the contemplation of 'eating and drinking after inspection' should be practiced.

children.text: § 665. tasya pañcatayasya vratasya bhedapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: § 665. To understand the divisions of that fivefold vow, he says —

children.text: deśasarvato ’ṇumahatī ||
children.translated_text: From partial and complete [abstention], [the vow is] minor (<s>aṇu</s>) and great (<s>mahat</s>).

children.text: § 666. deśa ekadeśaḥ. sarvaḥ sakalaḥ. deśaś ca sarvaś ca deśasarvau tābhyaṃ deśasarvataḥ. ‘viratiḥ’ ity anuvartate. aṇu ca mahac cāṇumahatī. vratābhisaṃbandhān napuṃsakaliṅganirdeśaḥ. yathāsaṃkhyam abhisaṃbadhyate. deśato viratir aṇuvrataṃ sarvato viratir mahāvratam iti dvidhā bhidyate pratyekaṃ vratam. etāni vratāni bhāvitāni varauṣadhavadyatnavate duḥkhanivṛttinimittāni bhavanti.
children.translated_text: § 666. '<s>Deśa</s>' means 'partial.' '<s>Sarva</s>' means 'complete.' From partial and complete [abstention] — from both. 'Abstention' (<s>virati</s>) continues [from the previous sūtra]. Minor and great — <s>aṇumahatī</s>. The neuter gender is used because of its connection with 'vow.' It is connected in order: partial abstention is a minor vow (<s>aṇu-vrata</s>); complete abstention is a great vow (<s>mahā-vrata</s>) — thus each vow is divided in two. These vows, when cultivated, become the cause of the cessation of suffering for the diligent, like a supreme medicine.

children.text: § 667. kim arthaṃ kathaṃ vā bhāvanaṃ teṣām ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 667. For what purpose and how are they to be contemplated? To this it is said —

children.text: tatsthairyārthaṃ bhāvanāḥ pañca pañca ||
children.translated_text: For their stability, there are five contemplations (<s>bhāvanā</s>) for each [vow], [totaling] five sets of five.

children.text: § 668. teṣāṃ vratānāṃ sthirīkaraṇāyaikaikasya vratasya pañca pañca bhāvanā veditavyāḥ. yady evam ādyasyāhiṃsāvratasya bhāvanāḥ kā ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 668. For the strengthening of each vow, five contemplations are to be known. If so, what are the contemplations of the first non-violence vow? To this it is said —

children.text: vāńmanoguptīryādānanikṣepaṇasamityālokitapānabhojanāni pañca ||
children.translated_text: Restraint of speech (<s>vāg-gupti</s>), restraint of mind (<s>mano-gupti</s>), carefulness in walking (<s>īryā-samiti</s>), carefulness in handling objects (<s>ādāna-nikṣepaṇa-samiti</s>), and inspecting one's food and drink (<s>ālokita-pāna-bhojana</s>) — these are the five.

children.text: § 669. vāgguptīḥ manoguptīḥ īryāsamitiḥ ādānānanikṣepaṇasamitiḥ ālokitapānabhojanam ity etāḥ pañcāhiṃsāvratasya bhāvanāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 669. Restraint of speech, restraint of mind, carefulness in walking, carefulness in handling objects, and inspecting one's food and drink — these are the five contemplations of the non-violence vow.

children.text: § 670. atha dvitīyasya vratasya kā ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 670. Now, what [are the contemplations] of the second vow? To this it is said —

children.text: krodhalobhabhīrutvahāsyapratyākhyānāny anuvīcībhāṣaṇaṃ ca pañca ||
children.translated_text: Renunciation of anger (<s>krodha</s>), greed (<s>lobha</s>), cowardice (<s>bhīrutva</s>), and levity (<s>hāsya</s>); and considered speech (<s>anuvīcī-bhāṣaṇa</s>) — these are the five.

children.text: § 671. krodhapratyākhyānaṃ lobhapratyākhyānaṃ bhīrutvapratyākhyānaṃ hāsyapratyākhyānam anivīcībhāṣaṇaṃ cety etāḥ pañca bhāvanā satyavratasya jñeyāḥ. anuvīcībhāṣaṇaṃ niravadyānubhāṣaṇam ity arthaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 671. Renunciation of anger, renunciation of greed, renunciation of cowardice, renunciation of levity, and considered speech — these five contemplations of the truthfulness vow should be known. 'Considered speech' (<s>anuvīcī-bhāṣaṇa</s>) means faultless deliberate speech.

children.text: § 672. idānīṃ tṛtīyasya vratasya kā bhāvanā ity atrāha —
children.translated_text: § 672. Now, what is the contemplation of the third vow? To this he says —

children.text: śūnyāgāravimocitāvāsaparoparodhākaraṇabhaikṣaśuddhisadharmāvisaṃvādāḥ pañca ||
children.translated_text: Dwelling in empty places (<s>śūnyāgāra</s>), dwelling in vacated abodes (<s>vimocitāvāsa</s>), not causing hindrance to others (<s>paroparodhākaraṇa</s>), purity in begging (<s>bhaikṣa-śuddhi</s>), and non-deception among co-religionists (<s>sadharma-avisaṃvāda</s>) — these are the five.

children.text: § 673. śūnyāgāreṣu giriguhātarukoṭarādiṣv āvāsaḥ. parakīyeṣu ca vimociteṣv āvāsaḥ. pareṣām uparodhākaraṇam. ācāraśāstramārgeṇa bhaikṣaśuddhiḥ. mamedaṃ tavedam iti sadharmabhir avisaṃvādaḥ. ity etāḥ pañcādattādānaviramaṇavratasya bhāvanāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 673. Dwelling in empty places such as mountain caves, tree-hollows, and the like. Dwelling in others' vacated abodes. Not causing hindrance to others. Purity in begging following the path of the code of conduct. Non-deception among co-religionists — 'this is mine, this is yours.' These are the five contemplations of the vow of abstention from taking what is not given.

children.text: § 674. athedānīṃ brahmacaryavratasya bhāvanā vaktavyā ity atrāha —
children.translated_text: § 674. Now the contemplations of the celibacy vow are to be stated — to this he says —

children.text: strīrāgakathāśravaṇatanmanoharāṅganirīkṣaṇapūrvaratānusmaraṇavṛṣyeṣṭarasasvaśarīrasaṃskāratyāgāḥ pañca ||
children.translated_text: Abandoning the hearing of stories of amorous attachment to women, gazing at their captivating limbs, recollection of former pleasures, aphrodisiac and desired foods, and adornment of one's own body — these are the five.

children.text: § 675. tyāgaśabdaḥ pratyekaṃ parisamāpyate. strīrāgakathāśravaṇatyāgaḥ tanmanoharāṅganirīkṣaṇatyāgaḥ pūrvaratānusmaraṇatyāgaḥ vṛṣyeṣṭarasatyāgaḥ svaśarīrasaṃskāratyāgaś ceti caturthavratasya bhāvanāḥ pañca vijñeyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 675. The word 'abandoning' (<s>tyāga</s>) is individually completed: abandoning the hearing of stories of amorous attachment to women; abandoning gazing at their captivating limbs; abandoning recollection of former pleasures; abandoning aphrodisiac and desired foods; and abandoning adornment of one's own body — these five contemplations of the fourth vow (celibacy) should be known.

children.text: § 676. atha pañcamavratasya bhāvanā kā ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 676. Now, what is the contemplation of the fifth vow? To this it is said —

children.text: manojñāmanojñendriyaviṣayarāgadveṣavarjanāni pañca ||
children.translated_text: Avoiding attachment and aversion toward pleasant and unpleasant sense-objects — these are the five.

children.text: § 677. pañcānām indriyāṇāṃ sparśanādīnām iṣṭāniṣṭeṣu viṣayeṣūpanipatiteṣu sparśādīṣu rāgavarjanāni pañca ākiṃcanyasya vratasya bhāvanāḥ pratyetavyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 677. When the objects of the five senses — touch and the rest — encounter pleasant and unpleasant sense-objects, the five [acts of] avoiding attachment should be understood as the contemplations of the non-possessiveness (<s>ākiñcanya</s>) vow.

children.text: § 678. kiṃcānyadyathāmīṣāṃ vratānāṃ draḍhimārthaṃ bhāvanāḥ pratīyante tadvipaścidbhir iti bhāvanopadeśaḥ, tathā tadarthaṃ tadvirodhiṣv apīty āha —
children.translated_text: § 678. Moreover, just as contemplations are understood for the strengthening of these vows — as recognized by the wise — so too [there are contemplations] regarding their opposites, for the same purpose — he says —

children.text: hiṃsādiṣv ihāmutrāpāyāvadyadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: Seeing the danger (<s>apāya</s>) and the blameworthiness (<s>avadya</s>) in violence and the like, in this world and the next.

children.text: § 679. abhyudayaniḥśreyasārthānāṃ kriyāṇāṃ vināśakaḥ prayogo ’pāyaḥ. avadyaṃ garhyam. apāyaś cāvadyaṃ cāpāyāvadye tayor darśanam apāyāvadyadarśanaṃ bhāvayitavyam. kva? ihāmutra ca. keṣu? hiṃsādiṣu. katham iti ced ucyate — hiṃsāyāṃ tāvat, hiṃsro hi nityodvejanīyaḥ satatānubaddhavairaś ca iha ca vadhabandhaparikleśādīn pratilabhate pretya cāśubhāṃ gatiṃ garhitaś ca bhavatīti hiṃsāyā vyuparamaḥ śreyān. tāthā anṛtavādī aśraddheyo bhavati ihaiva ca jihvācchedādīn pratilabhate mithyābhyākhānaduḥkhitebhyaś ca baddhavairebhyo bahūni vyasanāny avāpnoti pretya cāśubhāṃ gatiṃ garhitaś ca bhavatīti anṛtavacanād uparamaḥ śreyān. tathā stenaḥ paradravyāharaṇāsaktaḥ sarvasyodvejanīyo bhavati. ihaiva cābhighātavadhabandhahastapādakarṇanāsottarauṣṭhachedanabhedanasarvasvaharaṇādīn pratilabhate pretya cāśubhāṃ gatiṃ garhitaś ca bhavatīti steyād vyuparatiḥ śreyasī. tathā abrahmacarī madavibhramodbhrāntacitto vanagaja iva vāsitāvañcito vivaśo vadhabandhanaparikleśān anubhavati mohābhibhūtatvāc ca kāryākāryānabhijño na kiṃcit kuśalam ācarati parāṅganāliṅganasaṅgakṛtaratiś cehaiva vairānubandhano liṃgacchedanavadhabandhasarvasvaharaṇādīn apāyān prāpnoti pretya cāśubhāṃ gatim aśnute garhitaś ca bhavati ato viratir ātmahitā. tathā parigrahavān śakunir iva gṛhītamāṃsakhaṇḍo ’nyeṣāṃ tadarthināṃ patattriṇām ihaiva taskarādīnām abhibhavanīyo bhavati tadarjanarakṣaṇaprakṣayakṛtāṃś ca doṣān bahūn avāpnoti na cāsya tṛptir bhavati indhanair ivāgneḥ lobhābhibhūtatvāc ca kāryākāryānapekṣo bhavati pretya cāśubhāṃ gatim āskandate lubhdo ’yam iti garhitaś ca bhavatīti tadviramaṇaṃ śreyaḥ. evaṃ hiṃsādiṣv apāyāvadyadarśanaṃ bhāvanīyam.
children.translated_text: § 679. <s>Apāya</s> (danger) is an action that destroys [the means to] worldly prosperity and spiritual liberation. <s>Avadya</s> (blameworthiness) is that which is censurable. Both danger and blameworthiness — seeing them — should be contemplated. Where? In this world and the next. In what? In violence and the like. How? It is said: First, regarding violence — one who commits violence is always a source of fear, constantly beset by enmity; here [in this world] he receives killing, imprisonment, torment, and the like; hereafter he goes to an inauspicious destiny; and he is censured. Therefore, desisting from violence is better. Likewise, a speaker of falsehood becomes untrustworthy; here he receives cutting of the tongue and the like; from those aggrieved by false accusations, with whom enmity is formed, he incurs many calamities; hereafter he goes to an inauspicious destiny and is censured. Therefore, desisting from falsehood is better. Likewise, a thief, intent on stealing others' property, becomes a source of fear to all; here he receives assault, killing, imprisonment, cutting of hands, feet, ears, nose, and upper lip, confiscation of all property, and the like; hereafter he goes to an inauspicious destiny and is censured. Therefore, desisting from theft is better. Likewise, one who is unchaste, his mind agitated and bewildered by intoxication — like a forest elephant deceived by a she-elephant — helplessly experiences killing, imprisonment, and torment; and because he is overcome by delusion, he is unable to know what should and should not be done, and does nothing wholesome; through attachment to embracing others' wives, he here incurs enmity, mutilation, killing, imprisonment, confiscation of property, and other dangers; hereafter he attains an inauspicious destiny and is censured. Therefore, abstention is beneficial. Likewise, one who is possessive — like a bird that has seized a piece of meat — is here subject to being overpowered by thieves and others who desire the same; from acquiring, protecting, and losing [possessions], he incurs many faults; and there is no satisfaction for him — like fire [fed] by fuel; and because he is overcome by greed, he is heedless of what should and should not be done; hereafter he falls into an inauspicious destiny; and being [called] greedy, he is censured. Therefore, desisting from [possessiveness] is better. Thus, the contemplation of danger and blameworthiness in violence and the like should be cultivated.

children.text: § 680. hiṃsādiṣu bhāvanāntarapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 680. To establish another contemplation regarding violence and the like, he says —

children.text: duḥkham eva vā ||
children.translated_text: [They are] nothing but suffering.

children.text: § 681. hiṃsādayo duḥkham eveti bhāvayitavyāḥ. kathaṃ hiṃsādayo duḥkham? duḥkhakāraṇatvāt. yathā
annaṃ vai prāṇāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Food indeed is life-breath (<s>prāṇa</s>).'

children.text: iti. kāraṇasya kāranatvād vā. yathā
children.translated_text: Because the cause [is identified with] the effect. Just as:

children.text: dhanaṃ prāṇāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Wealth is life-breath.'

children.text: iti. dhanakāraṇam annapānakāraṇāḥ prāṇā iti. tathā hiṃsādayo ’sadvedyakarmakāraṇam. asadvedyakarma ca duḥkhakāraṇam iti duḥkhakāraṇe duḥkhakāraṇakāraṇe vā duḥkhopacāraḥ. tadete duḥkham eveti bhāvanaṃ parātmasākṣikam avagantavyam. nanu ca tatsarvaṃ na duḥkham eva; viṣayaratisukhasadbhāvāt? na tatsukham; vedanāpratīkāratvāt kacchūkaṇḍūyanavat.
children.translated_text: Wealth is the cause of food; food is the cause of life-breaths. Similarly, violence and the like are the cause of <s>asadvedya-karma</s> (pain-producing karma); and <s>asadvedya-karma</s> is the cause of suffering — thus the figurative usage of 'suffering' [applies to] the cause of suffering or the cause of the cause of suffering. This contemplation — 'these are nothing but suffering' — should be understood with both others and oneself as witness. [Objection:] But all that is not solely suffering, since the pleasure of sense-enjoyment exists? [Reply:] That is not [true] pleasure, since it does not cure [the underlying] feeling — like scratching an itch.
§ 681. Violence and the like should be contemplated as nothing but suffering. How are violence and the like suffering? Because they are causes of suffering. Just as [it is said]:

children.text: § 682. punar api bhāvanāntaram āha —
children.translated_text: § 682. He states yet another contemplation —

children.text: maitrīpramodakāruṇyamādhyasthyāni ca sattvaguṇādhikakliśyamānāvineyeṣu ||
children.translated_text: [One should cultivate] friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>), gladness (<s>pramoda</s>), compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>), and equanimity (<s>mādhyasthya</s>) toward beings, the virtuous, the suffering, and the wayward, respectively.

children.text: § 683. pareṣāṃ duḥkhānutpattyabhilāṣo maitrī. vadanaprasādādibhir abhivyajyamānāntarbhavitarāgaḥ pramodaḥ. dīnānugrahabhāvaḥ kāruṇyam. rāgadveṣapūrvakapakṣapātābhāvo mādhyasthyam. duṣkarmavipākavaśān nānāyoniṣu sīdantīti sattvā jīvāḥ. samyagjñānādibhiḥ prakṛṣṭā guṇādhikāḥ. asadvedyodayāpāditakleśāḥ kliśyamānāḥ. tattvārthaśravaṇagrahaṇābhyām asaṃpāditaguṇā avineyāḥ. eteṣu sattvādiṣu yathāsaṃkhyaṃ maitryādīni bhāvayitavyāni. sarvasattveṣu maitrī, guṇādikeṣu pramodaḥ, kliśyamāneṣu kāruṇyam, avineyeṣu mādhyasthyam iti. evaṃ bhāvayataḥ pūrṇāny ahiṃsādīni vratāni bhavanti.
children.translated_text: Section 683. The desire for the non-arising of suffering in others is <s>maitrī</s> (friendliness). Joy (<s>pramoda</s>) is the inner affection manifested through a cheerful countenance and the like. The disposition of compassion toward the afflicted is <s>kāruṇya</s> (compassion). The absence of partiality preceded by attachment or aversion is <s>mādhyasthya</s> (equanimity). Living beings (<s>sattvāḥ</s>) are souls (<s>jīvāḥ</s>) who suffer in various births due to the ripening of bad <s>karma</s>. Those who are distinguished by right knowledge and the like are the spiritually advanced (<s>guṇādhikāḥ</s>). Those afflicted by distress brought about by the rise of unwholesome <s>vedanīya</s> karma are the suffering ones (<s>kliśyamānāḥ</s>). Those who have not acquired virtues through hearing and grasping the meaning of reality are the unteachable (<s>avineyāḥ</s>). Toward these — beings and the rest — one should cultivate friendliness and the other [sentiments] in corresponding order: <s>maitrī</s> toward all beings, <s>pramoda</s> toward the spiritually advanced, <s>kāruṇya</s> toward the suffering, and <s>mādhyasthya</s> toward the unteachable. By cultivating thus, the vows of <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence) and the rest become complete.

children.text: § 684. punar api bhāvanāntaram āha —
children.translated_text: Section 684. He states yet another meditation —

children.text: jagatkāyasvabhāvau vā saṃvegavairāgyārtham ||
children.translated_text: Or [one should contemplate] the nature of the world and the body, for the sake of <s>saṃvega</s> (spiritual urgency) and <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion). ||

children.text: § 685. jagatsvabhāvas tāvad anādir anidhano vetrāsanajhallarīmṛdaṃganibhaḥ. atra jīvā anādisaṃsāre ’nantakālaṃ nānāyoniṣu duḥkhaṃ bhojaṃ bhojaṃ paryaṭanti. na cātra kiṃcin niyatam asti. jalabudbudopamaṃ jīvitam, vidyunmeghādivikāracapalā bhogasaṃpada iti. evam ādi jagatsvabhāvacintanāt saṃsārāt saṃvego bhavati. kāyasvabhāvaś ca anityatā duḥkhahetutva niḥsāratā aśucitvam iti.
evam ādi kāyasvabhāvacintanād viṣayarāganivṛtter vairāgyam upajāyate. iti jagatkāyasvabhāvau bhāvayitavyau.
children.translated_text: Thus, from contemplating the nature of the body, <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) arises through the cessation of attachment to sense objects. Therefore, one should meditate on the nature of the world and the body.

Section 685. The nature of the world, to begin with, is beginningless and endless, like the oscillation of a cane seat, a swing, or a drum. Here, souls wander for infinite time in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, experiencing suffering again and again in various births. And nothing here is fixed — life is like a water bubble; the wealth of enjoyments is as fleeting as the transformations of lightning and clouds. Thus, from contemplating the nature of the world, <s>saṃvega</s> (spiritual urgency) toward <s>saṃsāra</s> arises. And the nature of the body is impermanence, being a cause of suffering, essencelessness, and impurity.

children.text: § 686. atrāha; uktaṃ bhavatā hiṃsādinivṛttivratam iti, tatra na jānīmaḥ ke hiṃsādayaḥ kriyāviśeṣā ity atrocyate. yugapad vaktum aśakyatvāt tallakṣaṇanirdeśasya kramaprasaṃge yāsāv ādau coditā saiva tāvad ucyate —
children.translated_text: Section 686. Here one objects: you have stated the vow of abstaining from <s>hiṃsā</s> (violence) and the rest; but we do not know what specific actions constitute <s>hiṃsā</s> and the rest. To this it is replied: since their definitions cannot be stated all at once, and since a sequential exposition is appropriate, that which was enjoined first is stated first —

children.text: pramattayogāt prāṇavyaparopaṇaṃ hiṃsā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hiṃsā</s> (violence) is the destruction of <s>prāṇas</s> (vitalities) through the activity of one who is <s>pramatta</s> (negligent). ||

children.text: § 687. pramādaḥ sakaṣāyatvaṃ tadvānātmapariṇāmaḥ pramattaḥ. pramattasya yogaḥ pramattayogaḥ, tasmāt pramattayogāt indriyādayo daśaprāṇās teṣāṃ yathāsaṃbhavaṃ vyaparopaṇaṃ viyogakaraṇaṃ hiṃsety abhidhīyate. sā prāṇino duḥkhahetutvād adharmahetuḥ. ‘pramattayogāt’ iti viśeṣaṇaṃ kevalaṃ prāṇavyaparopaṇaṃ nādharmāyeti jñāpanārtham. uktaṃ ca —
viyojayati cāśubhir na ca vadhena saṃyujyate ||
children.translated_text: One who separates [vitalities] through unwholesome [dispositions] is not thereby conjoined with [the sin of] killing. ||

children.text:
iti ||
	  uktaṃ ca —
children.translated_text: Thus. || And it has been said —

children.text: uccālidamhi pāde iriyāsamidassa ṇiggamaṭṭhāṇe |
children.translated_text: When a foot has been raised, at the point of stepping forward in the <s>īryāsamiti</s> (careful walking),

children.text: āvāde [dhe] jja kuliṃgo marejja tajjogamāsejja ||
children.translated_text: If a mongoose should die at the spot where one steps, one would be connected with that [death] by <s>yoga</s> (activity). ||

children.text: ṇa hi tassa taṇṇimitto baṃdho suhumo vi desido samae |
children.translated_text: But for him, no bondage, even subtle, caused by that, has been taught by the <s>Jina</s>;

children.text: mucchāpariggaho tti ya ajjhappapamāṇado bhaṇido ||
children.translated_text: Because attachment-possession (<s>mūrcchāparigraha</s>) has been stated as the measure of one's own [sin]. ||

children.text: nanu ca prāṇavyaparopaṇābhāve ’pi pramattayogamātrād eva hiṃseṣyate. uktaṃ ca —
children.translated_text: But surely, even in the absence of destruction of vitalities, one would commit <s>hiṃsā</s> merely through the activity of negligence (<s>pramattayoga</s>). And it has been said —

children.text: maradu va jiyadu va jīvo ayadācārassa ṇicchidā hiṃsā |
children.translated_text: Whether a living being dies or lives, for one of non-righteous conduct, <s>hiṃsā</s> is certain;

children.text: payadassa ṇatthi baṃdho hiṃsāmitteṇa samidassa ||
children.translated_text: For one of righteous conduct who is careful (<s>samita</s>), there is no bondage even through the instrumentality of <s>hiṃsā</s>. ||

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ. atrāpi prāṇavyaparopaṇam asti bhāvalakṣaṇam. tathā coktam —
children.translated_text: This is not a fault. Here too there is destruction of vitalities, of the nature of [inner] disposition (<s>bhāvalakṣaṇa</s>). And thus it has been said —

children.text: svayam evātmanātmānaṃ hinasty ātmā pramādavān |
children.translated_text: The negligent soul harms itself, by itself, through its own [negligence];

children.text: pūrvaṃ prāṇyantarāṇāṃ tu paścāt syād vā na vā vadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The killing of other living beings may or may not follow afterward. ||

Section 687. <s>Pramāda</s> (negligence) is the state of having passions (<s>kaṣāyas</s>); one whose psychic disposition is characterized by that is called <s>pramatta</s> (negligent). The activity of the negligent one is <s>pramattayoga</s>; from that <s>pramattayoga</s>, the ten <s>prāṇas</s> (vitalities) — namely the senses and the rest — their severance (<s>vyaparopaṇa</s>), that is, causing separation, is called <s>hiṃsā</s>. Since it causes suffering to living beings, it is a cause of <s>adharma</s> (demerit). The qualifier 'through the activity of one who is negligent' is to indicate that mere destruction of vitalities does not [necessarily] constitute <s>adharma</s>. And it has been said —

children.text: § 688. āha abhihitalakṣaṇā hiṃsā. tadanantaroddiṣṭam anṛtaṃ kiṃ lakṣaṇam ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: Section 688. One says: <s>hiṃsā</s> has been defined. What is the definition of <s>anṛta</s> (falsehood), which was mentioned next? To this it is replied —

children.text: asadabhidhānam anṛtam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Anṛta</s> (falsehood) is the statement of what is not good (<s>asat</s>). ||

children.text: § 689. sacchandaḥ praśaṃsāvācī. sadasadapraśastam iti yāvat. asato ’rthasyābhidhānam asadabhidānam anṛtam. ṛtaṃ satyaṃ, na ṛtam anṛtam. kiṃ punar apraśastam? prāṇipīḍākaraṃ yat tad apraśastaṃ vidyamānārthaviṣayaṃ vā avidyamānārthaviṣayaṃ vā. uktaṃ ca prāgevāhiṃsāvrataparipālanārtham itaradvratam iti. tasmād dhiṃsākaraṃ vaco ’nṛtam iti niśceyam.
children.translated_text: Section 689. The word 'sat' has the laudatory sense. 'Asat' means that which is not praiseworthy. The statement (<s>abhidhāna</s>) of what is untrue (<s>asat</s>) is <s>asadabhidhāna</s>, which is <s>anṛta</s> (falsehood). <s>Ṛta</s> means truth; 'not <s>ṛta</s>' is <s>anṛta</s>. What then is 'not praiseworthy'? That which causes injury to living beings — that is unpraiseworthy, whether its object is existent or non-existent. And it has already been said that the other vows serve to protect the vow of <s>ahiṃsā</s>. Therefore, speech that causes <s>hiṃsā</s> should be determined as <s>anṛta</s>.

children.text: § 690. athānṛtānantaram uddiṣṭaṃ yat steyaṃ tasya kiṃ lakṣaṇam ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: Section 690. Now, what is the definition of <s>steya</s> (theft), which was mentioned after <s>anṛta</s>? To this he says —

children.text: adattādānaṃ steyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Steya</s> (theft) is taking what is not given (<s>adattādāna</s>). ||

children.text: § 691. ādānaṃ grahaṇam adattasyādānam adattādānaṃ steyam ity ucyate. yady evaṃ karmanokarmagrahaṇam api steyaṃ prāpnoti; anyenādattatvāt? naiṣa doṣaḥ, dānādāne yatra saṃbhavatas tatraiva steyavyavahāraḥ. kutaḥ. ‘adatta’ grahaṇasāmarthyāt. evam api bhikṣor grāmanagarādiṣu bhramaṇakāle rathyādvārādipraveśād adattādānaṃ prāpnoti? naiṣa doṣaḥ; sāmānyena muktatvāt. tathā hi — ayaṃ bhikṣuḥ pihitadvārādiṣu na praviśati amuktatvāt. athavā ‘pramattayogāt’ ity anuvartate. pramattayogād adattādānaṃ yat tat steyam ity ucyate. na ca rathyādi praviśataḥ pramattayogo ’sti. tenaitad uktaṃ bhavati, yatra saṃkleśapariṇāmena pravṛttis tatra steyaṃ bhavati bāhyvastuno grahaṇe cāgrahaṇe ca.
children.translated_text: Section 691. <s>Ādāna</s> means taking; taking of what is not given is <s>adattādāna</s>, which is called <s>steya</s> (theft). If so, even the taking of karmic and non-karmic matter would amount to theft, since it is not given by another? This is not a fault, for the term 'theft' applies only where the giving and taking [by persons] is possible. Why? Because of the force of the word 'not given' (<s>adatta</s>). Even so, when a monk wanders through villages and towns, would entering streets and doorways constitute taking what is not given? This is not a fault, because [those places] have been generally released [for public use]. For this monk does not enter closed doors and the like, since they have not been released. Alternatively, 'through the activity of one who is negligent' continues [from the earlier sūtra]. Taking what is not given through negligent activity — that is called <s>steya</s>. And there is no negligent activity for one entering streets and the like. By this it is stated that where there is activity proceeding from a disposition of moral defilement, there theft occurs, whether in taking or not taking external objects.

children.text: § 692. atha caturtham abrahma kiṃ lakṣaṇam ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: Section 692. Now, what is the definition of the fourth — <s>abrahma</s> (unchastity)? To this it is replied —

children.text: maithunām abrahma ||
children.translated_text: <s>Abrahma</s> (unchastity) is sexual intercourse (<s>maithuna</s>). ||

children.text: § 693. strīpuṃsayoś cāritramohodaye sati rāgapariṇāmāviṣṭayoḥ parasparasparśanaṃ prati icchā mithunam. mithunasya karma maithunam ity ucyate. na sarvaṃ karma. kutaḥ? loke śāstre ca tathā prasiddeḥ. loke tāvad āgopālādiprasiddhaṃ strīpuṃsayoḥ rāgapariṇāmanimittaṃ ceṣṭitaṃ maithunam iti. śāstre ’pi
aśvavṛṣabhayor maithuneccchāyām
children.translated_text: 'In the case of the desire for coupling of a horse and a bull' —

children.text: ity evam ādiṣu tad eva gṛhyate. api ca ‘pramattayogāt’ ity anuvartate tena strīpuṃsamithunaviṣayaṃ ratisukhārtaṃ ceṣṭitaṃ maithunam iti gṛhyate, na sarvam. ahiṃsādayo guṇā yasmin paripālyamāne bṛṃhanti vṛddhim upayānti tad brahma. na brahma abrahma iti. kiṃ tat? maithunam. tatra hiṃsādayo doṣāḥ puṣyanti. yasmān maithunasevanapravaṇaḥ sthāsnūṃś cariṣṇūn prāṇino hinasti mṛṣāvādam ācaṣṭe adattam ādatte acetanam itaraṃ ca parigṛahaṃ gṛhṇāti.
children.translated_text: in such [passages] the same meaning is taken. Moreover, 'through the activity of one who is negligent' continues [from before]; therefore, the activity between man and woman aimed at the pleasure of sexual enjoyment is what is taken as <s>maithuna</s>, not everything. <s>Brahma</s> is that in which, when observed, the virtues of <s>ahiṃsā</s> and the rest flourish and increase. What is not <s>brahma</s> is <s>abrahma</s>. What is that? <s>Maithuna</s> (sexual intercourse). For in that, faults such as <s>hiṃsā</s> and the rest proliferate. Since one who is inclined toward sexual indulgence injures stationary and mobile living beings, speaks falsehood, takes what is not given, and grasps possessions both sentient and insentient.

Section 693. When the delusion of conduct-deluding karma (<s>cāritramoha</s>) arises in a man and woman, and both are possessed by the disposition of passion (<s>rāgapariṇāma</s>), the mutual desire for each other's touch is <s>mithuna</s> (coupling). The action of coupling is called <s>maithuna</s>. Not every action [between them is meant]. Why? Because it is so established in common usage and in scripture. In common usage, <s>maithuna</s> is well-known — even among cowherds and others — as the activity between man and woman caused by the disposition of passion. In scripture too,

children.text: § 694. atha pañcamasya parigrahasya kiṃ lakṣaṇam ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: Section 694. Now, what is the definition of the fifth — <s>parigraha</s> (possessiveness)? To this he says —

children.text: mūrcchā parigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mūrcchā</s> (infatuation) is <s>parigraha</s> (possessiveness). ||

children.text: § 695. mūrcchety ucyate. kā mūrcchā? bahyānāṃ gomahiṣamaṇimuktāphalādīnāṃ cetanācetanānām ābyantarāṇāṃ ca rāgādīnām upadhīnām saṃrakṣaṇārjanasaṃskārādilakṣaṇāvyāvṛttir mūrcchā. nanu ca loke vātādiprakopaviśeṣasya mūrccheti prasiddhir asti tadgrahaṇaṃ kasmān na bhavati? satyam evam etat mūrcchir ayaṃ mohasāmānye vartate.
sāmānyacodanāś ca viśeṣeṣv avatiṣṭhante
children.translated_text: 'General injunctions apply to specific instances' —

children.text: ity ukte viśeṣe vyavasthitaḥ parigṛhyate; parigrahaprakaraṇāt. evam api bāhyasya parigrahatvaṃ na prāpnoti; ādhyātmikasya saṃgrahāt? satyam evam etat; pradhānatvād abhyantara eva saṃgṛhītaḥ. asaty api bāhye mamedam iti saṃkalpabān saparigraha eva bhavati.
children.translated_text: having been thus stated, the specific [meaning] is adopted in the context of <s>parigraha</s> (possessiveness). Even so, external possessiveness would not follow, since only the internal is included? True indeed; only the internal is included because of its primary nature. Even without external [possessions], one who has the thought 'this is mine' is indeed one who has <s>parigraha</s>.

children.text: atha bāhyaḥ parigraho na bhavaty eva, bhavati ca mūrcchākāraṇatvāt yadi mamedam iti saṃkalpaḥ parigrahaḥ; saṃjñānādy api parigrahaḥ prāpnoti, tad api hi mamedam iti saṃkalpyate rāgādipariṇāmavat? naiṣa doṣaḥ; ‘pramattayogāt’ ity anuvartate. tato jñānadarśanacāritravato ’pramattasya mohābhāvān na mūrcchāstīti niṣparigarahatvaṃ siddham. kiṃ ca teṣāṃ jñanādīnām aheyatvād ātmasvabhāvatvād aparigrahatvam. rāgādayaḥ punaḥ karmodayatantrā iti anātmasvabhāvatvād dheyāḥ. tatas teṣụ saṃkalpaḥ parigraha iti yujyate. tanmulāḥ sarve doṣāḥ. mamedam iti hi sati saṃkalpe saṃrakṣanādayaḥ saṃjāyante. tatra ca hiṃsāvaśyaṃ bhāvinī. tadartham anṛtaṃ jalpati. cauryaṃ vā ācarati. maithune ca karmaṇi prayatate. tatprabhavā narakādiṣu duḥkhaprakārāḥ.
children.translated_text: Now, if external <s>parigraha</s> does not exist at all — yet it does exist as a cause of <s>mūrcchā</s> (infatuation) — if the thought 'this is mine' is <s>parigraha</s>, then even consciousness and the like would be <s>parigraha</s>, since one also thinks 'this is mine' with respect to those, just as with the dispositions of attachment and the like? This is not a fault; 'through the activity of one who is negligent' continues [from before]. Therefore, since there is no delusion for the non-negligent one who possesses knowledge, perception, and conduct, there is no <s>mūrcchā</s>, and thus freedom from possessiveness is established. Moreover, because knowledge and the like are not to be abandoned and are the very nature of the self, they are not <s>parigraha</s>. But attachment and the like, being dependent on the rise of <s>karma</s>, are not the nature of the self and are therefore to be abandoned. Hence the thought [of possessiveness] regarding them is rightly called <s>parigraha</s>. All faults are rooted in that. For when the thought 'this is mine' exists, guarding and the like arise, and in that, <s>hiṃsā</s> inevitably follows. For that purpose one speaks falsehood, or commits theft, and strives in sexual activity. From that arise the varieties of suffering in hells and other [destinies].

Section 695. '<s>Mūrcchā</s>' is stated. What is <s>mūrcchā</s>? It is the unceasing [activity] characterized by the guarding, acquiring, refurbishing, and the like of external possessions — cows, buffaloes, gems, pearls, fruits, and the like, whether sentient or insentient — and of internal possessions (<s>upadhis</s>) such as attachment and the like. But surely, in common usage, <s>mūrcchā</s> is well-known as a particular aggravation of wind and the like [i.e., fainting] — why is that meaning not taken? True, but this root '<s>mūrcch</s>' operates in the general sense of delusion.

children.text: § 696. evam uktena prakāreṇa hiṃsādidoṣadarśino ’hiṃsādiguṇāhitacetasaḥ paramaprayatnasyā hiṃsādīni vratāni yasya santi saḥ —
children.translated_text: Section 696. Thus, one who sees the faults of <s>hiṃsā</s> and the rest in the manner described, whose mind is devoted to the virtues of <s>ahiṃsā</s> and the rest, and who possesses the vows of <s>ahiṃsā</s> and the rest through supreme effort — that person is —

children.text: niśśalyo vratī ||
children.translated_text: A person of vows (<s>vratī</s>) is one who is free from thorns (<s>niśśalya</s>). ||

children.text: § 697. śṛṇāti hinastīti śalyam. śarīrānupraveśi kāṇḍādipraharaṇaṃ śalyam iva śalyaṃ, yathā tat prāṇino bādhākaraṃ tathā śārīramānasabādhāhetutvāt karmodayavikāraḥ śalyam ity upacaryate. tat trividham — māyāśalyaṃ nidānaśalyaṃ mithyādarśanaśalyam iti. māyā nikṛtir vañcanā. nidānaṃ viṣayabhogākāṅkṣā. mithyādarśanam atatvaśraddhānam. etasmāt trividhāc chalyān niṣkrānto niśśalyo vratī ity ucyate. atra codyate — śalyābhāvān niḥśalyo vratābhisaṃbandhād vratī, na niśśalyatvād vratī bhavitum arhati. na hi devadatto daṇḍasaṃbandhāc chatrī bhavatīti. attrocyate — ubhayaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭasyeṣṭatvāt. na hiṃsādyuparatimātravratābhisaṃbandhād vratī bhavaty antareṇa śalyābhāvam. sati śalyāpagame vratasaṃbandhād vratī vivakṣito yathā bahukṣīraghṛto gomān iti vyapadiśyate. bahukṣīraghṛtābhāvāt satīṣv api goṣu na gomāṃs tathā saśalyatvāt satsv api vrateṣu na vratī. yas tu niḥśalyaḥ sa vratī.
children.translated_text: Section 697. That which pierces or injures is a thorn (<s>śalya</s>). A weapon such as an arrow or the like that penetrates the body is a thorn; similarly, the distortion arising from the fruition of <s>karma</s>, being a cause of physical and mental affliction, is figuratively called a thorn. It is threefold: the thorn of deceit (<s>māyāśalya</s>), the thorn of desire (<s>nidānaśalya</s>), and the thorn of wrong faith (<s>mithyādarśanaśalya</s>). <s>Māyā</s> is duplicity and deception. <s>Nidāna</s> is craving for the enjoyment of sense objects. <s>Mithyādarśana</s> is belief in what is not reality. One who has emerged from this threefold thorn is called a <s>niśśalya vratī</s> (a person of vows free from thorns). Here it is objected: he is <s>niśśalya</s> (thorn-free) because of the absence of thorns, and <s>vratī</s> (a person of vows) because of the connection with vows — he should not be called a <s>vratī</s> because of being thorn-free. For <s>Devadatta</s> is not called an umbrella-bearer because of his connection with a staff. To this it is replied: because both qualifications together are intended. One does not become a <s>vratī</s> merely through the connection with the vow of abstaining from <s>hiṃsā</s> and the like, without the absence of thorns. When there is freedom from thorns, one is designated a <s>vratī</s> through the connection with vows — just as one is called 'rich in cattle' when one has cows yielding abundant milk and ghee. Without abundant milk and ghee, even though one has cows, one is not [truly] 'rich in cattle.' Similarly, because of the presence of thorns, even though one has vows, one is not [truly] a <s>vratī</s>. But one who is free from thorns — that one is a <s>vratī</s>.

children.text: § 698. tasya bhedapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 698. In order to understand its classification, he says —

children.text: agāry anagāraś ca ||
children.translated_text: [The person of vows is] either a householder (<s>agārī</s>) or a homeless ascetic (<s>anagāra</s>). ||

children.text: § 699. pratiśrayārthibhiḥ aṃgyate iti agāraṃ veśma, tad vānagārī. na vidyate agāramasyety anagāraḥ. dvividho vratī agārī anagāraś ca. nanu cātra viparyayo ’pi prāpnoti śūnyāgāradevakulādyāvāsasya muner agāritvam anivṛttaviṣayatṛṣṇasya kutaścit kāraṇād gṛhaṃ vimucya vane vasato ’nagāratvaṃ ca prāpnotīti? naiṣa doṣaḥ; bhāvāgārasya vivakṣitatvāt. cāritramohodaye saty agārasaṃbandhaṃ pratyanivṛttaḥ pariṇāmo bhāvāgāram ity ucyate. sa yasyāsty asāv agārī vane vasann api. gṛhe vasann api tadabhāvād anagāra iti ca bhavati. nanu cāgāriṇo vratitvaṃ na prāpnoti; asakalavratatvāt? naiṣa doṣaḥ; naigamādinayāpekṣayā agāriṇo ’pi vratitvam upapadyate nagarāvāsavat. yathā gṛhe apavarake vā vasann api nagarāvāsa ity ucyeta tathā asakalavrato ’pi naigamasaṃgrahavyavahāranayāpekṣayā vratīti vyapadiśyate.
children.translated_text: Section 699. A dwelling (<s>agāra</s>) is a house desired by those seeking shelter; one who has that is an <s>agārī</s> (householder). One who does not have a dwelling is an <s>anagāra</s> (homeless one). The <s>vratī</s> (person of vows) is twofold: householder and homeless ascetic. But here, the reverse also might apply — a sage living in an empty house or temple would be a householder, while one who has not abandoned the thirst for sense objects but has left home for some reason and lives in the forest would be homeless? This is not a fault; because the 'dwelling' meant here is the psychic dwelling (<s>bhāvāgāra</s>). The psychic disposition that has not ceased with regard to the household connection when conduct-deluding <s>karma</s> (<s>cāritramoha</s>) has arisen is called the psychic dwelling (<s>bhāvāgāra</s>). One who has that is a householder, even while living in the forest. And one who lacks that is homeless, even while living in a house. But surely, the householder cannot be a <s>vratī</s>, since his vows are incomplete? This is not a fault; from the standpoint of the <s>naigama</s> and other viewpoints (<s>nayas</s>), the householder's status as a <s>vratī</s> is established, just like the designation 'city-dweller.' Just as one living in a house or a room is still called a 'city-dweller,' so too one with incomplete vows is designated a <s>vratī</s> from the standpoint of the <s>naigama</s> (collective) and <s>saṃgraha</s> (synthetic) viewpoints.

children.text: § 700. atrāha kiṃ hiṃsādīnām anyatam asmād yaḥ pratinivṛttaḥ sa khalv agārī vratī? naivam. kiṃ tarhi? paṃcatayyā api virater vaikalyena vivakṣita ity ucyate —
children.translated_text: Section 700. Here one asks: is one who has abstained from any one of <s>hiṃsā</s> and the rest a householder <s>vratī</s>? Not so. Then what? It is said that what is intended is an incomplete [observance] of all five abstentions —

children.text: aṇuvrato ’gārī ||
children.translated_text: A householder (<s>agārī</s>) is one who has minor vows (<s>aṇuvrata</s>). ||

children.text: § 701. ‘aṇu’ śabdo ’lpavacanaḥ. aṇūni vratāny asya aṇuvrato ’gārīty ucyate. katham asya vratānām aṇuvratam? sarvasāvadyanivṛttyasaṃbhavāt. kutas tarhy asau nivṛttaḥ? trasaprāṇivyaparopaṇān nivrattaḥ agārīty ādyam aṇuvratam. snehamohādivaśād gṛhavināśe grāmavināśe vā kāraṇam ity abhimatād asatyavacanān nivṛtto gṛhīti dvitīyam aṇuvratam. anyapīḍākaraṃ pārthivabhayādivaśād avaśyaṃ parityaktam api yadadattaṃ tataḥ pratinivṛttādaraḥ śrāvaka iti tṛtīyam aṇuvratam. upāttāyā anupāttāyāś ca paraṃganāyāḥ saṃgān nivṛttaratir gṛhīti caturtham aṇuvratam. dhanadhānyakṣetrādīnām icchāvaśāt kṛtaparicchedo gṛhīti paṃcamam aṇuvratam.
children.translated_text: § 701. The word '<s>aṇu</s>' means 'small.' One whose vows (<s>vrata</s>) are small is called '<s>aṇuvrata</s>' (possessing minor vows) — a householder (<s>agārin</s>). How are his vows 'minor'? Because complete abstention from all sinful activity is impossible [for a householder]. From what, then, has he abstained? Abstention from killing mobile living beings (<s>trasa-prāṇi-vyaparopaṇa</s>) — this is the first minor vow of the householder. Abstention from speaking falsehood motivated by affection, delusion, and the like, which would cause the destruction of a household or a village — this is the second minor vow of the householder. Respectful abstention from [taking] what is not given (<s>adatta</s>), even when it has necessarily been abandoned [by its owner] under duress such as fear of the king, which would cause harm to others — this is the third minor vow of the householder. Abstention from the pleasure of association with another's wife, whether approached or not approached — this is the fourth minor vow of the householder. Having voluntarily set a limit on wealth, grain, land, and the like — this is the fifth minor vow of the householder.

children.text: § 702 āha aparityaktāgārasya kim etāvān eva viśeṣa āhosvid asti kaścid anyo ’pīty ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 702. He asks: does the householder who has not renounced the household have only this much distinction, or is there something more? — to this he says —

children.text: digdeśānarthadaṇḍaviratisāmāyikaproṣadhopavāsopabhogaparibhogaparimāṇātithisaṃvibhāgavratasaṃpannaś ca ||
children.translated_text: And [the householder] is endowed with the vows of directional limitation (<s>dig-virati</s>), spatial limitation (<s>deśa-virati</s>), abstention from purposeless harm (<s>anarthadaṇḍa-virati</s>), periodic concentration (<s>sāmāyika</s>), fasting on sacred days (<s>proṣadhopavāsa</s>), limitation of consumables and non-consumables (<s>upabhoga-paribhoga-parimāṇa</s>), and sharing with guests (<s>atithi-saṃvibhāga</s>). ||

children.text: § 703. ‘virati’ śabdaḥ pratyekaṃ parisamāpyate. digviratiḥ deśaviratiḥ anarthadaṇḍaviratir iti etāni trīṇi guṇavratāni; ‘vrata’ śabdasya pratyekam abhisaṃbandhāt. tathā sāmāyikavrataṃ proṣadhopavāsavrataṃ upabhogaparibhogaparimāṇavrataṃ atithisaṃvibhāgavrataṃ etāni catvāri śikṣāvratāni. etair vrataiḥ saṃpanno gṛhī viratāvirata ity ucyate. tad yathā — dikprācyādiḥ tatra prasiddhair abhijñānair avadhiṃ kṛtvā niyamanaṃ digvirativratam. tato bahis trasasthāvaravyaparopaṇanivṛtter mahāvratatvam avaseyam. tatra lābhe saty api pariṇāmasya nivṛtter lobhanirāsaś ca kṛto bhavati. grāmādīnām avadhṛtaparimāṇaḥ pradeśo deśaḥ. tato bahir nivṛttir deśavirativratam. pūrvavad bahir mahāvratatvaṃ vyavasthāpyam. asaty upakāre pāpādānahetur anarthadaṇḍaḥ. tato viratir anarthadaṇḍaviratiḥ. anarthadaṇḍaḥ paṃcavidhaḥ — apadhyānaṃ pāpopadeśaḥ pramādācaritaṃ hiṃsāpradānaṃ aśubhaśrutir iti. tatra pareṣāṃ jayaparājayavadhabandhanāṅgacchedaparasvaharaṇādi kathaṃ syād iti manasā cintanam apadhyānam. tiryakkleśavāṇijyaprāṇivadhakārambhādiṣu pāpasaṃyuktaṃ vacanaṃ pāpopadeśaḥ. prayojanam antareṇa vṛkṣādichedanabhūmikuṭṭanasalilasecanādyavadhyakarma pramādācaritam. viṣayakaṇṭakaśāstrāgnirajjukaśādaṇḍādihiṃsopakaraṇapradānaṃ hiṃsāpradānam. hiṃsārāgādipravardhanaduṣṭakathāśravaṇaśikṣaṇavyāpṛtir aśubhaśrutiḥ. samekībhāve vartate. tadyathā saṃgataṃ ghṛtaṃ saṃgataṃ tailām ity ucyate ekībhūtam iti gamyate. ekatvena ayanaṃ gamanaṃ samayaḥ, samaya eva sāmāyikaṃ, samayaḥ prayojanam asyeti vā vigṛhya sāmāyikam. iyati deśe etāvati kāle ity avadhārite sāmāyike sthitasya mahāvratatvaṃ pūrvavad veditavyam. kutaḥ? aṇusthūlakṛtahiṃsādinivṛtteḥ. saṃyamaprasaṃga iti cet? na; tadghātikarmodayasadbhāvāt. mahāvratatvābhāva iti cet? tan na; upacārād rājakule sarvagatacaitrābhidhānavat. proṣadhaśabdaḥ parvaparyāyavācī. śabdādigrahaṇaṃ prati nivṛttautsukyāni paṃcānīṇdriyāṇy upetya tasmin vasantīty upavāsaḥ. caturvidhāhāraparityāga ity arthaḥ. proṣadhe upavāsaḥ proṣadhopavāsaḥ. svaśarīrasaṃskārakāraṇasnānagandhamālyābharaṇādivirahitaḥ śucāv avakāśe sādhunivāse caityālaye svaproṣadhopavāsagṛhe vā dharmakathāśravaṇaśrāvaṇacintanavihitāntaḥkaraṇaḥ sann upavasen nirārambhaḥ śrāvakaḥ. upabhogo ’śanapānagandhamālyādiḥ. paribhoga ācchādanaprāvaraṇālaṃkāraśayanāsanagṛhayānavāhanādiḥ tayoḥ parimāṇam upabhogaparibhogaparimāṇam. madhu māṃsaṃ madyaṃ ca sadā parihartavyaṃ trasaghātān nivṛttacetasā. ketakyarjunapuṣpādīni śṛṅgaveramūlakādīni bahujantuyonisthānāny anantakāyavyapadeśārhāṇi parihartavyāni bahughātālpaphalatvāt. yānavāhanābharaṇādiṣv etāvad eveṣṭam ato ’nyad aniṣṭam ity aniṣṭān nivartanaṃ kartavyaṃ kālaniyamena yāvaj jīvaṃ vā yathā śakti. saṃyamam avināśayann atatīty atithiḥ. athavā nāsya tithir astīty atithiḥ aniyatakālāgamana ity arthaḥ. atithaye saṃvibhāgo ’tithisaṃvibhāgaḥ. sa caturvidhaḥ; bhikṣopakaraṇauṣadhapratiśrayabhedāt. mokṣārtham abhyudyatāyātithaye saṃyamaparāyaṇāya śuddhāya śuddhacetasā niravadyā bhikṣā deyā. dharmopakaraṇāni ca samyagdarśanādyupabṛṃhaṇāni dātavyāni. auṣadham api yogyam upayojanīyam. pratiśrayayaś ca paramadharmaśraddhayā pratipādayitavya iti. ‘ca’ śabdo vakṣyamāṇagṛhasthadharmasamuccayārthaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 703. The word '<s>virati</s>' (abstention) is to be applied individually: directional abstention (<s>dig-virati</s>), spatial abstention (<s>deśa-virati</s>), and abstention from purposeless harm (<s>anarthadaṇḍa-virati</s>) — these are the three supplementary vows (<s>guṇa-vrata</s>), since the word '<s>vrata</s>' is connected with each individually. Similarly, the vow of periodic concentration (<s>sāmāyika-vrata</s>), the vow of fasting on sacred days (<s>proṣadhopavāsa-vrata</s>), the vow of limiting consumables and non-consumables (<s>upabhoga-paribhoga-parimāṇa-vrata</s>), and the vow of sharing with guests (<s>atithi-saṃvibhāga-vrata</s>) — these are the four disciplinary vows (<s>śikṣā-vrata</s>). A householder endowed with these vows is called 'partially restrained and partially unrestrained' (<s>viratāvirata</s>). Namely: the direction (<s>dik</s>) is the east and the like; having established boundaries by well-known landmarks therein, the [self-imposed] restriction is the vow of directional limitation (<s>dig-virati-vrata</s>). Beyond that, the abstention from killing mobile and immobile beings should be understood as equivalent to a great vow (<s>mahāvrata</s>). Thereby, even when gain is available [beyond the boundary], there is abstention of disposition, and the rejection of greed is accomplished. A specific area (<s>deśa</s>), such as a village and the like, whose extent has been determined, [constitutes the spatial limitation]; abstention from [activity] beyond that is the vow of spatial limitation (<s>deśa-virati-vrata</s>). As before, [the status of] great vow beyond [the limit] should be established. Purposeless harm (<s>anarthadaṇḍa</s>) is [activity] that causes sin without [any corresponding] benefit. Abstention from that is '<s>anarthadaṇḍa-virati</s>.' Purposeless harm is fivefold: evil contemplation (<s>apadhyāna</s>), instruction in sin (<s>pāpopadeśa</s>), heedless conduct (<s>pramādācarita</s>), giving instruments of violence (<s>hiṃsāpradāna</s>), and unwholesome listening (<s>aśubha-śruti</s>). Among these, mental deliberation such as 'how might defeat, victory, killing, imprisonment, mutilation, or seizure of another's property befall others' is evil contemplation (<s>apadhyāna</s>).

children.text: § 704. kaḥ punar asau —
children.translated_text: § 704. Now, who is that [householder]? —

children.text: māraṇāntikīṃ sallekhanāṃ joṣitā ||
children.translated_text: One who has accepted <s>sallekhanā</s> (ritual self-diminishment) unto death. ||

children.text: § 705. svapariṇāmopāttasyāyuṣa indriyāṇāṃ balānāṃ ca kāraṇavaśāt saṃkṣayo maraṇam. ‘anta’ grahaṇaṃ tadbhavamaraṇapratipattyartham. maraṇam anto maraṇāntaḥ. sa prayojanam asyeti māraṇāntikī. samyakkāyakaṣāyalekhanā sallekhanā. kāyasya bāhyasyābhyantarāṇāṃ ca kaṣāyāṇāṃ tatkāraṇahāpanakrameṇa samyaglekhanā sallekhanā. tām māraṇāntikīṃ sallekhanāṃ joṣihtā sevitā gṛhīty abhisaṃbadhyate. nanu ca vispaṣṭārthaṃ sevitety evaṃ vaktavyam? na; arthaviśeṣopapatteḥ. na kevalam iha sevanaṃ parigṛhyate. kiṃ tarhi? prītyartho ’pi. yasmād asatyāṃ prītau balān na salllekhanā kāryate. satyāṃ hi prītau svayam eva karoti. syān matam ātmavadhaḥ prāpnoti; svābhisandhipūrvakāyurādinivṛtteḥ? naiṣa doṣaḥ; apramattatvāt. ‘pramattayogāt prāṇavyaparopaṇaṃ hiṃsā’ ity uktam. na cāsya pramādayogo ’sti. kutaḥ. rāgādyabhāvāt. rāgadveṣamohāviṣṭasya hi viṣaśāstrādyupakaraṇaprayogavaśād ātmānaṃ ghnataḥ svaghāto bhavati. na sallekhanāṃ pratipannasya rāgādayaḥ santi tato nātmavadhadoṣaḥ. uktaṃ ca —

rāgādīṇam aṇuppā ahiṃsagattaṃ ti desidaṃ samaye |
	  tesiṃ ce uppattī hiṃseti jiṇehi ṇiddiṭṭhā ||
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] The non-arising of passions such as attachment and the like, and the state of non-violence — this has been taught in the scripture. But the arising of those [passions] has been declared by the <s>Jinas</s> to be violence.

children.text: kiṃ ca maraṇasayāniṣṭatvād yathā vaṇijo vividhapaṇyadānādānasaṃcayaparasya svagṛhavināśo ’niṣṭaḥ. tadvināśakāraṇe ca kutaścid upasthite yathāśakti pariharati. duṣparihāre ca paṇyavināśo yathā na bhavati tathā yatate. evaṃ gṛhastho ’pi vrataśīlapaṇyasaṃcaye pravartamānaḥ tadāśrayasya na pātam abhivāṃchati. tadupaplavakāraṇe copasthite svaguṇavirodhena pariharati. duṣparihāre ca yathā svaguṇavināso na bhavati tathā prayatata iti katham ātmavadho bhavet.
children.translated_text: Moreover, since death associated with it [sallekhanā] is not undesirable — just as for a merchant engaged in the collection of various goods through buying and selling, the destruction of his house is undesirable, and when a cause of its destruction presents itself from somewhere, he wards it off to the best of his ability, and when it is difficult to avert, he strives that at least the merchandise is not destroyed — similarly, even a householder engaged in accumulating the merchandise of vows and moral conduct does not desire the fall of the body which is their support.

§ 705. Death is the diminishment of the lifespan, sense organs, and powers acquired through one's own [karmic] disposition, due to [various] causes. The word '<s>anta</s>' (end) is for the purpose of indicating death within that very existence. Death is the end — '<s>maraṇānta</s>.' That which has it as its purpose is '<s>māraṇāntikī</s>' (unto death). Proper attenuating of the body and passions (<s>kāya-kaṣāya-lekhanā</s>) is <s>sallekhanā</s>. [It involves] the proper attenuating of the external body and the internal passions through the progressive relinquishment of their causes.

children.text: § 706. atrāha, ‘niḥśalyo vratī’ ity uktaṃ tatra ca tṛtīyaṃ śalyaṃ mithyādarśanam. tataḥ samyagdṛṣṭinā vratinā niḥśalyena bhavitavyam ity uktam. tatsamyagdarśanaṃ kiṃ sāpavādaṃ nirapavādam iti. ucyate — kasyacin mohanīyāvasthāviśeṣāt kadācid ime bhavaty apavādāḥ —
children.translated_text: § 706. Here one objects: it was said 'the one observing vows is free from thorns (<s>niḥśalya</s>),' and there the third thorn is wrong faith (<s>mithyādarśana</s>). Therefore, it has been stated that the observer of vows, possessing right faith, must be free from thorns. Is that right faith (<s>samyag-darśana</s>) with transgression (<s>sāpavāda</s>) or without transgression (<s>nirapavāda</s>)? It is said: due to particular states of deluding [karma], in some cases, at some times, these transgressions occur —

children.text: śaṅkākāṅkṣāvicikitsā ’nyadṛṣṭipraśaṃsāsaṃstavāḥ samyagdṛṣṭer aticārāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Doubt (<s>śaṅkā</s>), desire [for worldly pleasures] (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>), aversion [to ascetic practices] (<s>vicikitsā</s>), praising other [false] doctrines (<s>anyadṛṣṭi-praśaṃsā</s>), and extolling [those of wrong faith] (<s>saṃstava</s>) are the transgressions of one of right faith (<s>samyag-dṛṣṭi</s>). ||

children.text: § 707. niḥśaṃkitatvādayo vyākhyātāḥ ‘darśanaviśuddhiḥ’ ity atra. tatpratipakṣabhūtāḥ śaṃkādayo veditavyāḥ. atha praśaṃsāsaṃstavayoḥ ko viśeṣaḥ? manasā mityādṛṣṭer jñānacāritraguṇodbhāvanaṃ praśaṃsā, bhūtābhūtaguṇodbhāvavacanaṃ saṃstava ity ayam anayor bhedaḥ. nanu ca samyagdarśanam aṣṭāṅgam uktaṃ tasyāticārair apy aṣṭabhir bhavitavyam. naiṣa doṣaḥ; vrataśīleṣu paṃca paṃcāticārā ity uttaratra vivakṣuṇācāryeṇa praśaṃsāsaṃstavayor itarān aticārānantarbhāvya paṃcaivāticārā uktāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 707. Freedom from doubt and the rest have been explained under 'purity of faith' (<s>darśana-viśuddhi</s>). Their opposites — doubt and the rest — should be understood [as the transgressions]. Now, what is the distinction between 'praising' (<s>praśaṃsā</s>) and 'extolling' (<s>saṃstava</s>)? Mentally attributing qualities of knowledge and conduct to one of wrong faith is 'praising.' Verbally proclaiming existent or non-existent virtues [of those of wrong faith] is 'extolling' — this is the distinction between the two. [Objection:] But right faith was stated to have eight limbs.

children.text: § 708. āha, samyagdṛṣṭer aticārā uktāḥ. kim evaṃ vrataśīleṣv api bhavantīti? om ity uktvā tadaticārasaṃkhyānirdeśārtham āha
children.translated_text: § 708. He says: the transgressions of right faith have been stated. Do such [transgressions] also occur in vows and moral conduct? Yes — having replied thus, for the purpose of indicating the number of transgressions, he says —

children.text: vrataśīleṣu pañca pañca yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: In vows and moral conduct, [there are] five [transgressions] each, in order. ||

children.text: § 709. vratani ca śīlāni ca vrataśīlāni teṣu vrataśīleṣu. śīlagrahaṇam anarthakam; vratagrahaṇenaiva siddheḥ? nānarthakam; viśeṣajñāpanārthaṃ vratparirakṣaṇārthaṃ śīlām iti digviratyādīnīha ‘śīla’ grahaṇena gṛhyante.
children.translated_text: § 709. Vows and moral conduct [together form] 'vows-and-moral-conduct' (<s>vrata-śīla</s>); in those vows-and-moral-conduct. [Objection:] The mention of '<s>śīla</s>' (moral conduct) is purposeless, since everything is already accomplished by the mention of '<s>vrata</s>' (vow) alone. [Reply:] It is not purposeless; it is for the purpose of indicating a specific [category]. [The term] '<s>śīla</s>' is for the purpose of protecting the vows — by the mention of '<s>śīla</s>' here, [the supplementary vows such as] directional limitation and the rest are taken up.

children.text: § 710. agāryadhikārād agāriṇo vrataśīleṣu paṃca paṃcāticārā vakṣyamāṇā yathākramaṃ veditavyāḥ. tad yathā — ādyasya tāvad ahiṃsāvratasya —
children.translated_text: § 710. Since the topic is the householder, the five transgressions each of the householder's vows and moral conduct, which will be stated, should be understood in order. Namely: first, of the vow of non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā-vrata</s>) —

children.text: bandhavadhacchedātibhārāropaṇānnapānanirodhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Binding, beating, mutilation, overloading, and withholding food and drink. ||

children.text: § 711. abhimatadeśagatinirodhahetur bandhaḥ. danḍakaśāvetrādibhir abhighātaḥ prāṇiṇāṃ vadhaḥ, na prāṇavyaparopaṇam; tataḥ prāgevāsya vinivṛttatvāt. karṇanāsikādīnām avayavānām apanayanaṃ chedaḥ. nyāyyabhārād atiriktavāhanam atibhārāropaṇam. gavādīnāṃ kṣutpipāsābādhākaraṇam annapānanirodhaḥ. ete paṃcāhiṃsāṇuvratasyāticārāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 711. Binding (<s>bandha</s>) is the obstruction of movement to a desired place. Striking living beings with sticks, whips, canes, and the like is beating (<s>vadha</s>) — not the taking of life (<s>prāṇa-vyaparopaṇa</s>), since [the householder] has already abstained from that earlier. Removal of limbs such as ears, nose, and the like is mutilation (<s>cheda</s>). Imposing a load greater than what is proper is overloading (<s>atibhārāropaṇa</s>). Causing the suffering of hunger and thirst to cattle and the like is withholding food and drink (<s>annapāna-nirodha</s>). These are the five [transgressions of the vow of non-violence].

children.text: mithyopadeśarahobhyākhyānakūṭalekhakriyānyāsāpahārasākāramantrabhedāḥ ||
children.translated_text: False instruction (<s>mithyopadeśa</s>), revealing secrets (<s>rahobhyākhyāna</s>), forgery (<s>kūṭalekha-kriyā</s>), misappropriation of deposits (<s>nyāsāpahāra</s>), and breach of confidence (<s>sākāra-mantra-bheda</s>). ||

children.text: § 712. abhyudayaniḥśreyasārtheṣu kriyāviśeṣeṣu anyasyānyathā pravartanam atisaṃdhāpanaṃ vā mityopadeśaḥ. yat strīpuṃsābhyām ekānte ’nuṣṭhitasya kriyāviśeṣasya prakāśanaṃ tad rahobhyākhyānaṃ veditavyam. anyenānuktam ananuṣṭhitaṃ yat kiṃcit paraprayogavaśād evaṃ tenoktam anuṣṭhitam iti vaṃcanānimittaṃ lekhanaṃ kūṭalekhakriyā. hiraṇyāder dravyasya nikṣeptur vismṛtasaṃkhyālpasaṃkhyeyam ādadānasyaivam ity anujñāvacanaṃ nyāsāpahāraḥ. arthaprakaraṇāṅgavikārabhrūvikṣepādibhiḥ parākūtam upalabhya tadāviṣkaraṇam asūyādinimittaṃ yattatsākāramantrabheda iti kathyate. ta ete satyāṇuvratasya paṃcāticārā boddhavyāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 712. Instructing another falsely or deceiving [them] in specific practices concerning worldly prosperity and spiritual liberation is false instruction (<s>mithyopadeśa</s>). The disclosure of a specific act performed in private by a man and woman is what should be understood as revealing secrets (<s>rahobhyākhyāna</s>). Something not spoken by another and not done [by them] — [yet] saying through another's contrivance that 'it was spoken or done by that person' for the purpose of deception — is

children.text: stenaprayogatadāhṛtādānaviruddharājyātikramahīnādhikamānonmānapratirūpakavyavahārāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Employing a thief, accepting [goods] brought by such [a thief], acting against a hostile kingdom, short-weighing and over-measuring, and dealing in counterfeits. ||
