children.text: § 713. muṣṇantaṃ svayam eva vā prayuṅkte ’nyena vā prayojayati prayuktam anumanyate vā yataḥ sa stenaprayogaḥ. aprayuktenānumatena ca caureṇānītasya grahaṇaṃ tadāhṛtādānam. ucitanyāyād anyena prakāreṇa dānagrahaṇam atikramaḥ. viruddhaṃ rājyaṃ viruddharājyam viruddharājye ’tikramaḥ viruddharājyātikramaḥ. tatra hy alpamūlyalabhyāni mahārghyāṇi dravyāṇīti prayatnaḥ. prasthādi mānam, tulādyunmānam. etena nyūnenānyasmai deyam adhikenātmano grāhyam ity evam ādi kūṭaprayogo hīnādhikamānonmānam. kṛtrimair hiraṇyādibhir vañcanāpūrvako vyavahāraḥ pratirūpakavyavahāraḥ. ta ete pañcādattādānāṇuvratasyāticārāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 713. <s>Stenaprayoga</s> (employment of a thief) is when one personally engages in stealing, or causes another to steal, or approves of one who has been employed [to steal]. <s>Tadāhṛtādāna</s> (acceptance of stolen goods) is receiving what has been brought by a thief who was neither employed nor approved. <s>Atikrama</s> (transgression) is giving and receiving in a manner other than the proper method. <s>Viruddharājyātikrama</s> (transgression in a hostile kingdom) is [going to] a hostile kingdom where valuable goods can be obtained at low cost with effort. <s>Prastha</s> and the like are measures; balances and the like are weighing instruments. Using false measures and weights means: 'I should give less to another, and take more for myself'—this kind of fraudulent use is '<s>hīnādhika-mānonmāna</s>' (deficient and excessive measures and weights). <s>Pratirūpaka-vyavahāra</s> (counterfeit transactions) is commerce preceded by deception using counterfeit gold and the like. These are the five transgressions of the minor vow of non-stealing (<s>adattādāna-aṇuvrata</s>).

children.text: paravivāhakaraṇetvarikāparigṛhītāparigṛhītāgamanānaṅgakṛīḍākāmatīvrābhiniveśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Arranging another's marriage, visiting an unchaste woman, going to a married or unmarried [woman], non-genital play, and intense indulgence in lust [are the transgressions of the vow of contentment with one's spouse]. ||

children.text: § 714. kanyādānaṃ vivāhaḥ. parasya vivāhaḥ paravivāḥ. paravivāhasya karaṇaṃ paravivāhakaraṇam. parapuruṣāneti gacchatīity evaṃ śīlā itvarī. kutsitā itvarī kutsāyāṃ ka itvarikā. yā ekapuruṣabhartṛkā sā parigṛhītā. yā gaṇikātvena puṃścalītvena vā parapuruṣagamanaśīlā asvāmikā sā aparigṛhītā. parigṛhītā cāparigṛhītā ca parigṛhītāparigṛhīte. itvarike ca te parigṛhītāparigṛhīte ca itvarikāparigṛhītāparigṛhīte, tayor gamane itvarikāparigṛhītāparigṛhītāgamane. aṃga prajananaṃ yoniś ca, tato ’nyatra krīḍā anaṅgakrīḍā. kāmasya pravṛddhaḥ pariṇāmaḥ kāmatīvrābhiniveśaḥ. ta ete paṃca svadārasaṃtoṣavratasyāticārāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 714. The giving away of a maiden is marriage (<s>vivāha</s>). The marriage of another is '<s>paravivāha</s>.' The arranging of another's marriage is '<s>paravivāha-karaṇa</s>.' A woman who habitually goes to other men is called '<s>itvarī</s>' (an unchaste woman). A contemptible <s>itvarī</s> is '<s>itvarikā</s>' (a low unchaste woman). A woman who belongs to one man as her husband is '<s>parigṛhītā</s>' (married/claimed). A woman who, as a courtesan or as a loose woman, habitually goes to other men and has no owner is '<s>aparigṛhītā</s>' (unclaimed). Going to the <s>itvarikā</s> and to the married and unmarried [women]—these are '<s>itvarikā-parigṛhītā-aparigṛhītā-gamana</s>.' Play in [body parts] other than the genitals (<s>aṅga</s>) is '<s>anaṅga-krīḍā</s>' (non-genital play). The intensified disposition of lust is '<s>kāma-tīvrābhiniveśa</s>.' These are the five transgressions of the vow of contentment with one's own spouse (<s>svadāra-saṃtoṣa-vrata</s>).

children.text: kṣetravāstuhiraṇyasuvarṇadhanadhānyadāsīdāsakupyapramāṇātikramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Transgressions regarding the limits of fields, houses, silver, gold, wealth, grain, female and male servants, and other goods [are the transgressions of the vow of limiting possessions]. ||

children.text: § 715. kṣetraṃ sasyādhikaraṇam. vāstu agāram. hiraṇyaṃ rūpyādivyavahāratantram. suvarṇaṃ pratītam. dhanaṃ gavādi. dhānyaṃ vrīhyādi. dāsidāsaṃ bhṛtyastrīpuṃsavargaḥ. kupyaṃ kṣaumakārpāsakauśeyacandanādi. kṣetraṃ ca vāstu ca kṣetravāstu, hiraṇyaṃ ca suvarṇaṃ ca hiraṇyasuvarṇam, dhanaṃ ca dhānyaṃ ca dhanadhānyam, dāsī ca dāsaś ca dāsīdāsam. kṣetravāstu ca hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ ca dhanadhānyaṃ ca dāsīdāsaṃ ca kupyaṃ ca kṣetravāstuhiraṇyasuvarṇadhanadhānyadāsīdāsakupyāni. etāvān eva parigraho mama nānya iti paricchinnāṇupramāṇāt kṣetravāstvādiviṣayād atirekā atilobhavaśāt pramāṇātikramā iti pratyākhyāyante. ta ete parigrahaparimāṇavratasyāticārāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 715. <s>Kṣetra</s> (field) is the ground for crops. <s>Vāstu</s> (house) is a dwelling. <s>Hiraṇya</s> (silver) is the medium of commerce such as coined silver. <s>Suvarṇa</s> (gold) is well known. <s>Dhana</s> (wealth) is cattle and the like. <s>Dhānya</s> (grain) is rice and the like. Male and female servants—

children.text: § 716. uktā vratānām aticārāḥ śīlānām aticārā vakṣyante. tad yathā —
children.translated_text: § 716. The transgressions of the vows have been stated; the transgressions of the moral practices (<s>śīla</s>) will now be stated. They are as follows—

children.text: ūrdhvādhas tiryagvyatikramakṣetravṛddhismṛtyantarādhānāni ||
children.translated_text: Transgressing upward, downward, and sideways, extending the field, lapse of memory, and secreting [possessions]. ||

children.text: § 717. parimitasya digavadher atilaṃghanam atikramaḥ. sa samāsatas trividhhaḥ — ūrdhvātikramaḥ adho ’tikramas tiryagatikramaś ceti. tatra parvatādyārohaṇād ūrdhvātikramaḥ. kūpāvataraṇāder adho ’tikramaḥ. bilapraveśādes tiryagatikramaḥ. parigṛhītāyā diśo lobhāveśād ādhikyābhisandhiḥ kṣetravṛddhiḥ. sa eṣo ’tikramaḥ pramādān mohād vyāsaṃgād vā bhavatīty avaseyaḥ. ananusmaraṇaṃ smṛtyantarādhānam. ta ete digviramaṇasyāticārāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 717. Going beyond the prescribed limit of direction is transgression (<s>atikrama</s>). It is briefly of three kinds: upward transgression, downward transgression, and sideways transgression. Among these—

children.text: ānayanapreṣyaprayogaśabdarūpānupātapudgalakṣepāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Causing something to be brought, sending a messenger, employing signs, following sounds and forms, and throwing objects. ||

children.text: § 718. ātmanā saṃkalpite deśe sthitasya prayojanavaśād yatkiṃcid ānayety ājñāpanam ānayanam. evaṃ kurv iti niyogaḥ preṣyaprayogaḥ. vyāpārakarān puraṣān pratyabhyutkāsikādikaraṇaṃ śabdānupātaḥ.
svavigrahadarśanaṃ rūpānupātaḥ. loṣṭādinipātaḥ pudgalakṣepaḥ. ta ete deśaviramaṇasya pañcāticārāḥ.
children.translated_text: Seeing the shadow of one's own body [beyond the limit] is '<s>rūpānupāta</s>' (following a form). Throwing clods and the like is '<s>pudgala-kṣepa</s>' (throwing objects). These are the five transgressions of the [vow of] limited area of activity (<s>deśa-viramaṇa</s>).

§ 718. While remaining in a place determined by oneself, commanding 'bring something' due to some need is '<s>ānayana</s>' (causing to be brought). Directing 'do this'—that employment is '<s>preṣya-prayoga</s>' (sending a messenger).

children.text: kandarpakautkucyamaukharyāsamīkṣyādhikaraṇopabhogaparibhogānarthakyāni ||
children.translated_text: Lewdness, buffoonery, loquaciousness, unexamined excessive enjoyment and use, and purposelessness. ||

children.text: § 719. rāgodrekāt prahāsamiśro ’śiṣṭavākprayogaḥ kandarpaḥ. tadevobhayaṃ paratra duṣṭakāyakarmaprayuktaṃ kautkucyam. dhārṣṭyaprāyaṃ yatkiṃ vanānarthakaṃ bahupralāpitvaṃ maukharyam. asamīkṣya prayojanam ādhikyena karaṇam asamīkṣyādhikaraṇam. yāvatā ’rthenopabhogaparibhogau so ’rthas tato ’nyasyādhikyamānarthakyam. ta ete pañcānarthadaṇḍavirater aticārāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 719. <s>Kandarpa</s> (lewdness) is vulgar and improper speech mixed with laughter, arising from excess of passion. The same two [types of behavior], when involving evil bodily acts directed toward another, constitute <s>kautkucya</s> (buffoonery). Whatever is mainly characterized by boldness—

children.text: yogaduṣpraṇidhānānādarasmṛtyanupasthānāni ||
children.translated_text: Negligence in the threefold activity (<s>yoga</s>), inattention, and lapse of mindfulness. ||

children.text: § 720. yogo vyākhyātas trividhaḥ. tasya duṣṭaṃ praṇidhānaṃ yogaduṣpraṇidhānam — kāyaduṣpraṇidhānaṃ vāgduṣpraṇidhānaṃ manoduṣpraṇidhānam iti. anādaro ’nutsāhaḥ. anaikāgryaṃ smṛtyanupasthānam. ta ete pañca sāmāyikasyātikramāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 720. Activity (<s>yoga</s>) has been explained as threefold. Its faulty application is '<s>yoga-duṣpraṇidhāna</s>' (negligence in activity)—[comprising] faulty bodily application, faulty verbal application, and faulty mental application.

children.text: apratyavekṣitāpramārjitotsargādānasaṃstaropakramaṇānādarasmṛtyanupasthānāni ||
children.translated_text: Unexamined and unswept depositing and collecting, laying down and taking up, inattention, and lapse of mindfulness. ||

children.text: § 721. jantavaḥ santi na santi veti pratyavekṣaṇaṃ cakṣurvyāpāraḥ. mṛdunopakaraṇena yat kriyate prayojanaṃ tat pramārjitam. tadubhayaṃ pratiṣedhaviśiṣṭam utsargādibhis tribhir abhisaṃbadhyate — apratyavekṣitāpramārjitotsarga ity evam ādi. tatra apratyavekṣitāpramārjitāyāṃ bhūmau mūtrapurīṣotsargaḥ apratyavekṣitāpramārjitotsargaḥ. apratyavekṣitāpramārjitasyārhadācāryapūjopakaraṇasya gaṃdhamālyadhūpāder ātmaparidhānādyarthasya ca vastrāder ādānam apratyavekṣitāpramārjitādānam. apratyavekṣitāpramārjitasya prāvaraṇādeḥ saṃstarasyopakramaṇaṃ apratyavekṣitāpramārjitasaṃstaropakramaṇam. kṣudabhyarditatvād āvaśyakeṣv anādaro ’nutsāḥ. smṛtyanupasthānaṃ vyākhyātam. ta ete pañca proṣadhopavāsasyāticārāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 721. Examining—'are there living beings or not'—through the exercise of the eyes is '<s>pratyavekṣaṇa</s>' (examination). What is accomplished with a soft instrument is '<s>pramārjita</s>' (sweeping). Both of these, regarding [the acts of]—

children.text: sacittasaṃbandhasaṃmiśrābhiṣavaduṣpakvāhārāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Food connected with sentient beings, mixed [with sentient beings], fermented, and ill-cooked. ||

children.text: § 722. saha cittena vartate iti sacittaṃ cetanāvad dravyam. tadupaliṣṭaḥ saṃbandhaḥ. tadvyatikīrṇaḥ saṃmiśraḥ. kathaṃ punar asya sacittādiṣu pravṛttiḥ? pramādasaṃmohābhyām. dravo vṛṣyo vābhiṣavaḥ. asamyakpakvo duṣpakvaḥ. etair āhāro viśeṣyate — sacittāhāraḥ saṃbandhāhāraḥ saṃmiśrāhāro ’bhiṣavāhāro duṣpakvāhāra iti. ta ete pañca bhogopabhogaparisaṃkhyānasyāticāraḥ.
children.translated_text: § 722. That which exists together with consciousness (<s>citta</s>) is '<s>sacitta</s>' (sentient)—a substance possessing consciousness. Being placed upon that is '<s>saṃbandha</s>' (connection). Being mixed with that is '<s>saṃmiśra</s>' (mixture). But how does one [commit a transgression] regarding sentient [food] and the like?

children.text: sacittanikṣepāpidhānaparavyapadeśamātsaryakālātikramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Depositing on sentient things, covering with sentient things, misattributing [one's food] to another, jealousy, and exceeding the [proper] time. ||

children.text: § 723. sacitte padmapatrādau nikṣepaḥ sacittanikṣepaḥ. apidhānam āvaraṇam. sacittenaiva saṃbadhyate sacittāpidhānam iti. anyadātṛdeyārpaṇaṃ paravyapadeśaḥ. prayacchato ’py ādarābhāvo ’nyadātṛguṇāsahanaṃ vā mātsaryam. akāle bhojanaṃ kālātikramaḥ. ta ete pañcātithisaṃvibhāgaśīlāticārāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 723. Depositing on a sentient thing such as a lotus leaf is '<s>sacitta-nikṣepa</s>' (depositing on a sentient thing). <s>Apidhāna</s> (covering) is concealment—covering with a sentient thing. Offering what is to be given by another donor—

children.text: jīvitamaraṇāśaṃsāmitrānurāgasukhānubandhanidānāni ||
children.translated_text: Hoping for life and death, attachment to friends, attachment to pleasure, and making vows [for future enjoyment]. ||

children.text: § 724. āśaṃsanam āśaṃsā ākāṅkṣaṇam ity arthaḥ. jīvitaṃ ca maraṇaṃ ca jīvitamaraṇam, jīvitamaraṇasyāśaṃse jīvitamaraṇāśaṃse. pūrvasuhṛtsahapāṃsukrīḍanādyanusmaraṇaṃ mitrānurāgāḥ. anubhūtaprītiviśeṣasmṛtisamanvāhāraḥ sukhānubandhaḥ. bhogākā–ṅkṣayā niyataṃ dīyate cittaṃ tasmiṃs teneti vā nidānam. ta ete pañca sallekhanāyā aticārāḥ.
children.translated_text: § 724. Hoping (<s>āśaṃsā</s>) means longing, expectation. Life and death is '<s>jīvita-maraṇa</s>'; hoping for [continued] life and [a good] death are the two '<s>jīvita-maraṇāśaṃse</s>' (hopes for life and death). [Remembering] former friends, companions—

children.text: § 725. atrāha, uktaṃ bhavatā tīrthakaratvakāraṇakarmāsravanirdeśe ‘śaktitas tyāgatapasī ’ iti, punaś coktaṃ śīlavidhāne ‘atithisaṃvibhāga’ iti. tasya dānasya lakṣaṇam anirjñātaṃ taducyatām ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 725. Here one objects: you have stated in the exposition of the causes of influx of <s>Tīrthaṅkara</s> [name-determining <s>karma</s>] 'giving and austerity according to one's capacity,' and again in the prescription of moral conduct 'sharing with guests (<s>atithi-saṃvibhāga</s>)'—

children.text: anugrahārthaṃ svasyātisargo dānam ||
children.translated_text: Giving (<s>dāna</s>) is the relinquishing of one's own [property] for the purpose of benefiting [others]. ||

children.text: § 726. svaparopakāro ’nugrahaḥ. svopakāraḥ puṇyasaṃcayaḥ; paropakāraḥ samyagjñānādivṛddhiḥ. ‘sva’ śabdo dhanaparyāyavacanaḥ. anugrahārthaṃ svasyātisargas tyāgo dānaṃ veditavyam.
children.translated_text: § 726. Benefiting (<s>anugraha</s>) is the welfare of oneself and others. Self-welfare is the accumulation of merit (<s>puṇya</s>); the welfare of others is the increase of right knowledge and the like. The word '<s>sva</s>' (one's own) is a term for wealth. The relinquishing of one's own [wealth] for the purpose of benefiting [others]—

children.text: § 727. atrāha — uktaṃ dānaṃ tat kim aviśiṣṭaphalam āhosvid asti kaścit prativiśeṣa ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 727. Here one objects: giving has been stated; does it have an undifferentiated result, or is there some specific [variation]? To this he says—

children.text: vidhidravyadātṛpātraviśeṣāt tadviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The specific [result] of that [giving] depends on the specific method (<s>vidhi</s>), substance (<s>dravya</s>), donor (<s>dātṛ</s>), and recipient (<s>pātra</s>). ||

children.text: § 728. pratigrahādikramo vidhiḥ. viśeṣo guṇakṛtaḥ. tasya pratyekam abhisambandhaḥ kriyate — vidhiviśeṣo dravyaviśeṣo dātṛviseṣaḥ pātraviśeṣa iti. tatra vidhiviśeṣaḥ pratigrahādiṣv ādarānādarakṛto bhedaḥ. tapaḥsvādhyāyaparivṛddhihetutvādir dravyaviśeṣaḥ. anasūyāviṣādādir dātṛviśeṣaḥ. mokṣakāraṇaguṇasaṃyogaḥ pātraviśeṣaḥ. tataś ca puṇyaphalaviśeṣaḥ kṣityādiviśeṣād bījaphalaviśeṣavat.
children.translated_text: § 728. The procedure beginning with reception is the method (<s>vidhi</s>). The specific [quality] arises from virtues. The connection is made with each individually: specific method, specific substance, specific donor, specific recipient—

children.text: iti tattvārthavṛttau sarvārthasiddhisaṃjñikāyāṃ saptamo ’dhyāyaḥ || 7 ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh chapter of the <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>, the commentary on the <s>Tattvārthasūtra</s>. || 7 ||

children.text: athāṣṭhamo ’dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, the eighth chapter.

children.text: § 729. vyākhyāta āsravapadārthaḥ. tadanantaroddeśabhāgbandhapadārtha idānīṃ vyākhyeyaḥ. tasmin vyākhyeye sati pūrvaṃ bandhahetūpanyāsaḥ kriyate; tatpūrvakatvād bandhasyeti —
children.translated_text: § 729. The category of <s>āsrava</s> (influx) has been explained. The category of <s>bandha</s> (bondage), which was mentioned next in the enumeration, is now to be explained. When that is to be explained, first the statement of the causes of bondage is made—

children.text: mithyādarśanāviratipramādakaṣāyayogā bandhahetavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Wrong faith (<s>mithyādarśana</s>), non-restraint (<s>avirati</s>), negligence (<s>pramāda</s>), passions (<s>kaṣāya</s>), and activity (<s>yoga</s>) are the causes of bondage (<s>bandha</s>). ||

children.text: § 730. mithyādarśanādaya uktāḥ. kva? mithyādarśanaṃ tāvad uktam, ‘tattvārthaśraddhānaṃ samyagdarśanam’ ity atra tatpratipakṣabhūtam, āsravavidhāne ca kriyāsu vyākhyātaṃ mithyādarśanakriyeti. viratir uktā. tatpratipakṣabhūtā aviratir grāhyā. ājñāvyāpādanakriyā anākaṅkṣākriyety anayoḥ pramādasyāntarbhāvaḥ. sa ca pramādaḥ kuśaleṣv anādaraḥ. kaṣāyāḥ krodhādayaḥ anantānubandhyapratyākyānapratyākyānasaṃjvalanavikalpāḥ proktāḥ. kva? ‘indriyakaṣāyā’ ity atraiva. yogāḥ kāyādivikalpāḥ proktāḥ. kva? ‘kāyavāṅmanaḥkarma yogaḥ’ ity atra.
children.translated_text: § 730. Wrong faith and the rest have been stated. Where? Wrong faith, first, was stated [by implication] in 'belief in the categories of reality is right faith'—as its opposite, and in the exposition of influx—

children.text: § 731. mithyādarśanaṃ dvividham; naisargikaṃ paropadeśapūrvakaṃ ca. tatra paropadeśam antareṇa mithyātvakarmodayavaśād yad āvirbhavati tattvārthāśraddhānalakṣaṇaṃ tan naisargikam. paropadeśanimittaṃ caturvidham; kriyākriyāvādyajñānikavainayikavikalpāt. athavā pañcavidhaṃ mithyādarśanam — ekāntamithyādarśanaṃ viparītamithyādarśanaṃ saṃśayamithyādarśanaṃ vainayikamithyādarśanam ajñānikamithyādarśanaṃ ceti. tatra idam eva ittham eveti dharmidharmayor abhiniveśa ekāntaḥ.
puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam
children.translated_text: '<s>Puruṣa</s> (the self) alone is all this'—

children.text: iti vā nitya eva vā anitya eveti. sagrantho nirgranthaḥ, kevali kavalāhārī, strī sidhyatīty evam ādiḥ viparyayaḥ. samyagdarśanajñānacāritrāṇi kiṃ mokṣamāragaḥ syād vā na vety antarapakṣāparigrahaḥ saṃśayaḥ. sarvadevatānāṃ sarvasamayānāṃ ca samadarśanaṃ vainayikam. hitāhitaparīkṣāviraho ’jñānikatvam. uktaṃ ca —
children.translated_text: —or [it is asserted that the soul] is either eternal or non-eternal exclusively. [Wrong views such as:] the bound one (sagranatha) is the same as the unbound one (nirgrantha), the omniscient (kevalin) takes morsel-food, a woman can attain liberation—such and similar are the wrong views (viparyaya). The non-commitment to either position [in the form of] 'are right faith, right knowledge, and right conduct the path to liberation, or not?'—this is doubt (saṃśaya). The equal regard for all deities and all doctrines is the reverential error (vainayika). The absence of discrimination between what is beneficial and what is harmful is ignorance (ājñānikatva). And it has been said—

§ 731. Wrong faith (<s>mithyādarśana</s>) is twofold: innate (<s>naisargika</s>) and preceded by another's instruction (<s>paropadeśapūrvaka</s>). Among these, without another's instruction, that which manifests through the fruition of wrong-faith <s>karma</s>—

children.text:
āsidisadaṃ kiriyāṇaṃ akkiriyāṇaṃ taha ya hoi culasīdī |
	  sattaṭṭhamaṇṇāṇīṇaṃ veṇaiyāṇaṃ tu battisaṃ ||
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] Of the action-doctrines (kriyāvādins) and non-action-doctrines (akriyāvādins), there are also the lesser views (culasīdī); of the seven-fold and other ignorance-doctrines and the reverential doctrines, the total is thirty-two. ||

children.text: § 732. aviratir dvādaśavidhāḥ; ṣaṭkāyaṣaṭkaraṇaviṣayabhedāt. ṣodaśa kaṣāyā nava nokaṣāyās teṣām īṣadbhedo na bheda iti paṃcaviṃśatiḥ kaṣāyāḥ. catvāro manoyogaś catvāro vāgyogāḥ pañca kāyayogā iti trayodaśavikalpo yogaḥ. āhārakakāyayogāhārakamiśrakāyayogayoḥ pramattasaṃyate saṃbhavāt pañcadaśāpi bhavanti. pramādo ’nekavidhaḥ; śuddhyaṣṭakottamakṣamādiviṣayabhedāt. ta ete pañca bandhahetavaḥ samastā vyastāś ca bhavanti. tad yathā — mithyādṛṣṭeḥ paṃcāpi samuditā bandhahetavo bhavanti. sāsādhanasamyagdṛṣṭisamyaṅmithyādṛṣṭyasaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭīnām aviratyādayaś catvāraḥ. saṃyatāsaṃyatasyāviratir viratimiśrā pramādakaṣāyayogaś ca. pramattasaṃyatasya pramādakaṣāyayogāḥ. apramattādīnāṃ caturṇāṃ yogakaṣāyau. upaśāntakaṣāyakṣīṇakaṣāyasayogakevalinām eka eva yogaḥ. ayogakevalino na bandhahetuḥ.
children.translated_text: § 732. Non-restraint (<s>avirati</s>) is of twelve kinds, due to the differentiation of six classes of living beings and six modes of action. The sixteen <s>kaṣāyas</s> (passions) and nine <s>nokaṣāyas</s> (quasi-passions)—their partial difference is not [a full] difference—thus [there are] twenty-five <s>kaṣāyas</s>. Four types of mental activity (<s>manoyoga</s>), four types of vocal activity (<s>vāgyoga</s>), and five types of bodily activity (<s>kāyayoga</s>)—thus activity (<s>yoga</s>) has thirteen varieties. Since <s>āhārakakāyayoga</s> (assimilative-body activity) and <s>āhārakamiśrakāyayoga</s> (mixed assimilative-body activity) are possible in the stage of the restrained-with-negligence (<s>pramattasaṃyata</s>), there can also be fifteen. Negligence (<s>pramāda</s>) is of many kinds, due to the differentiation of purity, the group of eight, the highest forbearance, and so on. These five causes of bondage operate both collectively and individually. Namely: for one of wrong faith (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), all five causes of bondage are present together. For one with wrong faith accompanied by [partial] attainment (<s>sāsādhanasaṃyagdṛṣṭi</s>), one of mixed right-and-wrong faith (<s>saṃyaṅmithyādṛṣṭi</s>), and one of right faith without restraint (<s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>)—the four beginning with non-restraint. For the partially restrained (<s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>)—mixed non-restraint and restraint, negligence, passions, and activity. For the restrained-with-negligence (<s>pramattasaṃyata</s>)—negligence, passions, and activity. For the four beginning with the restrained-without-negligence (<s>apramatta</s>)—activity and passions. For the one with subsided passions (<s>upaśāntakaṣāya</s>), the one with destroyed passions (<s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s>), and the omniscient with activity (<s>sayogakevalin</s>)—activity alone. For the omniscient without activity (<s>ayogakevalin</s>)—there is no cause of bondage.

children.text: § 733. uktā bandhahetavaḥ. idānīṃ bandho vaktavya ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 733. The causes of bondage have been stated. Now bondage itself is to be explained; therefore he says—

children.text: sakaṣāyatvāj jīvaḥ karmaṇo yogyān pudgalān ādatte sa bandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of possessing passions (<s>sakaṣāyatva</s>), the soul (<s>jīva</s>) takes in material particles (<s>pudgalas</s>) fit for <s>karma</s>—that is bondage (<s>bandha</s>). ||

children.text: § 734. saha kaṣāyeṇa vartata iti sakaṣāyaḥ. sakaṣāyasya bhāvaḥ sakaṣātvam. tasmāt sakaṣāyatvād iti. punar hetunirdeśaḥ jaṭharāgnyāśayānurūpāhāragrahaṇavattīvramandamadhyamakaṣāyāśayānurūpasthityanubhavaviśeṣapratipattyartham. amūrtir ahasta ātmā kathaṃ karmādatta iti coditaḥ san ‘jīvaḥ’ ity āha. jīvanāj jīvaḥ prāṇādhāraṇād āyuḥsaṃbandhān nāyurvirahād iti. ‘karmayogyān’ iti laghunirdeśāt siddhe ‘karmaṇo yogyān’ iti pṛthagvibhaktyuccāraṇaṃ vākyāntarajñāpanārtham. kiṃ punas tadvākyāntaram? karmaṇo jīvaḥ sakaṣāyo bhavatīty ekaṃ vākyam. etad uktaṃ bhavati — ‘karmaṇaḥ’ iti hetunirdeśaḥ karmaṇo hetor jīvaḥ sakaṣāyo bhavati, nākarmasya kaṣāyalepo ’sti. tato jīvakarmaṇor anādisaṃbandha iti uktaṃ bhavati. tenāmūrto jīvo mūrtena karmaṇā kathaṃ badhyate iti codyam apākṛtaṃ bhavati. itarathā hi bandhasyādimattve ātyantikīṃ śuddhiṃ dadhataḥ siddhasyeva bandhābhāvaḥ prasajyeta. dvitīyaṃ vākyaṃ ‘karmaṇo yogyān pudgalān ādatte’ iti. arthavaśād vibhaktipariṇāma iti pūrvahetusaṃbandham tyaktvā ṣaṣṭhīsaṃbandham upaiti ‘karmaṇo yogyān’ iti. ‘pudgala’ vacanaṃ karmaṇas tādātmyakhyāpanārtham. tenātmaguṇo ’dṛṣṭo nirākṛto bhavati; tasya saṃsārahetutvānupapatteḥ. ‘ādatte’ iti hetuhetumadbhāvakhyāpanārtham. ato mithyādarśanādyāveśād ārdrīkṛtasyātmanaḥ sarvato yogaviśeṣāt teṣāṃ sūkṣmaikakṣetrāvagāhinām anantānantapradeśānāṃ pudgalānāṃ karmabhāvayogyānām avibhagenopaśleṣo bandha ity ākhyāyate. yathā bhājanaviśeṣe prakṣiptānāṃ vividharasabījapuṣpaphalānāṃ madirābhāvena pariṇāmas tathā pudgalānām apy ātmani sthitānāṃ yogakaṣāyavaśāt karmabhāvena pariṇāmo veditavyaḥ. ‘saḥ’ vacanam anyanivṛttyartham. sa eṣa bandho nānyo ’stīti. tena guṇaguṇibandho nivartito bhavati. karmādisādhano ‘bandha’-śabdo vyākhyeyaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 734. That which exists together with passions (<s>kaṣāya</s>) is <s>sakaṣāya</s>. The state of being <s>sakaṣāya</s> is <s>sakaṣāyatva</s>. Therefore, 'because of <s>sakaṣāyatva</s>.' The repeated specification of the cause is for the purpose of understanding the specific attainment of duration and experience corresponding to the disposition of intense, mild, and moderate passions—just as the intake of food corresponds to the condition of the gastric fire. When objected, 'how does the soul, which is immaterial and handless, take in <s>karma</s>?'—he replies with '<s>jīva</s>' (soul). <s>Jīva</s> means 'one who lives'—from sustaining life-breath, from connection with lifespan, not from absence of lifespan. Since the meaning is already established by the concise expression 'fit for <s>karma</s>' (<s>karmayogyān</s>), the separate articulation of case-endings as 'fit for <s>karma</s>' (<s>karmaṇo yogyān</s>) is for the purpose of indicating another sentence. What then is that other sentence? '<s>Karmaṇo jīvaḥ sakaṣāyo bhavati</s>'—'the soul becomes possessed of passions because of <s>karma</s>'—this is one sentence. What is stated amounts to this: '<s>karmaṇaḥ</s>' is an indication of cause—the soul becomes possessed of passions because of <s>karma</s> as the cause; one without <s>karma</s> has no taint of passions. From this it is stated that the relationship between the soul and <s>karma</s> is beginningless. Thereby the objection 'how is the immaterial soul bound by material <s>karma</s>?' is refuted. For otherwise, if bondage had a beginning, then for one who has attained absolute purity—namely, a liberated being—the absence of bondage would [absurdly] follow [even now]. The second sentence is '<s>karmaṇo yogyān pudgalān ādatte</s>' (it takes in particles fit for <s>karma</s>). Due to the force of meaning, there is a transformation of case-ending—abandoning the connection with the previous causal [ablative] sense, it assumes the genitive connection as 'fit for <s>karma</s>.' The word '<s>pudgala</s>' (material particle) is for the purpose of declaring the identity-nature of <s>karma</s>. Thereby the view that [<s>karma</s>] is an unseen quality of the self (<s>ātmaguṇa</s>) is refuted, since it cannot logically be the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>. The word '<s>ādatte</s>' (takes in) is for indicating the cause-effect relationship. Therefore, the intimate merging—without separation—of infinitely infinite spatial units of material particles that are subtle, occupying the same locus [as the soul], suitable for becoming <s>karma</s>, [taken in] from all directions through the particular activity of <s>yoga</s> by the soul that has been moistened by the influence of wrong faith and the rest—this is called bondage (<s>bandha</s>). Just as various substances of different flavors—seeds, flowers, and fruits—placed in a particular vessel undergo transformation into liquor, so too should the transformation of material particles residing in the soul into the nature of <s>karma</s> through the force of <s>yoga</s> and passions be understood. The word '<s>saḥ</s>' (that) is for the purpose of excluding others—'this alone is bondage and nothing else.' Thereby the bondage of quality and substance-possessor is excluded. The word '<s>bandha</s>' (bondage) should be explained as having <s>karma</s> and the rest as its means.

children.text: § 735. āha kim ayaṃ bandha ekarūpa eva, āhosvit prakārā apy asya santīty ata idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 735. One asks: is this bondage of a single nature, or does it have varieties? To this it is said—

children.text: prakṛtisthityanubhavapradeśās tadvidhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nature (<s>prakṛti</s>), duration (<s>sthiti</s>), experience (<s>anubhava</s>), and spatial extent (<s>pradeśa</s>) are its varieties (<s>vidhayaḥ</s>). ||

children.text: § 736. prakṛtiḥ svabhāvaḥ. nimbasya kā prakṛtiḥ? tiktatā. guḍasya kā prakṛtiḥ? madhuratā. tathā jñānāvaraṇasya kā prakṛtiḥ? arthānavagamaḥ. darśanāvaraṇasya kā prakṛtiḥ? arthānālokanam. vedyasya sadasallakṣaṇasya sukhaduḥkhasaṃvedanam. darśanamohasya tattvārthāśraddhānam. cāritramohasyāsaṃyamaḥ. āyuṣo bhavadhāraṇam. nāmno nārakādināmakaraṇam. gotrasyoccair nīccaiḥ sthānasaṃśabdanam. anantarāyasya dānādivighnakaraṇam. tadevaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ prakriyate prabhavaty asyā iti prakṛtiḥ. tatsvabhāvād apracyutiḥ sthitiḥ. yathā — ajāgomahiṣyādikṣīrāṇāṃ mādhuryasvabhāvād apracyutiḥ sthitiḥ. tathā jñānāvaraṇādīnām arthāvagamādisvabhāvād apracyutiḥ sthitiḥ. tadrasaviśeṣo ’nubhavaḥ yathā — ajāgomahiṣyādikṣīrāṇāṃ tīvramandādibhāvena rasaviśeṣaḥ. tathā karmapudgalānāṃ svagatasāmarthyaviśeṣo ’nubhavaḥ. iyattāvadhāraṇaṃ pradeśaḥ. karmabhāvapariṇatapudgalaskandhānāṃ paramāṇuparicchedenāvadhāraṇaṃ pradeṣaḥ. ‘vidhi’-śabdaḥ prakāravacanaḥ. ta ete prakṛtyādayaś catvāras tasya bandhasya prakārāḥ. tatra yoganimittau prakṛtipradeśau. kaṣāyanimittau sthityanubhavau. tatprakarṣāprakarṣabhedād tadbaṃdhavicitrabhāvaḥ. tathā coktam —
children.translated_text: § 736. <s>Prakṛti</s> means inherent nature. What is the nature of the neem tree? Bitterness. What is the nature of jaggery? Sweetness. Similarly, what is the nature of <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring karma)? The non-apprehension of objects. What is the nature of <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s> (perception-obscuring karma)? The non-illumination of objects. Of <s>vedanīya</s> (feeling-producing karma), characterized by good and bad—the experience of pleasure and pain. Of <s>darśanamoha</s> (faith-deluding karma)—disbelief in the categories of reality. Of <s>cāritramoha</s> (conduct-deluding karma)—non-restraint. Of <s>āyuṣ</s> (life-span karma)—the sustaining of existence. Of <s>nāma</s> (name-determining karma)—the producing of names such as hellish being and the rest. Of <s>gotra</s> (lineage-determining karma)—the designation of high and low status. Of <s>antarāya</s> (obstructive karma)—the obstruction of giving and the rest. Thus the characteristic, the effect, proceeds from and originates in this—hence it is <s>prakṛti</s>. The non-departure from that inherent nature is duration (<s>sthiti</s>). Just as the non-departure from the sweetness-nature of goat's, cow's, buffalo's, and other milks is their duration, so too the non-departure from the nature of non-apprehension of objects and the like of <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> and the rest is their duration. The specific intensity of that [nature] is experience (<s>anubhava</s>). Just as there is a specific variation of flavor—intense, mild, etc.—in the milks of goat, cow, buffalo, and others, so too the specific potency inherent in the karmic material particles is experience. The determination of quantity is spatial extent (<s>pradeśa</s>). The determination by counting the ultimate atoms of material aggregates that have been transformed into the nature of <s>karma</s> is spatial extent. The word '<s>vidhi</s>' means 'variety.' These four—<s>prakṛti</s> and the rest—are the varieties of that bondage. Among these, <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>pradeśa</s> (spatial extent) are caused by <s>yoga</s> (activity). <s>Sthiti</s> (duration) and <s>anubhava</s> (experience) are caused by <s>kaṣāya</s> (passions). Due to the differentiation of their intensity and mildness, there is the diversity of that bondage. And thus it has been said—

children.text:
jogā payaḍi-paesā ṭhidiaṇubhāgā kasāyado kuṇadi |
	  apariṇaducchiṇṇesu ya baṃdhaṭṭhidikāraṇaṃ ṇatthi ||
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] <s>Yoga</s> produces <s>prakṛti</s> (nature) and <s>pradeśa</s> (spatial extent); <s>sthiti</s> (duration) and <s>anubhava</s> (experience) are produced by <s>kaṣāya</s> (passions). Without the destruction of undeveloped [karmas], there is no ground for bondage-duration. ||

children.text: § 737. tatrādyasya prakṛtibandhasya bhedapradarśanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 737. In order to demonstrate the subdivisions of the first, namely <s>prakṛtibandha</s> (nature-bondage), he says—

children.text: ādyo jñānadarśanāvaraṇavedanīyamohanīyāyurnāmagotrāntarāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The first [type of bondage has these primary varieties]: <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring), <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s> (perception-obscuring), <s>vedanīya</s> (feeling-producing), <s>mohanīya</s> (deluding), <s>āyus</s> (life-span determining), <s>nāma</s> (name-determining), <s>gotra</s> (lineage-determining), and <s>antarāya</s> (obstructive). ||

children.text: § 738. ādyaḥ prakṛtibandho jñānāvaraṇādyaṣṭavikalpo veditavyaḥ. āvṛṇoty āvriyate ’neneti vā āvaraṇam. tat pratyekam abhisaṃbadhyate — jñānāvaraṇaṃ darśanāvaraṇam iti. vedayati vedyata iti vā vedanīyam. mohayati mohyate ’neneti vā mohanīyam. ety anena nārakādibhavam ity āyuḥ. namayaty ātmānaṃ namyate ’neneti vā nāma. uccair nīcaiś ca gūyate śabdyata iti vā gotram. dātṛdeyādīnām antaraṃ madhyametīty antarāyaḥ. ekenātmapariṇāmenādīyamānāḥ pudgalā jñānāvaraṇādyanekabhedaṃ pratipadyante sakṛdupabhuktānnapariṇāmarasarudhirādivat.
children.translated_text: § 738. The first, <s>prakṛtibandha</s> (nature-bondage), should be understood as having eight varieties beginning with <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s>. That which covers or by which [knowledge] is covered is <s>āvaraṇa</s> (obscuration). It connects with each individually—<s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring) and <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s> (perception-obscuring). That which causes experience or is experienced is <s>vedanīya</s> (feeling-producing). That which causes delusion or by which one is deluded is <s>mohanīya</s> (deluding). That by which one goes to hellish and other existences is <s>āyus</s> (life-span). That which bends the self or by which [the self] is bent is <s>nāma</s> (name-determining). That which is proclaimed as high or low status is <s>gotra</s> (lineage-determining). That which interposes between the giver, the gift, and the rest is <s>antarāya</s> (obstructive). Through a single self-modification, the material particles being taken in assume the manifold divisions of <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> and the rest—like food consumed at one time being transformed into chyme, blood, and so forth.

children.text: § 739. āha, ukto mūlaprakṛtibandho ’ṣṭavidhaḥ. idānīm uttaraprakṛtibandho vaktavya ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 739. One says: the primary nature-bondage (<s>mūlaprakṛtibandha</s>) has been stated as eightfold. Now the sub-type nature-bondage (<s>uttaraprakṛtibandha</s>) is to be explained; therefore he says—

children.text: pañcanavadvyaṣṭāviṃśaticaturdvicatvāriṃśaddvipañcabhedā yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: Five, nine, two, twenty-eight, four, forty-two, two, and five sub-types respectively. ||

children.text: § 740. dvitīyagrahaṇam iha kartavyaḥ; dvitīya uttaraprakṛtibandha evaṃ vikalpa iti? na kartavyam; pāriśeṣyāt siddheḥ. ādyo mūlaprakṛtibandho ’ṣṭavikalpa uktaḥ. tataḥ pāriśeṣyād ayam uttaraprakṛtivikalpavidhir bhavati. ‘bheda’ śabdaḥ pañcādibhir yathā kramam abhisaṃbandhyate — pañcabhedaṃ jñānāvaraṇīyaṃ navabhedaṃ darśanāvaraṇīyaṃ dvibhedaṃ vedanīyaṃ aṣṭāviṃśatibhedaṃ mohanīyaṃ caturbhedam āyuḥ dvicatvāriṃśadbhedaṃ nāma dvibhedaṃ gotraṃ paṃcabhedo ’ntarāya iti.
children.translated_text: § 740. Should the word 'second' be supplied here, [meaning] 'the second, the sub-type nature-bondage, has these varieties'? No, it need not be, since it is established by elimination. The first, the primary nature-bondage, has been stated as having eight varieties. Therefore, by elimination, this is the specification of sub-type varieties. The word 'sub-type' (<s>bheda</s>) connects with the numbers five and so on in sequence—<s>jñānāvaraṇīya</s> (knowledge-obscuring) has five sub-types, <s>darśanāvaraṇīya</s> (perception-obscuring) has nine sub-types, <s>vedanīya</s> (feeling-producing) has two sub-types, <s>mohanīya</s> (deluding) has twenty-eight sub-types, <s>āyus</s> (life-span) has four sub-types, <s>nāma</s> (name-determining) has forty-two sub-types, <s>gotra</s> (lineage-determining) has two sub-types, and <s>antarāya</s> (obstructive) has five sub-types.

children.text: § 741. yadi jñānāvaraṇīyaṃ paṃcabhedaṃ tatpratipattir ucyatām ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 741. If <s>jñānāvaraṇīya</s> (knowledge-obscuring karma) has five sub-types, let the specification of those be stated; therefore he says—

children.text: matiśrutāvadhimanaḥparyayakevalānām ||
children.translated_text: [The five sub-types are the obscuration] of <s>mati</s> (sensory knowledge), <s>śruta</s> (scriptural knowledge), <s>avadhi</s> (clairvoyant knowledge), <s>manaḥparyaya</s> (mind-reading knowledge), and <s>kevala</s> (omniscient knowledge). ||

children.text: § 742. matyādīni jñānāni vyākhyātāni. teṣām āvṛter āvaraṇabhedo bhavatīti paṃcottaraprakṛtayo veditavyāḥ. atra codyate — abhavyasya manaḥparyayajñānaśaktiḥ kevalajñānaśaktiś ca syād vā na vā. yadi syāt tasyābhavyatvābhāvaḥ. atha nāsti tatrāvaraṇadvayakalpanā vyartheti? ucyate — ādeśavacanān na doṣaḥ. dravyārthādeśān manaḥparyayakevalajñānaśaktisaṃbhavaḥ. paryāyārthādeśāt tacchaktyabhāvaḥ. yady evaṃ bhavyābhavyavikalpo nopapadyate; ubhayatra tacchaktisadbhāvāt? na śaktibhāvābhāvāpekṣayā bhavyābhavyavikalpa ity ucyate. kutas tarhi? vyaktisadbhāvāsadbhāvāpekṣayā. samyagdarśanādibhir vyaktir yasya bhaviṣyati sa bhavyaḥ. yasya tu na bhaviṣyati so ’bhavya iti. kanaketarapāṣāṇavat.
children.translated_text: § 742. The types of knowledge beginning with <s>mati</s> (sensory knowledge) have been explained [previously]. The sub-types of obscuration correspond to the obscuration of each of these—thus five sub-types should be understood. Here an objection is raised: does an <s>abhavya</s> (incapable of liberation) soul possess the capacity for <s>manaḥparyaya</s> (mind-reading) knowledge and <s>kevala</s> (omniscient) knowledge, or not? If it does, then its nature as <s>abhavya</s> would be negated. If it does not, then the postulation of two [additional] obscurations [for those types] would be pointless. It is replied: there is no fault, because of the teaching from [different] perspectives. From the perspective of substance (<s>dravyārthādeśa</s>), the capacity for <s>manaḥparyaya</s> and <s>kevala</s> knowledge is possible. From the perspective of modification (<s>paryāyārthādeśa</s>), that capacity is absent. If so, then the distinction between <s>bhavya</s> (capable of liberation) and <s>abhavya</s> would not hold, since in both cases that capacity exists [in substance]? It is not said that the distinction between <s>bhavya</s> and <s>abhavya</s> depends on the presence or absence of capacity. Then on what does it depend? On the presence or absence of manifestation. One for whom manifestation through right faith and the rest will occur is <s>bhavya</s>. One for whom it will never occur is <s>abhavya</s>—like a stone of the <s>kanaka</s> variety [which can never become gold].

children.text: § 743. āha, ukto jñānāvaraṇottaraprakṛtivikalpaḥ. idānīṃ darśanāvaraṇasya vaktavya ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 743. One says: the sub-type varieties of <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring karma) have been stated. Now the sub-types of <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s> (perception-obscuring karma) are to be stated; therefore he says—

children.text: cakṣuracakṣuravadhikevalānāṃ nidrānidrānidrāpracalāpracalāpracalāstyānagṛddhayaś ca ||
children.translated_text: The obscuration of <s>cakṣu</s> (visual perception), <s>acakṣu</s> (non-visual perception), <s>avadhi</s> (clairvoyant perception), and <s>kevala</s> (omniscient perception); and <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), <s>nidrānidrā</s> (deep sleep), <s>pracalā</s> (drowsiness), <s>pracalāpracalā</s> (intense drowsiness), and <s>styānagṛddhi</s> (somnambulism). ||

children.text: § 744. cakṣuracakṣuravadhikevalānām iti darśanāvaraṇāpekṣayā bhedanirdeśaḥ — cakṣurdarśanāvaraṇam acakṣurdarśanāvaraṇam avadhidarśanāvaraṇaṃ kevaladarśanāvaraṇam iti. madakhedaklamavinodanārthaḥ svāpo nidrā. tasyā upary upari vṛttir nidrānidrā. yā kriyātmānaṃ pracalayati sā pracalā śokaśramamadādiprabhavā āsīnasyāpi netragātravikriyāsūcikā. saiva punaḥ punar āvartamānā pracalāpracalā. svapne yathā vīryaviśeṣāvirbhāvaḥ sā styānagṛddhiḥ. styāyater anekārthatvāt svapnārtha iha gṛhyate, gṛddher api dīptiḥ. styāne svapne gṛddhyati dīpyate yad udayād ātmā raudraṃ bahukarma karoti sā styānagṛddhiḥ. iha nidrādibhir darśanāvaraṇaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyenābhisaṃbadhyate — nidrādarśanāvaraṇam nidrānidrādarśanāvaraṇam ity ādi.
children.translated_text: § 744. The expressions '<s>cakṣu</s>, <s>acakṣu</s>, <s>avadhi</s>, <s>kevala</s>' are specifications of sub-types with reference to <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s>—<s>cakṣurdarśanāvaraṇa</s> (visual-perception-obscuring), <s>acakṣurdarśanāvaraṇa</s> (non-visual-perception-obscuring), <s>avadhidarśanāvaraṇa</s> (clairvoyant-perception-obscuring), and <s>kevaladarśanāvaraṇa</s> (omniscient-perception-obscuring). Sleep (<s>nidrā</s>) is slumber for the purpose of dispelling intoxication, fatigue, and exhaustion. Its repeated occurrence upon itself is deep sleep (<s>nidrānidrā</s>). That which causes the body to move during activity is drowsiness (<s>pracalā</s>)—arising from grief, exertion, intoxication, and the like, indicated by the distortion of the eyes and limbs even while seated. That same [drowsiness] recurring again and again is intense drowsiness (<s>pracalāpracalā</s>). That in which a special manifestation of power occurs during sleep is somnambulism (<s>styānagṛddhi</s>). Since the root '<s>styā</s>' has multiple meanings, the meaning 'sleep' is taken here; and '<s>gṛddhi</s>' means 'brilliance.' That by whose arising the soul performs violent and manifold actions in sleep—that is <s>styānagṛddhi</s>. Here, sleep and the rest are connected with perception-obscuring [karma] by co-referentiality: <s>nidrādarśanāvaraṇa</s> (sleep-perception-obscuring), <s>nidrānidrādarśanāvaraṇa</s> (deep-sleep-perception-obscuring), and so on.

children.text: § 745. tṛtīyasyāḥ prakṛter uttaraprakṛtipratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 745. For the purpose of explaining the sub-types of the third type, he says—

children.text: sadasadvedye ||
children.translated_text: Pleasant feeling-producing (<s>sadvedya</s>) and unpleasant feeling-producing (<s>asadvedya</s>). ||

children.text: § 746. yad udayād devādigatiṣu śarīramānasasukhaprāptis tat sadvedyam. praśastaṃ vedyaṃ sadvedyam iti. yat phalaṃ duḥkham anekavidhaṃ tad asadvedyam. apraśastaṃ vedyam asadvedyam iti.
children.translated_text: § 746. That by whose fruition there is the attainment of bodily and mental pleasure in the destinies of gods and others is pleasant feeling-producing (<s>sadvedya</s>). Praiseworthy feeling-producing is <s>sadvedya</s>. That whose result is manifold suffering is unpleasant feeling-producing (<s>asadvedya</s>). Unpraiseworthy feeling-producing is <s>asadvedya</s>.

children.text: § 747. caturthyāḥ prakṛter uttaraprakṛtivikalpanidarśanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 747. For the purpose of demonstrating the sub-type varieties of the fourth type, he says—

children.text: darśanacāritramohanīyākaṣāyakaṣāyavedanīyākhyās tridvinavaṣoḍaśabhedāh samyaktvamithyātvatadubhayānyakaṣāyakaṣāyau hāsyaratyaratiśokabhayajugupsāstrīpunnapuṃsakavedā anantānubandhyapratyākhyānapratyākhyānasaṃjvalanavikalpāścaikaśaḥ krodhamānamāyālobhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those called <s>darśanamohanīya</s> (faith-deluding), <s>cāritramohanīya</s> (conduct-deluding), <s>akaṣāyakaṣāya</s> (quasi-passions), and <s>kaṣāyavedanīya</s> (passion-feeling), having three, two, nine, and sixteen sub-types respectively: <s>samyaktva</s> (right faith), <s>mithyātva</s> (wrong faith), and <s>samyaṅmithyātva</s> (mixed faith) are the [three sub-types of faith-deluding]; <s>akaṣāya</s> (quasi-passion) and <s>kaṣāya</s> (passion) [are the two sub-types of conduct-deluding]; laughter (<s>hāsya</s>), pleasure (<s>rati</s>), displeasure (<s>arati</s>), grief (<s>śoka</s>), fear (<s>bhaya</s>), disgust (<s>jugupsā</s>), female sex-passion (<s>strīveda</s>), male sex-passion (<s>puṃveda</s>), and neuter sex-passion (<s>napuṃsakaveda</s>) [are the nine quasi-passions]; and the four varieties each of <s>anantānubandhin</s> (infinitely-binding), <s>apratyākhyāna</s> (non-renunciation-causing), <s>pratyākhyāna</s> (partial-renunciation-obstructing), and <s>saṃjvalana</s> (smoldering) [passions]—namely, anger (<s>krodha</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), deceit (<s>māyā</s>), and greed (<s>lobha</s>). ||

children.text: § 748. darśanādayaś catvāraḥ tryādayo ’pi. tatra yathāsaṃkhyena saṃbandho bhavati — darśanamohanīyaṃ tribhedham, cāritramohanīyaṃ dvibhedam, akaṣāyavedanīyaṃ navavidham, kaṣāyavedanīyaṃ ṣoḍaśavidham iti.
children.translated_text: Section 748. <s>Darśana</s> (faith-related) and the rest are four; with three and so forth as well. There the connection is made numerically: <s>darśanamohanīya</s> (faith-deluding karma) is of three kinds, <s>cāritramohanīya</s> (conduct-deluding karma) is of two kinds, <s>akaṣāyavedanīya</s> (non-passion-feeling-producing karma) is of nine kinds, and <s>kaṣāyavedanīya</s> (passion-feeling-producing karma) is of sixteen kinds.

children.text: § 749. tatra darśanamohanīyaṃ tribhedham — samyaktvaṃ mithyātvaṃ tadubhayam iti. tad bandhaṃ pratyekaṃ bhūtvā satkarmāpekṣayā tridhā vyavatiṣṭhate. tatra yasyodayāt sarvajñapraṇītamārgaparāṅmukhas tattvārthaśraddhānanirutsuko hitāhitavicārāsamartho mithyādṛṣṭir bhavati tan mithyātvam. tad eva samyaktvaṃ śubhapariṇāmaniruddhasvarasaṃ yad audāsīnyenāvasthitam ātmanaḥ śraddhānaṃ na niruṇaddhi, tad vedayamānaḥ puruṣaḥ samyagdṛṣṭir ity abhidhīyate. tad eva mithyātvaṃ prakṣālanaviśeṣāt kṣīṇākṣīṇamadaśaktikodravavatsāmiśuddhasvarasaṃ tadubhayam ity ākhyāyate samyaṅmithyātvam iti yāvat. yasyodayād ātmano ’rdhaśuddhamadakodravaudanopayogāpāditamiśrapariṇāmavadubhayātmako bhavati pariṇāmaḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 749. Of these, <s>darśanamohanīya</s> (faith-deluding karma) is of three kinds: right faith (<s>samyaktva</s>), wrong faith (<s>mithyātva</s>), and a mixture of both (<s>tadubhaya</s>). That [karma], being a single bondage, on account of its wholesome karmic [manifestation], establishes itself in three ways. Among these, that by whose fruition one becomes averse to the path taught by the omniscient, uninterested in faith in the categories of reality, incapable of discriminating between beneficial and harmful — becoming a person of wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) — that is <s>mithyātva</s> (wrong faith). That same <s>samyaktva</s> (right faith), whose inherent force has been arrested by auspicious dispositions, which remains in a state of indifference and does not obstruct one's own faith — a person experiencing that is called one of right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>). That same <s>mithyātva</s>, due to a special degree of purification, having an inherent force that is partly diminished and partly undiminished — like intoxicating liquor mixed with <s>kodrava</s> (a coarse grain) — that is called <s>tadubhaya</s> (mixed), meaning <s>samyaṅmithyātva</s> (mixed right-and-wrong faith). By whose fruition there arises a mixed disposition in the soul, like the experience of consuming food made of half-purified intoxicating liquor and <s>kodrava</s>, partaking of both natures.

children.text: § 750. cāritramohanīyaṃ dvidhā; akaṣāyakaṣāyabhedāt. īṣad arthe nañaḥ prayogād īṣat kaṣāyo ’kaṣāya iti. akaṣāyavedanīyaṃ navavidham. kutaḥ. hāsyādibhedāt. yasyodayād dhāsyāvirbhāvas tad dhāsyam. yad udayād deśādiṣv autsukyaṃ sā ratiḥ. aratis tadviparītā. yad vipākāc chocanaṃ sa śokaḥ. yad udayād udvegas tad bhayam. yad udayād ātmadoṣasaṃvaraṇaṃ paradoṣāviṣkaraṇaṃ sā jugupsā. yad udayāt straiṇān bhāvān pratipadyate sa strīvedaḥ. yasyodayāt pauṃsnān bhāvānāskandati sa puṃvedaḥ. yad udayān nāpuṃsakān bhāvān upavrajati sa napuṃsakavedaḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 750. <s>Cāritramohanīya</s> (conduct-deluding karma) is twofold, due to the division into <s>akaṣāya</s> (non-passion) and <s>kaṣāya</s> (passion). Since the negative prefix 'a' is used in the sense of 'slight,' 'slight passion' is <s>akaṣāya</s>. <s>Akaṣāyavedanīya</s> (non-passion-feeling-producing karma) is of nine kinds. Why? Due to the division into laughter (<s>hāsya</s>) and the rest. That by whose fruition laughter manifests is <s>hāsya</s>. That by whose fruition there is eagerness toward places and the like is <s>rati</s> (liking). <s>Arati</s> (disliking) is the opposite of that. That by whose ripening there is lamentation is <s>śoka</s> (sorrow). That by whose fruition there is alarm is <s>bhaya</s> (fear). That by whose fruition there is concealment of one's own faults and exposure of others' faults is <s>jugupsā</s> (disgust). That by whose fruition one assumes feminine dispositions is <s>strīveda</s> (feminine sexual inclination). That by whose fruition one is impelled toward masculine dispositions is <s>puṃveda</s> (masculine sexual inclination). That by whose fruition one resorts to neuter dispositions is <s>napuṃsakaveda</s> (neuter sexual inclination).

children.text: § 751. kaṣāyavedanīyaṃ ṣoḍaśavidham. kutaḥ. anantānubandhyādivikalpāt. tad yathā — kaṣāyāḥ krodhamānamāyālobhāḥ. teṣām catasro ’vasthāḥ — anantānubandhino ’pratyākhyānāvaraṇāḥ pratyākhyānāvaraṇāḥ saṃjvalanāś ceti. anantasaṃsārakāraṇatvān mithyādarśanam anantam. tadanubandhino ’nantānubandhinaḥ krodhamānamāyālobhāḥ. yadudayād deśaviratiṃ saṃyamāsaṃyamākhyām alpām api kartuṃ na śaknoti te deśapratyākhyānam āvṛṇvanto ’pratyākhyānāvaraṇāḥ krodhamānamāyālobhāḥ. yadudayād viratiṃ kṛtsnāṃ saṃyamākhyāṃ na śaknoti kartuṃ te kṛtsnaṃ pratyākhyānam āvṛṇvantaḥ pratyākhyānāvaraṇāḥ krodhamānamāyālobhāḥ. samekībhāve vartate. saṃyamena sahāvasthānād ekībhūya jvalanti saṃyamo vā jvalaty eṣu satsv apīti saṃjvalanāḥ krodhamānamāyālobhāḥ. ta ete samuditāḥ santaḥ ṣoḍaśa kaṣāyā bhavanti.
children.translated_text: Section 751. <s>Kaṣāyavedanīya</s> (passion-feeling-producing karma) is of sixteen kinds. Why? Due to the subdivisions beginning with <s>anantānubandhin</s> (infinitely binding) and the rest. They are as follows: the passions (<s>kaṣāyas</s>) are anger (<s>krodha</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), deceit (<s>māyā</s>), and greed (<s>lobha</s>). They have four states: <s>anantānubandhin</s> (infinitely binding), <s>apratyākhyānāvaraṇa</s> (obstructing partial renunciation), <s>pratyākhyānāvaraṇa</s> (obstructing complete renunciation), and <s>saṃjvalana</s> (blazing). Because wrong faith (<s>mithyādarśana</s>), being the cause of infinite <s>saṃsāra</s>, is called 'infinite' (<s>ananta</s>), those that accompany it are called <s>anantānubandhin</s> — the anger, pride, deceit, and greed [of this class]. Those by whose fruition one cannot accomplish even the slightest partial restraint called <s>saṃyamāsaṃyama</s> (mixed discipline-and-non-discipline) — those, obstructing partial renunciation, are the <s>apratyākhyānāvaraṇa</s> anger, pride, deceit, and greed. Those by whose fruition one cannot accomplish complete restraint called <s>saṃyama</s> (discipline) — those, obstructing complete renunciation, are the <s>pratyākhyānāvaraṇa</s> anger, pride, deceit, and greed. The term relates to coexistence. Because they blaze together with restraint, or because restraint blazes even in their presence, they are called <s>saṃjvalana</s> — the anger, pride, deceit, and greed [of this class]. All these taken together are the sixteen passions (<s>kaṣāyas</s>).

children.text: § 752. mohanīyānantaroddeśabhāja āyuṣa uttaraprakṛtinirjñāpanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 752. In order to explain the sub-types of the next type after <s>mohanīya</s> (deluding karma), namely <s>āyus</s> (life-span determining karma), he says —

children.text: nārakatairyagyonamānuṣadaivāni ||
children.translated_text: Hellish (<s>nāraka</s>), animal (<s>tairyagyona</s>), human (<s>mānuṣa</s>), and celestial (<s>daiva</s>). ||

children.text: § 753. nārakādiṣu bhavasaṃbandhenāyuṣo vyapadeśaḥ kriyate. narakeṣu bhavaṃ nārakam āyuḥ, tiragyoniṣu bhavaṃ tairyagyonam, mānuṣeṣu bhavaṃ mānuṣam, deveṣu bhavaṃ daivam iti. narakeṣu tīvraśītoṣṇavedaneṣu yannimittaṃ dīrghajīvanaṃ tannārakam. evaṃ śeṣv api.
children.translated_text: Section 753. The designation of <s>āyus</s> (life-span karma) is made according to its connection with the [respective] existence (<s>bhava</s>) in the hellish and other [destinies]. That life-span which pertains to existence in the hells is <s>nāraka</s> (hellish) life-span; that pertaining to existence among animals is <s>tairyagyona</s> (animal) life-span; that pertaining to existence among humans is <s>mānuṣa</s> (human) life-span; and that pertaining to existence among gods is <s>daiva</s> (celestial) life-span. That on account of which there is long life in the hells, [places] of intense cold and hot suffering, is <s>nāraka</s> [life-span]. Similarly in the rest as well.

children.text: § 754. āyuś caturvidhaṃ vyākhyātam. tadanantaram uddiṣṭaṃ yan nāmakarma tad uttaraprakṛtinirṇayārtham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 754. <s>Āyus</s> (life-span karma) has been explained as fourfold. Next, what was enumerated as <s>nāmakarma</s> (name-determining karma) — in order to ascertain its sub-types, he says —

children.text: gatijātiśarīrāṅgopāṅganirmāṇabaṃdhanasaṃghātasaṃsthānasaṃhananasparśarasagaṃdhavarṇānupūrvyāgurulaghūpaghātaparaghātātapodyotocchvāsavihāyogatayaḥ pratyekaśarīratrasasubhagasusvaraśubhasūkṣmaparyāptisthirādeyayaśaḥkīrtisetarāṇi tīrthakaratvaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Destiny (<s>gati</s>), birth-class (<s>jāti</s>), body (<s>śarīra</s>), limbs and minor limbs (<s>aṅgopāṅga</s>), formation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>), binding (<s>bandhana</s>), compactness (<s>saṃghāta</s>), figure (<s>saṃsthāna</s>), bone-joint structure (<s>saṃhanana</s>), touch (<s>sparśa</s>), taste (<s>rasa</s>), smell (<s>gandha</s>), color (<s>varṇa</s>), sequential form (<s>ānupūrvya</s>), heaviness-lightness (<s>gurulaghu</s>), self-harm (<s>upaghāta</s>), harm-to-others (<s>paraghāta</s>), radiance (<s>ātapa</s>), lustre (<s>udyota</s>), respiration (<s>ucchvāsa</s>), and locomotion (<s>vihāyogati</s>); individual body (<s>pratyekaśarīra</s>), mobile (<s>trasa</s>), beloved (<s>subhaga</s>), attractive voice (<s>susvara</s>), beautiful (<s>śubha</s>), subtle (<s>sūkṣma</s>), fully developed (<s>paryāpti</s>), stable (<s>sthira</s>), attractive (<s>ādeya</s>), fame and glory (<s>yaśaḥkīrti</s>), and their opposites; and <s>tīrthakaratva</s> (the status of a ford-maker). ||

children.text: § 755. yad udayātmā bhavāntaraṃ gacchati sā gatiḥ. sā carturvidhā — narakagatis tiryaggatir manuṣyagatir devagatiś ceti. yan nimitta ātmano nārako bhāvas tan narakagatināma. evaṃ śeṣv api yojyam. tāsu narakādigatiṣv avyabhicāriṇā sādṛśyenaikīkṛto ’rthātmā jātiḥ. tannimittaṃ jātināma. tatpañcavidham — ekendriyajātināma dvīndriyajātināma trīndriyajātināma caturindriyajātināma pañcendriyajātināma ceti. yad udayād ātmā ekendriya iti śabdyate tad ekendriyajātināma. evaṃ śeṣv api yojyam. yad udayād ātmanaḥ śarīranirvṛttis tac charīranāma. tat pañcavidham — audārikaśarīranāma vaikriyikaśarīranāma āhārakaśarīranāma taijasaśarīranāma kārmaṇaśarīranāma ceti. teṣāṃ viśeṣo vyākhyātaḥ. yad udayād āṅgopāṅgavivekas tad āṅgopāṅganāma. tat trividham — audārikaśarīrāṅgopāṅganāma vaikriyikaśarīrāṅgopāṅganāma āhārakaśarīrāṅgopāṅganāma ceti. yan nimittāt pariniṣpattis tan nirmāṇam. tad dvividhaḥ — sthānanirmāṇaṃ pramāṇanirmāṇaṃ ceti. tajjātināmodayāpekṣaṃ cakṣurādīnāṃ sthānaṃ pramāṇaṃ ca nirvartayati. nirmīyate ’neneti nirmāṇam. śarīranamakarmodayavaśād upāttānāṃ pudgalānām anyonyapradeśasaṃśleṣaṇaṃ yato bhavati tad bandhananāma. yadudayād audārikādiśarīrāṇāṃ vivaravirahitānyo ’nyapradeśānupraveśena ekatvāpādanaṃ bhavati satsaṃghātanāma. yad udayād audārikādisarīrākṛtinirvṛttir bhavati tat saṃsthānanāma. tat ṣoḍhā vibhajyate — samacaturasrasaṃsthānanāma nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalasaṃsthānanāma svātisaṃsthānanāma kubjasaṃsthānanāma vāmanasaṃsthānanāma huṇḍasaṃsthānanāma ceti. yasyodayāt asthibandhanaviśeṣo bhavati tatsaṃhanananāma. tat ṣaḍvidham — vajrarṣabhanārācasaṃhanananāma vajranārācasaṃhanananāma nārācasaṃhanananāma ardhanārācasaṃhanananāma kīlikāsaṃhanananāma asaṃprāptāsṛpāṭikāsaṃhanananāma ceti. yasyodayāt sparśaprādurbhāvas tat sparśanāma. tad aṣṭavidham — karkaśanāma mṛdunāma gurunāma laghunāma snigdhanāma rūkṣanāma śītanāma uṣṇanāma ceti. yan nimitto rasavikalpas tad rasanāma. tat pañcavidham — tiktanāma kaṭukanāma kaṣāyanāma āmlanāma madhuranāma ceti. yad udayaprabhavo gandhas tad gandhanāma. tad dvividham — surabhigandhanāma asurabhigandhanāma ceti. yad dhetuko varṇavibhāgas tad varṇanāma. tat paṃcavidham — kṛṣṇavarṇanāma nīlavarṇanāma raktavarṇanāma hāridravaṛnanāma śuklavarṇanāma ceti. pūrvaśarīrākārāvināśo yasyodayād bhavati tad ānupūrvyanāma. tac caturvidham — narakagatiprāyogyānupūrvyanāma tiryaggatiprāyogyānupūrvyanāma manuṣyagatiprāyogyānupūrvyanāma devagatiprāyogyānupūrvyanāma ceti. yasyodayād ayaḥpiṇḍavad gurutvān nādhaḥ patati na cārkatūlavallaghutvād ūrdhvaṃ gacchati tad gurulaghunāma. yasyodayāt svayaṃkṛtodbandhanamaruprapatanādinimitta upaghāto bhavati tad upaghātanāma. yannimittaḥ paraśastrāder vyāghātas tat paraghātanāma. yadudayān nirvṛttam ātapanaṃ tadātapanama. tadāditye vartate. yan nimittam udyotananaṃ tad udyotanāma. tac candrakhadyotādiṣu vartate. yaddhetur ucchvāsas tad ucchvāsanāma. vihāya ākāśam. tatra gatinirvartakaṃ tad vihāyogatināma. tad dvividham — praśastāpraśastabhedāt. śarīranāmakarmodayān nirvartyamānaṃ śarīram ekātmopabhogakāraṇaṃ yato bhavati tat pratyekaśarīranāma. bahūnām ātmanām upabhogahetutvena sādhāraṇaṃ śarīraṃ yato bhavati tat sādhāraṇaśarīranāma. yadudayād dvīndriyādiṣu janma tat trasanāma. yannimitta ekendriyeṣu prādurbhāvas tat sthāvaranāma. yadudayād anyaprītiprabhavas tat subhaganāma. yadudayād rūpādiguṇopeto ’py aprītikaras tad durbhaganāma. yannimittaṃ manojñasvaranirvartanaṃ tat susvaranāma. tadviparītaṃ duḥsvaranāma. yad udayād ramaṇīyatvaṃ tac chubhanāma. tadviparītaṃ aśubhanāma. sūkṣmaśarīranirvartakaṃ sūkṣmanāma. anyabādhākaraśarīrakāraṇaṃ bādaranāma. yadudayād āhārādiparyāptinirvṛttiḥ tat paryāptināma. tat ṣaḍvidham — āhāraparyāptināma śarīraparyāptināma indriyaparyāptināma prāṇāpanaparyāptināma bhāṣāparyāptināma manaḥparyāptināma ceti. ṣaḍvidhaparyāptyabhāvahetur aparyāptināma. sthirabhāvasya nirvartakaṃ sthiranāma. tadviparītam asthiranāma. prabhopetaśarīrakāraṇam ādeyanāma. niṣprabhaśarīrakāraṇam anādeyanāma. puṇyaguṇakhyāpanakāraṇaṃ yaśaḥkīrtināma. tatpratyanīkaphalam ayaśaḥkīrtināma. ārhantyakāraṇaṃ tīrthakaratvanāma.
children.translated_text: Section 755. That by whose [fruition] the soul goes to another existence is <s>gati</s> (destiny). It is fourfold: hellish destiny (<s>narakagati</s>), animal destiny (<s>tiryaggati</s>), human destiny (<s>manuṣyagati</s>), and celestial destiny (<s>devagati</s>). That on account of which the soul has a hellish state is the hellish destiny <s>nāma</s> [karma]. Similarly in the rest as well. In those destinies of hell and so forth, the essential nature unified through invariable resemblance is <s>jāti</s> (birth-class). The corresponding <s>nāma</s> karma is called <s>jātināma</s>. It is fivefold: one-sensed birth-class <s>nāma</s>, two-sensed birth-class <s>nāma</s>, three-sensed birth-class <s>nāma</s>, four-sensed birth-class <s>nāma</s>, and five-sensed birth-class <s>nāma</s>. That by whose fruition the soul is designated as 'one-sensed' is the one-sensed birth-class <s>nāma</s>. Similarly in the rest. That by whose fruition the body of the soul is produced is <s>śarīranāma</s> (body name-karma). It is fivefold: <s>audārikaśarīranāma</s> (gross body), <s>vaikriyikaśarīranāma</s> (transformable body), <s>āhārakaśarīranāma</s> (assimilative body), <s>taijasaśarīranāma</s> (luminous body), and <s>kārmaṇaśarīranāma</s> (karmic body). Their distinctions have been explained. That by whose fruition the differentiation of limbs and minor limbs occurs is <s>āṅgopāṅganāma</s>. It is threefold: gross body limbs <s>nāma</s>, transformable body limbs <s>nāma</s>, and assimilative body limbs <s>nāma</s>. That on account of which completion [of the body] occurs is <s>nirmāṇa</s> (formation). It is twofold: formation of placement (<s>sthānanirmāṇa</s>) and formation of proportion (<s>pramāṇanirmāṇa</s>). Depending on the fruition of the respective birth-class <s>nāma</s>, it produces the placement and proportion of the eyes and other [organs]. <s>Nirmāṇa</s> means 'that by which [the body] is formed.' That by which the mutual interpenetration of spatial units of the material particles taken up through the fruition of body <s>nāma</s> karma occurs is <s>bandhananāma</s> (binding name-karma). That by whose fruition the gross and other bodies achieve unity through the interpenetration of one another's spatial units without gaps is <s>saṃghātanāma</s> (compactness name-karma). That by whose fruition the shape of the gross and other bodies is produced is <s>saṃsthānanāma</s> (figure name-karma). It is divided sixfold: symmetrical (<s>samacaturasra</s>), <s>nyagrodhaparimaṇḍala</s> (banyan-shaped), <s>svāti</s> (tapering), hunchbacked (<s>kubja</s>), dwarf (<s>vāmana</s>), and misshapen (<s>huṇḍa</s>). That by whose fruition a special configuration of bone-joints occurs is <s>saṃhanananāma</s> (bone-joint name-karma). It is sixfold: <s>vajraṛṣabhanārāca</s> (adamantine-bull-tubular), <s>vajranārāca</s> (adamantine-tubular), <s>nārāca</s> (tubular), <s>ardhanārāca</s> (half-tubular), <s>kīlikā</s> (riveted), and <s>asaṃprāptāsṛpāṭikā</s> (non-interlocking). That by whose fruition touch manifests is <s>sparśanāma</s> (touch name-karma). It is eightfold: hard (<s>karkaśa</s>), soft (<s>mṛdu</s>), heavy (<s>guru</s>), light (<s>laghu</s>), smooth (<s>snigdha</s>), rough (<s>rūkṣa</s>), cold (<s>śīta</s>), and hot (<s>uṣṇa</s>). That on account of which variation in taste occurs is <s>rasanāma</s> (taste name-karma). It is fivefold: bitter (<s>tikta</s>), pungent (<s>kaṭuka</s>), astringent (<s>kaṣāya</s>), sour (<s>āmla</s>), and sweet (<s>madhura</s>). That from whose fruition smell arises is <s>gandhanāma</s> (smell name-karma). It is twofold: pleasant smell (<s>surabhigandha</s>) and unpleasant smell (<s>asurabhigandha</s>). That which causes the differentiation of color is <s>varṇanāma</s> (color name-karma). It is fivefold: black (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>), blue (<s>nīla</s>), red (<s>rakta</s>), yellow (<s>hāridra</s>), and white (<s>śukla</s>). That by whose fruition the non-destruction of the previous body's form occurs is <s>ānupūrvyanāma</s> (sequential-form name-karma). It is fourfold: hellish destiny sequential-form, animal destiny sequential-form, human destiny sequential-form, and celestial destiny sequential-form. That by whose fruition [the soul], like an iron ball, neither falls downward due to heaviness nor rises upward due to lightness like cotton, is <s>gurulaghunāma</s> (heaviness-lightness name-karma). That by whose fruition self-harm occurs through self-inflicted hanging, falling from heights, and the like is <s>upaghātanāma</s> (self-harm name-karma). That on account of which the assault of weapons and the like by others occurs is <s>paraghātanāma</s> (harm-by-others name-karma). That by whose fruition radiance is produced is <s>ātapanāma</s> (radiance name-karma). That exists in the sun. That on account of which illumination occurs is <s>udyotanāma</s> (lustre name-karma). That exists in the moon, fireflies, and the like. That which causes respiration is <s>ucchvāsanāma</s> (respiration name-karma). <s>Vihāya</s> means 'space'; that which produces movement therein is <s>vihāyogatināma</s> (locomotion name-karma). It is twofold, due to the division into praiseworthy and unpraiseworthy. That by which the body produced through the fruition of body <s>nāma</s> karma becomes the cause of enjoyment for a single soul is <s>pratyekaśarīranāma</s> (individual body name-karma). That by which a body becomes common as the cause of enjoyment for many souls is <s>sādhāraṇaśarīranāma</s> (common body name-karma). That by whose fruition birth occurs among two-sensed and higher beings is <s>trasanāma</s> (mobile name-karma). That on account of which manifestation occurs among one-sensed beings is <s>sthāvaranāma</s> (immobile name-karma). That by whose fruition delight in others is produced is <s>subhaganāma</s> (beloved name-karma). That by whose fruition one, though endowed with qualities of beauty and the like, causes displeasure is <s>durbhaganāma</s> (disliked name-karma). That on account of which a pleasing voice is produced is <s>susvaranāma</s> (attractive-voice name-karma). Its opposite is <s>duḥsvaranāma</s> (repulsive-voice name-karma). That by whose fruition there is attractiveness is <s>śubhanāma</s> (beautiful name-karma). Its opposite is <s>aśubhanāma</s> (ugly name-karma). That which produces a subtle body is <s>sūkṣmanāma</s> (subtle name-karma). That which causes a body capable of obstructing others is <s>bādaranāma</s> (gross name-karma). That by whose fruition the completion of nourishment and the like occurs is <s>paryāptināma</s> (full-development name-karma). It is sixfold: nourishment-completion (<s>āhāraparyāpti</s>), body-completion (<s>śarīraparyāpti</s>), sense-organ-completion (<s>indriyaparyāpti</s>), respiration-completion (<s>prāṇāpānaparyāpti</s>), speech-completion (<s>bhāṣāparyāpti</s>), and mind-completion (<s>manaḥparyāpti</s>). That which causes the absence of sixfold completion is <s>aparyāptināma</s> (undeveloped name-karma). That which produces a stable condition is <s>sthiranāma</s> (stable name-karma). Its opposite is <s>asthiranāma</s> (unstable name-karma). That which causes a body endowed with splendor is <s>ādeyanāma</s> (attractive name-karma). That which causes a body devoid of splendor is <s>anādeyanāma</s> (unattractive name-karma). That which causes the manifestation of meritorious qualities and fame is <s>yaśaḥkīrtināma</s> (fame-and-glory name-karma). That which produces the opposite result is <s>ayaśaḥkīrtināma</s> (infamy name-karma). That which causes the status of an <s>Arhat</s> is <s>tīrthakaratvanāma</s> (ford-maker name-karma).

children.text: § 756. ukto nāmakarmaṇa uttaraprakṛtibhedaḥ. tadanantaroddeśabhājo gotrasya prakṛtibhedo vyākhyāyate —
children.translated_text: Section 756. The sub-types of <s>nāmakarma</s> (name-determining karma) have been stated. The sub-type division of <s>gotra</s> (lineage-determining karma), which is the next in the enumeration, is now explained —

children.text: uccairnīcaiś ca ||
children.translated_text: High (<s>uccais</s>) and low (<s>nīcais</s>). ||

children.text: § 757. gotraṃ dvividham — uccairgotraṃ nīcairgotram iti. yasyodayāl lokapūjiteṣu kuleṣu janma tac uccairgotram. yadudayād garhiteṣu kuleṣu janma tan nīcairgotram.
children.translated_text: Section 757. <s>Gotra</s> (lineage-determining karma) is twofold: <s>uccairgotra</s> (high lineage) and <s>nīcairgotra</s> (low lineage). That by whose fruition birth occurs in families honored by the world is <s>uccairgotra</s>. That by whose fruition birth occurs in despised families is <s>nīcairgotra</s>.

children.text: § 758. aṣṭamyāḥ karmaprakṛter uttaraprakṛtinirdeśārtham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 758. In order to indicate the sub-types of the eighth type of <s>karma</s>, he says —

children.text: dānalābhabhogopabhogavīryāṇām ||
children.translated_text: Of giving (<s>dāna</s>), gain (<s>lābha</s>), enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>), repeated enjoyment (<s>upabhoga</s>), and energy (<s>vīrya</s>). ||

children.text: § 759. antarāyāpekṣayā bhedanirdeśaḥ kriyate — dānasyāntarāyo lobhasyāntarāya ity ādi. dānādipariṇāmavyāghātahetutvāt tad vyapadeśaḥ. yadudayād dātukāmo ’pi na prayacchati, labdhukāmo ’pi na labhate, bhoktum icchann api na bhuṅkte, upabhoktum abhivāñchann api nopabhuṅkte, utsahitukāmo ’pi notsahate ta ete pañcāntarāyasya bhedāḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 759. The specification of sub-types is made with reference to <s>antarāya</s> (obstructive karma): obstruction of giving, obstruction of gain, and so forth. The designation is due to its being the cause of obstructing the fruition of giving and the rest. That by whose fruition one, though wishing to give, does not give; though wishing to gain, does not gain; though wishing to enjoy, does not enjoy; though wishing to experience repeatedly, does not experience; though wishing to exert energy, does not exert — these are the five sub-types of <s>antarāya</s> (obstructive karma).

children.text: § 760. vyākhyātāḥ prakṛtibandhavikalpāḥ. idānīṃ sthitibandhavikalpo vaktavyaḥ. sā sthitir dvividhā — utkṛṣṭā jaghanyā ca. tatra yāsāṃ karmaprakṛtīṇām utkṛṣṭā sthitiḥ samānā tannirdeśārtham ucyate —
children.translated_text: Section 760. The varieties of <s>prakṛtibandha</s> (bondage by type) have been explained. Now the variety of <s>sthitibandha</s> (bondage by duration) is to be stated. That duration is twofold: maximum (<s>utkṛṣṭā</s>) and minimum (<s>jaghanyā</s>). Among these, in order to indicate those types of <s>karma</s> whose maximum duration is the same, it is said —

children.text: āditas tisṛṇām antarāyasya ca triṃśatsāgaropamakoṭīkoṭyaḥ parā sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The maximum duration of the first three [types] and of <s>antarāya</s> (obstructive karma) is thirty <s>koṭīkoṭi</s> (crores of crores) <s>sāgaropamas</s> (ocean-measured time units). ||

children.text: § 761. madhye ’nte vā tisṛṇām grahaṇaṃ mābhūd iti ‘āditaḥ’ ity ucyate. ‘antarāyasya’ iti vacanaṃ vyavahitagrahaṇārtham. sāgaropamam uktaparimāṇam. koṭīṇāṃ koṭyaḥ koṭīkoṭyaḥ. para utkṛṣṭety arthaḥ. etad uktaṃ bhavati — jñānāvaraṇadarśanāvaraṇavedanīyāntarāyāṇām utkṛṣṭā sthitis triṃśatsāgaropamakoṭīkoṭya iti. sā kasya bhavati? mithyādṛṣṭeḥ saṃjñinaḥ paṃcendriyasya paryaptikasya. anyeṣām āgamāt saṃpratyayaḥ kartavyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 761. The word 'from the beginning' (āditaḥ) is stated so that the inclusion of the three [karmas] should not be from the middle or the end. The mention of '<s>antarāya</s>' (obstructive karma) is for the purpose of including what is separated [in the list]. The <s>sāgaropama</s> (ocean-measured time unit) is of the stated measure. <s>Koṭīkoṭi</s> means crores of crores. 'Para' means maximum. What is stated amounts to this: the maximum duration (<s>sthiti</s>) of <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring), <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s> (perception-obscuring), <s>vedanīya</s> (feeling-producing), and <s>antarāya</s> (obstructive) karmas is thirty <s>koṭīkoṭi</s> <s>sāgaropamas</s>. To whom does this apply? To one of wrong faith (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), possessing mind (<s>saṃjñin</s>), five-sensed, and fully developed (<s>paryāptaka</s>). For others, conviction should be formed from scripture.

children.text: § 762. mohanīyasyotkṛṣṭasthitipratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 762. In order to ascertain the maximum duration of <s>mohanīya</s> (deluding karma), he states —

children.text: saptatir mohanīyasya ||
children.translated_text: Seventy [<s>koṭīkoṭi</s> <s>sāgaropamas</s>] for <s>mohanīya</s> (deluding karma).

children.text: § 763. ‘sāgaropamakoṭīkoṭyaḥ parā sthitiḥ’ ity anuvartate. iyam api parā sthitir mithyādṛṣṭeḥ saṃjñinaḥ paṃcendriyasya paryāptakasyāvaseyā. itareṣāṃ yathāgamam avagamaḥ kartavyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 763. The phrase '<s>sāgaropama</s> <s>koṭīkoṭis</s> is the maximum duration' continues [from the previous sūtra]. This maximum duration too should be understood as applying to one of wrong faith (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), possessing mind, five-sensed, and fully developed. For others, understanding should be formed according to scripture.

children.text: § 764. nāmagotrayor utkṛṣṭasthitipratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 764. In order to ascertain the maximum duration of <s>nāma</s> (name-determining) and <s>gotra</s> (lineage-determining) karmas, he states —

children.text: viṃśatir nāmagotrayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Twenty [<s>koṭīkoṭi</s> <s>sāgaropamas</s>] for <s>nāma</s> and <s>gotra</s>.

children.text: § 765. ‘sāgaropamakoṭīkoṭyaḥ para sthitiḥ’ ity anuvartate. iyam api utkṛṣṭā sthitir mithyādṛṣṭeḥ saṃjñipaṃcendriyaparyāptakasya. itareṣāṃ yathāgamam avaboddhavyā.
children.translated_text: Section 765. The phrase '<s>sāgaropama</s> <s>koṭīkoṭis</s> is the maximum duration' continues. This maximum duration too belongs to one of wrong faith, five-sensed with mind, and fully developed. For others, it should be understood according to scripture.

children.text: § 766. athāyuṣaḥ kotkṛṣṭā sthitir ity ucyate —
children.translated_text: Section 766. Now the maximum duration of <s>āyuṣ</s> (life-span determining karma) is stated —

children.text: trayastriṃśatsāgaropamāṇy āyuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s> for <s>āyuṣ</s> (life-span determining karma).

children.text: § 767. punaḥ ‘sāgaropama’ grahaṇaṃ koṭīkoṭīnivṛttyartham. ‘parā sthitiḥ’ ity anuvartate. iyam api pūvoktasyaiva. śeṣāṇām āgamato ’vaseyā.
children.translated_text: Section 767. The word '<s>sāgaropama</s>' is repeated here to exclude <s>koṭīkoṭi</s> [as a unit]. The phrase 'maximum duration' continues. This too applies to the one described previously. For the rest, it should be understood from scripture.

children.text: § 768. uktotkṛṣṭā sthitiḥ. idānīṃ jaghanyā sthitir vaktavyā. tatra samānajaghanyasthitīḥ paṃca prakṛtīr avasthāpya tisṛṇāṃ jaghanyasthitipratipattyarthaṃ sūtradvayam upanasyate laghvartham —
children.translated_text: Section 768. The maximum duration has been stated. Now the minimum duration is to be stated. Having set aside five types (<s>prakṛtis</s>) that share the same minimum duration, two sūtras are introduced for the sake of brevity, to ascertain the minimum duration of three [types] —

children.text: aparā dvādaśa muhūrtā vedanīyasya ||
children.translated_text: The minimum [duration] of <s>vedanīya</s> (feeling-producing karma) is twelve <s>muhūrtas</s>.

children.text: § 769. aparā jaghanyā ity arthaḥ. vedanīyasya dvādaśa muhūrtāḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 769. 'Aparā' means minimum. The minimum duration of <s>vedanīya</s> is twelve <s>muhūrtas</s>.

children.text: nāmagotrayor aṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: Eight [<s>muhūrtas</s>] for <s>nāma</s> and <s>gotra</s>.

children.text: § 770. ‘muhūrtā’ ity anuvartate. ‘aparā sthitiḥ’ iti ca.
children.translated_text: Section 770. The word '<s>muhūrtas</s>' continues [from the previous sūtra], as does 'minimum duration.'

children.text: § 771. avasthāpitaprakṛtijaghanyasthitipratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 771. In order to state the minimum duration of the remaining types that were set aside, he says —

children.text: śeṣāṇām antarmuhūrtā ||
children.translated_text: For the rest, [the minimum duration is] less than one <s>muhūrta</s> (<s>antarmuhūrta</s>).

children.text: § 772. śeṣāṇām pañcānāṃ prakṛtīnām antarmuhūrtāparā sthitiḥ. jñānadarśanāvaraṇāntarāyāṇāṃ jaghanyā sthitiḥ sūkṣmasāṃparāye, mohanīyasya anivṛttibādarasāṃparāye. āyuṣaḥ saṃkhyeyavarṣāyuṣṣu tiryakṣu manuṣyeṣu ca.
children.translated_text: Section 772. The minimum duration of the remaining five types is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>. The minimum duration of <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring), <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s> (perception-obscuring), and <s>antarāya</s> (obstructive karmas) applies at the stage of subtle mixed passions (<s>sūkṣmasāṃparāya</s>); that of <s>mohanīya</s> at the stage of gross non-retreating passions (<s>anivṛttibādarasāṃparāya</s>); and that of <s>āyuṣ</s> among animals and humans with a countable number of years of life.

children.text: § 773. āha, ubhayī sthitir abhihitā. jñānāvaraṇādīnām athānubhavaḥ kiṃ lakṣaṇa ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: Section 773. One says: both [maximum and minimum] durations have been stated. Now, as to the experience (<s>anubhava</s>) of <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> and the rest — what is its nature? To this he replies —

children.text: vipāko ’nubhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Fruition (<s>vipāka</s>) is experience (<s>anubhava</s>).

children.text: § 774. viśiṣṭo nānāvidho vā pāko vipākaḥ. puṛvoktakaṣāyatīvramandādibhāvāsravaviśeṣād viśiṣṭaḥ pāko vipākaḥ. athavā dravyakṣetrakālabhavabhāvalakṣaṇanimittabhedajanitavaiśvarūpyo nānāvidhaḥ pāko vipākaḥ. asāv anubhava ity ākhyāyate. śubhapariṇāmānāṃ prakarṣabhāvāc chubhaprakṛtīnāṃ prakṛṣṭo ’nubhavaḥ aśubhaprakṛtīnāṃ nikṛṣṭaḥ. aśubhapariṇāmānāṃ prakarṣabhāvād aśubhaprakṛtīnāṃ prakṛṣṭo ’nubhavaḥ śubhaprakṛtīnāṃ nikṛṣṭaḥ. sa evaṃ pratyayavaśād upātto ’nubhavo dvividhā pravartate svamukhena paramukhena ca. sarvāsāṃ mūlaprakṛtīnāṃ svamukhenaivānubhavaḥ. uttaraprakṛtīnāṃ tulyajātīyānāṃ paramukhenāpi bhavati āyurdarśanacāritramohavarjānām. na hi narakāyurmukhena tiryagāyurmanuṣyāyur vā vipacyate. nāpi darśanamohaś cāritramohamukhena, cāritramoho vā darśanamohamukhena.
children.translated_text: Section 774. A special or manifold ripening is <s>vipāka</s> (fruition). Due to the particular influx (<s>āsrava</s>) characterized by the previously mentioned intense and mild states of <s>kaṣāyas</s> (passions), there is a special ripening, which is <s>vipāka</s>. Alternatively, <s>vipāka</s> is a manifold ripening produced by diversity arising from differences in substance (<s>dravya</s>), place (<s>kṣetra</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), existence (<s>bhava</s>), state (<s>bhāva</s>), characteristic, and cause. This is called <s>anubhava</s> (experience). When wholesome dispositions predominate, the experience of wholesome types is intense and that of unwholesome types is feeble. When unwholesome dispositions predominate, the experience of unwholesome types is intense and that of wholesome types is feeble. This experience, thus acquired through conditions, operates in two ways: through its own channel and through the channel of another. All primary types experience fruition through their own channel only. Among sub-types of the same class, experience through the channel of another also occurs, except for <s>āyus</s> (life-span), <s>darśana</s>-<s>moha</s> (faith-deluding), and <s>cāritra</s>-<s>moha</s> (conduct-deluding karmas). For indeed, animal life-span or human life-span does not ripen through the channel of hellish life-span. Nor does <s>darśanamoha</s> ripen through the channel of <s>cāritramoha</s>, or <s>cāritramoha</s> through the channel of <s>darśanamoha</s>.

children.text: § 775. āha abhyupemaḥ prāgupacitanānāprakārakarmavipāko ’nubhavaḥ. idaṃ tu na vijānīmaḥ kim ayam prasaṃkhyāto ’prasaṃkhyātaḥ? ity atrocyate prasaṃkhyāto ’nubhūyata iti brūmahe. kutaḥ? yataḥ —
children.translated_text: Section 775. One says: we have accepted that experience is the fruition of the various types of karma accumulated previously. But this we do not know — is this [experience] determinate or indeterminate? To this it is replied: we say it is experienced in a determinate manner. Why? Because —

children.text: sa yathānāma ||
children.translated_text: It [i.e., the experience] is according to name (<s>yathānāma</s>).

children.text: § 776. jñānāvaraṇasya phalaṃ jñānābhāvo darśanāvaraṇasyāpi phalaṃ darśanaśaktyuparodha ity evam ādy anvarthasaṃjñānirdeśāt sarvāsāṃ karmaprakṛtīnāṃ savikalpānām anubhavasaṃpratyayo jāyate.
children.translated_text: Section 776. The result of <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring karma) is the absence of knowledge; the result of <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s> (perception-obscuring karma) is the obstruction of the faculty of perception — thus, from the indication through meaningful names, conviction regarding the experience of all types of <s>karma</s>, including their sub-varieties, is established.
