children.text: § 835. ajño ’yaṃ na vetti paśusama ity evam ādy adhikeṣpavacanaṃ sahamānasya paramaduścaratapo ’nuṣṭhāyino nityam apramattacetaso me ’dyāpi jñānātiśayo notpadyata iti anabhisaṃdadhato ’jñānapariṣahajayo ’vagantavyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 835. For one who endures words of excessive reproach such as 'He is ignorant, he knows nothing, he is like an animal'; who practices supremely difficult austerities; whose mind is always free from negligence; who does not harbor the thought 'Even now no special knowledge has arisen in me' — the conquest of the ignorance-affliction (<s>ajñānapariṣaha</s>) should be understood.

children.text: § 836. paramavairāgyabhāvanāśuddhahṛdayasya viditasakalapadārthatattvasyārhadāyatanasadhudharmapūjakasya cirantanapravrajitasyādyāpi me jñānātiśayo notpadyate. mahopavāsādyanuṣṭhāyināṃ prātihāryaviśeṣāḥ prādur abhūvann iti pralāpamātram anarthikeyaṃ pravrajyā. viphalaṃ vrataparipālanam ity evam asamādadhānasya darśanaviśuddhiyogād adarśanapariṣahasahanam avasātavyam.
children.translated_text: Section 836. For one whose heart is purified by the contemplation of supreme dispassion; who has comprehended the reality of all categories; who worships the <s>Jina</s>-temple and the dharma of the saints; who has been a renunciant for a long time — [yet the thought arises:] 'Even now no special knowledge has arisen in me. Those who performed great fasts and other practices manifested special miraculous powers (<s>prātihārya</s>) — [therefore] this is mere idle talk; this renunciation is purposeless; the observance of vows is fruitless.' For one who does not entertain such thoughts, through the power of purity of faith — the endurance of the non-perception affliction (<s>adarśanapariṣaha</s>) should be ascertained.

children.text: § 837. evaṃ pariṣahān asaṃkalpopasthitān sahamānasyāsaṃkliṣṭacetaso rāgādipariṇāmāsravanirodhān mahān saṃvaro bhavati.
children.translated_text: Section 837. Thus, for one who endures the afflictions that present themselves unsought, with an unafflicted mind, there arises great <s>saṃvara</s> (stoppage of karmic influx) through the cessation of the influx caused by dispositions of attachment and the like.

children.text: § 838. āha, kim ime pariṣahāḥ sarve saṃsāramahāṭavīm atikramitum abhyudyatam abhidravanti uta kaścit prativiśeṣa ity atrocyate — amī vyākhyātalakṣaṇāḥ kṣudādayaś cāritrāntarāṇi prati bhājyāh. niyamena punaranayoḥ pratyetavyāḥ —
children.translated_text: Section 838. One asks: do all these afflictions assail one who has set out to cross the great forest of <s>saṃsāra</s>, or is there some specific [distribution]? To this it is replied: these afflictions, whose characteristics have been explained — hunger and the rest — are to be distributed among the different stages of conduct. However, for these two [stages] they must be specifically understood —

children.text: sūkṣmasāṃparāyachadmasthavītarāgayoś caturdaśa ||
children.translated_text: For one at the stage of subtle mixed passions (<s>sūkṣmasāṃparāya</s>) and for the omniscient-but-still-embodied (<s>chadmasthavītarāga</s>), [there are] fourteen. ||

children.text: § 839. kṣutpipāsāśītoṣṇadaṃśamaśakacaryāśayyāvadhālābharogatṛṇasparśamalaprajñājñānāni. ‘caturdaśa’ iti vacanād anyeṣāṃ pariṣahāṇām abhāvo veditavyaḥ. āha yuktaṃ tāvad vītarāgachadmasthe mohanīyābhāvāt tatkṛtavakṣyamāṇāṣṭapariṣahābhāvāc caturdaśaniyamavacanam. sūkṣmasāṃparāye tu mohodayasadbhāvāt ‘caturdaśa’ iti niyamo nopapadyata iti? tad ayuktam; sanmātratvāt. tatra hi kevalo lobhasaṃjvalanakaṣāyodayaḥ so ’py atisūkṣmaḥ. tato vītarāgachadmasthakalpatvāt ‘caturdaśa’ iti niyamas tatrāpi yujyate. nanu mohodayasahāyābhāvān mandodayayatvāc ca kṣudādivedanābhāvāt tatsahanakṛtapariṣahavyapadeśo na yuktim avatarati. tan na? kiṃ kāraṇam.
śaktimatrasya vivakṣitatvāt. sarvārthasiddhidevasya saptamapṛthivīgamanasāmarthyavyapadeśāvat.
children.translated_text: Because what is intended is merely the capacity [to endure]. Just as the being in <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s> heaven is described as having the power to go to the seventh hell [though he does not actually go].

Section 839. [These fourteen are:] hunger, thirst, cold, heat, gadfly-and-mosquito, wandering, sleep, assault, non-obtaining, disease, grass-contact, filth, wisdom, and ignorance. From the statement 'fourteen,' the absence of the remaining afflictions should be understood. One objects: the restriction to fourteen is reasonable for the passionless-but-still-embodied (<s>vītarāgachadmastha</s>), since due to the absence of <s>mohanīya</s> (deluding karma), the eight afflictions to be mentioned that are caused by it would be absent. But for the <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāya</s> stage, since the rise of <s>moha</s> does exist, the restriction to 'fourteen' is not justified? That is not correct; because [the moha] exists only in a mere trace. For there, only the rise of the <s>saṃjvalana</s> (blazing) sub-type of the passion of greed occurs, and even that is extremely subtle. Therefore, since [this stage] is virtually equivalent to the passionless-but-still-embodied, the restriction to 'fourteen' is justified there too. But surely, since there is no assistance from the rise of <s>moha</s>, and since the rise is feeble, the sensations of hunger and the like would be absent, and therefore the designation of 'affliction' based on their endurance would not be logically tenable? Not so. Why?

children.text: § 840. āha, yadi śarīravaty ātmani pariṣahasaṃnidhānaṃ pratijñāyate atha bhavati utpannakevalajñāne karmacatuṣṭayaphalānubhavanavaśavartini kiyanta upanipatantīty atrocyate. tasmin punaḥ —
children.translated_text: Section 840. One asks: if the presence of pariṣahas (afflictions to be endured) is accepted in the embodied soul, then how many afflictions befall one in whom kevalajñāna (omniscient knowledge) has arisen and who is subject to experiencing the fruits of the four [remaining] types of karma? To this it is replied. In that [omniscient being] again —

children.text: ekādaśa jine ||
children.translated_text: Eleven [pariṣahas] in the <s>Jina</s> (conqueror). ||

children.text: § 841. nirastaghātikarmacatuṣṭaye jine vedanīyasadbhāvāt tadāsrayā ekādaśapariṣahāḥ saṃti. nanu ca mohanīyodayasahāyābhāvāt kṣudādivedanābhāve pariṣahavyapadeśo na yuktaḥ? satyam evam etat — vedanābhāve ’pi dravyakarmasadbhāvāpekṣayā pariṣahopacāraḥ kriyate, niravaśeṣanirastajñānātiśaye cintānirodhābhāve ’pi tatphalakarma nirharaṇaphalāpekṣayā dhyānopacāravat. athavā — ekādaśa jine ‘na saṃti’ iti vākyaśeṣaḥ kalpanīyaḥ, sopaskāratvāt sūtrāṇām.
kalpyo hi vākyaśeṣo vākyaṃ ca vaktary adhīnam
children.translated_text: For indeed, the completion of a sentence is to be supplied, and a sentence is dependent on the speaker,

children.text: ity upagamāt. mohodayasahāyīkṛtakṣudādivedanābhāvāt ‘na santi’ iti vākyaśeṣaḥ.
children.translated_text: — by this acceptance [the alternative reading is justified]. Due to the absence of experience of hunger and the like, which is dependent on the fruition of <s>moha</s> (delusion), 'do not exist' is the sentence-completion.

Section 841. In the <s>Jina</s>, who has eliminated the four types of destructive (<s>ghātika</s>) karma, due to the existence of <s>vedanīya</s> (feeling-producing karma), eleven <s>pariṣahas</s> dependent on it exist. But is it not inappropriate to designate them as <s>pariṣahas</s> when there is no experience of hunger and the like due to the absence of the assistance of the fruition of <s>mohanīya</s> (deluding karma)? True, this is so — but even in the absence of [actual] experience, the figurative designation of <s>pariṣaha</s> is made with reference to the existence of <s>dravyakarma</s> (material karma), just as the figurative designation of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is applied with reference to the karma whose fruit is the removal [of obstacles], even when there is no cessation of thought in one whose excellence of knowledge has been completely cleared. Alternatively, 'eleven in the <s>Jina</s>' should be completed with 'do not exist' (na santi), since the sūtras require supplementary completion.

children.text: § 842. āha, yadi sūkṣmasāṃparāyādiṣu vyastāḥ pariṣahāḥ atha samastāḥ tāḥ kveti —
children.translated_text: Section 842. One asks: if the <s>pariṣahas</s> are distributed individually in the stages beginning with <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāya</s> (subtle passions), then where are they all present together? —

children.text: bādarasāṃparāye sarve ||
children.translated_text: All [<s>pariṣahas</s> are present] in the stage of gross passions (<s>bādarasāṃparāya</s>). ||

children.text: § 843. sāṃparāyaḥ kaṣāyaḥ. bādaraḥ sāṃparāyo yasya sa bādarasāṃparāya iti. nedaṃ guṇasthānaviśeṣagrahaṇam. kiṃ tarhi? arthanirdeśaḥ. tena pramattādīnāṃ saṃyatānāṃ grahaṇam. teṣu hi akṣīṇakaṣāyadoṣatvāt sarve saṃbhavanti. kasmin punaś cāritre sarveṣāṃ saṃbhavaḥ? sāmāyikacchedopasthāpanaparihāraviśuddhisaṃyameṣu pratyekaṃ sarveṣāṃ saṃbhavaḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 843. <s>Sāṃparāya</s> means passion (<s>kaṣāya</s>). One whose <s>sāṃparāya</s> is gross (<s>bādara</s>) is called <s>bādarasāṃparāya</s>. This is not a reference to a specific stage of spiritual development (<s>guṇasthāna</s>). What then? It is a statement of meaning. By this, the restrained ones (<s>saṃyatas</s>) beginning with the negligent (<s>pramatta</s>) are included. For in them, since the defect of undiminished passions remains, all [<s>pariṣahas</s>] are possible. In which type of conduct, then, is the occurrence of all [<s>pariṣahas</s>] possible? In each of the [types of] conduct — <s>sāmāyika</s> (equanimity), <s>cchedopasthāpana</s> (reinitiation), <s>parihāraviśuddhi</s> (purificatory restraint), and <s>saṃyama</s> (complete restraint) — the occurrence of all is possible.

children.text: § 844. āha, gṛhītam etat pariṣahāṇāṃ sthānaviśeṣāvadhāraṇaṃ, idaṃ tu na vidmaḥ kasyāḥ prakṛteḥ kaḥ kārya ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: Section 844. One says: we have understood this determination of the specific stages of the <s>pariṣahas</s>; but we do not know which [<s>pariṣaha</s>] is the effect of which type of karma — to this it is replied —

children.text: jñānāvaraṇe prajñājñāne ||
children.translated_text: [The <s>pariṣahas</s> of] wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) [belong to] <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring karma). ||

children.text: § 845. idam ayuktam vartate. kim atrāyuktam? jñānāvaraṇe satyajñānapariṣaha upapadyate, prajñāpariṣahaḥ punas tadapāye bhavatīti kathaṃ jñānāvaraṇe syāt? ity atrocyate — kṣāyopaśamikī prajñā anyasmin jñānāvaraṇe sati madaṃ janayati na sakalāvaraṇakṣaye iti jñānāvaraṇe satīty upapadyate.
children.translated_text: Section 845. This appears illogical. What is illogical here? When <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring karma) exists, the <s>pariṣaha</s> of ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) is understandable; but the <s>pariṣaha</s> of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) arises upon its removal — so how can it belong to <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s>? To this it is replied: the wisdom that arises from the partial destruction and partial subsidence (<s>kṣāyopaśamikī</s>) [of knowledge-obscuring karma] generates pride when some other <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> exists, but not upon the complete destruction of all obscuring [karma] — hence 'when <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> exists' is justified.

children.text: § 846. punar aparayo pariṣahayoḥ prakṛtiviśeṣanirdeśārtham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 846. In order to indicate the specific karmic type for two more <s>pariṣahas</s>, he says —

children.text: darśanamohāntarāyayor adarśanālābhau ||
children.translated_text: The [<s>pariṣahas</s> of] non-perception (<s>adarśana</s>) and non-gain (<s>alābha</s>) [belong respectively to] <s>darśanamoha</s> (faith-deluding karma) and <s>antarāya</s> (obstructive karma). ||

children.text:
§ 847. yathāsaṃkhyam abhisaṃbandhaḥ. darśanamohe adarśanapariṣaho, lābhāntarāye alābhapariṣaha iti.
	  āha, yady ādye mohanīyabhede ekaḥ pariṣahaḥ atha dvitīyasmin kati bhavantīty atrocyate —
children.translated_text: Section 847. The connection is according to enumeration: the <s>pariṣaha</s> of non-perception belongs to <s>darśanamoha</s> (faith-deluding karma), and the <s>pariṣaha</s> of non-gain belongs to <s>lābhāntarāya</s> (gain-obstructing karma). One asks: if one <s>pariṣaha</s> belongs to the first division of <s>mohanīya</s>, then how many belong to the second? To this it is replied —

children.text: cāritramohe nāgnyāratistrīniṣadyākrośayācanāsatkārapuraskārāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The [<s>pariṣahas</s> of] celibacy (<s>nāgnya</s>), dissatisfaction (<s>ārati</s>), women (<s>strī</s>), sitting posture (<s>niṣadyā</s>), abuse (<s>ākrośa</s>), begging (<s>yācanā</s>), non-honor (<s>asatkāra</s>), and non-respect (<s>apuraskāra</s>) [belong to] <s>cāritramoha</s> (conduct-deluding karma). ||

children.text: § 848. puṃvedodayādinimittatvān nāgnyādipariṣahāṇāṃ mohodayanimittatvaṃ pratipadyāmahe. niṣadyāpariṣahasya katham? tatrāpi prāṇipīḍāparihārārthatvāt. mohodaye sati prāṇipīḍāpariṇāmaḥ saṃjāyata iti.
children.translated_text: Section 848. Because the <s>pariṣahas</s> of celibacy and the rest are caused by the fruition of <s>puṃveda</s> (masculine sexual inclination) and the like, we understand them to be caused by the fruition of <s>moha</s> (delusion). How is the <s>pariṣaha</s> of sitting posture [included]? Because even in that case, it is for the purpose of avoiding harm to living beings. When the fruition of <s>moha</s> exists, the disposition to harm living beings arises.

children.text: § 849. avaśiṣṭapariṣahaprakṛtiviśeṣapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 849. In order to explain the specific karmic type of the remaining <s>pariṣahas</s>, he says —

children.text: vedanīye śeṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rest [belong to] <s>vedanīya</s> (feeling-producing karma). ||

children.text: § 850. uktā ekādaśa pariṣāhāḥ. tebhyo ’nye śeṣāḥ vedanīye sati ‘bhavanti’ iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. ke punas te? kṣutpipāsāśītoṣṇadaṃśamaśakacaryāśayyāvadharogatṛṇasparśamalapariṣahāḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 850. Eleven <s>pariṣahas</s> have been stated. The rest, other than those, exist 'when <s>vedanīya</s> is present' — this is the sentence-completion. And what are they? The <s>pariṣahas</s> of hunger (<s>kṣut</s>), thirst (<s>pipāsā</s>), cold (<s>śīta</s>), heat (<s>uṣṇa</s>), insect bites (<s>daṃśamaśaka</s>), wandering (<s>caryā</s>), lodging (<s>śayyā</s>), scolding (<s>avadha</s>), disease (<s>roga</s>), grass-pricks (<s>tṛṇasparśa</s>), and dirt (<s>mala</s>).

children.text: § 851 āha, vyākhyātanimittalakṣaṇavikalpāḥ pratyātmani prādurbhavantaḥ kati yugapad avatiṣṭhanta ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: Section 851. One asks: when these [<s>pariṣahas</s>], whose causes, characteristics, and varieties have been explained, arise in an individual, how many occur simultaneously? To this it is replied —

children.text: ekādayo bhājyā yugapad ekasminn aikonaviṃśateḥ ||
children.translated_text: One and more, to be distributed, simultaneously in a single [soul], up to nineteen. ||

children.text: § 852. āṅabhividhyarthaḥ. tena ekonaviṃśatir api kvacit yugapat saṃbavatīty avagamyate. tat katham? iti ced ucyate — śītoṣṇapariṣahayor ekaḥ śayyāniṣadyācaryāṇāṃ cānyatama eva bhavati ekasminn ātmani. kutaḥ? virodhāt. tattrayāṇām apagame yugapad ekātmanītareṣāṃ saṃbhavād ekonaviṃśativikalpā boddhavyāḥ. nanu prajñājñānayor api virodhād yugapad asaṃbhavaḥ? śrutajñānāpekṣayā prajñāpariṣahaḥ avadhijñānādyabhāvāpekṣayā ajñānapariṣaha iti nāsti virodhaḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 852. The prefix 'ā' has the sense of inclusion. Hence it is understood that nineteen too can occur simultaneously in some cases. How is that? If asked, it is replied: of the <s>pariṣahas</s> of cold and heat, only one [can occur at a time]; and of lodging, sitting posture, and wandering, only one [can occur at a time] in a single soul. Why? Due to mutual contradiction. When the three [contradictory pairs] are removed, since the simultaneous occurrence of the remaining [<s>pariṣahas</s>] in a single soul is possible, the variety of nineteen should be understood. But is there not also a contradiction between wisdom and ignorance, preventing their simultaneous occurrence? [No:] the <s>pariṣaha</s> of wisdom applies with reference to <s>śrutajñāna</s> (scriptural knowledge), while the <s>pariṣaha</s> of ignorance applies with reference to the absence of <s>avadhijñāna</s> (clairvoyant knowledge) and the like — hence there is no contradiction.

children.text: § 853. āha, uktā guptisamitidharmānuprekṣāpariṣahajayāḥ saṃvarahetavaḥ pañca. saṃvarahetuś cāritrasaṃjño vaktavya iti tadbhedapradarśanārtham ucyate —
children.translated_text: Section 853. One says: the five causes of <s>saṃvara</s> (stoppage) have been stated — the conquering of <s>guptis</s> (restraints of activity), <s>samitis</s> (carefulness), <s>dharma</s> (virtues), <s>anuprekṣā</s> (contemplation), and <s>pariṣaha</s> (afflictions). And since the cause of <s>saṃvara</s> called conduct (<s>cāritra</s>) is to be explained, in order to display its subdivisions, it is said —

children.text: sāmāyikacchedopasthāpanāparihāraviśuddhisūkṣmasāmparāyayathākhyātam iti cāritram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sāmāyika</s> (equanimity), <s>cchedopasthāpana</s> (reinitiation), <s>parihāraviśuddhi</s> (purificatory restraint), <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāya</s> (subtle passions), and <s>yathākhyāta</s> (conduct as proclaimed) — such is conduct (<s>cāritra</s>). ||

children.text: § 854. atra codyate — daśavidhe dharme saṃyama uktaḥ sa eva cāritram iti punar grahaṇam anarthakam iti? nānarthahakam; dharme ’ntarbhūtam api cāritram ante gṛhyate mokṣaprāpteḥ sakṣātkāraṇam iti jñāpanārtham. sāmāyikam uktam. kva? ‘digdeśānarthadaṇḍaviratisāmāyika — ’ ity atra. tad dvividhaṃ niyatakālam aniyatakālaṃ ca. svādhyāyādi niyatakālam. īryāpathādyaniyatakālam. pramādakṛtānarthaprabandhavilope samyakpratikriyā chedopasthāpanā vikalpanivṛttir vā. pariharaṇaṃ parihāraḥ prāṇivadhān nivṛttiḥ. tena viśiṣṭā śuddhir yasṃims tatparihāraviśuddhicāritram. atiśūkṣmakaṣāyatvāt sūkṣmasāṃparāyacāritram. mohanīyasya niravaśeṣasyopaśamāt kṣayāc ca ātmasvabhāvāvasthāpekṣālakṣaṇaṃ athākhyātacāritram ity ākhyāyate. pūrvacāritrānuṣṭhāyibhir ākhyātaṃ na tatprāptaṃ prāṅmohakṣayopaśamābhyām ity athākhyātam. athaśabdasyānantaryārthavṛttitatvān niravaśeṣamohakṣayopaśamānantaram āvirbhavatīty arthaḥ. ‘yathākhyātam’ iti vā; yathātmasvabhāvo ’vasthitas tathaivākhyātatvāt. ‘iti’ śabdaḥ parisamāptau draṣṭavyaḥ. tato yathākhyātacāritrāt sakalakarmakṣayaparisamāptir bhavtīti jñāpyate. sāmāyikādīnām ānupūrvyavacanam uttarottaraguṇaprakarṣakhyāpanārthaṃ kriyate.
children.translated_text: Section 854. Here it is objected: restraint (<s>saṃyama</s>) was stated under the ten-fold <s>dharma</s>; since that itself is conduct, the repetition is purposeless? It is not purposeless; although conduct is included within <s>dharma</s>, it is mentioned again at the end to indicate that it is the direct cause of attaining <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). <s>Sāmāyika</s> has been stated. Where? In 'abstinence from harming in direction, place, purposeless activities, <s>sāmāyika</s> —' in that context. It is twofold: of fixed duration and of unfixed duration. Study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) and the like are of fixed duration. Walking with care (<s>īryāpatha</s>) and the like are of unfixed duration. The proper remedial action upon the interruption of the continuity of faults caused by negligence is <s>cchedopasthāpana</s> (reinitiation), or the cessation of mental alternatives. Avoidance, namely <s>parihāra</s>, is abstention from killing living beings. The conduct distinguished by that purity is <s>parihāraviśuddhicāritra</s> (purificatory restraint conduct). Due to the extreme subtlety of passions, there is <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāyacāritra</s> (conduct of subtle passions). The conduct characterized by the state of abiding in one's own nature of the soul, arising from the complete subsidence or destruction of <s>mohanīya</s> (deluding karma) without remainder, is called <s>yathākhyātacāritra</s> (conduct as proclaimed). It is called <s>athākhyāta</s> ('then-proclaimed') [alternatively] because it was proclaimed by those who practiced the previous [stages of] conduct but was not attained by them before the subsidence or destruction of <s>moha</s> — since the word 'atha' has the meaning of 'immediately after,' the meaning is that it manifests immediately after the complete destruction or subsidence of <s>moha</s> without remainder. Or [it is called] <s>yathākhyāta</s> because it is proclaimed just as the soul's own nature abides. The word 'iti' is to be understood as indicating completion. From that, it is indicated that from <s>yathākhyāta</s> conduct, the complete destruction of all <s>karma</s> takes place. The sequential statement of <s>sāmāyika</s> and the rest is made to indicate the progressive superiority of each successive [stage].

children.text: § 855. āha, uktaṃ cāritram. tadanantaram uddiṣṭaṃ yat ‘tapasā nirjarā ca’ iti tasyedānīṃ tapaso vidhānaṃ kartavyam ity atrocyate. tad dvividhaṃ bāhyam ābhyantaraṃ ca. tatpratyekaṃ ṣaḍvidham. tatra bāhyabhedapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 855. One says: conduct has been stated. Next, what was enumerated as 'and <s>nirjarā</s> (shedding) through <s>tapas</s> (austerity)' — its prescription of austerity is now to be made. It is of two kinds: external (<s>bāhya</s>) and internal (<s>ābhyantara</s>). Each is sixfold. In order to explain the subdivisions of external [austerity], he says —

children.text: anaśanāvamaudaryavṛttiparisaṃkhyānarasaparityāgaviviktaśayyāsanakāyakleśā bāhyaṃ tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Anaśana</s> (fasting), <s>avamaudarya</s> (reduced diet), <s>vṛttiparisaṃkhyāna</s> (restriction of alms-seeking), <s>rasaparityāga</s> (giving up stimulating food), <s>viviktaśayyāsana</s> (solitary lodging), and <s>kāyakleśa</s> (bodily mortification) are external austerity (<s>bāhyatapaḥ</s>). ||

children.text: § 856. dṛṣṭaphalānapekṣaṃ saṃyamaprasiddhirāgocchedakarmavināśadhyānāgamāvāptyartham anaśanam. saṃyamaprajāgaradoṣapraśamasaṃtoṣasvādhyāyādisukhasiddhyartham avamaudaryam. bhikṣārthino muner ekāgārādiviṣayaḥ saṃkalpaḥ cintāvarodho vṛttiparisaṃkhyānam āśānivṛttyartham avagantavyam. indriyadarpanigrahanidrāvijayasvādhyāyasukhasiddhyādyartho ghṛtādivṛṣyarasaparityāgaś caturthaṃ tapaḥ. śūnyāgārādiṣu vivikteṣu jantupīḍāvirahiteṣu saṃyatasya śayyāsanam ābādhātyayabrahmacaryasvādhyāyadhyānādiprasiddhyarthaṃ kartavyam iti paṃcamaṃ tapaḥ. ātapasthānaṃ vṛkṣamūlanivāso nirāvaraṇaśayanaṃ bahuvidhapratimāsthānam ity evam ādiḥ kāyakleśaḥ tat ṣaṣṭaṃ tapaḥ. tatkim artham? dehaduḥkhatitikṣāsukhānabhiṣvaṅgapravacanaprabhāvanādyartham. pariṣahasyāsya ca ko viśeṣaḥ? yadṛcchayopanipatitaḥ pariṣahaḥ. svayaṃkṛtaḥ kāyakleśaḥ. bāhyatvam asya kutaḥ? bāhyadravyāpekṣatvāt parapratyakṣatvāc ca bāhyatvam.
children.translated_text: Section 856. <s>Anaśana</s> (fasting), without regard for visible results, is for the purpose of accomplishing restraint, the eradication of attachment, the destruction of <s>karma</s>, and the attainment of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and scripture. <s>Avamaudarya</s> (reduced diet) is for the purpose of accomplishing the restraint of alertness, removal of defects, contentment, and the pleasure of study and the like. The resolution of a mendicant seeking alms concerning a single house and the like — the restraint of expectation — is <s>vṛttiparisaṃkhyāna</s> (restriction of alms-seeking), to be understood as serving the cessation of desire. The giving up of stimulating foods such as ghee and the like, serving the purpose of subduing the pride of the senses, conquering sleep, and the pleasure of study — that is the fourth austerity. The lodging and sitting of the restrained one in solitary places such as empty houses and the like, free from harm to creatures — is to be practiced for the purpose of accomplishing freedom from affliction, celibacy, study, and meditation — that is the fifth austerity. Standing in the sun, dwelling at the foot of a tree, sleeping without cover, and various postures of standing meditation — such and the like is <s>kāyakleśa</s> (bodily mortification); that is the sixth austerity. For what purpose? For the purpose of endurance of bodily suffering, non-attachment to comfort, and the glorification of the teaching. And what is the difference between this and the <s>pariṣaha</s> [of the same name]? A <s>pariṣaha</s> befalls one spontaneously; <s>kāyakleśa</s> is self-imposed. Why is it called 'external'? Because it depends on external substances and is perceptible to others, it is external.

children.text: § 857. ābyantaratapobhedapradarśanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 857. In order to display the subdivisions of internal austerity, he says —

children.text: prāyaścittavinayavaiyāvṛttyasvādhyāyavyutsargadhyānāny uttaram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prāyaścitta</s> (expiation), <s>vinaya</s> (reverence), <s>vaiyāvṛttya</s> (service), <s>svādhyāya</s> (study), <s>vyutsarga</s> (renunciation), and <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) constitute the latter [i.e., internal austerity]. ||

children.text: § 858. katham asyābhyantaratvam? manoniyamanārthatvāt. pramādadoṣaparihāraḥ prāyaścittam. pūjyeṣv ādaro vinayaḥ. kāyaceṣṭayā dravyāntareṇa copāsanaṃ vaiyāvṛttyam. jñānabhāvanālasyatyāgaḥ svādhyāyaḥ. ātmātmīyasaṃkalpatyāgo vyutsargaḥ. cittavikṣepatyāgo dhyānam.
children.translated_text: Section 858. How is it internal? Because it is for the purpose of disciplining the mind. The remediation of defects arising from negligence is <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation). Respect toward those worthy of honor is <s>vinaya</s> (reverence). Service through bodily activity and through material means is <s>vaiyāvṛttya</s> (service). The cultivation of knowledge and abandonment of laziness is <s>svādhyāya</s> (study). The abandonment of attachment to the self and what belongs to the self is <s>vyutsarga</s> (renunciation). The abandonment of mental distraction is <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).

children.text: § 859. tadbhedapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 859. In order to explain their subdivisions, he says —

children.text: navacaturdaśapañcadvibhedā yathākramaṃ prāgdhyānāt ||
children.translated_text: They have nine, four, ten, five, and two subdivisions respectively, in order, [up to] before <s>dhyāna</s>. ||

children.text: § 860. ‘yathākramam’ iti vacanān navabhedaṃ prāyaścittam, vinayaś caturvidhaḥ, vaiyāvṛttyaṃ daśavidham, svādhyāyaḥ pañcavidhaḥ, dvibhedo vyutsarga ity abhisaṃbadyate. ‘prāgdhyānāt’ iti vacanaṃ dhyānasya bahuvaktavyatvāt paścād vakṣyata iti.
children.translated_text: Section 860. By the statement 'in order' (<s>yathākramam</s>), it is connected that <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) has nine subdivisions, <s>vinaya</s> (reverence) is fourfold, <s>vaiyāvṛttya</s> (service) is tenfold, <s>svādhyāya</s> (study) is fivefold, and <s>vyutsarga</s> (renunciation) is twofold. The statement 'before <s>dhyāna</s>' indicates that <s>dhyāna</s>, having much to be said about it, will be explained later.

children.text: § 861. ādyasya bhedasvarūpanirjñānārtham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 861. In order to ascertain the nature of the subdivisions of the first [i.e., expiation], he says —

children.text: ālocanapratikramaṇatadubhayavivekavyutsargatapaśchedaparihāropasthāpanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Confession (<s>ālocana</s>), repentance (<s>pratikramaṇa</s>), both combined (<s>tadubhaya</s>), separation (<s>viveka</s>), renunciation (<s>vyutsarga</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), reduction of status (<s>cheda</s>), expulsion (<s>parihāra</s>), and reinstatement (<s>upasthāpanā</s>). ||

children.text: § 862. tatra gurave pramādanivedanaṃ daśadoṣavivarjitam ālocanam. mithyāduṣkṛtābhidhānād abhivyaktapratikriyaṃ pratikramaṇam. [tadubhaya] saṃsarge sati viśodhanāt tadubhayam. saṃsaktānnapānopakaraṇādivibhajanaṃ vivekaḥ. kāyotsargādikaraṇaṃ vyutsargaḥ. anaśanāvamaudaryādilakṣaṇaṃ tapaḥ. divasapakṣamāsādinā pravrajyāhāpanaṃ chedaḥ. pakṣamāsādivibhāgena dūrataḥ parivarjanaṃ parihāraḥ. punar dīkṣāprāpaṇam upasthāpanā.
children.translated_text: Section 862. Among these, the reporting of one's negligence to the preceptor, free from the ten defects, is <s>ālocana</s> (confession). The explicit remedial action through the utterance 'I have done wrong' (<s>mithyā duṣkṛtam</s>) is <s>pratikramaṇa</s> (repentance). When both are combined, the purification is <s>tadubhaya</s> (both). The separation of mixed food, drink, utensils, and the like is <s>viveka</s> (separation). The practice of <s>kāyotsarga</s> (abandonment of the body) and the like is <s>vyutsarga</s> (renunciation). That characterized by fasting, reduced diet, and the like is <s>tapas</s> (austerity). The loss of monastic standing for a period of days, fortnights, months, and the like is <s>cheda</s> (reduction of status). Banishment to a distance for a period divided into fortnights, months, and the like is <s>parihāra</s> (expulsion). The re-granting of initiation is <s>upasthāpanā</s> (reinstatement).

children.text: § 863. vinayavikalpapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 863. In order to explain the subdivisions of reverence, he says —

children.text: jñānadarśanacāritropacārāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), faith (<s>darśana</s>), conduct (<s>cāritra</s>), and courtesy (<s>upacāra</s>). ||

children.text: § 864. ‘vinayaḥ’ ity adhikāreṇābhisaṃbandhaḥ kriyate. jñānavinayo darśanavinayaś cāritravinaya upacāravinayaś ceti. sabahumānaṃ mokṣārthaṃ jñānagrahaṇābhyāsasmaraṇādir jñānavinayaḥ. śaṃkādidoṣavirahitaṃ tattvārthaśraddhānaṃ darśanavinayaḥ. tadvataś cāritre samāhitacittatā cāritravinayaḥ. pratyakṣeṣv ācāryādiṣv abhyuthānābhigamanāñjalikaraṇādir upacāravinayaḥ. parokṣeṣv api kāyavāṅmano ’bhiraṃjalikriyāguṇasaṃkīrtanānusmaraṇādiḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 864. The connection is made with the governing term '<s>vinaya</s>' (reverence). Thus: reverence toward knowledge, reverence toward faith, reverence toward conduct, and reverence as courtesy. The acquisition, practice, remembrance, and the like of knowledge, with respect and for the purpose of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), is <s>jñānavinaya</s> (reverence toward knowledge). Faith in the categories of reality free from defects such as doubt and the like is <s>darśanavinaya</s> (reverence toward faith). Mental composure in conduct on the part of one possessing that [faith] is <s>cāritravinaya</s> (reverence toward conduct). Rising, approaching, saluting with folded hands, and the like toward teachers (<s>ācārya</s>) and others who are directly present is <s>upacāravinaya</s> (reverence as courtesy). Toward those not directly present as well, [there is reverence through] bodily, vocal, and mental salutation, glorification of qualities, remembrance, and the like.

children.text: § 865. vaiyāvṛttyabhedapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 865. In order to explain the subdivisions of service (<s>vaiyāvṛttya</s>), he says —

children.text: ācāryopādhyāyatapasviśaikṣaglānagaṇakulasaṃghasādhumanojñānām ||
children.translated_text: Of the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>), preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>), ascetic (<s>tapasvin</s>), student (<s>śaikṣa</s>), sick person (<s>glāna</s>), group (<s>gaṇa</s>), lineage (<s>kula</s>), community (<s>saṃgha</s>), mendicant (<s>sādhu</s>), and the virtuous (<s>manojña</s>). ||

children.text: § 866. vaiyāvṛttyaṃ daśadhā bhidyate. kutaḥ? viṣayabhedāt. ācāryavaiyāvṛttyam upādhyāyavaiyāvṛttyam ity ādi. tatra ācaranti tasmād vratānīty ācāryaḥ. mokṣārthaṃ śāstram upetya tasmād adhīyata ity upādhyāyaḥ. mahopavāsādyanuṣṭhāyī tapasvī. śikṣāśīlaḥ śaikṣaḥ. rujādikliṣṭaśarīro glānaḥ. gaṇaḥ sthavirasaṃtatiḥ. dīkṣakācāryaśiṣyasaṃstyāyaḥ kulam. cāturvarṇaśramaṇanivahaḥ saṃghaḥ. cirapravrajitaḥ sādhuḥ. manojño lokasaṃmataḥ. teṣāṃ vyādhipariṣahamithyātvādyupanipāte kāyaceṣṭayā dravyāntareṇa vā tatpratīkāro vaiyāvṛttyaṃ samādhyādhānavicikitsābhāvapravacanavātsalyādyabhivyaktyartham.
children.translated_text: § 866. Service (<s>vaiyāvṛttya</s>) is divided tenfold. How? Due to the differentiation of objects. Service to the teacher (<s>ācāryavaiyāvṛttya</s>), service to the preceptor (<s>upādhyāyavaiyāvṛttya</s>), and so on. Among these: one who teaches the vows, therefore [called] <s>ācārya</s> (teacher). One who, having approached a scripture for the sake of liberation, studies from it, therefore [called] <s>upādhyāya</s> (preceptor). One who practices great fasts and the like is an ascetic (<s>tapasvin</s>). One who is devoted to learning is a student (<s>śaikṣa</s>). One whose body is afflicted by illness and the like is ailing (<s>glāna</s>). The congregation (<s>gaṇa</s>) is the succession of elders (<s>sthavira</s>). The family (<s>kula</s>) is the group of disciples of the initiating teacher. The community (<s>saṃgha</s>) is the assembly of mendicants of the four orders. One long since ordained is a monk (<s>sādhu</s>). One who is pleasing and esteemed by the world [is the tenth]. Service to them—the remedying of affliction by bodily effort or by material means when illness, endurance [of hardship], onset of wrong faith, and the like occur—is <s>vaiyāvṛttya</s>, for the purpose of manifesting spiritual composure (<s>samādhi</s>), sustenance [of right conduct], absence of disgust, and affection for the teaching.

children.text: § 867. svādhyāyavikalpavijñānārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 867. For the purpose of understanding the varieties of self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), he says—

children.text: vācanāpracchanānuprekṣāmnāyadharmopadeśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Recitation (<s>vācanā</s>), questioning (<s>pracchanā</s>), contemplation (<s>anuprekṣā</s>), rehearsal (<s>āmnāya</s>), and religious instruction (<s>dharmopadeśa</s>). ||

children.text: § 868. niravadyagranthārthobhayapradānaṃ vācanā. saṃśayachedāya niścitabalādhānāya vā parānuyogaḥ pracchanā. adhigatārthasya manasābhyāso ’nuprekṣā. ghoṣaśuddhaṃ parivartanam āmnāyaḥ. dharmakathādyanuṣṭhānaṃ dharmopadeśaḥ. sa eṣa pañcavidhaḥ svādhyāyaḥ kim arthaḥ? prajñātiśayaḥ praśastādhyavasāyaḥ pramasaṃvegas tapovṛddhir aticāraviśuddhir ity evam ādy arthaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 868. The imparting of both the text and meaning of faultless scripture is recitation (<s>vācanā</s>). Questioning another for the purpose of removing doubt or for establishing firm conviction is questioning (<s>pracchanā</s>). The mental repetition of what has been understood is contemplation (<s>anuprekṣā</s>). Correct vocal rehearsal is <s>āmnāya</s>. The practice of religious discourse and the like is religious instruction (<s>dharmopadeśa</s>). This fivefold self-study—what is its purpose? Its purpose includes the excellence of wisdom, praiseworthy mental dispositions, spiritual urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>), increase of austerity, purification of transgressions, and so forth.

children.text: § 869. vyutsargabhedanirjñānārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 869. For the purpose of understanding the varieties of renunciation (<s>vyutsarga</s>), he says—

children.text: bāhyābhyantaropadhyoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of external and internal possessions (<s>upadhi</s>). ||

children.text: § 870. vyutsarjanaṃ vyutsargas tyāgaḥ. sa dvividhaḥ — bāhyopadhityāgo ’bhyantaropadhityāgaś ceti. anupāttaṃ vastudhanadhānyādi bāhyopadiḥ. krodhādir ātmabhāvo ’bhyantaropadhiḥ kāyatyāgaś ca niyatakālo yāvaj jīvaṃ vābhyantaropadhityāga ity ucyate. sa kim arthaḥ? nissaṅgatvanirbhayatvajīvitāśāvyudāsādyarthaḥ.
children.translated_text: § 870. <s>Vyutsarjana</s> is <s>vyutsarga</s>, meaning abandonment. It is twofold: abandonment of external possessions and abandonment of internal possessions. Things not taken up—material goods, wealth, grain, and the like—are external possessions (<s>bāhyopadhi</s>). Anger and the like, the states of the self, are internal possessions (<s>abhyantaropadhi</s>); and the abandonment of the body for a fixed period or for life is also called abandonment of internal possessions. What is its purpose? Its purpose is detachment, fearlessness, renunciation of the desire for life, and the like.

children.text: § 871. yad bahuvaktavyaṃ dhyānam iti pṛthagvyavasthāpitaṃ tasyedānīṃ bhedābhidhānaṃ prāptakālam. tadullaṅghya tasya prayoktṛsvarūpakālanirddhāraṇārtham ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 871. That which requires much exposition—namely meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>)—has been separately established. Now the time has come for the statement of its varieties. Setting that aside, for the purpose of determining its practitioner, essential nature, and time-limit, it is said—

children.text: uttamasaṃhananasyaikāgracintānirodho dhyānam āntarmuhūrtāt ||
children.translated_text: For one of the highest bodily frame (<s>uttamasaṃhanana</s>), the restraining of one-pointed thought is meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), [lasting] less than one <s>muhūrta</s> (<s>āntarmuhūrta</s>). ||

children.text: § 872. ādyaṃ tritayaṃ saṃhananam uttamaṃ vajrarṣabhanārācasaṃhananaṃ vajranārācasaṃhananaṃ nārācasaṃhananam iti. tat tritayam api dhvānasya sādhanaṃ bhavati.

mokṣasya tu ādyam eva. taduttamaṃ saṃhananaṃ yasya so ’yam uttamasaṃhananaḥ, tasyottamasaṃhananasyeti. anena prayoktṛnirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ. agraṃ mukham. ekam agramasyety ekāgraḥ. nānārthāvalambanena cintā parispandavatī, tasyā anyāśeṣamukhebyo vyāvartya ekasminn agre niyama ekāgracintānirodha ity ucyate. anena dhānyasvarūpam uktaṃ bhavati. muhūrta iti kālaparimāṇam. antargato muhūrto ’ntarmuhūrtaḥ. ‘ā antarmuhūrtāt’ ity anena kālavidhiḥ kṛtaḥ. tataḥ paraṃ durdharatvāt ekagracintāyāḥ. cintāyā nirodho yadi dhyānaṃ, nirodhaś cābhāvaḥ, tena dhyānam asatkharaviṣāṇavatsyāt? naiṣa doṣaḥ; anyacintānivṛttyapekṣayāsad iti cocyate, svaviṣayākārapravṛtteḥ sad iti ca; abhāvasya bhāvāntaravād hetvaṅgatvādibhir abhāvasya vastudharmatvasiddheś ca. athavā nāyaṃ bhāvasādhanaḥ, nirodhanaṃ nirodha iti. kiṃ tarhi? karmasādhanaḥ, ‘nirudhyata iti nirodhaḥ’. cintā cāsau nirodhaś ca cintānirodha iti. etad uktaṃ bhavati — jñānam evāparispandāgniśikhāvadavabhāsamānaṃ dhyānam iti.
children.translated_text: —but for liberation, only the first [is required]. One who possesses that highest bodily frame is said to be 'of the highest bodily frame' (<s>uttamasaṃhanana</s>). By this, the determination of the practitioner is accomplished. One-pointed thought is concentration on a single object. Its restraint—the cessation of the mind's fluctuation—is meditation. By this, the essential nature [of meditation] is determined. It exists for the duration of less than one <s>muhūrta</s>, because the mind cannot remain fixed on one object beyond that time. Thereafter, there is a change in the object of meditation. By this, the time-limit is determined. And it has been said—'for ascetics, the maximum duration of meditation is one <s>muhūrta</s>; the minimum of all is less than one <s>muhūrta</s>.'
§ 872. The first three bodily frames are the highest: <s>vajrarṣabhanārāca</s> (adamantine-bull-tubular), <s>vajranārāca</s> (adamantine-tubular), and <s>nārāca</s> (tubular). These three are—

children.text: § 873. tadbhedapradarśanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 873. For the purpose of demonstrating its varieties, he says—

children.text: ārttaraudradharmyaśuklāni ||
children.translated_text: Sorrowful (<s>ārta</s>), cruel (<s>raudra</s>), virtuous (<s>dharmya</s>), and pure (<s>śukla</s>). ||

children.text: § 874. ṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ, ardanam ārtivā, tatra bhavam ārtam. rudraḥ krūrāśayas tasya karma tatra bhavaṃ vā raudram. dharmo vyākhyātaḥ. dharmād anapetaṃ dharmyam. śuciguṇayogāc chuklam. tadetac caturvidhaṃ dhyānaṃ dvaividhyam aśnute. kutaḥ? praśastāpraśastabhedāt. apraśastam apuṇyāsravakāraṇatvāt. karmanirdahanasāmarthyāt praśastam.
children.translated_text: § 874. <s>Ṛta</s> means suffering; <s>ardana</s> means pain or distress; that which arises in connection with it is sorrowful (<s>ārta</s>). <s>Rudra</s> means one of cruel disposition; its activity, or that which arises therein, is cruel (<s>raudra</s>). <s>Dharma</s> means—

children.text: § 875 kiṃ punas tad iti ced ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 875. If one asks 'what further [about them]?', it is said—

children.text: pare mokṣahetū ||
children.translated_text: The latter two are causes of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). ||

children.text: § 876. param uttaram antyam. antyaṃ śuklam. tatsāmīpyād dharmyam api ‘param’ ity upacaryate. dvivacananirdeśasāmarthyād gaunam api gṛhyate. ‘pare mokṣahetū’ iti vacanāt pūrve ārtaraudre saṃsārahetū ity uktam bhavati. kutaḥ? tṛtīyasya sādhyasyābhāvāt.
children.translated_text: § 876. '<s>Para</s>' means higher, final. The final one is pure (<s>śukla</s>). Due to its proximity, the virtuous (<s>dharmya</s>) is also figuratively called '<s>para</s>' (higher). By the force of the dual number in the statement, both [dharmya and śukla] are understood to be causes of liberation.

children.text: § 877. tatrārtraṃ caturvidham. tatrādivikalpalakṣaṇanirdeśārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 877. Among these, the sorrowful (<s>ārta</s>) meditation is fourfold. For the purpose of stating the characteristic of its first variety, he says—

children.text: ārtam amanojñasya saṃprayoge tadviprayogāya smṛtisamanvāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sorrowful (<s>ārta</s>) meditation is the recollection and mental effort directed toward separation from an unpleasant [object] when in contact with it. ||

children.text: § 878. amanojñam apriyaṃ viṣakaṇṭakaśatruśastrādi, tadbādhākaraṇatvād ‘amanojñam’ ity ucyate. tasya saṃprayoge, sa kathaṃ nāma me na syād iti saṃkalpaś cintāprabandhaḥ smṛtisamanvāhāraḥ prathaman ārtam ity ākhyāyate.
children.translated_text: § 878. The unpleasant (<s>amanojña</s>) refers to what is disagreeable—poison, thorns, enemies, weapons, and the like—called 'unpleasant' because they cause affliction. When in contact with it—how [does one come into contact]?—

children.text: § 879. dvitīyasya vikalpasya lakṣaṇanirdeśārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 879. For the purpose of stating the characteristic of the second variety, he says—

children.text: viparitaṃ manojñasya ||
children.translated_text: The opposite, regarding the pleasant (<s>manojña</s>). ||

children.text: § 880. kuto viparitam? pūvoktāt. tenaitad uktam bhavati — manojñasyeṣṭasya svaputradāradhanāder viprayoge tatsaṃprayogāya saṃkalpaś cintāprabandho dvitīyam ārtam avagantavyam.
children.translated_text: § 880. Opposite to what? To what was stated before. Thus what is stated amounts to this: when separated from what is pleasant and desired—one's own sons, wife, wealth, and the like—the recollection and mental effort directed toward reunion with them is [the second type of sorrowful meditation].

children.text: § 881. tṛtīyasya vikalpasya lakṣaṇapratipādanārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 881. For the purpose of establishing the characteristic of the third variety, he says—

children.text: vedanāyāś ca ||
children.translated_text: And of painful sensation (<s>vedanā</s>). ||

children.text: § 882. ‘vedanā’ śabdaḥ sukhe duḥkhe ca vartamāno ’pi ārtasya prakṛtatvād duḥkhavedanāyāṃ pravartate, tasyā vātādivikārajanitavedanāyā upanipāte tasyā apāyaḥ katham nāma me syād iti saṃkalpaś cintāprabandhas tṛtīyam ārtam ucyate.
children.translated_text: § 882. Although the word '<s>vedanā</s>' (sensation) applies to both pleasure and pain, since sorrowful [meditation] is the subject, it refers to painful sensation. Its cause being bodily disorders such as those arising from wind (<s>vāta</s>) and the like—

children.text: § 883. turīyasārtasya lakṣaṇanirdeśārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 883. For the purpose of stating the characteristic of the fourth type of sorrowful [meditation], he says—

children.text: nidānaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And longing (<s>nidāna</s>). ||

children.text: § 884. bhogākāṅṣāturyasyānāgataviṣayaprāptiṃ prati manaḥpraṇidhānaṃ saṃkalpaś cintāprabandhas turīyam ārtaṃ nidānam ity ucyate.
children.translated_text: § 884. The mental fixation, resolve, and continuous thinking directed toward the attainment of future objects of enjoyment—the desire for pleasures—is the fourth sorrowful meditation called longing (<s>nidāna</s>).

children.text: § 885. tadetac caturvidham ārtam kiṃ svāmikam iti ced ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 885. If one asks to whom does this fourfold sorrowful meditation belong, it is said—

children.text: tadaviratadeśaviratapramattasaṃyatānām ||
children.translated_text: That [sorrowful meditation] belongs to the non-restrained (<s>avirata</s>), the partially restrained (<s>deśavirata</s>), and the restrained-with-negligence (<s>pramattasaṃyata</s>). ||

children.text: § 886. aviratā asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyantāḥ. deśaviratāḥ saṃyatāsaṃyatāḥ. pramattasaṃyatāḥ paṃcadaśapramādopetāḥ kriyānuṣṭhāyinaḥ. tatrāviratadeśaviratānāṃ caturvidham apy ārtaṃ bhavati; asaṃyamapariṇāmopetatvāt. pramattasaṃyatānāṃ tu nidānavarjyam anyad ārtatrayaṃ pramādodayodrekāt kadācit syāt.
children.translated_text: § 886. The non-restrained are those up to and including those of right faith without restraint (<s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>). The partially restrained are those with mixed restraint and non-restraint (<s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>). The restrained-with-negligence are those engaged in religious practice while still subject to the fifteen types of negligence.

children.text: § 887. vyākhyātam ārtaṃ saṃjñādibhiḥ. dvitīyasya saṃjñāhetusvāminirddhāraṇārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 887. The sorrowful meditation has been explained through [its] characteristics and the rest. For the purpose of determining the characteristics, cause, and possessor of the second [type of meditation], he says—

children.text: hiṃsānṛtasteyaviṣayasaṃrakṣaṇebhyo raudram aviratadeśaviratayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Cruel (<s>raudra</s>) meditation [arises] from violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>), falsehood (<s>anṛta</s>), theft (<s>steya</s>), and the guarding of possessions (<s>viṣayasaṃrakṣaṇa</s>); [it belongs] to the non-restrained (<s>avirata</s>) and the partially restrained (<s>deśavirata</s>). ||

children.text: § 888. hiṃsādīny uktalakṣaṇāni. tāni raudradhyānotpatter nimittī bhavantīti hetunirdeśo vijñāyate. tena hetunirdeśenānuvartamānaḥ ‘smṛtisamanvāhāraḥ’ abhisaṃbadhyate. hiṃsāyāḥ smṛtisamanvāhāra ity ādi. tadraudradhyānam aviratadeśaviratayor veditavyam. aviratasya bhavatu raudradhyānaṃ, deśaviratasya katham? tasyāpi hiṃsādyāveśād vittādisaṃrakṣaṇatantratvāc ca kadācid bhavitum arhati. tatpunar nārakādīnām akāraṇaṃ; samyagdarśanasāmarthyāt. saṃyatasya tu na bhavaty eva; tadārambhe saṃyamapracyuteḥ.
children.translated_text: § 888. Violence and the rest have their characteristics as previously stated. They serve as the causes for the arising of cruel meditation—thus the indication of cause is understood. By this indication of cause, through implication—

children.text: § 889. āha ‘pare mokṣahetū’ upadiṣṭe. tatrādyasya mokṣahetor dhyānasya bhedasvarūpasvāminirdeśaḥ kartavya ity ata āha —
children.translated_text: § 889. One says: 'the latter two are causes of liberation' has been taught. Of these, the first cause of liberation—[virtuous] meditation—its varieties, essential nature, and possessor are to be stated; therefore he says—

children.text: ājñāpāyavipākasaṃsthānavicayāya dharmyam ||
children.translated_text: Virtuous (<s>dharmya</s>) meditation is for the contemplation of the teaching (<s>ājñā</s>), transience (<s>apāya</s>), fruition (<s>vipāka</s>), and structure [of the universe] (<s>saṃsthāna</s>). ||

children.text: § 890. vicayanaṃ vicayo viveko vicāraṇety arthaḥ. ājñāpāyavipākasaṃsthānānāṃ vicaya ajñāpāyavipākasaṃsthānavicayaḥ. ‘smṛtisamanvāhāraḥ’ ity anuvartate. sa pratyekaṃ saṃbadhyate — ājñāvicayāya smṛtisamanvāhāraḥ ity ādi. tad yathā — upadeṣṭur abhāvān mandabuddhitvāt karmodayāt sūkṣmatvāc ca padārthanāṃ hetudṛṣṭāntoparame sati sarvajñapraṇītam āgamaṃ pramāṇī kṛtya ittham evedaṃ
nānyathāvādino jināḥ
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Jinas</s> do not speak otherwise'—

children.text: iti gahanapadārthaśraddhānād arthāvadhāraṇam ājñāvicayaḥ. athavā — svayaṃ viditapadārthatattvasya sataḥ paraṃ prati pipādayiṣoḥ svasiddhāntāvirodhena tattvasamarthanārthaṃ tarkanayapramāṇayojanaparaḥ smṛtisamanvāhāraḥ sarvajñājñāprakāśanārthatvād ājñāvicaya ity ucyate. jātyandhavanmityhyādṛṣṭayaḥ sarvajñapraṇītamārgād vimukhā mokṣārtinaḥ samyaṅmārgāparijñānāt sudūram evāpayantīti sanmārgāpāyacintanam apāyavicayaḥ. athavā — mithyādarśanajñānacāritrebhyaḥ kathaṃ nama ime prāṇino ’peyur iti smṛtisamanvāhāro ’pāyavicayaḥ. karmaṇāṃ jñānāvaraṇādīnāṃ dravyakṣetrakālabhavabhāvapratyayaphalānubhavanaṃ prati praṇidhānaṃ vipākavicayaḥ. lokasaṃsthānasvabhāvavicayāya smṛtisamanvāhāraḥ saṃsthānavicayaḥ. uttamakṣamādilakṣaṇo dharma uktaḥ. tasmād anapetaṃ dharmyaṃ dhyānaṃ caturvikalpam avaseyam. tadaviratadeśaviratapramattāpramattasaṃyatānāṃ bhavati.
children.translated_text: —from the faith in profound categories of reality, the ascertainment of meaning is the contemplation of the teaching (<s>ājñāvicaya</s>). Alternatively: for one who himself has understood the true nature of the categories of reality, the desire to communicate to others—

§ 890. <s>Vicayana</s> means <s>vicaya</s>—discrimination, investigation. The investigation of teaching, transience, fruition, and structure is the contemplation of teaching, transience, fruition, and structure (<s>ājñāpāyavipākasaṃsthānavicaya</s>). 'Recollection'—

children.text: § 891. trayāṇāṃ dhyānānāṃ nirupaṇaṃ kṛtam. idānīṃ śukladhyānaṃ nirūpapayitavyam. tadvakṣyamāṇacaturvikalpam. tatrādyayoḥ svāminirdeśārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 891. The exposition of three [types of] meditation has been completed. Now pure (<s>śukla</s>) meditation is to be explained. It is of four varieties, which will be stated. For the purpose of [specifying] the first two [varieties], he says—

children.text: śukle cādye pūrvavidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in the first [two stages] of pure (<s>śukla</s>) [meditation, only] those who possess prior knowledge (<s>pūrvavid</s>) [are qualified]. ||

children.text: § 892. vakṣyamāṇeṣu śukladhyānavikalpeṣu ādye śukladhyāne pūrvavido bhavataḥ śrutakevalina ity arthāḥ. ‘ca’ śabdena dharmyam api samuccīyate. tatra
vyākhyānato viśeṣapratipattiḥ
children.translated_text: 'Specific understanding [comes] from exposition'—

children.text: iti śreṇyārohaṇāt prāgdharmyaṃ, śreṇyoḥ śukle iti vyākhyāyate.
children.translated_text: —thus it is explained that virtuous meditation [occurs] before ascending the ladders [of spiritual progress], and pure meditation [occurs] on the [two] ladders.

§ 892. Among the varieties of pure meditation to be stated, in the first [two stages of] pure meditation, [only] those who possess prior knowledge are qualified—that is, those possessing <s>śrutakevala</s> (scriptural omniscience). By the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), virtuous [meditation is also included]—

children.text: § 893. avaśiṣṭe kasya bhavata ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: § 893. To whom do the remaining [two stages] belong? To this it is said—

children.text: pare kevalinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The latter [two stages belong] to the omniscient (<s>kevalin</s>). ||

children.text: § 894. prakṣīṇasakalajñānāvaraṇasya kevalinaḥ sayogasyāyogasya ca pare uttare śukladhyāne bhavataḥ.
children.translated_text: § 894. For the omniscient (<s>kevalin</s>)—one whose entire knowledge-obscuring [karma] has been destroyed—the latter, higher [two stages of] pure meditation belong both to the one with activity (<s>sayoga</s>) and the one without activity (<s>ayoga</s>).

children.text: § 895. yathāsaṃkhyaṃ tadvikalpapratipādanārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: § 895. For the purpose of explaining the varieties of those [stages] in sequence, this is stated—

children.text: pṛthaktvaikatvavitarkasūkṣmakriyāpratipātivyuparatakriyānivartīni ||
children.translated_text: Analytical with shifting [objects] (<s>pṛthaktvavitarka</s>), analytical with single [object] (<s>ekatvavitarka</s>), [meditation] with subtle bodily activity (<s>sūkṣmakriyāpratipāti</s>), and [meditation] with ceased activity leading to non-return (<s>vyuparatakriyānivartī</s>). ||

children.text: § 896. pṛthaktvavitarkam ekatvavitarkaṃ sūkṣmakriyāpratipāti vyuparatakriyānivarti ceti caturvidhaṃ śukladhyānam. vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇam apekṣya sarveṣām anvarthatvam avaseyam.
children.translated_text: § 896. Analytical with shifting objects (<s>pṛthaktvavitarka</s>), analytical with single object (<s>ekatvavitarka</s>), with subtle bodily activity (<s>sūkṣmakriyāpratipāti</s>), and with ceased activity leading to non-return (<s>vyuparatakriyānivartī</s>)—thus pure meditation is fourfold. It will be explained—

children.text: § 897. tasyālambanaviśeṣanirdhāraṇārtham āha —
children.translated_text: § 897. For the purpose of determining its specific objects of support, he says—

children.text: tryekayogakāyayogāyogānām ||
children.translated_text: [These four stages belong to those with] the three [types of yoga], single <s>yoga</s>, bodily <s>yoga</s> [alone], and absence of <s>yoga</s> respectively. ||

children.text: § 898. ‘yoga’ śabdo vyākhyātārthaḥ ‘kāyavāṅmanaḥkarma yogaḥ’ iti atra. uktaiś caturbhiḥ śukladhyānavikalpais triyogādīnāṃ caturṇāṃ yathāsaṃkhyenābhisaṃbandho veditavyaḥ. triyogasya pṛthaktvavitarkam, triṣu yogeṣv ekayogasyaikatvavitarkam, kāyayogasya sūkṣmakriyāpratipāti, ayogasya vyutparatakriyānivartīti.
children.translated_text: Section 898. The word '<s>yoga</s>' has been explained in the [sūtra] '<s>yoga</s> is the activity of body, speech, and mind.' The correlation of the four varieties of <s>śukla dhyāna</s> (pure meditation) with the four [stages] — three-<s>yoga</s>, etc. — should be understood in corresponding order: <s>pṛthaktva-vitarka</s> (analytical meditation with shifting) for the three-<s>yoga</s> [stage], <s>ekatva-vitarka</s> (analytical meditation without shifting) for [the stage with] one <s>yoga</s> among the three, <s>sūkṣma-kriyā-pratipāti</s> (meditation with subtle bodily activity) for [the stage of] bodily <s>yoga</s> [only], and <s>vyutparat-kriyā-nivartī</s> (meditation with cessation of all activity) for the <s>ayoga</s> (activity-free) [stage].

children.text: § 899. tatrādyayor viśeṣapratipattyartham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: Section 899. In order to distinguish the first two, this is stated —

children.text: ekāśraye savitarkavīcāre pūrve ||
children.translated_text: The first two [types of pure meditation] have a single basis and are accompanied by <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation) and <s>vīcāra</s> (analysis). ||

children.text: § 900. eka āśrayo yayos te ekāśraye. ubhe ’pi pariprāptaśrutajñānaniṣṭhenārabhyete, ity arthaḥ. vitarkaś ca vīcāraś ca vitarkavīcārau, saha vitarkavīcārābhyāṃ varteta iti savitarkavīcāre. pūrve pṛthaktvaikatvavitarke ity arthaḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 900. Those which have a single basis (<s>ekāśraya</s>) — that is, both are begun by one who has mastered <s>śruta-jñāna</s> (scriptural knowledge). <s>Vitarka</s> and <s>vīcāra</s> together are <s>vitarkavīcāra</s>; that which exists with <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vīcāra</s> is <s>savitarkavīcāra</s>. 'The first' refers to the <s>pṛthaktva</s> and <s>ekatva</s> [types of] <s>vitarka</s> [meditation].

children.text: § 901. tatra yathāsaṃkhyaprasaṃge ’niṣṭanivṛttyartham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: Section 901. In that context, to prevent the unwanted consequence of a strict numerical correspondence, this is stated —

children.text: avīcāraṃ dvitīyam ||
children.translated_text: The second is without <s>vīcāra</s> (analysis). ||

children.text: § 902. pūrvayor yad dvitīyaṃ tad avīcāraṃ pratyetavyam. etad uktaṃ bhavati — ādyaṃ savitarkaṃ savīcāraṃ ca bhavati. dvitīyaṃ savitarkam avīcāraṃ ceti.
children.translated_text: Section 902. Of the two previously mentioned, the second should be understood as without <s>vīcāra</s>. What is stated amounts to this: the first has both <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vīcāra</s>, while the second has <s>vitarka</s> but is without <s>vīcāra</s>.

children.text: § 903. atha vitarkavīcārayoḥ kaḥ prativiśeṣa ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: Section 903. Now, what is the specific distinction between <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vīcāra</s>? To this it is replied —

children.text: vitarkaḥ śrutam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vitarka</s> (deliberation) is scriptural [knowledge] (<s>śruta</s>). ||

children.text: § 904. viśeṣeṇa tarkaṇam ūhanaṃ vitarkaḥ śrutajñānam ity arthaḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 904. <s>Vitarka</s> is special reasoning or reflection — the meaning is <s>śruta-jñāna</s> (scriptural knowledge).

children.text: § 905. atha ko vīcāraḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 905. Now, what is <s>vīcāra</s> (analysis)?

children.text: vīcāro ’rthavyaṃjanayogasaṃkrāntiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vīcāra</s> (analysis) is the shifting among meaning (<s>artha</s>), expression (<s>vyañjana</s>), and activity (<s>yoga</s>). ||

children.text: § 906. artho dhyeyo dravyaṃ paryāyo vā. vyañjanaṃ vacanam. yogaḥ kāyavāṅmanaḥkarmalakṣaṇaḥ. saṃkrāntiḥ parivartanam. dravyaṃ vihāya paryāyam upaiti paryāyaṃ tyaktvā dravyam ity arthasaṃkrāntiḥ. ekaṃ śrutavacanam upādāya vacanāntaram ālambate tad api vihāyānyad iti vyañjanasaṃkrāntiḥ. kāyayogaṃ tyaktvā yogāntaraṃ gṛhṇāti yogāntaraṃ ca tyaktvā kāyayogam iti yogasaṃkrāntiḥ. evaṃ parivartanaṃ vīcāra ity ucyate. tad etat sāmānyaviśeṣanirdiṣṭaṃ caturvidhaṃ dharmyaṃ śuklaṃ ca pūvoditaguptyādibahuprakāropāyaṃ saṃsāranivṛttaye munir dhyātum arhati kṛtaparikarmā. tatra dravyaparamāṇuṃ bhāvaparamāṇuṃ vā dhyāyan nāhitavitarkasāmarthyaḥ arthavyaṃjane kāyavācasī ca pṛthaktvena saṃkrāmatā manasāparyaptibālotsāhavadavyavasthitenāniśitenāpi śastreṇa cirāt taruṃ chindann iva mohaprakṛtīr upaśamayan kṣapayaṃś ca pṛthaktvavitarkavīcāradhyānabhāgbhavati. sa eva punaḥ samūlatūlaṃ mohanīyaṃ nirdidhakṣann anantaguṇaviśuddhiyogaviśeṣam āśritya bahutarāṇāṃ jñānāvaraṇasahāyībhūtānāṃ prakṛtīnāṃ bandhaṃ nirundhan sthiti hrāsakṣayau ca kurvan śrutajñānopayogo nivṛttārthavyaṃjanayogasaṃkrāntiḥ avicalitamanāḥ kṣīṇakaṣāyo vaiḍūryamaṇir iva nirupalepo dhyātvā punar na nivartata ity uktam ekatvavitarkam. evam ekatvavitarkaśukladhyānavaiśvānaranirdagdhavātikarmendhanaḥ prajvalitakevalajñānagabhastimaṇḍalo meghapañjaranirodhanirgata iva gharmaraśmir vā bhāsamāno bhagavāṃs tīrthakara itaro vā kevalī lokeśvarāṇām abhigamanīyo ’rcanīyaś cotkarṣeṇāyuṣaḥ pūvakoṭīṃ deśonāṃ viharati. sa yadāntarmuhūrtaśeṣāyuṣkas tattulyasthitivedyanāmagotraś ca bhavati tadā sarvaṃ vāṅmanasayogaṃ bādarakāyayogaṃ ca parihāpya sukṣmakāyayogālambanaḥ sukṣmakriyāpratipātidhyānam āskanditum arahatīti. yadā punar antarmuhūrtaśeṣāyuṣkas tato ’dhikasthitiśeṣakarmatrayo bhavati sayogī tadātmopayogātiśayasya sāmāyikasahāyasya viśiṣṭakaraṇasya mahāsaṃvarasya laghukarmaparipācanasyāśeṣakarmareṇupariśātanaśaktisvābhāvyād daṇḍakapāṭaprataralokapūraṇāni svātmapradeśavisarpaṇataś caturbhiḥ samayaiḥ kṛtvā punar api tāvadbhir eva samayaiḥ samupahṛtapradeśavisaraṇaḥ samīkṛtasthitiśeṣakarmacatuṣṭayaḥ pūrvaśarīrapramāṇo bhūtvā sūkṣmakāyayogena sūkṣmakriyāpratipāti dhyānaṃ dhyāyati. tatas tadantaraṃ samucchinnakriyānivartidhyānam ārabhate. samucchinnaprāṇāpānapracārasarvakāyavāṅmanoyogasarvapradeśaparispandakriyāvyāpāratvāt samucchinnakriyānivartīty ucyate. tasmin samucchinnakriyānivartini dhyāne sarvabandhāsravanirodhasarvaśeṣakarmaśātanasāmarthyopapatter ayogikevalinaḥ saṃpūrṇayathākhyātacāritrajñānadarśanaṃ sarvasaṃsāraduḥkhajālapariṣvaṅgocchedajananaṃ sākṣān mokṣakāraṇam upajāyate. sa punar ayogakevalī bhagavāṃs tadā dhyānātiśayāgninirdagdhasarvamalakalaṃkabandhano nirastakiṭṭadhātupāṣāṇajātyakanakavallabdhātmā parinirvāti. tadetad dvividhaṃ tapo ’bhinavakarmāsravanirodhahetutvāt saṃvarakāraṇaṃ prāktanakarmarajovidhūnananimittatvān nirjarāhetur api bhavati.
children.translated_text: Section 906. <s>Artha</s> (meaning) is the object of meditation — either a substance (<s>dravya</s>) or a mode (<s>paryāya</s>). <s>Vyañjana</s> (expression) is verbal formulation. <s>Yoga</s> is characterized as activity of body, speech, and mind. <s>Saṃkrānti</s> is shifting. Leaving aside substance and taking up mode, or leaving mode and taking up substance — this is shifting of meaning (<s>artha-saṃkrānti</s>). Adopting one scriptural formulation and then grasping another, and abandoning that too for yet another — this is shifting of expression (<s>vyañjana-saṃkrānti</s>). Abandoning bodily <s>yoga</s> and taking up another <s>yoga</s>, and abandoning that and returning to bodily <s>yoga</s> — this is shifting of activity (<s>yoga-saṃkrānti</s>). Such shifting is called <s>vīcāra</s>. Thus, this fourfold meditation — <s>dharmya</s> (virtuous) and <s>śukla</s> (pure), described in general and specific terms — with the many kinds of means previously stated such as the <s>guptis</s> (restraints) and the rest, should be practiced by the sage who has prepared himself, for the cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therein, while meditating on a material atom (<s>dravya-paramāṇu</s>) or a psychic atom (<s>bhāva-paramāṇu</s>), one who has not exhausted the power of <s>vitarka</s>, shifting separately among meaning, expression, bodily activity, and speech, with a mind that is unsettled like the effort of an immature child — like slowly cutting a tree with a blunt and unsharpened tool — subsiding and destroying the types of <s>mohanīya</s> (deluding) <s>karma</s>, attains the <s>pṛthaktva-vitarka-vīcāra dhyāna</s> (analytical meditation with shifting). That same [practitioner], wishing to burn the <s>mohanīya karma</s> along with its root and seed, resorting to a special <s>yoga</s> of infinitely greater purity, blocking the bondage of the many types [of karma] that serve as auxiliaries to <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring karma), and effecting reduction and destruction of their duration — with <s>śruta-jñāna</s> as the instrument, with the shifting of meaning, expression, and activity ceased, with an unwavering mind, with passions destroyed, like a <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) gem free from blemish — having meditated, he does not turn back; this is called <s>ekatva-vitarka</s> [meditation]. Thus, with the fuel of speech and mind <s>karma</s> burned by the fire of <s>ekatva-vitarka śukla dhyāna</s>, with the blazing orb of <s>kevala-jñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge) radiant — shining like the sun emerging from a cage of clouds — the blessed <s>Tīrthaṅkara</s> or any other <s>kevalī</s> (omniscient), worthy of being approached and worshipped by the lords of the world, lives for a period slightly less than the maximum lifespan (<s>pūrvakoṭi</s>). When he has life remaining of less than one <s>muhūrta</s>, and the duration of his <s>vedanīya</s> (feeling), <s>nāma</s> (name), and <s>gotra</s> (lineage) karmas equals that, then, abandoning all activity of speech and mind and gross bodily activity, relying solely on subtle bodily activity, he is capable of ascending to the <s>sūkṣma-kriyā-pratipāti dhyāna</s> (meditation with subtle bodily activity). When, with life remaining of less than one <s>muhūrta</s>, the remaining duration of the three [other] karmas exceeds [that of life], the <s>sayogī</s> (one still with activity), by the natural power of the supreme excellence of self-realization, accompanied by <s>sāmāyika</s> (equanimity), the special purification, the great stoppage [of karmic influx], the ripening of light karma, and the capacity to shake off all remaining karmic particles — extending his own soul-units, fills the rod-shaped, door-panel-shaped, and raft-shaped [spaces] of the universe in four time-instants; then in an equal number of time-instants, withdrawing the extended soul-units, equalizing the remaining duration of the four [types of] karma, becoming equal to his former body-size, he meditates the <s>sūkṣma-kriyā-pratipāti dhyāna</s> through subtle bodily activity. Thereafter, within that [period], he commences the <s>samucchinna-kriyā-nivartī dhyāna</s> (meditation with complete cessation of activity). It is called 'cessation of all activity' because all activity — the movement of inhalation and exhalation, all activity of body, speech, and mind, and the vibration of all soul-units — has been completely cut off. In that <s>samucchinna-kriyā-nivartī dhyāna</s>, because there arises the capacity for the complete stoppage of all bondage and influx and the shedding of all remaining <s>karma</s>, there arises for the <s>ayogi-kevalī</s> (omniscient without activity) the complete <s>yathākhyāta-cāritra</s> (conduct-as-it-really-is), knowledge, and perception — the direct cause of liberation, which brings about the complete severance of the net of all worldly suffering. That blessed <s>ayoga-kevalī</s>, whose bonds of all impurity and defilement have been burned by the fire of that supreme meditation, having attained the true self like pure gold freed from dross, stone, and other metals — he attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s>. This twofold austerity is a cause of <s>saṃvara</s> (stoppage) because it prevents the influx of new <s>karma</s>, and is also a cause of <s>nirjarā</s> (shedding) because it is the means of shaking off previously accumulated karmic dust.

children.text: § 907. atrāha samyagdṛṣṭayaḥ kiṃ sarve samanirjarā āhosvit kaścid asti prativiśeṣa ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: Section 907. Here one asks: do all those with right faith (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) have the same degree of <s>nirjarā</s> (karmic shedding), or is there some specific variation? To this it is replied —

children.text: samyagdṛṣṭiśrāvakaviratānantaviyojakadarśanamohakṣapakopaśamakopaśāntamohakṣapakakṣīṇamohajināḥ kramaśo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇanirjarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those with right faith (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), lay followers (<s>śrāvaka</s>), the partially restrained (<s>virata</s>), those engaged in separating the infinite [passions] (<s>anantaviyojaka</s>), those destroying faith-deluding [karma] (<s>darśanamohakṣapaka</s>), those subsiding [passions] (<s>upaśamaka</s>), those with subsided passions (<s>upaśāntamoha</s>), those destroying [passions] (<s>kṣapaka</s>), those with destroyed passions (<s>kṣīṇamoha</s>), and the <s>Jinas</s> — [each] successively has <s>nirjarā</s> that is innumerably greater [than the previous]. ||

children.text: § 908. ta ete daśa samyagdṛṣṭyādayaḥ kramaśo ’saṃkhyeyaguṇanirjarāḥ. tad yathā — bhavyaḥ paṃcedndriyasaṃjñī paryāptakā pūrvoktakālalabdhyādisahāyaḥ pariṇāmaviśuddhyā vardhamānaḥ krameṇāpūrvakaraṇādisopānapaṅktyotplavamāno bahutarakarmanirjaro bhavati. sa eva punaḥ prathamasamyaktvaprāptinimittasaṃnidhāne sati samyagdṛṣṭir bhavann asaṃkhyeyaguṇanirjaro bhavati. sa eva punaś cāritramohakarmavikalpāpratyākhyānāvaraṇakṣayopaśamanimittapariṇāmaprāptikāle viśuddhiprakarṣayogāt śrāvako bhavan tato ’saṃkhyeyaguṇanirjaro bhavati. sa eva punaḥ pratyātyākhyānāvaraṇakṣayopaśamakāraṇapariṇāmaviśuddhiyogād viratavyapadeśabhāk san tato ’saṃkhyeyaguṇanirjaro bhavati. sa eva punar anantānubandhikrodhamānamāyālobhānāṃ viyojanaparo bhavati yadā tadā pariṇāmaviśuddhiprakarṣayogāt tato ’saṃkhyeyaguṇanirjaro bhavati. sa eva punar darśanamohaprakṛtitrayatṛṇanicayaṃ nirdidhakṣan pariṇāmaviśuddhyatiśayayogād darśanamohakṣapakavyapadeśabhāk pūvoktād asaṃkhyeyaguṇanirjaro bhavati. evaṃ saḥ kṣāyikasamyagdṛṣṭir bhūtvā śreṇyārohanābhimukhaś cāritramohopaśamaṃ prati vyāpriyamāṇo viśuddhiprakarṣayogād upaśamakavyapadeśam anubhavan pūrvoktād asaṃkhyeyaguṇanirjaro bhavati. sa eva punar aśeṣacāritramohopaśamanimittasaṃnidhāne pariprāprāptopaśāntakaṣāyavyapadeśaḥ pūrvoktād asaṃkhyeyaguṇanirjaro bhavati. sa eva punaś cāritramohakṣapaṇaṃ pratyabhimukhaḥ pariṇāmaviśuddhyā varddhamānaḥ kṣapakavyapadeśam anubhavan pūrvoktād asaṃkhyeyaguṇanirjaro bhavati. sa yadā niḥśeṣacāritramohakṣapaṇakāraṇapariṇāmābhimukhaḥ kṣīṇakaṣāyavyapadeśam āskandan pūrvoktād asaṃkhyeyaguṇanirjaro bhavati. sa eva dvitīyaśukladhyānānalanirdagdhaghātikarmanicayaḥ san jinavyapadeśabhāk pūrvoktād asaṃkhyeyaguṇanirjaro bhavati.
children.translated_text: Section 908. These ten — those with right faith and the rest — successively have <s>nirjarā</s> that is innumerably greater. That is as follows: a soul that is capable of liberation (<s>bhavya</s>), five-sensed, possessing mind (<s>saṃjñin</s>), fully developed (<s>paryāptaka</s>), aided by the previously mentioned temporal aptitudes and the like, increasing in purity of disposition, gradually ascending through the ladder-steps of <s>apūrvakaraṇa</s> (unprecedented operation) and the like — sheds increasingly more <s>karma</s>. That same [soul], when the occasion for the first attainment of right faith (<s>samyaktva</s>) is at hand, becoming one of right faith, has <s>nirjarā</s> that is innumerably greater. That same [soul], at the time of attaining the disposition caused by the subsidence-cum-destruction of the <s>apratyākhyānāvaraṇa</s> (partial-vow-preventing) variety of conduct-deluding <s>karma</s>, by the excellence of purifying <s>yoga</s>, becoming a lay follower (<s>śrāvaka</s>), has <s>nirjarā</s> innumerably greater than that. That same [soul], through the purity of disposition caused by the subsidence-cum-destruction of the <s>pratyākhyānāvaraṇa</s> (total-vow-preventing) karma, attaining the designation of the restrained (<s>virata</s>), has <s>nirjarā</s> innumerably greater than that. That same [soul], when engaged in separating the four infinite-binding passions — anger, pride, deceit, and greed — by the excellence of purity of disposition, has <s>nirjarā</s> innumerably greater than that. That same [soul], wishing to burn the heap of the three types of faith-deluding <s>karma</s> like a pile of straw, by the surpassing excellence of purity of disposition, attaining the designation of one who destroys faith-deluding [karma], has <s>nirjarā</s> innumerably greater than the previous. Similarly, that same [soul], having attained <s>kṣāyika samyagdarśana</s> (indestructible right faith), facing the ascent of the ladder [of spiritual progress], striving toward the subsidence of conduct-deluding <s>karma</s>, experiencing the designation of the subsider by the excellence of purity, has <s>nirjarā</s> innumerably greater than the previous. That same [soul], when the occasion for the complete subsidence of conduct-deluding <s>karma</s> is at hand, having attained the designation of one with subsided passions, has <s>nirjarā</s> innumerably greater than the previous. That same [soul], facing the destruction of conduct-deluding <s>karma</s>, increasing in purity of disposition, experiencing the designation of the destroyer, has <s>nirjarā</s> innumerably greater than the previous. When that same [soul] faces the disposition that causes the complete destruction of conduct-deluding <s>karma</s>, ascending to the designation of one with destroyed passions, he has <s>nirjarā</s> innumerably greater than the previous. That same [soul], having burned the entire stock of destructive (<s>ghātika</s>) <s>karmas</s> by the fire of the second <s>śukla dhyāna</s>, attaining the designation of <s>Jina</s>, has <s>nirjarā</s> innumerably greater than the previous.

children.text: § 909. āha, samyagdarśanasaṃnidhāne ’pi yady asaṃkhyeyaguṇanirjaratavāt parasparato na sāmyam esāṃ kiṃ tarhi śravakavad amī viratādayo guṇabhedān na nirgranthatām arhantīti? ucyate, naitad evam. kutaḥ. yasmād guṇabhedād anyo ’nyaviśeṣe ’pi naigamādinayavyāpārāt sarve ’pi hi bhavanti —
children.translated_text: Section 909. One says: if even in the presence of right faith, there is no equality among these [stages] because each has <s>nirjarā</s> innumerably greater [than the previous], then should not those who are restrained and the rest, like the lay follower, be excluded from the designation of <s>nirgrantha</s> (unattached monk) due to differences in spiritual qualities? It is replied: this is not so. Why? Because despite the difference in qualities and mutual distinction, through the operation of the <s>naigama</s> and other viewpoints (<s>nayas</s>), all of them are —

children.text: pulākabakuśakuśīlanirgranthasnātakā nirgranthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pulākas</s>, <s>bakuśas</s>, <s>kuśīlas</s>, <s>nirgranthas</s>, and <s>snātakas</s> — [all are called] <s>nirgranthas</s> (unattached monks). ||

children.text: § 910. uttaraguṇabhāvanāpetamanaso vrateṣv api kvacit kadācit paripūrṇatām apariprāpnuvanto ’viśuddhapulākasādṛśyāt pulākā ity ucyante. nairgranthyaṃ prati sthitā akhaṇḍitavratāḥ śarīropakaraṇavibhūṣānuvartino ’viviktaparivārā mohaśabalayuktā bakuśāh. śabalaparyāyavācī bakuśaśabdaḥ. kuśīlā dvividhāḥ — pratisevanākuśīlāḥ kaṣāyakuśīlā iti. aviviktaparigrahāḥ paripūrṇobhayāḥ kathaṃcid uttaraguṇavirādhinaḥ pratisevanākuśīlāḥ. vaśīkṛtānyakaṣāyodayāḥ saṃjvalanamātratantrāḥ kaṣāyakuśīlāḥ. udakadaṇḍarājivadanabhivyaktodayakarmāṇaḥ ūrdhvaṃ muhūrtād udbhidyamānakevalajñānadarśanabhājo nirgranthāḥ. prakṣīṇaghātikarmāṇaḥ kevalino dvividhāḥ snātakāḥ. ta ete paṃcāpi nirgranthāḥ. cāritrapariṇāmasya prakarṣāprakarṣabhede saty api naigamasaṃgrahādinayāpekṣayā sarve ’pi te nirgranthā ity ucyante.
children.translated_text: Section 910. Those whose minds are devoid of the cultivation of higher virtues, who sometimes fail to fully observe even the vows — due to their resemblance to impure husks — are called <s>pulākas</s> (husk-like monks). Those who are established on the path toward the state of <s>nirgrantha</s>, whose vows are unbroken, but who attend to bodily accessories and adornment, who keep an undiscriminating retinue, and who are tinged with delusion — these are <s>bakuśas</s> (mixed monks). The word <s>bakuśa</s> is a synonym for 'mixed' (<s>śabala</s>). <s>Kuśīlas</s> (lax monks) are of two kinds: <s>pratisevanā-kuśīlas</s> (lax in practice) and <s>kaṣāya-kuśīlas</s> (lax due to passions). Those with undiscriminating possessions, complete in both [knowledge and conduct], yet somehow violating the higher virtues, are <s>pratisevanā-kuśīlas</s>. Those who have subdued the rise of other passions and are governed only by the <s>saṃjvalana</s> (blazing) [sub-type of passion] are <s>kaṣāya-kuśīlas</s>. Those whose <s>karma</s> has a manifest rise like the [clear marks of a] water-[drop], staff, lotus-line, and face, who are about to attain <s>kevala-jñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge) and <s>kevala-darśana</s> (omniscient perception) within one <s>muhūrta</s>, are <s>nirgranthas</s> (the fully unattached). Those whose destructive (<s>ghātika</s>) <s>karmas</s> are destroyed, the omniscient ones (<s>kevalins</s>), are of two kinds and are called <s>snātakas</s> (the bathed ones). All five of these are [called] <s>nirgranthas</s>. Although there are differences of degree in the excellence of conduct-disposition, from the standpoint of the <s>naigama</s> (collective), <s>saṃgraha</s> (synthetic), and other viewpoints, all of them are called <s>nirgranthas</s>.

children.text: § 911. teṣāṃ pulākādīnāṃ bhūyo ’pi viśeṣapratipattyartham āha —
children.translated_text: Section 911. For the further specific understanding of these <s>pulākas</s> and the rest, he says —

children.text: saṃyamaśrutapratisevanātīrthaliṃgaleśyopapādasthānavikalpataḥ sādhyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are to be analyzed according to [the categories of] restraint (<s>saṃyama</s>), scripture (<s>śruta</s>), lapsing (<s>pratisevanā</s>), <s>tīrtha</s> (order), external marks (<s>liṅga</s>), <s>leśyā</s> (soul-coloring), birth-place (<s>upapāda</s>), and [spiritual] stage (<s>sthānavikalpa</s>). ||

children.text: § 912. te ete pulākādayaḥ saṃyamādibhir aṣṭabhir anuyogaiḥ sādhyā vyākheyāḥ. tad yathā — pulākabakuśapratisevanākuśīlā dvayoḥ saṃyamayoḥ sāmāyikacchedopasthāpanayor vartante. kaṣāyakuśīlā dvayoḥ saṃyamayoḥ parihāraviśuddhisūkṣamasāmparāyayoḥ pūrvayoś ca. nirgranthasnātakā ekasminn eva yathākhyātasaṃyame santi.
children.translated_text: Section 912. These <s>pulākas</s> and the rest are to be analyzed — that is, explained — by means of these eight investigative categories (<s>anuyogas</s>) beginning with restraint. That is as follows: <s>pulākas</s>, <s>bakuśas</s>, and <s>pratisevanā-kuśīlas</s> operate in two types of restraint: <s>sāmāyika</s> (equanimous) and <s>chedopasthāpana</s> (re-initiation after lapse). <s>Kaṣāya-kuśīlas</s> operate in two types of restraint: <s>parihāra-viśuddhi</s> (purification through avoidance) and <s>sūkṣma-sāṃparāya</s> (subtle mixed passions), as well as in the two former types. <s>Nirgranthas</s> and <s>snātakas</s> exist in the single [type of] restraint called <s>yathākhyāta</s> (conduct-as-it-really-is).

children.text: § 913. śrutaṃ — pulākabakuśapratisevanākuśīlā utkarṣenābhinnākṣaradaśapūrvadharāḥ. kaṣāyakuśīlā nirgranthāś caturdaśapūrvadharāḥ. jaghanyena pulākasya śrutam ācāravastu. bakuśakuśīlanirgranthānāṃ śrutam aṣṭau pravacanamātaraḥ. snātakā apagataśrutāḥ kevalinaḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 913. Regarding scripture (<s>śruta</s>): <s>pulākas</s>, <s>bakuśas</s>, and <s>pratisevanā-kuśīlas</s> at most possess the <s>daśapūrva</s> (ten <s>Pūrvas</s>) with unbroken syllables. <s>Kaṣāya-kuśīlas</s> and <s>nirgranthas</s> possess the fourteen <s>Pūrvas</s>. At minimum, the scripture of a <s>pulāka</s> is the <s>Ācāra-vastu</s> (rules of conduct). The scripture of <s>bakuśas</s>, <s>kuśīlas</s>, and <s>nirgranthas</s> is the eight <s>Pravacanamātaras</s> (mothers of the doctrine). <s>Snātakas</s>, having transcended scripture, are omniscient (<s>kevalins</s>).

children.text: § 914. pratisevanā — pañcānāṃ mūlaguṇanāṃ rātribhojanavarjanasya ca parābhiyogād balād anyatamaṃ pratisevamānaḥ pulāko bhavati. bakuśo dvividhaḥ — upakaraṇabakuśaḥ śarīrabakuśaś ceti. tatropakaraṇabakuśo bahuviśeṣayuktopakaraṇākāṃkṣī. śarīrasaṃskārasevī śarīrabakuśaḥ. pratisevanākuśīlo mūlaguṇān avirādhayann uttaraguṇeṣu kāṃcid virādhanāṃ pratisevate. kaṣāyakuśīlanirgranthasnātakānāṃ pratisevanā nāsti.
children.translated_text: Section 914. Regarding <s>pratisevanā</s> (relapse): one who, under compulsion or force from others, resorts to the violation of any one of the five fundamental virtues (<s>mūlaguṇas</s>) and the avoidance of eating at night becomes a <s>pulāka</s> (husk-monk). A <s>bakuśa</s> (imperfect monk) is of two kinds: <s>upakaraṇabakuśa</s> (imperfect in equipment) and <s>śarīrabakuśa</s> (imperfect regarding the body). Of these, the <s>upakaraṇabakuśa</s> is one who desires equipment endowed with many special features. The <s>śarīrabakuśa</s> is one who indulges in bodily adornment. The <s>pratisevanākuśīla</s> (one prone to relapse) does not violate the fundamental virtues but resorts to some violation in the supplementary virtues (<s>uttaraguṇas</s>). For the <s>kaṣāyakuśīla</s> (passion-prone monk), the <s>nirgrantha</s> (unfettered monk), and the <s>snātaka</s> (bathed-in-knowledge monk), there is no relapse.

children.text: § 915. tīrtham iti sarve sarveṣāṃ tīrthakarāṇāṃ tīrtheṣu bhavanti.
children.translated_text: Section 915. Regarding the <s>tīrtha</s> (ford, i.e., religious order): all [five types of monks] belong to the <s>tīrthas</s> of all <s>Tīrthaṅkaras</s>.

children.text: § 916. liṅgaṃ dvividhaṃ — dravyaliṅgaṃ bhāvaliṅgaṃ ceti. bhāvaliṅgaṃ pratītya sarve paṃca nirgranthā liṃgino bhavanti. dravyaliṃgaṃ pratītya bhājyāḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 916. The distinguishing mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is of two kinds: material mark (<s>dravyaliṅga</s>) and dispositional mark (<s>bhāvaliṅga</s>). With reference to the dispositional mark, all five types of <s>nirgranthas</s> (unfettered monks) possess the mark. With reference to the material mark, they must be differentiated.
