children.text: § 917. leśyāḥ — pulākasyottarās tisraḥ bakuśapratisevanākuśīlayoḥ ṣaḍ api. kaṣāyakuśīlasya catasra uttaraḥ. sūkṣmasāmparāyasya nirgranthasnātakayoś ca śuklaiva kevalā. ayogā aleśyāḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 917. Regarding colorations (<s>leśyās</s>): for the <s>pulāka</s>, the three higher [colorations apply]; for the <s>bakuśa</s> and <s>pratisevanākuśīla</s>, all six. For the <s>kaṣāyakuśīla</s>, the four higher ones. For the <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāya</s> (one at the stage of subtle passions), the <s>nirgrantha</s>, and the <s>snātaka</s>, only the white (<s>śukla</s>) coloration. Those without activity (<s>ayoga</s>) are without coloration.

children.text: § 918. upapādaḥ — pulākasyotkṛṣṭa upapāda utkṛṣṭasthitideveṣu sahasrāre. bakuśapratisevanākuśīlayor dvāviṃśatisāgaropamasthitiṣu āraṇācyutakalpayoḥ. kaṣāyakuśīlanirgranthayos trayastriṃśatsāgaropamasthitiṣu sarvārthasiddhau. sarveṣām api jaghanyaḥ saudharmakalpe dvisāgaropamasthitiṣu. snātakasya nirvāṇam iti.
children.translated_text: Section 918. Regarding rebirth (<s>upapāda</s>): the maximum rebirth of the <s>pulāka</s> is among the gods of the highest duration in the <s>Sahasrāra</s> heaven. For the <s>bakuśa</s> and <s>pratisevanākuśīla</s>, it is in the <s>Āraṇa</s> and <s>Acyuta</s> heavens with a duration of twenty-two <s>sāgaropamas</s>. For the <s>kaṣāyakuśīla</s> and <s>nirgrantha</s>, it is in <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s> heaven with a duration of thirty-three <s>sāgaropamas</s>. For all of them, the minimum is in the <s>Saudharma</s> heaven with a duration of two <s>sāgaropamas</s>. For the <s>snātaka</s>, there is <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation).

children.text: § 919. sthānam — asaṃkhyeyāni saṃyamasthānāni kaṣāyanimittāni bhavanti. tatra sarvajaghanyāni labdhisthānāni pulākakaṣāyakuśīlayoḥ. tau yugapad asaṃkhyeyāni sthānāni gacchataḥ. tataḥ pulāko vyucchidyate. kaṣāyakuśīlas tato ’saṃkhyeyāni sthānāni gacchaty ekākī. tataḥ kaṣāyakuśīlapratisevanākuśīlabakuśā yugapad asaṃkhyeyāni sthānāni gacchanti. tato bakuśo vyucchidyate. tato ’py asaṃkhyeyāni sthānāni gatvā pratisevanākuśīlo vyucchidyate. tato ’py asaṃkhyeyāni sthānāni gatvā kaṣāyakuśīlo vyucchidyate. ata ūrdhvam akaṣāyasthānāni nirgranthaḥ pratipadyate. so ’py asaṃkhyeyāni sthānāni gattvā vyucchidyate. ata ūrdhvam ekaṃ sthānaṃ gatvā snātako nirvāṇaṃ prāpnotīty eteṣāṃ saṃyamalabdhir anantaguṇā bhavati.
children.translated_text: Section 919. Regarding the stages (<s>sthāna</s>): the stages of restraint (<s>saṃyamasthānas</s>) caused by passions are innumerable. Among these, the <s>pulāka</s> and <s>kaṣāyakuśīla</s> have the lowest attainment stages. Those two simultaneously pass through innumerable stages. Then the <s>pulāka</s> is discontinued. The <s>kaṣāyakuśīla</s> then proceeds alone through innumerable stages. Then the <s>kaṣāyakuśīla</s>, <s>pratisevanākuśīla</s>, and <s>bakuśa</s> simultaneously pass through innumerable stages. Then the <s>bakuśa</s> is discontinued. After passing through innumerable further stages, the <s>pratisevanākuśīla</s> is discontinued. After passing through innumerable further stages, the <s>kaṣāyakuśīla</s> is discontinued. Above that, the <s>nirgrantha</s> attains the passionless stages. He too, after passing through innumerable stages, is discontinued. Above that, after passing through one stage, the <s>snātaka</s> attains <s>nirvāṇa</s> — thus the restraint-attainment of these [monks] is infinitely greater [at each successive level].

children.text: iti tattvārthavṛttau sarvārthasiddhisaṃjñikāyāṃ navamo ’dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ || 9 ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter of the <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>, the commentary on the <s>Tattvārthasūtra</s>. || 9 ||

children.text: atha daśamo ’dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins the tenth chapter.

children.text: § 920. āha, ante nirdiṣṭasya mokṣasyedānīṃ svarūpābhidhānaṃ prāptakālam iti. satyam evam. mokṣaprāptiḥ kevalajñānāvāptir pūrvaketi kevalajñānotpattikāraṇam ucyate —
children.translated_text: Section 920. One says: it is now time to state the nature of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), which was mentioned last [in the enumeration]. That is indeed so. Since the attainment of <s>mokṣa</s> is preceded by the attainment of <s>kevalajñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge), the cause of the arising of <s>kevalajñāna</s> is stated —

children.text: mohakṣayāj jñānadarśanāvaraṇāntarāyakṣayāc ca kevalam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kevala</s> (omniscience) [arises] from the destruction of <s>moha</s> (delusion) and from the destruction of <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s> (knowledge-obscuring), <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s> (perception-obscuring), and <s>antarāya</s> (obstructive) [karmas]. ||

children.text: § 921. iha vṛttikaraṇaṃ nyāyyam. kutaḥ? laghutvāt. katham? ekasya ‘kṣaya’ śabdasyākaraṇād vibhaktyantaranirdeśasya cābhāvāt ‘ca’ śabdasya cāprayogāl laghu sūtraṃ bhavati ‘mohajñānadarśanāvaraṇāntarāyakṣayāt kevalam’ iti. satyam etat, kṣayakramapratipādanārtho vākyabhedena nirdeśaḥ kriyate. prāgeva mohaṃ kṣayam upanīyāntarmuhūrtaṃ kṣīṇakaṣāyavyapadeśam avāpya tato yugapaj jñānadarśanāvaraṇāntarāyāṇāṃ kṣayam kṛtvā kevalam avāpnoti iti. tatkṣayo hetuḥ kevalotpatter iti hetulakṣaṇo vibhaktinirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ. kathaṃ prageva mohaḥ kṣayam upanīyate iti ced ucyate — bhavyaḥ samyagdṛṣṭiḥ pariṇāmaviśuddhyā vardhamāno ’saṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭisaṃyatāsaṃyatapramattāpramattaguṇasthāneṣu kasmiṃs cin mohasya sapta prakṛtīḥ kṣayam upanīya kṣāyikasamyagdṛṣṭir bhūtvā kṣapakaśreṇyārohanābhimukho ’dhaḥpravṛttakaraṇam apramattasthāne pratipādyāpūrvakaraṇaprayogeṇāpūrvakaraṇakṣapakaguṇasthānavyapadeśam anubhūya tatrābhinavaśubhābhisandhitanūkṛtapāpaprakṛtisthityanubhāgo vivardhitaśubhakarmānubhavo ’nivṛttikaraṇaprāptyānivṛttibādarasāṃparāyakṣapakaguṇasthānam adhiruhya tatra kaṣāyāṣṭakaṃ naṣṭaṃ kṛtvā napuṃsakavedanāśaṃ samāpādya strīvedam unmūlya nokakaṣāyaṣaṭkaṃ puṃvede prakṣipya kṣapayitvā puṃvedaṃ krodhasaṃjvalane, krodhasaṃjvalanaṃ mānasaṃjvalane, mānasaṃjvalanaṃ māyāsaṃjvalane, māyāsaṃjvalanaṃ ca lobhasaṃjvalane krameṇa bādarakṛṣṭivibhāgena vilayam upanīya lobhasaṃjvalanaṃ tanūkṛtya sūkṣmasāmparāyakṣapakatvam anubhūya niravaśeṣaṃ mohanīyaṃ nirmūlakaṣāyaṃ kaṣitvā kṣīṇakaṣāyatām adhiruhyāvatāritamohanīyabhāra upāntyaprathame samaye nidrāpracale pralayam upanīya pañcānāṃ jñānāvaraṇānāṃ caturṇām darśanāvaraṇānāṃ pañcānām antarāyāṇāṃ cāntam ante samupanīya tadanantraṃ jñānadarśanasvabhāvaṃ kevalaparyāyam apratarkyavibhūtiviśeṣam avāpnoti.
children.translated_text: Section 921. Here, a compound construction would be proper. Why? Because of brevity. How? By not using a second instance of the word 'kṣaya' (destruction) and by omitting the indication through a different case-ending and not employing the word 'ca' (and), the sūtra would be brief: 'from the destruction of delusion, knowledge-obscuring, perception-obscuring, and obstructive [karmas] — omniscience.' This is true; however, the statement is made with a sentence-division for the purpose of indicating the sequence of destruction. First, having brought <s>moha</s> (delusion) to destruction and obtaining the designation of <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s> (one whose passions are destroyed) for less than one <s>muhūrta</s>, then simultaneously accomplishing the destruction of <s>jñānāvaraṇa</s>, <s>darśanāvaraṇa</s>, and <s>antarāya</s>, one attains <s>kevala</s> (omniscience). Their destruction is the cause of the arising of omniscience — thus the ablative case indicating cause is used. How is <s>moha</s> brought to destruction first? It is stated: a worthy soul with right faith, increasing in purity of disposition, at some point in the stages of <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, <s>saṃyatāsaṃyata</s>, <s>pramatta</s>, and <s>apramatta</s>, having destroyed seven sub-types of <s>moha</s>, becomes one of <s>kṣāyikasamyagdṛṣṭi</s> (destructional right faith). Then, facing the ascent of the <s>kṣapaka</s> (destruction) ladder, establishing the <s>adhaḥpravṛttakaraṇa</s> (downward process) in the <s>apramatta</s> stage, and through the operation of <s>apūrvakaraṇa</s> (unprecedented process) experiencing the designation of the <s>apūrvakaraṇa</s>-<s>kṣapaka</s> spiritual stage — there, with the duration and fruition of sinful karmic types attenuated by newly produced auspicious mental resolutions and with the experience of wholesome karma intensified — ascending to the <s>anivṛttibādarasāṃparāya</s>-<s>kṣapaka</s> spiritual stage through the attainment of <s>anivṛttikaraṇa</s> (non-retreating process), there having destroyed the eight-fold <s>kaṣāya</s> (passion-group), having accomplished the destruction of neuter gender, having uprooted feminine gender, having cast the six quasi-passions (<s>nokaṣāya</s>) into masculine gender and destroyed them, [then destroying] masculine gender within <s>saṃjvalana</s> (blazing) anger, <s>saṃjvalana</s> anger within <s>saṃjvalana</s> pride, <s>saṃjvalana</s> pride within <s>saṃjvalana</s> deceit, and <s>saṃjvalana</s> deceit within <s>saṃjvalana</s> greed — sequentially bringing them to dissolution through the method of gross extraction-division, attenuating <s>saṃjvalana</s> greed, experiencing the state of <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāya</s>-<s>kṣapaka</s>, having ploughed up the <s>mohanīya</s> karma entirely with its passions uprooted, ascending to the state of <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s> (one whose passions are destroyed) — with the burden of <s>mohanīya</s> cast down — at the penultimate moment, bringing <s>nidrā</s> (sleep) and <s>pracalā</s> (drowsiness) to dissolution, and at the final moment bringing the five <s>jñānāvaraṇas</s>, four <s>darśanāvaraṇas</s>, and five <s>antarāyas</s> to their ultimate end — immediately thereafter attains <s>kevala</s> (omniscience), which is of the nature of knowledge and perception, an extraordinary manifestation of inconceivable power.

children.text: § 922. āha kasmād dhetor mokṣaḥ kiṃ lakṣaṇaś cety atrocyate —
children.translated_text: Section 922. One asks: from what cause does <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) [arise], and what is its defining characteristic? To this it is replied —

children.text: bandhahetvabhāvanirjarābhyāṃ kṛtsnakarmavipramokṣo mokṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The complete release from all <s>karma</s>, through the absence of the causes of bondage and through <s>nirjarā</s> (shedding), is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). ||

children.text: § 923. mithyādarśanādihetvābhāvād abhinavakarmābhāvaḥ pūrvoditanirjarāhetusaṃnidhāne cārjitakarmanirāsaḥ. tābhyāṃ bandhahetvabhāvanirjarābhyām iti hetulakṣaṇavibhaktinirdeśaḥ. tato bhavasthitihetusamīkṛtaśeṣakarmāvasthasya yugapad ātyantikaḥ kṛtsnakarmavipramokṣo mokṣaḥ pratyetavyaḥ. karmābhāvo dvividhaḥ — yatnasādhyo ’yatnasādhyaś ceti. tatra caramadehasya nārakatiryagdevāyuṣām abhāvo na yatnasādhyaḥ, asattvāt. yatnasādhya ita ūrdhvam ucyate — asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭyādiṣu caturṣu guṇasthāneṣu kasmiṃś cit saptaprakṛtikṣayaḥ kriyate. nidrānidrāpracalāpracalāstyānagṛddhinarakagatitiryaggatyekadvitricaturindriyajātinarakagatitiryaggatiprāyogyānupūrvyātapodyotasthāvarasūkṣmasādhāraṇasaṃjñikānāṃ ṣoḍaśānāṃ karmaprakṛtināmanivṛttibādarasāmparāyasthāne yugapat kṣayaḥ kriyate. tataḥ paraṃ tatraiva kaṣāyāṣṭakaṃ naṣṭaṃ kriyate. napuṃsakavedaḥ strīvedaś ca krameṇa tatraiva kṣayam upayāti. nokaṣāyaṣaṭkaṃ ca sahaikenaiva prahāreṇa vinipātayati. tataḥ puṃvedasaṃjvalanakrodhamānamāyāḥ krameṇa tatraivātyantikaṃ dvaṃsam āskandanti. lobhasaṃjvalanaḥ sūkṣmasāmparāyānte yātyantam. nidrāpracale kṣīṇakaṣāyavītarāgacchadmasthasyopāntyasamaye pralayam upavrajataḥ. paṃcānāṃ jñānāvaraṇānāṃ caturṇāṃ darśanāvaraṇānāṃ paṃcānām antarāyāṇāṃ ca tasyaivāntyasamaye prakṣayo bhavati. anyataravedanīyadevagatyaudārikavaikriyikāhārakataijasakārmaṇaśarī

-paṃcabandhanapaṃcasaṃghātasaṃsthānaṣaṭkaudārikavaikriyikāhārakaśarīrāṅgopāṅgaṣaṭsaṃhananapaṃcapraśastavarṇapaṃcāpraśastavarṇagandhadvayapaṃcapraśastarasapañcāpraśastarasasparśāṣṭakadevagatiprāyogyānupūrvyāgurulaghūpaghātaparaghātochvāsapraśastāpraśastavihāyogatyaparyāptakapratyekaśarīrasthirāsthiraśubhāśubhadurbhagasusvaraduḥsvarānādeyāyaśaḥkīrtinirmāṇanāmanīcair gotrākhyā dvāsaptatiprakṛtayo ’yogakevalina upāntyasamaye vināśam upayānti. anyataravedanīyamanuṣyāyurmanuṣyagatipañcendriyajātimanuṣyagatiprāyogyānupūrvītrasabādaraparyāptakasubhagādeyayaśaḥkīrtitīrthakaranāmoccairgotrasaṃjñikānāṃ trayodaśānāṃ prakṛtīnām ayogakevalinaś caramasamaye vyucchedo bhavati.
children.translated_text: five bonds, five aggregates, six bodily frames, the limbs and minor limbs of gross, transformative, and assimilative bodies, six bone-joint structures, five praiseworthy colors, five unpraiseworthy colors, two smells, five praiseworthy tastes, five unpraiseworthy tastes, eight touches, the sequential-form karma of celestial destiny, non-heavy-non-light, self-destructive capacity, other-destructive capacity, respiration, praiseworthy and unpraiseworthy locomotion, undeveloped, individual body, stable and unstable, beautiful and ugly, misfortune, attractive and repulsive voice, unattractiveness, infamy, power of transformation, and low lineage — these seventy-two types reach destruction at the penultimate moment of the omniscient without activity (<s>ayogakevalin</s>). The thirteen types — namely, either-type <s>vedanīya</s>, human life-span, human destiny, five-sensed birth, the sequential-form karma of human destiny, mobile, gross, fully developed, fortunate, attractive, fame, the name-karma of a ford-maker, and high lineage — reach their final cessation at the last moment of the <s>ayogakevalin</s>.

Section 923. From the absence of causes such as wrong faith (<s>mithyādarśana</s>) and the rest, there is the absence of fresh karma; and in the presence of the previously stated causes of <s>nirjarā</s> (shedding), there is the removal of previously accumulated karma. 'Through the absence of the causes of bondage and through <s>nirjarā</s>' — thus the ablative case indicating cause is used. Thereupon, the complete and final release from all karma simultaneously, for one whose remaining karma — which served as the cause of continued existence — has been exhausted, should be understood as <s>mokṣa</s>. The absence of karma is of two kinds: that which is accomplished by effort and that which is accomplished without effort. Of these, the absence of hellish, animal, and celestial life-spans for one in the final body is not accomplished by effort, since they [simply] do not exist. What is accomplished by effort is stated henceforth: at some point in the four spiritual stages beginning with <s>asaṃyatasamyagdṛṣṭi</s>, the destruction of seven sub-types is accomplished. The sixteen karmic types — namely, <s>nidrānidrā</s>, <s>pracalāpracalā</s>, <s>styānagṛddhi</s>, hellish destiny, animal destiny, one-sensed, two-sensed, three-sensed, and four-sensed birth-types, the sequential-form karmas of hellish and animal destinies, heat, radiance, immobile, subtle, and common-body — are simultaneously destroyed at the <s>anivṛttibādarasāṃparāya</s> stage. Then, at that very stage, the eight-fold passion-group is destroyed. Neuter gender and feminine gender are sequentially destroyed at that very stage. The six quasi-passions are also struck down with a single blow together. Then masculine gender, <s>saṃjvalana</s> anger, pride, and deceit sequentially meet their final destruction at that very stage. <s>Saṃjvalana</s> greed reaches its end at the conclusion of the <s>sūkṣmasāṃparāya</s> stage. Sleep and drowsiness reach dissolution at the penultimate moment of the <s>kṣīṇakaṣāya</s>-<s>vītarāgachadmastha</s> (passionless-but-still-embodied) stage. The five <s>jñānāvaraṇas</s>, four <s>darśanāvaraṇas</s>, and five <s>antarāyas</s> are completely destroyed at his final moment. The seventy-two types — namely, either-type <s>vedanīya</s>, celestial destiny, gross physical body, transformative body, assimilative body, luminous body, karmic body,

children.text: § 924. āha, kim āsāṃ paudgalikīnām eva dravyakarmaprakṛtīnāṃ nirāsān mokṣo ’vasīyate uta bhāvakarmaṇo ’pīty atrocyate —
children.translated_text: Section 924. One asks: is liberation established merely from the removal of these material karmic types (<s>dravyakarmaprakṛtis</s>) that are material in nature, or also from the [removal] of psychic karma (<s>bhāvakarma</s>)? To this it is replied —

children.text: aupaśamikādibhavyatvānāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And [from the cessation] of the <s>aupaśamika</s> (subsidence-born) and other [psychic states], and of <s>bhavyatva</s> (the capacity for liberation). ||

children.text: § 925. kim? ‘mokṣaḥ’ ity anuvartate. bhavyatvagrahaṇam anyapāriṇāmikanivṛttyartham. tena pāriṇāmikeṣu bhavyatvasyaupaśamikādīnāṃ ca bhāvānām abhāvān mokṣo bhavatīty abhyupagamyate.
children.translated_text: Section 925. What? 'Liberation' continues [from the previous sūtra]. The mention of <s>bhavyatva</s> is for the purpose of excluding the cessation of the <s>pāriṇāmika</s> (natural) [states]. Thus it is accepted that liberation occurs from the absence of <s>aupaśamika</s> and other psychic states, along with <s>bhavyatva</s>, among the <s>pāriṇāmika</s> states.

children.text: § 926. āha, yady apavargo bhāvoparateḥ pratijñāyate, nanu aupaśamikādibhāvanivṛttivatsarvakṣāyikabhāvanivṛttivyapadeśo muktasya prāpnotīti. syād etat evaṃ yadi viśeṣo nocyate. asty atra viśeṣa ity apavādavidhānārtham idam ucyate —
children.translated_text: Section 926. One objects: if liberation is claimed to follow from the cessation of [psychic] states, would not the designation of cessation of the <s>kṣāyika</s> (destructional) states also apply to the liberated being, just as the cessation of <s>aupaśamika</s> and other states [is affirmed]? This would be so if no distinction were stated. There is a distinction here, and for the purpose of stating the exception, this is said —

children.text: anyatra kevalasamyaktvajñānadarśanasiddhatvebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Except for <s>kevalasamyaktva</s> (absolute right faith), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>darśana</s> (perception), and <s>siddhatva</s> (the state of being liberated). ||

children.text: § 927. anyatraśabdāpekṣayā ‘kā’ nirdeśaḥ. kevalasamyaktvajñānadarśanasiddhatvebhyo ’nyatrānyasminn ayaṃ vidhir iti. yadi catvāra evāvaśiṣyante, anantavīryādīnāṃ nivṛttiḥ prāpnoti? naiṣa doṣaḥ, jñānadarśanāvinābhāvitvād anantavīryādīnām aviśeṣaḥ, anantasāmarthyahīnasyānantāvabodhavṛttyabhāvāj jñānamayatvāc ca sukhasyeti. anākaratvān muktānām abhāva ity cen na; atītānantaraśarīrākāratvāt.
children.translated_text: Section 927. The designation is in the ablative case in relation to the word 'anyatra' (except). The rule applies 'to everything other than <s>kevalasamyaktva</s>, <s>jñāna</s>, <s>darśana</s>, and <s>siddhatva</s>.' If only four remain, would not the cessation of infinite energy (<s>anantavīrya</s>) and the like be entailed? This is no defect, because <s>anantavīrya</s> and the like are inseparable from knowledge and perception, and there is no distinction [to be made], since one lacking infinite capacity cannot have the functioning of infinite cognition, and because bliss is of the nature of knowledge. If it is objected that the liberated have no [bodily] form and therefore [these qualities] are absent — no, because they have the form of the immediately preceding body.

children.text: § 928. syān mataṃ, yadi śarīrānuvidhāyī jīvaḥ, tadabhāvāt svābhāvikalokākāśapradeśaparimāṇatvāt tāvad visarpaṇaṃ prāpnotīti. naiṣa doṣaḥ. kutaḥ? kāraṇāhāvāt. nāmakarmasaṃbandho hi saṃharaṇavisarpaṇakāraṇam. tadabhāvāt punaḥ saṃharaṇavisarpaṇābhāvaḥ.
children.translated_text: Section 928. It may be thought: if the soul conforms to the body, then in its absence, since the soul has the measure of the spatial units of innate space (<s>lokākāśa</s>), it would spread out. This is no defect. Why? Because of the absence of the cause. For it is the connection with <s>nāma</s> (name-determining) karma that is the cause of contraction and expansion. In the absence of that, there is no further contraction or expansion.

children.text: § 929. yadi kāraṇābhāvān na saṃharaṇaṃ na visarpaṇaṃ tarhi gamanakāraṇābhāvād ūrdhvagamanam api na prāpnoti adhastiryaggamanābhāvāt, tato yatra muktas tatraivāvasthānaṃ prāpnotīty. atrocyate —
children.translated_text: Section 929. If, due to the absence of a cause, there is neither contraction nor expansion, then due to the absence of a cause of motion, upward movement also should not occur, since there is no downward or lateral movement — and therefore [the soul] should remain wherever it was liberated. To this it is replied —

children.text: tadanantaram ūrdhvaṃ gacchatyā lokāntāt ||
children.translated_text: Immediately thereafter, it goes upward to the end of the universe (<s>lokānta</s>). ||

children.text: § 930. tasyānantaram. kasya? sarvakarmavipramokṣasya. āṅabhividhyarthaḥ. ūrdhvaṃ gacchatyā lokāntāt.
children.translated_text: Section 930. 'Immediately thereafter' — after what? After the complete release from all karma. The prefix 'ā' is for the purpose of [indicating] thoroughness. It goes upward to the end of the universe.

children.text: § 931. anupadiṣṭahetukam idam ūrdhvagamanaṃ katham adhyavasātum śakyam ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: Section 931. How can this upward movement, for which no cause has been taught, be ascertained? To this it is replied —

children.text: pūrvayogād asaṅgatvād bandhacchedāt tathāgatipariṇāmāc ca ||
children.translated_text: Due to the prior impulse of activity (<s>pūrvayoga</s>), due to non-attachment (<s>asaṅgatva</s>), due to the severing of bondage (<s>bandhaccheda</s>), and due to the inherent tendency to move thus (<s>tathāgatipariṇāma</s>). ||

children.text: § 932. āha, hetvarthaḥ puṣkalo ’pi dṛṣṭāntasamarthanam antareṇābhipretārthasādhanāya nālam ity atrocyate —
children.translated_text: Section 932. One objects: even though the reasoning through causes is abundant, without the support of an illustration, it is insufficient to establish the intended meaning. To this it is replied —

children.text: āviddhakulālacakravadvyapagatalepālābuvaderaṇḍabījavadagniśikhāvac ca ||
children.translated_text: Like a potter's wheel once set in motion (<s>āviddhakulālacakra</s>), like a gourd freed from its coating (<s>vyapagatalepālābu</s>), like a castor seed (<s>eraṇḍabīja</s>), and like a flame of fire (<s>agniśikhā</s>). ||

children.text: § 933. pūrvasūtre vihitānāṃ hetūnām atroktānāṃ dṛṣṭāntānāṃ ca yathāsaṃkhyam abhisaṃbandho bhavati. tad yathā — kulālaprayogāpāditahastadaṇḍacakrasaṃyogapūrvakaṃ bhramaṇam. uparante ’pi tasmin pūrvaprayogād ā saṃskārakṣayād bhramati. evaṃ bhavasthenātmanāpavargaprāptaye bahuśo yatpraṇidhānaṃ tadabhāve ’pi tadāveśapūrvakaṃ muktasya gamanam avasīyate. kiṃ ca, asaṅgatvāt. yathā mṛttikālepajanitagauravam alābudravyaṃ jale ’dhaḥpatitaṃ jalakledaviśliṣṭamṛttikābandhanaṃ laghu sadūrdhvam eva gacchati tathā karmabhārākrāntivaśīkṛta ātmā tadāveśavaśāt saṃsāre aniyamena gacchati. tatsaṅgavimuktas tūparyevopayāti. kiṃ ca, bandhacchedāt. yathā bījakośabandhacchedāt eraṇḍabījasya gatir dṛṣṭā tathā manuṣyādibhavaprāpakagatijātināmādisakalakarmabandhacchedān muktasya ūrdhvagatir avasīyate. kiṃ ca, tathāgatipariṇāmāt. yathā tiryakplavanasvabhāvasamīraṇasaṃbandhanirutsukā pradīpaśikhā svabhāvād utpatati tathā muktātmāpi nānagativikārakāraṇakarmanirvāraṇe saty ūrdhvagatisvabhāvād ūrdhvam evārohati.
children.translated_text: Section 933. The causes stated in the previous sūtra and the illustrations mentioned here are connected in corresponding order. As follows: a potter's wheel, set in motion by the application of the hand, stick, and wheel working together, continues to spin even after that [initial] effort ceases, due to the residual momentum from the prior impulse, until that momentum is exhausted. Similarly, the soul while in worldly existence (<s>bhavastha</s>) has repeatedly made resolves for the attainment of liberation (<s>apavarga</s>); even in the absence of those [resolves after liberation], the upward movement of the liberated one is understood as proceeding through the force of that [prior] impulse. Furthermore, because of non-attachment (<s>asaṅgatva</s>): just as a gourd, made heavy by a coating of clay, when submerged in water, upon the clay bond being dissolved by the moisture of the water, becomes light and rises upward, so too the soul, subjugated by the weight of karmic burden, moves without fixed direction in <s>saṃsāra</s> due to the force of karmic influence; but when freed from that attachment, it ascends upward only. Furthermore, because of the severing of bondage: just as the movement of a castor seed is observed upon the severing of its seed-pod bond, so too the upward movement of the liberated one is understood upon the severing of all karmic bonds — destiny (<s>gati</s>), species (<s>jāti</s>), name (<s>nāma</s>), and the like — that cause existence as humans and so forth. Furthermore, because of the transformation toward that [upward] direction: just as a flame, indifferent to its connection with wind whose nature is lateral movement, rises upward by its own nature, so too the liberated soul, when there is no karma causing downward or lateral directional modification, ascends upward only, by its own nature of upward movement.

children.text: § 934. āha, yadi mukta ūrdhvagatisvabhāvo lokāntād ūrdhvam api kasmān notpatatīty atrocyate —
children.translated_text: Section 934. One objects: if the liberated soul has an inherent nature of upward movement, why does it not fly upward beyond the boundary of the universe? To this it is replied —

children.text: dharmāstikāyābhāvād ||
children.translated_text: Because of the absence of <s>dharmāstikāya</s> (the substance of motion) [beyond the universe].

children.text: § 935. gatyupagrahakāraṇabhūto dharmāstikāyo nopary astīty aloke gamanābhāvaḥ. tadabhāve ca lokālokavibhāgābhāvaḥ prasajyate.
children.translated_text: Section 935. The <s>dharmāstikāya</s>, which serves as the auxiliary cause for movement, does not exist above [the universe]; hence there is no movement in the non-universe (<s>aloka</s>). And in its absence, the distinction between universe and non-universe would become untenable.

children.text: § 936. āha, amī parinivṛttā gatijātyādibhedakāraṇābhāvād atītabhedavyavahārā eveti. asti kathaṃcid bhedo ’pi. kutaḥ —
children.translated_text: Section 936. One says: those who have attained final liberation (<s>parinivṛtta</s>), being devoid of the causes of distinction such as destiny and species, have transcended the conventional usage of distinctions. Yet there is some distinction in a certain respect. How so? —

children.text: kṣetrakālagatiliṅgatīrthacāritrapratyekabudddhabodhitajñānāvagāhanāntarasaṃkyālpabahutvataḥ sādhyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The liberated ones (<s>siddhas</s>) are to be analyzed according to place (<s>kṣetra</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), destiny (<s>gati</s>), gender (<s>liṅga</s>), <s>tīrtha</s>, conduct (<s>cāritra</s>), whether self-enlightened or enlightened by another (<s>pratyekabuddhabodhita</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), bodily extent (<s>avagāhana</s>), interval (<s>antara</s>), number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>), and comparative quantity (<s>alpababutva</s>).

children.text: § 937. kṣetrādibhir dvādaśābhir anuyogaiḥ siddhāḥ sadhyā vikalpyā ity arthaḥ, pratyutpannabhūtānugrahatantranayadvayavivakṣāvaśāt. tad yathā — kṣetreṇa tāvat kasmin kṣetre sidhyanti? pratyutpannagrāhinayāpekṣayā siddhikṣtre svapradeśe ākāśapradeśe vā siddhir bhavati. bhūtagrāhinayāpekṣayā janma prati pañcadaśasu karmabhūmiṣu, saṃharaṇaṃ prati mānuṣyakṣetre siddhiḥ. kālena kasmin kāle siddhiḥ? pratyutpannanayāpekṣayā ekasamaye siddhyan siddho bhavati. bhūtaprajñāpananayāpekṣayā janmato ’viśeṣeṇotsarpiṇyavasarpiṇyor jātaḥ sidhyati. viśeṣeṇāvarsarpiṇyāṃ suṣamaduḥṣamāyā antye bhāge duḥṣamasuṣamāyāṃ ca jātaḥ sidhyati. na tu duḥṣamāyāṃ jāto duḥṣamāyāṃ sidhyati. anyadā naiva sidhyati. saṃharaṇataḥ sarvasmin kāle utsarpiṇyām avasarpiṇyāṃ ca sidhyati. gatyā kasyāṃ gatau siddhiḥ? siddhigatau manuṣyagatau vā. liṃgena kena siddhiḥ? avedatvena tribhyo vā vedebhyaḥ siddhir bhāvito na dravyataḥ. dravyataḥ pulliṃgenaiva. athavā nirgranthaliṃgena. sagranthaliṃgena vā siddhir bhūtapūrvanayāpekṣayā. tīrthena, tīrthasiddhiḥ dvedhā tīrthakaretaravikalpāt. itare dvividhāḥ sati tīrthakare siddhā asati ceti. cāritreṇa kena sidhyati. avyapadeśenaikacatuḥpañcavikalpacāritreṇa vā siddhiḥ. svaśaktiparopadeśanimittajñānabhedāt pratyekabuddhabodhitavikalpaḥ. jñānena kena? ekena dvitricaturbhiś ca jñānaviśeṣaiḥ siddhiḥ. ātmapradeśavyāpitvam avagāhanam. tad dvividham, utkṛṣṭajaghanyabhedāt. tatrotkṛṣṭaṃ paṃcadhanuḥśatāni pañcaviṃśatyuttarāṇi. jaghanyam ardhacaturthāratnayo deṣonāḥ. madhye vikalpāḥ. ekasminn avagāhe sidhyati. kim antaram? sidhyatāṃ siddhānām anantaraṃ jaghanyena dvau samayau utkarṣeṇāṣṭau. antaraṃ jaghanyenaikaḥ samayaḥ utkarṣeṇa ṣaṇmāsāḥ. saṃkhyā, jaghanyena ekasamaye ekaḥ sidhyati. utkarṣeṇāṣṭottaraśatasaṃkhyāḥ. kṣetrādibhedabhinnānāṃ parasparataḥ saṃkhyāviśesṣo ’lpabahutvam. tad yathā — pratyutpannanayāpekṣayā siddhikṣetre sidhyantīti nāsty alpabahutvam. bhūtapūrvanayāpekṣayā tu cintyate, kṣetrasiddhā dvividhā — janmataḥ saṃharaṇataś ca. tatrālpe saṃharaṇasiddhāḥ. janmasiddhāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. kṣetrāṇāṃ vibhāgaḥ karmabhūmir akarmabhūmiḥ samudro dvīpa ūrdhvam adhas tiryag iti. tatra stokā ūrdhvalokasiddhāḥ. adholokasiddhāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. tiryaglokasiddhāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. sarvataḥ stokāḥ samudrasiddhāḥ. dvīpasiddhāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. evaṃ tāvad aviśeṣeṇa. sarvataḥ stokā lavaṇodasiddhāḥ. kālodasiddhāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. jambūdvīpasiddhāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. dhātakīkhaṇḍasiddhāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇāḥ. puṣkaradvīpārdhasiddhāḥ saṃkhyeyaguṇā iti. evaṃ kālādivibhāge ’pi yathā gamam alpabahutvaṃ veditavyam. || TAS 10 ||
children.translated_text: Section 937. The <s>siddhas</s> (liberated ones) are to be analyzed — that is, differentiated — by twelve investigative categories beginning with place (<s>kṣetra</s>), from the viewpoint of both the present-grasping and past-grasping doctrinal standpoints. As follows: regarding place — in which place do they attain liberation? From the standpoint of the present-grasping doctrine, liberation occurs in the <s>siddhi</s>-field, in one's own spatial units, or in a spatial unit of space. From the standpoint of the past-grasping doctrine, with respect to birth, [liberation occurs for those born] in the fifteen <s>karmabhūmis</s> (lands of action); with respect to the final gathering [of karma], liberation occurs in the human realm. Regarding time — at what time does liberation occur? From the present-standpoint, one who attains liberation at one time-instant is liberated. From the standpoint of past designation, without distinction, one born in either the ascending (<s>utsarpiṇī</s>) or descending (<s>avasarpiṇī</s>) cycle attains liberation. Specifically, one born in the last part of the <s>suṣamaduḥṣamā</s> era or in the <s>duḥṣamasuṣamā</s> era of the descending cycle attains liberation. But one born in the <s>duḥṣamā</s> era does not attain liberation in the <s>duḥṣamā</s> era, nor does liberation ever occur at other times. With respect to the final gathering, liberation occurs at all times, in both ascending and descending cycles. Regarding destiny — in which destiny does liberation occur? In the <s>siddhi</s>-destiny or the human destiny. Regarding gender — by which gender? By the state of non-gender (<s>avedatva</s>), or from [any of] the three genders liberation occurs in the psychic sense, not materially; materially, only through the male gender. Or, with the mark of the unattached (<s>nirgrantha</s>); or liberation with the mark of the attached (<s>sagrantha</s>), from the standpoint of the past doctrine. Regarding <s>tīrtha</s> — <s>tīrtha</s>-liberation is twofold, by the distinction of whether [attained] through a <s>tīrthakara</s> or otherwise. The others are twofold: those liberated when a <s>tīrthakara</s> exists and when one does not. Regarding conduct — by which conduct does one attain liberation? By the <s>avyapadeśa</s> (indeterminate) conduct, or by the one-, four-, or five-fold varieties of conduct. The distinction of self-enlightened (<s>pratyekabuddha</s>) and enlightened-by-another (<s>bodhita</s>) arises from the difference between knowledge arising from one's own power and that arising from another's instruction. Regarding knowledge — by which [knowledge]? Liberation occurs through one, two, three, or four specific types of knowledge. The pervading of the soul's spatial units is the bodily extent (<s>avagāhana</s>). It is twofold: maximum and minimum. The maximum is five hundred and twenty-five bow-lengths. The minimum is three and a half cubits, slightly less. In between there are [various] possibilities. Liberation occurs at one [particular] bodily extent. What is the interval? Between those attaining liberation and the [previously] liberated, the minimum [duration of liberation activity] is two time-instants, the maximum is eight. The interval [between successive liberations] is at minimum one time-instant, at maximum six months. Regarding number: at minimum, one attains liberation at one time-instant. At maximum, one hundred and eight. The comparative quantity (<s>alpababutva</s>) is the numerical distinction among those differentiated by place and other categories in relation to each other. As follows: from the standpoint of the present doctrine, [all] attain liberation in the <s>siddhi</s>-field, so there is no comparative distinction. But from the standpoint of the past doctrine, it is analyzed: those liberated with respect to place are twofold — by birth and by final gathering. Among these, fewer are those liberated by final gathering; those [liberated] by birth are countably more. The division of places is: <s>karmabhūmi</s>, <s>akarmabhūmi</s>, ocean, island, above, below, and transverse. Among these, few are those liberated in the upper world; those liberated in the lower world are countably more; those liberated in the transverse world are countably more [still]. Among all, fewest are the ocean-liberated; island-liberated are countably more. Thus far, without distinction. Of all, fewest are those liberated at <s>Lavaṇoda</s> (Salt Ocean); those liberated at <s>Kāloda</s> (Black-water Ocean) are countably more; those liberated at <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> are countably more; those liberated at <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s> are countably more; those liberated at <s>Puṣkaradvīpārdha</s> are countably more. Similarly, in the division by time and the rest, the comparative quantities should be understood accordingly. || TAS 10 ||

children.text: svargāpavargasukham āptumanobhir āryair jainendraśāsanavarāmṛtasārabhūtā |
children.translated_text: By noble ones desiring the bliss of heaven and liberation, the essence of the supreme nectar of <s>Jaina</s> teaching,

children.text: sarvārthasiddhir iti sadbhir upāttanāmā tattvārthavṛttir aniśaṃ manasā pradhāryā || 1 ||
children.translated_text: this [work] called <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s> by the virtuous — the commentary on the <s>Tattvārtha</s> [sūtra] — should be constantly contemplated in the mind. || 1 ||

children.text: tattvārthavṛttim uditāṃ viditārthatattvāḥ śṛṇvanti ye paripaṭhanti ca dharmabhaktyā |
children.translated_text: Those who, knowing the truth of meaning, listen to this <s>Tattvārthavṛtti</s> as it has been expounded, and recite it with devotion to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: haste kṛtaṃ paramasiddhisukhāmṛtaṃ tair martyāmareśvarasukheṣu kim asti vācyam ||2||
children.translated_text: for them the nectar of supreme liberation-bliss is in hand — what need be said of the pleasures of mortals, lords of gods? || 2 ||

children.text: yenedam apratihataṃ sakalārthatattvam udyotitaṃ vimalakevalalocanena |
children.translated_text: He by whom this unobstructed truth of all categories was illuminated through the pure eye of omniscience (<s>kevalajñāna</s>),

children.text: bhaktyā tam adbhutaguṇaṃ praṇamāmi vīramārānnarāmaragaṇārcitapādapīṭham || 3 ||
children.translated_text: to that <s>Vīra</s> of wondrous qualities, whose footstool is worshipped by hosts of <s>Māras</s>, humans, and gods — to him I bow with devotion. || 3 ||
Section 938.

children.text: iti tattvārthavṛttau sarvārthasiddhisaṃjñikāyāṃ daśamo ’dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth chapter in the <s>Tattvārthavṛtti</s> named <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>.

children.text: śubhaṃ bhavatu sarveṣām |
children.translated_text: May there be auspiciousness for all.
